rule: wall framing must not have stud spacing that exceeds the maximum permitted span of the cladding or sheathing material attached to it
conditions: wall framing supports cladding or sheathing

subject: Wall Framing
rule: wall framing must be laterally braced against buckling about its weak axis
conditions: wall framing uses slender columns or studs in compression

subject: Wall Framing
rule: wall framing must not contain wood members with moisture content above 19% at time of enclosure
conditions: wall framing is wood

subject: Wall Cladding
rule: Wall cladding must be securely attached to the substrate or support structure
conditions: wall cladding is installed as a non-structural facing
exceptions: temporary or removable cladding systems explicitly designed for demountability

subject: Wall Cladding
rule: Wall cladding must provide a weather-resistant barrier that prevents moisture ingress to the underlying wall assembly
conditions: cladding is used as the exterior finish of a building envelope
exceptions: interior-only wall cladding applications where moisture control is handled by separate systems

subject: Wall Cladding
rule: Wall cladding must not trap moisture against the substrate or within its own layers
conditions: cladding is installed on exterior walls
exceptions: cladding materials and assemblies specifically designed to manage bulk water through intentional drainage and ventilation gaps

subject: Wall Cladding
rule: Wall cladding must have provision for differential movement (thermal expansion and contraction) relative to the substrate
conditions: cladding material has a coefficient of thermal expansion significantly different from the substrate
or the cladding spans large continuous areas such that restrained expansion would cause buckling or cracking
exceptions: cladding systems with inherently negligible thermal movement or those bonded with fully accommodating adhesives proven over the full service temperature range

subject: Wall Damp-Proofing
rule: A wall damp-proof course (DPC) must form a continuous, unbroken barrier across the full thickness of the wall to prevent moisture bridging
conditions: wall construction includes a damp-proof course
exceptions: walls where the DPC is deliberately omitted in historically-sensitive breathable construction where moisture management relies entirely on vapor-permeable materials and drainage cavities

subject: Wall Damp-Proofing
rule: A wall damp-proof course (DPC) must be located at least 150 mm above finished ground level (or paving level) to prevent rainwater splash-back and bridging
conditions: wall has a damp-proof course and is adjacent to external ground or paving

subject: Wall Damp-Proofing
rule: A wall damp-proof course (DPC) must not be bridged by external render, earth, mortar, paving, or any other material that extends from below to above the DPC level
conditions: wall has a damp-proof course
exceptions: engineered bridging that forms part of a designed drainage plane system and is detailed to prevent water penetration

subject: Wall Opening/Window
rule: a wall opening/window must have a lintel or structural header spanning the opening
conditions: opening width exceeds the structural capacity of the surrounding wall material to bridge the gap without support
exceptions: opening is in a non-loadbearing infill panel where the surrounding frame provides support
opening is small enough that the surrounding masonry can arch over it without additional support

subject: Wall Opening/Window
rule: a wall opening/window must be weather-sealed at all penetrations between the frame and the wall
conditions: opening is exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: opening is a fully interior window between conditioned spaces

subject: Wall Opening/Window
rule: a wall opening/window must not have glass or infill that projects unsupported beyond the frame

subject: Wall Lintel
rule: wall lintel must be capable of supporting the load imposed by the wall, floor, or roof above its opening
conditions: lintel spans an opening in a load-bearing wall

subject: Wall Lintel
rule: wall lintel must have sufficient bearing (end support) length on each side of the opening
conditions: lintel is supported by masonry or concrete wall construction

subject: Wall Lintel
rule: wall lintel must not be installed with inadequate vertical clearance above the opening to accommodate its depth and deflection
conditions: lintel is sized to span a specific opening dimension

subject: Wall Tie
rule: wall ties must be corrosion-resistant in exterior cavity walls
conditions: wall is a cavity wall with exterior exposure
exceptions: interior non-load-bearing walls not exposed to moisture

subject: Wall Tie
rule: wall ties must be installed with correct orientation (drip feature pointing downward)
conditions: tie type includes a drip feature (e.g., wire or butterfly ties)
exceptions: ties without a drip feature orientation requirement

subject: Wall Tie
rule: wall ties must not bridge the cavity (must be fully embedded within mortar joints at both ends with no continuous path for water)
conditions: cavity wall construction

subject: Wall Tie
rule: wall ties must be spaced at maximum intervals per structural design (not exceeding manufacturer or code maximum spacing)
conditions: any wall with wall ties
exceptions: areas with reduced loading or non-structural partitions where alternate design is approved

subject: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
rule: wall footer/foundation wall must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: when supporting a superstructure
exceptions: when founded on deep foundation elements (piles, piers) that transfer load to deeper strata

subject: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
rule: wall footer/foundation wall must be placed below frost depth
conditions: in climates subject to seasonal freezing
exceptions: when foundation is designed as frost-protected shallow foundation per engineered design
when soil is non-frost-susceptible and verified by geotechnical investigation

subject: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
rule: wall footer/foundation wall must not be placed on organic soils, uncompacted fill, or debris

subject: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
rule: wall footer/foundation wall must have minimum width and reinforcement per structural design for the applied loads
conditions: when supporting a superstructure

subject: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
rule: wall footer/foundation wall must be constructed with concrete or masonry of sufficient strength to resist soil and structural loads

subject: Strip Footing
rule: strip footing must transfer load to soil without exceeding bearing capacity
exceptions: when supporting a structure that has been designed with deep foundation system that bypasses the strip footing

subject: Strip Footing
rule: strip footing must be placed below the frost line
conditions: in climates where seasonal ground freezing occurs
exceptions: when the strip footing is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation techniques per engineering code

subject: Strip Footing
rule: strip footing must be continuous along the length of the supported wall
exceptions: when discontinuous pad footings are designed for specific structural conditions such as openings or columns

subject: Strip Footing
rule: strip footing must not be placed on uncompacted fill
exceptions: when fill is engineered, compacted to specified density, and verified by geotechnical testing

subject: Isolated Pad Footing
rule: isolated pad footing must have a minimum bearing area to prevent excessive soil pressure exceeding allowable bearing capacity
conditions: soil bearing capacity is known
column load is known

subject: Isolated Pad Footing
rule: isolated pad footing must have a minimum depth to resist punching shear at the column-footing interface
conditions: column is of concrete or steel transferring concentrated load

subject: Isolated Pad Footing
rule: isolated pad footing must not be placed on uncompacted or uncontrolled fill
conditions: footing supports a structural load

subject: Isolated Pad Footing
rule: isolated pad footing must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement for corrosion and fire resistance
conditions: footing contains steel reinforcement
footing is cast-in-place or precast concrete

subject: Isolated Pad Footing
rule: isolated pad footing must not have tension at its base under service loads
conditions: footing is unreinforced or plain concrete

subject: Combined Footing
rule: combined footing must bear on soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity to support the applied loads without excessive settlement or bearing failure
conditions: when used as a foundation element
exceptions: when designed as a piled combined footing that transfers load to deeper strata

subject: Combined Footing
rule: combined footing must have a minimum concrete cover over reinforcement as required by code for cast-in-place concrete in soil contact
conditions: when reinforced concrete is used as the footing material
exceptions: when protected by an impermeable membrane or other durable corrosion protection system

subject: Combined Footing
rule: combined footing must not experience net uplift under any load combination without adequate anchorage or mass to resist uplift forces
conditions: when the combined footing supports structures subject to overturning or uplift loads

subject: Combined Footing
rule: combined footing must be placed below the frost line in frost-susceptible soils
conditions: when constructed in a climate with seasonal ground freezing and frost-susceptible soil conditions
exceptions: when the footing is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation techniques per applicable code

subject: Raft Foundation / Mat Foundation
rule: raft foundation must be thick enough to distribute building loads to the soil without exceeding soil bearing capacity
conditions: building is founded on soil with low bearing capacity
building load is concentrated at columns or walls

subject: Raft Foundation / Mat Foundation
rule: raft foundation must have continuous steel reinforcement in both top and bottom mats
conditions: raft thickness exceeds 300 mm
raft is reinforced concrete
exceptions: non-reinforced plain concrete rafts on very low loads and competent rock may omit top reinforcement

subject: Raft Foundation / Mat Foundation
rule: raft foundation must not be placed on fill material that is uncontrolled or uncompacted
conditions: raft bears directly on fill rather than natural ground or engineered fill
exceptions: engineered fill placed under strict geotechnical control (e.g., layer thickness, moisture, compaction testing) is acceptable

subject: Raft Foundation / Mat Foundation
rule: raft foundation must have a minimum depth of cover over reinforcement in compliance with corrosion exposure class
conditions: raft is reinforced concrete exposed to soil or groundwater
exceptions: where raft is protected by an effective waterproofing membrane system that is guaranteed for the design life

subject: Pile Foundation
rule: pile foundation must be embedded to a depth that transfers structural loads to competent bearing stratum
conditions: soil bearing capacity at founding depth is less than applied load
exceptions: piles designed as friction piles in homogeneous deep clay where skin friction alone provides adequate capacity

subject: Pile Foundation
rule: pile foundation must not be placed in expansive or collapsible soils without mitigation such as void forms or telescoping sleeves
conditions: site soils exhibit high plasticity index (>30) or collapse potential upon wetting

subject: Pile Foundation
rule: pile cap must have a minimum thickness adequate to transfer pile reactions without punching shear failure
conditions: pile cap is used to distribute loads from superstructure to multiple piles
exceptions: single-pile foundations where the pile extends directly into the structure

subject: Pile Foundation
rule: pile foundation must not be constructed in frozen ground without mitigating thaw-induced settlement
conditions: permafrost or seasonally frozen ground present at pile depth
exceptions: thermopiles or piles with thermal protection systems that maintain frozen ground stability

subject: Pile Cap
rule: pile cap must have minimum dimensions to adequately transfer loads from the superstructure to the piles
conditions: when pile cap supports columns or walls

subject: Pile Cap
rule: pile cap must have sufficient thickness to resist punching shear around each pile and column
conditions: when subject to concentrated loads from columns or piles

subject: Pile Cap
rule: pile cap must not have its bottom reinforcement placed directly on the ground without adequate cover
conditions: when cast in-situ against soil

subject: Pile Cap
rule: pile cap must be cast with concrete of adequate strength to handle compressive and shear stresses at the pile-cap interface
conditions: when designed per limit state code

subject: Grade Beam
rule: grade beam must be supported on continuous undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: grade beam is load-bearing
grade beam transfers wall or column loads to soil
exceptions: grade beam is supported on deep foundation elements such as piles or caissons

subject: Grade Beam
rule: grade beam must not be placed on frozen ground
conditions: construction occurs in cold-climate regions where seasonal frost is present
exceptions: ground is thermally protected or thawed immediately before placement

subject: Grade Beam
rule: grade beam must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcing steel as required by code for soil contact
conditions: grade beam contains steel reinforcement
grade beam is cast in contact with soil

subject: Grade Beam
rule: grade beam must have continuous longitudinal reinforcement through construction joints or splices must be fully developed
conditions: grade beam is designed as a continuous structural element
exceptions: joint is designed as a deliberate expansion or contraction joint with load-transfer devices

subject: Foundation Wall
rule: foundation wall must extend below the frost line
conditions: in regions where the ground freezes
exceptions: if the foundation is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation techniques in accordance with applicable codes

subject: Foundation Wall
rule: foundation wall must not be constructed on uncompacted or organic soil
exceptions: if the soil is entirely removed and replaced with engineered fill per geotechnical specifications

subject: Foundation Wall
rule: foundation wall must be continuous and load-bearing around the entire building perimeter
conditions: for buildings with load-bearing perimeter walls
exceptions: buildings designed with a structural frame that transfers all loads directly to isolated footings or piles, where foundation walls serve only as infill or enclosure

subject: Foundation Wall
rule: foundation wall must have dampproofing or waterproofing applied to the exterior face below grade
conditions: in habitable buildings where the foundation wall encloses occupied space below grade
exceptions: in arid climates with no groundwater and where code does not require it
for unconditioned crawlspaces designed to permit airflow and drainage

subject: Foundation Wall
rule: foundation wall must be laterally supported at the top by the floor diaphragm or structural tie
conditions: for tall foundation walls (e.g., basement walls) subject to lateral earth pressure
exceptions: walls designed as cantilever retaining walls with sufficient reinforcement and base fixity to resist lateral loads without top support

subject: Slab-on-Grade
rule: slab-on-grade must have a minimum thickness of structural fill or crushed stone base below the concrete to prevent frost heave and provide uniform support
conditions: in cold climates where frost depth exceeds slab thickness
on expansive or compressible soils
exceptions: when slab is structurally reinforced to span across non-uniform soil conditions
when soil is non-frost-susceptible and adequately drained

subject: Slab-on-Grade
rule: slab-on-grade must have a vapor barrier or retarder placed directly beneath the concrete
conditions: when the slab is interior and receives a moisture-sensitive floor covering such as wood, vinyl, or carpet
exceptions: when slab is exterior (e.g., patio, sidewalk) where moisture migration is not a serviceability concern

subject: Slab-on-Grade
rule: slab-on-grade must be provided with control joints or reinforcement to limit cracking from shrinkage and thermal movement
conditions: when slab area exceeds approximately 150 ft² (14 m²) per panel
exceptions: when slab is continuously reinforced with steel or fiber mesh to control crack widths without discrete joints

subject: Slab-on-Grade
rule: slab-on-grade must_not be placed directly on organic topsoil or uncompacted fill

subject: Slab-on-Grade
rule: slab-on-grade must have the top of slab elevation at least 150 mm (6 in) above the adjacent exterior finish grade
conditions: when slab is at the lowest occupied level of a building
when located in a region subject to rainfall or surface water flow
exceptions: when site has positive drainage away from building in all directions and a waterproofing system is used at slab edge

subject: Basement Foundation
rule: Basement foundation must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: Foundation is shallow (spread footing or mat)
exceptions: Deep foundation systems (piles, caissons) transfer load to competent strata below

subject: Basement Foundation
rule: Basement foundation must extend below the frost line
conditions: Location experiences seasonal ground freezing
exceptions: Frost-protected shallow foundation design with insulation per code

subject: Basement Foundation
rule: Basement foundation must not have continuous standing water against its exterior wall
exceptions: Designs with a fully engineered waterproofing and drainage system that actively prevents hydrostatic pressure on the wall

subject: Crawlspace Foundation
rule: Crawlspace foundation must have a minimum clearance between the bottom of the floor joists and the ground
conditions: Foundation type is crawlspace

subject: Crawlspace Foundation
rule: Crawlspace foundation must have ventilation openings in the perimeter wall
conditions: Foundation type is crawlspace
No engineered moisture management system (e.g., encapsulated crawlspace with vapor barrier and dehumidification)
exceptions: Encapsulated crawlspace with an approved mechanical ventilation or dehumidification system may eliminate venting requirements

subject: Crawlspace Foundation
rule: Crawlspace foundation must not have organic material (wood debris, stumps, plants) left in the crawlspace before closing
conditions: Foundation type is crawlspace

subject: Crawlspace Foundation
rule: Crawlspace foundation must have a vapor retarder covering the exposed earth floor
conditions: Foundation type is crawlspace

subject: Pier Foundation
rule: pier foundation must bear on competent load-bearing soil or engineered fill of adequate capacity
conditions: foundation is designed for vertical load transfer
exceptions: foundation is designed to transfer load to deep piles or caissons that bypass surface soils

subject: Pier Foundation
rule: pier foundation must extend below the frost line
conditions: site is located in a climate zone with seasonal ground freezing
foundation supports a structure sensitive to frost heave
exceptions: foundation is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation details per applicable code exceptions

subject: Pier Foundation
rule: pier foundation must not be placed on fill or disturbed soil without verification of compaction and bearing capacity
conditions: fill was placed without engineered compaction testing
exceptions: fill material has been geotechnically tested and approved as engineered structural fill meeting design bearing requirements

subject: Pier Foundation
rule: pier foundation must have a minimum concrete compressive strength adequate for the design loads
conditions: pier is constructed of cast-in-place concrete
exceptions: design uses a different material system (e.g., treated timber, precast concrete, or steel) with its own strength requirements per code

subject: Pier Foundation
rule: pier foundation must be installed plumb (vertical) within allowable tolerance
conditions: pier is designed for vertical load transfer
exceptions: design specifically calls for battered (raking) piers at a defined angle

subject: Foundation Drainage System
rule: foundation drainage system must drain water away from the building foundation to at least the minimum horizontal distance specified by code
conditions: building has a foundation
foundation is in contact with soil
site receives precipitation or has groundwater
exceptions: building on permafrost where drainage would thaw permafrost
building in permanently arid region with no groundwater and no precipitation reaching foundation

subject: Foundation Drainage System
rule: foundation drainage system must not discharge onto adjacent property in a manner that causes damage or nuisance
conditions: drainage system outfalls above grade
adjacent property exists within drainage path
exceptions: adjacent property is unoccupied public right-of-way
adjacent property owner has granted drainage easement

subject: Foundation Drainage System
rule: foundation drainage pipe must have a minimum slope of 1% (1/8 inch per foot) toward the discharge point
conditions: system uses gravity-fed perforated or solid drain pipe
exceptions: system uses pumped or siphonic drainage

subject: Foundation Drainage System
rule: foundation drainage aggregate or filter fabric must not allow migration of fine soil particles into the drain pipe
conditions: system includes granular backfill or geotextile wrap around perforated pipe
exceptions: drainage system is a prefabricated composite drain board with integral filter that does not use loose aggregate

subject: Dampproofing Coating
rule: Dampproofing coating must form a continuous, unbroken membrane across the entire substrate surface
conditions: Dampproofing coating is applied as a liquid-applied or trowel-applied material

subject: Dampproofing Coating
rule: Dampproofing coating must not be applied over surfaces with sharp protrusions, debris, or contaminants that prevent full adhesion
conditions: Dampproofing coating is applied to concrete or masonry substrates

subject: Subgrade Base Course
rule: Subgrade base course must be composed of granular material that is free-draining
conditions: When used in pavement construction
When placed below the water table
exceptions: When specifically designed as a stabilized or treated base course where fines are bound by cement or other binders

subject: Subgrade Base Course
rule: Subgrade base course must have a minimum CBR (California Bearing Ratio) value of 20 at the required compaction density
conditions: When used as a structural layer in flexible pavement design

subject: Subgrade Base Course
rule: Subgrade base course must_not contain organic material or highly plastic clay

subject: Steel Beam
rule: Steel beam must have a minimum depth-to-span ratio to prevent excessive deflection under design loads
conditions: beam is simply supported
beam carries gravity loads
exceptions: beam is designed as a cambered member
beam is part of a deflection-controlled system with active compensation

subject: Steel Beam
rule: Steel beam must not have lateral-torsional buckling unbraced length exceed the limiting length specified by code without adequate lateral bracing
conditions: beam is subject to bending about its major axis
beam has a non-compact or slender cross-section
exceptions: beam is fully braced against lateral displacement of the compression flange at all load points
beam is designed as a non-structural element carrying no bending load

subject: Steel Beam
rule: Steel beam end connections must transfer design reactions without exceeding connection element capacities
conditions: beam is load-bearing
beam is connected to supports via bolted or welded connections
exceptions: beam is intentionally discontinuous and not part of the load path

subject: Steel Beam
rule: Steel beam must not be loaded beyond its plastic moment capacity unless designed as a ductile fuse element
conditions: beam is part of a gravity or lateral force-resisting system
exceptions: beam is specifically detailed as a ductile link in an eccentrically braced frame or similar engineered fuse system that permits controlled yielding

subject: Reinforced Concrete Beam
rule: Reinforced concrete beam must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement to prevent corrosion and fire exposure
conditions: Beam is exposed to environment
Beam is part of fire-rated structure
exceptions: Beam is protected by permanent cladding or fireproofing that provides equivalent protection

subject: Reinforced Concrete Beam
rule: Reinforced concrete beam must have reinforcement (tensile steel) in the tension zone
conditions: Beam is subject to flexural loading
exceptions: Beam is unreinforced and designed as plain concrete where tensile stresses are below concrete tensile strength (rare, limited to very small or non-structural elements)

subject: Reinforced Concrete Beam
rule: Reinforced concrete beam must not have reinforcement ratio exceeding the balanced (or maximum) reinforcement ratio
conditions: Beam is designed for flexure under ultimate loads

subject: Reinforced Concrete Beam
rule: Reinforced concrete beam must have stirrups (shear reinforcement) when design shear force exceeds concrete shear capacity
conditions: Beam is subject to shear forces exceeding the nominal shear strength of the concrete section alone

subject: Reinforced Concrete Beam
rule: Reinforced concrete beam must have adequate anchorage/development length for reinforcement bars
conditions: Reinforcement bars are present in the beam
exceptions: Mechanical anchorage devices (hooks, heads, or couplers) provide equivalent force transfer

subject: Timber Beam
rule: timber beam must have a minimum cross-sectional dimension to resist bending and shear stresses
conditions: beam is a structural element
beam is load-bearing
exceptions: beam is purely decorative and carries no load

subject: Timber Beam
rule: timber beam must not have notches or holes that reduce its effective cross-section beyond code-allowed limits
conditions: beam is in a loadbearing configuration
exceptions: notches/holes are within permitted zones (e.g., near supports) and are fully accounted for in engineered design

subject: Timber Beam
rule: timber beam must have a maximum span-to-depth ratio that prevents excessive deflection
conditions: beam spans between two or more supports
beam carries occupancy or live loads
exceptions: beam is part of a system where deflection is accommodated (e.g., independent cladding)

subject: Timber Beam
rule: timber beam must have adequate lateral bracing or be proportioned to prevent lateral-torsional buckling
conditions: beam has a high depth-to-width ratio (slender cross-section)
beam is not continuously restrained by decking or diaphragm
exceptions: beam is very short with low slenderness ratio where buckling is not a failure mode

subject: Composite Beam
rule: composite beam must have shear connectors between the steel section and the concrete slab
conditions: steel-concrete composite beam
exceptions: beams where full composite action is not required and slip is permitted by design

subject: Composite Beam
rule: composite beam must have the concrete slab in compression and the steel section in tension under positive bending
conditions: simply supported composite beam under gravity loading
exceptions: continuous composite beams where negative moment regions may reverse this distribution

subject: Composite Beam
rule: composite beam must not have the concrete slab thickness less than the minimum required for fire resistance and structural depth
conditions: composite beam with a concrete slab on metal decking

subject: Composite Beam
rule: composite beam web must not be designed with a depth-to-thickness ratio that permits local buckling before reaching design capacity
conditions: steel section of a composite beam subject to significant shear
exceptions: beams where web stiffeners are provided to prevent local buckling

subject: Lintel Beam
rule: A lintel beam must span the full width of the opening it bridges
conditions: the lintel is installed over a door, window, or other wall opening

subject: Lintel Beam
rule: A lintel beam must be supported on each end by sufficient bearing surface (minimum bearing length)
conditions: the lintel is installed over a wall opening

subject: Lintel Beam
rule: A lintel beam must be axially aligned with the wall plane and not tilt or rotate out of plane
conditions: the lintel is installed in a masonry or concrete wall

subject: Precast Prestressed Beam
rule: Precast prestressed beam must have minimum concrete cover over prestressing strands to prevent corrosion and fire damage
conditions: Exposed to environment
Interior conditioned space
exceptions: Protected interior environment with fire-rated encapsulation

subject: Precast Prestressed Beam
rule: Precast prestressed beam must not have strand eccentricity that exceeds the section's tension capacity at transfer of prestress
conditions: At prestress transfer stage (before any superimposed load)
exceptions: When debonding or draped strands are specifically designed to control top fiber tension

subject: Precast Prestressed Beam
rule: Precast prestressed beam must have adequate shear reinforcement (stirrups) in regions where principal tension exceeds concrete tensile capacity
conditions: Reaction zones and concentrated load points
Regions with large shear-to-moment ratios
exceptions: Solid slabs or shallow beams where shear is carried by concrete alone per code

subject: Precast Prestressed Beam
rule: Precast prestressed beam must be designed for the full prestress force at transfer to not overstress concrete beyond allowable compressive stress
conditions: Immediately after prestress transfer
exceptions: When high-strength concrete is used with verified early-age strength exceeding minimum required

subject: Precast Prestressed Beam
rule: Precast prestressed beam must have temporary stability during handling, transport, and erection
conditions: Before final connection and diaphragm/roof slab installation
exceptions: When beam is propped or braced at intermediate points during handling

subject: Tie Beam
rule: tie beam must be continuous through supports or properly lapped/spliced
conditions: tie beam is used to resist axial tension forces
in seismically active regions
exceptions: when tie beam is intentionally designed as a pinned or simple connection element with explicit detailing for discontinuity

subject: Tie Beam
rule: tie beam must have minimum cross-sectional dimension of at least 200mm (or as specified by local code)
conditions: tie beam is part of reinforced concrete framed structure
exceptions: when a lighter non-structural tie beam is used only for architectural alignment and explicitly excluded from lateral load-resisting system

subject: Tie Beam
rule: tie beam must not be placed fully below slab level without proper waterproofing and corrosion protection
conditions: tie beam is located at grade or in contact with soil
exceptions: when tie beam is designed with appropriate waterproofing membrane, drainage, and corrosion-resistant reinforcement

subject: Ring Beam / Plinth Beam
rule: Ring beam / plinth beam must be continuous around the entire building perimeter
conditions: Building has a ring beam or plinth beam at foundation/plinth level
exceptions: Segmented or post-tensioned designs specifically engineered to behave as continuous via connections

subject: Ring Beam / Plinth Beam
rule: Ring beam / plinth beam must not have unreinforced joints or cold joints without proper dowel reinforcement across the joint
conditions: Concrete ring beam or plinth beam is cast in multiple pours
exceptions: Joints designed as deliberate construction joints with keyed surfaces and adequate dowel bars per structural design

subject: Ring Beam / Plinth Beam
rule: Ring beam / plinth beam must be placed at a minimum depth below finished ground level to protect against frost heave in frost-susceptible soils
conditions: Building is located in a region with frost potential
Soil is frost-susceptible
exceptions: Building on a foundation system that is adequately protected against frost by other means (e.g., insulation, non-frost-susceptible backfill)

subject: Ring Beam / Plinth Beam
rule: Ring beam / plinth beam must be reinforced with minimum longitudinal reinforcement as required by structural code to resist tensile and temperature/shrinkage stresses
conditions: Concrete ring beam or plinth beam
exceptions: Precast or pre-stressed systems verified by structural design to meet strength without minimum code reinforcement

subject: Transfer Beam
rule: a transfer beam must have sufficient reinforcement to resist the tensile forces induced by the loads it transfers
conditions: when used as a structural element transferring loads from discontinuous columns or walls to supporting elements below

subject: Transfer Beam
rule: the depth of a transfer beam must be adequate to prevent excessive deflection under service loads
conditions: when spanning across openings or transferring concentrated loads

subject: Transfer Beam
rule: a transfer beam must not lack continuity with its supporting vertical elements (columns or walls)
conditions: at beam-column or beam-wall joints

subject: Spandrel Beam
rule: Spandrel beam must have adequate flexural and shear capacity to resist lateral load transfer from the floor diaphragm to the supporting columns or walls
conditions: When serving as part of the lateral force-resisting system
When diaphragm action transfers horizontal forces through the spandrel
exceptions: When the structure uses a separate lateral system (e.g., braced frames or shear walls) that bypasses the spandrel

subject: Spandrel Beam
rule: Spandrel beam must have a minimum horizontal bearing length of at least 90 mm (3.5 in) on masonry or concrete supports
conditions: When the spandrel beam is supported on masonry or concrete walls or pilasters
exceptions: When engineering analysis demonstrates adequate bearing under code provisions for a reduced dimension
When bearing is on steel brackets or corbels designed per AISC standards

subject: Spandrel Beam
rule: Spandrel beam must not have its tension reinforcement interrupted or inadequately developed at the beam-column joint
conditions: In reinforced concrete spandrel beams
In seismic design categories D, E, or F
exceptions: When alternative ductile detailing per ACI 318 Chapter 18 provides equivalent development

subject: Spandrel Beam
rule: Spandrel beam must be provided with proper anchorage to the floor diaphragm to ensure complete in-plane load transfer
conditions: When the spandrel beam is part of a diaphragm chord or collector element
exceptions: When the diaphragm is designed to transfer forces through an alternate load path (e.g., drag struts directly to vertical elements)

subject: Cantilever Beam
rule: cantilever beam must have a fixed or continuous support at one end
exceptions: a beam with both ends free (non-cantilever) is a different entity

subject: Cantilever Beam
rule: cantilever beam must not have a support at its free end

subject: Cantilever Beam
rule: cantilever beam must have its upper fiber in tension under gravity load
conditions: when subjected to downward vertical loads (e.g., self-weight, live load)

subject: Structural Column
rule: structural column must have a continuous load path from supported elements to foundation
conditions: column is load-bearing
exceptions: aesthetic/non-structural columns (decorative only, not part of structural system)

subject: Structural Column
rule: structural column must be laterally braced in both orthogonal directions
conditions: column is part of a frame structure
column height exceeds 10x its least lateral dimension
exceptions: columns designed as cantilevers where lateral stability is provided by alternative means (e.g., fixed base with moment connection)

subject: Structural Column
rule: structural column must not be placed in a location that conflicts with required egress paths or exit corridors
conditions: building is occupied by people
column is in a means-of-egress path

subject: Steel Column
rule: steel column must have adequate axial load capacity for the imposed loads
conditions: when column is load-bearing

subject: Steel Column
rule: steel column must be laterally braced at intervals not exceeding the unbraced length limits
conditions: when column is subject to compressive loads

subject: Steel Column
rule: steel column must not have a slenderness ratio exceeding the code-prescribed maximum

subject: Steel Column
rule: steel column base plate must be anchored to the foundation
conditions: when column is a vertical structural element

subject: Decorative Column
rule: A decorative column must not be load-bearing unless explicitly designed and detailed for structural loading
conditions: Decorative column is not labeled or documented as structural
exceptions: Column is explicitly designed, detailed, and specified as a structural member

subject: Decorative Column
rule: A decorative column must be positively attached to the structure with engineered connections

subject: Decorative Column
rule: A decorative column must have expansion/contraction joints or gaps at top and bottom if the material has a coefficient of thermal expansion different from the supporting structure
conditions: Column material differs structurally from the building frame material
exceptions: Column and supporting structure are of the same material with compatible movement characteristics

subject: Decorative Column
rule: A decorative column must not obstruct required egress width or fire-exit paths
conditions: Column is located in a means of egress corridor, aisle, or exit path
exceptions: Clear width around the column still meets applicable building code minimums

subject: Reinforced Concrete Column
rule: reinforced concrete column must have minimum cross-sectional dimensions to prevent buckling under design loads
conditions: column is structural (not architectural or decorative)

subject: Reinforced Concrete Column
rule: reinforced concrete column's longitudinal reinforcement ratio must exceed the minimum required to resist tensile stresses from bending and eccentric loading
conditions: column is structural (not architectural or decorative)
column carries eccentric or lateral loads
exceptions: purely axially loaded columns where code minimum still applies for ductility but tensile resistance is not structurally critical

subject: Reinforced Concrete Column
rule: reinforced concrete column must have transverse reinforcement (ties or spirals) spaced closely enough to confine the core concrete and prevent buckling of longitudinal bars
conditions: column is structural (not architectural or decorative)

subject: Reinforced Concrete Column
rule: reinforced concrete column must not have less concrete cover than the minimum specified to protect reinforcement from corrosion and fire
conditions: column is exposed to environment or fire ratings apply
exceptions: interior columns in controlled environments where cover is reduced per code allowance for strictly controlled conditions

subject: Timber Column
rule: timber column must have adequate slenderness ratio to prevent buckling under design loads
conditions: column is axially loaded
column height exceeds 10 times its least lateral dimension
exceptions: column is fully braced against lateral deflection at intermediate points

subject: Timber Column
rule: timber column must be connected such that load is transferred axially through full cross-section or through verified metal connectors
conditions: column is load-bearing

subject: Timber Column
rule: timber column must not be in direct contact with concrete or masonry at its base without a capillary break or damp-proof membrane
conditions: column base bears on concrete slab, footing, or masonry wall
exceptions: column is made of preservative-treated or naturally durable heartwood species rated for ground contact

subject: Timber Column
rule: timber column must be protected from exposure to sustained moisture or direct weathering
conditions: column is located outdoors or in a wet interior space (e.g., shower, untreated basement)
exceptions: column is preservative-treated or of naturally durable species for the exposure condition
column is designed as sacrificial (replaceable)

subject: Masonry Column
rule: masonry column must have adequate load-bearing capacity for its design loads
conditions: when used as a structural element

subject: Masonry Column
rule: masonry column must have a height-to-thickness (slenderness) ratio within code-prescribed limits
conditions: when acting as a load-bearing element

subject: Masonry Column
rule: masonry column must be laterally supported at intervals that prevent buckling
conditions: when the column is tall or unrestrained along its height

subject: Masonry Column
rule: masonry column must not be constructed in freezing weather without appropriate protection
conditions: when mortar or grout is wet and susceptible to freeze-thaw damage

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column must satisfy equilibrium of axial load, bending moment, and shear at all sections
conditions: Under all factored load combinations

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column must have sufficient shear connection between steel and concrete components to ensure composite action
conditions: When relying on composite action for strength or stiffness

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column must not exceed its axial load capacity under any load combination

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column must not have net tension in the steel section that exceeds the tensile capacity of the steel-to-concrete connection or the steel itself
conditions: When the column is subjected to uplift or overturning forces

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column concrete cover to steel section must meet minimum fire resistance and corrosion protection requirements
conditions: For fire-rated construction or exposed environments

subject: Composite Column
rule: Composite column slenderness ratio must not exceed code limits for composite compression members

subject: Column Capital
rule: column capital must transfer load from the beam/slab above to the column shaft below
conditions: column capital is used as a structural load-transfer element

subject: Column Capital
rule: column capital must have sufficient bearing area to prevent punching shear failure at the column junction
conditions: column capital is located at the top of a reinforced concrete column supporting a flat slab or flat plate

subject: Column Capital
rule: column capital must not reduce the clear headroom below the minimum required by applicable building code
conditions: building is occupied by people

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must transfer axial load from column to supporting foundation without exceeding bearing capacity of supporting material
conditions: column is in compression
base plate sits on concrete or masonry support

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must have sufficient thickness to resist bending due to upward bearing pressure from the support
conditions: base plate is loaded in compression
exceptions: base plate is rigidly grouted such that bending stresses are negligible

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must be anchored to the foundation with a minimum number of anchor bolts to prevent uplift or overturning
conditions: column is subject to net uplift force or overturning moment
exceptions: column is purely gravity-loaded and has no tensile demand under any load combination

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must not be less than the cross-sectional dimensions of the column it supports
exceptions: column is set on a centrally loaded pedestal wider than the column and base plate is designed per engineering analysis

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must have a flat bearing surface in contact with the support
exceptions: use of levelling nuts and grout is specified to achieve full bearing after erection

subject: Column Base Plate
rule: column base plate must have edge distance to anchor bolts sufficient to prevent bolt pull-through or plate edge failure
conditions: anchor bolts are present

subject: Column Formwork
rule: column formwork must withstand the full hydrostatic head of wet concrete without bursting or excessive deflection
conditions: when using liquid concrete with standard slump
exceptions: when using self-compacting concrete with significantly reduced pressure characteristics
when formwork is designed with controlled deflection joints

subject: Column Formwork
rule: column formwork must be leak-tight at all joints to prevent grout loss

subject: Column Formwork
rule: column formwork must not be stripped before the concrete has reached sufficient compressive strength to support its own weight and any anticipated construction loads
exceptions: when using accelerated curing methods with verified early strength test results

subject: Column Formwork
rule: column formwork ties and clamps must be capable of resisting the lateral thrust of concrete without loosening during pour

subject: Column Fireproofing
rule: Column fireproofing must cover the full structural height of the column between the floor slab and the ceiling or roof deck above
conditions: The column is part of a building requiring fire-resistance-rated construction
Fireproofing is applied to a structural column
exceptions: Columns that are fire-engineered with an alternative performance-based solution validated by fire testing or computational modeling
Columns located in spaces exempt from fire rating per applicable building code

subject: Column Fireproofing
rule: Column fireproofing must maintain continuity at beam-to-column connections (no unprotected gaps at joints)
conditions: The column has intersecting beams or girders that require fire protection
exceptions: Connections specifically designed and tested to achieve the required fire-resistance rating without spray-applied fireproofing

subject: Column Fireproofing
rule: Column fireproofing must not be applied over surfaces contaminated with oil, grease, rust scale, or loose mill scale
conditions: The substrate is steel
Fireproofing is spray-applied
exceptions: Surfaces that have been properly cleaned and prepared per manufacturer specifications

subject: Column Fireproofing
rule: Column fireproofing material thickness must not be less than the minimum specified by the tested assembly listing or manufacturer's design
conditions: Fireproofing has been specified for a required fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Thickness reductions validated by engineering analysis and approved by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Column Splice
rule: column splice must transfer axial force between connected column segments
conditions: column splice is used in a load-bearing column

subject: Column Splice
rule: column splice must develop the required moment capacity when part of a moment-resisting frame
conditions: column is part of a moment-resisting frame (i.e., the splice is subject to bending)

subject: Column Splice
rule: column splice must not be located at the same elevation as a beam-to-column connection unless specifically designed for combined detailing
conditions: both splice and beam connection occur at the same floor level
exceptions: connections are specifically designed and detailed for combined effects per code provisions

subject: Column Splice
rule: column splice must provide adequate bolt or weld capacity to resist factored design loads
conditions: splice uses bolted or welded connections

subject: Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: column reinforcement cage must have concrete cover of at least the minimum specified depth (typically 40mm for internal, 50mm for external according to code)
conditions: when cage is placed in formwork and concrete is to be poured
exceptions: when protected by permanent formwork or a sacrificial layer that provides equivalent protection against corrosion and fire

subject: Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: column reinforcement cage must not have longitudinal bar splices located in the potential plastic hinge zone (typically the top and bottom 1/6 of the column clear height) unless they are designed as fully ductile splices
conditions: in seismic design categories and moment-resisting frames
exceptions: when the splice is mechanically coupled and tested to meet ductility requirements equivalent to the unspliced bar

subject: Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: column reinforcement cage must have transverse ties or hoops spaced at no more than the maximum permitted spacing (typically the smaller of 16× longitudinal bar diameter, 48× tie bar diameter, or the least column dimension)
conditions: for all reinforced concrete columns
exceptions: when a rational design analysis demonstrates that larger spacing still provides adequate confinement and buckling restraint, which is rarely accepted in practice

subject: Floor Slab
rule: floor slab must have a minimum thickness sufficient to resist design loads without excessive deflection
conditions: when slab is part of structural floor system
when slab spans between supports
exceptions: non-structural topping slabs not designed for load transfer

subject: Floor Slab
rule: floor slab must not have a downward slope toward any interior occupied area
conditions: when the slab is in an interior conditioned space
when the slab is part of a habitable floor
exceptions: intentionally sloped floors such as ramps or amphitheaters

subject: Floor Slab
rule: floor slab must be supported by a continuous load-bearing substrate or structural frame capable of carrying the slab's self-weight plus superimposed loads
conditions: for all suspended slabs
for slabs on grade where the subgrade is not competent
exceptions: slabs on grade over properly compacted fill that meets bearing capacity requirements

subject: Roof Slab
rule: roof slab must maintain minimum slope for drainage (typically ≥ 1/8" per foot for flat roofs, ≥ 1/4" per foot for low-slope roofs)
conditions: roof slab is horizontal (not pitched as part of primary roof structure)
roof is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: internal conditioned spaces with no rain exposure
roof slab designed as a planter or green roof with integrated drainage layer

subject: Roof Slab
rule: roof slab must be waterproofed or have a continuous waterproof membrane
conditions: roof slab separates interior occupied space from exterior weather exposure
exceptions: unoccupied open parking structure where water infiltration into the slab is acceptable
roof slab that is itself a non-habitable deck with open joints

subject: Roof Slab
rule: roof slab must not have deflection exceeding span/240 under full design load (or stricter for brittle finishes)
conditions: roof slab is part of a structural frame supporting occupancy or finishes

subject: Slab Edge / Spandrel Slab
rule: slab edge / spandrel slab must not exceed the maximum allowable deflection under design loads
conditions: used in structural applications
designed to building code requirements

subject: Slab Edge / Spandrel Slab
rule: spandrel slab must have a continuous load path to the supporting structure
conditions: serving as a primary lateral or gravity load-resisting element

subject: Slab Edge / Spandrel Slab
rule: slab edge must be protected against water intrusion at the interface with adjacent building envelope components
conditions: exposed to exterior environment
exceptions: interior slab edges not exposed to weather

subject: Ground/Foundation Slab
rule: ground/foundation slab must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill of adequate bearing capacity
conditions: Slab is load-bearing
Structure is not pile-founded
exceptions: Slab is structurally suspended on piles or deep foundations

subject: Ground/Foundation Slab
rule: ground/foundation slab must be provided with a capillary break or vapour barrier between the slab and the subgrade
conditions: Slab is in contact with the ground
exceptions: Slab is designed as a permeable or intentionally drained pavement system

subject: Ground/Foundation Slab
rule: ground/foundation slab must be reinforced with steel or equivalent tensile reinforcement when spanning over soft spots, openings, or non-continuous support
conditions: Slab has openings, soft zones beneath, or discontinuous bearing
exceptions: Slab is thick enough to act as an unreinforced mass concrete element and tensile stresses are verified as low

subject: Ground/Foundation Slab
rule: ground/foundation slab must not be placed on frozen ground
conditions: Construction occurs in a climate subject to freezing temperatures
exceptions: Ground is artificially thawed and maintained above freezing until concrete cures

subject: Ground/Foundation Slab
rule: ground/foundation slab must have a minimum thickness adequate for the imposed loads and soil conditions

subject: Precast Hollow-Core Slab
rule: Precast hollow-core slab must have its hollow cores oriented parallel to the span direction
conditions: When used as a floor or roof structural element
exceptions: Non-structural applications where orientation is irrelevant

subject: Precast Hollow-Core Slab
rule: Precast hollow-core slab must not be subjected to point loads without a structural topping or load-distribution system
conditions: When the slab is used without a cast-in-place topping
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified load capacities are verified for the specific point load location and magnitude

subject: Precast Hollow-Core Slab
rule: Precast hollow-core slab must not have openings cut through the webs without edge stiffening or manufacturer approval
conditions: When the opening intersects a core void or web
exceptions: Openings located entirely within a single core that does not affect adjacent webs, per manufacturer's approved cutting plan

subject: Precast Hollow-Core Slab
rule: Precast hollow-core slab must have minimum end bearing of 75 mm on masonry or 50 mm on steel/concrete supports
conditions: When used in simply-supported floor/roof applications
exceptions: Manufacturer-specific design values confirmed by structural calculations

subject: Suspended Slab
rule: suspended slab must have adequate thickness to resist bending and shear under design loads
conditions: when spanning between supports
under anticipated dead and live loads

subject: Suspended Slab
rule: suspended slab must contain tensile reinforcement (steel or equivalent) to resist bending moments
conditions: when constructed of reinforced concrete
when spanning between supports
exceptions: prestressed concrete with appropriately designed tendons
slabs using engineered fiber-reinforced polymer reinforcement with proven tensile capacity

subject: Suspended Slab
rule: suspended slab must be connected to a structural load path that transfers forces to foundations
conditions: in any building structure

subject: Composite Steel Deck Slab
rule: Composite steel deck slab must have a minimum concrete cover over the top of the steel deck
conditions: When used as a structural floor or roof diaphragm

subject: Composite Steel Deck Slab
rule: Composite steel deck slab must have shear connectors (studs) to achieve composite action between steel deck and concrete
conditions: When designed as a composite structural element transmitting horizontal shear

subject: Composite Steel Deck Slab
rule: Composite steel deck must not span beyond its unshored construction limit without temporary shoring
conditions: During wet concrete placement before concrete cures

subject: Composite Steel Deck Slab
rule: Composite steel deck slab must have a minimum slab thickness (total depth) not less than the deck manufacturer's specified minimum
conditions: For any composite deck application

subject: Composite Steel Deck Slab
rule: Composite steel deck must not be used in fire-resistance-rated assemblies without the required fireproofing or fire-rated topping
conditions: When the building code requires a fire-resistance rating for the floor/roof assembly

subject: Post-Tensioned Slab
rule: Post-tensioned slab must have its tendons fully encapsulated in concrete or grout
conditions: The slab uses bonded post-tensioning
exceptions: Unbonded post-tensioning systems where tendons are greased and sheathed

subject: Post-Tensioned Slab
rule: Post-tensioned slab must not have tendons stressed before concrete reaches specified minimum compressive strength
conditions: Any post-tensioned slab

subject: Post-Tensioned Slab
rule: Post-tensioned slab must have anchorage zones designed to resist bursting and spalling forces
conditions: All post-tensioned slabs with anchored tendons

subject: Post-Tensioned Slab
rule: Post-tensioned slab must not have un-bonded tendons in exterior spans without proper corrosion protection
conditions: Unbonded post-tensioning system used in exterior spans or exposed environments
exceptions: Interior spans in controlled indoor environments with proper encapsulation

subject: Slab Formwork
rule: Slab formwork must be designed to support all construction loads (wet concrete, reinforcement, workers, equipment, and impact) without collapse or excessive deflection
conditions: during concrete placement and curing

subject: Slab Formwork
rule: Slab formwork must be stripped only after the concrete has achieved sufficient strength to support its own weight and any applied loads
conditions: post-concrete placement

subject: Slab Formwork
rule: Slab formwork must not have gaps or openings through which wet concrete can leak uncontrollably
conditions: during concrete placement

subject: Slab Formwork
rule: Slab formwork must be aligned to the correct slab elevation and geometry within specified tolerances before concrete placement
conditions: prior to concrete placement

subject: Slab Reinforcement
rule: slab reinforcement must have minimum concrete cover as specified by structural code to prevent corrosion and maintain fire resistance
conditions: when reinforcement is exposed to environment or interior conditioned space
exceptions: post-tensioned unbonded tendons with dedicated corrosion protection systems

subject: Slab Reinforcement
rule: slab reinforcement must not have lap splices located in regions of maximum tensile stress unless specifically detailed for that condition
conditions: when using non-contact lap splices in conventionally reinforced slabs
exceptions: mechanical couplers or welded splices designed for tension are used at the location

subject: Slab Reinforcement
rule: slab reinforcement must be anchored to develop full tensile capacity at simple supports and at discontinuities
conditions: for bottom reinforcement in continuous or simply supported slabs
exceptions: if a strut-and-tie model or refined analysis shows anchorage is not required at that specific location

subject: Slab Reinforcement
rule: slab reinforcement must be placed at the correct depth (effective depth) within the slab section as required by structural design
conditions: for all flexural and temperature/shrinkage reinforcement

subject: Slab Vapour Barrier
rule: Slab vapour barrier must be continuous across the entire floor area
conditions: when a vapour barrier is specified for a concrete slab-on-grade
exceptions: where discontinuities are required for structural joints

subject: Slab Vapour Barrier
rule: Slab vapour barrier must be placed directly beneath the concrete slab, not on top of it
conditions: for below-grade or on-grade vapour barrier applications
exceptions: when a vapour barrier is deliberately installed above slab as part of a specific flooring system (e.g., certain epoxy systems) — but this is a different functional layer

subject: Slab Vapour Barrier
rule: Slab vapour barrier must not be installed on both sides of a concrete slab
conditions: for a single concrete slab on grade

subject: Slab Edge Insulation
rule: Slab edge insulation must be installed continuously around the perimeter of the concrete slab, with no gaps or breaks in the thermal envelope.
conditions: When slab-on-grade construction is used
When the building has a conditioned space at grade level
exceptions: Where the slab edge is not part of the conditioned space boundary (e.g., unconditioned garage slabs)

subject: Slab Edge Insulation
rule: Slab edge insulation must extend vertically to the depth required by the local frost line or a minimum of 600 mm below grade, whichever is greater.
conditions: When the slab-on-grade serves a conditioned space
In climates with freezing ground temperatures
exceptions: Where local codes or geotechnical reports demonstrate no frost concern

subject: Slab Edge Insulation
rule: Slab edge insulation must not be installed below the finished grade in a manner that creates a termite path hidden from inspection.
conditions: In termite-prone regions
exceptions: Where termite-protective materials (e.g., treated insulation, physical barriers) and a visible inspection gap are provided

subject: Slab Edge Insulation
rule: Slab edge insulation must be protected from physical damage where exposed above grade.
conditions: When the insulation is located above the finished exterior grade
exceptions: Where the insulation material is inherently impact-resistant and UV-stable for exterior exposure

subject: Slab Underside Fireproofing
rule: slab underside fireproofing must form a continuous, uninterrupted layer on the slab underside
conditions: when fire-resistance-rated construction is required by building code
exceptions: areas specifically exempted by code (e.g., some parking structures under certain conditions)

subject: Slab Underside Fireproofing
rule: slab underside fireproofing must not be applied over surfaces that are wet, frosty, or contaminated with oil, grease, or release agents
conditions: during application of spray-applied fire-resistive materials (SFRM)

subject: Slab Underside Fireproofing
rule: slab underside fireproofing must have thickness as specified in the fire-resistance-rated design listing
conditions: when the fireproofing is the primary fire-resistive material for the assembly rating
exceptions: thinner alternative tested assemblies that have been listed by a recognized testing agency

subject: Slab Waterproofing
rule: Slab waterproofing must be continuous across the entire slab surface without gaps or breaks
conditions: applies to all concrete slabs in contact with soil or exposed to weather

subject: Slab Waterproofing
rule: Slab waterproofing must be applied to a clean, dry, and smooth substrate
conditions: prior to application of any waterproofing membrane or coating
exceptions: certain self-adhering membranes designed for green/damp concrete may tolerate limited moisture

subject: Slab Waterproofing
rule: Slab waterproofing must be protected from damage during subsequent construction
conditions: where waterproofing is installed prior to backfilling, slab covering, or traffic

subject: Slab Waterproofing
rule: Waterproofing membrane must not be installed at temperatures below the manufacturer's specified minimum application temperature
conditions: for liquid-applied or sheet membranes with temperature-dependent curing or adhesion

subject: Window Frame
rule: window frame must be structurally connected to the surrounding wall opening
conditions: when frame is load-bearing or part of the primary building envelope
exceptions: decorative window frames not integrated into the structure

subject: Window Frame
rule: window frame must accommodate the sash or glazing unit within its rebate
conditions: when the window is intended to contain operable sash or fixed glazing

subject: Window Frame
rule: window frame must not have dimensions that prevent proper sealing against air and water infiltration
conditions: when the frame interfaces with the wall opening and includes weatherstripping or gaskets
exceptions: temporary/construction-only frames not intended for weather barrier

subject: Window Frame
rule: window frame material must be compatible with the fasteners and sealants used in assembly
conditions: when dissimilar metals or chemically incompatible materials contact each other
exceptions: when isolation layers (e.g., barrier coatings, gaskets) separate the materials

subject: Window Sash
rule: window sash must be smaller than the rough opening it fits into
conditions: window is installed in a framed wall opening

subject: Window Sash
rule: window sash must not have a glazing area that exceeds the structural capacity of its framing members
conditions: sash contains glass panes

subject: Window Sash
rule: window sash must be able to open and close fully within its frame without binding
conditions: sash is an operable (not fixed) window type

subject: Window Sash
rule: window sash must maintain a weathertight seal when in the closed position
conditions: sash is designed to be closed against a frame or meeting rail

subject: Window Glazing
rule: window glazing must be made of a translucent or transparent material (e.g., glass, polycarbonate)
conditions: building has windows
exceptions: decorative/solid panels that are not intended for light transmission

subject: Window Glazing
rule: window glazing must be securely fixed within its frame to prevent falling out
exceptions: operable windows that are designed to open/close but remain captive in their tracks

subject: Window Glazing
rule: window glazing must not contain sharp exposed edges where occupants can contact them
conditions: window is within reachable height (below 2 m from floor)
exceptions: edges are protected by a frame, seal, or trim that covers the cut edge

subject: Window Sill
rule: window sill must slope outward away from the window (minimum 5 degrees or 1:12 pitch) to shed water
conditions: sill is exposed to exterior weather
sill has a horizontal or near-horizontal top surface
exceptions: sill is purely interior decorative element with no weather exposure
sill has an active drainage channel or drip system engineered to remove water by other means

subject: Window Sill
rule: window sill must project beyond the wall face (at least 15-20 mm) to form a drip edge that prevents water from running back onto the wall below
conditions: sill is on an exterior wall
sill is exposed to wind-driven rain
exceptions: building has a fully rainscreened façade system where water is managed at the cladding plane

subject: Window Sill
rule: window sill must not be level or slope inward toward the window
conditions: sill is on an exterior wall
sill top surface is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: sill has a fully integrated gutter or drainage system that actively channels water away from the window

subject: Window Sill
rule: window sill must have a minimum thickness sufficient to resist the design wind load without excessive deflection
conditions: sill spans an opening and is not continuously supported along its length
sill is made of a non-ductile material such as stone, concrete, or terracotta
exceptions: sill is fully supported by underlying structure at intervals not exceeding safe span limits
sill is made of material with proven capacity at the given span (e.g., engineered steel lintel acting as combined sill-header)

subject: Window Head
rule: window head must be at least as high as the top of the window frame it crowns
conditions: window head is present above a window opening

subject: Window Head
rule: window head must have a weatherproof seal or flashing at its juncture with the wall above
conditions: window head is exposed to exterior weather
exceptions: window is fully interior (non-exterior wall)

subject: Window Head
rule: window head must not block the operable travel path of the window sash
conditions: the window is operable (awning, casement, double-hung, etc.)
exceptions: fixed (non-operable) window

subject: Window Jamb
rule: window jamb must be dimensionally compatible with the window frame rough opening to allow proper assembly
conditions: for any operable or fixed window installation

when used as perimeter or compression seal

screens for ventilation-only where insect entry is acceptable

window serves as an emergency escape or rescue opening per building code

subject: Casement Window
rule: casement window hardware must allow the sash to seal against the frame when closed

subject: Casement Window
rule: casement window must not rely on vertical sliders or horizontal tracks for its primary opening mechanism

subject: Double-Hung Window

rule: double-hung window must have a weatherstripping seal between the upper and lower sashes and between sashes and frame

rule: double-hung window sash width must be less than frame opening width to permit vertical sliding

subject: Sliding Window

subject: Sliding Window
rule: sliding window must have a latch or locking mechanism to secure the closed position

subject: Sliding Window
rule: sliding window must not have the sliding sash wider than the fixed sash in a two-panel configuration
conditions: two-panel configuration

subject: Sliding Window
rule: sliding window sash must have weatherstripping along the sliding interface

rule: awning window must have operating hardware (crank, push bar, or motorized actuator) accessible from the interior for opening and closing

exceptions: fixed (non-operable) awning window variants

subject: Awning Window
rule: awning window must be hinged at the top of the sash

subject: Awning Window
rule: awning window must not open inward

subject: Awning Window
rule: awning window must have a weatherstripping seal along the header, sill, and jambs to prevent air and water infiltration when closed

subject: Fixed Window
rule: fixed window must have its frame securely anchored to the building structure

subject: Fixed Window
rule: fixed window must be glazed with a material that is rigid and spans the full opening of the frame

subject: Fixed Window
rule: fixed window must not have operable sash or moving parts that create openings in the building envelope

subject: Fixed Window
rule: fixed window must maintain a weather-tight seal between frame and glazing

subject: Bay Window

subject: Bay Window
rule: bay window must have a weatherproof flashings and seal at the junction with the exterior wall

subject: Bay Window
rule: bay window must not project beyond property line or setback limits
exceptions: where local zoning codes expressly permit encroachments for architectural features such as bay windows within specified projection limits

subject: Bay Window
rule: glazed panels of bay window must be tempered or laminated safety glass if within hazardous locations (e.g., below 0.5 m from floor level or near doors)
conditions: the glass is within 0.5 m of the finished floor
the glass is adjacent to a door or walkway

subject: Skylight

exceptions: a snow guard or thermal system is installed to prevent sliding/falling ice

subject: Skylight

conditions: skylight separates conditioned interior space from exterior
interior finish is vapor-impermeable
exceptions: skylight is in an unconditioned space such as a vented attic

subject: Door Frame
rule: door frame must be rigid enough to maintain its shape under normal door operation

subject: Door Frame
rule: door frame must have a clear opening dimension that accommodates the intended door leaf with necessary clearance

subject: Door Frame
rule: door frame must be anchored to the surrounding wall structure in a way that prevents racking or shifting under load

subject: Door Frame
rule: door frame must not have twists or warps that exceed the adjustment range of the hinges and latch

subject: Door Leaf

conditions: door leaf is side-hinged

subject: Door Leaf
rule: door leaf thickness must be compatible with hinge and lock hardware

subject: Door Leaf
rule: door leaf must not exceed maximum weight capacity of its hinges

subject: Door Leaf
rule: door leaf in a fire-rated assembly must have a fire-resistance rating equal to or greater than the wall
conditions: door leaf is part of a fire-rated wall assembly

subject: Door Leaf
rule: door leaf in an egress path must swing in the direction of egress travel

door leaf is in a means of egress
exceptions: residential dwelling units
doors serving fewer than 50 occupants where local code permits inward swing

subject: Door Leaf
rule: door leaf must have a minimum clear width when fully open
conditions: door leaf is in a means of egress or accessible route

subject: Door Hardware
rule: Door hardware must have a means of manual operation accessible from the egress side
conditions: The door is used as an exit or egress component
Building is occupied
exceptions: Electrically locked doors that automatically unlock upon power failure and building fire alarm
Doors serving areas with alternative means of egress

subject: Door Hardware
rule: Door hardware must not allow a door to be locked from the egress side without a readily accessible releasing device
conditions: Door is an exit door serving an occupied space

Controlled egress doors in healthcare facilities where code permits

subject: Door Hardware
rule: Door hardware must be rated for the fire-resistance rating of the door assembly in which it is installed

subject: Door Hardware
rule: Door hardware must not obstruct or reduce the required clear opening width of the door
conditions: Door serves as a means of egress

subject: Door Hardware
rule: Door hardware used on accessible routes must be operable with one hand without tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist

Building is subject to ADA or equivalent accessibility codes
exceptions: Hardware on doors not required to be accessible (e.g., mechanical rooms, service corridors not on accessible route)

subject: Door Threshold
rule: door threshold must be raised above the finished floor level on the exterior side to prevent water ingress

door exposed to weather
exceptions: interior doors only
doors in fully enclosed conditioned vestibules where drainage is otherwise handled

subject: Door Threshold
rule: door threshold must not create a trip hazard exceeding allowable vertical height deviation

door in a path required to comply with accessibility standards
exceptions: single-family residential where local code exempts interior thresholds under a specified height

subject: Door Threshold
rule: door threshold must have a positive sloped surface or be designed to shed water away from the interior
conditions: exterior door
threshold exposed to rain or snow

subject: Door Threshold
rule: door threshold must be securely anchored to prevent movement under foot traffic
conditions: threshold in a high-traffic doorway
exceptions: temporary or non-walkable thresholds (e.g., decorative only)

subject: Door Sill

subject: Door Sill
rule: door sill must not be lower than the finished floor level of the interior space

subject: Door Sill
rule: door sill must provide a continuous weather seal at the bottom of the door assembly when the door is closed
conditions: The door is an exterior door exposed to weather
exceptions: Interior doors where no weather seal is required

subject: Door Glazing

glazing is fully or partially glazed panel in the door

subject: Door Glazing

conditions: glazing is required to be safety glass

subject: Door Glazing
rule: door glazing must not have exposed sharp edges after installation
conditions: glazing is installed in an operable door panel

door is exposed to exterior conditions

subject: Swinging Door

conditions: The door is hung on hinges

subject: Swinging Door
rule: A swinging door must not have the swing arc obstructed by floor-mounted hardware, steps, or changes in floor level

subject: Sliding Door

subject: Sliding Door

conditions: glazed sliding door
installation in a hazardous location such as near a bathtub, shower, or within 24 inches of a walking surface where the glass is less than 60 inches above the floor

subject: Folding Door

subject: Folding Door
rule: folding door panels must not exceed the lateral load capacity of the top track or bottom guide

subject: Folding Door
rule: a folding door must have clear path for panel stacking when fully opened

subject: Revolving Door

subject: Revolving Door
rule: Revolving door wings must not create a direct open passage between exterior and interior

subject: Revolving Door

subject: Revolving Door

conditions: when door serves as part of a required means of egress

subject: Revolving Door

for pedestrian use doors

subject: Automatic Door Operator

for swinging doors with closing force above specified threshold

subject: Automatic Door Operator
rule: automatic door operator must not close with a force exceeding the maximum allowed by applicable safety standard

subject: Door Closer
rule: door closer must be sized correctly for the door leaf weight and width
conditions: any door closer installation

subject: Door Closer
rule: door closer must comply with applicable fire door assembly listing requirements

rule: Door lockset must be compatible with the door thickness and backset dimension for which it is designed

subject: Door Hinge

conditions: when hinge is installed on a door assembly

subject: Door Hinge

subject: Door Hinge

subject: Door Hinge
rule: door hinge must not have sharp edges or protrusions that present a laceration hazard under normal use

subject: Kickplate

door has a bottom gap to finished floor

subject: Kickplate

Interior doors exceeding standard residential dimensions

When using expansion anchors or chemical anchors

subject: Curtain Wall Frame

subject: Curtain Wall Frame

subject: Curtain Wall Frame
rule: curtain wall frame must not allow water infiltration through joints between frame members and glazing

subject: Curtain Wall Frame
rule: curtain wall frame must be positively anchored to the building structure at each floor level

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing Panel

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing Panel

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing Panel
rule: curtain wall glazing panel must have a minimum edge cover / bite dimension as specified by the glazing manufacturer or structural analysis

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing Panel
rule: curtain wall glazing panel must not exceed its allowable interstory drift capacity relative to the building structure

subject: Curtain Wall Spandrel Panel

subject: Curtain Wall Spandrel Panel

subject: Curtain Wall Spandrel Panel

subject: Curtain Wall Gaskets & Glazing Beads

subject: Curtain Wall Thermal Break

subject: Curtain Wall Thermal Break

subject: Curtain Wall Anchors & Brackets
rule: curtain wall anchors and brackets must be capable of supporting the full dead load of the curtain wall panel system

subject: Curtain Wall Anchors & Brackets
rule: curtain wall anchors and brackets must accommodate differential movement between the curtain wall frame and the building structure without losing structural integrity

curtain wall is structurally glazed or stick-built

subject: Curtain Wall Anchors & Brackets
rule: curtain wall anchors and brackets must not create a thermal bridge that causes condensation within the wall assembly

subject: Curtain Wall Anchors & Brackets

subject: Stick-Built Curtain Wall

subject: Stick-Built Curtain Wall

subject: Stick-Built Curtain Wall

subject: Unitized Curtain Wall

subject: Unitized Curtain Wall

subject: Unitized Curtain Wall

subject: Unitized Curtain Wall
