subject: Structural Glazing Curtain Wall

subject: Structural Glazing Curtain Wall
rule: Structural glazing curtain wall must accommodate differential movement between the building structure and the curtain wall system

subject: Structural Glazing Curtain Wall
rule: Structural glazing curtain wall must not allow water penetration through the pressure-equalized cavity or drainage paths to reach the interior

subject: Structural Glazing Curtain Wall

rule: Structural glazing curtain wall must have thermally broken frames if employed in climates where interior-exterior temperature differential causes condensation on interior surfaces

subject: Point-Supported (Spiderman) Curtain Wall
rule: point-supported (spiderman) curtain wall must not have unrestrained glass edge free-span exceeding manufacturer-rated panel span capacity

subject: Cable-Net Curtain Wall

conditions: system is installed and in use
exceptions: system is in a state of controlled deconstruction

subject: Cable-Net Curtain Wall
rule: cable-net curtain wall must not have glass panels that exceed the maximim allowable deflection under design wind load
conditions: under design wind load conditions

subject: Cable-Net Curtain Wall

for all specified design wind load cases

subject: Curtain Wall Gasket

subject: Curtain Wall Gasket

when the sealant is the primary structural attachment of glass to frame
exceptions: when the structural sealant joint is designed with mechanical backup or retention clips

subject: Curtain Wall Structural Silicone Sealant

conditions: when local building codes require fall-safe secondary attachment
when the curtain wall is installed above occupiable space or public areas
exceptions: when a project-specific engineered assessment and authorities having jurisdiction approve a purely structural sealant system

subject: Curtain Wall Structural Silicone Sealant
rule: curtain wall structural silicone sealant must be fully cured before the curtain wall assembly is put under wind or handling load
conditions: during fabrication and installation

subject: Stair Flight

stair flight serves occupied floors

subject: Stair Flight

stair flight is in a public or common area
exceptions: private stairs within a dwelling unit where local code may permit omission

subject: Stair Flight
rule: stair flight must have a minimum headroom clearance (typically 6 feet 8 inches minimum)

subject: Stair Flight
rule: stair flight must not have a riser height that varies by more than 3/8 inch between adjacent risers

subject: Stair Flight
rule: stair flight must have a minimum width (typically 36 inches clear for egress stairs)

subject: Stair Landing
rule: stair landing must have a minimum width and depth that meet building code egress requirements
conditions: landing serves as part of means of egress
landing is at a doorway

subject: Stair Landing
rule: stair landing must not have a vertical change in elevation (tripping hazard) across its walking surface

subject: Stair Landing
rule: stair landing must be structurally capable of supporting the design live load (typically 100 psf for residential, 100-150 psf for commercial egress)

subject: Stair Landing
rule: stair landing surface must provide slip resistance adequate for anticipated wet or dry conditions

landing is in a pool or shower area

wet or outdoor conditions possible

used in means of egress or public access

stairs with supplementary child-proof mesh or barriers that close the opening

subject: Stair Stringer

exceptions: winders or spiral stairs where geometry varies intentionally and is designed per code

subject: Stair Nosing

exceptions: nosingless monolithic tread designs where tread and riser are formed as a single continuous surface

subject: Stair Nosing

subject: Stair Nosing

subject: Handrail

conditions: when installed on stairs
when installed on ramps
when installed on elevated platforms
exceptions: handrails designed for children or accessibility may have shorter gripping segments at different heights

subject: Handrail

conditions: when serving stairs
when serving ramps
in commercial buildings
exceptions: residential applications may follow local code variations (typically 900–1000 mm)
handrails for children may be lower

subject: Handrail
rule: handrail must not have projections or protrusions that could catch clothing or cause injury
conditions: when installed in any egress path or public area

subject: Handrail
rule: handrail must return to the wall, floor, or post or terminate in a smooth rounded end
conditions: when installed at the top or bottom of a stair flight or ramp run
exceptions: handrails continuous around a landing need no termination

subject: Handrail
rule: handrail must withstand a minimum concentrated load of 0.9 kN applied in any direction
conditions: when installed as part of a guardrail system
when serving as a required egress component
exceptions: handrails purely decorative and not serving as fall protection may have lower loading requirements

subject: Newel Post
rule: newel post must be securely fastened to the floor or stair structure
conditions: used as a structural support for handrail
exceptions: decorative newel post not intended to bear load

subject: Newel Post
rule: newel post must have a minimum diameter or cross-section adequate for its load
conditions: serving as a structural support for handrail system

subject: Newel Post
rule: newel post must not have sharp edges or corners at handrail height
conditions: located where people can contact it

exceptions: exception for existing historic installations where code grandfathering applies

subject: Guardrail / Balustrade

conditions: applies where fall protection is required (e.g., open sides of stairs, landings, balconies, roofs)

rule: guardrail or balustrade must not have horizontal elements or climbing aids that facilitate climbing by children
conditions: applies to guardrails in locations accessible to young children (e.g., schools, daycare, residential balconies)

subject: Guardrail / Balustrade
rule: guardrail or balustrade must not reduce the required width of the means of egress below the minimum clear width

subject: Baluster
rule: baluster vertical orientation must be within 5 degrees of plumb

baluster is installed in a railing system

subject: Baluster
rule: baluster spacing must not exceed 4 inches clear distance between adjacent balusters

applicable building code requires 4-inch sphere exclusion

subject: Baluster
rule: baluster must not have sharp edges or projections that could cause laceration or entrapment
conditions: baluster is within graspable reach of users (typically up to 60 inches above walking surface)

subject: Baluster
rule: baluster must be securely fastened at both top and bottom connections to resist design lateral loads

subject: Stair Underlayment

subject: Stair Underlayment

subject: Stair Finish Flooring

subject: Spiral Stair

conditions: used as primary egress
occupant-use stair
exceptions: monumental or decorative stairs not intended for regular use

subject: Spiral Stair

conditions: used as primary egress
occupant-use stair
exceptions: monumental or decorative stairs not intended for regular use

subject: Spiral Stair

subject: Spiral Stair

subject: Spiral Stair

conditions: Stair is supported at ends only
Standard residential or commercial application
exceptions: Stair is cantilevered from a central stringer or spine beam with engineered connection

Occupiable building

Occupiable building

Private stairs within a single dwelling unit

ramp serves as an accessible route

short ramp runs less than 6 inches rise

subject: Switchback Ramp

subject: Folded / Dogleg Ramp

subject: Helical Ramp

subject: Wheelchair Ramp
rule: wheelchair ramp must have a clear width of at least 36 inches (914 mm) between handrails or curbs
conditions: ramp is for public or common use

subject: Wheelchair Ramp
rule: wheelchair ramp must have edge protection on both sides where there is no wall or handrail
conditions: ramp is elevated more than 2 inches above adjacent grade or surface

subject: Wheelchair Ramp
rule: wheelchair ramp landings must have a slope no steeper than 1:48 (2%) in any direction
conditions: landing is at top, bottom, or turn of ramp

subject: Wheelchair Ramp
rule: wheelchair ramp must have handrails on both sides if the rise exceeds 6 inches
conditions: ramp rise is greater than 6 inches
exceptions: ramp serving only a private residence where local code may not require handrails for very short ramps

subject: Ramp Reinforcement / Structure
rule: ramp reinforcement/structure must have sufficient load-bearing capacity for the design loads (dead, live, snow, wind, vehicle, etc.)

subject: Ramp Reinforcement / Structure
rule: ramp reinforcement/structure must maintain a minimum cross-sectional dimension as required by structural codes for the material used

subject: Ramp Reinforcement / Structure
rule: ramp reinforcement/structure must have design detailing that prevents reinforcement corrosion (e.g., minimum concrete cover over steel)

subject: Ramp Reinforcement / Structure
rule: ramp reinforcement/structure must_not have lap splices or anchorages placed in regions of maximum bending moment unless specially designed

subject: Ramp Lighting
rule: ramp lighting must provide minimum illuminance of 10 lux on the ramp surface for safe egress
conditions: when ramp is part of an accessible egress path
when lighting is active/operational
exceptions: emergency backup lighting with separate power source may temporarily replace primary ramp lighting during power failure

subject: Ramp Lighting
rule: ramp lighting must be weather-sealed to at least IP65 rating when installed outdoors
conditions: when ramp lighting is installed in an exterior/unconditioned location
exceptions: ramp lighting installed under full roof cover with walls may be IP44

subject: Ramp Lighting
rule: ramp lighting must not create glare exceeding 45-degree shielding angle at normal eye height
conditions: when ramp lighting fixtures are mounted at 7 ft or lower above the ramp surface

subject: Ramp Lighting
rule: ramp lighting fixtures must be rated for wet location if within 5 ft of grade
conditions: when ramp is at or below grade level
when ramp is located in a region subject to rain/snow

subject: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
rule: ramp foundation / abutment must transfer ramp loads to ground without excessive settlement or rotation
conditions: ramp spans over soil or compressible fill
abutment supports bridge or ramp superstructure

subject: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
rule: ramp foundation / abutment must not be undermined by scour or erosion
conditions: abutment is located in or adjacent to a watercourse
ramp foundation is on erodible soil

subject: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
rule: ramp foundation / abutment must have a minimum bearing capacity factor of safety ≥ 2.0 under static loads

subject: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
rule: ramp foundation / abutment must not experience sliding failure along its base
conditions: abutment is not keyed into rock or not on a steep slope

subject: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
rule: ramp foundation / abutment must be located above the design flood elevation or be designed for flood loading and scour
conditions: abutment is within a floodplain

subject: Accessible Egress System
rule: An accessible egress system must provide at least one means of egress that is accessible to persons with disabilities
conditions: building is required to be accessible
exceptions: buildings exempt from accessibility requirements under applicable code

subject: Accessible Egress System
rule: An accessible egress system must not rely solely on elevators as the only accessible means of egress
conditions: building has floors above or below the level of exit discharge
exceptions: buildings with an area of refuge and standby power per code exceptions for certain high-rise buildings

subject: Accessible Egress System
rule: An accessible egress system must have accessible egress components (exit stairs, ramps, doors, corridors) that comply with accessible route dimensional and clearance requirements

subject: Accessible Egress System
rule: An accessible egress system must include area of refuge or an equivalent alternative where the accessible egress path is not continuous at each floor level
conditions: building has more than one story above or below grade
exceptions: buildings with a sprinkler system throughout may have reduced area of refuge requirements per some code versions

subject: Ramp-to-Stair Combination
rule: When a ramp transitions into a stair, the walking surface must not have a change in level greater than the stair riser height without a landing or transition platform
conditions: ramp directly abuts stair without intermediate landing
exceptions: a compliant landing of at least 60 inches length is provided between ramp and stair

subject: Ramp-to-Stair Combination
rule: The handrail system must maintain continuous graspability across the ramp-to-stair transition without a gap or offset that breaks hand contact
conditions: ramp and stair share a common handrail system
exceptions: handrails terminate at an intermediate landing and a separate handrail begins on the stair

subject: Ramp-to-Stair Combination
rule: The stair nosing must not be placed within the ramp run such that a user's foot or mobility aid encounters the nosing as an unexpected obstruction
conditions: ramp and stair share the same path of travel without a separating landing

subject: Ramp-to-Stair Combination
rule: The slope of the ramp must not exceed 1:12 immediately preceding the stair where the user transitions from ascending/descending the ramp to stepping onto the stair
conditions: ramp leads directly into a stair without an intermediate level landing

subject: Suspended Ceiling
rule: suspended ceiling must be supported by the building structure above via hangers, wires, or brackets
conditions: suspended ceiling is installed

subject: Suspended Ceiling
rule: suspended ceiling must not have direct rigid contact with walls on all sides unless expansion/control joints are provided
conditions: ceiling area exceeds approximately 2500 sq ft per direction
or room dimensions exceed 50 ft in any direction
exceptions: small rooms where thermal movement is negligible

subject: Suspended Ceiling
rule: suspended ceiling must maintain a minimum plenum clearance for access to building services
conditions: above-ceiling contains mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems requiring maintenance
exceptions: ceiling with no services above it

subject: Ceiling Grid / T-Bar System
rule: Ceiling grid / T-bar system must have its structural members (main tees, cross tees) securely attached to the building structure above via hanger wires or channels at the prescribed spacing
conditions: Used as a suspended ceiling system

subject: Ceiling Grid / T-Bar System
rule: Ceiling grid / T-bar system must not be installed without accounting for seismic restraint where required by applicable building code
conditions: Building is located in a seismically active region
Local building code requires seismic design for suspended ceilings

subject: Ceiling Grid / T-Bar System
rule: Ceiling grid / T-bar system must provide proper clearance (typically minimum gap) between the top of ceiling tiles and any overhead building components

subject: Plaster Ceiling
rule: a plaster ceiling must not be installed over wet or green (uncured) timber lath or framing
conditions: when timber lath or framing is used as the substrate

subject: Plaster Ceiling
rule: a plaster ceiling must have a minimum thickness of at least 10 mm (3/8 inch) for single-coat work or 16 mm (5/8 inch) for two-coat work
conditions: when applied over metal or gypsum lath
exceptions: proprietary thin-coat plaster systems specifically engineered for thinner application

subject: Plaster Ceiling
rule: a plaster ceiling must not have unsupported joints or edges exceeding 150 mm (6 inches) beyond the nearest lath or substrate support
conditions: when applied over lath

subject: Gypsum Board Ceiling
rule: Gypsum board ceiling must not be installed in areas exposed to direct water spray or continuous high humidity without moisture-resistant backing or waterproofing
conditions: When installed in wet areas such as showers, pool enclosures, or exterior soffits
exceptions: When the ceiling assembly includes a complete vapor barrier and moisture-resistant gypsum board (e.g., type X or MR board) with properly sealed joints

subject: Gypsum Board Ceiling
rule: Gypsum board ceiling must have all joints taped and finished with joint compound before painting or texturing
conditions: When the ceiling is intended as a finished interior surface
exceptions: When panels are installed as an exposed industrial ceiling where gaps and unfastened edges are part of the design

subject: Gypsum Board Ceiling
rule: Gypsum board ceiling must be fastened to supports at spacing not exceeding the manufacturer's specified maximum
conditions: For all installations

subject: Gypsum Board Ceiling
rule: Gypsum board ceiling must not be installed with direct contact between the board edge and a masonry or concrete wall without a control joint or expansion gap
conditions: When adjacent to masonry or concrete walls

subject: Acoustic Ceiling System
rule: Acoustic ceiling system must be suspended or attached to a structural support above
conditions: When used as a dropped/ suspended ceiling

subject: Acoustic Ceiling System
rule: Acoustic ceiling system must not be installed in locations exposed to continuous direct water spray or saturation
conditions: When ceiling is not specifically rated for wet/damp conditions
exceptions: Cementitious acoustic boards or specialty moisture-rated acoustic panels designed for wet environments

subject: Acoustic Ceiling System
rule: Acoustic ceiling system must have accessibility provisions for above-ceiling services
conditions: When ceiling encloses mechanical, electrical, or plumbing services that require maintenance access

subject: Metal Ceiling Panel
rule: Metal ceiling panel must be installed with adequate acoustic insulation backing to prevent noise transmission and reverberation in occupied spaces below
conditions: when installed in occupiable spaces
when used as finished ceiling surface
exceptions: when specified as acoustic-permeable metal panels designed for sound absorption

subject: Metal Ceiling Panel
rule: Metal ceiling panel must not be installed in exterior or unconditioned environments without specified corrosion-resistant coating and moisture management provisions
conditions: when exposed to outdoor conditions
when in unconditioned spaces with humidity fluctuations
when in coastal or industrial environments
exceptions: when panel is fabricated from inherently corrosion-resistant metal such as stainless steel or anodized aluminum with verified corrosion resistance

subject: Metal Ceiling Panel
rule: Metal ceiling panel grid suspension system must accommodate thermal expansion and contraction
conditions: in spaces with temperature variation exceeding 15°C
when panel span exceeds 1200mm

subject: Coffered Ceiling
rule: coffered ceiling panels must be supported by a structural grid of beams or joists at regular intervals
conditions: applies to any coffered ceiling installation
exceptions: decorative faux coffered ceilings that are non-structural and surface-mounted to an already-supported substrate

subject: Coffered Ceiling
rule: coffered ceiling depth must not exceed the available plenum height minus minimum clearances for MEP systems
conditions: where the plenum contains mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems
exceptions: buildings with no overhead MEP distribution in the plenum

subject: Coffered Ceiling
rule: coffered ceiling must have a fire-resistance rating compliant with the occupancy type and building code
conditions: where the coffered ceiling serves as a fire-resistance-rated floor/ceiling assembly
exceptions: installations where fire rating is provided by other elements and the ceiling is purely decorative and non-rated

subject: Ceiling Soffit
rule: ceiling soffit must maintain a minimum clearance to structural elements above to prevent crushing or load transfer
conditions: where soffit is suspended below structure
in occupiable spaces
exceptions: soffit designed as structural element itself

subject: Ceiling Soffit
rule: ceiling soffit must not enclose hidden cavities without fire-stopping where required by fire code
conditions: soffit forms a concealed space
soffit crosses fire-resistance-rated assemblies or compartments
exceptions: soffit cavity is sprinklered
soffit is part of a rated assembly tested with the cavity

subject: Ceiling Soffit
rule: ceiling soffit must provide a positive attachment to supporting structure capable of resisting gravity and uplift loads
conditions: soffit is overhead
soffit is of non-negligible weight (e.g., gypsum board, metal panel, or tile)

subject: Ceiling Soffit
rule: ceiling soffit must not obstruct required emergency egress path or reduce headroom below code minimum
conditions: soffit is located in a means of egress corridor or path
exceptions: soffit is fire-rated and complies with specific headroom exceptions in applicable code

subject: Tray Ceiling
rule: tray ceiling must have a minimum slope or drainage provision to prevent ponding water
conditions: when tray ceiling is exposed to weather
when tray ceiling is located outdoors
exceptions: when tray ceiling is fully enclosed and weather-protected
when tray ceiling is designed as a strictly interior architectural feature with no exposure to precipitation

subject: Tray Ceiling
rule: tray ceiling must not have a slope that exceeds the maximum allowed by ceiling finish material
conditions: when used as an interior architectural ceiling finish surface
exceptions: when the tray ceiling is structural deck only with no finished ceiling applied

subject: Vaulted Ceiling
rule: vaulted ceiling must be laterally restrained at its base to prevent spreading under gravity loads
conditions: ceiling is constructed as a masonry or stone vault
ceiling is a true arch form (not a decorative false vault)
exceptions: vault is a reinforced concrete shell with integral tie action
vault is suspended from independent structural frame above

subject: Vaulted Ceiling
rule: vaulted ceiling must not have continuous horizontal tension at the springing line without a load path to a thrust-resisting element
conditions: vault is a barrel, groin, or rib vault
exceptions: vault incorporates a modern ring beam or post-tensioned edge member designed to absorb thrust

subject: Cove / Cornice Moulding
rule: Cove / Cornice Moulding must provide a continuous horizontal projection that returns water away from the wall face
conditions: when used as exterior trim at roof-to-wall or eave junction
when installed on a sloped roof edge
exceptions: when used as purely interior decorative moulding with no weather exposure

subject: Cove / Cornice Moulding
rule: Cove / Cornice Moulding must not create a flat upward-facing horizontal surface that traps water
conditions: when installed at exterior eaves or roof edges
exceptions: when a separate drip edge or flashing is provided above the moulding to shed water clear

subject: Ceiling Access Panel
rule: ceiling access panel must be installed in a location that provides clear and unobstructed access
conditions: when the ceiling access panel is intended for maintenance access to building services (e.g., HVAC, plumbing, electrical)
exceptions: when the panel is a fire-rated access door and local codes permit limited clearance due to fire-resistance requirements

subject: Ceiling Access Panel
rule: ceiling access panel must support the same fire-resistance rating as the ceiling assembly in which it is installed
conditions: when the ceiling assembly is fire-rated
exceptions: when the building code explicitly allows unrated penetrations in that specific assembly type

subject: Ceiling Access Panel
rule: ceiling access panel must not be installed directly above electrical panels or equipment that require front clearance per code
conditions: when the access panel is located in the same vertical plane as electrical distribution equipment requiring dedicated working space
exceptions: when the panel is frameless and fully recessed, presenting no projection into the electrical working space

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Light Fixture
rule: ceiling-mounted light fixture must have a structure rated to support its weight

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Light Fixture
rule: ceiling-mounted light fixture must not be installed on a surface that cannot withstand its operating temperature
conditions: fixture uses high-wattage incandescent or halogen lamps

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Light Fixture
rule: ceiling-mounted light fixture's electrical connections must be enclosed in a listed junction box
conditions: fixture is hardwired to building electrical supply
exceptions: fixture is listed and marked for use without a separate junction box (e.g., some integrated LED fixtures with built-in wiring compartment)

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Light Fixture
rule: ceiling-mounted light fixture must not be installed where its clearance from combustible materials is less than the manufacturer's specified minimum
exceptions: fixture is specifically rated for zero-clearance installation against combustibles

subject: Ceiling Diffuser / Grille
rule: ceiling diffuser/grille must be installed with clear path for airflow to/from the duct opening
conditions: when used as part of an HVAC air distribution system
exceptions: decorative or non-operational grilles explicitly designed without airflow function

subject: Ceiling Diffuser / Grille
rule: ceiling diffuser/grille must be mechanically fastened or clipped to the ceiling grid or duct
conditions: when installed in a suspended ceiling system
exceptions: integrated lay-in diffusers that rest securely by weight and grid geometry without fasteners

subject: Ceiling Diffuser / Grille
rule: ceiling diffuser/grille must not be installed such that its face is fully obstructed by ceiling tiles, beams, or other building elements
exceptions: diffusers designed for sidewall or slot discharge where the face is intentionally partially concealed

subject: Ceiling Insulation
rule: ceiling insulation must have a vapor retarder on the warm side of the assembly
conditions: in climate zones with significant heating degree days
where the insulation is permeable to moisture vapor
exceptions: when a dedicated air barrier and ventilation strategy prevents condensation without a vapor retarder
in very hot-humid climates where vapor retarder placement may be on the exterior side

subject: Ceiling Insulation
rule: ceiling insulation must not be compressed or crushed during installation
conditions: when using fibrous or cellular insulation materials such as fiberglass, mineral wool, or cellulose

subject: Ceiling Insulation
rule: ceiling insulation must maintain an air gap or ventilation channel between the insulation and the roof deck when required by the roof type
conditions: when the roof assembly is a cold roof / ventilated roof design
when the roof deck is constructed of materials susceptible to moisture damage
exceptions: in unventilated (hot roof / warm roof) assemblies where the insulation is applied directly above the roof deck

subject: Cable Tray / Conduit (in Ceiling Plenum)
rule: Cable tray / conduit in ceiling plenum must be supported by hangers, trapeze, or other approved supports independent of the ceiling grid or ceiling suspension system
conditions: When installed in a ceiling plenum space used for air handling
exceptions: When specifically designed and approved as part of an integrated ceiling support system with engineered certification

subject: Cable Tray / Conduit (in Ceiling Plenum)
rule: Cable tray / conduit in ceiling plenum must not compromise the fire-resistance rating of the ceiling assembly
conditions: When the ceiling plenum is part of a fire-resistance-rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly
exceptions: When the ceiling assembly is specifically designed to permit penetrations with approved through-penetration firestop systems that maintain the rating

subject: Cable Tray / Conduit (in Ceiling Plenum)
rule: Cable tray / conduit in ceiling plenum must have a metallic or plenum-rated nonmetallic construction suitable for the plenum air-handling environment
conditions: When the ceiling plenum is used as an air return or supply plenum
exceptions: Non-plenum-rated cable or conduit may be used if enclosed in a metallic raceway that itself is plenum-rated

subject: Cable Tray / Conduit (in Ceiling Plenum)
rule: Cable tray / conduit in ceiling plenum must not block access to fire dampers, sprinkler heads, or other fire-protection devices
conditions: When fire dampers, sprinklers, or smoke detectors are present in or above the ceiling plenum
exceptions: When clearance distances per NFPA 13 or the applicable code are maintained around each device

subject: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
rule: fire dampers and smoke dampers installed in ceiling assemblies must be listed and labeled in accordance with fire-resistance ratings
conditions: damper is installed in a fire-resistance-rated ceiling assembly

subject: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
rule: fire dampers must close fully and positively upon activation of the fusible link or release device
conditions: damper is a fire damper

subject: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
rule: smoke dampers must close fully and seal against leakage when activated by a smoke detector signal
conditions: damper is a smoke damper

subject: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
rule: fire dampers and smoke dampers must not be installed where the duct transitions to a flexible duct section that cannot support the damper's weight or maintain its position
conditions: damper is installed in a duct system

subject: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
rule: access doors or panels must be provided for inspection and servicing of fire dampers and smoke dampers installed above ceilings
conditions: damper is installed in a concealed ceiling space
exceptions: where the damper is located directly adjacent to a removable ceiling tile that provides equivalent access

subject: Ceiling Cloud / Baffle
rule: Ceiling cloud / baffle must be independently supported from the structure above, not hung from or resting on ceiling tiles or light fixtures
conditions: when installed as a suspended acoustic treatment
exceptions: when designed as an integral part of a structural ceiling system with engineered load path

subject: Ceiling Cloud / Baffle
rule: Ceiling cloud / baffle must maintain minimum clearance from sprinkler heads to allow unobstructed water spray pattern
conditions: when sprinkler system is present in the same ceiling plane
exceptions: when fire engineering analysis demonstrates alternative coverage is achieved

subject: Ceiling Cloud / Baffle
rule: Ceiling cloud / baffle must not obstruct return air path or HVAC supply diffusers
conditions: when ceiling plenum is used for return air

subject: Ceiling Cloud / Baffle
rule: Ceiling cloud / baffle must not contact or compress thermal insulation above it
conditions: when thermal insulation is present in the ceiling plenum
exceptions: when insulation is type-rated for contact with suspended elements

subject: Metal Linear Ceiling
rule: Metal linear ceiling panels must be clipped or locked into carriers to prevent dislodgement under gravity or lateral loads
conditions: Ceiling installed in horizontal or sloped orientation

subject: Metal Linear Ceiling
rule: Metal linear ceiling must not be installed where exposed to continuous chloride-laden or acidic environments without adequate corrosion-resistant finish
conditions: Environment with persistent high humidity, salt spray (coastal/industrial), or chemical fumes (e.g., pool halls, kitchens, laboratories)
exceptions: Panels with verified corrosion-resistant coating (e.g., PVDF, anodized finish, stainless steel substrate)

subject: Metal Linear Ceiling
rule: Linear metal ceiling panel ends must bear on or be captured by support carriers at each end
conditions: Panel span length exceeds manufacturer's unsupported span rating
exceptions: Manufacturer-tested clip system that supports panels at intermediate points only

subject: Open-Grid / Egg-Crate Ceiling
rule: open-grid / egg-crate ceiling must have a minimum structural connection to the building frame
conditions: when used as a suspended ceiling system

subject: Open-Grid / Egg-Crate Ceiling
rule: open-grid / egg-crate ceiling must not support superimposed loads (e.g., heavy equipment, storage) unless specifically designed as a load-bearing platform
conditions: when used as a decorative or acoustic ceiling
exceptions: when the grid system is structurally engineered and rated for additional loads

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panel
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must be installed with adequate clearance from other ceiling-mounted components (lighting, sprinklers, HVAC diffusers) to prevent thermal interference or obstruction of radiant heat transfer
conditions: When installed in a suspended ceiling grid
exceptions: Integrated multi-functional panels specifically designed to combine radiant heating/cooling with other services

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panel
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must not be installed below non-ducted or vented roof spaces where condensation from the panel surface could drip onto occupants or interior finishes
conditions: When used for cooling (chilled ceiling application)
exceptions: Where a vapor barrier and condensate collection system is integrated into the panel design

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panel
rule: Radiant ceiling panel water/glycol supply temperature must remain above the space dew point when the panel is used for cooling
conditions: When used in cooling mode
exceptions: Panels with integrated humidity control or active condensation management systems

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panel
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must be connected to a hydronic circuit with pressure and temperature ratings compatible with the panel manufacturer's specifications
conditions: When hydronic (water-based) radiant panels are used
exceptions: Electric radiant ceiling panels have no hydronic connection

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger / Wire
rule: a ceiling suspension hanger or wire must be vertically aligned (plumb) to transfer only axial tensile loads
conditions: when installed as a vertical suspension element
exceptions: when specifically designed as an angled bracing wire with engineered connections at both ends

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger / Wire
rule: a ceiling suspension hanger or wire must be positively attached (e.g., wrapped, looped, or clipped) at both ends such that it cannot slip or detach under its design load
conditions: for all suspended ceiling installations

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger / Wire
rule: a ceiling suspension hanger or wire must not be used as the primary lateral bracing element for the ceiling plane unless specifically designed as a splay wire with proper anchorage
conditions: when the hanger/wire is vertical and of small diameter (typical 12-gauge or smaller)
exceptions: splay wires intentionally installed at an angle and designed for lateral restraint

subject: Furring Channel / Hat Channel
rule: furring channel / hat channel must be fastened to structural substrate at regular intervals
conditions: when used as a furring or hat channel for cladding or ceiling attachment
exceptions: when adhesive attachment system is specifically engineered and approved for the application

subject: Furring Channel / Hat Channel
rule: furring channel / hat channel must not bridge building envelope air/vapor barrier without seal
conditions: when installed over an air barrier or vapor retarder membrane
exceptions: when the membrane is self-sealing or when a gasket/sealant is applied at each fastener penetration

subject: Exposed Ceiling (System)
rule: exposed ceiling system must be designed to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction
conditions: when exposed to direct sunlight
when spanning large areas
when installed in climates with significant temperature swings
exceptions: when the ceiling is constructed from materials with negligible thermal expansion coefficients (e.g., certain specialized composites)

subject: Exposed Ceiling (System)
rule: exposed ceiling system must not have materials or finishes that produce hazardous falling debris upon failure
conditions: when installed above occupied spaces
when the ceiling is at a height greater than 2.5 meters
exceptions: when a secondary safety net or catch system is installed below

subject: Exposed Ceiling (System)
rule: exposed ceiling system must be fire-rated to the same standard as the building's required fire-resistance rating for the compartment
conditions: when the exposed ceiling forms part of a fire-rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly
exceptions: when the building code permits exposed structures in sprinklered buildings with specific tradeoffs

subject: Ceiling Plenum
rule: ceiling plenum must not contain occupied workspaces or habitable rooms
conditions: space is used as a return air plenum
exceptions: when explicitly designed as a habitable ceiling space with appropriate fire and life safety provisions

subject: Ceiling Plenum
rule: ceiling plenum must maintain clearance from combustible materials within the air-handling pathway
conditions: plenum is used as a return air plenum
exceptions: materials are listed and approved for plenum use per building code

subject: Ceiling Plenum
rule: ceiling plenum must be accessible for maintenance of building services located within it
conditions: plenum contains mechanical, electrical, or fire-protection equipment

subject: Stud Partition
rule: stud partition must be laterally braced to prevent buckling under axial load
conditions: stud partition is load-bearing
stud partition height exceeds permitted unbraced length
exceptions: partition is non-load-bearing and only subject to self-weight

subject: Stud Partition
rule: stud partition must have a maximum spacing that does not exceed the structural design limits for the cladding applied
conditions: stud partition supports cladding or finish material

subject: Stud Partition
rule: stud partition must not have notching or drilling that reduces the stud cross-section below code-minimum structural capacity
conditions: stud is load-bearing
exceptions: notching/drilling is within allowable zone and size per governing code

subject: Stud Partition
rule: stud partition must be tied to top and bottom track/plate connections

subject: Demountable Partition
rule: demountable partition must be laterally stable when installed
conditions: when spanning floor-to-ceiling or between structural supports

subject: Demountable Partition
rule: demountable partition must not exceed maximum deflection limits under design lateral loads
conditions: when subject to wind or occupant-induced lateral forces

subject: Demountable Partition
rule: demountable partition must have a means of acoustic sealing at all perimeters
conditions: when the partition is specified for acoustic separation between spaces
exceptions: partitions that are purely visual screens with no acoustic requirement

subject: Demountable Partition
rule: demountable partition must be capable of being removed without damaging adjacent building elements
conditions: when classified as a demountable (reusable) system

subject: Glazed Partition
rule: glazed partition must be supported at head and base
conditions: when used as a full-height partition

subject: Glazed Partition
rule: glazed partition must not have point loads applied directly to the glass surface
exceptions: glass specifically laminated and rated for point-fixing

subject: Glazed Partition
rule: glazed partition must be constructed from safety glass (toughened or laminated)

subject: Glazed Partition
rule: glazed partition must have edge protection or be marked to prevent impact collision
conditions: when the partition is at floor level and in a circulation path

subject: Sliding Partition
rule: sliding partition must be supported by an overhead track or bottom guide rail
conditions: partition is top-hung
partition is ceiling-mounted

subject: Sliding Partition
rule: sliding partition must have a clear lateral stacking zone equal to its full width
conditions: partition is designed to fully retract and stack compactly
exceptions: partition is a folding/accordion type that stacks in place
partition is a pocket door type that retracts into a wall cavity

subject: Sliding Partition
rule: sliding partition must not have fixed obstructions (columns, ducts, piping) in its travel path

subject: Acoustic Partition
rule: acoustic partition must have no uncontrolled air gaps along its perimeter
conditions: when used as an acoustically rated assembly
exceptions: if partition is intentionally vented for mechanical systems and acoustic performance is not required at that location

subject: Acoustic Partition
rule: acoustic partition must have a mass per unit area that meets or exceeds the specified minimum for the required sound transmission class
conditions: when a minimum STC rating is specified in the design
exceptions: if a coupled or tuned resonant assembly (e.g., tuned mass-spring-mass) is engineered to achieve the STC target with lower mass

subject: Acoustic Partition
rule: acoustic partition must_not have rigid structural connections (short circuits) between opposite faces that bypass the resilient layer
conditions: when partition uses a resilient channel or staggered-stud / double-stud construction for sound isolation
exceptions: intentional rigid connections at seismic bracing locations if acoustically detailed to isolate the bracing from both faces

subject: Fire-rated Partition
rule: Fire-rated partition must have a fire-resistance rating (FRR) equal to or greater than the rating required by the governing building code for its location and occupancy
conditions: Partition separates fire compartments
Partition is used as a fire wall, fire barrier, or fire partition per code definition
exceptions: Partition is purely decorative and does not serve a fire separation function
Local authority has accepted a performance-based alternative

subject: Fire-rated Partition
rule: Fire-rated partition must be constructed of materials listed in the approved building code for the required fire-resistance rating
conditions: Partition is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Alternative materials approved via engineering judgement or testing per ASTM E119 / UL 263

subject: Fire-rated Partition
rule: Fire-rated partition must not have unprotected penetrations that exceed the size or type allowed by the building code for the required rating
conditions: Partition has service penetrations (pipes, ducts, cables, etc.)
exceptions: Penetrations are protected by an approved firestop system with a corresponding FT rating equal to the partition rating

subject: Fire-rated Partition
rule: Fire-rated partition must extend from the floor slab to the underside of the floor or roof deck above (or to a rated ceiling assembly), forming a complete smoke- and fire-tight seal
conditions: Partition is a fire barrier or fire partition per code
exceptions: Partition terminates at a smoke-tight, rated ceiling assembly that is part of an approved design

subject: Fire-rated Partition
rule: Fire-rated partition must not have doors, windows, or other openings with a fire-protection rating lower than the required partition rating
conditions: Partition contains openings for doors, windows, louvers, or access panels
exceptions: Opening protective assemblies (doors, windows) have been tested and rated per NFPA 252 or ASTM E119 and carry a rating at least equal to the partition rating

subject: Operable Partition
rule: Operable partition must be fully retracted into its storage pocket when not in use
conditions: Operable partition is a folding or sliding type
exceptions: Operable partition is a removable/demountable type

subject: Operable Partition
rule: Operable partition must not obstruct fire egress paths when in any position

subject: Operable Partition
rule: Operable partition must have a clear stacking/retraction zone equal to its full panel width
conditions: Partition is a top-hung or folding type that stacks
exceptions: Partition is a vertical-lift type that stores in a ceiling plenum without lateral stacking

subject: Toilet Cubicle Partition
rule: Toilet cubicle partition must have a minimum height to prevent visibility over the top when occupied
conditions: installed in a public or shared washroom
exceptions: cubicles designated as accessible/ambulatory with reduced height requirements

subject: Toilet Cubicle Partition
rule: Toilet cubicle partition must have a lockable door latch mechanism

subject: Toilet Cubicle Partition
rule: Toilet cubicle partition must not have floor-to-ceiling gaps at the bottom that allow visual intrusion from outside
exceptions: standard clearance gaps (typically 100–150 mm above finished floor) for cleaning and drainage are permitted and not considered a violation

subject: Toilet Cubicle Partition
rule: Toilet cubicle partition must be fabricated from moisture-resistant materials
conditions: installed in a wet or humid environment

subject: Toilet Cubicle Partition
rule: Toilet cubicle partition must be anchored to the floor or wall structure to resist lateral loads

subject: Partition Framing
rule: Partition framing must be laterally braced to resist out-of-plane loads
conditions: when partition height exceeds typical code limits
in seismic design categories D, E, or F
exceptions: freestanding partitions not attached to structure

subject: Partition Framing
rule: Partition framing studs must not have unsupported spans exceeding their maximum allowable unbraced length per structural analysis

subject: Partition Insulation
rule: partition insulation must be installed with a continuous vapor retarder on the warm side of the assembly
conditions: when the partition separates conditioned from unconditioned space
when the partition is located in a climate zone with significant heating or cooling demand
exceptions: in assemblies designed to be vapor-permeable (e.g., certain mass wall or drying assemblies)

subject: Partition Insulation
rule: partition insulation must completely fill the cavity without gaps or compression
conditions: when insulation is installed within framed cavities (stud walls, furring channels)
exceptions: intentionally vented cavities designed for drainage or drying

subject: Partition Insulation
rule: partition insulation must not be installed in direct contact with a moisture source without a drainage plane or waterproof barrier
conditions: when the partition is below grade or adjacent to earth
when the partition is in a wet assembly such as a shower wall
exceptions: insulation materials specifically rated for below-grade or continuous moisture exposure (e.g., closed-cell spray foam, rigid XPS)

subject: Partition Furring
rule: Partition furring must be structurally connected to the supporting substrate (wall, ceiling, or floor) at intervals sufficient to resist lateral and gravity loads
conditions: When used as a substrate for finish materials (e.g., drywall, tile)
exceptions: Freestanding partition furring that is self-supporting and not attached to a substrate

subject: Partition Furring
rule: Partition furring must not bridge a control joint or expansion gap in the supporting substrate without an appropriate break or slip joint
conditions: When installed across a designed movement joint in the wall, floor, or ceiling
exceptions: When the furring system is designed as part of a non-load-bearing, articulated assembly specifically engineered to accommodate movement

subject: Partition Furring
rule: Partition furring components must not be fabricated from materials that are incompatible with the adjacent substrate or finish materials in a way that causes galvanic corrosion or chemical degradation
conditions: When dissimilar metals are used in contact, or when chemically reactive materials (e.g., untreated steel with moisture-reactive substrates) are combined
exceptions: When an effective隔离 layer (separable isolation layer) or coating is provided between incompatible materials

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU)
rule: AHU condensate drain pan must have a functional gravity drain line to a safe disposal point
conditions: AHU includes a cooling coil
condensate will be produced during operation
exceptions: unit is installed in a location where condensate is collected via an active pump system designed for that purpose

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU)
rule: AHU outdoor air intake must not face directly into prevailing wind without a weatherproof hood or louver
conditions: AHU has an outdoor air intake duct opening to the exterior environment

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU)
rule: AHU supply air temperature must not be set below the dew point of ambient air surrounding the unit casing when the casing is uninsulated
conditions: AHU casing is uninsulated
surrounding ambient temperature and humidity can produce condensate on cold surfaces

subject: Partition Base/Skirting
rule: partition base/skirting must be compatible with the floor finish material (e.g., adhesive, mechanical fastening must work with tile, carpet, wood, or VCT)
conditions: when the skirting is installed at the junction between partition and finished floor
exceptions: when the skirting is a monolithic pour or cast-in-place element that bonds directly to the substrate without separate finish

subject: Partition Base/Skirting
rule: partition base/skirting must not create a tripping hazard or sharp exposed edge at the transition to the finished floor
conditions: when the skirting projects more than 5 mm from the finished wall face or has an exposed edge at walking level
exceptions: when the skirting is in an area not intended for pedestrian traffic (e.g., inside a mechanical shaft, above ceilings)

subject: Partition Base/Skirting
rule: partition base/skirting must allow for differential movement between the partition and the floor slab
conditions: when the partition frame and floor slab are of dissimilar materials or when the partition spans a structural joint or expansion joint
exceptions: when the partition is fully isolated from the structure on its own independent foundation (e.g., free-standing acoustic wall not tied to the slab)

subject: Partition Base/Skirting
rule: partition base/skirting must not block required undercut ventilation gaps at the bottom of doors or partitions
conditions: when the partition includes a door with an undercut required for return air flow, or when the partition requires a bottom clearance for HVAC pressure equalization
exceptions: when the space has a dedicated mechanical return air path that does not rely on door undercuts

subject: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
rule: VAV box inlet must be connected to a supply air duct that delivers conditioned air from the air handling unit

subject: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
rule: VAV box must have a functional damper actuator that modulates based on zone thermostat demand

subject: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
rule: VAV box must have a minimum airflow setpoint to prevent stale air or poor ventilation at low damper positions

subject: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
rule: VAV box must not be installed in a location that lacks access for maintenance and filter replacement

subject: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
rule: FCU condensate drain line must have a continuous downward slope (minimum 1/8 inch per foot) to allow gravity drainage
conditions: FCU has a cooling coil
FCU produces condensate
exceptions: FCU is equipped with a condensate pump to actively remove condensate

subject: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
rule: FCU return air filter must be present and installed upstream of the cooling coil
conditions: FCU is connected to an air distribution system
FCU has a cooling coil
exceptions: FCU is a specialized cleanroom unit with HEPA filtration integrated elsewhere in the system

subject: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
rule: FCU chilled water supply temperature must not be below the dew point of the entering air when the FCU is not equipped with adequate condensate management
conditions: FCU uses chilled water as cooling medium
FCU lacks a condensate collection and drainage system

subject: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
rule: FCU fan motor must be electrically grounded
conditions: FCU has an electric fan motor
exceptions: FCU uses an air-powered (induction) terminal unit with no electric motor

subject: Chiller
rule: chiller must be installed on a level, structurally adequate surface that can support its operating weight
conditions: permanent installation
floor-mounted chiller

subject: Chiller
rule: chiller must have unobstructed airflow across its condenser coils
conditions: air-cooled chiller

subject: Chiller
rule: chiller must not be exposed to ambient temperatures outside its rated operating range
conditions: outdoor installation

subject: Chiller
rule: chiller refrigerant circuit must be sealed and leak-free

subject: Chiller
rule: chiller must be connected to a properly sized and functioning chilled water loop with adequate flow
conditions: water-cooled chiller
water-source chiller

subject: Boiler
rule: boiler must have a properly sized pressure relief valve installed
conditions: boiler is a closed-loop hot water or steam system
exceptions: boilers operating at atmospheric pressure with no potential for overpressure

subject: Boiler
rule: boiler must have a low-water cutoff device
conditions: boiler is a steam boiler or a hot water boiler with automatic firing
exceptions: manually fired boilers with constant attendance where operator can visually verify water level

subject: Boiler
rule: boiler must not operate without adequate combustion air supply
conditions: boiler is fuel-fired (gas, oil, or solid fuel)
exceptions: electric boilers which produce no combustion

subject: Boiler
rule: boiler flue gas exhaust must be properly vented to outside atmosphere
conditions: boiler is fuel-fired
exceptions: electric boilers with no combustion products

subject: Boiler
rule: boiler must have a working temperature limit control (high-limit switch)
conditions: boiler is a hot water boiler with automatic firing
exceptions: manually controlled boilers with constant operator attendance

subject: Ductwork
rule: ductwork must be sealed to prevent air leakage at joints and seams
conditions: when ductwork is part of an air distribution system for HVAC
exceptions: ducts used solely for exhaust or ventilation where leakage is intentional or non-critical

subject: Ductwork
rule: ductwork must not be routed through fire-rated assemblies without approved fire dampers where required
conditions: when duct penetrates a fire-resistance-rated wall, floor, or ceiling assembly
exceptions: ducts that are part of a tested through-penetration firestop system listed for the specific assembly type without dampers

subject: Heat Pump
rule: Heat pump outdoor unit must be installed on a level, stable surface capable of supporting its weight
conditions: For split-system air-source heat pumps with an outdoor condensing unit
exceptions: Wall-mounted units that are specifically designed for vertical installation per manufacturer specifications

subject: Heat Pump
rule: Heat pump must have adequate clearance around the outdoor unit for proper airflow
conditions: For air-source heat pumps with an outdoor unit that relies on ambient air for heat exchange

subject: Heat Pump
rule: Heat pump refrigerant circuit must be sealed and leak-free

subject: Heat Pump
rule: Heat pump must not be installed where condensate drainage cannot be directed away from the building and walking surfaces
conditions: For heat pumps that produce condensate during heating or cooling operation
exceptions: Units with built-in condensate management systems that fully evaporate or recirculate condensate per manufacturer design

subject: Diffuser / Grille / Register
rule: Diffuser/grille/register must be securely fastened to the supporting duct, wall, ceiling, or floor structure
exceptions: Temporary or mock-up installations where safety is ensured by other means

subject: Diffuser / Grille / Register
rule: Diffuser/grille/register must have a minimum free area to maintain design airflow at the specified static pressure
conditions: When used as a terminal device on a forced-air HVAC system

subject: Diffuser / Grille / Register
rule: Diffuser/grille/register must not be located where it directly draws in contaminated or recirculated exhaust air
conditions: Outdoor air intake or fresh-air applications

subject: Thermostat / Zone Controller
rule: Thermostat must be mounted on an interior wall, not on an exterior wall
conditions: Wall-mounted installation
exceptions: When manufacturer explicitly states exterior wall is acceptable

subject: Thermostat / Zone Controller
rule: Thermostat must not be installed near heat sources such as radiators, appliances, direct sunlight, or supply registers
conditions: Any installation

subject: Thermostat / Zone Controller
rule: Thermostat must be installed at a height of approximately 1.2–1.5 m (48–60 in) above the floor
conditions: Any installation
exceptions: When required for accessibility by building code (e.g., ADA requirements)

subject: Thermostat / Zone Controller
rule: Thermostat must not be installed behind doors, in corners with poor air circulation, or behind furniture
conditions: Any installation

subject: Pump (Hydronic)
rule: A hydronic pump must be installed with proper suction and discharge piping support to prevent excessive stress on the pump casing
conditions: pump is installed in a closed-loop hydronic system
pump has flanged or threaded connections
exceptions: pump is supported entirely by its own baseplate with independent foundation

subject: Pump (Hydronic)
rule: A hydronic pump must not operate below its minimum continuous flow rate as specified by the manufacturer
conditions: pump is centrifugal type
pump handles water or water-glycol mixtures
exceptions: pump is specifically designed and certified for recirculation service with low-flow bypass

subject: Pump (Hydronic)
rule: A hydronic pump must have net positive suction head available (NPSHa) greater than net positive suction head required (NPSHr) at all operating conditions
conditions: pump takes suction from a closed or open hydronic system

subject: Pump (Hydronic)
rule: A hydronic pump must not exceed its maximum allowable working pressure (MAWP)
conditions: pump is installed in a closed hydronic loop with potential for thermal expansion or pressure surges
exceptions: system is protected by properly sized and maintained pressure relief valves set below pump MAWP

subject: Expansion Tank
rule: expansion tank must be located at the highest point in the hydronic piping system (or at the point of no pressure change when the pump is off)
conditions: system uses a closed-loop hydronic heating or cooling system
tank is a plain steel or bladder-type expansion tank (not a compression tank with air vent)
exceptions: when the expansion tank is used as a compression tank and system includes an air separator at the proper location

subject: Expansion Tank
rule: expansion tank must not be isolated from the system by a check valve
conditions: tank is piped into a closed hydronic system
exceptions: when a check valve is installed as part of a specifically designed fill/air-separation bypass that still maintains thermal expansion access

subject: Expansion Tank
rule: expansion tank must be sized to absorb the net increase in water volume from minimum to maximum operating temperature at the installed system pressure

subject: Expansion Tank
rule: expansion tank must have a properly sized air-charge side (pre-charge pressure) set to match the cold-fill pressure at the tank location
conditions: tank is a bladder or diaphragm type
exceptions: plain steel expansion tanks (non-bladder) rely on an air control system and do not have a pre-charge

subject: Expansion Tank
rule: expansion tank must be installed with a shutoff valve (and a drain valve when bladder type) to allow servicing without draining the system
conditions: tank is a bladder or diaphragm type
exceptions: plain steel compression tanks where the tank is integral to the air control system

subject: Condenser Coil
rule: condenser coil must have unobstructed airflow across its finned surface
conditions: when installed in an HVAC system
when used for heat rejection
exceptions: when coil is submerged in liquid (e.g., water-cooled condenser)

subject: Condenser Coil
rule: condenser coil must not have airflow direction opposite to manufacturer-specified fan flow
conditions: when equipped with a dedicated fan
when installed in a forced-draft or induced-draft configuration

subject: Condenser Coil
rule: condenser coil must be fabricated from materials compatible with the refrigerant and operating pressure
conditions: when in contact with refrigerant

subject: Condenser Coil
rule: condenser coil must maintain continuous refrigerant circuit without leaks

subject: Cooling Tower
rule: Cooling tower water circulation must remain closed-loop or continuously treated to prevent biological growth (e.g., Legionella)
conditions: Cooling tower is of the wet (evaporative) type
exceptions: Dry cooling towers (closed-circuit dry cooling) have no water spray, thus no biological growth risk

subject: Cooling Tower
rule: Cooling tower must be located such that plume discharge does not re-enter building fresh air intakes
conditions: Cooling tower discharges visible water vapor/mist plume
exceptions: Cooling towers located on dedicated remote structures or with engineered plume abatement systems that guarantee no re-entrainment

subject: Cooling Tower
rule: Cooling tower basin must not freeze solid
conditions: Cooling tower is installed in a climate where ambient temperature drops below 0°C (32°F)
exceptions: Cooling towers with engineered winterization (basin heaters, continuous water flow, or complete drain-down system) that prevent ice formation

subject: Cooling Tower
rule: Cooling tower structural support must be rated for total operating weight (dry weight + water volume in basin and piping)
conditions: Cooling tower is roof-mounted or installed on an elevated structure
exceptions: Cooling towers installed at grade on a concrete slab

subject: Cooling Tower
rule: Cooling tower must have unobstructed airflow on all intake sides as specified by manufacturer

subject: Damper (Fire / Smoke / Volume)
rule: A fire/smoke damper must close fully upon actuation without obstruction
conditions: Damper is used in a fire-rated barrier
Damper is fire/smoke rated
exceptions: Dampers specifically listed and tested for leakage-rated smoke control applications where partial closure is permitted under engineered smoke management system

subject: Damper (Fire / Smoke / Volume)
rule: A fire/smoke damper must not be installed where the airflow velocity exceeds the damper's rated velocity
conditions: Damper is installed in an HVAC duct system

subject: Damper (Fire / Smoke / Volume)
rule: A fire/smoke damper must be accessible for periodic inspection and testing after installation
conditions: Damper is installed in a concealed location (above ceiling, within shaft, etc.)
exceptions: Dampers installed in locations where local jurisdiction explicitly waives access requirements via alternative engineered equivalency

subject: Humidifier / Dehumidifier
rule: humidifier/dehumidifier must have a condensate collection or drainage system
conditions: when operating as a dehumidifier
when condensation is produced
exceptions: solid-desiccant dehumidifiers that absorb moisture without condensation

subject: Humidifier / Dehumidifier
rule: humidifier/dehumidifier must not have electrical components directly exposed to the condensation path or water supply
conditions: always applicable
exceptions: components rated and sealed to IPX7 or higher immersion standards

subject: Energy Recovery Wheel (ERV/HRV)
rule: ERV/HRV exhaust and supply air streams must remain fully separated (no cross-contamination)
conditions: wheel is operating
exceptions: purge sector or dedicated exhaust-only configurations designed to handle cross-flow

subject: Energy Recovery Wheel (ERV/HRV)
rule: the wheel matrix must be able to rotate freely without mechanical binding
conditions: wheel is installed

subject: Energy Recovery Wheel (ERV/HRV)
rule: wheel rotational speed must not exceed the manufacturer's maximum rated RPM
conditions: wheel is driven by a motor

subject: Energy Recovery Wheel (ERV/HRV)
rule: condensate from the recovery wheel (or its adjacent section) must not drain into the supply airstream
conditions: wheel is operating below the dew point of the exhaust air
unit has a condensate management system

subject: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
rule: outdoor air intake must be located at least 10 feet (3 m) horizontally from any known source of contamination (e.g., exhaust outlets, plumbing vents, garbage storage, or loading docks)
conditions: ventilation system includes outdoor air intake
exceptions: exception applies when the separation distance is reduced due to building or site constraints and the intake is protected by an approved alternate method (e.g., HEPA filtration, enhanced stack height, or intake relocation above the contamination source)

subject: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
rule: exhaust louver discharge must be directed away from any outdoor air intake or operable opening to prevent re-entrainment of exhaust air
conditions: louver serves as exhaust outlet
exceptions: exception when exhaust air is classified as non-hazardous and dispersion modeling demonstrates safe dilution at the intake location

subject: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
rule: louver must be sized to maintain face velocity below the manufacturer's maximum allowed value (typically 300-500 fpm for intake, 500-800 fpm for exhaust) to prevent water penetration and noise
conditions: louver is exposed to wind-driven rain

subject: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
rule: louver must have a bird screen or mesh with maximum 1/2-inch (13 mm) openings installed on the back face
conditions: louver opens to the exterior
exceptions: exception when louver is specifically designed with integral bird protection that provides equivalent exclusion

subject: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
rule: intake louver must not be located within 10 feet of any building exhaust or vent termination on the same or adjacent structure
conditions: louver functions as outdoor air intake

subject: Refrigerant Piping
rule: refrigerant piping must be insulated to prevent condensation
conditions: piping operates below ambient dew point temperature
exceptions: piping is located in a conditioned space where ambient dew point is always below pipe temperature

subject: Refrigerant Piping
rule: refrigerant piping must not have oil traps that prevent oil return
conditions: system uses compressor oil that must circulate with refrigerant
piping includes vertical risers
exceptions: system has an active oil management system that overcomes trapped oil

subject: Refrigerant Piping
rule: refrigerant piping must be leak-tight

subject: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
rule: Refrigerant piping for a VRF system must be properly sized for the specific combination of indoor units and outdoor units served
conditions: When designing refrigerant piping network

subject: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
rule: VRF system outdoor units must be installed in a location with adequate air circulation and clearance per manufacturer specifications
conditions: For all VRF installations

subject: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
rule: Refrigerant pipe length between outdoor unit and farthest indoor unit must not exceed the manufacturer's maximum allowable piping length

subject: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
rule: The elevation difference between outdoor unit and indoor units must not exceed manufacturer-specified maximum vertical separation

subject: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
rule: A VRF system must have a common refrigerant circuit — all indoor units on the same system must use the same type of refrigerant
conditions: Within a single VRF system branch

subject: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
rule: RTU must be installed on a structurally adequate roof or support frame capable of bearing its weight
conditions: RTU is roof-mounted
exceptions: RTU is ground-mounted

subject: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
rule: RTU must have unobstructed condenser/evaporator airflow intake and exhaust

subject: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
rule: RTU must not be installed where flue gases or nearby exhaust vents can re-enter the outdoor air intake
conditions: RTU uses combustion (gas/electric heat with outdoor-air intake)
exceptions: Intake is ducted from a separate uncontaminated location

subject: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
rule: RTU electrical supply voltage and phase must match its nameplate rating

subject: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
rule: RTU refrigerant lines must be leak-free (closed circuit integrity)
conditions: RTU includes mechanical cooling (DX system)

subject: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
rule: UFAD plenum must be sealed against air leakage to adjacent unconditioned spaces
conditions: plenum serves as return air path
plenum is below raised floor
exceptions: plenum is intentionally connected to outdoor air intake for ventilation

subject: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
rule: UFAD plenum must allow access for cleaning and maintenance
conditions: plenum is constructed as a concealed underfloor space

subject: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
rule: UFAD plenum must not contain materials that off-gas volatile organic compounds (VOCs) into the airstream
conditions: plenum is used as a supply air pathway
exceptions: materials are encapsulated with impermeable VOC barrier rated for HVAC use

subject: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
rule: UFAD plenum floor panels must be removable or have access panels to permit routing and modification of underfloor cabling and ductwork
conditions: plenum contains power, data, or telecom cabling

subject: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
rule: UFAD plenum must have positive drainage to prevent water accumulation
conditions: plenum is below grade or on a concrete slab
plenum may be subject to water intrusion from leaks, condensation, or flooding
exceptions: plenum is strictly above grade with no water intrusion pathways

subject: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
rule: Mechanical/plant room floor must be rated for the static and dynamic loads of mechanical equipment
conditions: Room contains permanently installed mechanical or electrical equipment
exceptions: Rooms with no floor-mounted equipment (wall-mounted only)

subject: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
rule: Mechanical/plant room must have adequate ventilation or mechanical exhaust to prevent accumulation of heat, fumes, or combustible gases
conditions: Room contains combustion equipment (boilers, generators, gas-fired heaters) or equipment that generates heat above ambient
exceptions: Rooms containing only low-voltage electrical panels with no heat/fume sources

subject: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
rule: Mechanical/plant room must have floor drainage or a water-tight curb at openings to prevent water damage from equipment leaks or condensate
conditions: Room contains water-cooled equipment, boilers, chillers, water heaters, or condensate-producing equipment
exceptions: Dry plant rooms containing only electrical switchgear and no water-bearing equipment

subject: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
rule: Mechanical/plant room must have adequate structural fire separation (fire-rated construction) from adjacent occupied spaces and means of egress
conditions: Room contains fuel-burning equipment, high-voltage electrical equipment, or other fire-risk equipment
exceptions: Rooms with no fire-risk equipment (e.g., a room containing only a small air-handling unit with no fuel source)

subject: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
rule: Mechanical/plant room must have equipment access paths and clearances that meet manufacturer and code minimums for service and egress
conditions: Room contains equipment requiring periodic maintenance, inspection, or replacement
exceptions: Rooms with only automated equipment that is never accessed (highly uncommon)

subject: Water Supply System
rule: Water supply system piping must be protected against backflow to prevent contamination of potable water
conditions: system is connected to a potable water source
exceptions: system is entirely separated from potable supply and labeled as non-potable

subject: Water Supply System
rule: Water supply system must maintain minimum positive pressure at all fixtures under design flow conditions
conditions: system is a pressurized (mains-fed or pumped) distribution network
exceptions: system is a gravity-fed non-potable supply with no fixture pressure requirement

subject: Water Supply System
rule: Water supply system piping must not be directly connected to a sewer or waste pipe

subject: Drainage and Vent System
rule: The drainage and vent system must maintain a continuous slope toward the drain outlet
conditions: system is installed on a roof or horizontal surface
exceptions: systems using siphonic drainage where pipe is designed to run full and self-cleans under negative pressure

subject: Drainage and Vent System
rule: The drainage and vent system must have a vent opening that allows air intake to prevent siphonage and trap seal loss
conditions: system includes a sanitary drainage stack or trap
exceptions: systems with air admittance valves (AAVs) that open only under negative pressure are permitted where code allows

subject: Drainage and Vent System
rule: The drainage and vent system must not discharge sewage or drainage directly onto the ground, roof, or into the atmosphere without treatment
exceptions: stormwater drainage directed to permeable ground surfaces where permitted by local code
temporary emergency overflow events

subject: Drainage and Vent System
rule: The drainage and vent system must have cross-connection control to prevent non-potable water from entering the potable water supply
conditions: system is connected to or located adjacent to a potable water supply

subject: Stormwater Drainage System
rule: stormwater drainage system must have continuous hydraulic path from catchment to outfall

subject: Stormwater Drainage System
rule: stormwater drainage system must have a minimum slope to maintain self-cleansing velocity
conditions: piped drainage system
exceptions: systems designed with pressurized flushing or mechanical cleaning

subject: Stormwater Drainage System
rule: stormwater drainage system must not have closed conduit undersized relative to design storm event
exceptions: system designed with intentional surcharge and overflow pathways for larger events

subject: Stormwater Drainage System
rule: stormwater drainage system must not discharge onto adjacent property without legal easement
exceptions: public right-of-way or approved stormwater utility outfall

subject: Water Heaters
rule: water heater must have a temperature and pressure relief (T&P) valve
conditions: for storage-type water heaters
for closed water supply systems
exceptions: tankless/on-demand water heaters that lack storage tanks

subject: Water Heaters
rule: water heater must be installed with a pan and drainage for units in locations where leakage could cause damage
conditions: when water heater is installed above habitable space
when water heater is installed indoors on upper floors
exceptions: units installed in a garage or basement with floor drains directly below
tankless units with negligible leakage risk

subject: Water Heaters
rule: water heater must not be installed in a location where flammable vapors are present
conditions: for gas-fired water heaters with an open flame or pilot light
exceptions: electric water heaters that produce no ignition source

subject: Plumbing Fixtures
rule: plumbing fixtures must have a supply of potable water at adequate pressure
conditions: fixture requires fresh water for operation
exceptions: fixtures that use only recirculated non-potable water (e.g., certain industrial cooling or irrigation connections)

subject: Plumbing Fixtures
rule: plumbing fixtures must be connected to an approved drainage/waste system
conditions: fixture generates liquid waste or wastewater
exceptions: fixtures designed solely for potable water dispensing with no waste output (e.g., a drinking fountain on a closed-loop cooler)

subject: Plumbing Fixtures
rule: plumbing fixtures must not have a direct cross-connection between potable water supply and a non-potable source or waste line
conditions: fixture is connected to a potable water supply
exceptions: installations with an approved air gap or backflow prevention device that complies with code

subject: Plumbing Fixtures
rule: plumbing fixtures must have a trap that maintains a water seal when connected to a sanitary drainage system
conditions: fixture is connected to a building sanitary drainage system and has an integral or required trap
exceptions: fixtures with built-in mechanical or electronic trap seal替代 devices that are code-approved
fixtures that drain directly to an open site drain not connected to building sewer

subject: Pumps
rule: pump suction piping must be sized to prevent cavitation
conditions: when pump is handling liquid
when pump is operating above atmospheric pressure
exceptions: self-priming pumps with internal recirculation loops

subject: Pumps
rule: pump must not operate below minimum continuous flow rate specified by manufacturer
conditions: when pump is of centrifugal type
exceptions: pumps with recirculation bypass lines that maintain minimum flow

subject: Pumps
rule: pump must have a positive net positive suction head available (NPSHa) greater than net positive suction head required (NPSHr)
conditions: when handling liquid
when operating continuously

subject: Piping and Fittings
rule: Piping and fittings must maintain pressure integrity under intended operating conditions without leakage
conditions: system is pressurized

subject: Piping and Fittings
rule: Piping and fittings must be compatible with the fluid being conveyed to prevent chemical degradation or contamination

subject: Piping and Fittings
rule: Piping and fittings must not exceed their rated temperature and pressure limits

subject: Piping and Fittings
rule: Piping and fittings must be adequately supported to prevent excessive stress, sagging, or joint failure

subject: Backflow Prevention Devices
rule: Backflow prevention devices must be installed so that the critical level (C-L) marking is at least the required height above the flood level rim of the downstream fixture or receptor they serve
conditions: Device is a pressure vacuum breaker (PVB)
Device is a reduced pressure zone (RPZ) assembly
Device is a double check valve assembly
Device is an atmospheric vacuum breaker (AVB)
exceptions: Devices approved for below-grade installation with specific listing and local code variance

subject: Backflow Prevention Devices
rule: Backflow prevention devices must not be installed in a location where they can be submerged or flooded
conditions: Device is not specifically rated and listed for submerged operation
