exceptions: Devices listed and approved for submergence under the applicable plumbing code

subject: Backflow Prevention Devices
rule: Backflow prevention devices must be installed with adequate clearance for maintenance and testing access

subject: Backflow Prevention Devices
rule: Backflow prevention devices must be installed in accordance with manufacturer's direction for orientation (e.g., vertical or horizontal position)

subject: Natural Gas Piping System
rule: Natural gas piping system must be leak-tight at all joints and connections
conditions: system is pressurized

subject: Natural Gas Piping System
rule: Natural gas piping system must not be installed in enclosed spaces without ventilation
exceptions: space is continuously monitored by gas detection with automatic shutoff

subject: Natural Gas Piping System
rule: Natural gas piping must not be located where it can be subjected to temperatures exceeding 250°F (121°C)
exceptions: piping material is specifically rated for higher temperatures

subject: Natural Gas Piping System
rule: Natural gas piping must be properly supported with hangers or supports at intervals specified by code
conditions: piping is horizontal

subject: Natural Gas Piping System
rule: Natural gas piping system must have a means of isolating (shutoff valve) at the point of entry to a building
conditions: piping enters a building

subject: Medical Gas System
rule: Medical gas system piping must be continuous with no unions or connections concealed within walls, floors, or ceilings
conditions: piping is installed in enclosed spaces
exceptions: approved access panels or service openings are provided at each connection

subject: Medical Gas System
rule: Medical gas system must not share piping, valves, or outlets with any non-medical gas system

subject: Medical Gas System
rule: Medical gas system must have a dedicated secondary (emergency) power supply that automatically activates upon loss of primary power
conditions: system includes electrically operated alarm systems or source equipment
exceptions: facility has a redundant manual backup protocol approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Medical Gas System
rule: Medical gas system outlets must be non-interchangeable (gas-specific) and color-coded per gas type

subject: Medical Gas System
rule: Medical gas system piping must be cleaned and capped to prevent debris ingress before and during installation
conditions: piping is installed in a construction environment with potential for dust or debris

subject: Compressed Air System
rule: compressed air receiver tank must have a properly rated pressure relief valve
conditions: system includes a compressed air receiver tank
receiver tank is ASME code stamped

subject: Compressed Air System
rule: compressed air piping must not be constructed from PVC or other brittle plastic
conditions: piping is installed downstream of the compressor discharge
system operating pressure exceeds 150 psi or 40°F temperature threshold potential exists
exceptions: PVC schedule 80 used only for low-pressure (below 100 psi) open-vented blow-off lines where personnel cannot be present

subject: Compressed Air System
rule: compressed air system must not discharge oil-contaminated condensate directly into sanitary or storm sewer without appropriate treatment
conditions: lubricated compressor type (oil-flooded rotary screw or reciprocating)
condensate contains free oil or oil emulsion
exceptions: zero-oil (oil-free class 0) compressor where condensate has been verified oil-free per ISO 8573-1

subject: Compressed Air System
rule: compressed air intake must be located in a clean, dry area away from combustion engine exhaust and other contaminants
conditions: compressor intake is located indoors or near a potential contamination source

subject: Fire Standpipe System
rule: fire standpipe system must have a verified water supply capable of meeting required flow and pressure demands
conditions: building is equipped with a fire standpipe system
exceptions: none

subject: Fire Standpipe System
rule: fire standpipe system must not have any obstruction, closed valve, or blockage between the water supply and the hose connections
conditions: building is equipped with a fire standpipe system
exceptions: valves that are normally locked open and supervised in the open position are permitted

subject: Fire Standpipe System
rule: fire standpipe system must be designed so that the maximum static pressure at any hose connection does not exceed 175 psi (12.1 bar) unless pressure-reducing devices are installed
conditions: building is equipped with a fire standpipe system
system is classified as Class I or Class III standpipe
exceptions: pressure-reducing valves or other approved pressure control devices are provided at each outlet to limit flowing pressure to 100 psi

subject: Fire Standpipe System
rule: fire standpipe system must not have a dead-end supply pipe exceeding the length permitted by code for the pipe diameter and system classification
conditions: building is equipped with a fire standpipe system
exceptions: dead-end lengths permitted by applicable code (e.g., NFPA 14) for the specific pipe size are allowed

subject: Conduit & Raceway System
rule: Conduit & raceway system must maintain minimum bending radius for all conductors
conditions: Metallic conduit is used
Non-metallic conduit is used
Any cable type is installed within the raceway
exceptions: Flexible conduits specifically rated for tighter bends as per manufacturer specification
Factory-fabricated bends that are UL-listed

subject: Conduit & Raceway System
rule: Conduit & raceway system must not exceed maximum fill percentage per the National Electrical Code
conditions: More than one conductor is present in the raceway

subject: Conduit & Raceway System
rule: Conduit & raceway system must be electrically continuous and properly bonded to ground
conditions: Metallic conduit or raceway is used
exceptions: Non-metallic raceways (e.g., PVC) which do not serve as equipment grounding conductor

subject: Conduit & Raceway System
rule: Conduit & raceway system must not be installed where ambient temperature exceeds the rated temperature of the raceway or its conductors
conditions: Raceway is located in a high-temperature environment (e.g., boiler room, rooftop in direct sun, near steam pipes)
exceptions: Raceway and conductors specifically derated and listed for the elevated temperature

subject: Conduit & Raceway System
rule: Conduit & raceway system must be supported at maximum intervals specified by code
conditions: Raceway is installed exposed (not embedded in concrete)
exceptions: Raceway specifically listed for alternative support spacing per manufacturer engineering evaluation

subject: Cable Tray & Ladder System
rule: cable tray and ladder system must be supported at intervals that prevent excessive sagging and maintain cable bend radius
conditions: when supporting cables with minimum bend radius requirements
when installed in horizontal orientation
exceptions: when manufacturer specifies alternative support spacing for specific load ratings

subject: Cable Tray & Ladder System
rule: cable tray and ladder system must not be used as a walkway or climbing surface
conditions: during installation
during operation
during maintenance
exceptions: when specifically designed and rated for foot traffic per manufacturer certification

subject: Cable Tray & Ladder System
rule: cable tray and ladder system must be electrically bonded and grounded
conditions: when metallic construction is used
when part of an electrical power or control cable installation
exceptions: when tray is electrically isolated by design (e.g., non-conductive material, isolated segment for cathodic protection)

subject: Cable Tray & Ladder System
rule: cable tray and ladder system must maintain minimum separation from heat sources
conditions: when installed near steam lines, flues, or other high-temperature equipment
exceptions: when a thermal barrier or heat shield with certified performance rating is installed

subject: Main Switchboard
rule: Main Switchboard must be located in a dedicated electrical room or enclosure with controlled access
conditions: building contains electrical distribution equipment
switchboard rated above 600V or 800A
exceptions: single-family residential dwellings where local code allows exposed location

subject: Main Switchboard
rule: Main Switchboard must have minimum working clearance of 36 inches (914 mm) in front of the equipment
conditions: switchboard is floor-mounted
voltage 0-150V to ground

subject: Main Switchboard
rule: Main Switchboard must not be installed in a location subject to water intrusion or condensation
conditions: any building
exceptions: switchboard is specifically rated NEMA 4X or IP66 for wet locations

subject: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
rule: Distribution board must have a dead-front construction (no live parts accessible without tools)
conditions: permanent installation
building electrical system

subject: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
rule: Distribution board must have an appropriate short-circuit current rating (SCCR) equal to or greater than the prospective short-circuit current at its point of installation
conditions: connected to mains power supply

subject: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
rule: Distribution board must not be installed in a location where ambient temperature exceeds its rated maximum operating temperature
conditions: indoor or enclosed installation

subject: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
rule: Distribution board enclosure must have a minimum ingress protection (IP) rating appropriate for its installation environment
conditions: outdoor installation
or installation in damp/wet locations
or installation in dusty environments

subject: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
rule: Distribution board must have a properly sized and bonded equipment grounding conductor connected to its enclosure
conditions: part of a grounded electrical system

subject: Sub-Distribution Board
rule: Sub-distribution board must be installed with a minimum IP rating appropriate for its installed environment
conditions: board is located outdoors
board is located in a wet/damp area
board is located in a dusty environment
exceptions: board is located in a clean, dry, climate-controlled indoor environment

subject: Sub-Distribution Board
rule: Sub-distribution board must not be installed where it is accessible to unauthorized personnel without a lockable door or barrier
conditions: board is in a public area
board is in a common corridor accessible to non-electrical staff
exceptions: board is within a secured electrical room
board is in a private dwelling unit

subject: Sub-Distribution Board
rule: Sub-distribution board must have its neutral bus bar and protective earth bus bar bonded only at the point of origin (first point of disconnection)
conditions: board is a sub-board downstream of the main distribution board
system uses TN-S or TN-C-S earthing arrangement

subject: Circuit Breaker & Fuse Assembly
rule: circuit breaker must interrupt current flow when an overcurrent condition is detected
conditions: under rated load conditions
within specified voltage range
exceptions: when specifically designed for non-interrupting fused disconnect applications

subject: Circuit Breaker & Fuse Assembly
rule: fuse element must not remain continuous after clearing a fault
conditions: when subjected to current exceeding its rated interrupting capacity

subject: Circuit Breaker & Fuse Assembly
rule: circuit breaker and fuse assembly must have accessible line and load terminals with adequate clearance for arc flash mitigation
conditions: when installed in a panelboard or enclosed assembly
exceptions: when designed as a sealed, non-serviceable unit with permanent encapsulation

subject: Circuit Breaker & Fuse Assembly
rule: enclosure of a circuit breaker or fuse assembly must not exceed rated temperature rise under continuous load
conditions: at rated continuous current
in ambient temperature not exceeding 40°C per standard
exceptions: when derated per manufacturer instructions for elevated ambient conditions

subject: Metering & Monitoring Equipment
rule: Metering and monitoring equipment must be installed in locations that are accessible for reading, maintenance, and calibration
conditions: equipment is installed for ongoing use
exceptions: equipment installed in hazardous environments where access would pose a safety risk

subject: Metering & Monitoring Equipment
rule: Metering and monitoring equipment must not be installed in locations subject to flooding, standing water, or direct water spray unless rated for that environment
conditions: equipment is not specifically rated for wet or submerged conditions

subject: Metering & Monitoring Equipment
rule: Metering and monitoring equipment must have electrical supply that matches its rated voltage and current requirements
conditions: equipment requires external electrical power to operate
exceptions: self-powered or energy-harvesting metering devices

subject: Earthing & Grounding System
rule: Earthing & Grounding System must provide a continuous metallic path to earth with sufficiently low impedance
conditions: system is present in the building

subject: Earthing & Grounding System
rule: Earthing & Grounding System must have all metallic parts of the electrical installation bonded to the earth electrode
conditions: system is present in the building
exceptions: separately derived systems where isolation is intentionally maintained per code

subject: Earthing & Grounding System
rule: Earthing & Grounding System must not have any intentional interruption or switch in the grounding electrode conductor
conditions: system is present in the building
exceptions: where permitted by code for testing purposes using listed disconnectable fittings

subject: Switch & Socket Outlet
rule: switch and socket outlet must be rated for the electrical load (current and voltage) of the connected circuit

subject: Switch & Socket Outlet
rule: switch and socket outlet must be installed with proper insulation and ingress protection (IP rating) appropriate for the installation environment
conditions: installation location is outdoors, wet, or dusty

subject: Switch & Socket Outlet
rule: switch and socket outlet must be securely fixed to a mounting surface or enclosure

subject: Lightning Protection System
rule: lightning protection system must have a continuous low-impedance path to ground
conditions: system is installed
exceptions: non-conventional charge dissipation systems that intentionally avoid low-impedance grounding

subject: Lightning Protection System
rule: lightning protection system must not be installed on structures containing explosives or flammable materials unless specifically designed for hazardous locations
conditions: structure contains explosive or highly flammable materials
exceptions: system is designed and certified per explosive-atmosphere standards (e.g., IEC 60079, NFPA 780 hazardous location requirements)

subject: Lightning Protection System
rule: lightning protection system conductors must be mechanically connected (not solely taped or wire-nutted)
conditions: conductors are joined
exceptions: temporary test connections

subject: Lightning Protection System
rule: lightning protection system must not share bonding conductors with electrical power grounding conductors in a manner that creates a hazardous parallel path
conditions: system is bonded to the building grounding electrode system
exceptions: intentional equipotential bonding via a single bonding point at the service entrance as permitted by code

subject: Hypothetical: Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting system must have a dedicated backup power source (battery, generator, or central UPS) that activates within 10 seconds of normal power failure
conditions: system is required to provide illumination during power loss
exceptions: systems serving only exit signs that are self-illuminating via photoluminescent materials

subject: Hypothetical: Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting luminaires must not be connected to the same branch circuit as general lighting in the same area
conditions: emergency luminaires are wired from a normal panelboard
exceptions: when the emergency lighting derives from the same circuit via an integral transfer device listed for the purpose

subject: Hypothetical: Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting system must maintain minimum egress illumination level (typically 1 fc along egress path, 0.1 fc in open areas) for at least 90 minutes after loss of normal power
conditions: system is installed in a building required to comply with adopted life-safety codes

subject: Hypothetical: Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting fixtures must be listed or labeled for emergency use per applicable product safety standard
conditions: fixtures are permanently installed and connected to emergency power

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system must be connected to an electrical grounding system
conditions: installed in any building or facility

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system must not be installed in a location exposed to water intrusion, flooding, or dripping liquids
conditions: installed indoors or in an enclosure
exceptions: equipment is specifically rated and certified for wet locations (e.g., NEMA 4X or IP66+ enclosure)

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system must have adequate ventilation or cooling to remove heat generated during normal operation and battery charging
conditions: installed in an enclosed space or equipment room
exceptions: equipment is specifically designed for passive/convection cooling and ambient temperature is within manufacturer limits

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system batteries must not be installed in a sealed airtight enclosure without hydrogen gas venting or explosion-proof rating
conditions: battery type is valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA) or flooded lead-acid
exceptions: battery type is lithium-ion with no hydrogen off-gassing and enclosure is certified for that chemistry

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system must be electrically rated to handle the connected load without exceeding its nameplate capacity
conditions: actively supplying power to downstream equipment

subject: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
rule: UPS system input and output electrical connections must be installed with conductors sized according to the applicable electrical code for the system's rated current and overcurrent protection
conditions: hardwired installation (not plug-in)

subject: Hypothetical: Standby Generator System
rule: Standby generator system must have adequate ventilation for combustion and cooling air
conditions: system uses internal combustion engine
exceptions: generator located outdoors with unobstructed natural airflow

subject: Hypothetical: Standby Generator System
rule: Standby generator system must not be installed in a location subject to flooding below the engine air intake elevation
conditions: generator installed at grade level or below grade

subject: Hypothetical: Standby Generator System
rule: Standby generator system must have an automatic transfer switch that isolates from utility supply when generator is running
conditions: generator provides backup power to building loads

subject: HVAC Power Connection
rule: HVAC power connection must be electrically rated to handle the full locked-rotor amperage (LRA) and continuous load current of the connected HVAC unit
conditions: When connecting to any HVAC unit

subject: HVAC Power Connection
rule: HVAC power connection must have a disconnecting means (disconnect switch or breaker) within sight of the HVAC unit and readily accessible
conditions: Per electrical code requirements for fixed HVAC equipment

subject: HVAC Power Connection
rule: HVAC power connection must not be energized before the HVAC unit is properly installed, grounded, and bonded
conditions: During installation and commissioning

subject: Power Busway & Bus Duct
rule: Busway and bus duct must be supported at intervals not exceeding manufacturer specifications
conditions: installed in horizontal orientation
installed in vertical orientation
exceptions: when designed with continuous support per engineering analysis

subject: Power Busway & Bus Duct
rule: Busway and bus duct must not be installed in direct contact with combustible materials
conditions: installed indoors
installed in plenum spaces
exceptions: when listed for direct contact with combustible materials per UL/CSA listing

subject: Power Busway & Bus Duct
rule: Busway and bus duct must be installed with expansion joints or flexible sections where the straight run length exceeds manufacturer thermal expansion limits
conditions: straight run length exceeds manufacturer limit
environmental temperature variation exceeds 50°F range
exceptions: when engineered to accommodate thermal expansion via sliding joints or offsets documented in submittal

subject: Power Busway & Bus Duct
rule: Power busway and bus duct must be installed with conductor phase sequence matching the connected source and load equipment
conditions: three-phase system

subject: Transformers (Step-down)
rule: step-down transformer must be located on a fire-resistant (non-combustible) surface
conditions: transformer contains mineral oil or other combustible insulating fluid
exceptions: dry-type transformers with no combustible fluids

subject: Transformers (Step-down)
rule: step-down transformer must not be installed in a location where standing water can accumulate around the enclosure
conditions: transformer is pad-mounted or ground-level installed
exceptions: transformer is specifically rated for submersion or wet location (e.g., submersible type)

subject: Transformers (Step-down)
rule: step-down transformer must have its enclosure (tank or casing) bonded to the grounding electrode system
exceptions: transformer is double-insulated and listed as not requiring grounding

subject: Transformers (Step-down)
rule: step-down transformer must not be operated with its primary overcurrent protection device omitted or bypassed
exceptions: none — overcurrent protection is always required per code

subject: Electrical Room / Closet
rule: Electrical room/closet must have a door that swings outward (or is rated for the space) and provides at least the minimum working clearance required by electrical code in front of all electrical panels and equipment
conditions: room contains electrical panel(s) or switchgear requiring access
exceptions: door swing may be restricted if a corridor or egress path cannot accommodate outward swing, provided an alternative code-compliant arrangement is approved

subject: Electrical Room / Closet
rule: Electrical room/closet must not contain any water or steam piping, drain lines, or other plumbing not directly serving the electrical equipment
conditions: space is dedicated to electrical distribution equipment
exceptions: fire sprinkler piping is permitted if it meets clearance and drip-protection requirements

subject: Electrical Room / Closet
rule: Electrical room/closet must have a fire-resistance rating and rated enclosure consistent with its location and the building type
conditions: room serves as an electrical equipment room that is not an exterior standalone structure
exceptions: small electrical closets in fully sprinklered buildings may have reduced ratings per local code

subject: Cable Management Accessories
rule: cable management accessories must be rated for the maximum voltage of any cable they support or contact
conditions: the accessory is used in an electrical installation where voltage ratings apply
exceptions: accessories that are electrically insulating and verified by testing to withstand higher voltages without tracking or breakdown

subject: Cable Management Accessories
rule: cable management accessories must not have sharp edges or burrs that can damage cable insulation
conditions: the accessory contacts or supports cables where insulation integrity is required

subject: Cable Management Accessories
rule: cable management accessories must be made of materials compatible with the environment to prevent corrosion-induced failure
conditions: the accessory is installed in a corrosive environment (e.g., outdoor, marine, chemical plant, or high-humidity area)
exceptions: accessories that are protected by an effective barrier coating or cathodic protection system verified for the specific environment

subject: Cable Management Accessories
rule: cable management accessories must support the combined weight of all cables they carry without mechanical failure
conditions: the accessory is used to support cables in a vertical or horizontal run

subject: Sprinkler Head
rule: sprinkler head must be positioned below the ceiling or roof deck to allow heat from a fire to reach the fusible element or heat sensor
conditions: when installed in an automatic fire sprinkler system
exceptions: sidewall sprinklers may be mounted on walls with deflectors oriented horizontally or downward

subject: Sprinkler Head
rule: sprinkler head must not be obstructed by building elements, stored materials, or finishes within its coverage area
conditions: in all occupied spaces
exceptions: sprinklers with extended coverage or specially listed obstructions allowances per NFPA 13

subject: Sprinkler Head
rule: sprinkler head must have a clearance distance to high-rack storage, ceiling fans, light fixtures, and ductwork as specified by product listing and NFPA 13
conditions: where installed in spaces with ceilings, ductwork, or storage racks
exceptions: sprinklers specifically listed for installation within shelving or with reduced clearance

subject: Sprinkler Head
rule: sprinkler head must not be painted (field-applied paint, coatings, or finishes) unless specifically factory-applied and listed for that finish
conditions: during construction or renovation

subject: Fire Suppression Piping Network
rule: fire suppression piping network must maintain adequate pressure and flow rate to deliver water to all sprinkler heads simultaneously during a fire event
conditions: system is designed for automatic fire suppression

subject: Fire Suppression Piping Network
rule: fire suppression piping network must not have any section isolated by closed valves that would prevent water flow to any required sprinkler during a fire scenario
conditions: system is in service and fire suppression is required
exceptions: sections intentionally taken out of service for maintenance with compensatory fire protection measures in place

subject: Fire Suppression Piping Network
rule: fire suppression piping network must be hydraulically designed such that the most remote sprinkler receives minimum required flow and pressure as specified by applicable fire code
conditions: system is designed to NFPA 13 or equivalent standard

subject: Fire Suppression Piping Network
rule: fire suppression piping network must not be constructed from materials that are not listed or approved for fire sprinkler service

subject: Fire Suppression Piping Network
rule: fire suppression piping network must have a reliable water supply connection that cannot be inadvertently shut off during a fire

subject: Fire Suppression Agent Storage Tank
rule: Fire suppression agent storage tank must maintain a leak-tight containment envelope to prevent agent escape
conditions: When storing any fire suppression agent (gas, liquid, or chemical)

subject: Fire Suppression Agent Storage Tank
rule: Fire suppression agent storage tank must withstand its maximum allowable working pressure without rupture
conditions: For pressurized storage tanks (e.g., nitrogen-pressurized or stored-pressure systems)
exceptions: Atmospheric-pressure tanks storing non-pressurized agents are exempt from this pressure-holding requirement

subject: Fire Suppression Agent Storage Tank
rule: Fire suppression agent storage tank must not be located where ambient temperature exceeds the agent's rated storage temperature range
conditions: When the agent has a defined safe storage temperature range specified by manufacturer or code

subject: Fire Suppression Agent Storage Tank
rule: Fire suppression agent storage tank must be supported such that mechanical loads do not cause structural failure of the tank shell, nozzles, or piping connections

subject: Dry Pipe Valve
rule: Dry pipe valve must be installed only in environments where the ambient temperature remains above 4°C (40°F) at all times
conditions: Valve is located in an unconditioned space
Valve is exposed to outdoor temperatures
exceptions: Valve and associated piping are protected by a listed enclosure with auxiliary heat tracing that maintains minimum temperature

subject: Dry Pipe Valve
rule: Dry pipe valve must not be subjected to water column pressure exceeding its rated working pressure
conditions: System is connected to a municipal or pumped water supply with variable pressure
exceptions: A pressure-reducing valve is installed upstream and set to the rated pressure

subject: Dry Pipe Valve
rule: Dry pipe valve must be provided with a local indicating alarm that activates when the valve trips (water enters the piping)
conditions: Valve is part of a fire sprinkler system serving an occupied building
exceptions: System is monitored by a continuously attended fire alarm control panel that provides equivalent remote indication

subject: Fire Suppression Zone Valve
rule: Fire suppression zone valve must be installed in an accessible location for manual operation and maintenance

subject: Fire Suppression Zone Valve
rule: Fire suppression zone valve must be listed/labeled for its intended fire protection service

subject: Fire Suppression Zone Valve
rule: Fire suppression zone valve must not be installed in a location where it could be obstructed or rendered inaccessible by stored materials or building finishes

subject: Tamper Switch
rule: tamper switch must detect cover removal or enclosure opening
conditions: when used in security or access-controlled applications
when required by applicable safety or security standards
exceptions: tamper switches installed in fully supervised circuits where any disconnection is immediately detected through continuity monitoring

subject: Tamper Switch
rule: tamper switch must not have exposed energized terminals when the enclosure is open
conditions: when the switch is part of a mains-voltage or hazardous-energy circuit
exceptions: when the switch is a low-voltage, SELV-rated device and is inherently touch-safe

subject: Tamper Switch
rule: tamper switch must remain functional throughout its rated environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, vibration)
conditions: when deployed in outdoor or uncontrolled indoor environments

subject: Water Mist Suppression System
rule: water mist suppression system must be supplied with potable or treated water free of suspended solids and debris
conditions: system is a closed-loop or open-nozzle water mist system
exceptions: seawater systems specifically designed for marine applications with appropriate filtration

subject: Water Mist Suppression System
rule: water mist suppression system must_not be installed in areas where the ambient temperature can drop below the freezing point of the water supply without adequate freeze protection
conditions: system uses water as the extinguishing agent
system is located in an unconditioned space or climate with freezing risk
exceptions: systems using an anti-freeze premix solution listed for the application
systems with trace heating and insulation designed for the ambient conditions

subject: Water Mist Suppression System
rule: water mist suppression system must be designed with filtration rated to at least the minimum mesh size specified by the nozzle manufacturer
conditions: system uses nozzles with orifice diameters less than 2 mm

subject: Water Mist Suppression System
rule: water mist suppression system storage tanks (if using stored-pressure or stored-water configurations) must be protected against over-pressurization
conditions: system includes stored-pressure water mist cylinders or pressurized water tanks

subject: Foam Suppression System
rule: foam suppression system must have a dedicated water supply or foam concentrate reservoir sized to deliver the required discharge density for the full design duration
conditions: system is wet-pipe or pre-action type
system is designed for fire suppression

subject: Foam Suppression System
rule: foam suppression system piping must not be shared with domestic or other non-fire-protection water systems

subject: Foam Suppression System
rule: foam concentrate must be stored within its specified temperature range (typically 40°F–100°F / 4°C–38°C depending on concentrate type)
exceptions: tank is rated for extreme temperatures with manufacturer approval

subject: Foam Suppression System
rule: foam suppression system discharge must not be directed at energized electrical equipment unless the foam is specifically listed for Class C hazards
conditions: system is in an area containing energized electrical equipment
exceptions: foam concentrate is tested and listed for use on energized electrical equipment per NFPA 11 or equivalent

subject: Foam Suppression System
rule: foam suppression system must have a proportioning device that maintains the correct concentration ratio (e.g., 1%, 3%, 6%) within ±30% of nominal over the full flow range

subject: Standpipe System
rule: standpipe system must be connected to a reliable water supply capable of maintaining required pressure and flow during design duration
conditions: system is required by code for the building occupancy/height
exceptions: alternative automatic fire suppression system with equivalent coverage is approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Standpipe System
rule: standpipe system must not have any isolation valves in the normally closed position that would block water flow to any required hose connection
conditions: system is installed and operational
exceptions: valves are locked open with tamper switches monitored by fire alarm system and closed only for maintenance with pre-planned temporary measures

subject: Standpipe System
rule: standpipe system piping must be sized such that the system can deliver the required flow at the most hydraulically remote hose connection while maintaining minimum residual pressure
conditions: system serves more than one floor or is a Class I or III standpipe

subject: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
rule: Kitchen hood suppression system must have a verified agent supply (e.g., wet chemical, CO2, or clean agent) for its designed fire class
conditions: system is installed and intended to be operational
exceptions: pre-engineered systems that rely on a stored agent that has not been verified at time of inspection but is documented

subject: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
rule: Kitchen hood suppression system must not have obstructed or blocked nozzle discharge paths
conditions: system is installed
exceptions: temporary obstructions that are removed prior to system activation per design clearance

subject: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
rule: Kitchen hood suppression system must have a mechanical or electrical means of automatically shutting off fuel/gas to the cooking appliances upon activation
conditions: system is installed over gas-fired cooking equipment

subject: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
rule: Kitchen hood suppression system must not be installed without a compatible listed exhaust hood and duct arrangement
conditions: system is part of a commercial kitchen ventilation assembly
exceptions: systems that are independently listed as a stand-alone unit with integral hood

subject: Fire Hydrant Connection
rule: fire hydrant connection must have unobstructed access from a fire apparatus access road
conditions: building is equipped with a fire hydrant connection
exceptions: alternative fire suppression water supply systems are approved by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Fire Hydrant Connection
rule: fire hydrant connection must be located within the required distance of the building or fire department connection
conditions: building has a fire sprinkler or standpipe system requiring a fire department connection
exceptions: alternate supply arrangements are approved by the fire code official

subject: Fire Hydrant Connection
rule: fire hydrant connection must not be obstructed by fences, landscaping, vehicles, or stored materials
conditions: fire hydrant connection is installed on the property
exceptions: temporary obstructions during emergency operations by fire personnel

subject: Fire Hydrant Connection
rule: fire hydrant connection must have sufficient flow and pressure to meet the fire flow demand of the building
conditions: building requires a fire hydrant for fire protection
exceptions: alternative approved water supply systems provide equivalent protection

subject: Fire Hydrant Connection
rule: fire hydrant connection must have a visible identification marker (sign, flag, or reflector) when located in areas subject to snow accumulation or poor visibility
conditions: hydrant is located in a region with seasonal snow or potential visibility obstruction
exceptions: hydrant is immediately visible from the fire apparatus access road at all times without markers

subject: Fire Pump
rule: Fire pump must be connected to a reliable water supply

subject: Fire Pump
rule: Fire pump must be located in a room or space with adequate ventilation and drainage

subject: Fire Pump
rule: Fire pump must have a controller that is listed and compatible with the pump driver

subject: Fire Pump
rule: Fire pump must not be installed in a location subject to freezing temperatures unless the pump, piping, and water supply are protected from freezing
conditions: pump is in an unconditioned space or climate with freezing temperatures
exceptions: When pump room is heated and all water-containing components are freeze-protected or located above frost line with heat tracing and insulation

subject: Fire Pump
rule: Fire pump suction pipe and fitting size must be at least equal to the pump suction connection size

subject: Fire Suppression Riser Room
rule: Fire suppression riser room must have adequate floor drainage (floor drain or trench drain) to handle water discharge from riser testing, draining, and potential leaks
conditions: Room contains fire standpipe or sprinkler riser
Room is located at or below grade where gravity drainage is possible
exceptions: Room with a dedicated sump pump system that actively removes accumulated water

subject: Fire Suppression Riser Room
rule: Fire suppression riser room must not have a ceiling that fully encloses the riser without access panels
conditions: Room has a suspended or drywall ceiling
exceptions: No ceiling is installed (open structure)
Entire ceiling is designed as removable panels

subject: Fire Suppression Riser Room
rule: Fire suppression riser room must have a floor that prevents water migration to adjacent spaces
conditions: Room is adjacent to habitable spaces or electrical rooms
Room floor is at same level as adjacent spaces
exceptions: Room floor is sloped to drain internally with no door threshold passage
Room is isolated with a waterproof curb or raised threshold

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car must have a functioning braking system independent of the hoist cable
conditions: installed in a passenger or freight elevator

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car floor must be level with the landing within tolerance when stopped at a floor
conditions: elevator is operational and serving passengers or cargo

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car must have a means of emergency communication (e.g., alarm bell or phone) accessible to occupants
conditions: car is designed to carry passengers

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car must not have any unguarded openings or gaps exceeding code limits in the car enclosure
conditions: car is in service

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car must have a door or gate that prevents occupants from falling into the hoistway
conditions: car serves passenger-accessible floors
exceptions: observation cars with special guardrail designs explicitly approved by code authority

subject: Elevator Car
rule: elevator car must have adequate rated capacity for the maximum intended load

subject: Hoistway/Shaft
rule: A hoistway/shaft must be continuous vertically with no horizontal offsets.
conditions: The hoistway contains an elevator car or counterweight.

subject: Hoistway/Shaft
rule: A hoistway/shaft must be enclosed by fire-resistance-rated construction.
conditions: The hoistway penetrates more than one story.
exceptions: Non-combustible open shafts in certain atrium designs where building codes specifically allow omitted enclosure with active fire suppression.

subject: Hoistway/Shaft
rule: A hoistway/shaft must not have unprotected openings into occupied spaces on multiple floors.
conditions: The shaft contains mechanical, electrical, or plumbing lines that could serve as fire or smoke paths.
exceptions: Shafts designed and constructed as part of a naturally ventilated smoke control system where openings are intentionally provided and engineered.

subject: Hoistway/Shaft
rule: A hoistway/shaft that contains an elevator must have a pit at the bottom that is dry and free of standing water.
conditions: The hoistway contains an elevator car.

subject: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller
rule: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller must be installed in a location that provides adequate ventilation and heat dissipation (ambient temperature within manufacturer-specified range, typically 0–40°C)
conditions: Controller is installed indoors
Controller uses air-cooled heat sink
exceptions: Manufacturer specifically certifies the controller for extended temperature range

subject: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller
rule: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller must have a working emergency stop (E-Stop) circuit that physically disconnects motor power

subject: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller
rule: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller must not be installed in a location subject to washing down with water or hose spray
conditions: Controller is not rated IPX5 or higher
exceptions: Controller enclosure is explicitly rated for hose-directed water (e.g., IP65+)

subject: Traction/ Hydraulic System
rule: Hydraulic fluid must be contained within sealed system components
conditions: system contains hydraulic fluid
exceptions: intentional fluid release for emergency pressure relief

subject: Traction/ Hydraulic System
rule: Hydraulic system must not operate above its rated maximum pressure

subject: Traction/ Hydraulic System
rule: Traction motor must not exceed its rated thermal limit during continuous operation
exceptions: short-duration overload during emergency or starting conditions as per design specification

subject: Traction/ Hydraulic System
rule: Hydraulic oil must maintain adequate cleanliness level per ISO 4406 standard

subject: Traction/ Hydraulic System
rule: Traction/hydraulic system must have a means of overpressure protection (e.g., relief valve)
conditions: system is pressurized

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door must latch securely in both open and closed positions

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door must not open outward beyond its hinge limit

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door seal must compress to prevent air and water ingress around the perimeter
conditions: when door is closed

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door handle must return to neutral position when released

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door must have a mechanical secondary latch (safety catch) that prevents full opening if the primary latch is not engaged
conditions: for side-hinged doors

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door glass must not shatter into sharp fragments on breakage
conditions: for side-window glass within the door assembly

subject: Car Doors
rule: car door must not contact the vehicle body during normal opening or closing

subject: Elevator Landing Doors
rule: Elevator landing doors must be fire-rated to match the fire-resistance rating of the hoistway enclosure
conditions: building has a fire-rated hoistway enclosure
applicable building code requires fire-rated hoistway doors
exceptions: elevator serving an open/unenclosed hoistway where code permits non-rated doors

subject: Elevator Landing Doors
rule: Elevator landing doors must have a clearance between door panels and the hoistway entrance not exceeding the maximum specified in the applicable elevator code (typically 10 mm or less)
conditions: elevator is a passenger or freight elevator

subject: Elevator Landing Doors
rule: Elevator landing doors must not open into the hoistway unless positively locked and interlocked

subject: Elevator Landing Doors
rule: Elevator landing doors must be equipped with a door-zone monitoring device that prevents the car from moving when any landing door is unlatched
conditions: elevator car is power-operated

subject: Elevator Landing Doors
rule: Elevator landing doors must withstand the static force required by code (typically 300 lb applied horizontally) without exceeding specified deflection limits

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: Safety brake/governor must be directly connected to the elevator car via mechanical linkage (ropes, rods, or cables)
conditions: Applies to traction and hydraulic elevators with mechanical overspeed governors

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: Governor rope tension must be maintained within specified range during all operating conditions
conditions: Applies when governor rope is used as the mechanical linkage

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: Safety brake must engage automatically when governor detects overspeed exceeding the designed trip speed threshold
exceptions: During maintenance where governor is deliberately bypassed with lockout/tagout procedures in place

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: Safety brake jaws or wedges must not contact the guide rail under normal operating conditions

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: Governor must be mounted in a location accessible for periodic inspection and testing

subject: Safety Brake/Governor
rule: The safety gear actuation mechanism must apply braking force progressively (not instantaneously) to avoid decelerating the car at rates exceeding structural/safety limits

subject: Traveling Cable
rule: Traveling cable must be long enough to allow the full range of motion of the connected moving machinery without exceeding its maximum allowable bend radius at any point of travel
conditions: cable is used on a moving machine component
cable is subject to bending during motion

subject: Traveling Cable
rule: Traveling cable must not be tensioned or loaded beyond its rated tensile capacity during normal operation
conditions: cable is suspended or dragged during motion

subject: Traveling Cable
rule: Traveling cable must be supported by a cable carrier, festoon system, or other strain-relief mechanism that prevents direct tension on the cable terminations
conditions: cable travels horizontally or vertically with moving equipment
cable length exceeds a few meters
exceptions: very short traveling cables where self-weight bending is negligible

subject: Traveling Cable
rule: Traveling cable must be rated for the required number of flex cycles over its service life without conductor fatigue failure
conditions: cable undergoes repeated bending during operation

subject: Hall Call Fixtures
rule: Hall call fixtures must be mounted at a height accessible to wheelchair users per ADA guidelines
conditions: building is located in a jurisdiction that adopts ADA or equivalent accessibility standards
exceptions: facility is a single-family residence not subject to ADA

subject: Hall Call Fixtures
rule: Hall call fixtures must not be located where they could be obstructed by a door's swing path
conditions: fixture is adjacent to a doorway

subject: Hall Call Fixtures
rule: Hall call fixture button faces must have tactile identifiers (e.g., raised arrows or Braille) adjacent to each button
conditions: fixture is intended for use by the general public
exceptions: facility is a private residence with no public access

subject: Hall Call Fixtures
rule: Hall call fixtures must be wired to the correct voltage and phase as specified by the elevator controller manufacturer

subject: Machine Room (if separate)
rule: A machine room must have a means of ventilation to prevent overheating of equipment
conditions: machine room contains heat-producing equipment such as elevators, HVAC units, or electrical panels
exceptions: machine room is not enclosed and is open to ambient air

subject: Machine Room (if separate)
rule: A separate machine room must not be located in a flood-prone area subject to standing water ingress
conditions: machine room houses critical mechanical or electrical equipment
exceptions: machine room is flood-proofed with watertight construction and sump pumping rated for the flood event

subject: Machine Room (if separate)
rule: A machine room must have structural floor loading capacity rated for the equipment it houses
conditions: machine room contains equipment with concentrated static or dynamic loads heavier than typical occupancy loads

subject: Machine Room (if separate)
rule: A separate machine room must have adequate space around equipment for maintenance access and egress
conditions: machine room contains serviceable mechanical or electrical equipment

subject: Pit
rule: pit must have a means of egress (exit) for personnel if it is an occupied space
conditions: pit is occupied by personnel
pit is classified as a confined space
exceptions: pit is less than 1.2 m deep and not classified as a confined space

subject: Pit
rule: pit must have drainage or a means to remove accumulated water
conditions: pit is below grade or subject to water ingress
exceptions: pit is designed as a sealed dry pit with no water source

subject: Pit
rule: pit must not have unprotected openings at floor level where personnel could inadvertently fall in
conditions: pit is open-topped and located in a pedestrian-accessible area
exceptions: pit is permanently covered with a load-rated grate or lid
pit is surrounded by a guardrail at least 1.1 m high

subject: Truss/Balustrade Assembly
rule: truss/balustrade assembly must have all structural connections fully secured (bolted, welded, or pinned) before accepting any superimposed load
conditions: when the assembly functions as a load-bearing component
under any expected load condition (dead load, live load, wind load)
exceptions: pre-tensioned or pre-stressed assemblies designed for controlled joint slip

subject: Truss/Balustrade Assembly
rule: truss/balustrade assembly must not exceed its buckling capacity under axial compression in any member
conditions: when any truss member is in compression
exceptions: members specifically designed as tension-only elements that are not intended to carry compression

subject: Truss/Balustrade Assembly
rule: truss/balustrade assembly must have its base or footing connections adequately anchored to resist overturning and sliding forces
conditions: when the assembly is freestanding or laterally unsupported at the top
exceptions: assemblies rigidly fixed at both top and bottom such that no net overturning moment develops

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have a rated load capacity clearly marked on the unit

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have a mechanical or electrical locking device to prevent platform movement when the lift is not in use or when the landing door/gate is open

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have an obstruction-sensing safety edge or reversing mechanism on the leading edge of the platform

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must not have a travel path that includes floor openings or gaps greater than the code-specified maximum (typically 1/2 inch or 13 mm) at landings

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have a manually operated emergency lowering device accessible from the platform
conditions: lift serves more than one landing
lift is electrically powered

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have a pit or obstruction at the bottom of travel to prevent the platform from descending below its lowest designed landing level by more than a code-permitted tolerance
conditions: lift has a vertical travel path with a lower landing

subject: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
rule: platform lift / wheelchair lift must have handrails or guardrails on all open sides of the platform where the gap to adjacent structure exceeds 4 inches (100 mm)
conditions: platform is open on one or more sides
lift is not entirely enclosed within a hoistway

subject: Step Chain and Pallet System
rule: Step chain links must be uniformly oriented to prevent binding during rotation
conditions: When chain is under load
During normal operation

subject: Step Chain and Pallet System
rule: Pallet dogs (driving lugs) must not exceed the maximum load-bearing capacity of the chain links
conditions: When pallets are being conveyed

subject: Step Chain and Pallet System
rule: Chain pitch must match the sprocket tooth spacing
conditions: At all drive and idler sprockets

subject: Step Chain and Pallet System
rule: Pallet system must have a positive locating or guiding mechanism to prevent pallet drift on the chain
conditions: During horizontal or inclined conveyance

subject: Handrail (Moving)
rule: Moving handrail must be rigidly attached to the moving platform or structure it serves
conditions: handrail is attached to a moving walkway, escalator, or similar transport system
exceptions: handrails designed as flexible barriers for specialized applications

subject: Handrail (Moving)
rule: Moving handrail must move at the same linear speed as the walking surface it accompanies
conditions: handrail is part of an escalator or moving walkway system

subject: Handrail (Moving)
rule: Moving handrail must not have exposed pinch points where the handrail enters or exits its guide track

subject: Handrail Drive Mechanism
rule: handrail drive mechanism must be capable of moving the handrail at a speed that matches the escalator steps or moving walkway pallets within a tolerance
conditions: when the escalator or moving walkway is in operation

subject: Handrail Drive Mechanism
rule: handrail drive mechanism must not generate handrail surface temperatures that exceed safe touch limits during continuous operation
conditions: under rated load and maximum ambient temperature conditions

subject: Handrail Drive Mechanism
rule: handrail drive mechanism must maintain sufficient traction between the drive wheels and the handrail to prevent slipping under all rated load conditions

subject: Drive Motor and Gearbox
rule: drive motor and gearbox must be lubricated with appropriate oil or grease to prevent metal-to-metal contact and overheating
conditions: unit is oil-lubricated type
unit has grease fittings
exceptions: hermetically sealed or maintenance-free gearboxes that are factory-filled for life

subject: Drive Motor and Gearbox
rule: drive motor and gearbox must not exceed its rated torque or power capacity during continuous operation
conditions: under any sustained load condition

subject: Drive Motor and Gearbox
rule: drive motor and gearbox must have the motor shaft and gearbox input shaft correctly aligned within the coupling manufacturer's specified tolerance
conditions: when motor and gearbox are coupled via a shaft coupling
exceptions: direct-integrated motor-gearbox units where shafts are aligned by design

subject: Drive Motor and Gearbox
rule: drive motor and gearbox must be provided with adequate cooling to maintain operating temperature within the manufacturer's specified range
conditions: when ambient temperature exceeds the designed-for range
when duty cycle is continuous or high-load
exceptions: intermittent-duty units operating well below rated capacity where natural convection suffices

subject: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
rule: drive shaft must be concentric with the sprocket bore within specified tolerance
conditions: when sprocket is mounted on drive shaft
exceptions: when using flexible coupling or keyless locking mechanism designed for misalignment

subject: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
rule: sprocket teeth must match the chain pitch exactly
conditions: for roller chain drive systems

subject: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
rule: drive shaft must not exceed its torsional yield strength under maximum rated load

subject: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
rule: sprocket must have a keyway or equivalent positive torque transmission feature
conditions: when torque is transmitted from shaft to sprocket via keyed connection
exceptions: when using taper-lock bushings, splines, or interference-fit connections that provide equivalent torque transfer

subject: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
rule: drive shaft must be supported by bearings at minimum two points
conditions: when shaft length exceeds 3x its diameter
exceptions: for very short stub shafts cantilevered with a single bearing designed for overhung loads

subject: Step Guide Rails/Track
rule: Step guide rails/track must be aligned with the mating component (e.g., sliding door, drawer, or moving panel) along the full travel path
conditions: The step guide rail/track is used to guide linear motion of a door, drawer, or panel

subject: Step Guide Rails/Track
rule: Step guide rails/track must not have protrusions or discontinuities that obstruct the path of the rolling or sliding element
conditions: The rail/track guides rolling elements such as wheels or bearings
exceptions: Intentional step features designed as stops or positional detents that are part of the intended function

subject: Newel (Handrail Base)
rule: newel base must be securely fastened to the tread or stringer
conditions: newel is load-bearing
handrail system is installed
exceptions: decorative newel posts not part of structural railing system

subject: Newel (Handrail Base)
rule: newel base must not obstruct the required clear width of the stairway
conditions: newel is mounted on stair tread

subject: Newel (Handrail Base)
rule: newel base hole or mortise must not reduce the structural capacity of the tread or stringer below minimum requirements
conditions: newel is installed by embedding into tread or stringer

subject: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
rule: Landing platform must have a load-bearing capacity sufficient for the maximum expected landing weight
conditions: when used for aircraft or vehicle landing
exceptions: when designated as emergency egress only with no landing function

subject: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
rule: Landing platform surface must be slip-resistant under wet conditions
conditions: when exposed to weather
when used for personnel access

subject: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
rule: Landing platform must have guardrails or edge protection on all open sides
conditions: when elevated more than 30 inches above adjacent surface
when used for personnel access
exceptions: at designated landing edges where vehicles or aircraft access the platform

subject: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
rule: Landing platform must not have standing water accumulation
conditions: when exposed to weather

subject: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
rule: Landing platform must not obstruct required emergency egress pathways
conditions: when located in or adjacent to means of egress
exceptions: when the platform itself is part of the approved egress path

subject: Comb Plate
rule: The comb plate must be positioned such that its teeth face upward toward the distributing plate or register
conditions: When used in match plate or pattern plate configuration

subject: Comb Plate
rule: The comb plate must have a flat back face that sits flush against the pattern plate or match plate
conditions: When used as part of a foundry molding assembly

subject: Controller/Panel
rule: controller/panel must be mounted in a location where ambient temperature stays within its rated operating range
conditions: controller/panel contains active electronic or electrical components that generate heat and are sensitive to heat
exceptions: controller/panel is specifically rated for and tested at the expected extreme temperature

subject: Controller/Panel
rule: controller/panel must be installed such that its IP/ingress protection rating matches or exceeds the environmental exposure of its location
conditions: controller/panel is located outdoors or in a wet/dusty environment
exceptions: controller/panel is placed inside a secondary weatherproof enclosure that provides the required protection

subject: Controller/Panel
rule: controller/panel must not be subjected to continuous vibration or mechanical shock exceeding its rated tolerance
conditions: controller/panel is mounted on or near rotating machinery, engines, compressors, or in seismic zones
exceptions: controller/panel is mounted on vibration isolators or dampers that bring transmitted vibration below rated levels

subject: Controller/Panel
rule: controller/panel power supply voltage must remain within the manufacturer-specified tolerance range at all times
conditions: controller/panel is connected to a live electrical supply
exceptions: controller/panel includes an integrated voltage regulator, UPS, or power conditioner that ensures input stays within range

subject: Emergency Stop Switch
rule: Emergency stop switch must be readily accessible without requiring tools or keys to reach
exceptions: Switches located in locked enclosures where only authorized personnel have access may require a key, provided the key is immediately available

subject: Emergency Stop Switch
rule: Emergency stop switch must be colored red with a yellow background or yellow surround
exceptions: Custom color schemes may be permitted per specific industry standards if equivalent visibility is maintained

subject: Emergency Stop Switch
rule: Emergency stop switch must not automatically reset when released
conditions: Switch is of the push-button or pull-cord type

subject: Emergency Stop Switch
rule: Emergency stop switch must directly disconnect power or interrupt the hazardous energy source (not rely solely on software or programmable logic)
exceptions: Categories 3 or 4 safety systems with redundant hardware monitoring and certified safety-rated software may be used where hardwiring is impractical, but the switch circuit itself must still be hardwired

subject: Safety Sensors and Switches
rule: Safety sensors and switches must be physically installed and electrically connected to the system they are intended to monitor or control
conditions: when used in a safety-critical application
exceptions: sensors used only for non-safety monitoring or diagnostics

subject: Safety Sensors and Switches
rule: Safety sensors and switches must not be bypassed, shunted, or disabled during normal operation
conditions: when the system is in operational or active mode
exceptions: during maintenance or testing with explicit lockout/tagout procedures in place

subject: Safety Sensors and Switches
rule: Safety switches must achieve and maintain positive-opening operation of their normally closed contacts
conditions: when classified as a positive-opening safety switch per IEC 60947-5-1 or equivalent standard
exceptions: non-positive-opening switches used in non-safety monitoring roles

subject: Machine Room (Integrated)
rule: Machine room (integrated) must have fire-rated enclosure with minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating when the building exceeds 2 storeys or has a floor area greater than 2000 m²
conditions: building exceeds 2 storeys
or building floor area exceeds 2000 m²
exceptions: sprinkler-protected entire building

subject: Machine Room (Integrated)
rule: Machine room (integrated) must have a minimum ceiling height of 2.4 m

subject: Machine Room (Integrated)
rule: Machine room (integrated) must have a floor drain or trench drain connected to building drainage system
conditions: room contains water-cooled equipment
or contains boilers/chillers
or contains condensate-producing equipment
exceptions: only dry electrical equipment (switchgear, transformers) is present and no water-bearing equipment exists

subject: Machine Room (Integrated)
rule: Machine room (integrated) must not have openings or penetrations directly into habitable spaces without fire-rated seal
exceptions: penetrations fitted with approved firestop systems maintaining the fire-resistance rating of the enclosure

subject: Machine Room (Integrated)
rule: Machine room (integrated) must have mechanical ventilation capable of maintaining temperature below 40°C and providing air changes for equipment heat rejection
conditions: room contains heat-producing equipment (motors, transformers, boilers, chillers)
exceptions: equipment is self-ventilated to outdoors and the room contains no other heat sources

subject: Escalator Pit
rule: escalator pit must have a drain at the lowest point
conditions: pit collects water or cleaning runoff
pit is not continuously submerged in groundwater
exceptions: pit is designed as a sealed/watertight sump with no drainage outlet

subject: Escalator Pit
rule: escalator pit must have a minimum clearance depth that permits safe access for maintenance
conditions: pit depth exceeds 600 mm
pit is accessible to maintenance personnel
exceptions: pit is designed as an infill/zero-depth pit with no access requirement

subject: Escalator Pit
rule: escalator pit must not contain habitable or occupied space

subject: Escalator Pit
rule: escalator pit sump pump (if installed) must have a dedicated discharge path that does not flood adjacent spaces
conditions: pit is equipped with a sump pump rather than a gravity drain

subject: Escalator Truss
rule: escalator truss must be designed to support the full dead load of the escalator system plus the design live load (passenger load)
conditions: when installed as part of an escalator system

subject: Escalator Truss
rule: escalator truss must not have any missing or broken load-bearing members (chords, diagonals, or welds)
conditions: during operation

subject: Escalator Truss
rule: escalator truss must have end connections (supports) that are capable of transferring all design loads to the building structure
conditions: at each support point

subject: Railing (Fixed) Adjacent to Escalator
rule: railing adjacent to escalator must have a handrail on at least one side
conditions: escalator is installed
exceptions: railing is purely decorative and not intended for occupant support

subject: Railing (Fixed) Adjacent to Escalator
rule: railing adjacent to escalator must not have horizontal elements that allow climbing
conditions: railing is located where children under 5 may be present

subject: Railing (Fixed) Adjacent to Escalator
rule: railing adjacent to escalator must have balusters spaced to prevent passage of a 4-inch sphere
conditions: railing serves as a guard at a drop-off exceeding 30 inches

subject: Travelator/Moving Walk
rule: Travelator/Moving Walk must have a handrail speed synchronized with the walking surface speed
conditions: passenger-carrying application

subject: Travelator/Moving Walk
rule: Travelator/Moving Walk must have an emergency stop (E-stop) device accessible at each landing

subject: Travelator/Moving Walk
rule: Travelator/Moving Walk must not have a step/pallet gap exceeding allowable limits at the comb plate

subject: Travelator/Moving Walk
rule: Travelator/Moving Walk inclination must not exceed 12 degrees from horizontal

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator must have brakes capable of stopping and holding a fully loaded escalator under all operating conditions
conditions: heavy-duty/metro installation

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator steps must comply with dimensional standards for tread depth and riser height to prevent entrapment and passenger fall

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator must have a continuous handrail moving in synchronization with the steps

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator truss must have sufficient structural capacity to support dead load plus live load (passengers) without collapse or excessive deflection

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator must not have step gaps that exceed safety code maximum (typically 6 mm vertical / 3 mm horizontal at comb plate)

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator must be equipped with emergency stop controls (E-stop buttons) at both landings and accessible to passengers
conditions: public metro/heavy-duty installation

subject: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
rule: escalator drive system must include a non-reversing device (anti-runaway brake) to prevent reversal of direction under load
conditions: heavy-duty/metro escalator with incline greater than 30 degrees

subject: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
rule: inclined elevator must have a braking system capable of stopping and holding the car on the maximum incline under all load conditions
conditions: inclined elevator operates on a slope greater than 15 degrees from horizontal

subject: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
rule: inclined elevator carriage must be guided by rails or tracks that prevent derailment under all load and wind conditions

subject: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
rule: inclined elevator must not have a friction-only hold mechanism as the sole means of stopping on the incline

subject: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
rule: inclined elevator must have a mechanism to prevent passenger compartment tilt beyond the designed pitch angle
conditions: carriage is designed with passenger compartment that is not fixed at the track angle
exceptions: carriage is a fixed cabin rigidly attached to the track-following frame at the line's grade

subject: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
rule: inclined elevator must not have a cable that can abrade against the structure or terrain along its path
conditions: elevator uses a haulage cable or counterweight cable
exceptions: cable is fully enclosed in a conduit or guide sheave system that prevents contact

subject: Lighting Fixture
rule: lighting fixture must be listed as suitable for the intended location type (e.g., damp, wet, or dry location) by a recognized testing laboratory
conditions: installed in a building

subject: Lighting Fixture
rule: lighting fixture must not be installed such that its heat output can ignite adjacent combustible materials
conditions: installed near combustible construction or materials
exceptions: fixtures listed with zero-clearance or insulation-contact (IC) rating

subject: Lighting Fixture
rule: lighting fixture must be securely attached to a building structure capable of supporting its weight

subject: Lamp / Light Source
rule: Lamp/light source must have a rated voltage that matches the supply voltage of the circuit it is connected to
conditions: When connected to a fixed electrical circuit
exceptions: If the lamp includes an integrated driver or ballast that accepts a range of input voltages

subject: Lamp / Light Source
rule: Lamp/light source must not generate surface temperatures that exceed the ignition temperature of adjacent materials under normal operation
conditions: When installed in contact with or in proximity to combustible materials
exceptions: If the luminaire design provides a thermal barrier or is specifically rated for insulation contact (IC-rated)

subject: Lamp / Light Source
rule: Lamp/light source must have mechanical attachment that prevents unintentional dislodging under expected vibration and gravitational forces
conditions: When installed in a position where failure could cause the lamp to fall or shift

subject: Ballast / Driver
rule: ballast or driver must not generate heat exceeding its rated thermal limit during continuous operation
conditions: continuous operation
rated load conditions
exceptions: short-duration transient conditions explicitly accounted for in design specifications

subject: Ballast / Driver
rule: ballast must provide rated output current within specified tolerance to the driver/LED load
conditions: when connected to a properly matched LED load within the ballast's specified operating range

subject: Ballast / Driver
rule: driver must have overvoltage and overcurrent protection that activates before downstream components are damaged
conditions: when input power is applied
exceptions: if the driver lacks such protection by design and the system relies on external protection — but this is rare and itself a violation of typical safety standards

subject: Lighting Switch
rule: Lighting switch must be installed in an accessible location where it can be reached for manual operation
conditions: switch is intended for manual user operation
exceptions: automated or remote-controlled switches with no manual interface

subject: Lighting Switch
rule: Lighting switch must be mounted on a wall or approved electrical box at standard height
conditions: switch is a fixed installation in a building

subject: Lighting Switch
rule: Lighting switch must_not be installed in a location where it could be exposed to direct water spray or immersion
conditions: switch is not rated for wet/damp locations
exceptions: switch is UL/CSA listed for wet locations and has appropriate weatherproof cover

subject: Lighting Switch
rule: Lighting switch conductors must be rated for the electrical load (amperage and voltage) of the connected lighting circuit

subject: Emergency Lighting System
rule: Emergency lighting system must automatically activate within 10 seconds of normal lighting supply failure
conditions: normal AC lighting supply is interrupted
emergency mode is required

subject: Emergency Lighting System
rule: Emergency lighting system must provide minimum illumination of 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux) along the egress path at floor level
conditions: building is occupied
egress path is in use during emergency

subject: Emergency Lighting System
rule: Emergency lighting system must not rely solely on a single centralized battery that serves non-emergency loads
conditions: central battery system is used as the emergency power source

subject: Emergency Lighting System
rule: Emergency lighting luminaires must be listed to UL 924 (or equivalent standard)
conditions: luminaire is installed in a location subject to building code enforcement

subject: Emergency Lighting System
rule: Emergency lighting system must be tested automatically or manually at intervals not exceeding 30 days
conditions: system is installed and operational

subject: Lighting Control Panel
rule: Lighting control panel must be installed in a location that is accessible for operation and maintenance
conditions: When panel serves as primary lighting control for an occupied space
exceptions: When panel is a remote or secondary panel controlled via network from a primary accessible panel

subject: Lighting Control Panel
rule: Lighting control panel must be installed in an environment within its rated temperature and humidity range

subject: Lighting Control Panel
rule: Lighting control panel must not be installed in a location subject to direct water spray or immersion
conditions: Unless panel is specifically rated for wet or damp locations
exceptions: Panels with NEMA 3R, 4, or higher ingress protection rating that are listed for wet locations

subject: Lighting Control Panel
rule: Lighting control panel must have its overcurrent protection device sized to not exceed the panel's ampere rating

subject: Exit Sign
rule: Exit sign must be continuously illuminated (or actively powered) whenever the building is occupied
conditions: Building is occupied or the egress path is required to be functional
exceptions: Facility is permanently unoccupied and decommissioned
Sign uses self-luminous (non-electric) technology that meets code without external power

subject: Exit Sign
rule: Exit sign must be visible and legible from the egress path it serves
conditions: Sign is installed to mark an exit or egress direction
exceptions: Path is not intended for occupant egress (e.g., maintenance-only access)

subject: Exit Sign
rule: Exit sign must not be located where it can be confused with or obscured by other signage, decorations, or building elements
conditions: Sign is installed in a public or occupant-accessible area

subject: Exit Sign
rule: Exit sign must be connected to a reliable power source (building primary supply or battery backup)
conditions: Sign is electrically powered (not self-luminous)
exceptions: Sign uses self-luminous radioluminescent or photoluminescent technology that does not require electrical connection

subject: Lighting Conductor / Track
rule: lighting conductor track must be electrically continuous along its entire length

subject: Lighting Conductor / Track
rule: lighting conductor track must not have sharp bends or kinks with an internal angle less than 90 degrees

subject: Lighting Conductor / Track
rule: lighting conductor track must be securely fixed to the building structure at intervals not exceeding the maximum specified by applicable standards

subject: Lighting Conductor / Track
rule: lighting conductor track must be installed on the outermost surface of the building (not buried inside walls or insulation)
exceptions: Concealed conductors are permitted if specifically designed with appropriate insulation and clearance per standards

subject: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
rule: Lighting diffuser/lens must be made from a translucent or transparent material

subject: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
rule: Lighting diffuser/lens must not block the intended light output path between the lamp and the illuminated space

subject: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
rule: Lighting diffuser/lens material must withstand the operating temperature of the adjacent light source
conditions: when used with a lamp that generates heat
exceptions: when the light source is a fully encapsulated LED panel with negligible heat output below the material's lowest softening point

subject: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
rule: Lighting diffuser/lens must fit securely within its housing or frame to prevent falling
conditions: when installed overhead or in a ceiling-mounted luminaire

subject: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
rule: Lighting diffuser/lens must not create a fire ignition risk via light concentration
conditions: when used with a directional or high-intensity light source
exceptions: when the lens is optically designed to spread rather than concentrate light (no focusing effect)

subject: Reflector / Baffle / Louver
rule: reflector/baffle/louver must be physically supported or attached to a stable structure
conditions: when used as a standalone architectural or lighting component

subject: Reflector / Baffle / Louver
rule: reflector/baffle/louver must not block required egress or emergency exit paths
conditions: when installed in or adjacent to means of egress
when located in a path required for emergency evacuation
exceptions: when specifically designed as a frangible/breakaway louver that yields under egress forces
