subject: Reflector / Baffle / Louver
rule: reflector/baffle/louver must not collapse under self-weight and expected imposed loads (e.g., wind, snow, maintenance load)
conditions: when installed in any exterior or overhead application

subject: Mounting Bracket / Hanger
rule: Mounting bracket / hanger must be capable of supporting the full dead load of the attached component plus any live loads without plastic deformation or fracture

subject: Mounting Bracket / Hanger
rule: Mounting bracket / hanger must have a safety factor against static failure of at least the minimum required by applicable structural code (typically 1.5 to 5 depending on material and application)

subject: Mounting Bracket / Hanger
rule: Mounting bracket / hanger must not be installed on a substrate that lacks sufficient strength to carry the bracket's applied loads

subject: Mounting Bracket / Hanger
rule: Mounting bracket / hanger must be positively secured (e.g., mechanical fastener, welded, or interlocked) and not rely solely on friction or gravity to retain position under all expected load directions

subject: Lighting Circuit / Feeder
rule: Lighting circuit / feeder conductors must be sized to carry the connected load without exceeding their ampacity rating
conditions: continuous load scenario
exceptions: when protected by an upstream overcurrent device set to a lower rating

subject: Lighting Circuit / Feeder
rule: Lighting circuit / feeder must be protected against overcurrent by a properly rated fuse, circuit breaker, or other overcurrent protective device
exceptions: certain elevator feeders per NEC 620.61(D)

subject: Lighting Circuit / Feeder
rule: Lighting circuit grounded (neutral) conductor must not be switched or opened by a disconnecting means

subject: Daylighting Integration
rule: daylighting aperture must have a direct, unobstructed line of sight to the sky or exterior light source
conditions: when the system includes any aperture intended for daylighting

subject: Daylighting Integration
rule: daylighting aperture must not be blocked by permanent opaque construction within its intended light path
conditions: for any aperture designated as a primary daylight source
exceptions: temporary or movable shading devices that can be opened

subject: Wall Sconce
rule: wall sconce must be securely attached to a structural wall or framing member capable of supporting its weight
conditions: when mounted on wall

subject: Wall Sconce
rule: wall sconce must not generate heat that exceeds the temperature rating of adjacent wall materials
conditions: when the sconce contains an incandescent, halogen, or high-wattage LED light source
exceptions: sconces designed for use with specialized heat-dissipating mounting blocks that maintain safe interface temperatures

subject: Wall Sconce
rule: wall sconce electrical enclosure must be rated for the installation environment (damp-rated if in a damp location, wet-rated if exposed to direct water)
conditions: when installed in a bathroom, exterior covered area, or other location exposed to moisture or humidity

subject: Recessed Downlight / Can Light
rule: Recessed downlight housing must be rated for contact with insulation (IC-rated) when installed in insulated ceilings
conditions: installed in a ceiling that contains or is adjacent to thermal insulation
exceptions: non-IC rated housing may be used if insulation is kept at least 3 inches away from the housing and no insulation is placed above it

subject: Recessed Downlight / Can Light
rule: Recessed downlight must have a vapor-tight seal or gasket when installed in a building thermal envelope
conditions: installed in an exterior ceiling or roof assembly that forms part of the building's thermal envelope
exceptions: downlights not penetrating the air barrier or installed in interior ceilings only

subject: Recessed Downlight / Can Light
rule: Recessed downlight must not have gaps larger than 1/2 inch between the trim and ceiling drywall
conditions: installed in a finished ceiling assembly

subject: Recessed Downlight / Can Light
rule: Recessed downlight housing must have a thermal protector (autothermal reset) that disconnects power if the fixture exceeds safe operating temperature
conditions: installed in a ceiling where the ambient temperature may exceed the fixture's rated maximum
exceptions: fixtures designed with inherently limited heat output (e.g., low-wattage LED with passive cooling verified by UL listing)

subject: High-Bay / Low-Bay Luminaire
rule: luminaire must be rated for the mounting height (high-bay ≥ 20 ft, low-bay < 20 ft)
conditions: installed in an indoor commercial or industrial space

subject: High-Bay / Low-Bay Luminaire
rule: luminaire must not be installed in direct contact with combustible materials unless explicitly fire-rated
conditions: mounted in a location with exposed combustible construction or storage
exceptions: luminaire carries a specific fire-rated enclosure listing (e.g., UL 1598 fire-rated or IC-rated)

subject: Strip Light / Linear Fixture
rule: strip light / linear fixture must be connected to a suitable electrical power supply within its rated voltage and current
conditions: when installed and intended to emit light

subject: Strip Light / Linear Fixture
rule: strip light / linear fixture must not have its LED chips or internal electronics exposed to moisture beyond its rated IP (Ingress Protection) level
conditions: when installed in a location where moisture, condensation, or water ingress is possible
exceptions: fixtures specifically rated for wet/damp locations with appropriate IP rating (e.g., IP65, IP67)

subject: Strip Light / Linear Fixture
rule: strip light / linear fixture must be mounted on a surface or structure capable of supporting its weight
conditions: when installed overhead or on vertical surfaces

subject: Strip Light / Linear Fixture
rule: strip light / linear fixture must not generate surface temperatures exceeding the fire ignition threshold of adjacent combustible materials
conditions: when installed in contact with or in proximity to combustible materials such as wood, fabric, or insulation
exceptions: fixtures with certified thermal protection and safe temperature ratings verified for the specific mounting surface

subject: Landscape / Exterior Lighting
rule: exterior lighting must be weather-rated (IP65 or higher for exposed locations)
conditions: fixture is exposed to rain or moisture
fixture is installed outdoors
exceptions: fixture is installed in a fully enclosed weatherproof housing
fixture is rated for dry/indoor use only and protected by canopy or overhang

subject: Landscape / Exterior Lighting
rule: exterior lighting must not be aimed directly at adjacent dwelling windows at a height that causes nuisance glare
conditions: adjacent residential property exists within 15 meters
light source is mounted less than 2.5m above ground level
exceptions: light is shielded and emits no light above 90 degrees from vertical

subject: Landscape / Exterior Lighting
rule: exterior lighting must be connected to a ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protected circuit
conditions: lighting is mains-voltage (120V-277V)
installation is in a location accessible to the public or within reach of damp ground
exceptions: fixture is low-voltage (less than 30V) and powered by an approved transformer

subject: Landscape / Exterior Lighting
rule: landscape lighting must not compromise root flare or structural roots of existing trees
conditions: trenching or excavation is required for underground wiring
tree trunk diameter exceeds 150mm at 1.4m height
exceptions: wiring is surface-mounted with no soil disturbance within the dripline

subject: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable
rule: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable must be properly terminated at both ends to ensure signal integrity
conditions: when used for digital communication protocols (e.g., DALI, DMX, KNX, BACnet)
exceptions: when the cable is installed as a spare/unt terminated stub intended for future use and clearly labeled as such

subject: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable
rule: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable must not share the same conduit or cable tray with power cables above 50V without proper separation barrier
conditions: when the cable is not specifically rated and shielded for EMI/RFI immunity in mixed-voltage environments
exceptions: when the communication cable has an overall braided shield rated for the expected interference and the installation complies with applicable electrical code

subject: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable
rule: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable must maintain the specified topology (daisy-chain, star, or free-topology) as defined by the protocol manufacturer
conditions: when the bus protocol specifies a mandatory topology (e.g., DALI requires daisy-chain; DMX requires daisy-chain with termination)
exceptions: when using a protocol that explicitly supports multiple topologies and the device addressing scheme accommodates the chosen layout

subject: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable
rule: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable must not exceed the maximum bus length specified by the protocol standard
conditions: when using any standardized lighting control protocol
exceptions: when a manufacturer-approved repeater, hub, or bridge is installed within the length limit to extend the bus

subject: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU)
rule: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU) must be installed in a location accessible to fire department personnel and building occupants without requiring keys, tools, or special equipment to reach
conditions: applies to all new installations
applies to building fire alarm systems
exceptions: security facilities where controlled access is approved by the fire code official

subject: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU)
rule: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU) must not be installed in an area subject to physical damage, impact, or environmental contamination (dust, moisture, corrosive atmosphere)
conditions: all installations
exceptions: when housed in a NEMA-rated enclosure appropriate to the environment

subject: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU)
rule: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU) must be connected to a dedicated branch circuit and cannot share a neutral or ground with non-fire-alarm equipment
conditions: new installations
system retrofits affecting power supply

subject: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU)
rule: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU) must be provided with a secondary (standby) power source capable of operating the system for a minimum duration per code
conditions: all fire alarm systems per NFPA 72
exceptions: systems in buildings with automatic sprinkler systems meeting alternative requirements may have reduced standby duration

subject: Smoke Detector
rule: Smoke detector must be installed on a ceiling or high on a wall (within 12 inches of the ceiling) where smoke will naturally rise and accumulate
conditions: Building interior
Fixed installation in occupied space
exceptions: Sloped ceilings where mounting location follows manufacturer's slope-specific instructions
Areas with high airflow where smoke dispersion prevents accumulation (requires alternative detector type)

subject: Smoke Detector
rule: Smoke detector must not be installed near air supply vents, windows, or fans where airflow would divert smoke away from the detector
conditions: Any indoor installation
exceptions: When manufacturer explicitly certifies the model for airflow-prone locations

subject: Smoke Detector
rule: Smoke detector must be installed at least 20 feet from kitchens and bathrooms to prevent nuisance alarms from cooking fumes and steam
conditions: Residential occupancies
Non-commercial cooking areas
exceptions: When using photoelectric-type detectors with nuisance-alarm-rejection technology per manufacturer specification
Commercial kitchens with dedicated fire suppressions systems that use heat detectors instead

subject: Manual Pull Station (Manual Call Point)
rule: A manual pull station (manual call point) must be located within the designated path of egress travel
conditions: building is required to have a fire alarm system with manual initiation

subject: Manual Pull Station (Manual Call Point)
rule: A manual pull station (manual call point) must be mounted at a height between 42 inches (1.07 m) and 48 inches (1.22 m) above the finished floor
exceptions: installations covered by ADA accessibility guidelines for reach ranges may permit adjustment within 48 inches maximum high reach

subject: Manual Pull Station (Manual Call Point)
rule: A manual pull station (manual call point) must not be obstructed by any permanent or temporary object that prevents visual identification or physical access

subject: Notification Appliance
rule: notification appliance must have a visible or audible signaling method

subject: Notification Appliance
rule: notification appliance must be listed to UL 1971 (for visible) or UL 464 (for audible)
conditions: when installed in a fire alarm system subject to NFPA 72 or building code enforcement

subject: Notification Appliance
rule: notification appliance must not be installed where ambient noise exceeds its output rating minus 15 dBA
conditions: when used for audible occupant notification

subject: Notification Appliance
rule: notification appliance must have a minimum light output of 15 candela for sleeping area strobes
conditions: when used as a visible notification appliance in a sleeping area

subject: Notification Appliance
rule: notification appliance must be mounted with its strobe light located between 80 and 96 inches above floor level
conditions: when it contains a visible strobe and is installed in a wall-mounted configuration
exceptions: ceiling-mounted installations have different height requirements

subject: Fire Alarm Bell / Sounder
rule: Fire alarm bell/sounder must be connected to a fire alarm control panel (FACP) or initiating device circuit
conditions: The device is part of an automatic fire alarm system
exceptions: Standalone battery-operated smoke alarms that incorporate an integral sounder

subject: Fire Alarm Bell / Sounder
rule: Fire alarm bell/sounder must be installed in a location where its audible output is not obstructed by walls, doors, or large equipment that would prevent occupants from hearing the alarm
conditions: The sounder serves as the primary means of occupant notification for a given area
exceptions: Areas where visible notification appliances (strobes) are used as the primary means due to occupant hearing impairment

subject: Fire Alarm Bell / Sounder
rule: Fire alarm bell/sounder must be supplied with power of the correct voltage and polarity as specified by the manufacturer

subject: Voice Evacuation System
rule: Voice Evacuation System must have a redundant (primary/backup) power supply
conditions: system serves as the primary means of occupant evacuation notification
exceptions: building has a dedicated emergency generator that powers the system via a fail-safe transfer switch with automatic start and sufficient fuel capacity

subject: Voice Evacuation System
rule: Voice Evacuation System must not share audio pathways or control equipment with non-emergency paging or background music systems unless those pathways are electrically supervised and fail-safe to emergency priority
conditions: the system is integrated with a general-purpose public address system

subject: Voice Evacuation System
rule: Voice Evacuation System must achieve minimum intelligibility (e.g., STI ≥ 0.50 or per applicable code) at all occupant locations served
exceptions: spaces not intended for occupancy or those protected by alternative approved evacuation notification methods

subject: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
rule: fire alarm control panel enclosure must be constructed of materials with a fire resistance rating appropriate to its location
conditions: enclosure houses life safety equipment
enclosure installed in building
exceptions: where local authority having jurisdiction explicitly waives requirement

subject: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
rule: fire alarm control panel enclosure must not allow ingress of water or moisture that could damage internal components
conditions: enclosure installed indoors or outdoors

subject: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
rule: fire alarm control panel enclosure must be lockable to prevent unauthorized access

subject: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
rule: fire alarm control panel enclosure must have a door or cover that opens fully to allow service access

subject: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
rule: fire alarm control panel enclosure must not contain or be fabricated from materials that are incompatible with the electrical components housed inside (no galvanic corrosion risk)
exceptions: where dissimilar metals are properly isolated with dielectric barriers

subject: Backup Battery / Power Supply
rule: Backup battery / power supply must be located in a well-ventilated area to prevent accumulation of explosive gases (e.g., hydrogen from lead-acid batteries).
conditions: battery type is lead-acid or other vented chemistry
exceptions: sealed/lithium batteries with certified integrated venting

subject: Backup Battery / Power Supply
rule: Backup battery / power supply must not be installed directly adjacent to ignition sources or open flames.
conditions: battery type is lead-acid or other flammable-electrolyte chemistry

subject: Backup Battery / Power Supply
rule: Backup battery / power supply must be electrically isolated from the main service when the system is being serviced (lockout/tagout capability).
conditions: system includes a manual transfer switch or is hardwired into building electrical

subject: Backup Battery / Power Supply
rule: Backup battery / power supply must have overcurrent protection (fuse or breaker) on the output conductors.
conditions: battery capacity exceeds 100 Ah or output current exceeds 20 A
exceptions: integrated battery management system (BMS) that provides equivalent protection

subject: Backup Battery / Power Supply
rule: Backup battery / power supply must not be installed in a location subject to flooding or standing water.
exceptions: battery and all connections are rated for submersion (e.g., IP68 rated marine enclosure)

subject: Fire Alarm Wiring / Cabling
rule: Fire alarm wiring/cabling must be installed in a manner that maintains fire-resistive rating of barriers it penetrates
conditions: when passing through fire-rated walls
when passing through fire-rated floors
when passing through fire-rated partitions
exceptions: when penetration is protected by a listed firestop system that restores the fire-resistance rating

subject: Fire Alarm Wiring / Cabling
rule: Fire alarm wiring/cabling must not be routed through or within plenum spaces unless it is plenum-rated (FPLP or equivalent)
conditions: when installed in air-handling plenums
when installed in spaces used for environmental air return
exceptions: when wiring is enclosed in metallic conduit that meets fire code requirements for plenum installations

subject: Fire Alarm Wiring / Cabling
rule: Fire alarm wiring/cabling must be electrically supervised for integrity (continuity monitoring)
conditions: for initiating device circuits (IDC)
for signaling line circuits (SLC)
for notification appliance circuits (NAC)

subject: Fire Alarm Wiring / Cabling
rule: Fire alarm wiring/cabling must be installed with minimum 1/4-inch derating distance from Class 1 power circuits
conditions: when running in the same raceway
when running in the same cable tray
when running in the same enclosure
exceptions: when separated by a grounded metal barrier

subject: Conduit / Raceway for Fire Alarm Cables
rule: Conduit / raceway for fire alarm cables must be installed as a continuous pathway from end to end without breaks that expose cables
conditions: used for fire alarm system wiring
exceptions: when using listed cable types that are permitted to be installed without raceway per applicable code

subject: Conduit / Raceway for Fire Alarm Cables
rule: Conduit / raceway for fire alarm cables must not share the same enclosure with electric light or power conductors
conditions: when installed in the same raceway or enclosure
exceptions: unless the power conductors are part of a fire alarm system power supply and comply with separation requirements

subject: Conduit / Raceway for Fire Alarm Cables
rule: Conduit / raceway for fire alarm cables must be securely supported at intervals not exceeding the code-prescribed spacing
conditions: installed in any orientation
exceptions: where cables are installed in a manner that provides equivalent support per engineering judgment and code approval

subject: Conduit / Raceway for Fire Alarm Cables
rule: Conduit / raceway for fire alarm cables must not exceed its fill capacity as defined by applicable code for the number and size of cables installed
conditions: when more than one cable is installed in the raceway

subject: Detector Base
rule: Detector Base must provide a stable, rigid mounting surface for the detector element

subject: Detector Base
rule: Detector Base must not introduce magnetic or electrical interference to the detector element
conditions: when the detector is sensitive to electromagnetic fields

subject: Detector Base
rule: Detector Base must have a thermal expansion coefficient compatible with the detector element to prevent mechanical stress over operating temperature range
conditions: when operating over a temperature range exceeding ±10°C

subject: Detector Base
rule: Detector Base must be electrically grounded
conditions: when the base is made of conductive material
exceptions: if the base is expressly designed as an isolated floating reference

subject: Beam Detector (Projected Beam Smoke Detector)
rule: projected beam smoke detector must have an uninterrupted line of sight between transmitter and receiver
conditions: device type is projected beam smoke detector
exceptions: reflector-type beam detectors may fold the path

subject: Beam Detector (Projected Beam Smoke Detector)
rule: projected beam smoke detector must not be installed where the beam path will be permanently obstructed by building structure, equipment, or stored materials
conditions: device type is projected beam smoke detector

subject: Beam Detector (Projected Beam Smoke Detector)
rule: projected beam smoke detector must be mounted on rigid structural elements capable of maintaining alignment
conditions: device type is projected beam smoke detector

subject: Aspiration / Air-Sampling Smoke Detector (ASD)
rule: ASD sampling pipe network must provide air-tight integrity across all joints and connections
conditions: Aspirating smoke detection system installed

subject: Aspiration / Air-Sampling Smoke Detector (ASD)
rule: ASD sampling holes must not be obstructed by debris, paint, or dust accumulation
conditions: ASD installed as an active air-sampling system

subject: Aspiration / Air-Sampling Smoke Detector (ASD)
rule: ASD must be connected to a dedicated or compatible fire alarm control panel
conditions: ASD used as part of a life-safety fire detection system

subject: Flame Detector
rule: Flame detector must be positioned with unobstructed line of sight to the area being protected
conditions: When used for open-area (non-ducted) flame detection
exceptions: Areas where line-of-sight is physically impossible and alternative detection methods are used

subject: Flame Detector
rule: Flame detector must not be exposed to direct sunlight or high-intensity artificial light sources within its spectral sensitivity range
conditions: For UV and IR-type flame detectors
exceptions: Detectors specifically designed with solar-blind or false-alarm-rejection technology that filters out steady-state solar/artificial radiation

subject: Flame Detector
rule: Flame detector must be mounted such that its field of view is not blocked by opaque structural elements (beams, columns, equipment)
conditions: In any installation where the detector is relied upon for area coverage
exceptions: None — partial blockage still creates blind zones that violate the detection coverage area

subject: Flame Detector
rule: Flame detector must be rated for the ambient temperature range of its installed environment
conditions: When installed in extreme-temperature environments (e.g., boilers, turbines, foundries, cold storage)
exceptions: Temperate indoor environments where ambient stays within standard commercial detector ratings (typically -20°C to +55°C)

subject: Gas Detector (CO / Combustible Gas)
rule: gas detector (CO / combustible gas) must be installed in locations where gas accumulation is possible, such as near gas appliances, furnaces, garages, or parking structures
conditions: indoor installation
enclosed space containing fuel-burning equipment or vehicle storage

subject: Gas Detector (CO / Combustible Gas)
rule: gas detector (CO / combustible gas) must be connected to a continuously available power source (hardwired or with battery backup)

subject: Gas Detector (CO / Combustible Gas)
rule: gas detector (CO / combustible gas) must not be installed in dead air spaces, behind obstructions, or in locations where airflow is blocked (e.g., behind doors, in corners, above cabinets)

subject: Gas Detector (CO / Combustible Gas)
rule: gas detector (CO / combustible gas) must be mounted at the appropriate height relative to the target gas density (CO at breathing height ~5 ft from floor; combustible gas near ceiling for lighter-than-air gas)
conditions: specific gas type is known (CO vs combustible gas)

subject: Interface Relay / Control Module
rule: Interface Relay / Control Module must have labeled and polarity-protected wiring connections to prevent miswiring that would cause device failure or system malfunction
conditions: When the module is field-wired
When the module uses DC power
exceptions: Modules with built-in reverse polarity protection that renders miswiring non-destructive

subject: Interface Relay / Control Module
rule: Interface Relay / Control Module must not be installed in a location where ambient temperature exceeds its rated operating temperature range
conditions: When the module is installed inside an enclosure or near heat-generating equipment
exceptions: Modules specifically rated for the elevated ambient temperature with documented de-rating or forced cooling

subject: Interface Relay / Control Module
rule: Interface Relay / Control Module must have its rated voltage applied; applying a voltage higher than the rated coil/input voltage will destroy the module
conditions: During initial energization
When the supply voltage is uncontrolled or not fused
exceptions: Modules with wide-range universal power supplies that explicitly accept the applied voltage

subject: Door Holder / Magnetic Door Release
rule: must be connected to a fire alarm system or building management system that provides a signal to release the door upon alarm activation
conditions: installed in a fire-rated doorway
part of a fire/smoke compartmentation system
exceptions: manually operated door holders not tied to alarm systems

subject: Door Holder / Magnetic Door Release
rule: must fail safe — the door must close (release) upon loss of power to the electromagnetic holder
conditions: electrically powered magnetic door holder

subject: Door Holder / Magnetic Door Release
rule: the holding force rating must be sufficient to resist the door-closing force of the installed door closer under normal building pressurization conditions
conditions: used in conjunction with a door closer on a self-closing door assembly
exceptions: doors with no closer (gravity-closed or free-swinging doors)

subject: Intrusion Detection System
rule: Intrusion Detection System must have a continuously available power source (mains, battery backup, or both) during its intended operating period
conditions: system is active and monitoring
exceptions: system is explicitly designed for passive/non-powered operation with mechanical-only detection (rare, specialized equipment)

subject: Intrusion Detection System
rule: Intrusion Detection System must have a communication path (hardwired or wireless) between its sensors and the central control/annunciation point
conditions: system has spatially separated sensors and control unit
exceptions: fully self-contained standalone alarm unit where sensor and annunciator are integrated into a single device body with no remote components

subject: Intrusion Detection System
rule: Intrusion Detection System sensors must not be placed in locations where environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, airflow, airborne debris) exceed the manufacturer's rated operating range
conditions: sensor type has published environmental ratings
exceptions: sensors specifically designed and rated for the environmental extreme in question

subject: Access Control System
rule: Access control system must have a means of fail-safe or fail-secure state defined per door
conditions: System controls physical egress doors
Doors serve occupied spaces
exceptions: Detention facilities where fail-secure is mandated and life-safety code specifically permits it
Areas with dual-function requirements where delayed egress is separately approved

subject: Access Control System
rule: Access control system must not allow a single credential to unlock two independent secure perimeters in one action without an intervening secure zone
conditions: System uses card, biometric, or mobile credentials to unlock doors
Door groups are configured for anti-passback or high-security zones
exceptions: Mantrap/interlock systems where both doors are part of a single controlled portal

subject: Access Control System
rule: Access control system must have backup power sufficient to maintain all locked doors in their required state for a minimum duration
conditions: System is served by mains electrical power
System controls fail-secure locks that require power to remain locked
exceptions: Systems with purely fail-safe locks that unlock on power loss

subject: CCTV / Video Surveillance System
rule: CCTV camera must have an unobstructed field of view to its designated coverage area
conditions: when the camera is installed for surveillance or monitoring purposes
exceptions: cameras used solely for general area illumination sensing or non-visual detection

subject: CCTV / Video Surveillance System
rule: CCTV camera housing must be rated for the environmental conditions of its installation location
conditions: when installed outdoors
when installed in wet, dusty, corrosive, or extreme-temperature environments
exceptions: cameras installed exclusively in climate-controlled indoor environments with no exposure to moisture, dust, or corrosive agents

subject: CCTV / Video Surveillance System
rule: CCTV camera must be powered within its rated voltage and current specifications

subject: CCTV / Video Surveillance System
rule: CCTV video signal transmission path must not exceed the maximum cable length for the chosen transmission standard
conditions: when using analog coax (e.g., RG-59)
when using passive twisted-pair or USB extenders without active repeaters
exceptions: when using active repeaters, fiber optic converters, or IP transmission over a properly designed network

subject: Motion Detector / PIR Sensor
rule: Motion detector / PIR sensor must have a clear line of sight to the monitored area
conditions: sensor uses passive infrared (PIR) technology
sensor is stationary (non-rotating)
exceptions: sensor is combined with other detection technologies that do not require line of sight (e.g., ultrasonic, microwave)

subject: Motion Detector / PIR Sensor
rule: Motion detector / PIR sensor must not be exposed to direct sunlight or strong direct heat sources
conditions: sensor is PIR-based
sensor is installed indoors or outdoors without dedicated sun shielding
exceptions: sensor is specifically designed with active compensation and filtering for direct solar radiation, and manufacturer explicitly approves such placement

subject: Motion Detector / PIR Sensor
rule: Motion detector / PIR sensor must be oriented such that the detection axis is perpendicular to the expected direction of motion
conditions: sensor is PIR-based with Fresnel lens or segmented pyroelement
target is a person walking
exceptions: sensor uses a quad-element or multi-element array with omnidirectional detection pattern

subject: Glass Break Detector
rule: Glass break detector must be mounted on a rigid, non-vibrating surface
conditions: wall-mounted
ceiling-mounted

subject: Glass Break Detector
rule: Glass break detector must_not be placed behind sound-absorbing materials (e.g., heavy curtains, upholstered furniture, acoustic panels)

subject: Glass Break Detector
rule: Glass break detector must have a direct line of sight to the protected glass

subject: Glass Break Detector
rule: Glass break detector must_not be installed in areas with sustained ambient noise above the device's rated tolerance for the glass-break frequency band

subject: Electronic Lock / Magnetic Lock
rule: Electronic lock / magnetic lock must have a continuous and stable power supply to maintain its locking state
conditions: Electrically operated lock
fail-secure (power-to-lock) configuration
exceptions: Fail-safe (power-to-unlock) configurations where lock defaults to unlocked on power loss

subject: Electronic Lock / Magnetic Lock
rule: Electronic lock / magnetic lock must be mounted on a rigid, aligned surface with proper gap tolerance
conditions: Magnetic lock type (electromagnetic)

subject: Electronic Lock / Magnetic Lock
rule: Electronic lock / magnetic lock must_not be installed where ambient magnetic fields exceed the lock's rated tolerance
conditions: Proximity to large transformers, MRI rooms, or industrial induction equipment

subject: Electronic Lock / Magnetic Lock
rule: Electronic lock must have fail-safe/fail-secure behavior consistent with life safety code requirements for the egress path
conditions: Lock installed on a means of egress door

subject: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
rule: Card Reader / Keypad Reader must be mounted within the specified read range of the credential media (e.g., card or fob)

subject: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
rule: Card Reader / Keypad Reader must be weather-sealed to the manufacturer's IP rating when installed outdoors
conditions: installed outdoors
exposed to weather

subject: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
rule: Card Reader / Keypad Reader must_not be installed in a location where the keypad or reader face is exposed to direct sunlight more than the manufacturer's specification
conditions: reader model has optical or infrared components
reader model is not rated for high UV exposure

subject: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
rule: Card Reader / Keypad Reader must be connected to a power supply that matches the specified voltage and current ratings

subject: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
rule: Card Reader / Keypad Reader must_not have its communication wiring (Wiegand, OSDP, etc.) run in parallel with AC power cables without proper shielding
conditions: communication wiring is unshielded
parallel run exceeds manufacturer's specified distance
exceptions: shielded cable is used per manufacturer specification

subject: Biometric Scanner
rule: biometric scanner must have a secure enclosure that prevents physical tampering with sensor and processing components
conditions: when deployed in unsupervised public or semi-public areas
exceptions: scanner integrated into a supervised security checkpoint with constant human monitoring

subject: Biometric Scanner
rule: biometric scanner must_not have optical or capacitive sensor surfaces exposed to direct sustained sunlight above 45°C ambient temperature
conditions: scanner uses optical fingerprint sensor or capacitive sensor
exceptions: sensor is rated and tested for extended high-temperature operation per manufacturer specification

subject: Biometric Scanner
rule: biometric scanner must have a clear line-of-sight or defined contact area free of obstructions between the biometric trait and the sensor
conditions: scanner captures fingerprint, iris, face, or palm
exceptions: scanner designed for multi-modal capture where one modality compensates for obstruction of another

subject: Emergency Exit / Request-to-Exit Device
rule: Emergency exit / request-to-exit device must be connected to a fire alarm or security control system such that activation triggers an alarm
conditions: The device is installed in a building with a monitored fire alarm or security system
exceptions: Buildings not required by code to have a monitored alarm system

subject: Emergency Exit / Request-to-Exit Device
rule: Emergency exit / request-to-exit device must not be wired in a way that prevents manual unlocking or immediate egress from the inside
conditions: The device is installed on an exit door serving an occupied space

subject: Emergency Exit / Request-to-Exit Device
rule: Emergency exit / request-to-exit device must not require more than one releasing operation to exit
conditions: The device is installed on a means of egress door

subject: Emergency Exit / Request-to-Exit Device
rule: Emergency exit / request-to-exit device must have a means of defeating or bypassing the request-to-exit delay when the egress is for an actual emergency (e.g., immediate free egress upon panic hardware activation)
conditions: The device incorporates a delayed-egress feature (e.g., 15-second delay)
exceptions: Installations not under the delayed-egress provisions of NFPA 101 (e.g., non-egress doors)

subject: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
rule: Security camera must be mounted on a structurally adequate surface capable of supporting its weight and wind load
conditions: permanent installation
outdoor installation

subject: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
rule: Security camera must have an unobstructed line of sight to its target area
conditions: surveillance functionality is required

subject: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
rule: Outdoor security camera must be rated for the environmental conditions of its installation location (temperature range, humidity, ingress protection)
conditions: outdoor installation

subject: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
rule: Security camera must not be installed in a location where it violates jurisdictional privacy laws regarding surveillance of private spaces
conditions: applicable privacy regulations exist

subject: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
rule: Security camera power supply must match the camera's rated voltage and current requirements
conditions: wired power configuration

subject: Digital Video Recorder (DVR) / Network Video Recorder (NVR)
rule: DVR/NVR must be installed in a location with adequate ventilation and within specified operating temperature range
conditions: Unit contains internal cooling fan(s)
Device generates heat during operation
exceptions: Units specifically rated for extended temperature ranges (e.g., military/industrial grade)

subject: Digital Video Recorder (DVR) / Network Video Recorder (NVR)
rule: DVR/NVR must have a sufficiently rated power supply delivering continuous, clean power within specified voltage tolerances
conditions: Unit is mains-powered (non-PoE-only models)
exceptions: Units powered solely via PoE+ with adequate switch capacity

subject: Digital Video Recorder (DVR) / Network Video Recorder (NVR)
rule: DVR/NVR must not be installed in a location where condensation can form on internal components
conditions: Installation environment lacks climate control
Ambient humidity regularly exceeds 85% RH
exceptions: Units with conformal-coated circuit boards and sealed enclosures rated for high-humidity environments

subject: Digital Video Recorder (DVR) / Network Video Recorder (NVR)
rule: Hard drives installed in DVR/NVR must meet the manufacturer's specification for surveillance-rated (24/7 continuous write) drives
conditions: Unit uses replaceable SATA hard drives (not fully solid-state)
exceptions: Units with enterprise-grade SSDs rated for sustained write workloads

subject: Intercom / Video Intercom System
rule: Intercom / Video Intercom System must have a dedicated power supply (AC mains or Power over Ethernet) with appropriate voltage and current rating
exceptions: Battery-powered portable intercom units

subject: Intercom / Video Intercom System
rule: Intercom / Video Intercom System must have a minimum IP rating (e.g., IP54 for outdoor, IP20 for indoor) if installed in a location exposed to weather, dust, or moisture
conditions: System is installed outdoors
System is installed in a damp or dusty indoor environment
exceptions: System is installed exclusively in a conditioned, clean indoor environment with controlled humidity

subject: Intercom / Video Intercom System
rule: Intercom / Video Intercom System must have a continuous electrical ground path from the unit to the building's grounding electrode system
conditions: System is mains-powered (not PoE or battery)
exceptions: Class II (double-insulated) devices with no earth connection requirement

subject: Intercom / Video Intercom System
rule: Intercom / Video Intercom System must_not share a conduit with Class 1 (mains-voltage) power circuits unless separated by a listed divider or both circuits are functionally associated
conditions: System wiring is low-voltage (e.g., 12-24 VDC, Cat5e/Cat6 PoE)

subject: Intercom / Video Intercom System
rule: Intercom / Video Intercom System's outdoor station must have an operating temperature range that includes the local climate extremes
conditions: Any part of the system is installed outdoors
exceptions: System is installed in a climate-controlled enclosure

subject: Perimeter Fence / Gate with Sensor
rule: sensor must maintain a clear line of sight to its detection zone
conditions: sensor is optical (photoelectric, infrared, laser, or camera-based)
exceptions: sensor is non-optical (e.g., buried seismic, magnetic, or microwave fence sensor)

subject: Perimeter Fence / Gate with Sensor
rule: gate must not obstruct the sensor detection zone when in the open position
conditions: gate swing or slide path intersects the sensor's line of sight or detection field

subject: Perimeter Fence / Gate with Sensor
rule: fence height must be at least the minimum specified by applicable security standard or local code
conditions: fence serves a security or access-control function
exceptions: fence is purely decorative with no security requirement

subject: Perimeter Fence / Gate with Sensor
rule: gate motor and sensor wiring must be protected against mechanical damage and weather ingress
conditions: gate is automated

subject: Panic / Duress Alarm Button
rule: Panic / duress alarm button must be readily accessible and unobstructed at all times

subject: Panic / Duress Alarm Button
rule: Panic / duress alarm button must not be easily mistaken for a non-emergency control (e.g., light switch, thermostat)

subject: Panic / Duress Alarm Button
rule: Panic / duress alarm button must be wired or configured to remain functional during a general power failure

subject: Panic / Duress Alarm Button
rule: Panic / duress alarm button must not be installed in a location that is locked or otherwise inaccessible to the intended user during normal occupancy
exceptions: Exception for secure areas where only authorized personnel require duress capability, provided a button is placed inside the secure zone for those personnel.

subject: Field Controllers / PLCs
rule: Field Controllers / PLCs must be installed in environments within their rated operating temperature range
conditions: Controller is installed in conditioned or unconditioned space

subject: Field Controllers / PLCs
rule: Field Controllers / PLCs must be powered with the correct voltage and current rating as specified by the manufacturer

subject: Field Controllers / PLCs
rule: Field Controllers / PLCs must not be directly exposed to liquid ingress or continuous condensation
conditions: Controller does not have an IP/NEMA rating for wet locations
exceptions: Controller is specifically rated IP65/IP66/IP67 or NEMA 4/4X/6 for wet environments

subject: Field Controllers / PLCs
rule: Field Controllers / PLCs must have an enclosure providing protection against the ingress of solid particulates appropriate to the installation environment
conditions: Controller is installed in an environment with airborne dust, debris, or conductive particulates
exceptions: Controller is installed in a cleanroom or other controlled environment where particulate levels are negligible

subject: Sensors (Temperature, Humidity, CO2, Pressure)
rule: sensors must be placed within their specified environmental operating ranges for temperature, humidity, and pressure
conditions: sensor deployment in any environment
exceptions: sensors specifically rated for extended ranges with manufacturer documentation

subject: Sensors (Temperature, Humidity, CO2, Pressure)
rule: CO2 sensors must not be placed in locations with direct airflow from vents, open windows, or breathing zones of occupants
conditions: CO2 sensor installation in occupied indoor spaces

subject: Sensors (Temperature, Humidity, CO2, Pressure)
rule: temperature sensors must not be placed in direct sunlight or adjacent to heat-emitting equipment
conditions: temperature sensors used for ambient space temperature measurement
exceptions: sensors specifically intended to measure equipment temperature or outdoor solar-exposed conditions

subject: Sensors (Temperature, Humidity, CO2, Pressure)
rule: humidity sensors must not be placed in locations subject to direct condensation, steam, or water spray
conditions: humidity sensors used for indoor environmental monitoring
exceptions: sensors rated for wet/damp environments per manufacturer specification

subject: Actuators (Valve, Damper, Relay)
rule: Actuator voltage and control signal ratings must match the building management system (BMS) or controller output specifications
conditions: When connected to a BMS or digital controller

subject: Actuators (Valve, Damper, Relay)
rule: Actuator must not be installed in an environment exceeding its rated temperature, humidity, or ingress protection (IP/NEMA) limits
conditions: Outdoor, rooftop, mechanical room, or plenum installation

subject: Actuators (Valve, Damper, Relay)
rule: Actuator torque or force rating must be greater than or equal to the maximum required torque/force of the valve or damper it drives
conditions: When directly coupled to a valve stem or damper shaft

subject: Actuators (Valve, Damper, Relay)
rule: Actuator must be mechanically compatible with the valve or damper mounting interface (shaft size, coupling type, mounting bracket)
conditions: When physically coupling actuator to valve/damper

subject: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
rule: BMS control network cabling must be continuous and unbroken between the BMS controller and field devices
conditions: When using wired communication protocols (e.g., BACnet MS/TP, Modbus RTU)
exceptions: When using wireless communication as the primary medium between controller and device

subject: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
rule: BMS control network cabling must not exceed the maximum segment length specified for the communication protocol in use
conditions: For any wired bus topology (RS-485, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus)
exceptions: When using properly specified repeaters or active extenders that segment the bus

subject: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
rule: BMS control network bus must have proper termination resistors installed at both physical ends of the bus segment
conditions: When using RS-485-based protocols (BACnet MS/TP, Modbus RTU)
exceptions: When using protocols or device families that integrate internal termination

subject: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
rule: BMS control network cabling must not be run in parallel with power cables carrying 50V or more without proper separation distance
conditions: For unshielded twisted pair (UTP) bus cabling
exceptions: When using properly shielded/data-grade cable with grounded shield and adequate physical separation is achieved

subject: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
rule: Each device on a daisy-chained BMS bus must have the same polarity (A+/B- or similar) consistently wired across all devices
conditions: For all wired RS-485 bus topologies

subject: Building Energy Metering Hardware
rule: Building Energy Metering Hardware must be installed in a location that allows safe access for reading, maintenance, and calibration
conditions: metering hardware is permanently installed
exceptions: remotely-readable metering hardware with no need for physical access

subject: Building Energy Metering Hardware
rule: Building Energy Metering Hardware must not be installed in locations where ambient temperature exceeds the manufacturer's rated operating range
conditions: hardware is not specifically rated for extreme temperatures
exceptions: hardware is specifically rated and certified for the temperature conditions of that location

subject: Building Energy Metering Hardware
rule: Building Energy Metering Hardware must not be installed in locations where it would be submerged or exposed to standing water
conditions: hardware is not rated for wet or submerged locations
exceptions: hardware is IP-rated for wet/submersion conditions

subject: Alarm Annunciation Panel
rule: Alarm Annunciation Panel must be installed in a location that is continuously accessible to authorized personnel
conditions: panel is indoors
exceptions: small unmanned substations where remote alarming is provided

subject: Alarm Annunciation Panel
rule: Alarm Annunciation Panel must be powered from an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or backup source that maintains operation during mains failure
exceptions: facilities where local code explicitly permits loss of annunciation on mains failure and no life-safety alarms are annunciated

subject: Alarm Annunciation Panel
rule: Alarm Annunciation Panel must not be installed in a location where ambient noise exceeds the panel's audible alarm output rating
conditions: panel produces audible alerts
exceptions: panel is supplemented by a visual strobe or remote alerting device that satisfies the same detection function

subject: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface
rule: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface must be electrically supervised for integrity of all signaling and control circuits
conditions: system is active (not bypassed for maintenance)

subject: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface
rule: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface must not share control equipment or power supply with non-life-safety systems unless specifically listed for that purpose
exceptions: listed combination fire alarm/building control panels that are UL/ULC listed for life safety use

subject: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface
rule: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface must provide a visual and audible notification signal within 10 seconds of alarm initiation in every occupied space
conditions: occupancy group is assembly, educational, residential, or health care
system is in alarm condition
exceptions: spaces where NFPA 72 permits visible-only notification for sleeping areas with audible alarms in corridors

subject: Primary Structural Frame
rule: primary structural frame must support all dead and live loads imposed upon it
conditions: building occupancy requires load-bearing structure

subject: Primary Structural Frame
rule: primary structural frame must transfer loads to the foundation without exceeding material stress limits

subject: Primary Structural Frame
rule: primary structural frame must not have unresolved discontinuities in the load path

subject: Primary Structural Frame
rule: primary structural frame must maintain stability under lateral loads (wind, seismic)
conditions: building is located in a region with wind or seismic design requirements

subject: Secondary Structural Framing
rule: Secondary structural framing must be designed and rated to support all applicable dead loads, live loads, snow loads, wind loads, seismic loads, and other environmental loads specified by code
conditions: When used as part of the primary load path
When subjected to code-specified loading

subject: Secondary Structural Framing
rule: Secondary structural framing must not have any connections that are incapable of transferring design loads between members
conditions: At all splice, end, and intermediate connection points

subject: Secondary Structural Framing
rule: Secondary structural framing must be laterally braced or designed to resist lateral-torsional buckling under design loads
conditions: For long-span purlins and girts subject to compression flange buckling

subject: Secondary Structural Framing
rule: Secondary structural framing must not be fabricated from materials that lack minimum specified yield strength and ductility for the application
conditions: When specified by structural design documents and applicable material standards (ASTM, CSA, etc.)

subject: Bracing System
rule: bracing system must provide lateral load resistance in all primary structural directions
conditions: structural necessity
exceptions: temporary construction conditions where perimeter scaffolding or ground anchors temporarily provide lateral stability

subject: Bracing System
rule: bracing system must not create vertical load path discontinuity
conditions: when bracing elements interrupt gravity-load-carrying columns or walls
exceptions: when explicit load-transfer detailing (collectors, drag struts) is provided to redirect gravity loads around the brace

subject: Bracing System
rule: bracing system must be designed for both tension and compression forces in each braced bay
conditions: when using concentric bracing configurations (X-bracing, Chevron, etc.)
exceptions: tension-only bracing systems (e.g., rod-bracing) where slender elements are designed to go slack in compression but buckle elastically without damage — though these are limited to low-seismic or non-cyclic loading applications

subject: Roof Framing System
rule: roof framing system must have a drainage path that directs water off the roof surface
conditions: applicable to any building with a roof
exceptions: buildings with no roof (e.g., unroofed courtyards or open structures)

subject: Roof Framing System
rule: roof framing system must resist gravity loads (dead load + live load including snow where applicable) without exceeding member stress limits
conditions: applicable to any roof that supports load
exceptions: non-structural decorative roofs that carry no load

subject: Roof Framing System
rule: roof framing system must not allow condensation to accumulate within the assembly to the point of material degradation
conditions: applicable in climates where interior-to-exterior temperature differential creates condensation risk
exceptions: unconditioned buildings where interior and exterior conditions are equalized

subject: Floor Framing System
rule: Floor framing system must transfer all vertical loads to columns, walls, or foundations
conditions: For any occupied or habitable floor
exceptions: Floating floor systems in non-structural contexts (e.g., raised access floors)

subject: Floor Framing System
rule: Floor framing system must have deflection limited to prevent damage to brittle finishes and ensure occupant comfort
conditions: When supporting finished ceilings, partitions, or occupancy
exceptions: Industrial floors with no brittle finishes and no occupant sensitivity

subject: Floor Framing System
rule: Floor framing must not have spans that exceed the structural capacity of the framing members
conditions: For any span between supports

subject: Floor Framing System
rule: Floor framing system must provide lateral load resistance through diaphragm action or be connected to a separate lateral system
conditions: When the floor serves as the horizontal diaphragm of the lateral force-resisting system
exceptions: Floors in structures where lateral loads are resisted entirely by other elements (e.g., moment frames independent of the floor diaphragm)

subject: Foundation Connections
rule: foundation connections must transfer all building loads to the ground without excessive settlement
conditions: all buildings

subject: Foundation Connections
rule: foundation connections must maintain structural continuity between the foundation and the superstructure
conditions: all buildings
exceptions: seismically isolated buildings where controlled decoupling is intentional

subject: Foundation Connections
rule: foundation connections must not allow relative lateral movement between the foundation and the structure under design lateral loads
conditions: buildings not designed with a seismic isolation system

subject: Foundation Connections
rule: foundation connections must be designed to resist corrosion and environmental degradation for the intended service life
conditions: buildings in aggressive environments (coastal, industrial, high moisture)

subject: Foundation Connections
rule: foundation connections must not be constructed on frost-susceptible soils without extending below the frost line
conditions: buildings in cold climates where seasonal freezing occurs
exceptions: buildings where the foundation system is designed to accommodate frost heave (e.g., insulated shallow foundations)

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Structural steel connections must transfer all design loads (tension, compression, shear, moment) between connected members without rupture or excessive deformation
conditions: Connection is part of primary load path
exceptions: Temporary or construction-stage connections not carrying permanent design loads

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Bolted structural steel connections must not experience bolt shear failure or bolt tension failure below the factored design load
conditions: Connection uses bolts as primary fasteners

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Welded structural steel connections must not have weld fracture or inadequate weld throat thickness below the minimum required by code
conditions: Connection uses welded joints

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Structural steel connections must have sufficient ductility to allow inelastic deformation redistribution before brittle fracture
conditions: Connection is in a seismic force-resisting system
OR connection is subject to significant cyclic loading

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Structural steel connections must not have net section fracture at bolt holes below the tensile rupture strength of the connected member
conditions: Connection has bolt holes that reduce the cross-sectional area of a tension member

subject: Structural Steel Connections
rule: Structural steel connections must maintain dimensional fit such that all bolts can be inserted and tightened without excessive force that damages the connection
conditions: Connection is bolted

subject: Composite Decking
rule: Composite decking must have adequate positive drainage (minimum slope of 1/8" per foot)
conditions: used as exterior walking surface
installed over solid substrate or roof structure
exceptions: decking installed over spaced joists with open gap below (free-draining substructure)

subject: Composite Decking
rule: Composite decking must not be installed with zero or negative gap (no gap between boards)
conditions: solid-surface composite decking planks installed side-by-side

subject: Composite Decking
rule: Composite decking must not be fastened directly through the top surface into a metal substructure
conditions: using standard face screws (non-self-tapping)
metal substructure is standard-galvanized steel
exceptions: manufacturer-certified self-tapping screws specifically rated for steel substructure are used

subject: Composite Decking
rule: Composite decking must have a maximum cantilever distance not exceeding manufacturer's specified limit
conditions: decking extends beyond last support joist

subject: Trusses and Space Frames
rule: Trusses and space frames must have all members connected at nodes that resist both tension and compression
conditions: For any truss or space frame structure
exceptions: Cable-stayed or tension-only systems that rely entirely on cable elements

subject: Trusses and Space Frames
rule: Trusses and space frames must not use members that are susceptible to buckling under the design compressive loads
conditions: For compression members in any truss or space frame
exceptions: Members designed with sufficient slenderness ratio and bracing per structural codes

subject: Trusses and Space Frames
rule: Trusses and space frames must have a statically determinate or properly analyzed statically indeterminate layout with adequate load paths
conditions: For all truss and space frame configurations
exceptions: Structures where explicit second-order analysis accounts for all instability modes

subject: Trusses and Space Frames
rule: Trusses must not have pinned connections that develop unintended moments beyond their design capacity
conditions: For trusses designed with idealized pinned connections
exceptions: Connections specifically designed as moment-resisting or where joint stiffness is explicitly accounted for in analysis

subject: Corridor Lighting
rule: corridor lighting must be fed from a life safety or essential branch of the emergency power system in facilities required to have emergency lighting
conditions: facility has emergency power system
corridor serves as egress path
exceptions: corridor has no occupancy or egress function
local code permits battery-unit egress lighting in lieu of generator-fed branch

subject: Corridor Lighting
rule: corridor lighting must not be controlled by an occupancy sensor that turns lights off when no motion is detected for any period shorter than the code-required timeout for egress paths
conditions: corridor is a means of egress
exceptions: sensor has an integral override that maintains illumination during emergency mode
sensor is set to a code-compliant timeout (typically 15-30 minutes minimum)

subject: Corridor Lighting
rule: corridor lighting must provide a minimum of 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux) at the floor level along the egress path
conditions: corridor is designated as a means of egress
exceptions: local authority having jurisdiction specifies a different minimum illuminance level

subject: Ceiling Finish
rule: ceiling finish must have a smooth, continuous surface appropriate for the intended occupancy
conditions: when the ceiling serves as a finished interior surface visible to occupants
exceptions: exposed structural or industrial ceilings where the finish is intentionally omitted

subject: Ceiling Finish
rule: ceiling finish must be fire-rated to match or exceed the fire-resistance rating required by the building code for the assembly it is part of
conditions: when the ceiling is part of a fire-resistance-rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly
exceptions: ceilings in one- and two-family dwellings where code allows reduced ratings
sprinklered buildings where code permits trade-offs

subject: Ceiling Finish
rule: ceiling finish must not trap moisture against the substrate or within the ceiling cavity
conditions: when the substrate is moisture-sensitive (gypsum board, wood, or acoustical tile)
when the ceiling is in a humid or wet location (bathroom, kitchen, indoor pool, laundry)
exceptions: when a dedicated vapor-permeable assembly is designed and verified by a building science specialist

subject: Ceiling Finish
rule: ceiling finish must be securely attached to the substrate or suspension system to prevent falling hazard
conditions: all cases
exceptions: temporary installations for construction or events where daily inspection is performed

subject: Emergency Exit Sign
rule: Emergency exit sign must be continuously illuminated or self-luminous during building occupancy
conditions: building is occupied

subject: Emergency Exit Sign
rule: Emergency exit sign must be internally or externally illuminated to a minimum luminance contrast ratio against its background
exceptions: photoluminescent signs that meet UL 924 charging and discharge requirements

subject: Emergency Exit Sign
rule: Emergency exit sign must_not be placed where it can be obscured by doors, curtains, decorations, or stored objects

subject: Emergency Exit Sign
rule: Emergency exit sign must be connected to the building emergency or standby power supply
conditions: sign is electrically powered
sign does not contain self-contained battery backup meeting code-required duration
exceptions: self-luminous (non-electric) signs with no power connection

subject: Emergency Exit Sign
rule: Emergency exit sign must_not be mounted higher than the maximum allowable height above the floor

subject: Corridor Fire Door
rule: corridor fire door must have a self-closing device
conditions: door is installed in a means of egress corridor
door serves an occupancy other than a dwelling unit
exceptions: door leads directly to the exterior and is not required to be self-closing by adopted code

subject: Corridor Fire Door
rule: corridor fire door must have a fire resistance rating of at least 20 minutes
conditions: door separates a corridor from other spaces

subject: Corridor Fire Door
rule: corridor fire door must not be held open by a latch or device that prevents automatic closing upon fire alarm
conditions: door is equipped with a hold-open device
exceptions: hold-open device is connected to a fire alarm system and releases upon alarm or power failure

subject: Corridor Fire Door
rule: corridor fire door must have door sweeps or bottom seals to limit smoke passage
conditions: door is required to have a smoke and draft control gasketing by adopted code
building is equipped with an engineered smoke control system

subject: Corridor Fire Door
rule: corridor fire door leaf must not exceed 48 inches in width
conditions: door leads to a means of egress corridor

subject: Corridor Wall Base
rule: Corridor wall base must provide a continuous fire-resistance-rated seal at the junction between the corridor wall and the floor slab to prevent flame and smoke spread.
conditions: Corridor is part of a fire-resistance-rated egress path
Wall is a fire-rated assembly
exceptions: Where local building code explicitly permits unrated corridor walls (e.g., small buildings with sprinkler exceptions)

subject: Corridor Wall Base
rule: Corridor wall base must not obstruct required floor-level air gap or undercut for HVAC return air path when the corridor is used as a plenum.
conditions: Corridor is designed as a return-air plenum
Undercut or transfer grille is the engineered path for air movement
exceptions: When mechanical design provides an alternative return-air path (e.g., ducted returns)

subject: Corridor Wall Base
rule: Corridor wall base must be rigidly attached to resist lateral impact loads from stretchers, gurneys, carts, and wheelchairs without detachment.
conditions: Corridor serves a healthcare, institutional, or high-traffic public facility
exceptions: None — detachment creates a trip hazard and renders the base non-functional as a protective element

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail must have a height between 34 and 38 inches (864-965 mm) measured vertically from the stair nosing or walking surface to the top of the handrail gripping surface
conditions: handrail serves a stairway or ramp
applies to corridor handrails that are part of a required means of egress
exceptions: handrails on stairs serving dwelling units may be between 34-38 inches as well, but some jurisdictions allow variations when serving a single dwelling unit
if the handrail is on a landing and not part of a required egress stair, a different height range may apply

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail gripping surface must have a cross-section diameter between 1.25 and 2 inches (32-51 mm) or provide equivalent graspability profile
conditions: handrail is required by building code for egress or accessibility
exceptions: handrails with non-circular profiles that provide an equivalent gripping surface may have different dimensions if they meet graspability testing per code

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail must have a continuous gripping surface without obstructions that interrupt hand travel
conditions: handrail is installed along a corridor serving as a means of egress
exceptions: newel posts at turns or landings are permitted where the handrail continuity is maintained around the inside turn

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail must have a minimum clearance of 1.5 inches (38 mm) between the handrail gripping surface and any adjacent wall or surface
conditions: handrail is mounted on or adjacent to a wall
exceptions: none

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail must not project more than 4.5 inches (114 mm) into the required corridor width
conditions: corridor is a required means of egress with a minimum clear width per code
exceptions: projection is measured at the handrail height only; below the handrail the corridor must maintain full required clear width

subject: Corridor Handrail
rule: Corridor handrail must return to a wall, guard, or floor at both ends, or be terminated in a smooth and safe manner
conditions: handrail terminates in a corridor
exceptions: handrails that continue into a guard or are continuous around a stairwell need not terminate

subject: Corridor Floor Drain
rule: corridor floor drain must be at the lowest point of the corridor floor
conditions: corridor floor is sloped for drainage

subject: Corridor Floor Drain
rule: corridor floor drain must have a trap seal that remains primed
conditions: drain connects to sanitary sewer system
exceptions: drain discharges to a trapped indirect waste receptor

subject: Corridor Floor Drain
rule: corridor floor drain must not be installed in locations that require a gradient steeper than the maximum allowable floor slope
conditions: corridor serves accessible egress path

subject: Corridor Floor Drain
rule: corridor floor drain must have a removable strainer that is flush with the finished floor
conditions: drain is in an occupied corridor
exceptions: drain is in a mechanical/utility corridor not intended for pedestrian traffic

subject: Corridor Wall Protection
rule: Corridor wall protection must have a minimum impact resistance rating (e.g., impact test per ASTM or equivalent) to withstand cart and equipment impacts in the corridor
conditions: Corridor is used for patient transport or equipment movement
Wall protection is installed in a healthcare or high-traffic facility
exceptions: Corridor walls are constructed of a material inherently resistant to impact damage (e.g., reinforced concrete with no finish vulnerable to cracking)

subject: Corridor Wall Protection
rule: Corridor wall protection must not create sharp edges, projections, or snag hazards at any exposed edge or corner
conditions: Wall protection is installed in an egress corridor or accessible route
exceptions: Edges are located above 80 inches (2.03 m) from finished floor and not in an accessible path of travel

subject: Corridor Wall Protection
rule: Corridor wall protection must be continuous or have tight joints/seals to prevent moisture ingress behind the protection system
conditions: Wall protection is installed in a location subject to cleaning with liquids or where condensation may occur
exceptions: A fully sealed substrate behind the protection (e.g., continuous waterproof membrane) allows for drainage and drying without wall damage

subject: Corridor Ceiling Grid
rule: Corridor ceiling grid must align with corridor wall edges and maintain consistent module spacing
conditions: Continuous suspended ceiling is used in corridor
exceptions: Curved or non-rectilinear corridor layouts

subject: Corridor Ceiling Grid
rule: Corridor ceiling grid must be suspended at a height that accommodates corridor door head clearance and overhead MEP routing
conditions: Corridor has doors opening into it
Corridor contains overhead ductwork or piping

subject: Corridor Ceiling Grid
rule: Corridor ceiling grid must not have main tees or cross tees that interfere with sprinkler head spray patterns or smoke detector coverage
conditions: Fire suppression or detection devices are present in the corridor ceiling

subject: Corridor Smoke Barrier
rule: A corridor smoke barrier must form a continuous barrier from floor slab to the underside of the floor or roof slab above
conditions: When used as a smoke barrier in a corridor
exceptions: When the barrier terminates at a fire-rated ceiling assembly that itself provides continuity

subject: Corridor Smoke Barrier
rule: Corridor smoke barrier must not contain unprotected openings that permit smoke passage
conditions: When doors or other penetrations are present in the barrier
exceptions: Doors in smoke barriers may have required clearances if equipped with smoke gaskets or automatic-closing devices

subject: Corridor Smoke Barrier
rule: Corridor smoke barrier must have a fire-resistance rating of at least 1 hour when the building is equipped with an automatic sprinkler system throughout
conditions: When the corridor smoke barrier is part of a smoke control system or required by applicable building code
exceptions: Some codes permit lower ratings or no rating in fully sprinklered buildings; check local amendments

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must be readily accessible without obstruction
conditions: Cabinet is installed in a building
exceptions: Temporary obstruction during maintenance with warning signage

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must be mounted securely to a structural wall or support
conditions: Cabinet is wall-mounted

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must not obstruct egress paths
conditions: Cabinet is installed along a means of egress

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must have its operating instructions or signage visible
conditions: Cabinet contains a fire extinguisher

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must not be installed in locations where ambient temperature exceeds the extinguisher's rated range
conditions: Cabinet is installed outdoors or in unconditioned spaces

subject: Fire Extinguisher Cabinet
rule: Fire extinguisher cabinet must be installed with the handle between 1.2 m and 1.5 m above the floor
conditions: Cabinet is installed for general public use
exceptions: ADA-compliant alternate mounting heights for accessibility

subject: Corridor Kickplate
rule: corridor kickplate must be mounted at the bottom of a door or opening to protect the wall/surface from impacts
conditions: kickplate is installed on a corridor door or opening
exceptions: door without a solid wall surface below it (e.g., fully glazed floor-to-ceiling) or where kickplate is not part of the design

subject: Corridor Kickplate
rule: corridor kickplate must be fire-rated to match the door/frame assembly's fire resistance rating when installed in a fire-rated corridor wall
conditions: the corridor wall and door assembly are fire-rated, and the kickplate forms part of the door assembly
exceptions: non-fire-rated corridor walls or doors, or where the kickplate is applied as a non-structural overlay that does not compromise the assembly's rating

subject: Corridor Kickplate
rule: corridor kickplate must not project into the required egress path width
conditions: kickplate is installed in a corridor that serves as a means of egress
exceptions: kickplate is recessed or flush-mounted so it does not reduce the clear width below code minimum

subject: Corridor Glazing
rule: corridor glazing must not create a level change or step in the walking surface within the corridor
conditions: corridor serves as an accessible egress path
glazing is floor-to-floor or full-height
exceptions: glazing is set back from the path of travel and the walking surface remains continuous

subject: Corridor Glazing
rule: corridor glazing must be laminated or tempered safety glazing when it is within 18 inches of the floor and the corridor is a means of egress
conditions: glazing is within 18 inches of the finished floor
corridor is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: glazing is protected by a permanent guardrail or handrail that prevents human impact

subject: Corridor Glazing
rule: corridor glazing must not reduce the required corridor width below the minimum egress width mandated by code
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress
exceptions: projections such as handrails are allowed up to 4.5 inches into the required width per IBC

subject: Corridor HVAC Diffuser
rule: Corridor HVAC diffuser must be positioned within the ceiling grid such that its face is flush with or slightly recessed from the finished ceiling plane
conditions: installed in a suspended ceiling system
exceptions: exposed ductwork design where diffuser is intentionally surface-mounted

subject: Corridor HVAC Diffuser
rule: Corridor HVAC diffuser must not be located within 300 mm of a sprinkler head
conditions: corridor is sprinkler-protected

subject: Corridor HVAC Diffuser
rule: Corridor HVAC diffuser must be installed with its airflow pattern not directed toward a fire door or smoke barrier
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress

subject: Corridor Smoke Detector
rule: Corridor smoke detector must be listed and labeled in accordance with the applicable product standard (e.g., UL 268 or EN 54-7) for smoke detection

subject: Corridor Smoke Detector
rule: Corridor smoke detector must be installed on the ceiling or not more than 12 inches below the ceiling (NFPA 72 requirements)
exceptions: Where the ceiling is of a beam or coffered construction, alternative placement rules per NFPA 72 may apply

subject: Corridor Smoke Detector
rule: Corridor smoke detector must not be located in areas of high airflow (e.g., directly in front of supply air diffusers) that would delay smoke entry or dilute smoke concentration

subject: Corridor Smoke Detector
rule: Corridor smoke detector must have its spacing not exceed the maximum rated spacing per NFPA 72 (typically 30 ft on smooth ceilings, half that in corridors)

subject: Corridor Smoke Detector
rule: Corridor smoke detector must not be mounted in dead-air spaces near corners or where airflow is stagnant

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Head
rule: corridor sprinkler head must be positioned to provide unobstructed coverage of the entire corridor width
conditions: sprinkler head is installed in a corridor
exceptions: corridor width is less than sprinkler's listed coverage width

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Head
rule: corridor sprinkler head must not be installed within 12 inches of a wall or partition unless listed for such proximity
conditions: sprinkler is a standard spray sprinkler in a corridor
exceptions: sprinkler is specifically listed for close-wall mounting

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Head
rule: corridor sprinkler head must have clearance from overhead obstructions (ducts, pipes, lights) per its listing to prevent spray pattern blockage
conditions: obstructions exist below the sprinkler deflector in the corridor
exceptions: sprinkler is specifically listed for obstructed mounting

subject: Corridor Junction Box
