rule: Corridor junction box must have a sealed enclosure rated for the installed environment (e.g., IP44 or higher for outdoor/corridor locations)
conditions: Installed in any location where moisture, dust, or physical contact is possible

subject: Corridor Junction Box
rule: Corridor junction box must have a secured, non-detachable cover or lid fastened with screws or equivalent locking mechanism
conditions: Any installation where the junction box is accessible to building occupants or maintenance personnel

subject: Corridor Data Outlet
rule: Corridor data outlet must be connected to a suitable network backbone path (cable tray, conduit, or accessible ceiling plenum)
conditions: when located in a corridor that provides horizontal cable distribution
exceptions: when corridor has no accessible pathway infrastructure and alternate routing is used

subject: Corridor Data Outlet
rule: Corridor data outlet faceplate must be flush with the finished wall surface and not protrude into the accessible corridor width
conditions: when mounted on a wall in an occupied corridor

subject: Corridor Data Outlet
rule: Corridor data outlet must not be installed in a location where it will be subject to direct liquid splash or spray (e.g., directly above drinking fountains, adjacent to janitorial sinks)
exceptions: if outlet and connections are rated for wet/damp locations per NEC 110.11 and NEMA enclosure rating

subject: Corridor Electrical Outlet
rule: Corridor electrical outlet must be supplied by a branch circuit rated at least 15 amperes for 120V receptacles
conditions: outlet is in a corridor that is part of a building's interior circulation

subject: Corridor Electrical Outlet
rule: Corridor electrical outlet must not be located within 6 feet of a sink, bathtub, or shower
conditions: corridor contains a sink, bathtub, or shower within 6 feet
exceptions: GFCI-protected receptacles are permitted in certain locations as allowed by code

subject: Corridor Electrical Outlet
rule: Corridor electrical outlet must have a cover plate installed over the receptacle
conditions: outlet is installed and accessible in a finished corridor

subject: Corridor Electrical Outlet
rule: Corridor electrical outlet must be mounted at a height that complies with local building code (typically 12-18 inches from finished floor to center of receptacle)
conditions: corridor is in a building subject to adopted building codes
exceptions: ADA-required heights may differ for accessible corridors

subject: Corridor Thermostat
rule: Corridor thermostat must be located on an interior wall, not on an exterior wall
conditions: thermostat is installed in a building with conditioned corridor spaces
exceptions: corridor is unconditioned and serves only as a fire-rated passage

subject: Corridor Thermostat
rule: Corridor thermostat must not be placed near a heat source such as a radiator, supply diffuser, or kitchen exhaust
conditions: thermostat controls HVAC for the corridor zone

subject: Corridor Thermostat
rule: Corridor thermostat must be installed at a height between 48 and 60 inches above the finished floor
conditions: thermostat serves an occupied corridor where occupant comfort is regulated
exceptions: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) accessible controls requirement may specify a different height range (max 48 inches reach)

subject: Corridor Corner Guard
rule: corridor corner guard must be securely attached to the wall or corner structure
conditions: installed in a corridor
used as a protective bumper

subject: Corridor Corner Guard
rule: corner guard material must be able to withstand impact without fracturing or detaching
conditions: located in a traffic area where impacts from carts, equipment, or pedestrians are expected

subject: Corridor Corner Guard
rule: corridor corner guard must not protrude into the accessible path of travel beyond code-maximum projections
conditions: installed in a means of egress or ADA-accessible route

subject: Corridor Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: acoustic ceiling panel must be accessible for maintenance above the ceiling
conditions: when ceiling plenum contains building services (e.g., HVAC, electrical, plumbing)
when the corridor is part of a means of egress requiring ceiling access
exceptions: when a dedicated access panel or hatch is provided at regular intervals
when the ceiling is designed as a fully removable grid system

subject: Corridor Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: acoustic ceiling panel must not impede fire-rated corridor enclosure performance
conditions: when the corridor is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: when the ceiling assembly itself is fire-rated as part of the rated construction

subject: Corridor Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: acoustic ceiling panel must not shed fibers or particles that could contaminate occupied space
conditions: when the corridor serves healthcare, cleanroom, or sensitive occupancy areas
exceptions: when panels are specifically manufactured as cleanroom-rated or with encapsulated edges

subject: Corridor LVP Flooring
rule: Corridor LVP flooring must have continuous vapor barrier below grade or on concrete slabs in contact with ground
conditions: LVP installed below grade
LVP installed on concrete slab in direct contact with ground
exceptions: Slab has been tested and proven dry with no moisture vapor emission
Climate zone with no ground moisture concern (arid regions)

subject: Corridor LVP Flooring
rule: Corridor LVP flooring must maintain minimum expansion gap of 1/4 inch at all fixed vertical obstructions (walls, columns, door frames)
conditions: Continuous runs longer than 40 feet
Perimeter of any LVP installation
exceptions: Manufacturer specifies a different gap dimension for that specific product

subject: Corridor LVP Flooring
rule: Corridor LVP flooring must not be installed over subfloor with deflection exceeding L/360 under design loads
conditions: Any corridor LVP installation

subject: Corridor Epoxy Floor Coating
rule: Corridor epoxy floor coating must be slip-resistant (minimum coefficient of friction ≥ 0.5 when wet)
conditions: coating is applied in a corridor subject to foot traffic
coating may become wet from cleaning or spills
exceptions: corridor is permanently restricted to personnel in slip-resistant footwear only

subject: Corridor Epoxy Floor Coating
rule: Corridor epoxy floor coating must not contain or emit volatile organic compounds above regulatory thresholds during or after curing
conditions: coating is applied in an occupied or occupiable interior corridor
exceptions: corridor is sealed from the occupied building and all workers are using full supplied-air respirators with continuous air monitoring

subject: Corridor Epoxy Floor Coating
rule: Corridor epoxy floor coating must be coved up the wall at least 100 mm (4 inches) at the wall-floor junction
conditions: coating is applied in a corridor requiring wash-down cleaning
corridor serves a food, healthcare, or wet-process area
exceptions: the wall-floor junction is continuously sealed by a monolithic waterproof membrane rated for the same exposure

subject: Corridor Door Closer
rule: corridor door closer must provide automatic closure force to return the door to its latched position
conditions: door is installed in a fire-rated corridor
door is equipped with a self-closing device
exceptions: electromagnetic hold-open devices that release upon fire alarm activation

subject: Corridor Door Closer
rule: corridor door closer must not prevent the door from opening with a force exceeding allowable accessibility limits
conditions: door serves an accessible path of travel
exceptions: fire-rated doors where closing force is governed by fire code minimums, but must still comply with ADA maximum opening force limits

subject: Corridor Door Closer
rule: corridor door closer must have a backcheck feature that engages before the door reaches its fully open position
conditions: door is located in a high-traffic corridor
door opens into the corridor path of travel

subject: Corridor Door Closer
rule: corridor door closer must maintain latching speed adjustment to ensure the door fully latches without slamming
conditions: door is part of a fire-rated smoke barrier assembly

subject: Corridor Door Frame
rule: corridor door frame must have a clear opening width of at least 813 mm (32 inches) in the open position
conditions: applies to corridors serving an occupant load of 10 or more
applicable under most building codes (e.g., IBC, ADA)
exceptions: existing buildings undergoing limited alteration where reduction is permitted by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Corridor Door Frame
rule: corridor door frame must not reduce the corridor width below the required minimum width
conditions: door frame is located in a means of egress corridor

subject: Corridor Door Frame
rule: corridor door frame must not have a leading-edge projection of more than 100 mm (4 inches) into the corridor when the door is fully open
conditions: door swings into the corridor

subject: Corridor Partition Wall
rule: Corridor partition wall must provide minimum 1-hour fire-resistance rating
conditions: building is classified as a means of egress corridor
building is of combustible construction type
exceptions: building is fully sprinklered and local code allows reduction to 30-minute rating

subject: Corridor Partition Wall
rule: Corridor partition wall must not contain unprotected openings that permit smoke passage
conditions: wall serves a smoke-protected means of egress corridor
exceptions: openings are protected by smoke-rated doors or dampers

subject: Corridor Partition Wall
rule: Corridor partition wall must extend from the floor slab to the underside of the floor or roof deck above
conditions: wall is required to have a fire-resistance rating

subject: Corridor Partition Wall
rule: Corridor partition wall must have a minimum nominal thickness of 3½ inches (89 mm) when constructed of metal studs and gypsum board
conditions: wall is loadbearing or is rated for fire resistance
construction uses steel stud framing with gypsum board finish

subject: Corridor Threshold
rule: corridor threshold must provide a minimum clear opening width of at least the corridor width it serves
conditions: corridor serves as an egress path
threshold is part of a door assembly in a means of egress
exceptions: existing construction where alteration is infeasible and approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Corridor Threshold
rule: corridor threshold must not have a vertical elevation change exceeding 1/2 inch
conditions: threshold is part of an accessible route
exceptions: thresholds in existing buildings where compliance is technically infeasible and the change does not exceed 3/4 inch with beveled edges

subject: Corridor Threshold
rule: corridor threshold must be slip-resistant
conditions: threshold is located in a public or common area
threshold is exposed to moisture or exterior conditions

subject: Corridor Threshold
rule: corridor threshold must not create a trip hazard at the transition between different flooring materials
conditions: the threshold separates two different finished floor surfaces
exceptions: thresholds designed with a tapered or beveled transition that does not exceed 1:2 slope

subject: Corridor Threshold
rule: corridor threshold in a fire-rated corridor must be fire-rated to match the corridor wall rating
conditions: corridor is required to have a fire-resistance rating
threshold is part of an opening in a fire-rated wall assembly
exceptions: openings protected by an approved fire door assembly tested as a complete unit including the threshold

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Piping
rule: corridor sprinkler piping must maintain minimum 1-inch clearance from structural elements to allow for thermal expansion and prevent physical damage
conditions: when installed in concealed spaces
when routed through structural penetrations
exceptions: when listed sprinklers and piping have specific manufacturer approval for reduced clearance

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Piping
rule: corridor sprinkler piping must not obstruct the required egress width of the corridor
conditions: when corridor serves as a means of egress
exceptions: when sprinkler piping is installed above a ceiling that maintains full headroom clearance per code

subject: Corridor Sprinkler Piping
rule: corridor sprinkler piping must have hangers and supports spaced per NFPA 13 maximum intervals
conditions: for all fire sprinkler piping installations

subject: Landing
rule: landing must have a walking surface that is level enough to prevent occupants from falling
conditions: landing serves an occupied space
landing is at a change in elevation

subject: Landing
rule: landing must have a minimum clear depth of at least 36 inches in the direction of travel
conditions: landing serves a doorway or stairway

subject: Landing
rule: landing must not be obstructed by a door swing that reduces its clear usable area below code minimum
conditions: landing is at a doorway
exceptions: door does not swing over the landing

subject: Landing
rule: landing must be slip-resistant when wet
conditions: landing is exterior or in a wet area

subject: Balustrade
rule: balustrade must have a height that prevents a person from falling through or over it
conditions: when adjacent to a change in level greater than the threshold defined by applicable building code
on stairs, landings, balconies, mezzanines, and similar elevated surfaces
exceptions: handrails on stairs may have a lower minimum height where code permits

subject: Balustrade
rule: balustrade must have infill openings small enough to prevent a child's head or body from passing through
conditions: where the balustrade is located at a change in level that poses a fall hazard

subject: Balustrade
rule: balustrade must be capable of resisting the minimum design loads specified by applicable building code without collapse or excessive deflection
conditions: at all locations where a balustrade is required

subject: Balustrade
rule: balustrade must not have sharp edges, corners, or projections that could cause injury to a person
conditions: on any surface that could contact a person's body, especially hands and arms

subject: Nosing
rule: nosing must provide a detectable tactile warning where a pedestrian path meets a vehicular way at the same grade
conditions: tactile warning zone is required by accessibility code
path and vehicular way are at the same level without a curb
exceptions: vehicular way is closed to motorized traffic
path is separated by a curb of at least 2 inches in height

subject: Nosing
rule: nosing must not have a projecting lip greater than 0.5 inches beyond the riser below on a stair tread
conditions: nosing is part of a stair tread
exceptions: stair is not required to comply with accessibility standards (e.g., private residential stairs with fewer than 2 risers)

subject: Nosing
rule: nosing must have a minimum contrast of 70% light reflectance value difference from the adjacent tread or floor surface
conditions: nosing serves as a visual cue on accessible routes
exceptions: nosing is in a space not required to be accessible under applicable code

subject: Smoke Vent
rule: smoke vent must be located at the high point of a smoke zone or compartment
conditions: when used for natural smoke exhaust
exceptions: mechanical smoke exhaust systems may use ducts with inlets at any location

subject: Smoke Vent
rule: smoke vent must have a net free area meeting the minimum required by the applicable building code or fire engineering design

subject: Smoke Vent
rule: smoke vent must not be obstructed by equipment, ducts, or structural elements that block its opening or airflow path

subject: Smoke Vent
rule: smoke vent actuator or opening mechanism must remain operational at the temperature it will be exposed to during a fire
conditions: when the vent is power-operated or automatic
exceptions: gravity-drop or fusible-link devices designed for the temperature class

subject: Stairwell Wall
rule: Stairwell walls must be fire-rated with a minimum fire-resistance rating as required by building code (typically 1–2 hours depending on building height and occupancy)
conditions: Building exceeds a certain height threshold
Building is of a type requiring fire-rated enclosed exits (most commercial, multi-family, institutional, and assembly occupancies)
exceptions: Single-family dwellings or very small buildings where code does not require enclosed stairwells

subject: Stairwell Wall
rule: Stairwell walls must not contain penetrations that compromise the fire-resistance rating (e.g., unprotected ductwork, pipes, or electrical conduits that bypass fire dampers or firestopping)
conditions: Stairwell is required to be a fire-rated enclosure
exceptions: Fire-rated assemblies with properly rated penetration seals, fire dampers, or firestop systems that maintain the required fire-resistance rating

subject: Stairwell Wall
rule: Stairwell walls must be continuous from the lowest level to the highest level served, with no openings to other building spaces except through fire-rated doors
conditions: Stairwell serves as a required means of egress
exceptions: Where building codes specifically permit stairwell discharge through an exit passageway or directly to the exterior at grade

subject: Stairwell Wall
rule: Doors in stairwell walls must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: Stairwell serves as a required means of egress
Door serves an occupant load of 50 or more OR the stairwell is part of an exit enclosure
exceptions: Doors serving a very small occupant load (typically fewer than 50) in some jurisdictions do not require egress swing

subject: Stairwell Door
rule: A stairwell door must be self-closing or automatically close upon activation of the fire alarm system
conditions: The building is equipped with a fire alarm system
The stairwell serves as a means of egress
exceptions: Doors that are held open by electromagnetic devices that release upon fire alarm signal

subject: Stairwell Door
rule: A stairwell door must not be locked from the egress side (the side exiting into the stairwell)
conditions: The door leads into a required exit stairwell
exceptions: Doors in security-controlled areas where special egress hardware (e.g., delayed-egress locks) is permitted by code

subject: Stairwell Door
rule: A stairwell door must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: The stairwell serves an occupant load of 50 or more
Or the door is part of a required exit enclosure
exceptions: Doors in dwelling units or private stairwells serving fewer than 50 occupants where code permits inward swing

subject: Stairwell Lighting
rule: emergency stairwell lighting must remain illuminated at all times during building occupancy
conditions: building is occupied
stairwell serves as means of egress
exceptions: during testing or maintenance with alternative safety measures in place
when building is unoccupied and secured

subject: Stairwell Lighting
rule: stairwell lighting must not be controlled by a standard wall switch without override protection
conditions: stairwell is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: switch is a key-operated switch or a switch with a guard and is clearly marked for emergency personnel only

subject: Stairwell Lighting
rule: stairwell lighting must provide minimum illumination level of 10 lux (1 foot-candle) along the egress path at all times
conditions: stairwell is a required means of egress

subject: Stairwell Pressurization System
rule: stairwell pressurization system must maintain minimum positive pressure differential of 0.05 inches water gauge (12.5 Pa) across the stairwell door relative to the occupied floor when the door is closed
conditions: building equipped with mechanical smoke control system
stairwell designated as means of egress
exceptions: during commissioning or testing with all doors open and system operating in test mode

subject: Stairwell Pressurization System
rule: stairwell pressurization system must not allow the maximum pressure differential across any stairwell door to exceed the door-opening force limits specified in applicable building code (typically 30 lbf or 133 N at the door handle)
conditions: building is occupied
stairwell doors are used for means of egress
exceptions: where automatic door-opening devices or power-assist operators are provided to overcome the higher force

subject: Stairwell Pressurization System
rule: stairwell pressurization system must activate upon sprinkler water flow or smoke detection signal in the building
conditions: system is part of a smoke control system designed per NFPA 92

subject: Stairwell Pressurization System
rule: stairwell pressurization system must not introduce supply air at a temperature that could cause stratification or thermal discomfort exceeding code limits within the stairwell
conditions: heating or cooling coil is integrated into the pressurization fan system

subject: Stairwell Pressurization System
rule: stairwell pressurization fan must be located such that the fan intake is not exposed to outdoor wind pressures that could reverse fan flow or reduce delivered pressure below minimum required differential
conditions: fan intake is located on building exterior or roof
exceptions: where wind tunnel testing or CFD analysis demonstrates no adverse wind effect at the specific intake location under all prevailing wind conditions

subject: Stairwell Floor Finish
rule: stairwell floor finish must be slip-resistant
conditions: stairwell is a means of egress
finish is exposed walking surface

subject: Stairwell Floor Finish
rule: stairwell floor finish must have a class I or II flame spread rating (or comply with local code for enclosed exit stairs)
conditions: stairwell serves as a required exit enclosure

subject: Stairwell Fire Barrier Signage
rule: stairwell fire barrier signage must be constructed of fire-rated materials that meet the required fire-resistance rating for the barrier being penetrated
conditions: signage is attached directly to or penetrates a fire barrier

subject: Stairwell Fire Barrier Signage
rule: stairwell fire barrier signage must not reduce the fire-resistance rating of the barrier below code-required minimum

subject: Stairwell Fire Barrier Signage
rule: stairwell fire barrier signage must be permanently affixed and remain legible under smoke conditions

subject: Stairwell Fire Barrier Signage
rule: stairwell fire barrier signage must not obstruct the required egress width or opening of any fire door
conditions: signage is located on or adjacent to a fire door within the stairwell barrier

subject: Heat Exchanger
rule: heat exchanger must not have trapped air pockets in fluid circuits
conditions: when containing liquid working fluid
exceptions: self-venting designs with proper air elimination devices

subject: Heat Exchanger
rule: heat exchanger tubes must withstand maximum operating pressure without rupture
conditions: during normal operation
exceptions: none — pressure containment is fundamental to safe operation

subject: Heat Exchanger
rule: heat exchanger must have adequate thermal expansion accommodation
conditions: when temperature difference between shell and tubes exceeds material limits
exceptions: designs where materials have identical thermal expansion coefficients under all operating temperatures

subject: Circulation Pump
rule: circulation pump must be primed before operation to prevent dry running
conditions: pump is not self-priming
pump is located above the liquid source
exceptions: pump is a self-priming type
pump is submerged (below liquid level)

subject: Circulation Pump
rule: circulation pump must not operate against a closed discharge valve for more than a few seconds
conditions: pump is centrifugal type
exceptions: pump has a minimum flow recirculation line (bypass) that is open
pump has an automatic pressure relief or recirculation valve

subject: Circulation Pump
rule: circulation pump must have a net positive suction head available (NPSHa) greater than net positive suction head required (NPSHr)
conditions: pump is located above the liquid source
exceptions: pump is installed in a flooded suction configuration (liquid source above pump)

subject: Expansion Vessel
rule: expansion vessel must be installed with a volume at least equal to the calculated expansion volume of the system
conditions: when used in a closed hydronic heating or cooling system

subject: Expansion Vessel
rule: expansion vessel must have a pre-charge pressure equal to the system static pressure at the vessel location
conditions: when using a sealed pre-charged expansion vessel in a closed hydronic system

subject: Expansion Vessel
rule: expansion vessel must not be installed on the suction side of a circulating pump unless the vessel is sized for the lower pressure
conditions: in pumped hydronic systems
exceptions: if vessel is specifically rated and sized for suction-side conditions

subject: Expansion Vessel
rule: expansion vessel must be connected to the system at a point where the water temperature does not exceed the vessel's rated maximum temperature
conditions: in hot-water heating or solar thermal systems

subject: Hot Water Cylinder / Calorifier
rule: hot water cylinder / calorifier must have a pressure relief valve / temperature and pressure (T&P) relief valve installed on the vessel or its connecting pipework
conditions: closed-loop pressurized system
exceptions: open-vented (non-pressurized) systems that rely on a vent pipe to atmosphere

subject: Hot Water Cylinder / Calorifier
rule: hot water cylinder / calorifier must not be installed without adequate thermal insulation on the vessel body
conditions: unit is intended to store heated water for later use
exceptions: factory-insulated units where the insulation is integral and cannot be removed

subject: Hot Water Cylinder / Calorifier
rule: hot water cylinder / calorifier must have a dedicated cold water feed with a non-return valve (check valve) on the inlet
conditions: pressurized (mains-pressure) hot water system
exceptions: gravity-fed open-vented systems where backflow is prevented by the open vent

subject: Hot Water Cylinder / Calorifier
rule: hot water cylinder / calorifier must have an expansion vessel or an approved expansion relief arrangement if it is a sealed (unvented) system
conditions: sealed/unvented pressurized system
exceptions: systems where the pressure relief valve discharges to a tundish and drain is considered sufficient by local code, but only for very small cylinders (<15 L)

subject: Cold Water Storage Tank
rule: cold water storage tank must be located above the highest fixture it serves to provide adequate gravity pressure
conditions: gravity-fed system
no booster pump is used
exceptions: system includes a pressure booster pump

subject: Cold Water Storage Tank
rule: cold water storage tank must have an overflow pipe with diameter at least equal to the inlet pipe diameter
conditions: tank is connected to a mains water supply

subject: Cold Water Storage Tank
rule: cold water storage tank must have a watertight lid or cover
conditions: tank stores potable water

subject: Cold Water Storage Tank
rule: cold water storage tank must not be located directly above electrical panels or switchgear
conditions: tank is installed indoors
exceptions: a watertight secondary containment tray with leak detection is installed below the tank

subject: Cold Water Storage Tank
rule: cold water storage tank must have a properly-sized vent pipe to prevent vacuum collapse during drainage
conditions: tank is closed (non-atmospheric design) with a sealed lid
tank outlet is valved and can be isolated
exceptions: tank is fully open to atmosphere (no sealed lid)

subject: Piping Manifold
rule: piping manifold must have clear isolation valves on each branch to allow individual equipment shutdown without affecting other branches
conditions: manifold serves multiple equipment connections
system is designed for maintenance or repair
exceptions: single-branch manifold where isolation is provided upstream

subject: Piping Manifold
rule: piping manifold must not have dead-leg branches that exceed code-defined length-to-diameter ratio without flow provisions
conditions: manifold handles fluids that can stagnate or biogrow
system is subject to sanitary or process-quality standards
exceptions: temporary connections with documented flushing protocol
systems handling non-stagnating media such as dry gas

subject: Piping Manifold
rule: piping manifold must have pressure rating equal to or greater than the maximum system operating pressure at the manifold location

subject: Piping Manifold
rule: piping manifold must not create a trapped low point where condensate or sediment can accumulate without a drain provision
conditions: manifold orientation is horizontal or sloped downward toward a closed end
fluid handled may contain condensable vapor or particulates
exceptions: manifolds designed with continuous blowdown or purge system

subject: Valve Assembly
rule: Valve assembly must have a stem-to-disc connection that transfers torque without slipping
conditions: quarter-turn valve
rotary valve

subject: Valve Assembly
rule: Valve assembly must have a pressure-containing body rated for at least the maximum system design pressure
conditions: any pressurized piping system
exceptions: non-pressurized gravity drain applications

subject: Valve Assembly
rule: Valve assembly must not have internal flow passages smaller than the connected piping bore
conditions: full-bore or full-port valve application
exceptions: reduced-port/venturi valves where controlled pressure drop is intentional

subject: Valve Assembly
rule: Valve assembly must have a packing or seal system that prevents external leakage along the stem
conditions: stem extends through the pressure boundary (all conventional valves)
exceptions: hermetically sealed bellows-sealed or diaphragm-sealed valves where no dynamic stem seal exists

subject: Electrical Switchgear Panel
rule: Electrical switchgear panel must have a clearly marked nameplate or label indicating voltage rating, current rating, and fault current rating
conditions: panel is installed in a permanent location
panel is connected to an electrical supply

subject: Electrical Switchgear Panel
rule: Electrical switchgear panel must have an accessible disconnect means that isolates all ungrounded supply conductors
conditions: panel serves as service equipment or is fed from another panel

subject: Electrical Switchgear Panel
rule: Electrical switchgear panel must_not have any energized exposed live parts when the enclosure door is closed and secured
conditions: panel is installed and in service

subject: Electrical Switchgear Panel
rule: Electrical switchgear panel must be rated for the available fault current at its point of installation
conditions: panel is connected to a source of electrical power

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must be installed within its rated ambient temperature range
conditions: VSD is in operation

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must not be exposed to liquid ingress or condensing humidity
conditions: VSD is installed in a non-sealed enclosure
exceptions: VSD has a manufacturer-specified ingress protection (IP) rating suitable for wet environments

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must have its input power supply voltage within the manufacturer's rated tolerance
conditions: VSD is connected to mains power

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must be connected to a motor whose rated current does not exceed the VSD's rated output current
conditions: VSD is driving a motor

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must have its heat sink or cooling fan unobstructed to allow free airflow
conditions: VSD is air-cooled
exceptions: VSD is liquid-cooled per manufacturer specification

subject: Variable Speed Drive (VSD)
rule: VSD must not be installed in a location subject to continuous vibration exceeding the manufacturer's specified limits
conditions: VSD is mounted in a fixed installation
exceptions: VSD is specifically rated for high-vibration environments

subject: Fire Suppression System Header
rule: A fire suppression system header must be connected to a water supply or fire suppression agent source capable of delivering the required flow and pressure for the system it serves

subject: Fire Suppression System Header
rule: Fire suppression system header must have a rated pressure capacity at least equal to the maximum anticipated system operating pressure

subject: Fire Suppression System Header
rule: Fire suppression system header must not have closed valves or blockages between the supply source and the branch lines it feeds during normal stand-by operation

subject: Plant Room Floor Drainage Trench
rule: plant room floor drainage trench must have a continuous fall (gradient) toward the intended outlet to prevent standing water
conditions: trench is serving a plant room floor
exceptions: trench is designed as a level holding/containment system (e.g., chemical spill containment) where standing water is intentional

subject: Plant Room Floor Drainage Trench
rule: plant room floor drainage trench must be liquid-tight and not leak into surrounding soil or building structure
conditions: trench is cast in-situ or prefabricated within the building floor slab
exceptions: trench is an open drainage swale in a ventilated, non-occupied exterior plant area designed for infiltration

subject: Plant Room Floor Drainage Trench
rule: plant room floor drainage trench must not have any pipe or conduit crossing through it that would obstruct wastewater flow
conditions: trench is intended as a gravity drainage path
exceptions: crossing services are sleeved or encased in a manner that maintains the full flow cross-section and allows cleaning access

subject: Plenum / Pipe Duct Enclosure
rule: Plenum / pipe duct enclosure must not contain occupied occupancy or habitable space
conditions: When serving as an air return or supply plenum
exceptions: Fully sprinklered buildings where local code permits incidental occupancy

subject: Plenum / Pipe Duct Enclosure
rule: Plenum / pipe duct enclosure must be constructed of non-combustible materials or materials with a flame spread index of 25 or less
conditions: When used as a return air plenum as defined by mechanical code
exceptions: Fully sprinklered buildings with additional fire detection per engineered equivalency

subject: Plenum / Pipe Duct Enclosure
rule: Plenum / pipe duct enclosure must be sealed against air leakage and not connect to any adjacent non-plenum space through unsealed openings
conditions: When the enclosure forms part of a ducted air distribution system
exceptions: Exhaust or relief openings specifically designed for pressure equalization

subject: Acoustic Louver
rule: Acoustic louver must have free air path through its blades
conditions: When used for ventilation air intake or exhaust

subject: Acoustic Louver
rule: Acoustic louver must have acoustic infill material that does not obstruct airflow beyond rated static pressure loss
conditions: When sound attenuation is the primary design purpose

subject: Acoustic Louver
rule: Acoustic louver must not have blade spacing that exceeds the acoustic performance target for the required STC rating
conditions: When a specific STC (Sound Transmission Class) rating is required by specification

subject: Plant Room Ventilation Fan
rule: the plant room ventilation fan must be electrically connected to a power source
conditions: fan is electrically powered

subject: Plant Room Ventilation Fan
rule: the plant room ventilation fan must have unobstructed airflow path to both intake and exhaust openings

subject: Plant Room Ventilation Fan
rule: the plant room ventilation fan impeller must not contact the fan casing or housing

subject: Plant Room Equipment Base / Plinth
rule: plant room equipment base / plinth must be capable of supporting the static and dynamic loads of the mounted equipment without excessive deformation or failure
conditions: when supporting mechanical or electrical plant equipment
exceptions: temporary installations during construction before final equipment is placed

subject: Plant Room Equipment Base / Plinth
rule: plant room equipment base / plinth must not transmit vibration from mounted equipment to the building structure at levels that exceed structural or occupancy limits
conditions: when supporting rotating or reciprocating mechanical equipment such as pumps, compressors, or generators
exceptions: when equipment is specifically designed with integral vibration isolation that decouples the plinth

subject: Plant Room Equipment Base / Plinth
rule: plant room equipment base / plinth must have a minimum height above finished floor level sufficient to prevent water ingress into equipment
conditions: in plant rooms subject to floor washing, potential flooding, or where equipment is sensitive to moisture
exceptions: when equipment is rated for wet conditions and the floor drainage system provides equivalent protection

subject: Vibration Isolator / Spring Mount
rule: A vibration isolator / spring mount must be adequately loaded within its designed load range (typically 50-100% of rated capacity) to function properly
conditions: When installed as part of a mechanical or structural vibration isolation system

subject: Vibration Isolator / Spring Mount
rule: A vibration isolator / spring mount must not be short-circuited by rigid elements bridging between the isolated mass and the supporting structure
conditions: When installed to isolate mechanical equipment or structural elements from their support
exceptions: Temporary restraints used during installation or transport, which must be removed prior to operation

subject: Vibration Isolator / Spring Mount
rule: A vibration isolator / spring mount must have lateral stability or be provided with external lateral restraint to prevent buckling under horizontal forces
conditions: When the spring aspect ratio (height-to-diameter) exceeds 1.0 or when significant lateral loads are expected (e.g., wind, seismic)

subject: Fuel Oil / Gas Supply Line Termination
rule: Fuel oil / gas supply line termination must be located in a well-ventilated area to prevent accumulation of flammable gases
conditions: Fuel oil or gas supply line is present
Termination point is indoors or in a confined space
exceptions: Termination is directly connected to a sealed, vented combustion appliance

subject: Fuel Oil / Gas Supply Line Termination
rule: Fuel oil / gas supply line termination must not be located within 3 feet of any building opening (door, window, gravity vent, or combustion air intake)
conditions: Fuel oil or gas supply line terminates outdoors
exceptions: When local code permits reduced clearance with a listed gas vent terminal and engineered shielding

subject: Fuel Oil / Gas Supply Line Termination
rule: Fuel oil / gas supply line termination must be above the local snow accumulation depth or flood level, with a minimum elevation of 12 inches above grade
conditions: Termination is at grade or below potential snow/flood level
exceptions: Where the supply line enters a building below grade with a listed below-grade gas valve and sealed sleeve assembly

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must have a continuous, sealed passage from appliance to exterior termination
conditions: combustion appliance is connected

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must not pass through fire-rated assemblies without maintaining the fire rating
conditions: flue passes through a wall, floor, or ceiling that requires a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: approved firestop or fire-rated assembly system specifically listed for that purpose is used

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must be constructed of materials rated for the exhaust gas temperature of the connected appliance

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must not have an internal cross-section that is smaller than the appliance flue outlet

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must drain any condensate away from the appliance
conditions: condensing appliance (e.g., high-efficiency furnace or boiler) is connected

subject: Flue / Chimney Connection
rule: flue / chimney connection must maintain minimum clearance to combustible materials as specified by code and manufacturer

subject: Backflow Preventer
rule: Backflow preventer must be installed with the correct orientation (flow direction arrow aligned with actual flow)
conditions: backflow preventer is a line-size or reduced-pressure-zone type
system is pressurized
exceptions: non-mechanical backflow preventers such as air gaps have no directional requirement

subject: Backflow Preventer
rule: Backflow preventer must have a minimum clearance for servicing and testing, typically 12 inches below and 6 inches on each side for reduced-pressure-zone assemblies
conditions: assembly type (RPZ or double-check) that requires periodic testing and maintenance
exceptions: point-of-use backflow preventers installed at individual fixtures may have reduced clearance allowances per local code

subject: Backflow Preventer
rule: Backflow preventer must not be installed in a location subject to flooding or standing water
conditions: device contains test cocks, relief ports, or vent openings (e.g., RPZ, pressure vacuum breaker)
exceptions: fully submersible backflow preventers rated for flood conditions

subject: Backflow Preventer
rule: Backflow preventer must not be installed where ambient temperature can drop below freezing
conditions: device contains trapped water pockets (all backflow preventers with check valves or relief valves)
exceptions: units rated and listed for freeze protection
installation includes approved heat tracing and insulation per manufacturer specifications

subject: Drive Aisle
rule: drive aisle width must accommodate the design vehicle turning radius
conditions: when the aisle is used for vehicular access
exceptions: pedestrian-only aisles

subject: Drive Aisle
rule: drive aisle must have a minimum vertical clearance for the design vehicle
conditions: when the aisle is used for vehicular access

subject: Drive Aisle
rule: drive aisle must have a maximum gradient not exceeding the design vehicle's climbing/braking capability
conditions: when the aisle is sloped

subject: Drive Aisle
rule: drive aisle surface must not have an abrupt drop-off or step that exceeds the design vehicle's ground clearance
conditions: when the aisle is used for vehicular access
exceptions: where a speed table or curb ramp is designed to be traversable at low speed

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space floor must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: outdoor parking space
uncovered parking space
exceptions: indoor structured parking with active drainage system
parking space with permeable pavement surface designed for infiltration

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space must not have a slope exceeding 5% in the parking direction
conditions: parking space intended for passenger vehicles

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space must have a minimum width of 2.4 meters (8 feet) for standard parking
conditions: standard automobile parking space
exceptions: compact car spaces explicitly designated as compact
accessible spaces which require wider dimensions

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space must have a minimum length of 5 meters (16.5 feet)
conditions: standard automobile parking space
head-in or parallel parking configuration
exceptions: spaces designed exclusively for motorcycles or scooters

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space adjacent to a wall or column must have additional clearance of at least 0.3 meters (1 foot)
conditions: parking space bordered on one side by a wall, column, or solid barrier

subject: Parking Space
rule: parking space must provide a minimum vertical clearance of 2.1 meters (7 feet)
conditions: enclosed or covered parking space
parking structure
exceptions: spaces designated for low-clearance vehicles only (e.g., motorcycles)

subject: Guidance System
rule: A guidance system must maintain a clear, unobstructed path between the guidance emitter and the receiver/target during operation
conditions: Line-of-sight guidance (e.g., optical, laser, radio beam)
exceptions: Systems using non-line-of-sight guidance (e.g., inertial, GPS, terrain-reference)

subject: Guidance System
rule: Guidance system electronics and optics must not exceed their rated operating temperature range
conditions: Any guidance system containing active electronics or optical components

subject: Guidance System
rule: Guidance system must not have software timing that allows the controlled vehicle to reach a decision point before guidance computes the next command
conditions: Real-time closed-loop guidance (e.g., missile terminal homing, drone waypoint navigation)

subject: Guidance System
rule: Guidance system reference frame alignment must be consistent between the guidance computer and the vehicle's actuators
conditions: Any guidance system that outputs commands to vehicle control surfaces or thrust vectors

subject: Ventilation System
rule: ventilation system must maintain at least minimum outdoor airflow rate as specified by applicable building code or standard
conditions: when system is operational
for occupied spaces
exceptions: emergency shutdown conditions
fire/smoke control mode

subject: Ventilation System
rule: ventilation system must not recirculate air containing hazardous contaminants
conditions: in spaces with known contamination sources
e.g., laboratories, chemical storage, or areas with biological hazards
exceptions: if air is passed through HEPA or equivalent filtration that removes the contaminant

subject: Ventilation System
rule: ventilation system intake must be located away from sources of outdoor contaminants
conditions: all installations

subject: Ventilation System
rule: ventilation system must have a means of fire/smoke detection and automatic shutdown or mode change
conditions: when system serves multiple zones or floors
when required by applicable fire code
exceptions: systems in single-occupancy single-story structures where code does not require it

subject: Car Park Lighting
rule: Car park lighting luminaires must have a minimum ingress protection rating of IP65
conditions: Outdoor car park
Uncovered car park
exceptions: Covered/indoor car parks may use IP44 or higher

subject: Car Park Lighting
rule: Car park lighting must not be installed where the minimum mounting height is below 2.5 meters above the driving surface
conditions: Any car park accessible to vehicles
exceptions: Designs using专门 low-mounted bollard lighting systems with vehicle impact protection

subject: Car Park Lighting
rule: Car park lighting power supply must be protected by a residual-current device (RCD) with a rated residual operating current not exceeding 30 mA
conditions: Outdoor or semi-enclosed car park
exceptions: SELV (Safety Extra-Low Voltage) systems below 50 V AC

subject: Pedestrian Walkway
rule: Pedestrian walkway must have a minimum clear width of at least the value required by applicable accessibility codes (typically 900–1200 mm for two-way passage)
conditions: walkway is accessible to the public
walkway is intended for two-way pedestrian traffic
exceptions: walkways in single-occupancy private spaces with no public access

subject: Pedestrian Walkway
rule: Pedestrian walkway must have a slip-resistant walking surface
conditions: walkway is exposed to rain, snow, or moisture
walkway has a sloped surface
exceptions: temporary decorative walkways not intended for wet-weather use and clearly signed as such

subject: Pedestrian Walkway
rule: Pedestrian walkway must not have a step or single-riser change in level that is not accompanied by a ramp or alternative accessible path
conditions: walkway is on a primary accessible route
exceptions: walkways that are explicitly designated as stair-only routes with an alternative accessible path adjacent

subject: Pedestrian Walkway
rule: Pedestrian walkway must have handrails on both sides when the level change exceeds the threshold defined in building codes (typically 1 m in vertical rise)
conditions: walkway is a ramp or stepped walkway
vertical rise exceeds local code threshold
exceptions: walkways less than the code-specified rise

subject: Pedestrian Walkway
rule: Pedestrian walkway must have headroom clearance of at least 2.0 m (or applicable local code minimum) above the walking surface
conditions: walkway is covered or passes under an obstruction
exceptions: walkways explicitly designed for children only (e.g., in a children's museum) with appropriate warning signage

subject: Car Park Slab
rule: car park slab must be designed for vehicular live loads (minimum 2.5 kPa uniformly distributed or 9 kN per wheel, or local code equivalent)
conditions: slab is part of a multi-storey or ground-level open parking structure
vehicular access is permitted on the slab

subject: Car Park Slab
rule: car park slab must have a minimum concrete cover to reinforcement of 25 mm (or 50 mm if exposed to de-icing salts) per structural durability codes
conditions: slab is constructed of reinforced concrete
exceptions: if surface is protected by a bonded waterproofing membrane and a separate wear course, thinner cover may be accepted by a structural engineer

subject: Car Park Slab
rule: car park slab must not have a cross-fall or drainage gradient steeper than 1:50 (2%)
conditions: slab is an exposed upper-level or roof parking deck where vehicular traffic occurs

subject: Drainage System
rule: A drainage system must have a continuous gravity-driven flow path from collection point to discharge point
conditions: The drainage system serves a building or site
exceptions: Systems employing active pumping as primary conveyance (e.g., basement sump systems)
Vacuum drainage systems

subject: Drainage System
rule: A drainage system must not have its outlet at a lower elevation than any upstream invert where solids can settle
conditions: The system conveys solids-laden water (e.g., sanitary sewer, storm drain with debris)
exceptions: Systems with active flushing or grinder pumps that resuspend solids

subject: Drainage System
rule: A drainage system must be sized to convey the design storm event without surcharging above fixture drain inlets or floor drains
conditions: The system is a stormwater or combined drainage system

subject: Drainage System
rule: A drainage system must have at least one means of venting to prevent siphoning of trap seals
conditions: The system is a sanitary drainage system with plumbing fixtures
exceptions: Single-fixture systems where fixture is direct-connected to a vented stack

subject: Drainage System
rule: A drainage system must provide a minimum slope of 1% (1/8 inch per foot) for pipes 3 inches in diameter or smaller
conditions: The drainage pipe is 3 inches or smaller in nominal diameter
exceptions: Manufacturer-certified self-scouring velocity verified for lesser slope

subject: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal
rule: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal roof must have a drainage path to prevent water accumulation and structural damage
conditions: portal has a roof
roof is horizontal or near-horizontal
exceptions: portal is entirely open/uncovered with no roof element

subject: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal
rule: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal must have a minimum clear height that accommodates the tallest vehicle permitted in the facility
conditions: portal provides vehicular access
exceptions: facility has separate dedicated entrance/exit for oversized vehicles

subject: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal
rule: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal must not have a ramp slope exceeding the maximum drivable gradient for vehicles
conditions: portal includes a ramp for grade transition

subject: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal
rule: Car Park Entrance/Exit Portal must have a minimum clear width that accommodates the widest vehicle permitted in the facility plus operational clearance
conditions: portal provides vehicular access

subject: Ticket Booth
rule: ticket booth must have a weatherproof enclosure to protect occupant and equipment from precipitation
conditions: booth is outdoors
booth is staffed or contains electronic equipment
exceptions: booth is a virtual/unstaffed kiosk with no electronics requiring weather protection

subject: Ticket Booth
rule: ticket booth must have a clear visual opening or window for ticket transactions
conditions: booth is staffed for direct customer transactions
exceptions: booth serves only automated/remote transactions with no customer-facing interaction

subject: Ticket Booth
rule: ticket booth must not have a solid barrier that blocks all visibility between attendant and approaching customers
conditions: booth is staffed

subject: Ticket Booth
rule: ticket booth floor must be elevated above adjacent ground level or include drainage to prevent standing water entry
conditions: booth is outdoors
booth has a floor

subject: Bicycle Rack
rule: Bicycle rack must be securely anchored to the ground or wall to prevent tipping or theft
conditions: rack is freestanding or mounted in a publicly accessible location
exceptions: portable/event-only racks that are intentionally temporary and supervised

subject: Bicycle Rack
rule: Bicycle rack must not obstruct required egress paths or fire access routes
conditions: rack is placed near building entrances, sidewalks, or driveways

subject: Bicycle Rack
rule: Bicycle rack must provide a minimum of two points of contact with the bicycle frame for locking
conditions: rack is intended for secure public or employee bicycle parking
exceptions: racks designed purely as decorative elements or short-term event valet parking where bikes are attended

subject: Painted Line Marking
rule: painted line marking must be applied to a clean, dry, and prepared substrate surface
conditions: surface is to receive paint

subject: Painted Line Marking
rule: painted line marking must not be applied during rain, high humidity, or when ambient/surface temperature is below the paint manufacturer's minimum specified temperature
conditions: weather-dependent application

subject: Painted Line Marking
rule: painted line marking must have a minimum dry film thickness as specified by the paint manufacturer for the intended traffic or wear condition
conditions: marking is subject to vehicular or pedestrian traffic

subject: Vehicle Barrier
rule: vehicle barrier must be of sufficient height to block the target vehicle type
conditions: barrier is intended to stop vehicular intrusion
exceptions: barrier is only a visual/psychological deterrent with no stopping requirement

subject: Vehicle Barrier
rule: vehicle barrier must be structurally anchored to resist the design impact load
conditions: barrier is fixed/permanent rather than portable
exceptions: barrier is a free-standing temporary barrier relying only on mass and friction (e.g., water-filled jersey barriers)

subject: Vehicle Barrier
rule: vehicle barrier must not have sharp protrusions or edges at pedestrian-accessible surfaces
conditions: barrier is located in an area where pedestrians may be present

subject: Vehicle Barrier
rule: vehicle barrier must maintain a continuous load path from impact face to ground or structural reaction point
conditions: barrier is designed to resist vehicle impact
exceptions: sacrificial/crash-rated barriers designed to deform and be replaced after a single impact

subject: Private office
rule: Private office must have at least one operable door for egress
conditions: Occupied by one or more persons
exceptions: Spaces with direct ground-level openings to exterior that serve as alternative egress

subject: Private office
rule: Private office must be enclosed by walls or partitions that provide visual and acoustic separation from adjacent spaces
conditions: Designated as a private enclosed office

subject: Private office
rule: Private office must not have floor area less than the minimum required by applicable building code
exceptions: Existing buildings under grandfathered nonconforming-use provisions

subject: Open-plan area
rule: open-plan area must have at least one means of egress path to a fire exit or exit stair
conditions: occupant load exceeds 50 persons
space is located above or below grade

subject: Open-plan area
rule: open-plan area must have a floor-to-ceiling height of at least 2.4 m (8 ft) for habitable occupancy
conditions: space is designated as habitable or occupiable
exceptions: mezzanines or loft areas within the open-plan space may have lower clearance under specific code allowances

subject: Open-plan area
rule: open-plan area must have a smoke exhaust or natural ventilation opening area of at least 2% of the floor area if the space is not sprinklered
conditions: open-plan area exceeds 200 m² in floor area
space is not equipped with automatic sprinkler system
exceptions: mechanical smoke control system may substitute for natural ventilation

subject: Open-plan area
rule: open-plan area must not have an enclosed room with no natural light or ventilation wholly within the open-plan footprint without a dedicated mechanical supply
conditions: interior room exceeds 30 m²

subject: Meeting room (small)
rule: A meeting room must have at least one means of egress (door or unobstructed path to an exit)
conditions: room is occupied by people
exceptions: rooms less than 5 m² with direct access to an open-plan area that has its own egress path

subject: Meeting room (small)
rule: Meeting room must have a minimum floor-to-ceiling height of at least 2.1 m (or local code minimum)
conditions: room is intended for seated occupancy
exceptions: rooms with a historical/heritage exemption where the existing structure cannot be altered

subject: Meeting room (small)
rule: Meeting room must not have a floor area less than the minimum required by local building code for an occupied habitable room

subject: Office desk
rule: Office desk must have a horizontal work surface that is flat and stable
conditions: used for writing or computer work

subject: Office desk
rule: Office desk must be at a height that allows a seated user's forearms to be approximately parallel to the floor when typing or writing
conditions: designed for seated use
exceptions: standing desks that are height-adjustable

subject: Office desk
rule: Office desk must_not have sharp edges or corners at arm/leg height that would cause injury during normal use
conditions: used in a workspace where people sit and move their legs under the desk

subject: Office chair
rule: Office chair must have a stable base (e.g., five-point star base) to prevent tipping under normal seated use

subject: Office chair
rule: Office chair's seat must be able to support a static vertical load of at least the rated occupant weight without structural failure
exceptions: Specialized lightweight demonstration or display chairs not intended for occupancy

subject: Office chair
rule: Office chair must have a gas lift or height-adjustment mechanism that does not fail catastrophically (e.g., explosive decompression) under rated load

subject: Office chair
rule: Office chair casters must not detach from the base under normal rolling and swiveling loads
conditions: Chair is equipped with casters/wheels
exceptions: Chairs designed with fixed glides instead of casters

subject: Office chair
rule: Office chair must not have sharp edges or protruding components on surfaces contacted by the user during normal seated posture

subject: Reception desk
rule: Reception desk must have a clear leg/knee space height of at least 700 mm for wheelchair user access
conditions: if the desk is used as a check-in or service counter where visitors approach from the front
exceptions: If the desk is purely a decorative or back-of-house storage surface not intended for direct public interaction

subject: Reception desk
rule: Reception desk must have a work surface height between 700 mm and 800 mm from finished floor for writing and computer use
conditions: if the desk includes a seated workstation for a receptionist
exceptions: If the receptionist works exclusively at a standing-height station (counter height 900–1100 mm)

subject: Reception desk
rule: Reception desk must not have sharp edges or corners at accessible approach heights below 1000 mm
conditions: if the desk is located in a publicly accessible area
exceptions: None — this applies universally to any public-facing reception desk

subject: Reception desk
rule: Reception desk must have a minimum clear width opening of 900 mm for the receptionist's egress path
conditions: if the desk encloses the receptionist on three sides or has a gate/barrier
exceptions: If the desk is a simple open table with no enclosed area

subject: Presentation screen / whiteboard
rule: Presentation screen / whiteboard must be mounted at a height that allows a seated audience to see the full display area without obstruction
conditions: when used in a presentation or meeting room with a seated audience

subject: Presentation screen / whiteboard
rule: Presentation screen / whiteboard must not be placed where direct sunlight or strong artificial light causes disabling glare on the writing/display surface
conditions: when the board is used for writing or projection

subject: Presentation screen / whiteboard
rule: Presentation screen / whiteboard must have clearance in front that accommodates a presenter and at least one person's viewing distance without encroaching on egress paths
conditions: in rooms used for presentations or collaboration

subject: Conference table
rule: Conference table must have a level, stable top surface to support objects

subject: Conference table
rule: Conference table must have a minimum height-to-width ratio that prevents tip-over under typical lateral loads

subject: Conference table
rule: Conference table must not have sharp edges or corners at seated-user height that pose laceration or injury risk

subject: Conference table
rule: Conference table legs or support structure must be positioned to not interfere with standard seated knee and leg clearance

subject: Conference table
rule: Conference table surface material must be non-absorbent and cleanable to prevent permanent staining or bacterial growth
conditions: if the table is used in a food-and-beverage-permitted environment
exceptions: Tables in non-food meeting rooms where no beverages are allowed may use unfinished surfaces

subject: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet
rule: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet must be stable against tipping when fully loaded
conditions: freestanding unit
height greater than width
exceptions: unit is secured to wall or floor
unit is designed with anti-tip mechanism that engages automatically

subject: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet
rule: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet must not have doors or drawers that obstruct each other when opened simultaneously
conditions: unit has multiple doors or drawers
doors or drawers are adjacent or stacked
exceptions: interlock mechanism prevents simultaneous opening of conflicting doors/drawers

subject: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet
rule: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet must have a means to prevent drawers from being pulled completely out of the cabinet
conditions: unit has full-extension or pull-out drawers
exceptions: drawers are designed to be removable for service and have a release mechanism that requires deliberate action

subject: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet
rule: Storage cabinet / filing cabinet must have handles or pulls that provide sufficient grip for the intended load
conditions: unit has drawers or doors weighing more than 5 kg when fully loaded
exceptions: unit uses push-to-open or electronic release mechanism

subject: Raised access floor
rule: raised access floor panels must be capable of supporting the design live load without excessive deflection or failure
conditions: when the raised access floor is used to support occupiable loads or equipment
exceptions: when the floor is designated as non-load-bearing decorative/access-only

subject: Raised access floor
rule: pedestal and understructure system must provide adequate stability against lateral overturning or buckling under design loads
conditions: when pedestal-mounted raised access floor exceeds 150 mm in height or supports significant lateral loads
exceptions: low-height pedestal systems (under 150 mm) with full perimeter support may not require independent lateral bracing

subject: Raised access floor
rule: raised access floor must not be installed directly over a floor drain without a sealed, grated, or otherwise protected cover that prevents objects falling into the drain
conditions: when a floor drain exists in the subfloor directly beneath the raised access floor
exceptions: when the drain is sealed and rendered permanently inoperable, or when the raised floor panel above the drain is designed as a non-removable, load-rated cover

subject: Raised access floor
rule: raised access floor must provide a minimum clearance height between subfloor and underside of panels that accommodates all routed services (cables, conduits, piping) without compression or crushing
conditions: when the plenum space is used for routing of building services
exceptions: when the plenum is intentionally left empty

subject: Suspended ceiling system
rule: A suspended ceiling system must have a minimum clearance (plenum space) of at least 3 inches (76 mm) between the top of the ceiling grid and the bottom of the structure above
conditions: Ceiling is installed below a structural floor or roof deck
Plenum is used for any building services (electrical, mechanical, plumbing)
exceptions: The structure above is itself a finished ceiling surface with no services in the cavity

subject: Suspended ceiling system
rule: The suspended ceiling grid must be laterally braced to resist seismic forces in seismically active regions
conditions: Building is located in Seismic Design Category C, D, E, or F per ASCE 7
Ceiling area exceeds 144 square feet (13.4 m²)
exceptions: Ceiling is designed as a free-floating system with documented seismic isolation per code

subject: Suspended ceiling system
rule: A suspended ceiling system must not be used as a structural support platform for equipment, ductwork, or piping
conditions: Ceiling grid is standard lay-in type (non-engineered support system)
exceptions: The ceiling system is specifically engineered and rated for additional loads, with documented structural capacity and manufacturer approval

subject: Suspended ceiling system
rule: The hanger wires of a suspended ceiling system must be attached to the structure above (not to other ceiling components, ducts, pipes, or mechanical systems)
conditions: System uses wire-hanger suspension method
exceptions: Alternate engineered suspension system with full structural analysis and building official approval

subject: Suspended ceiling system
rule: A suspended ceiling in a fire-resistance-rated assembly must be installed with listed fire-resistant materials and maintain the required fire rating continuity
conditions: Ceiling is part of a rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly
Building code requires fire-rated separation
exceptions: The ceiling is not part of a rated assembly (e.g., purely aesthetic with no fire-resistance requirement)

subject: Cable tray / conduit
rule: Cable tray / conduit must not have sharp edges or burrs that can damage cable insulation
conditions: applicable to all metallic cable trays and conduits
exceptions: if edges are properly deburred or covered with protective bushings

subject: Cable tray / conduit
rule: Cable tray / conduit must be electrically continuous and properly grounded
conditions: when used as an equipment grounding conductor per code
exceptions: when separate grounding conductor is provided and the tray is not relied upon for ground path

subject: Cable tray / conduit
rule: Cable tray / conduit must not exceed manufacturer's maximum allowable fill ratio
conditions: for power and lighting cables

subject: Cable tray / conduit
rule: Cable tray / conduit must be installed with proper supports at intervals not exceeding code-prescribed spacing
conditions: for all cable tray and conduit runs

subject: Cable tray / conduit
rule: Cable tray / conduit must not be installed in locations where ambient temperature exceeds its rated temperature limit
exceptions: if thermal insulation or heat shielding is provided to keep the component within its rated temperature

subject: Fire alarm device
rule: Fire alarm device must be connected to a verified continuous power source (mains or battery backup)
conditions: when installed as a life-safety system component
exceptions: None — standalone non-safety equipment exempt but this is a fire alarm device

subject: Fire alarm device
rule: Fire alarm device must not be installed in locations where ambient temperature exceeds its rated operating range
conditions: when installed in any building environment
exceptions: Devices specifically listed/rated for high-temperature environments (e.g., heat detectors rated for boiler rooms)

subject: Fire alarm device
rule: Fire alarm device must not be obstructed by building elements or furnishings that impair detection or notification coverage
conditions: for smoke detectors, heat detectors, and audible/visual notification appliances
exceptions: None — NFPA 72 and equivalent codes mandate clear space (typically 18–24 inches) around devices

subject: Fire alarm device
rule: Fire alarm device must be installed at a maximum spacing compliant with applicable code (e.g., NFPA 72, EN 54) for its type
conditions: for spot-type smoke detectors, heat detectors, and sprinkler flow switches
exceptions: None — spacing limits are prescriptive code requirements

subject: Power outlet / data jack
rule: power outlet or data jack must have proper grounding for safety
conditions: power outlet is installed

subject: Power outlet / data jack
rule: power outlet must not be installed within a specified minimum distance from a water source or in a wet location without appropriate weatherproofing
conditions: power outlet is in a bathroom, kitchen, outdoors, or other wet/damp location
exceptions: outlet is GFCI-protected and rated for wet/damp locations as per code

subject: Power outlet / data jack
rule: data jack must be installed with proper clearance from high-voltage power lines or power outlets to avoid electromagnetic interference and safety hazards
conditions: data jack is installed in the same wall box or within a defined minimum separation distance from AC power wiring
exceptions: jack uses shielded cabling and separated raceways per code

subject: Power outlet / data jack
rule: power outlet must be rated for the electrical load and voltage of the circuit it serves
conditions: outlet is connected to a branch circuit

subject: Window / curtain wall (office)
rule: Window / curtain wall (office) must provide a weather-tight seal against air and water infiltration at all perimeter joints
conditions: when installed as an exterior building enclosure component
exceptions: temporary or mockup installations not intended for occupancy

subject: Window / curtain wall (office)
rule: Window / curtain wall (office) must have a minimum safety glass type (tempered or laminated) where the glazed area is subject to human impact or thermal stress
conditions: when glazing is located within 600 mm of a walking surface
when glazing is in a door or sidelight
when glazing area exceeds 1.5 m²
exceptions: annealed glass in fully protected locations where no human impact is possible

subject: Window / curtain wall (office)
rule: Window / curtain wall (office) must not have continuous thermal bridging across the insulated envelope through its frame assembly
conditions: when the curtain wall or window forms part of the conditioned building envelope
exceptions: thermally broken assemblies where the frame incorporates an insulating polymer barrier between interior and exterior metal

subject: Window / curtain wall (office)
rule: Window / curtain wall (office) must be structurally anchored to the building structure to transfer wind load and self-weight without failure
conditions: for all permanent installations

subject: Interior door (office)
rule: Interior door (office) must have a minimum clear opening width of 0.81 m (32 inches) for accessibility
conditions: When the door serves an accessible path of travel
Where building codes require accessible egress
exceptions: Doors in existing buildings where alteration is infeasible and alternative accessible routes are available

subject: Interior door (office)
rule: Interior door (office) must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: When the door serves as an exit access door
When the room has an occupant load greater than 50 people
exceptions: Doors not serving as exit access or egress components

subject: Interior door (office)
rule: Interior door (office) must not have a locking mechanism that requires special knowledge or tools to unlock from the egress side
conditions: When the door is used for egress
When the door is in a means of egress path
exceptions: Doors serving storage or utility rooms not on an egress path

subject: Window blind / shade
rule: window blind or shade must not obstruct emergency egress or fire escape routes
conditions: when installed in a room used for occupancy
when the window serves as an emergency escape or rescue opening
exceptions: blinds or shades that automatically retract or release upon fire alarm activation
blinds or shades that can be fully opened or removed without tools and with a single operation

subject: Window blind / shade
rule: window blind or shade must maintain adequate clearance from heat sources such as radiators, baseboard heaters, or space heaters
conditions: when installed near a heat source that reaches surface temperatures above 60°C (140°F)
exceptions: blinds or shades made of non-combustible or fire-rated materials certified for use above heat sources

subject: Window blind / shade
rule: window blind must not have accessible looped cords or chains when installed in a location accessible to young children
conditions: in any childcare facility, preschool, nursery, or residential setting where children under 6 years old may be present
exceptions: cordless blinds or shades
blinds with inaccessible or breakaway cords that meet ASTM F4004 or EN 13120 safety standards

subject: Window blind / shade
rule: motorized window blind or shade must be connected to a power supply with ground-fault circuit-interrupter (GFCI) protection when installed within 1.8 m (6 ft) of a water source
conditions: when the blind or shade is motorized and electrically powered
when the installation location is within 1.8 m of a sink, bathtub, shower, or other plumbing fixture
exceptions: battery-powered motorized blinds with no mains electrical connection

subject: Water Closet (WC) / Toilet Bowl
rule: Water closet bowl must have a trap (integral or connected) to maintain a water seal that prevents sewer gas ingress
conditions: connected to building drainage system

subject: Water Closet (WC) / Toilet Bowl
rule: Water closet bowl must have a rim or internal passages that allow flushing water to clear waste from the bowl surface

subject: Water Closet (WC) / Toilet Bowl
rule: Water closet bowl must not have a discharge outlet smaller than the minimum required by code (typically 3-inch nominal) for soil/waste drainage
conditions: connected to building drainage system

subject: Lavatory / Sink
rule: Lavatory sink drain outlet must be connected to a sanitary drainage system
conditions: sink is installed and operational

subject: Lavatory / Sink
rule: Lavatory sink waste pipe must have a trap (P-trap or S-trap) to prevent sewer gases from entering the building
conditions: sink is connected to a drainage system

subject: Lavatory / Sink
rule: Lavatory sink supply lines must not be connected to a wastewater or drainage pipe
conditions: sink is connected to any piping system

subject: Lavatory / Sink
rule: Lavatory sink must have a vent connected to the drain system to prevent siphonage of the trap seal
conditions: sink drain is connected to a drainage system
exceptions: sink may use an air admittance valve (AAV) as an alternative to a conventional vent

subject: Lavatory / Sink
rule: Lavatory sink bowl must be watertight with no leaks through joints or the basin itself
conditions: sink is intended to hold or convey water

subject: Grab Bar
rule: grab bar must be anchored to a structural substrate capable of supporting the maximum applied load (typically 250 lb minimum) without failure
conditions: installed in a wet or accessible location
required by accessibility code
exceptions: temporary or non-load-bearing decorative grab bars not intended for weight support

subject: Grab Bar
rule: grab bar must have a slip-resistant gripping surface
conditions: located in a wet environment such as a shower or pool area

subject: Grab Bar
rule: grab bar must not have sharp edges or protrusions that could cause injury

subject: Grab Bar
rule: grab bar must have a minimum clearance from the wall (typically 1.5 inches) to allow hand grip
exceptions: recessed or flush-mounted grab bar designs where finger clearance is achieved by an alternative geometry

subject: Toilet Paper Dispenser
rule: toilet paper dispenser must be mounted at a height that allows users to reach the toilet paper
conditions: when installed in a toilet stall or restroom

subject: Toilet Paper Dispenser
rule: toilet paper dispenser must not block the toilet or adjacent fixtures
conditions: when installed adjacent to a toilet

subject: Soap Dispenser
rule: soap dispenser must be positioned above or adjacent to a sink or washbasin
conditions: when installed in a hand-washing environment
exceptions: automatic touchless dispensers in public spaces may be freestanding with integrated drip tray

subject: Soap Dispenser
rule: soap dispenser must not leak at any connection point or seam under normal operating pressure
conditions: when containing liquid soap

subject: Soap Dispenser
rule: soap dispenser must have a refill or replacement mechanism accessible without destructive disassembly
conditions: when designed for more than one use
exceptions: single-use/disposable dispensers

subject: Waste Receptacle
rule: waste receptacle must have an opening large enough to accept the intended waste type
conditions: intended waste type is known
exceptions: sealed/contained hazardous waste receptacles that are not user-loadable

subject: Waste Receptacle
rule: waste receptacle must not have openings that allow unintended escape of contained waste
exceptions: receptacles designed for composting aeration where controlled airflow is intentional

subject: Waste Receptacle
rule: waste receptacle must have a base that provides stability against tipping under expected load
conditions: receptacle is freestanding and not permanently mounted
exceptions: receptacles designed to be structurally integrated into a larger assembly that provides stability

subject: Shower Stall
rule: Shower stall floor/membrane must have continuous slope to drain
conditions: shower stall is intended to collect and drain water
exceptions: stall designed as a dry/utility shower that drains through a grated floor without membrane slope

subject: Shower Stall
