exceptions: screens designed for laser projection with very narrow viewing angles or specialized high-gain applications where a specular component is intentional

subject: Projection Screen
rule: Projection screen gain must be ≥ 0.8
conditions: any projection screen used with a standard projector (non-self-illuminating)

subject: Built-in Credenza / Media Cabinet
rule: Built-in Credenza / Media Cabinet must be laterally braced or anchored to prevent tipping under lateral load
conditions: When installed as a freestanding or floor-mounted unit taller than 30 inches (762 mm) above finished floor
exceptions: Unit is installed between two walls or other fixed elements that prevent lateral movement in both directions

subject: Built-in Credenza / Media Cabinet
rule: Built-in Credenza / Media Cabinet must not have combustible materials (e.g., untreated wood, foam) directly in contact with a heat source such as a recessed fireplace, radiator, or HVAC register built into the cabinet cavity
conditions: When the unit encloses or is adjacent to a heat-producing appliance or building service
exceptions: Heat source is listed for zero-clearance installation and manufacturer's instructions permit direct contact with cabinet materials
A code-compliant thermal barrier (e.g., Type X gypsum, air gap with proper ventilation) is provided between the heat source and combustible cabinet components

subject: Cable Management System
rule: cable management system must not exceed the cable bend radius specified by the cable manufacturer
conditions: cable is bent during installation or operation
exceptions: cables specifically designed for repeated tight bending such as some flexible cords

subject: Cable Management System
rule: cable management system must support the self-weight of all installed cables plus applicable ice loading without collapse
conditions: system is installed in an outdoor or unconditioned environment subject to ice accumulation
exceptions: indoor-only installations where ice loading is not possible

subject: Cable Management System
rule: cable management system must not impose compressive or tensile forces on cable connections that exceed the connector manufacturer's rated pull-out force
conditions: cables are terminated with mechanical connectors or lugs at equipment
exceptions: cables that use strain-relief clamps independent of the cable management system

subject: Window Blinds / Motorized Shades
rule: Motorized shades must have a power supply (hardwired or battery) to operate
exceptions: Manually operated blinds/shades without motorization

subject: Window Blinds / Motorized Shades
rule: Window blinds/shades must be mounted on a structurally adequate support surface (wall, ceiling, or window frame)

subject: Window Blinds / Motorized Shades
rule: Motorized shades must not have their motor or wiring exposed to direct water spray or immersion
conditions: shades are motorized
exceptions: Specially rated outdoor/waterproof motorized shades with IP-rated motors and sealed enclosures

subject: Window Blinds / Motorized Shades
rule: Blind/shade width must not exceed the structural capacity of the mounting brackets and fasteners

subject: Floor Box / Power Outlet
rule: floor box / power outlet must be installed in a location that is accessible for maintenance and use
conditions: when installed in floors such as concrete slabs or raised access flooring
exceptions: when the outlet is installed in a wall box rather than a floor box

subject: Floor Box / Power Outlet
rule: floor box / power outlet must not be installed where it will be exposed to standing or pooling water
conditions: when installed outdoors or in wet/damp interior locations (e.g., basements, wash-down areas)
exceptions: when the product is specifically rated and listed for wet locations (e.g., UL wet-rated floor box with sealed cover)

subject: Floor Box / Power Outlet
rule: floor box / power outlet must have a cover or lid that is flush with the finished floor surface
conditions: when installed in a walking surface floor area
exceptions: when installed in a non-traffic area such as under fixed equipment where tripping is not a hazard

subject: Floor Box / Power Outlet
rule: floor box / power outlet must not be installed such that it compromises the fire-resistance rating of the floor assembly
conditions: when installed through a fire-rated floor slab or deck
exceptions: when the floor box assembly is listed and installed with approved firestop systems preserving the rating

subject: Room Sound Masking System
rule: Room Sound Masking System must produce a sound spectrum that is statistically uniform across the covered frequency range (typically 125–8000 Hz)
conditions: when system is installed and operational
exceptions: temporary system tuning or commissioning periods

subject: Room Sound Masking System
rule: Room Sound Masking System must maintain sound pressure level within ±1.5 dB of the target level at all listener positions in the covered zone
conditions: after final calibration and under normal HVAC operation

subject: Room Sound Masking System
rule: Room Sound Masking System must not produce audible tones, harmonics, or periodic modulations in the occupied space
conditions: when system is operating in normal mode

subject: HVAC Zone Damper / Thermostat
rule: HVAC zone damper must be electrically or pneumatically actuated to open and close in response to thermostat or building management system signals
conditions: When used in a forced-air HVAC system with zone control
exceptions: Manual dampers in strictly manually-controlled zones

subject: HVAC Zone Damper / Thermostat
rule: HVAC zone thermostat must be located in the zone it controls, not in a separate or unconditioned space
conditions: When the thermostat is the primary temperature sensing element for that zone
exceptions: Wireless remote sensors that are separate from the thermostat setpoint interface can be in the zone while the user interface is elsewhere

subject: HVAC Zone Damper / Thermostat
rule: Zone damper must not fully close all supply paths serving a zone that contains a heating or cooling coil that can still be active
conditions: When the damper is the only airflow path through the coil
and the coil's heating/cooling source can be independently enabled
exceptions: Systems with dedicated safety high-limit or freeze-protection controls that override the damper position

subject: Door with Privacy Lock
rule: Door with privacy lock must have a latch or bolt that engages with the door frame when closed
conditions: Door is a swing-type door
Door is closed
exceptions: Electromagnetic locks that use magnetic force only

subject: Door with Privacy Lock
rule: Door with privacy lock must allow emergency override from the outside if the door is in a means of egress path
conditions: Door is located on an exit route or means of egress
exceptions: Doors serving rooms with fewer than 50 occupants and where building code allows privacy-only locking without override (e.g., single-occupancy restroom)

subject: Door with Privacy Lock
rule: Door with privacy lock must not use a key-operated deadbolt that requires a key from both sides
conditions: Door is intended for privacy function (not security)
exceptions: None — a privacy lock by definition must allow unlock from outside without a key in emergencies

subject: Door with Privacy Lock
rule: Privacy lock mechanism must not obstruct the door's ability to close fully and latch
conditions: Door is installed and operational
exceptions: None — this would make the door inoperable

subject: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
rule: UPS must be located in a room with adequate ventilation to prevent hydrogen gas accumulation from lead-acid batteries
conditions: when using vented lead-acid (VLA) batteries
exceptions: if using valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA) or lithium-ion batteries that do not vent hydrogen under normal operation

subject: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
rule: UPS batteries must be installed on a floor that can support their dead weight load
conditions: when batteries are floor-mounted rather than rack or wall-mounted

subject: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
rule: UPS system must be bonded to the facility's equipment grounding conductor

subject: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
rule: UPS must not be installed in a location where ambient temperature exceeds its specified operating range
exceptions: short-term operation at elevated temperature may be permissible per manufacturer specs, typically up to 40°C

subject: Server Racks & Cabinets
rule: Server rack mounting rails must be spaced at 19 inches (482.6 mm) horizontally between front mounting hole centers
conditions: rack is designed for standard EIA-310 equipment mounting
exceptions: non-standard racks such as 23-inch telecom racks or proprietary open-frame racks designed for non-19-inch equipment

subject: Server Racks & Cabinets
rule: Server rack vertical mounting holes must align vertically with a hole-to-hole pitch of 1.75 inches (44.45 mm), corresponding to 1U increments
conditions: rack uses the standard U (rack unit) height increment system
exceptions: non-standard-height cabinets designed for proprietary equipment that does not follow the U increment system

subject: Server Racks & Cabinets
rule: Server cabinet must have front and rear doors (or equivalent removable panels) that allow tool-less access to equipment
conditions: cabinet is enclosed and intended for active IT equipment installation
exceptions: open-frame racks (not enclosed cabinets) which by design lack doors

subject: Server Racks & Cabinets
rule: Server cabinet must not have a solid front door that completely blocks airflow across mounted equipment
conditions: cabinet is enclosed and houses active, air-cooled IT equipment
exceptions: cabinets housing only passive patch panels or equipment with self-contained liquid cooling that does not rely on through-cabinet airflow

subject: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
rule: PDU must have proper grounding/bonding per electrical code
conditions: when connected to an electrical supply
exceptions: double-insulated PDU designs that are certified and do not require a safety ground

subject: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
rule: PDU must not exceed its rated current capacity on any output branch
conditions: during normal continuous operation
exceptions: brief inrush during equipment startup within manufacturer-specified limits

subject: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
rule: PDU must have overcurrent protection (fuse or circuit breaker) on each output branch
conditions: when the PDU provides multiple output receptacles
exceptions: single-output PDUs where input protection covers the entire unit

subject: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
rule: PDU enclosure must not have exposed live conductive parts accessible to touch
conditions: during normal operation with enclosure closed

subject: Precision/Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC/CRAH)
rule: CRAC/CRAH unit must have a dedicated condensate drain line connected to an approved disposal point
conditions: unit produces condensate during normal operation
unit is not air-cooled with external condenser
exceptions: unit uses chilled water with no dehumidification cycle and no condensate production

subject: Precision/Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC/CRAH)
rule: CRAC/CRAH unit supply air temperature must not be set below the dew point of the room air if the room has no vapor barrier
conditions: room lacks a continuous vapor barrier in walls/ceiling/floor
exceptions: room is designed as a cold-aisle containment system with sealed vapor barrier

subject: Precision/Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC/CRAH)
rule: CRAC/CRAH unit must have a minimum clearance for service access on at least one side
conditions: unit is installed indoors
exceptions: unit is designed for zero-clearance service access from front only

subject: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
rule: Overhead cable tray and ladder rack must be horizontally supported at intervals not exceeding manufacturer-rated or code-specified maximum span
conditions: Installed in a non-continuous run
Contains cables

subject: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
rule: Overhead cable tray and ladder rack must be secured against uplift from wind loads when installed outdoors
conditions: Installed outdoors
Exposed to wind

subject: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
rule: Overhead cable tray and ladder rack must not block access to fire suppression systems, sprinklers, or fire detection devices
conditions: Installed in a ceiling space or overhead plenum
Fire suppression or detection devices are present

subject: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
rule: Overhead cable tray and ladder rack must not obstruct means of egress or reduce required headroom below code minimum
conditions: Installed in a pathway used for egress
Above walking surfaces

subject: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
rule: Overhead cable tray and ladder rack must be fabricated from or coated with materials rated for the fire classification of the occupancy space
conditions: Installed in a space with defined fire-resistance rating requirements
exceptions: Where cables inside are already listed as plenum-rated and the tray is treated as cable support only

subject: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
rule: clean agent fire suppression system must be designed to maintain agent concentration within the protected enclosure for the required hold time (typically 10 minutes)
conditions: enclosure is normally occupied
system uses total flooding design

subject: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
rule: clean agent discharge must not expose personnel to agent concentrations that exceed the No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) for the specific agent in occupied spaces
conditions: enclosure is normally occupied during discharge
agent is classified as a chemical extinguishing agent with an established NOAEL
exceptions: unoccupied spaces with delayed entry protocols and warning signage

subject: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
rule: the protected enclosure must have automatic suppression of HVAC and damper closure upon system actuation to prevent agent loss
conditions: system is a total flooding clean agent system

subject: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
rule: clean agent storage cylinders must be located outside the protected enclosure or in a dedicated room with appropriate temperature control
conditions: agent is stored in pressurized cylinders
storage area is not environmentally conditioned for the agent's rated temperature range
exceptions: cylinders rated and tested for the ambient temperature conditions within the protected enclosure

subject: Server Room Access Control System
rule: system must enforce at least two independent authentication factors before granting door access to the server room
conditions: facility contains server room
access control system is electronically actuated
exceptions: emergency egress override (fail-safe exit) where no authentication is required for life safety

subject: Server Room Access Control System
rule: system must not allow a single point of failure to disable all authentication methods simultaneously
conditions: system is deployed for production server room access control
exceptions: facilities with a single designated security officer continuously present 24/7 is an exception only where local code permits

subject: Server Room Access Control System
rule: system must lock the door when fire alarm is not active (fail-secure for security, fail-safe for egress)
conditions: system is installed on a means of egress door to a server room
exceptions: local fire code may require fail-safe locking (door unlocks on fire alarm) for the egress direction; in that case the inward (room side) remains fail-safe but the outward (corridor side) must still be secured during normal operation

subject: Grounding & Bonding Busbar
rule: grounding and bonding busbar must be electrically continuous with the grounding electrode system
conditions: when installed as part of the electrical power system
exceptions: when used only as a reference point for instrumentation and isolated from the power ground

subject: Grounding & Bonding Busbar
rule: grounding and bonding busbar must be sized to carry the available fault current without thermal damage
conditions: when connected to a service or separately derived system

subject: Grounding & Bonding Busbar
rule: grounding and bonding busbar must not be installed in a location exposed to corrosive environmental conditions unless rated for that environment
conditions: when the busbar material is copper or aluminum without corrosion protection
exceptions: busbar materials specifically rated for corrosive environments, such as tinned or stainless steel equivalents

subject: Grounding & Bonding Busbar
rule: grounding and bonding busbar must be bonded to all metallic enclosures and raceways entering the same enclosure
conditions: when the busbar serves as the system bonding jumper location in a separately derived system
exceptions: when the metallic enclosure is isolated by a non-conductive grommet or fitting to prevent parallel ground paths in specific sensitive installations

subject: Reinforced Concrete
rule: Reinforced concrete must have adequate concrete cover over reinforcing steel to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: When exposed to environmental moisture
When required to have fire resistance rating
exceptions: When protected by an additional impermeable cladding or coating system that provides equivalent protection

subject: Reinforced Concrete
rule: Reinforced concrete must not have reinforcement less than the minimum required cross-sectional area for crack control
conditions: For any structural member
exceptions: Non-structural concrete elements verified by analysis to have negligible tensile stress

subject: Reinforced Concrete
rule: Reinforced concrete must have reinforcement properly detailed with adequate lap splice or mechanical connection length to develop full bar yield strength
conditions: Where continuity of reinforcement is required at construction joints or bar end points
exceptions: When bars are continuous and do not require splicing

subject: Reinforced Concrete
rule: Reinforced concrete must not have aggregate larger than 3/4 of the minimum clear spacing between reinforcing bars
conditions: In any reinforced concrete member where concrete must flow between reinforcement
exceptions: Self-consolidating concrete with verified passing ability per ASTM C1621

subject: High-Performance Concrete
rule: High-Performance Concrete must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 55 MPa (8,000 psi) at 28 days
conditions: when specified as structural grade high-performance concrete
exceptions: when specifically designed for non-structural applications with documented lower strength requirements

subject: High-Performance Concrete
rule: High-Performance Concrete must have a water-to-cementitious materials ratio (w/cm) not exceeding 0.40
conditions: for structural hardened-state performance requirements
exceptions: when high-range water reducers (superplasticizers) are used to maintain workability at a higher w/cm ratio while still meeting strength requirements

subject: High-Performance Concrete
rule: High-Performance Concrete must not be placed without a specified curing method that maintains moisture for a minimum of 7 days
conditions: for any application requiring the defined performance characteristics
exceptions: when using specialized self-curing or internal curing admixtures validated by testing

subject: Concrete Formwork
rule: Concrete formwork must remain in place until the concrete has reached sufficient strength to support its own weight and any applied loads
conditions: during construction
for cast-in-place concrete
exceptions: when using engineered falsework systems designed for early stripping

subject: Concrete Formwork
rule: Concrete formwork must not deflect under the pressure of wet concrete beyond the tolerances specified in the formwork design
conditions: during concrete placement and curing

subject: Concrete Formwork
rule: Concrete formwork must provide a tight seal at all joints to prevent loss of cement paste (grout leakage)
conditions: for all poured concrete elements
exceptions: when formwork is intentionally designed with controlled leakage for architectural surface texture

subject: Concrete Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
rule: rebar must have minimum concrete cover to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: when exposed to outdoor or moist environments
when fire resistance is required
exceptions: when stainless steel or epoxy-coated rebar is used

subject: Concrete Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
rule: rebar must not be exposed to chlorides in concentrations that exceed threshold for corrosion initiation
conditions: when in marine environment
when exposed to deicing salts
exceptions: when rebar is stainless steel, galvanized, or otherwise corrosion-resistant

subject: Concrete Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
rule: rebar must not be placed with less than the minimum specified lap splice length
conditions: when lapping bars to transfer tensile forces
exceptions: when mechanical couplers or welded splices are used in lieu of lap splices

subject: Concrete Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
rule: rebar must have a minimum bend diameter to prevent cracking or fracture during bending
conditions: when rebar is bent on site or prefabricated with hooks or stirrups

subject: Concrete Slab
rule: Concrete slab must have sufficient thickness to resist applied bending moments and shear forces without cracking or failure
conditions: slab is structural (load-bearing)
exceptions: non-structural topping slabs not designed for structural loads

subject: Concrete Slab
rule: Concrete slab must have reinforcement providing minimum area of steel to control cracking from shrinkage and temperature
conditions: slab is cast-in-place reinforced concrete
exceptions: unreinforced/precast panels designed as plain concrete with adequate joints

subject: Concrete Slab
rule: Concrete slab must not be placed on frozen ground or subgrade
conditions: slab-on-grade

subject: Concrete Slab
rule: Concrete slab must have adequate cover over reinforcement to prevent corrosion
conditions: slab is exposed to exterior environment or moisture

subject: Concrete Slab
rule: Concrete slab must be provided with control/construction joints at appropriate spacing to accommodate shrinkage
conditions: large continuous slab area
no post-tensioning
exceptions: post-tensioned slabs designed to resist shrinkage without joints

subject: Concrete Beam
rule: concrete beam must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement to prevent corrosion and fire-induced spalling
conditions: beam is exposed to exterior environment
beam is in a fire-rated assembly
exceptions: beam is fully encapsulated in a fireproofing system that provides equivalent protection

subject: Concrete Beam
rule: concrete beam must not have less than minimum tension reinforcement ratio specified by code
conditions: beam is reinforced concrete (not plain concrete)

subject: Concrete Beam
rule: concrete beam must not have stirrups spaced wider than maximum permitted shear spacing
conditions: beam is subjected to shear forces exceeding concrete shear capacity

subject: Concrete Beam
rule: concrete beam must have adequate anchorage length for all longitudinal reinforcement at supports
conditions: beam is continuous or fixed at supports
exceptions: beam is simply supported with positive moment only and hooked bars are used

subject: Concrete Beam
rule: concrete beam must have its neutral axis depth limited to ensure tension-controlled failure mode
conditions: beam is subjected to flexure

subject: Concrete Column
rule: concrete column must be designed for axial load transfer
conditions: when used as a vertical load-bearing member
exceptions: non-structural decorative concrete columns not intended to carry loads

subject: Concrete Column
rule: concrete column must have minimum cross-sectional dimension or reinforcement ratio to prevent buckling
conditions: when the column is slender (height-to-dimension ratio exceeds code limits)

subject: Concrete Column
rule: concrete column must not have a concrete compressive strength below the minimum specified for structural use
conditions: for any structural concrete column

subject: Concrete Column
rule: concrete column must be provided with adequate cover to reinforcement
conditions: when reinforced with steel rebar

subject: Concrete Column
rule: concrete column must be vertically aligned within allowable tolerance
conditions: for all structural columns

subject: Concrete Wall
rule: concrete wall must be designed to resist lateral loads (wind or seismic) based on local building code requirements
conditions: when used as a structural wall
in any building taller than one story
in seismic zones or high-wind regions
exceptions: non-structural veneer walls that are independently supported

subject: Concrete Wall
rule: concrete wall must have a minimum thickness of 150 mm when cast-in-place and exposed to weather
conditions: for cast-in-place structural concrete walls
exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: walls with approved protective cladding or coating systems that provide equivalent durability
non-load-bearing partition walls not exposed to weather

subject: Concrete Wall
rule: concrete wall must not have construction joints located at regions of maximum shear or moment unless specifically detailed as a structural connection
conditions: for structural concrete walls
exceptions: joints designed as intentional seismic joints with engineered reinforcement across the joint

subject: Concrete Foundation
rule: concrete foundation must extend below the frost line
conditions: foundation is located in a climate with seasonal freezing
exceptions: foundation is built on bedrock where frost heave is not possible

subject: Concrete Foundation
rule: concrete foundation must have continuous bearing on undisturbed soil or engineered fill of adequate capacity
exceptions: foundation is supported entirely on deep piles or caissons that transfer load below bearing stratum

subject: Concrete Foundation
rule: concrete foundation must not be placed on organic topsoil, uncompacted fill, or frozen ground
exceptions: organic material or frozen ground is fully removed and replaced with engineered fill before placement

subject: Concrete Foundation
rule: concrete foundation must have minimum compressive strength as specified by structural design loads

subject: Concrete Foundation
rule: concrete foundation must have steel reinforcement where tensile stresses are expected
conditions: foundation is subject to bending or tensile forces (e.g., retaining walls, mat foundations, or footings on compressible soil)
exceptions: foundation is a plain concrete footing designed only for compressive stress with no tension

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair tread depth and riser height must comply with building code ratios (typically 2R + T = 24–25 inches) for safe pedestrian use
conditions: stair serves as means of egress
stair is accessible to building occupants
exceptions: private stairs within a single dwelling unit may have slightly relaxed ratios in some jurisdictions

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair must have a minimum width of at least 36 inches (or applicable code minimum) for egress pathways
conditions: stair serves as a required means of egress
stair serves more than one dwelling unit
exceptions: stairs within a single dwelling unit may have reduced widths under some codes

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair must have continuous handrails on at least one side
conditions: stair has four or more risers

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair must not have open risers where the opening is large enough to allow passage of a 4-inch sphere
conditions: stair has open risers
stair is part of a building with young children likely to occupy
exceptions: stairs not serving areas accessible to children

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair must have a landing at the top and bottom of each flight
conditions: stair is more than 12 feet in vertical rise
stair is part of a means of egress

subject: Concrete Stair
rule: concrete stair must have a minimum tread depth of 11 inches (for egress stairs)
conditions: stair serves as a means of egress
exceptions: private stairs within a dwelling unit

subject: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
rule: expansion joint must allow for differential thermal movement between adjacent concrete sections
conditions: joint type is expansion joint
adjacent concrete sections are exposed to temperature variations
exceptions: joint is in a climate-controlled environment with negligible temperature fluctuation

subject: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
rule: construction joint must not be placed at locations of maximum bending moment in the structural element
conditions: joint type is construction joint
element is a beam, slab, or structural member subject to bending

subject: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
rule: contraction joint must be cut to a depth of at least one-quarter of the slab thickness
conditions: joint type is contraction joint
joint is in a concrete slab on grade
exceptions: joint is a decorative score line not intended to control cracking

subject: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
rule: expansion joint must not be filled with rigid material that would prevent joint movement
conditions: joint type is expansion joint

subject: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
rule: waterstop must be continuous through construction joints in below-grade or water-retaining structures
conditions: joint type is construction joint
structure is below grade or water-retaining
exceptions: joint is in a dry interior slab not exposed to water

subject: Concrete Anchor / Embedment
rule: concrete anchor embedment depth must meet manufacturer's specified minimum to develop full tensile capacity
conditions: anchor is cast-in-place or post-installed adhesive/mechanical
exceptions: engineer-designed shallow embedment specifically calculated for reduced loads

subject: Concrete Anchor / Embedment
rule: concrete anchor must not be placed within minimum edge distance specified by manufacturer or code
conditions: anchor is tension-loaded
exceptions: edge distance is specifically verified with a concrete breakout capacity calculation

subject: Concrete Anchor / Embedment
rule: concrete anchor must not be installed when base concrete has not reached minimum specified compressive strength
conditions: anchor is post-installed and torque/expansion dependent
exceptions: anchor type is specifically rated for early-age or green concrete

subject: Concrete Anchor / Embedment
rule: concrete anchor spacing must not be less than minimum center-to-center distance specified by manufacturer
conditions: multiple anchors are installed in a group and share a common tension load path
exceptions: engineered group reduction factor is applied per ACI 318 or equivalent

subject: Concrete Topping / Screed
rule: Concrete topping / screed must have a minimum thickness to ensure structural integrity and prevent cracking under load
conditions: when used as a structural topping on floors or roofs
when subjected to pedestrian or light vehicular traffic
exceptions: when serving purely as a leveling screed with no structural function and no traffic loading

subject: Concrete Topping / Screed
rule: Concrete topping / screed must be bonded to the substrate or reinforced to prevent delamination
conditions: when applied as a bonded topping over a concrete base
exceptions: when designed as an unbonded or floating screed with appropriate reinforcement and thickness

subject: Concrete Topping / Screed
rule: Concrete topping / screed must not be applied over a substrate with standing water or frost
conditions: during installation

subject: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
rule: timber frame must have continuous load path from roof to foundation
conditions: structural integrity required
vertical load bearing

subject: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
rule: timber frame connections must be detailed to accommodate dimensional changes from moisture content variation
conditions: timber members are solid wood
exposed to variable humidity
exceptions: members are fully encased in climate-controlled enclosure with stable relative humidity

subject: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
rule: timber frame must not have direct wood-to-ground contact without moisture barrier
conditions: column bases or sill plates bear on or near grade
exceptions: wood members are preservative-treated for ground contact
wood is of a naturally durable heartwood species rated for ground contact

subject: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
rule: timber frame lateral stability system must be provided (braced frame, diaphragm, or shear wall)
conditions: frame spans more than one story
frame is not fully enclosed by non-structural lateral-resisting elements

subject: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
rule: timber frame beam-to-column connections must resist both gravity and imposed lateral forces
conditions: connection is designed as moment-resisting (not purely pinned)
exceptions: the lateral system is provided entirely by separate elements (e.g., steel braces, concrete core)

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Stud walls must have vertical studs spaced at no more than the maximum permitted spacing for the given timber grade, section size, and design loads
conditions: Load-bearing wall
Timber grade and section size known
exceptions: Non-load-bearing partition walls using different spacing standards

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Joists must not have notches or holes in the middle third of the span except where specifically designed and reinforced
conditions: Timber joist spanning between supports
exceptions: Where an engineered reinforcement or proprietary joist system explicitly permits penetrations in that zone

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Joists and rafters must have a minimum bearing length (typically 35 mm on timber supports, 90 mm on masonry) at each end support
conditions: End-supported joist or rafter
exceptions: Where proprietary metal joist hangers or brackets provide equivalent load transfer and are designed for reduced bearing

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Rafters must be tied at eaves level (via ceiling joists, collar ties, or engineered connectors) to resist outward thrust
conditions: Pitched roof rafter pair
Roof is not a truss or vaulted design
exceptions: Structurally designed ridge beams and ridge connections that resolve thrust
Engineered portal frame or moment-resisting connections

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Studs, joists, and rafters must not have a moisture content above the maximum permitted (typically 20% for structural timber) at the time of enclosure
conditions: Enclosed in a wall, floor, or roof assembly
exceptions: Timber engineered for and certified as suitable for wet service conditions

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Load-bearing stud walls must be braced against lateral out-of-plane buckling (by sheathing, diagonal bracing, or rigid connections)
conditions: Load-bearing wall with no continuous rigid sheathing on at least one face
exceptions: Walls where lateral support is provided by perpendicular walls or diaphragms at close intervals

subject: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
rule: Nogs (dwangs, blocking) between studs must be installed at mid-height where wall height exceeds permitted unbraced stud length (typically 2.7 m for common sections)
conditions: Stud height greater than the code-defined unbraced length for the given stud section
exceptions: Where sheathing provides continuous lateral restraint

subject: Timber Truss
rule: Timber truss must have all joints properly connected (e.g., nailed, bolted, or gusset-plated) to transfer axial forces
conditions: When used as a load-bearing structural component

subject: Timber Truss
rule: Timber truss members must not be notched or damaged in a way that reduces their cross-sectional area below the design capacity
conditions: When the truss is designed to carry a specified load
exceptions: Where notching is accounted for in structural engineering analysis and approved in design

subject: Timber Truss
rule: Timber truss must have its connections designed to resist tension forces (uplift) at support points
conditions: In roof applications exposed to wind uplift
exceptions: Where the truss is not subject to uplift forces (e.g., fully sheltered interior application)

subject: Timber Decking / Subflooring
rule: Timber decking/subflooring must be installed with adequate spacing (typically 3-5mm) between boards to allow for natural wood expansion and contraction due to moisture changes
conditions: Solid timber boards used
Decking installed in exterior or semi-exposed environment
exceptions: Engineered composite decking that specifies zero-gap installation

subject: Timber Decking / Subflooring
rule: Timber decking/subflooring must have a minimum slope of 1:50 (or 2%) away from the building structure for water drainage
conditions: Used as exterior decking
Used as subflooring over a ventilated crawl space or exposed to rainfall
exceptions: Decking over a fully waterproofed membrane with integral drainage system designed to 0% slope

subject: Timber Decking / Subflooring
rule: Timber decking/subflooring must not be installed in direct ground contact without a capillary break or pressure treatment rated for ground contact
conditions: Timber is untreated or treated only for above-ground use
exceptions: Timber specifically rated and treated for ground-contact use (e.g., CCA or ACQ treated to UC4B or higher)

subject: Timber Cladding / Siding
rule: Timber cladding/siding must have an air gap (ventilated cavity) behind it on exterior walls
conditions: when installed on exterior walls in climates with significant rainfall or humidity
when installed over a weather-resistive barrier
exceptions: when installed as a decorative interior finish only
when manufacturer's system explicitly certifies direct application as a rain-screen equivalent

subject: Timber Cladding / Siding
rule: Timber cladding/siding must be treated or naturally durable against moisture, insects, and fungal decay
conditions: when used in exterior or exposed applications
when in contact with or near ground level
exceptions: when used solely as an interior decorative finish in a conditioned, dry environment with no moisture exposure

subject: Timber Cladding / Siding
rule: Timber cladding/siding must not be directly embedded in or in continuous contact with concrete or masonry without an impermeable separation layer
conditions: at base of wall where cladding approaches ground or foundation level
exceptions: when timber is specifically rated for ground-contact use and an engineered drainage system is provided

subject: Timber Cladding / Siding
rule: Timber cladding/siding must be installed with provision for differential movement (slotted fixings or similar)
conditions: when board lengths exceed typical seasonal movement thresholds (generally over 2-3 meters)
when installed in climates with significant seasonal humidity variation
exceptions: when using engineered timber products with documented zero-movement characteristics for the full service life

subject: Timber Doors and Window Frames
rule: timber door and window frames must be protected from direct moisture contact to prevent rot and decay
conditions: installed in exterior walls
exceptions: frames constructed from naturally durable or preservative-treated timber rated for ground/weather contact

subject: Timber Doors and Window Frames
rule: timber door and window frames must not be installed in direct ground contact
conditions: used as door frames or window frames in buildings
exceptions: frames specifically designed and rated as 'ground-contact' pressure-treated timber

subject: Timber Doors and Window Frames
rule: timber window frames must accommodate the differential thermal and moisture movement between timber and glass
conditions: assembled with glass panes

subject: Timber Doors and Window Frames
rule: timber doors must not warp beyond the clearance provided by the frame
conditions: installed as operable swing doors
exceptions: doors with engineered laminated construction that guarantees dimensional stability under specified conditions

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must have a minimum tread depth of at least 254 mm (10 inches) for residential stairs
conditions: Used as egress stairs
Residential occupancy
exceptions: Spiral stairs where code permits reduced tread depth

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must have a maximum riser height of 196 mm (7.75 inches) for residential stairs
conditions: Used as egress stairs
Residential occupancy

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must not have a gap between balusters greater than 100 mm (4 inches)
conditions: Guardrail or handrail balusters

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must have a handrail on at least one side of stairs with a width of more than 1000 mm (39 inches)
conditions: Stair width exceeds 1000 mm

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must have a guardrail on open sides where the drop exceeds 600 mm (24 inches)
conditions: Open side of stairs or landing
Drop height exceeds 600 mm

subject: Timber Stairs and Railings
rule: timber stairs and railings must be constructed from timber that is rated for structural use (e.g., graded lumber or engineered wood with published strength values)
conditions: Load-bearing stair components (stringers, treads, rails)

subject: Heavy Timber Fireproofing / Encapsulation
rule: Heavy timber fireproofing/encapsulation material must be non-combustible or have a listed fire-resistance rating when applied to achieve a specific hourly rating
conditions: When fireproofing is required by building code for heavy timber construction
When the assembly is required to meet a specific fire-resistance rating (e.g., 1-hour, 2-hour)

subject: Heavy Timber Fireproofing / Encapsulation
rule: Encapsulation material must maintain adhesion or mechanical attachment under fire exposure for the required duration
conditions: When spray-applied fire-resistive material (SFRM) is used on heavy timber

subject: Heavy Timber Fireproofing / Encapsulation
rule: Heavy timber fireproofing must not impede the natural charring behavior that provides heavy timber's inherent fire resistance
conditions: When the fireproofing is applied directly to structural heavy timber elements intended to be designed for charring
exceptions: When the encapsulation is designed as part of a fully rated fire-resistance assembly that replaces reliance on char layer

subject: Heavy Timber Fireproofing / Encapsulation
rule: Fireproofing material must not contain halogens or other compounds that release toxic or corrosive smoke at concentrations exceeding code limits when exposed to fire
conditions: When the building is occupied
When the fireproofing is applied in interior, occupied spaces
exceptions: When the material is part of an approved alternative that meets life-safety smoke toxicity requirements

subject: Timber-Concrete Composite System
rule: A timber-concrete composite system must have adequate shear connection between timber and concrete layers to transfer longitudinal shear forces
conditions: When used in any structural application (floors, decks, bridges)

subject: Timber-Concrete Composite System
rule: The concrete layer in a timber-concrete composite system must be cured and at minimum design strength before the composite system is loaded to design capacity
conditions: When cast-in-place concrete is used for the composite slab
exceptions: Precast concrete planks or prefabricated timber-concrete elements assembled after full curing

subject: Timber-Concrete Composite System
rule: Timber-concrete composite system must not allow direct contact between unprotected timber and moisture that cannot drain away
conditions: In exterior applications or where the system is exposed to precipitation or condensation
exceptions: Timber is pressure-treated with preservatives suitable for wet service conditions and the system is designed for wet exposure

subject: Timber Connection Hardware
rule: Timber connection hardware must have load-rated capacity stated by manufacturer
conditions: when used in structural load-bearing connections
exceptions: decorative or non-structural applications where load rating is not required

subject: Timber Connection Hardware
rule: Timber connection hardware must be corrosion-resistant or treated for the exposure environment
conditions: when used in exterior, damp, or chemically aggressive environments
exceptions: interior dry applications where corrosion is not a concern

subject: Timber Connection Hardware
rule: Timber connection hardware must not induce splitting in the timber member
conditions: when fasteners (nails, screws, bolts) are installed near timber edges or ends
or when multiple fasteners are closely spaced
exceptions: where engineered detailing (e.g., pre-drilling, reduced fastener diameter) explicitly accounts for and mitigates splitting

subject: Structural Steel Columns
rule: structural steel columns must transfer vertical gravity loads from supported elements to the foundation
conditions: the column is part of the primary load-bearing frame

subject: Structural Steel Columns
rule: structural steel columns must maintain axial load capacity without exceeding the material yield strength under factored design loads
conditions: the column is designed per limit-state design codes (e.g., AISC 360, Eurocode 3)

subject: Structural Steel Columns
rule: structural steel columns must be connected to the foundation with sufficient embedment or base anchorage to resist overturning and uplift forces
conditions: the column is subject to lateral loads (wind, seismic) or net uplift

subject: Structural Steel Columns
rule: structural steel columns must not have net cross-section reductions due to holes or notches that reduce the effective area below that required for the design axial load
conditions: the column contains bolt holes, copes, or cutouts

subject: Structural Steel Columns
rule: structural steel columns must have a slenderness ratio (KL/r) that does not exceed the code-prescribed maximum for compressive members
conditions: the column is designed as a compression member per AISC or equivalent code

subject: Structural Steel Beams
rule: structural steel beam must have sufficient cross-sectional area to resist applied bending moment
conditions: beam is in flexure
beam is part of load-bearing structure

subject: Structural Steel Beams
rule: structural steel beam must have adequate shear capacity at supports
conditions: beam is loaded
beam is simply supported or continuous

subject: Structural Steel Beams
rule: structural steel beam must not be loaded beyond its lateral-torsional buckling capacity without adequate bracing
conditions: beam has unbraced length exceeding limit
beam is in flexure about its strong axis
exceptions: beam is fully braced laterally at close intervals

subject: Structural Steel Beams
rule: structural steel beam must have web-to-flange welds with adequate throat thickness to transfer shear flow
conditions: beam is a welded plate girder or built-up section
exceptions: beam is rolled (single-piece) section such as W-shape which has no weld

subject: Steel Trusses
rule: steel trusses must be designed to carry their self-weight plus applicable dead and live loads without yielding or buckling
conditions: trusses are used as load-bearing elements

subject: Steel Trusses
rule: steel truss connections (welded or bolted) must be designed to transfer all factored forces between members without rupture or excessive deformation
conditions: trusses include connections between members

subject: Steel Trusses
rule: steel trusses must not be used without consideration of lateral-torsional buckling of compression chords and bracing requirements
conditions: truss is subject to compressive axial forces in its top chord or other compression members

subject: Steel Trusses
rule: steel truss members must not exceed their slenderness ratio limits as prescribed by applicable design code (AISC, Eurocode, etc.)
conditions: truss is designed per a structural steel code

subject: Steel Girders
rule: Steel girders must have adequate lateral bracing or lateral-torsional restraint to prevent buckling under design loads
conditions: Used as beams or flexural members
Unbraced length exceeds limiting value per design code
exceptions: Girders designed to resist buckling through increased section properties (compact/plastic sections) where code permits

subject: Steel Girders
rule: Steel girders must not be loaded beyond their yield strength under factored design loads

subject: Steel Girders
rule: Steel girder connections (bolted or welded) must be designed to transfer all design forces between connected members

subject: Steel Girders
rule: Steel girders must have sufficient fire protection to maintain load-bearing capacity for the required fire resistance rating
conditions: Building code requires fire resistance rating for the occupancy and structure type
exceptions: Girders in open structures or unoccupied areas where code explicitly waives fire protection

subject: Steel Bracing Systems
rule: Steel bracing systems must be continuous through the diaphragm or collector to complete the lateral load path
conditions: When connecting to roof or floor diaphragms
In seismic or lateral-force-resisting systems
exceptions: Where a deliberate discontinuity is designed as a fuse or energy dissipation device

subject: Steel Bracing Systems
rule: Steel bracing systems must not have net tension-only elements when designed for seismic load reversal
conditions: In seismic design categories D, E, or F
When bracing is part of the primary lateral force-resisting system
exceptions: Where a full buckling-restrained brace (BRB) or special concentrically braced frame (SCBF) detailing accommodates compression

subject: Steel Bracing Systems
rule: Steel brace member slenderness must not exceed the code limit for the assigned seismic force-resisting system
conditions: For concentrically braced frames (CBF) in seismic applications
exceptions: Buckling-restrained braced frames (BRBF) where the brace core is designed to yield in both tension and compression

subject: Steel Moment Frames
rule: Steel moment frame beams and columns must be connected with fully restrained (FR) moment connections capable of transferring full plastic moment capacity of the member
conditions: When used as part of the lateral force-resisting system (LFRS)
exceptions: Partially restrained (PR) connections may be used if specifically designed and verified for the expected demands through testing or advanced analysis

subject: Steel Moment Frames
rule: Steel moment frame beams must have adequate lateral bracing at hinge locations expected under design seismic or wind loading
conditions: When the frame is part of the lateral force-resisting system and inelastic behavior is anticipated
exceptions: Beams with compact sections and low Lb/Lp ratios that can be demonstrated to remain stable without discrete bracing per AISC 358

subject: Steel Moment Frames
rule: Column splices in steel moment frames must not be located within the anticipated plastic hinge zone
conditions: In seismic design categories D, E, or F
exceptions: If splice is demonstrated by testing or analysis to develop the required rotation capacity without strength degradation

subject: Steel Moment Frames
rule: The panel zone of beam-to-column connections in steel moment frames must have sufficient shear strength to resist the forces delivered by adjoining beams
conditions: All moment frame connections

subject: Steel Base Plates
rule: steel base plate must have sufficient thickness to prevent buckling under design compressive load
conditions: when used as load-bearing connection element
under compressive loading
exceptions: if base plate is stiffened with additional ribbing or stiffeners that provide equivalent buckling resistance

subject: Steel Base Plates
rule: steel base plate must not have hole spacing that violates minimum edge distance requirements per applicable steel design code
conditions: when anchor bolts are used for connection
exceptions: if project-specific testing or engineered analysis demonstrates adequacy of reduced edge distance

subject: Steel Base Plates
rule: steel base plate must bear on a level surface of sufficient compressive strength to resist applied loads without crushing
conditions: in all installations
exceptions: if designed for a grouted connection where grout provides load transfer

subject: Steel Base Plates
rule: steel base plate must be positively attached to the supporting foundation to resist uplift and lateral forces
conditions: when structure is subject to wind, seismic, or overturning loads
exceptions: if the structure is designed as purely gravity-loaded with no uplift or lateral force demand

subject: Steel Connections & Fasteners
rule: bolted connections must have sufficient bolt preload to prevent joint slip under design loads
conditions: bolted connection
load-bearing joint
static or fatigue loading
exceptions: slip-critical connections designed for controlled slip

subject: Steel Connections & Fasteners
rule: welded connections must have full penetration or adequate throat thickness to transmit design forces
conditions: welded connection
load-carrying weld
exceptions: non-structural tack welds or temporary fixtures

subject: Steel Connections & Fasteners
rule: steel fasteners must not be operated below their rated temperature without ductility provisions
conditions: carbon steel or high-strength bolt
low ambient temperature below -20°C
exceptions: fasteners specifically rated and tested for low-temperature service (e.g., cryogenic grades)

subject: Steel Connections & Fasteners
rule: bolted connections must have minimum edge distance to prevent shear tear-out
conditions: bolted connection
plate or member in tension
exceptions: design verified by experimental testing showing adequate capacity at smaller edge distance

subject: Composite Steel Decking
rule: Composite steel decking must be installed with ribs oriented to span between supports (perpendicular to primary beams)
conditions: When used as structural decking in composite slab systems
Deck profile is trapezoidal or re-entrant
exceptions: When manufacturer's engineering analysis and test data validate alternative orientation for a specific profile

subject: Composite Steel Decking
rule: Composite steel decking must be supported by a minimum end bearing length as specified by manufacturer (typically 38-50 mm on steel supports)
conditions: When acting as permanent formwork and composite reinforcement

subject: Composite Steel Decking
rule: Composite steel decking must not be used where the applied service load exceeds the deck profile's published span-load capacity
conditions: Under wet concrete construction loads
Under final service loads including live load

subject: Composite Steel Decking
rule: Composite steel decking must be adequately shored when the deck span exceeds the unshored capacity limit for the specified slab thickness
conditions: During concrete placement and curing before composite strength develops

subject: Composite Steel Decking
rule: Composite steel decking side laps must be properly interlocked and fastened at intervals specified by manufacturer
conditions: Adjacent deck sheets are installed side-by-side

subject: Steel Shear Studs
rule: Steel shear studs must be welded with complete 360-degree fusion at the base to the underlying steel beam or deck
conditions: When used as shear connectors in composite steel-concrete construction

subject: Steel Shear Studs
rule: Steel shear studs must have a minimum height-to-diameter ratio as specified by design code to ensure proper shear connector behavior
conditions: When designed as headed shear stud connectors per AISC or Eurocode provisions

subject: Steel Shear Studs
rule: Steel shear studs must not be placed in tension zones of concrete where they would be subjected to direct tensile pull-out without supplemental anchorage
conditions: When studs are relied upon for composite action in negative moment regions

subject: Steel Stairs & Railings
rule: steel stair stringers must be designed to support the full design load including dead load, live load, and lateral loads
conditions: stairs are structural
stairs serve occupant egress or access
exceptions: stairs that are purely decorative and not designed for occupancy

subject: Steel Stairs & Railings
rule: steel stair treads must have slip-resistant surface or treatment
conditions: stairs are accessible to building occupants or the public

subject: Steel Stairs & Railings
rule: steel stair handrails must be continuous on both sides of the stair flight
conditions: stairs have a total rise greater than 600 mm (approx. 24 in)
exceptions: stairs serving single dwelling units where local code permits handrail on one side only

subject: Steel Stairs & Railings
rule: steel railings must withstand a concentrated load of at least 500 N applied horizontally at any point on the top rail
conditions: railing serves as a guard (fall protection)

subject: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
rule: Light-gauge steel framing must be protected from galvanic corrosion when in direct contact with dissimilar metals
conditions: When light-gauge steel framing is in direct contact with incompatible dissimilar metals (e.g., aluminum, copper) in the presence of an electrolyte
exceptions: When an effective dielectric barrier (e.g., gasket, coating, tape) is provided between the metals
When both metals are in an interior dry environment with no moisture exposure

subject: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
rule: Light-gauge steel framing members must not have web crippling or local flange buckling at points of concentrated load without reinforcement
conditions: Where concentrated loads (e.g., from beams, joists, or equipment) are applied to the thin-walled section
exceptions: When bearing stiffeners, web doublers, or other reinforcement are installed at the load point

subject: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
rule: Light-gauge steel framing must have minimum edge distance for screw fasteners as specified by the manufacturer or applicable design standard
conditions: When screw fasteners are used to connect light-gauge steel members or attach sheathing
exceptions: None — this is a direct strength and serviceability requirement

subject: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
rule: Light-gauge steel framing must not be used as a component of the primary lateral-force-resisting system in a building exceeding the height limit permitted by the governing building code without engineering analysis and special detailing
conditions: For buildings taller than the prescriptive height limit in the applicable building code (e.g., IBC/ASCE 7 limits for cold-formed steel lateral systems)
exceptions: When a registered design engineer provides a complete analysis and special detailing per approved alternative methods

subject: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
rule: Light-gauge steel framing must incorporate corrosion protection (e.g., hot-dip galvanizing or equivalent coating) for exterior or exposed applications
conditions: When light-gauge steel framing is used in exterior walls, roofs, or any location exposed to weather or condensation
exceptions: When the framing is fully encapsulated within a continuously conditioned interior space with no moisture exposure
When stainless steel or other inherently corrosion-resistant material is substituted

subject: Steel Canopies & Canopy Supports
rule: steel canopy structure must be capable of supporting its own weight (self-weight) plus expected live loads (snow, rain, wind) without collapse
conditions: Canopy is structural (not purely decorative)
Canopy is attached to a building or freestanding
exceptions: Temporary canopies explicitly designed for single-use event with no occupancy beneath

subject: Steel Canopies & Canopy Supports
rule: canopy must not pond water — standing water on the canopy surface is prohibited
conditions: Canopy has a solid (non-perforated) upper surface
exceptions: Canopy surface is intentionally designed as a water-collection feature with engineered overflow and structural capacity for water load

subject: Steel Canopies & Canopy Supports
rule: canopy support structure must be secured against wind uplift
conditions: Canopy is exposed to wind (outdoor or semi-outdoor location)

subject: Steel Canopies & Canopy Supports
rule: canopy must not obstruct required emergency egress paths from the building
conditions: Canopy is located adjacent to building exits
Canopy is at or near ground level
exceptions: Canopy is positioned above the minimum required clear height for egress (typically 7'-6" or per applicable code)

subject: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
rule: steel roof trusses and purlin systems must transfer roof loads to supporting columns or walls

subject: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
rule: steel roof trusses and purlin systems must have sufficient connection strength at all joints and bearing points

subject: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
rule: steel roof trusses and purlin systems must accommodate thermal expansion and contraction

subject: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
rule: steel roof trusses and purlin systems must be designed for wind uplift forces
conditions: system exposed to wind loads

subject: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
rule: steel roof trusses and purlin systems must not exceed allowable stress limits under combined dead, live, and environmental loads

subject: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU must have at least two glass lites separated by a sealed air or gas space
conditions: when configured as a sealed insulating unit

subject: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU edge seal must be continuous and airtight

subject: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU cavity must contain a desiccant within the spacer system
conditions: when the cavity is filled with air or any gas other than vacuum
exceptions: vacuum IGUs where the cavity is evacuated

subject: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU must not have glass-to-glass contact between adjacent lites under normal service conditions

subject: Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must not be cut, drilled, or edge-worked after heat treatment
conditions: after the tempering process has been completed
during fabrication or installation
exceptions: waterjet cutting or CNC grinding performed before tempering, or using annealed glass that is later tempered

subject: Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must be installed with edge clearance and shock-absorbing setting blocks or gaskets to prevent hard contact with the frame
conditions: when used in framing systems (storefront, curtain wall, railing, door)
exceptions: fully monolithic bonded structural glazing where the glass is silicone-bonded without mechanical bite

subject: Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must not be used in applications where nickel sulfide inclusions can cause spontaneous fracture without risk mitigation
conditions: when heat-soak testing (per ASTM C1048) has not been performed
in overhead glazing or other life-safety locations where falling broken glass would cause injury
exceptions: fully laminated tempered glass where inner ply retains fragments after breakage
locations not accessible to occupants (e.g., non-occupiable roof glazing with protective screen below)

subject: Low-E Coated Glass
rule: Low-E coated glass must have the low-emissivity coating on the correct interior-facing side of the insulating glass unit (IGU)
conditions: When used in a sealed insulating glass unit (IGU) with two or more panes
exceptions: Single-pane applications where coating placement is not governed by IGU sealing requirements

subject: Low-E Coated Glass
rule: Low-E coated glass must not have the coating applied to surfaces that will be exposed to exterior weathering or frequent physical contact
conditions: When used in fenestration applications where one face of the glass is exposed to outdoor environment
exceptions: Self-cleaning or specialized Low-E products explicitly designed for exterior-surface coating

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing
rule: curtain wall glazing must accommodate building movement and deflection without glass breakage or water infiltration
conditions: building is subject to wind loads
building is subject to seismic loads
building is subject to thermal expansion

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing
rule: curtain wall glazing must provide a watertight and airtight seal between interior and exterior

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing
rule: curtain wall glazing must not be load-bearing for gravity loads from the building structure above

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing
rule: curtain wall glazing must have a structural path to transfer wind load to the building structure

subject: Wired Glass
rule: Wired glass must not be used in horizontal or near-horizontal overhead glazing applications where human impact or falling debris is possible
conditions: overhead glazing
skylights
canopies
walkway covers
exceptions: Where the glazing is protected by an additional structural barrier above it

subject: Wired Glass
rule: Wired glass must not be used in fire-rated glazing where a fire-resistance rating exceeding 60 minutes is required
conditions: fire-rated assemblies
fire doors
fire windows requiring > 60 minute rating

subject: Wired Glass
rule: Wired glass must not be used in areas requiring safety glazing per building code (e.g., doors, sidelites, low windows, shower enclosures) unless it meets CPSC 16 CFR 1201 impact standards
conditions: locations defined as hazardous by IBC/IRC safety glazing requirements
full-glass doors
bathtub and shower enclosures
glazing within 24 inches of walking surface
exceptions: Where local code still permits "approved" wired glass with a higher breakage load than standard (rare and jurisdiction-dependent)

subject: Glass Balustrade
rule: glass balustrade must be made of laminated or tempered safety glass
conditions: when used as a barrier or guard against falls
when installed at height greater than 0.5m above adjacent floor or ground
exceptions: when the balustrade is not serving as a fall-protection barrier (e.g. purely decorative feature not accessible to occupants)

subject: Glass Balustrade
rule: glass balustrade must have a top rail or handrail that meets load-bearing requirements
conditions: when the balustrade serves as a guardrail at height greater than 0.75m
when the glass panels are frameless or point-fixed (no continuous structural frame)
exceptions: when a structural engineer certifies the glass panels themselves can withstand the full design live load (typically 0.74 kN/m or per applicable code) without a top rail

subject: Glass Balustrade
rule: glass balustrade must not have exposed sharp edges on the top or grasping surface
conditions: when accessible to users
when within hand-contact zone

subject: Glass Balustrade
rule: glass balustrade fixings and brackets must be designed for the glass panel thickness and loading
conditions: for all structural installations

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must be designed to withstand its self-weight and imposed loads without exceeding its allowable stress
conditions: when used in load-bearing applications

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must not experience tensile stress exceeding its design strength at the edge or surface

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must be heat-treated (tempered or heat-strengthened) when used in a location where human impact is possible
conditions: when used in balustrades, guardrails, doors, or other locations accessible to occupants
exceptions: laminated glass with annealed inner plies may be used if the laminate provides equivalent post-breakage safety

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must be laminated or otherwise configured to retain broken fragments after fracture when used overhead or in fall-hazard locations
conditions: when used overhead (skylights, canopies, fins above head height) or as guarding (balustrades, curtain walls above grade)

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must be designed with a compatible interlayer that does not degrade under UV exposure or moisture ingress
conditions: when laminated glass is exposed to exterior environmental conditions

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must not have direct metal-to-glass contact without a compliant gasket or setting block
conditions: at any point of support or connection to the building frame

subject: Structural Glass
rule: Structural glass must accommodate thermal expansion and building frame movements without inducing unacceptable stress
conditions: when installed in a facade or curtain wall system subject to thermal cycling or differential movement

subject: Glass Partition
rule: glass partition must be constructed from tempered or laminated safety glass
conditions: when used as a physical barrier
when located in areas accessible to occupants

subject: Glass Partition
rule: glass partition must be supported by a structural frame or anchoring system capable of transferring wind and impact loads to the building structure

subject: Glass Partition
rule: glass partition must not contact hard building elements (e.g., concrete, steel) directly without isolation gaskets or cushioning materials

subject: Glass Partition
rule: glass partition must not be installed where it interrupts a required fire-resistance-rated separation unless it is a fire-rated glass assembly
conditions: when the partition is located in a fire-resistance-rated wall or corridor
exceptions: if the glass assembly has a fire-resistance rating equal to the surrounding construction

subject: Glass Canopy
rule: glass canopy must resist wind uplift loads to prevent structural failure or dislodgement
conditions: glass canopy is external or exposed to wind
exceptions: canopy is fully enclosed and not subject to wind exposure

subject: Glass Canopy
rule: glass canopy must be sloped or have a drainage system to prevent water ponding
conditions: glass canopy is horizontal or near-horizontal
exceptions: canopy is designed specifically as a flat rain-screen with active drainage infrastructure

subject: Glass Canopy
rule: glass in canopy must be safety glazing (tempered or laminated)
conditions: canopy is overhead or within accessible reach

subject: Glass Canopy
rule: glass canopy must not allow accumulation of snow load beyond design capacity
conditions: canopy is located in a climate with snow
exceptions: canopy is designed with active snow-melt or shedding system verified by structural analysis

subject: Glass Canopy
rule: glass canopy must have fall-arrest or protective barrier if walking surface is accessible above ground level
conditions: canopy is designed as a walkable surface or accessible roof above grade
exceptions: canopy is not accessible to occupants (e.g., purely ornamental, no access)

subject: Glass Floor Panel
rule: glass floor panel must have a load-rated (tempered or laminated) glass construction rated for live loads
conditions: when used as a walking surface
when installed in publicly accessible areas

subject: Glass Floor Panel
rule: glass floor panel must have a slip-resistant surface treatment or coating
conditions: when used on horizontal walking surfaces
when exposed to moisture or foot traffic

subject: Glass Floor Panel
rule: glass floor panel must not have exposed sharp edges or corners accessible to users
conditions: when installed at floor level
when accessible to pedestrians

subject: Glass Floor Panel
rule: glass floor panel must be supported on all four edges or be specifically engineered for point-supported (frameless) installation
conditions: when spanning any opening larger than 300 mm in any direction

subject: Glass Floor Panel
rule: glass floor panel must have a minimum thickness determined by structural calculation for the design live load and span
conditions: when installed as a load-bearing walking surface

subject: Glass Skylight
rule: Glass skylight must be made of tempered or laminated safety glass
conditions: when installed in overhead/roof application
exceptions: when protected by a wire mesh or other fall-protection barrier below the skylight

subject: Glass Skylight
rule: Glass skylight must have a slope of at least 1/4 inch per foot (minimum 2% slope) to allow water drainage
conditions: when installed on a flat or low-slope roof

subject: Glass Skylight
rule: Glass skylight must not be installed in areas subject to impact loads (e.g., hail zones, falling debris) without impact-resistant glazing
conditions: when located in geographic regions with frequent hailstorms or in areas where overhead debris is possible

subject: Glass Skylight
rule: Glass skylight must have a condensation management system or be installed in climate-controlled environments where dew point is not reached on the interior surface
conditions: when installed in buildings with high interior humidity or in cold climates
exceptions: when the skylight is a ventilated unit designed to allow condensation to evaporate without damaging the structure

subject: Glass Skylight
rule: Glass skylight must not be installed directly below rooftop equipment or other objects that could shed ice or debris onto the glass
exceptions: when a protective shield or deflector is installed above the skylight

subject: Glass Block
rule: Glass block must be laid with proper mortar joints to maintain structural integrity
conditions: when used in load-bearing or self-supporting walls/panels
when mortar-set installation method is used
exceptions: precast glass block panels with reinforced structural framing that bypasses mortar as primary structural connection

subject: Glass Block
rule: Glass block must not be used in fire-rated wall assemblies unless the specific glass block system carries a fire-resistance rating
conditions: when installed in locations requiring a fire-resistance-rated barrier per building code
exceptions: glass block systems that have been tested and rated for the required fire-resistance duration

subject: Glass Block
rule: Glass block panels must include horizontal and vertical expansion joints at structural interfaces to accommodate thermal movement
conditions: when installed in exterior walls or in environments with significant temperature variation
when panel dimensions exceed manufacturer-recommended limits
exceptions: very small panel sizes within manufacturer-specified expansion-free range

subject: Glass Block
rule: Glass block must not be used in structural applications that require significant bending or tensile load capacity
conditions: when subject to lateral wind loads beyond manufacturer limits
when used in overhead or canopy applications without supplemental support structure
exceptions: glass block systems specifically engineered with reinforcing bars and tested for such loads

subject: Thermal Insulation
rule: thermal insulation must maintain a continuous unbroken layer to prevent thermal bridging
conditions: when used as part of the building envelope
exceptions: penetrations for services that are properly sealed and insulated around

subject: Thermal Insulation
rule: thermal insulation material must not be compressed beyond its manufacturer-specified design limit
conditions: when installed in cavities, roofs, or framed assemblies
exceptions: materials specifically designed and rated for load-bearing insulation applications

subject: Thermal Insulation
rule: thermal insulation must be dry during and after installation to the degree required by its material type
conditions: for insulation materials whose thermal performance degrades with moisture content (e.g., mineral wool, cellulose, fiberglass)
exceptions: closed-cell foam insulations and materials specifically rated for wet installation (e.g., certain spray foams)

subject: Acoustic Insulation
rule: Acoustic insulation must not be compressed beyond its rated recovery limit during installation
conditions: Compression occurs during installation or fastening
exceptions: Materials specifically designed as compressed insulation bats that regain thickness

subject: Acoustic Insulation
rule: Acoustic insulation must maintain continuous contact with both faces of the cavity or assembly it is installed within
conditions: Insulation is installed in a wall, floor, or ceiling cavity
exceptions: Decoupled double-stud assemblies where an intentional air gap is part of the acoustic design

subject: Acoustic Insulation
rule: Acoustic insulation must not get wet or remain in contact with liquid water
conditions: Insulation is fibrous (e.g., fiberglass, mineral wool) or porous
exceptions: Closed-cell foam acoustic insulation that is inherently water-resistant and hydrophobic

subject: Cavity Wall Insulation
rule: Cavity wall insulation must be installed in a cavity that is clean and free of debris
conditions: Cavity wall construction with masonry outer and inner leaves

subject: Cavity Wall Insulation
rule: Cavity wall insulation must not bridge the cavity to create a continuous path for moisture transfer from outer to inner leaf
conditions: Cavity wall with insulation installed in the cavity space

subject: Cavity Wall Insulation
rule: Cavity wall insulation must maintain an clear air gap of at least 50mm below damp-proof course level
conditions: Cavity wall with damp-proof course present
exceptions: Where specific detailing with proprietary cavity trays and weepholes manages water ingress below DPC level

subject: Cavity Wall Insulation
rule: Cavity wall insulation materials must be of a type that does not absorb and retain moisture within the cavity
conditions: Cavity wall construction exposed to wind-driven rain
exceptions: Closed-cell foam insulations specifically designed for wet exposure

subject: Duct Insulation
rule: duct insulation must be applied to all ductwork carrying conditioned air
conditions: ductwork carries heated or cooled air intended for occupied spaces
exceptions: ducts located within conditioned spaces where heat loss/gain does not affect system performance

subject: Duct Insulation
rule: duct insulation must have a vapor retarder on the exterior side (cooling applications)
conditions: duct carries cooled air and is located in a warm, humid environment
insulation is external jacket type
exceptions: insulation is closed-cell foam with integral vapor barrier
duct is in a dehumidified space

subject: Duct Insulation
rule: duct insulation must not be compressed or crushed during installation or service
conditions: insulation is fibrous (fiberglass, mineral wool) with an R-value dependent on trapped air
exceptions: compression is unavoidable and accounted for by specifying extra thickness to achieve target R-value at compressed state

subject: Duct Insulation
