rule: duct insulation thickness must be sufficient to prevent surface condensation on cooling ducts
conditions: duct carries chilled air below the dew point of the surrounding air
duct is in an unconditioned or humid space
exceptions: duct surface is continuously monitored and actively heated above dew point

subject: Rigid Board Insulation
rule: Rigid board insulation must have a continuous air barrier on at least one side to prevent condensation within the assembly
conditions: when used within an exterior wall or roof assembly
when the assembly includes both warm and cold temperature sides

subject: Rigid Board Insulation
rule: Rigid board insulation must be installed in a manner that prevents thermal bridging at joints between boards
conditions: when used as a continuous exterior insulation layer

subject: Rigid Board Insulation
rule: Rigid board insulation must not be exposed to prolonged direct sunlight or UV radiation without protective covering
conditions: for polyisocyanurate, extruded polystyrene (XPS), and expanded polystyrene (EPS) types

subject: Floor Insulation
rule: Floor insulation must have a continuous air barrier on the warm side of the insulation to prevent moisture-laden air from condensing within the insulation layer
conditions: in conditioned spaces
in climates with significant heating or cooling seasons
exceptions: breathable/vapor-open assemblies specifically designed to allow drying to both sides

subject: Floor Insulation
rule: Floor insulation must not be compressed below its designed nominal thickness within cavity spaces
conditions: when installed between joists, trusses, or structural framing members

subject: Batt Insulation
rule: batt insulation must maintain air space between vapor barrier and sheathing when used in exterior wall applications
conditions: used in exterior wall assemblies where vapor barrier is required
exceptions: when insulation is unfaced and no vapor barrier is used
when insulation is installed in climate zones that do not require vapor retarders

subject: Batt Insulation
rule: batt insulation must not be compressed or squeezed into cavities that are undersized relative to its nominal thickness
conditions: during installation in stud bays or joist cavities

subject: Loose-Fill Insulation
rule: Loose-fill insulation must be installed only in enclosed cavities or attics with a vapor barrier and air barrier to prevent moisture infiltration and fiber migration
conditions: When used in horizontal applications such as attic floors
When used in enclosed wall cavities
exceptions: When specifically designed for open-blow applications with exposed membrane encapsulation

subject: Loose-Fill Insulation
rule: Loose-fill insulation must not be installed below grade or in direct contact with the ground
conditions: All applications
exceptions: None — no loose-fill product is rated for below-grade or earth-contact use due to capillary moisture wicking

subject: Loose-Fill Insulation
rule: Loose-fill insulation must be kept at least 3 inches away from recessed lighting fixtures and other heat-emitting devices unless the fixtures are IC-rated and the insulation is approved for contact
conditions: When recessed lighting fixtures are present in the same ceiling or attic plane
exceptions: When all fixtures are IC (insulation contact) rated and the loose-fill insulation manufacturer has approved direct contact

subject: Loose-Fill Insulation
rule: Loose-fill insulation must not be installed in a slope exceeding the manufacturer's stated maximum angle for that product
conditions: When applied on sloped surfaces such as cathedral ceilings or raked roofs
exceptions: None — exceeding the stated slope causes gravitational settling, void formation, and thermal bridging

subject: Structural Insulated Panels (SIPs)
rule: SIPs must be protected from continuous moisture exposure to prevent core delamination and structural failure
conditions: When used in exterior wall, roof, or foundation applications

subject: Structural Insulated Panels (SIPs)
rule: SIPs must not have their foam core exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods without UV-resistant cladding
conditions: When installed in exterior applications before final cladding is applied

subject: Structural Insulated Panels (SIPs)
rule: SIP joints must be sealed with an engineered air-seal system to prevent air infiltration at panel interfaces
conditions: When SIPs form the building envelope assembly

subject: Insulated Concrete Forms (ICFs)
rule: ICF walls must have continuous rigid insulation on both the interior and exterior sides of the concrete core
conditions: Used as above-grade exterior wall assembly
exceptions: When used as below-grade foundation walls where only exterior insulation is required for thermal break

subject: Insulated Concrete Forms (ICFs)
rule: ICF forms must remain continuously interconnected and braced until concrete is fully cured
conditions: During concrete placement and curing phase

subject: Insulated Concrete Forms (ICFs)
rule: ICF wall assemblies must not have the foam insulation exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods without UV-resistant coating or cladding
conditions: Exterior exposure of expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam surface
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified UV-resistant coatings applied within the rated exposure window

subject: Insulated Concrete Forms (ICFs)
rule: ICF walls must incorporate a vapor retarder appropriate to the climate zone on the warm-in-winter side of the assembly
conditions: In climate zones with heating degree days above 4000 (cold climates)
exceptions: When hygrothermal modeling demonstrates the assembly will dry to the interior and no vapor retarder is needed per IRC/IBC

subject: Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor retarder must be installed on the warm side of the building envelope assembly relative to the conditioned space and the local climate zone
conditions: Building envelope assembly includes a vapor retarder
Assembly separates conditioned from unconditioned space
exceptions: Climate zones with very low heating demand (e.g., Zone 1-2 in some codes allow omission or neutral placement)
Assemblies designed to dry inward (e.g., certain hot-humid climate strategies)

subject: Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor retarder must not have two vapor-retarding layers in the same assembly unless a drying path is provided between them
conditions: Multiple vapor-retarding materials are used in one assembly
exceptions: Both layers are permeable enough to allow drying (Class III or higher)

subject: Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor retarder must maintain continuity of the vapor-retarding plane at seams, penetrations, and interfaces
conditions: Vapor retarder is installed
exceptions: Intentional vented or drained assemblies designed to handle moisture bypass

subject: Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor retarder must not be installed on both sides of a wall assembly
conditions: Wall assembly separates conditioned from unconditioned space
exceptions: Allows drying to both exterior and interior (e.g., both layers are Class III or one side is intentionally vented)

subject: Thermal Break
rule: A thermal break must maintain continuous separation between interior and exterior conductive paths
conditions: Used in fenestration assemblies (windows, doors, curtain walls)
Located in climate zones with significant indoor-outdoor temperature differential

subject: Thermal Break
rule: Thermal break material must have low thermal conductivity (typically k ≤ 0.5 W/m·K)
conditions: Used in any building envelope assembly

subject: Thermal Break
rule: Thermal break must not have voids, gaps, or discontinuities that create a direct thermal path across the assembly
conditions: Installed in any building envelope system

subject: Bituminous Membrane
rule: Bituminous membrane must not be directly exposed to prolonged ultraviolet (UV) radiation without protective coating or covering
conditions: Used as exposed top layer of roofing or waterproofing
exceptions: Membrane formulated with UV-stabilizers specifically rated for exposed use by manufacturer

subject: Bituminous Membrane
rule: Bituminous membrane must be installed on a surface temperature above the minimum application temperature specified by the manufacturer
conditions: Installation using torch-applied or self-adhesive methods
exceptions: Cold-applied adhesive systems that do not require elevated substrate temperature for adhesion

subject: Bituminous Membrane
rule: Bituminous membrane must not be installed directly over wet or frost-covered substrate
conditions: Any installation

subject: Bituminous Membrane
rule: Bituminous membrane laps and seams must be fully bonded to prevent water ingress
conditions: All installation configurations

subject: EPDM Membrane
rule: EPDM membrane must be installed in a single-ply sheet configuration over the roof substrate
conditions: when used as roof covering
exceptions: when membrane is prefabricated into reinforced panels with certified seam welding

subject: EPDM Membrane
rule: EPDM membrane must not be left exposed to direct ultraviolet radiation without a protective coating or ballast layer
conditions: when EPDM is the topmost layer of the assembly
exceptions: when membrane is UV-stabilized grade certified for exposed application

subject: EPDM Membrane
rule: EPDM membrane must be fully adhered or mechanically fastened at laps and terminations to prevent wind uplift
conditions: in wind zones with basic wind speed exceeding 110 mph per ASCE 7
exceptions: when a heavy ballast system (minimum 10 psf) is used per engineering design

subject: Liquid-Applied Membrane
rule: Liquid-applied membrane must be applied to a clean, dry, and sound substrate
conditions: Used as waterproofing on roofs, decks, or below-grade surfaces
exceptions: Primed or specially prepared substrates that meet manufacturer requirements

subject: Liquid-Applied Membrane
rule: Liquid-applied membrane must be applied within the manufacturer-specified ambient and substrate temperature range
conditions: All applications
exceptions: Products specifically formulated for cold-weather or hot-weather application

subject: Liquid-Applied Membrane
rule: Liquid-applied membrane must not be applied during precipitation or when precipitation is imminent
conditions: Outdoor applications
exceptions: None — liquid water in the uncured film causes washout, pinholes, and loss of continuity

subject: Liquid-Applied Membrane
rule: Liquid-applied membrane must reach the specified dry film thickness
conditions: Used as primary waterproofing layer
exceptions: None — thickness below spec directly reduces tensile strength and puncture resistance

subject: PVC/TPO Membrane
rule: PVC/TPO membrane must be installed with a minimum thickness that prevents puncture and tear under expected service loads
conditions: when used as the primary waterproofing layer on low-slope roofs
when subject to foot traffic or hail exposure
exceptions: when a separate protective layer (e.g., walkway pads, gravel ballast) is installed over the membrane

subject: PVC/TPO Membrane
rule: PVC/TPO membrane seams must be heat-welded with overlapping material to form a watertight bond
conditions: when used as a single-ply roofing membrane
exceptions: self-adhered or solvent-weld variants of PVC/TPO that specify alternative approved seam methods

subject: PVC/TPO Membrane
rule: PVC/TPO membrane must not be installed in direct contact with incompatible materials such as unprimed asphalt, coal tar, or solvent-based adhesives
conditions: when membrane is fully adhered or laid directly over existing roofing or substrates
exceptions: when a compatible separation layer (e.g., nonwoven polyester, gypsum board) is placed between the membrane and the incompatible material

subject: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
rule: Self-adhered sheet membrane must be applied to a clean, dry, and properly prepared substrate
conditions: When used as a waterproofing or air barrier layer
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified surface treatments that differ from standard preparation

subject: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
rule: Self-adhered sheet membrane must not be applied at temperatures below the manufacturer's minimum application temperature
conditions: During installation
exceptions: Use of manufacturer-approved cold-weather application procedures or adhesive primers that extend the low-temperature range

subject: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
rule: Self-adhered sheet membrane must be protected from direct UV exposure within the time limit specified by the manufacturer
conditions: When exposed to sunlight during construction or in temporary exposed applications
exceptions: Membranes specifically rated and tested for long-term UV exposure

subject: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
rule: Self-adhered sheet membrane laps must be installed with the minimum overlap width specified by the manufacturer
conditions: At all membrane-to-membrane seam overlaps and end laps
exceptions: Manufacturer-approved detail assemblies using mastic or sealant in lieu of standard lap width

subject: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
rule: Self-adhered sheet membrane must not be applied over sharp projections, rough surfaces, or unsealed penetrations without proper treatment
conditions: At penetrations, ties, fasteners, or substrate irregularities
exceptions: Use of manufacturer-approved primers, patching compounds, or flashings that smooth and seal the penetration

subject: Drainage Composite / Protection Board
rule: Drainage composite / protection board must be installed with its drainage channels oriented to allow water flow toward the designated drainage outlet
conditions: the component is used as part of a roof or below-grade waterproofing system
exceptions: the board is used solely as a protection layer without drainage function (e.g., over a fully bonded waterproofing membrane that does not require drainage)

subject: Drainage Composite / Protection Board
rule: Drainage composite / protection board must not be subjected to compressive loads exceeding its specified compressive strength rating
conditions: the board is installed in a load-bearing application such as a green roof, plaza deck, or vehicular pavement

subject: Drainage Composite / Protection Board
rule: Drainage composite / protection board must have a filter fabric layer (when specified) placed on the correct side to prevent soil or fines migration into the drainage core
conditions: the board is used in contact with soil, growing medium, or granular backfill
exceptions: the board is manufactured with an integrated fabric that is non-detachable and factory-oriented

subject: Membrane Lap Sealant / Primer
rule: Membrane lap sealant/primer must be compatible with the underlying membrane material to achieve adhesion
conditions: When used to seal laps in membrane roofing systems

subject: Membrane Lap Sealant / Primer
rule: Membrane lap sealant/primer must not be applied to wet, frosty, or contaminated surfaces
conditions: During installation or repair of membrane laps

subject: Membrane Lap Sealant / Primer
rule: Membrane lap sealant/primer must be applied within its specified temperature range
conditions: When field-applying lap sealant or primer

subject: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
rule: Metal flashing / counter-flashing must be lapped and sealed at joints to prevent water ingress
conditions: Where used as through-wall flashing, counter-flashing, or cap flashing at roof-to-wall intersections
exceptions: Continuously welded or factory-fabricated single-piece flashing sections

subject: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
rule: Metal flashing / counter-flashing must be installed with proper end dams or turned-up edges at terminations
conditions: At horizontal or sloped ends where flashing terminates, and at changes in direction
exceptions: Flashing that drains freely to an exposed surface with no adjacent wall assembly below

subject: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
rule: Metal counter-flashing must not be installed without being locked into or covering the top edge of the base flashing or through-wall flashing
conditions: At roof-to-wall intersections where counter-flashing overlaps base flashing
exceptions: Systems using continuous reglet or receiver that mechanically holds both flashings

subject: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
rule: Metal flashing / counter-flashing must be installed with a minimum positive slope (pitch) directing water away from the building interior
conditions: Horizontal or nearly horizontal flashing surfaces such as sills, ledges, set-back ledges, or coping tops
exceptions: Factory-sloped coping or pre-pitched flashing sections designed for zero-slope installation

subject: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
rule: Metal flashing / counter-flashing must be separated by a capillary break from adjacent porous materials
conditions: Where flashing contacts masonry, concrete, or stone
exceptions: Flashing bonded with a full-bed sealant that completely eliminates the capillary gap

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
rule: below-grade waterproofing system must form a continuous watertight barrier around the entire below-grade structure
conditions: permanent below-grade occupancy or habitable space exists
groundwater table is within or above the depth of the lowest occupied floor
exceptions: structures that are intentionally designed to allow controlled groundwater ingress (e.g., drainage slab design in garages with no habitable use below grade)

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
rule: below-grade waterproofing system must be applied on the positive side (exterior/wet side) of the below-grade structure
conditions: the waterproofing system is of the membrane type (sheet or liquid-applied)
there is permanent below-grade occupancy
exceptions: interior negative-side waterproofing may be used when exterior access is physically impossible (e.g., existing structures undergoing remediation where excavation is infeasible)

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
rule: below-grade waterproofing system must be protected from damage during backfilling and construction
conditions: the waterproofing membrane has been installed
compacted granular or earth backfill will be placed against the wall
exceptions: shotcrete or cast-in-place concrete walls that integrate waterproofing into the concrete mix may not require separate protection board

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
rule: below-grade waterproofing system must not be installed on surfaces that are wet, frost-covered, or have standing water
conditions: the waterproofing is a bonded membrane (sheet or liquid-applied)
exceptions: self-healing or hydraulic cementitious systems designed specifically for application on damp surfaces

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
rule: below-grade waterproofing system must be detailed to accommodate structural movement and settlement without tearing
conditions: the structure is founded on compressible soils
the building includes deep basement levels subject to differential settlement
exceptions: structures on solid rock with negligible predicted movement

subject: Roof Waterproofing System (Low-Slope)
rule: low-slope roof waterproofing membrane must be continuous and monolithic across the entire roof surface
conditions: low-slope roof (slope less than approximately 2:12 or 14 degrees)
exceptions: roofs that are fully covered by ballast or a separate protective wearing course where membrane joints are directly lapped and sealed according to manufacturer specifications

subject: Roof Waterproofing System (Low-Slope)
rule: low-slope roof waterproofing membrane must have a positive drainage path directing water to controlled outlets
conditions: low-slope roof (slope less than approximately 2:12 or 14 degrees)
exceptions: roofs designed as plaza decks or inverted roof membrane assemblies (IRMA) where water drains through a drainage layer above the membrane and the membrane acts as a secondary barrier — but even these require a drainage path to outlets

subject: Roof Waterproofing System (Low-Slope)
rule: low-slope roof waterproofing membrane must be protected from direct UV radiation exposure unless the membrane material is specifically UV-resistant
conditions: low-slope roof (slope less than approximately 2:12 or 14 degrees)
membrane material is not inherently UV-stable (e.g., APP-modified bitumen is UV-resistant; SBS-modified bitumen, EPDM, and many single-ply membranes require protection)
exceptions: membranes rated/listed by manufacturer as UV-stable for exposed installation without protective coating, ballast, or covering

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must have a waterproof membrane layer beneath growing medium and drainage components
conditions: any green roof assembly

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must have a drainage layer to prevent standing water and root suffocation
conditions: any green roof assembly

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must have a root barrier layer to prevent root penetration into the waterproof membrane and structure
conditions: any green roof assembly with vegetation having aggressive root systems
any extensive or intensive green roof with woody or deep-rooted plants
exceptions: green roofs using only shallow-rooted sedum mats where the root barrier is integrated into the drainage mat and manufacturer confirms no separate layer is needed

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must not exceed the structural load capacity of the supporting building roof deck
conditions: any green roof assembly

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must have a slope that allows drainage without causing erosion of growing medium
conditions: any green roof assembly

subject: Green / Vegetated Roof System
rule: green roof system must not use growing medium that retains water beyond the drainage capacity of the assembly
conditions: any green roof assembly

subject: Clay Brick
rule: Clay bricks must be protected from sustained water saturation (e.g., via a damp-proof course, flashing, or capillary break) when used in contact with or near the ground in exterior walls
conditions: clay brick used in exterior wall assembly
brick in contact with or within 150 mm of finished grade
exceptions: bricks rated as severe weathering (SW) and installed with full-bed mortar and tooled joints in a well-drained assembly where testing confirms no freeze-thaw damage

subject: Clay Brick
rule: Clay bricks must not be laid when the ambient temperature is below 4 °C (40 °F) unless an approved cold-weather masonry plan (including heated materials and enclosure) is in effect
conditions: clay brick masonry construction in progress
exceptions: mortar modified with an approved non-chloride accelerator and all materials maintained above freezing until initial set

subject: Concrete Brick
rule: concrete brick must have minimum compressive strength for load-bearing applications
conditions: when used in structural/load-bearing walls or elements
exceptions: non-load-bearing applications such as decorative veneers or partitions

subject: Concrete Brick
rule: concrete brick must not have moisture content exceeding threshold before installation in freezing climates
conditions: when installed in climates subject to freeze-thaw cycles

subject: Concrete Brick
rule: concrete brick must be cured before use

subject: Concrete Brick
rule: concrete brick must have adequate bond strength with mortar
conditions: when assembled into masonry walls

subject: Glass Brick
rule: Glass brick must be used only in non-load-bearing applications
conditions: When used in walls as infill
When used in partitions
When used in decorative openings
exceptions: Specially engineered glass brick structural systems designed by a structural engineer

subject: Glass Brick
rule: Glass brick must not be installed where direct impact is expected
conditions: When used at ground level
When used in areas with vehicular traffic
When used in handrail or guardrail assemblies
exceptions: Laminated or tempered glass brick assemblies specifically rated for impact resistance

subject: Glass Brick
rule: Glass brick must accommodate thermal expansion and contraction
conditions: When installed in exterior walls
When span exceeds manufacturer's recommended maximum
exceptions: Interior applications with stable temperature conditions within manufacturer limits

subject: Glass Brick
rule: Glass brick must not be used in fire-rated wall assemblies unless specifically tested and rated
conditions: When fire separation is required between building areas
When required by building code
exceptions: Glass brick assemblies that have been tested and listed with a fire-resistance rating per applicable building code

subject: Brick Wall Assembly
rule: a brick wall assembly must have a foundation or structural support capable of bearing its dead load
conditions: when acting as a load-bearing wall
exceptions: when the wall is non-load-bearing (curtain wall, infill panel) and fully supported by adjacent structure

subject: Brick Wall Assembly
rule: a brick wall assembly must not be built without adequate lateral bracing or tie-back anchors
conditions: when the wall is freestanding or taller than its unsupported height limit
exceptions: when the wall is a low garden/retaining wall below code-stipulated height and self-stabilizing

subject: Brick Wall Assembly
rule: a brick wall assembly must have weep holes or equivalent drainage provisions at the base of the cavity
conditions: when the wall is a cavity wall or veneer wall with an air gap
exceptions: when the wall is a solid masonry wall without a cavity (no trapped moisture zone)

subject: Brick Arch
rule: a brick arch must have a keystone at the crown
conditions: true arch (not a corbeled arch)
voussoir construction

subject: Brick Arch
rule: brick arch voussoirs must be wedge-shaped (tapered) to enable radial compression
conditions: true arch construction

subject: Brick Arch
rule: a brick arch must not span a gap wider than the maximum stable span for its rise-to-span ratio and material strength
conditions: unreinforced masonry arch
exceptions: segmental or semicircular arches with engineered backfill and reinforced abutments

subject: Brick Arch
rule: a brick arch must have abutments or piers capable of resisting the horizontal thrust
conditions: any arch subject to gravity loads

subject: Brick Veneer
rule: brick veneer must be installed with a minimum 25 mm (1 inch) air cavity between the brick and the sheathing/backup wall
conditions: brick veneer installed as exterior cladding over a framed or masonry backup wall
construction in regions requiring drainage behind cladding
exceptions: thin brick veneer adhered directly to substrate (adhered veneer) does not require this cavity

subject: Brick Veneer
rule: brick veneer must be provided with weep openings at the bottom of the cavity (above flashing) to allow drainage of any water that enters the cavity
conditions: brick veneer with air cavity as per above condition
continuous flashing present at base of veneer
exceptions: adhered veneer systems without a cavity

subject: Brick Veneer
rule: brick veneer must not be used as the primary lateral or gravity load-resisting structural element (e.g., must not replace studs, beams, or columns for building lateral resistance)
conditions: brick veneer used as non-structural cladding over a structural backup system
exceptions: engineered masonry walls designed as structural shear walls (these are not 'veneer' but structural masonry)

subject: Brick Veneer
rule: brick veneer anchorage (ties) must connect the brick to the structural backup wall at maximum 600 mm (24 inches) on center horizontally and 400 mm (16 inches) on center vertically
conditions: brick veneer over framed or masonry backup wall
standard residential/commercial veneer installation
exceptions: engineered tie spacing approved by a structural engineer for specific loading conditions

subject: Brick Pillar/Pier
rule: a brick pillar/pier must be vertically aligned and bear directly on a foundation capable of supporting its full dead and live loads
conditions: when used as a structural support element

subject: Brick Pillar/Pier
rule: a brick pillar/pier must have a height-to-thickness (slenderness) ratio that prevents buckling under design loads
conditions: when used as a load-bearing element

subject: Brick Pillar/Pier
rule: a brick pillar/pier must not be constructed with unfired (mud) bricks or non-load-bearing units in a load-bearing application
conditions: when the pillar/pier is intended to carry structural loads

subject: Brick Pillar/Pier
rule: a brick pillar/pier must not have unreinforced horizontal masonry joints that are unfilled or have inadequate mortar bedding
conditions: when the pillar/pier is load-bearing

subject: Brick Coping
rule: brick coping must be installed with a positive slope away from the wall face to shed water
conditions: when used as a wall cap or parapet coping

subject: Brick Coping
rule: brick coping must have a drip edge or projection beyond the wall face below
conditions: when installed at the top of a wall or parapet

subject: Brick Coping
rule: brick coping must not be laid with head joints aligned vertically in consecutive courses (running bond must have joints offset)
conditions: when composed of multiple brick units in more than one course

subject: Brick Coping
rule: brick coping must be anchored or secured against wind uplift
conditions: when installed as a loose-laid or non-adhered coping on a parapet or free-standing wall
exceptions: if coping units are heavy enough (e.g., large precast) and friction alone resists design wind loads — but this is rare for individual brick units

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must have wall ties connecting inner and outer leaves
conditions: Cavity width exceeds 50mm
Wall height exceeds any single storey
exceptions: Wall is fully load-bearing masonry without cavity

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must have cavity width of at least 50mm and no more than 150mm
conditions: Wall is a ventilated or insulated cavity wall
exceptions: Specially engineered narrow cavity systems with proprietary ties and full structural calculations

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must not have mortar droppings or debris bridging the cavity

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must have weep holes at the base of the outer leaf above any flashing
conditions: Wall is above ground level
Wall has horizontal damp-proof course or flashing at base
exceptions: Wall has a drained cavity system with proprietary drainage channels

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must have its cavity extending at least 150mm below the damp-proof course level
conditions: Wall has a damp-proof course
exceptions: Wall is designed with a proprietary cavity tray system that provides equivalent protection

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must not have thermal insulation that completely fills the cavity without provision for drainage
conditions: Full-fill cavity insulation is used
exceptions: Insulation material is closed-cell and water-repellent with a proven drainage design
Wall is in a climate zone with negligible wind-driven rain exposure per local code

subject: Brick Cavity Wall
rule: Brick cavity wall must have ties with drip features (or be suitably inclined) to prevent water bridging across the cavity
exceptions: Wall ties made of non-absorbent material with no continuous water path

subject: Brick Lintel
rule: A brick lintel must be supported at both ends by masonry or structural framing to transfer vertical loads
conditions: Used in load-bearing wall
Spanning an opening such as a window or door

subject: Brick Lintel
rule: A brick lintel must not be used where the opening span exceeds the safe allowable span of unreinforced brick masonry
conditions: Lintel is unreinforced brick masonry
Opening serves a structural wall
exceptions: Lintel is reinforced with embedded steel or prestressed elements

subject: Brick Lintel
rule: A brick lintel must be at least as wide as the wall in which it is installed
conditions: Lintel is in a solid masonry wall

subject: Standard Hollow CMU
rule: Standard Hollow CMU must have minimum 25% solid area when used in load-bearing applications per ASTM C90
conditions: when used in load-bearing walls or applications
exceptions: non-load-bearing partitions or veneer applications

subject: Standard Hollow CMU
rule: Standard Hollow CMU must net compressive strength at least 1900 psi (13.1 MPa) for load-bearing applications per ASTM C90
conditions: when used in load-bearing walls or applications
exceptions: non-load-bearing applications where lower strength may be acceptable per structural design

subject: Standard Hollow CMU
rule: Standard Hollow CMU must not have web thickness less than 0.75 inches (19 mm) for units 6 inches or wider
conditions: for units with nominal width of 6 inches or greater

subject: Standard Hollow CMU
rule: Standard Hollow CMU must not have face shell thickness less than 1.0 inch (25 mm) for units 6 inches or wider
conditions: for units with nominal width of 6 inches or greater

subject: Solid CMU
rule: Solid CMU must have a minimum bearing length at supports
conditions: when used as a beam or lintel
when spanning an opening

subject: Solid CMU
rule: Solid CMU must not be used below grade without proper waterproofing
conditions: when in contact with soil
exceptions: if waterproofing membrane and drainage system are installed

subject: Solid CMU
rule: Solid CMU must not be unreinforced in seismic design categories D, E, or F
conditions: when located in high seismic zones
when used as a loadbearing wall

subject: Solid CMU
rule: Solid CMU must have control joints at maximum 20-foot intervals
conditions: in loadbearing walls
in long wall runs
exceptions: if wall is internally reinforced to control cracking

subject: Lightweight CMU
rule: Lightweight CMU must have a minimum compressive strength of 1900 psi (13.1 MPa) when used in load-bearing applications
conditions: when used in load-bearing walls or structural applications

subject: Lightweight CMU
rule: Lightweight CMU must not have an oven-dry density exceeding 105 lb/ft³ (1680 kg/m³)

subject: Lightweight CMU
rule: Lightweight CMU must have a maximum water absorption rate as specified by ASTM C90 for the given density grade

subject: Ground-Face/Polished CMU
rule: Ground-Face/Polished CMU must have a minimum net area compressive strength of 1900 psi (13.1 MPa) when used in loadbearing applications
conditions: When used in loadbearing walls or structural applications
exceptions: Non-loadbearing applications such as veneers or interior partitions

subject: Ground-Face/Polished CMU
rule: Ground-Face/Polished CMU must not have exposed steel reinforcement or metallic aggregates that can corrode and cause surface spalling
conditions: When polished surface is exposed to weather or exterior environments
When the CMU contains embedded steel or metallic aggregate within the exposed face
exceptions: Interior applications with controlled humidity
When metallic components are fully sealed with corrosion-resistant coating verified to remain intact after polishing

subject: Glazed/Faced CMU
rule: Glazed/Faced CMU must be installed with proper mortar joints to maintain structural integrity
conditions: When used as a structural wall system
exceptions: Dry-stacked CMU systems specifically designed for mortarless assembly

subject: Glazed/Faced CMU
rule: Glazed/Faced CMU must not be exposed to freeze-thaw cycles without appropriate water-resistant glazing or sealing
conditions: When installed in exterior applications in climates with freezing temperatures
exceptions: Units specifically rated and tested for freeze-thaw exposure without additional sealing

subject: Glazed/Faced CMU
rule: Glazed/Faced CMU must be installed on a level, structurally adequate foundation capable of supporting the wall load
conditions: When used in load-bearing applications

subject: Glazed/Faced CMU
rule: Glazed/Faced CMU must not have the glazed face used as a structural bearing surface for concentrated loads
exceptions: Where the glazed unit is specifically designed and tested for such loading

subject: Interlocking/Retaining Wall CMU
rule: Interlocking/retaining wall CMU must be designed to resist overturning and sliding under lateral earth and water pressures
conditions: when used as a retaining wall
when backfilled
exceptions: when temporary shoring or alternative restraint systems are used and verified by a geotechnical engineer

subject: Interlocking/Retaining Wall CMU
rule: Interlocking/retaining wall CMU must have adequate drainage (weep holes or drainage aggregate) to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup behind the wall
conditions: when retaining soil
when groundwater or infiltration is possible
exceptions: where a waterproofing system with positive drainage is verified to fully prevent water accumulation

subject: Interlocking/Retaining Wall CMU
rule: Interlocking/retaining wall CMU units must not be stacked beyond their manufacturer-specified unreinforced height limit without engineered reinforcement
conditions: when used in gravity or cantilever retaining wall mode
exceptions: where structural reinforcement (grid, geogrid, or rebar) is designed per IBC/ACI 530

subject: Interlocking/Retaining Wall CMU
rule: Interlocking/retaining wall CMU must be installed on a properly compacted base foundation with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: for all permanent retaining wall installations
exceptions: temporary walls on engineered bedrock verified by soils report

subject: Aerated Autoclaved Concrete (AAC) Block
rule: AAC block must not be used in direct contact with soil or in below-grade applications without an appropriate damp-proof membrane or waterproofing barrier
conditions: AAC block is used in foundation walls
AAC block is in contact with earth
exceptions: AAC block is protected by a continuous damp-proof membrane
AAC block is treated with an approved integral water repellent and applied with waterproof coating

subject: Aerated Autoclaved Concrete (AAC) Block
rule: AAC block must be protected from direct exposure to freeze-thaw cycles when saturated
conditions: AAC block is in an exterior application in climate zones with freezing temperatures
AAC block is exposed to moisture sources (rain, splash, snow)
exceptions: AAC block is protected by a drained and ventilated rainscreen cladding
AAC block has a continuous exterior insulation and weather barrier system

subject: Aerated Autoclaved Concrete (AAC) Block
rule: AAC block must be supported on a continuous level footing or base that prevents point loading and differential settlement
conditions: AAC block is used as loadbearing walling
AAC block walls are of masonry construction
exceptions: The AAC assembly is designed as non-loadbearing infill within a structural frame

subject: Aerated Autoclaved Concrete (AAC) Block
rule: AAC block mortar joints must be thin (1-3 mm) using purpose-manufactured thin-bed adhesive, not conventional thick-bed cement mortar
conditions: AAC block is laid as masonry

subject: CMU Lintel Block
rule: CMU lintel block must be placed above an opening (door, window, or other penetration) in a masonry wall
conditions: When used in load-bearing or non-load-bearing masonry walls

subject: CMU Lintel Block
rule: CMU lintel block must be laid with the open/web side facing up when used as a bond beam or lintel
conditions: When used to receive reinforcement and grout over an opening

subject: CMU Lintel Block
rule: CMU lintel block must not be used without reinforcement and grout fill when spanning an opening
conditions: When the lintel is load-bearing or spans more than a nominal width (e.g., greater than 600 mm)
exceptions: Non-load-bearing applications over very narrow openings (e.g., small conduits) where local codes permit unreinforced lintels

subject: CMU Corner Block
rule: CMU Corner Block must have a minimum compressive strength of 1900 psi (13.1 MPa) for load-bearing applications
conditions: when used in load-bearing walls
exceptions: non-load-bearing interior partitions

subject: CMU Corner Block
rule: CMU Corner Block must maintain a minimum nominal face shell thickness of 3/4 inch (19 mm) for standard 8-inch units
conditions: when manufactured as standard hollow CMU
exceptions: specially designed non-standard units with equivalent structural performance

subject: CMU Corner Block
rule: CMU Corner Block must not have a web thickness less than 3/4 inch (19 mm) for standard 8-inch units
conditions: when manufactured as standard hollow load-bearing CMU

subject: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
rule: CMU half block / stretcher block must have a minimum nominal face width of 4 inches (actual ~3-5/8 inches)
conditions: When used as a modular masonry unit in a wall assembly

subject: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
rule: CMU half block / stretcher block must have compression strength meeting ASTM C90 requirements for loadbearing units (minimum 1900 psi net area)
conditions: When used in loadbearing walls
exceptions: Non-loadbearing partition applications

subject: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
rule: CMU half block / stretcher block must not have face shells thinner than the minimum specified in ASTM C90 (minimum 3/4 inch for 4-inch units, 1 inch for 6-inch and larger)
conditions: When manufactured as a standard hollow CMU
exceptions: Solid units where minimum face shell thickness does not apply

subject: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
rule: CMU half block / stretcher block must have maximum water absorption within ASTM C90 limits (maximum 10 lb/ft³ for lightweight, 13 lb/ft³ for medium weight, 15 lb/ft³ for normal weight)
conditions: When exposed to exterior environmental conditions
exceptions: Interior-only applications with no moisture exposure

subject: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
rule: CMU half block / stretcher block must not exceed ASTM C90 dimensional tolerances (maximum ±1/8 inch in width, ±1/8 inch in height, ±3/16 inch in length)
conditions: When used in a grouted or reinforced wall system requiring alignment

subject: Horizontal Joint Reinforcement
rule: Horizontal joint reinforcement must have a minimum embedment length of 6 inches (or as specified by structural design) into the mortar bed on each side of a masonry wythe
conditions: When used in reinforced masonry walls
When spanning across control joints or expansion joints

subject: Horizontal Joint Reinforcement
rule: Horizontal joint reinforcement must be completely embedded in mortar, with no exposed or protruding portions after installation
conditions: Always applicable when joint reinforcement is installed

subject: Horizontal Joint Reinforcement
rule: Horizontal joint reinforcement must not be placed across an uninterrupted control joint or seismic isolation joint without a proprietary slip-tie or purpose-designed connector that accommodates movement
conditions: When control joints or seismic joints are present in the wall

subject: Horizontal Joint Reinforcement
rule: The lap splice length for horizontal joint reinforcement must be at least 16 inches or as specified by applicable building code (e.g., TMS 402/602) for the given wire diameter
conditions: When two pieces of joint reinforcement are overlapped (spliced)

subject: Vertical Rebar in CMU
rule: Vertical rebar in CMU must be fully embedded within grouted cells
conditions: CMU wall construction
reinforced masonry

subject: Vertical Rebar in CMU
rule: Vertical rebar in CMU must have minimum clear distance between bars to allow grout flow
conditions: grouted CMU walls
multiple vertical bars in same cell

subject: Vertical Rebar in CMU
rule: Vertical rebar in CMU must not be placed where it obstructs required cell grouting
conditions: partially grouted CMU construction

subject: Vertical Rebar in CMU
rule: Vertical rebar in CMU must be adequately lapped or continuous through the wall height
conditions: multi-story CMU walls
walls taller than single rebar length

subject: CMU Control Joint / Expansion Joint Material
rule: CMU control joint / expansion joint material must be placed at intervals where cracking from thermal or moisture movement is expected in masonry walls
conditions: CMU wall construction
unreinforced masonry
walls without sufficient reinforcement to control cracking
exceptions: walls fully reinforced with designed crack control
walls with bonded waterproofing or cladding systems that accommodate movement independently

subject: CMU Control Joint / Expansion Joint Material
rule: CMU control joint / expansion joint material must be compressible and able to accommodate cyclic movement without extrusion or bond failure
conditions: all CMU control joint applications

subject: CMU Control Joint / Expansion Joint Material
rule: CMU control joint / expansion joint material must not be rigid or bonded to masonry on both sides (must function as a plane of weakness)
conditions: vertical control joints in CMU walls
exceptions: isolation joints at dissimilar materials where full separation is intended

subject: CMU Wall Ties / Anchors
rule: CMU wall ties/anchors must be corrosion-resistant (hot-dip galvanized, stainless steel, or equivalent)
conditions: Any CMU wall tie or anchor installation in exterior walls or below-grade applications
exceptions: Interior non-load-bearing partition walls with no exposure to moisture

subject: CMU Wall Ties / Anchors
rule: CMU wall ties/anchors must provide a minimum embedment depth of 1.5 inches (38 mm) into the masonry bed joint
conditions: Standard CMU wall construction with wire ties or adjustable anchors
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified embedment depths listed in an approved evaluation report may supersede when tested for equivalent performance

subject: CMU Wall Ties / Anchors
rule: CMU wall ties/anchors must not be spaced more than the maximum allowable spacing (typically 32 inches o.c. horizontally and 16 inches o.c. vertically for veneer ties)
conditions: Anchoring masonry veneer to a backing wall
exceptions: Engineered designs with rational analysis and approved alternate spacing per building code

subject: CMU Washout Access / Cleanout
rule: CMU washout access / cleanout must be located at or near the lowest point of the masonry wall section or cavity being cleaned
conditions: CMU wall construction includes a cavity or interior space requiring washout debris removal

subject: CMU Washout Access / Cleanout
rule: CMU washout access / cleanout must remain accessible after wall completion for inspection and cleaning
conditions: Cleanout is installed within a CMU wall assembly

subject: CMU Washout Access / Cleanout
rule: CMU washout access / cleanout must not be located where it compromises the structural integrity of the masonry wall
conditions: Cleanout is installed in a load-bearing CMU wall

subject: CMU Wall Assembly (grouted & reinforced)
rule: CMU wall assemblies (grouted & reinforced) must have reinforcement placed and grouted before the grout achieves initial set
conditions: Wall is loadbearing
Wall is grouted and reinforced

subject: CMU Wall Assembly (grouted & reinforced)
rule: CMU wall assemblies (grouted & reinforced) must not have vertical reinforcement spaced more than the code-maximum spacing
conditions: Wall is in a seismic design category C, D, E, or F
Wall is loadbearing
exceptions: Engineered design with special detailing approved by the building official

subject: CMU Wall Assembly (grouted & reinforced)
rule: CMU walls must have cleanout openings at the bottom of each vertical cell that contains reinforcement
conditions: Wall is grouted and reinforced
Grout is of the type requiring inspection of the cell before pouring
exceptions: Grout lift height is less than 5 feet and the cell is visibly clean from the top

subject: CMU Wall Assembly (grouted & reinforced)
rule: CMU wall assemblies (grouted & reinforced) must not be grouted in freezing weather without proper protection
conditions: Ambient temperature is below 40°F (4°C) at time of grouting
Wall is being grouted
exceptions: Grout and masonry are protected and maintained above 40°F until grout reaches 75% of specified strength

subject: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
rule: CMU cavity wall assembly must include a continuous air barrier (e.g., sealed membrane, rigid insulation with taped joints, or fluid-applied coating) on the interior side of the masonry wythe to prevent uncontrolled air infiltration and exfiltration through the wall system
conditions: Wall assembly is designed as an exterior building envelope system
exceptions: Wall is purely interior and not part of the building envelope

subject: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
rule: CMU cavity wall assembly must include a continuous drainage plane and weeps at the base of the cavity to allow moisture that enters the cavity (through the outer wythe) to drain out
conditions: Wall assembly is exposed to exterior weather (rain, snow, or wind-driven moisture)
exceptions: Wall is entirely protected from moisture intrusion by an overhang or rainscreen cladding that prevents water entry into the cavity

subject: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
rule: CMU cavity wall assembly must have through-wall flashing at all interruptions in the cavity (e.g., at floor lines, window heads, and the wall base) to direct water out via weeps
conditions: Wall includes openings, floor-level transitions, or a foundation termination
exceptions: Wall has no horizontal interruptions or openings and uses a monolithic drainage plane without terminations

subject: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
rule: CMU cavity wall assembly must not have rigid insulation that bridges the full cavity and creates a continuous thermal connection (i.e., a thermal bridge) between the inner and outer wythes
conditions: Insulation is installed within the cavity space between CMU wythes
exceptions: Insulation is intentionally designed as part of a thermally broken system where a separate thermal break layer is provided at all connection points

subject: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
rule: CMU cavity wall assembly must include corrosion-resistant ties (e.g., hot-dip galvanized or stainless steel) connecting the two wythes at proper spacing
conditions: Wall has two structurally independent wythes that require lateral connection
exceptions: Wall uses a single wythe composite action design or structural bond beams that eliminate the need for discrete ties

subject: CMU Veneer System (Anchored)
rule: Anchored CMU veneer must have a minimum air gap (cavity) between the veneer and the backup wall
conditions: veneer is applied over a backup wall
exceptions: system is applied as adhered veneer directly to substrate

subject: CMU Veneer System (Anchored)
rule: Anchored CMU veneer must include corrosion-resistant shelf angles supporting the veneer at each floor level or at maximum height intervals
conditions: veneer height exceeds one story or the maximum unsupported height specified in building code

subject: CMU Veneer System (Anchored)
rule: Anchored CMU veneer must have weeps and flashings at the base of the cavity and above all openings

subject: CMU Veneer System (Anchored)
rule: Anchored CMU veneer must not be used as the primary lateral load-resisting system

subject: CMU Retaining Wall System
rule: CMU retaining wall system must have adequate drainage (weep holes or gravel backfill) to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup behind the wall
conditions: wall retains soil
wall height exceeds 1 meter
exceptions: wall is designed as a waterproof basement wall with engineered waterproofing and drainage board system

subject: CMU Retaining Wall System
rule: CMU retaining wall system must have a foundation/base that extends below the frost line
conditions: located in a climate with seasonal freezing
exceptions: soil is non-frost-susceptible (e.g., clean sand or gravel) and drainage prevents ice lens formation

subject: CMU Retaining Wall System
rule: CMU retaining wall system must not have unreinforced masonry walls exceeding a height-to-thickness ratio that would cause buckling under lateral earth pressure
conditions: wall is unreinforced
exceptions: wall is laterally supported at top and bottom by floor slabs or other structural elements

subject: Rebar Cage (Reinforcement Cage)
rule: Rebar cage must have concrete cover of at least the minimum specified thickness (typically 40mm for interior, 50mm for exterior, or per design code)
conditions: When embedded in concrete
When used in reinforced concrete structure
exceptions: Where cover is reduced per structural engineering analysis and approved by engineer of record
Where specific code provisions allow reduced cover (e.g., precast elements under controlled conditions)

subject: Rebar Cage (Reinforcement Cage)
rule: Rebar cage must not have lap splices shorter than the minimum development length specified in the governing design code
conditions: When longitudinal bars are lap-spliced
exceptions: Where mechanical couplers or welded splices are used instead of lap splices
Where engineered splice length is formally approved and exceeds code minimum

subject: Rebar Cage (Reinforcement Cage)
rule: Rebar cage must have transverse ties or stirrups at spacing no greater than the maximum specified by the design code (typically the smaller of 16x longitudinal bar diameter, 48x tie bar diameter, or least member dimension)
conditions: In columns or compression members with longitudinal rebar
exceptions: Where structural analysis demonstrates that larger spacing is adequate and is approved

subject: Reinforcing Mesh (Welded Wire Fabric)
rule: Welded wire fabric must be fully embedded within the concrete cover
conditions: When used as reinforcement in concrete elements

subject: Reinforcing Mesh (Welded Wire Fabric)
rule: Reinforcing mesh must not have a lap splice length less than the code-specified minimum
conditions: When adjacent sheets are lapped to transfer tension forces

subject: Reinforcing Mesh (Welded Wire Fabric)
rule: Welded wire fabric must not be placed where there is inadequate concrete cover to prevent corrosion
conditions: When exposed to environmental moisture or deicing salts

subject: Reinforcing Mesh (Welded Wire Fabric)
rule: Reinforcing mesh must be properly anchored at supports to prevent displacement during concrete placement
conditions: When used in slabs or walls where concrete is cast in place

subject: Galvanized Rebar
rule: Galvanized rebar must have sufficient concrete cover to prevent corrosion
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete structures
when exposed to environmental moisture or chlorides
exceptions: when used in non-structural or temporary applications where corrosion is acceptable

subject: Galvanized Rebar
rule: Galvanized rebar must not be welded using standard carbon-steel welding methods without special precautions
conditions: when welding is used for splicing or connection
exceptions: when using specially formulated zinc-compatible welding rods and procedures approved for galvanized steel

subject: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
rule: Epoxy-coated rebar must not be welded
conditions: When used as concrete reinforcement
exceptions: Pre-qualified welding procedures specifically tested for epoxy-coated rebar

subject: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
rule: Epoxy-coated rebar must have its coating repaired if damaged prior to concrete placement
conditions: When coating damage exceeds 2% of the bar surface area per linear foot
Or when bare steel is exposed

subject: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
rule: Epoxy-coated rebar must not be bent or straightened after coating application unless bending is performed by an approved method
conditions: Field bending or straightening
exceptions: Bending at room temperature using a bending machine approved by the engineer of record

subject: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
rule: Epoxy-coated rebar must be stored on cribbing or non-absorbent supports and protected from direct sunlight
conditions: During on-site storage prior to placement

subject: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
rule: Epoxy-coated rebar must not be used in elevated-temperature applications exceeding 150°F (65°C) continuously
conditions: When exposed to sustained service temperatures above 150°F

subject: Stainless Steel Rebar
rule: Stainless steel rebar must have a minimum concrete cover to prevent chloride-induced corrosion
conditions: When used in corrosive environments
When exposed to chloride ions (e.g., marine settings, deicing salts)
exceptions: When rebar is additionally protected by epoxy coating or other corrosion protection system

subject: Stainless Steel Rebar
rule: Stainless steel rebar must not be placed in direct electrical contact with carbon steel rebar
conditions: When both stainless and carbon steel rebar are used in the same structural element
exceptions: When electrical isolation is provided between the two metals

subject: Stainless Steel Rebar
rule: Stainless steel rebar must meet minimum yield strength and ductility requirements per applicable structural code
conditions: When used as primary reinforcement in load-bearing concrete structures

subject: GFRP Rebar (Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rebar)
rule: GFRP rebar must not be bent on-site at sharp angles (radius less than manufacturer-specified minimum bend diameter)
conditions: GFRP rebar is used as primary reinforcement in concrete
exceptions: Prefabricated bent shapes supplied by manufacturer

subject: GFRP Rebar (Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rebar)
rule: GFRP rebar must be protected from direct sunlight exposure exceeding manufacturer-specified duration prior to concrete encasement
conditions: GFRP rebar is stored on-site or placed but not yet covered by concrete
exceptions: Rebar is stored under opaque UV-resistant covering

subject: GFRP Rebar (Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rebar)
rule: GFRP rebar must not be welded or subjected to temperatures above the glass transition temperature of its resin matrix
conditions: GFRP rebar is used in any structural application

subject: GFRP Rebar (Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rebar)
rule: GFRP rebar must be anchored with development lengths at least the minimum specified for GFRP (not steel) per governing design code
conditions: GFRP rebar is used as tension reinforcement in concrete members
exceptions: Manufacturer-specific mechanical anchorage devices have been tested and approved for equivalent performance

subject: Stirrups (Shear Reinforcement)
rule: Stirrups must be adequately anchored around the longitudinal reinforcement to develop their yield strength
conditions: When stirrups are designed as shear reinforcement in reinforced concrete members

subject: Stirrups (Shear Reinforcement)
rule: Stirrups must not be spaced farther apart than the maximum permitted spacing per the governing design code
conditions: When stirrups are used as shear reinforcement in beams, columns, or slabs

subject: Stirrups (Shear Reinforcement)
rule: Stirrups must have a minimum cross-sectional area (or diameter) not less than the code-specified minimum shear reinforcement
conditions: When stirrups are required in a reinforced concrete member per design
exceptions: Members where analysis shows shear demand is less than half the concrete shear capacity and no minimum reinforcement is required by code

subject: Ties (Column Ties / Beam Ties)
rule: beam tie must be continuous through the beam-column joint
conditions: in moment-resisting frames
seismic design category B or higher
exceptions: when a mechanical coupler or welded splice of equal or greater strength is used at the joint face

subject: Ties (Column Ties / Beam Ties)
rule: column tie spacing must not exceed the least dimension of the column cross-section
conditions: for columns in compression
longitudinal bar diameter less than 32 mm
exceptions: when specially detailed boundary elements are used instead of ties in walls

subject: Ties (Column Ties / Beam Ties)
rule: beam tie must be closed with a 135-degree hook if used for seismic confinement
conditions: in seismic hooks for hoops
ACI 318 or equivalent code jurisdiction
exceptions: for non-seismic ties that only serve shear resistance and are not required to confine concrete

subject: Ties (Column Ties / Beam Ties)
rule: the diameter of a column tie must not be less than 6 mm
conditions: any reinforced concrete column
exceptions: when approved by a structural engineer and local building code allows smaller diameter for light construction

subject: Spiral Reinforcement (Helical Ties)
rule: Spiral reinforcement (helical ties) must have a minimum clear spacing between coils not less than the larger of 25 mm (1 inch) or 1.33 times the maximum aggregate size of the concrete
conditions: Spiral reinforcement used in concrete columns or compression members

subject: Spiral Reinforcement (Helical Ties)
rule: Spiral reinforcement must not have a pitch (spacing between turns) that exceeds 75 mm (3 inches) or one-sixth of the core diameter
conditions: Spiral used in confined concrete columns per ACI 318 / similar codes

subject: Spiral Reinforcement (Helical Ties)
rule: Spiral reinforcement must have at least 1.5 turns of extra spiral at each end of the member
conditions: Spiral ties used in columns or piles

subject: Spiral Reinforcement (Helical Ties)
rule: Spiral reinforcement bar diameter must not be less than 10 mm (3/8 inch)
conditions: Spiral used as transverse reinforcement in compression members

subject: Dowels (Dowling Bars)
rule: Dowels (dowling bars) must have a diameter that allows insertion into pre-drilled holes without excessive force or risk of binding
conditions: when used as alignment/connection dowels in precast concrete
when used in timber joinery
exceptions: When designed as expandable or wedge-type dowels

subject: Dowels (Dowling Bars)
rule: Dowels must not have a length shorter than the depth of the holes they engage
conditions: when used for structural connection or alignment

subject: Dowels (Dowling Bars)
rule: Dowels must be made of a material with sufficient shear strength to resist the design loads without fracturing
conditions: when used in structural connections transferring shear loads

subject: Dowels (Dowling Bars)
rule: Dowels must not have surface contaminants (oil, rust scale, loose debris) that prevent bonding when used with adhesive
conditions: when installed with adhesive (e.g., epoxy-grouted dowels)

subject: Reinforcement Couplers (Mechanical Connectors)
rule: reinforcement couplers must have a tensile strength equal to or greater than the specified reinforcement being connected
conditions: when used as a full-strength connection in tension zones
when connecting bars designed to develop yield stress
exceptions: connectors specifically designed and tested for partial-strength or compression-only applications

subject: Reinforcement Couplers (Mechanical Connectors)
rule: reinforcement couplers must be installed with the correct embedment length and torque as specified by the manufacturer
conditions: for threaded-type couplers
for swaged-type couplers
for any coupler type requiring mechanical tightening

subject: Reinforcement Couplers (Mechanical Connectors)
rule: reinforcement couplers must not be positioned in regions of maximum moment unless specifically designed and tested for cyclic/seismic loading
conditions: in seismic design categories requiring ductile detailing
in moment frames or ductile shear walls
exceptions: couplers that have been Type 2 tested per ACI 318 or equivalent standards for seismic applications

subject: Reinforcement Couplers (Mechanical Connectors)
rule: reinforcement couplers must maintain the specified concrete cover over the coupler body as required for the surrounding reinforcement
conditions: in corrosion-prone environments
in fire-resistance-rated assemblies
exceptions: when project-specific testing demonstrates equivalent performance with reduced cover

subject: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
rule: Reinforcement cover blocks (spacers) must have compressive strength at least equal to the specified concrete grade of the surrounding member
conditions: When used as bar supports in reinforced concrete
exceptions: When manufacturer provides certified test data demonstrating adequate performance at lower strength for the specific application

subject: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
rule: Reinforcement cover blocks must not contain materials that cause galvanic corrosion when in contact with reinforcement steel
conditions: When in contact with steel reinforcement bars

subject: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
rule: Reinforcement cover blocks (spacers) must maintain the specified concrete cover to reinforcement without movement during concrete placement
conditions: During concrete pouring and vibration

subject: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
rule: Plastic reinforcement cover blocks must be fire-resistant to at least the same rating as the structural element they serve
conditions: When plastic spacers are used in fire-rated structural elements
exceptions: When additional fire protection measures are independently provided

subject: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
rule: Reinforcement cover blocks must not chemically degrade or leach substances that attack concrete or reinforcement

subject: Chair Reinforcement (Rebar Chairs)
rule: rebar chairs must be adequately spaced to prevent concrete failure under load
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete slabs or footings
concrete is wet during placement
exceptions: when engineered design specifically allows wider spacing with verified load distribution

subject: Chair Reinforcement (Rebar Chairs)
rule: rebar chairs must be made of or coated with corrosion-resistant material when used in exterior or exposed concrete
conditions: when used in exterior slabs, bridge decks, or other weather-exposed concrete
exceptions: when chairs are entirely encapsulated within a corrosion-protected assembly or when sacrificial design is accepted

subject: Chair Reinforcement (Rebar Chairs)
rule: rebar chairs must not exceed the specified concrete cover tolerance
conditions: when concrete cover is specified in structural drawings
exceptions: when chairs are designed as integral stay-in-place forms with documented cover compliance

subject: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
rule: Tension reinforcement (main longitudinal bars) must have a specified yield strength (fy) that meets or exceeds the minimum required by the governing design code for the intended load conditions
conditions: When used as primary flexural reinforcement in reinforced concrete members

subject: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
rule: Tension reinforcement (main longitudinal bars) must be detailed with sufficient development length or anchorage beyond the critical section to develop the required bar stress
conditions: Where bars are terminated along a member span or at supports

subject: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
rule: Tension reinforcement (main longitudinal bars) must not be spliced at locations of maximum stress unless the splice is designed as a mechanical or welded connection capable of developing the full bar strength
conditions: When lap splices are used in flexural members
exceptions: When a full-tension mechanical or welded splice is provided and tested to meet code requirements

subject: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
rule: Tension reinforcement (main longitudinal bars) must have minimum clear spacing between parallel bars not less than the maximum bar diameter, 1.33 times the maximum aggregate size, or the code-specified minimum (typically 1 inch or 25 mm)
conditions: In all cast-in-place reinforced concrete members

subject: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
rule: Tension reinforcement (main longitudinal bars) must be provided with minimum concrete cover as specified by the governing code for the exposure condition and fire rating
conditions: In all reinforced concrete members exposed to weather, earth contact, or fire

subject: Compression Reinforcement
rule: compression reinforcement must be placed in the compression zone of the structural member
conditions: for reinforced concrete beams
for reinforced concrete columns
for reinforced concrete slabs

subject: Compression Reinforcement
rule: compression reinforcement must be proportioned and detailed to prevent buckling of the compression bars
conditions: when longitudinal compression reinforcement is used in columns or beams

subject: Compression Reinforcement
rule: compression reinforcement must not exceed the maximum allowable reinforcement ratio for the section
conditions: for reinforced concrete flexural members

subject: Compression Reinforcement
rule: compression reinforcement must be adequately anchored into the surrounding concrete beyond the point of inflection or at supports
conditions: where compression reinforcement is terminated or developed in continuous members

subject: Compression Reinforcement
rule: compression reinforcement must not be placed outside the confinement core defined by transverse reinforcement in columns
conditions: for seismic-resistant reinforced concrete columns

subject: Temperature & Shrinkage Reinforcement
rule: Temperature and shrinkage reinforcement must be provided in structural concrete members where the tensile stress from restrained volume change or thermal gradients could cause cracking
conditions: Member is a structural concrete slab, wall, or similar plate-type element
Tensile stresses from temperature change or shrinkage are expected to exceed concrete tensile strength
exceptions: Non-structural concrete elements
Mass concrete where internal temperature rise is controlled
Members where prestressing provides equivalent crack control

subject: Temperature & Shrinkage Reinforcement
rule: Temperature and shrinkage reinforcement ratio must not be less than the code-specified minimum (typically 0.0018 times gross concrete area for grade 60 steel)
conditions: Reinforcement is deformed bar of specified yield strength (e.g., Grade 60)
Member is a structural slab
exceptions: Where structural analysis shows reinforcement is not required and crack widths are acceptable
For slabs-on-grade where joints control cracking

subject: Temperature & Shrinkage Reinforcement
rule: Temperature and shrinkage reinforcement must not be spaced farther apart than the maximum specified spacing (typically 5 times slab thickness nor 18 inches)
conditions: Reinforcement is in a structural concrete slab
exceptions: Where alternative analysis demonstrates adequate crack control at wider spacing

subject: Moisture-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Moisture-resistant gypsum board must be installed with a vapor retarder on the warm side of the assembly
conditions: when used in exterior wall assemblies
in climate zones with high indoor humidity or cold climates
exceptions: when the assembly is designed as a 'drying' assembly with specific vapor-permeable WRB and no interior vapor retarder per building science best practice

subject: Moisture-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Moisture-resistant gypsum board must not be used in continuously wet or submerged conditions
conditions: any application where the board will be in direct contact with standing water
or subject to continuous liquid water exposure such as shower floors or exterior soffits without backing

subject: Moisture-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Moisture-resistant gypsum board must be installed with a minimum 1/4-inch gap above finished floor surfaces in wet areas
conditions: when installed in bathrooms
showers
or other wet areas with floor finishes
exceptions: when the gap is detailed per local code to be less (rare, not recommended)

subject: Moisture-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Moisture-resistant gypsum board must not be used as a tile substrate in shower compartments where code requires cementitious backer board or equivalent
conditions: when local building code explicitly prohibits gypsum-based products as tile backing in shower compartments
e.g., IRC P2709.1 or IBC 1210
exceptions: when specifically listed in an approved manufacturer's assembly and approved by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Fire-Resistant Gypsum Board (Type X)
rule: Fire-Resistant Gypsum Board (Type X) must be installed with all edges supported by framing or approved clips
conditions: Used in wall or ceiling membrane assemblies
Fire-rated assembly required
exceptions: Installation over solid backing such as existing wall or concrete

subject: Fire-Resistant Gypsum Board (Type X)
rule: Fire-Resistant Gypsum Board (Type X) must not be used in applications where sustained moisture or direct water contact is expected without appropriate moisture-resistant treatment
conditions: Exterior exposure
Wet areas such as showers or pool enclosures
exceptions: When a moisture-resistant variant (e.g., Type X with water-resistant core) is specified

subject: Mold-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Mold-resistant gypsum board must be installed in dry conditions before enclosing
conditions: When installed in new construction or renovation
exceptions: None

subject: Mold-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Mold-resistant gypsum board must not be used in continuous direct contact with standing water or in submerged applications
conditions: In wet areas such as shower floors, pool surrounds, or flood-prone zones
exceptions: None

subject: Mold-Resistant Gypsum Board
rule: Mold-resistant gypsum board must be installed with a vapor retarder when used on the warm side of exterior walls in cold climates
conditions: In climate zones with significant heating degree days (ASHRAE climate zones 5 and above)
exceptions: When the assembly is designed as a drying assembly per building science principles (e.g., certain vented cladding systems)

subject: Vapor-Retarder Gypsum Board
rule: vapor-retarder gypsum board must be installed on the warm side of the assembly relative to the vapor drive
conditions: assembly is subject to interior-to-exterior vapor drive
board is used as the primary vapor retarder
exceptions: board is used in a climate zone where vapor drive direction reverses seasonally and a Class III vapor retarder is permitted by code

subject: Vapor-Retarder Gypsum Board
rule: vapor-retarder gypsum board must not be exposed to sustained temperatures above 125 °F (52 °C)
conditions: board is installed in a location subject to elevated ambient temperatures such as near uninsulated steam pipes, boiler rooms, or attics in hot climates
exceptions: manufacturer has provided written documentation or testing that the specific product tolerates higher temperatures

subject: Vapor-Retarder Gypsum Board
rule: vapor-retarder gypsum board must be installed with vapor-retarder facing continuous and sealed at all joints, penetrations, and edges
conditions: board is serving as the primary air and vapor barrier in the assembly
exceptions: assembly uses a separate dedicated air barrier system upstream of the gypsum board

subject: Vapor-Retarder Gypsum Board
rule: vapor-retarder gypsum board must not be used as a structural shear panel to resist lateral loads
conditions: board is part of a lateral-force-resisting system such as a shear wall
exceptions: product is specifically tested and rated for shear resistance per applicable building code

subject: Gypsum Board Wall Partition
rule: gypsum board wall partition must be supported by a structural frame (studs) at top and bottom tracks and at intervals not exceeding the manufacturer's maximum spacing
conditions: used as a load-bearing or non-load-bearing interior partition

subject: Gypsum Board Wall Partition
rule: gypsum board wall partition must not have board joints aligned with door/window openings unless the opening is framed with additional stud supports
conditions: partition contains an opening for a door or window

subject: Gypsum Board Corner Bead
rule: gypsum board corner bead must be installed at all external corners of gypsum board assemblies
conditions: when gypsum board is used as a finished wall or ceiling surface
exceptions: when a different corner finishing system (e.g., bullnose corner bead, metal trim, or no bead per specification) is explicitly designed

subject: Gypsum Board Corner Bead
rule: gypsum board corner bead must be fabricated from corrosion-resistant material
conditions: when installed in areas exposed to moisture, such as bathrooms, kitchens, or basements
exceptions: when the corner bead is made of PVC/vinyl which is inherently corrosion-resistant

subject: Gypsum Board Corner Bead
rule: gypsum board corner bead must be compatible with the joint compound and finishing system used
conditions: when paper-faced or vinyl corner beads are used

subject: Gypsum Board Corner Bead
rule: gypsum board corner bead must not be installed with exposed fasteners that are not covered by joint compound
conditions: when the corner bead is part of a finished wall surface
exceptions: when the corner bead is intentionally left exposed as an architectural detail

subject: Gypsum Board Shaft Wall Assembly
rule: Gypsum board shaft wall assembly must provide a fire-resistance rating of at least 1 hour when specified as part of a fire-rated shaft enclosure
conditions: Assembly is used to enclose a vertical shaft (e.g., elevator, stair, mechanical shaft)
Fire-rated shaft is required by building code

subject: Gypsum Board Shaft Wall Assembly
rule: Gypsum board shaft wall assembly must maintain continuous attachment from the floor slab below to the underside of the floor or roof slab above without gaps
conditions: Assembly is installed as a fire-rated shaft enclosure

subject: Gypsum Board Shaft Wall Assembly
rule: Gypsum board shaft wall assembly must not be used as a lateral load-resisting element (shear wall) unless specifically designed and detailed for that purpose
conditions: Assembly is designated as non-structural shaft wall enclosure only

subject: Gypsum Board Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: gypsum board fasteners (screws/nails) must be fabricated from corrosion-resistant material or be protected against corrosion when used in exterior or high-moisture environments
conditions: exterior exposure
high-moisture interior (e.g., bathrooms, showers, locker rooms)
areas subject to condensation

subject: Gypsum Board Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: gypsum board fasteners must not be overdriven such that the fastener head breaks or punches through the paper face of the gypsum board
conditions: all gypsum board installations

subject: Gypsum Board Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: gypsum board fasteners (screws) must have a minimum thread length that engages the steel stud or wood framing member to a depth sufficient for pull-out resistance
conditions: attachment to steel studs
attachment to wood studs

subject: Gypsum Board Joint Tape and Compound
rule: Gypsum board joint tape and compound must be applied before painting or final surface finishing
conditions: When used as part of a drywall finishing system
Where gypsum board joints are to be concealed or covered
exceptions: When exposed finish is intentionally desired (e.g., industrial aesthetic)

subject: Gypsum Board Joint Tape and Compound
rule: Gypsum board joint tape and compound must be compatible with the specific gypsum board type
conditions: When the gypsum board has a specialty facing or core (e.g., fire-resistant, moisture-resistant, mold-resistant)
exceptions: Standard paper-faced gypsum board can accept nearly all common joint compounds and tapes without issue

subject: Gypsum Board Joint Tape and Compound
