rule: Gypsum board joint compound must not be applied or allowed to cure at ambient temperatures below the manufacturer's specified minimum
conditions: During application and curing of the joint compound
exceptions: When using a low-temperature-formulated compound specifically rated for cold-weather application

subject: Cement-Lime Mortar
rule: Cement-lime mortar must not be used in freezing or below-freezing temperatures during application and initial curing
conditions: Ambient temperature at time of application is at or below 0°C (32°F)
exceptions: Enclosed and heated construction site where mortar temperature can be maintained above freezing

subject: Cement-Lime Mortar
rule: Cement-lime mortar must be fully cured and reached specified compressive strength before being subjected to design loads
conditions: Mortar is in a load-bearing masonry wall or structural element
exceptions: Non-structural applications such as decorative veneers or parging

subject: Cement-Lime Mortar
rule: Cement-lime mortar must not be mixed with Portland cement alone without the specified lime content per the mix design
conditions: Mortar is being batched on-site or specified for a masonry assembly
exceptions: Pre-blended factory-manufactured mortar meeting ASTM C270 proportions

subject: Cement-Lime Mortar
rule: Cement-lime mortar must not be applied in thickness exceeding the manufacturer's or ASTM standard specified joint thickness (typically greater than 3/8 inch or 9.5 mm for bed joints)
conditions: Mortar is applied as bed joints in masonry construction
exceptions: Engineered special conditions explicitly designed with thicker joints and verified by structural analysis

subject: Lime Mortar
rule: lime mortar must not be used in load-bearing structural applications without appropriate hydraulic or cementitious additives
conditions: when used as the primary binder in structural elements
when subjected to significant compressive or tensile loads
exceptions: when used in repointing historic masonry where original structure already bears loads through other mechanisms
when used in non-load-bearing applications such as finishes, plasters, or decorative work

subject: Lime Mortar
rule: lime mortar must not be used in continuously wet or submerged conditions unless it is a hydraulic lime formulation
conditions: when exposed to persistent moisture
when in contact with groundwater without drainage
when fully submerged
exceptions: hydraulic lime (NHL 2, 3.5, or 5) can tolerate wet conditions appropriate to its hydraulic grade
non-hydraulic lime can be used in sheltered external masonry with adequate drying cycles

subject: Lime Mortar
rule: lime mortar must not be used in freezing conditions before it has adequately cured and dried
conditions: when ambient temperatures are expected to fall below 5°C within the curing period
when fresh mortar has not achieved sufficient carbonation before first frost
exceptions: if protective measures (insulation, heating, enclosures) maintain temperature above 5°C during curing

subject: Stucco Mortar
rule: Stucco mortar must have a minimum compressive strength of 800 psi when cured
conditions: when used as exterior wall cladding

subject: Stucco Mortar
rule: Stucco mortar must not be applied over a surface without a proper metal lath or approved substrate
conditions: when applied as a three-coat system over frame construction
exceptions: when applied over solid masonry or concrete surfaces that provide sufficient bond

subject: Stucco Mortar
rule: Stucco mortar must not be applied when ambient temperature is below 40°F (4°C) and falling
conditions: during application and for 48 hours after application

subject: Stucco Mortar
rule: Stucco mortar must incorporate ASTM C150 Type I/II Portland cement as a binding agent
conditions: for traditional Portland-cement-based stucco systems
exceptions: when using pre-blended factory-mixed stucco products with alternative binders certified to meet equivalent performance standards

subject: Mortar Bed
rule: mortar bed must be placed on a stable, clean, and properly prepared substrate that can support the weight of the mortar and any subsequent layers
conditions: mortar bed is installed as a base for tile, stone, or similar finish materials

subject: Mortar Bed
rule: mortar bed must have a minimum thickness sufficient to prevent cracking under expected loads
conditions: mortar bed is used in flooring or roofing applications
exceptions: thin-set mortar applications where the mortar bed is replaced by a thin adhesive layer

subject: Mortar Bed
rule: mortar bed must not be placed directly over a vapor barrier without a bonding layer or reinforcement
conditions: mortar bed is applied over a vapor retarder or waterproofing membrane
exceptions: systems specifically designed with bonded mortar beds over membranes using appropriate bonding agents

subject: Mortar Joint
rule: mortar joint must have a minimum compressive strength sufficient to bear the loads transferred from adjacent masonry units
conditions: mortar is in a load-bearing wall or structure
exceptions: non-load-bearing partitions or decorative veneers where no structural load is transferred

subject: Mortar Joint
rule: mortar joint must not have a thickness greater than specified by structural design or code
conditions: mortar joint is in a structural masonry wall
exceptions: deliberate raked or recessed joints designed for architectural effect where structural capacity is separately verified

subject: Mortar Joint
rule: mortar joint must have full and complete contact between mortar and masonry units
conditions: joint is in a load-bearing or water-resisting assembly

subject: Mortar Joint
rule: mortar joint must not have a width less than the minimum specified by code for the masonry type
conditions: joint is in any masonry construction
exceptions: thin-bed mortars specifically designed and tested for thin joints in autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) or similar systems

subject: Mortar Joint
rule: mortar joint must have adequate bond strength to resist lateral (wind/seismic) loads
conditions: wall is exposed to lateral loads from wind or seismic forces
exceptions: free-standing non-structural walls not designed for lateral resistance

subject: Tile Adhesive/Thinset
rule: Tile adhesive/thinset must be mixed with water or a specified liquid additive in the correct proportion as prescribed by the manufacturer
conditions: When preparing mortar from dry powder
exceptions: Pre-mixed ready-to-use adhesives that require no field mixing

subject: Tile Adhesive/Thinset
rule: Tile adhesive/thinset must be applied within its open time (also called 'pot life' or 'working time') before the surface skims over
conditions: During installation of tiles

subject: Tile Adhesive/Thinset
rule: Tile adhesive/thinset must not be applied to frozen substrates or when ambient temperature is below the manufacturer's minimum (typically 5°C / 40°F)
conditions: During cold-weather installation
exceptions: Products specifically formulated and certified for low-temperature application

subject: Tile Adhesive/Thinset
rule: Tile adhesive/thinset must not be spread by buttering the back of the tile (spot-bonding) as the sole method of adhesion on floor applications subject to traffic
conditions: Floor tile installations subject to foot or vehicular traffic
exceptions: Small-area repairs under 0.5 m² where full coverage is verified by pull-test

subject: Expansion Joint Sealant
rule: Expansion joint sealant must remain flexible across the full range of design movement
conditions: When installed in a working expansion joint
Where thermal or structural movement is expected
exceptions: Non-moving or static joints that do not require sealant flexibility

subject: Expansion Joint Sealant
rule: Expansion joint sealant must not experience tensile stress exceeding its elongation-at-break capacity
conditions: At the maximum design joint width opened condition

subject: Expansion Joint Sealant
rule: Expansion joint sealant must maintain continuous adhesion to both joint substrates
conditions: Throughout all design movement cycles
exceptions: Intentionally debonded backer-rod or bond-breaker tape applications where sealant is designed to adhere only to two side faces

subject: Expansion Joint Sealant
rule: Expansion joint sealant must be chemically compatible with adjacent substrate materials
conditions: When in contact with substrates such as concrete, metal, plastic, or existing sealants
exceptions: When a compatible primer or bond-breaker is interposed to prevent direct contact

subject: Firestop Sealant
rule: Firestop sealant must be compatible with the substrate materials it contacts
conditions: When applied to any building joint, penetration, or opening
exceptions: When manufacturer compatibility documentation is not available to support adhesion and bond performance

subject: Firestop Sealant
rule: Firestop sealant must have a tested fire-resistance rating equal to or greater than the fire-resistance rating of the wall or floor assembly it is installed in
conditions: When used as part of a through-penetration firestop system or for sealing gaps in fire-rated assemblies
exceptions: When the sealant is installed in a non-rated assembly or as part of a system listed with a different rating per ASTM E814 or UL 263 testing

subject: Firestop Sealant
rule: Firestop sealant must not be applied over or in contact with incompatible sealants or coatings that prevent proper adhesion or intumescent activation
conditions: When the existing material is a silicone, acrylic, or other sealant not listed as compatible by the firestop manufacturer
exceptions: When the firestop manufacturer specifically lists the existing sealant/coating as compatible through published systems testing

subject: Glazing Sealant
rule: glazing sealant must remain within its service temperature range during application and throughout its service life
conditions: sealant is installed in an exterior or thermally unregulated environment
exceptions: sealant specifically formulated for extreme temperature applications with documented performance data

subject: Glazing Sealant
rule: glazing sealant must be compatible with all adjacent materials it contacts
conditions: sealant contacts metal, glass, gaskets, or other building materials in the glazing assembly
exceptions: manufacturer has published compatibility test data showing no adverse reaction for the specific material pair

subject: Glazing Sealant
rule: glazing sealant must not come into direct contact with bituminous materials
conditions: sealant is part of a glazing assembly where bituminous products (asphalt, coal tar, etc.) are present in the adjacent construction
exceptions: a compatible barrier layer separates the sealant from the bituminous material

subject: Roofing Sealant/Lap Cement
rule: Roofing sealant/lap cement must not be applied to wet or frost-covered surfaces
conditions: Application of roofing sealant or lap cement
exceptions: Products specifically formulated for wet-surface application

subject: Roofing Sealant/Lap Cement
rule: Roofing sealant/lap cement must be applied at temperatures above the manufacturer's minimum specified temperature (typically 40°F/4°C)
conditions: Field application of roofing sealant or lap cement
exceptions: Products specifically formulated and labeled for cold-weather application

subject: Roofing Sealant/Lap Cement
rule: Roofing sealant/lap cement must be applied at a minimum thickness sufficient to ensure continuous coverage across the entire bonding surface
conditions: Bonding roofing membrane laps or sealing roof penetrations

subject: Epoxy Adhesive
rule: epoxy adhesive must be stored and applied within its specified temperature range
conditions: during storage
during mixing
during application
during curing
exceptions: formulations specifically engineered for extreme-temperature use

subject: Epoxy Adhesive
rule: epoxy adhesive must not be applied to contaminated surfaces
conditions: surface preparation prior to bonding
exceptions: adhesives explicitly formulated for wet or contaminated substrates with validated procedures

subject: Epoxy Adhesive
rule: epoxy adhesive must not exceed its pot life during application
conditions: during mixing and working stage

subject: Wallcovering Adhesive
rule: wallcovering adhesive must be compatible with the substrate material to which it is applied
conditions: adhesive is applied to a substrate

subject: Wallcovering Adhesive
rule: wallcovering adhesive must not be applied to surfaces that are wet, frosty, or have standing moisture
conditions: adhesive is being applied on-site
exceptions: adhesive specifically formulated for wet applications

subject: Wallcovering Adhesive
rule: wallcovering adhesive must have sufficient initial tack to hold the wallcovering in place until the adhesive cures
conditions: adhesive is used for vertical wall applications
exceptions: adhesive is a setting-type that requires mechanical support during cure

subject: Wallcovering Adhesive
rule: wallcovering adhesive must not contain solvents that damage or discolor the wallcovering material
conditions: adhesive is in direct contact with the wallcovering

subject: Panel/Drywall Adhesive
rule: Panel/Drywall adhesive must be compatible with the substrate material (e.g., gypsum board, wood, masonry) to which it is applied
conditions: adhesive is used to bond drywall or panel to a substrate
exceptions: mechanically fastened systems where adhesive is not used

subject: Panel/Drywall Adhesive
rule: Panel/Drywall adhesive must not be applied to surfaces that are wet, frost-covered, or below the manufacturer's minimum application temperature
conditions: adhesive is being applied on-site during construction
exceptions: adhesives specifically formulated for low-temperature or wet-surface application and tested per manufacturer specifications

subject: Panel/Drywall Adhesive
rule: Panel/Drywall adhesive must not contain asbestos or other banned hazardous substances
conditions: adhesive is used in building construction

subject: Sealant Backer Rod
rule: sealant backer rod must be compatible with the sealant material it contacts
conditions: when used as a backing material for sealant joints

subject: Sealant Backer Rod
rule: sealant backer rod must not be installed in a compressed state beyond its recommended compression ratio
conditions: when installed in a sealant joint

subject: Sealant Backer Rod
rule: sealant backer rod must be a closed-cell type when used in applications exposed to moisture or water immersion
conditions: when used in applications exposed to moisture or water immersion

subject: Primer/Sealer for Sealants
rule: primer/sealer for sealants must be chemically compatible with both the substrate and the sealant it precedes
conditions: primer/sealer is used to prepare a surface before applying a sealant

subject: Primer/Sealer for Sealants
rule: primer/sealer for sealants must not be applied to a wet, frost-covered, or contaminated surface
conditions: primer/sealer is applied in field conditions before sealant installation
exceptions: primer manufacturer specifically formulated the product for damp-surface application and provides written approval

subject: Primer/Sealer for Sealants
rule: primer/sealer for sealants must be fully cured or flashed off before the sealant is applied, unless otherwise specified by the manufacturer
conditions: a separate primer/sealer coating is applied as a distinct layer before sealant

subject: Fully-Adhered Membrane
rule: Fully-adhered membrane must be installed over a suitable substrate that is clean, dry, and free of voids or debris
conditions: when used as primary roof waterproofing layer
exceptions: none

subject: Fully-Adhered Membrane
rule: Fully-adhered membrane must not be installed when ambient temperature or substrate temperature is below the manufacturer's minimum application temperature
conditions: during installation
exceptions: none

subject: Fully-Adhered Membrane
rule: Fully-adhered membrane must not be installed over wet or frost-covered surfaces
conditions: during installation
exceptions: none

subject: Ballasted Membrane
rule: ballasted membrane roof must maintain uniform ballast coverage across the membrane surface
conditions: ballasted membrane roofing system
exceptions: designated walkway pads or service zones where ballast is intentionally removed

subject: Ballasted Membrane
rule: ballast stone size must be sufficient to resist wind uplift forces for the building's location and height
conditions: ballasted membrane roofing system

subject: Ballasted Membrane
rule: ballasted membrane must not be installed on roofs with a slope greater than the manufacturer's maximum allowable slope
conditions: ballasted membrane roofing system

subject: Mechanically-Fastened Membrane
rule: Mechanically-fastened membrane must be installed with sufficient tension to prevent fluttering or billowing under wind uplift loads
conditions: installed on roofs with slope less than 1:12
building located in wind zone with design wind speed greater than 30 m/s
exceptions: membrane protected by heavy ballast system that fully suppresses wind-induced motion

subject: Mechanically-Fastened Membrane
rule: Fastener spacing must not exceed the membrane manufacturer's specified maximum
conditions: any mechanically-fastened membrane installation
exceptions: engineer-specified spacing based on project-specific wind tunnel testing that demonstrates equivalent performance

subject: Mechanically-Fastened Membrane
rule: Mechanically-fastened membrane must not be installed over compressible insulation without a slip sheet or structural deck
conditions: insulation with compression strength below 30 psi (207 kPa)
exceptions: insulation manufacturer has published data confirming compatibility with direct attachment through compressible insulation

subject: Mechanically-Fastened Membrane
rule: Mechanically-fastened membrane must have a minimum fastener pull-out resistance of 1.5 times the design wind uplift pressure at each fastener
conditions: any mechanically-fastened membrane installation

subject: Torch-Applied Membrane
rule: Torch-applied membrane must be installed on a substrate that is dry, clean, and free of frost or ice
conditions: Installation in cold or wet weather conditions
exceptions: Enclosed/heated temporary shelter is provided around the work area

subject: Torch-Applied Membrane
rule: Torch-applied membrane must not be installed when wind conditions exceed 15 mph (or manufacturer's specification)
conditions: Open-roof installation above ground level
Use of open-flame torch
exceptions: Wind shielding is erected and manufacturer approves

subject: Torch-Applied Membrane
rule: Torch-applied membrane must be fully adhered over its entire surface with no fishmouths, wrinkles, or unbonded edges

subject: Protection Board / Cover Board
rule: Protection board / cover board must be laid over the waterproofing membrane without penetrating it
conditions: When used as a protective layer in roof or terrace assemblies
exceptions: When the protection board itself serves as the walking surface and is mechanically fastened through the membrane with approved sealed penetrations

subject: Protection Board / Cover Board
rule: Protection board must have sufficient compressive strength to resist the expected superimposed loads without crushing or deforming into the membrane
conditions: When installed below ballast, pavers, green-roof assemblies, or mechanical equipment

subject: Protection Board / Cover Board
rule: Protection board must not degrade or chemically react with the waterproofing membrane it contacts
conditions: When the board is made of materials such as extruded polystyrene, polyisocyanurate, or recycled rubber composites
exceptions: When chemical compatibility has been verified by the membrane manufacturer for the specific product pairing

subject: Protection Board / Cover Board
rule: Protection board joints must be staggered relative to the underlying membrane joints or seams
conditions: When installed in multi-layer assemblies

subject: Protection Board / Cover Board
rule: Protection board must be sufficiently thick to prevent point-load puncture from above (e.g., from foot traffic or dropped tools)
conditions: When used in accessible roof areas or construction zones

subject: Membrane Flashing / Flashing Strips
rule: Membrane flashing / flashing strips must be installed at all roof-to-wall intersections, roof edges, penetrations, and changes in roof plane to prevent water entry
conditions: When used in roofing assemblies
When the assembly is exposed to precipitation or moisture
exceptions: Zero-roof-pitch buildings in arid climates where no precipitation management is required

subject: Membrane Flashing / Flashing Strips
rule: Membrane flashing / flashing strips must not be installed upside down or with reversed lap direction relative to water flow
conditions: When installed on any sloped or drainage-directed surface

subject: Membrane Flashing / Flashing Strips
rule: Membrane flashing / flashing strips must be continuously bonded or mechanically fastened at all edges and seams to prevent wind uplift or moisture bypass
conditions: In roof assemblies subject to wind loads or weather exposure

subject: Membrane Flashing / Flashing Strips
rule: Membrane flashing / flashing strips must be compatible with the adjacent membrane and substrate materials to prevent chemical degradation or delamination
conditions: When in direct contact with another membrane
adhesive
primer
or sealant

subject: Roof Membrane Adhesive / Bonding Agent
rule: Roof membrane adhesive must be chemically compatible with both the membrane and the substrate to which it is applied
conditions: When bonding membrane to substrate or another membrane layer
Any adhesive-based roof system
exceptions: Mechanically fastened or ballasted systems that do not use adhesive

subject: Roof Membrane Adhesive / Bonding Agent
rule: Roof membrane adhesive must not trap moisture between membrane layers or between membrane and substrate
conditions: When applied in multi-ply or fully adhered systems
exceptions: Breathable adhesive systems specifically designed to allow vapor transmission

subject: Roof Membrane Adhesive / Bonding Agent
rule: Roof membrane adhesive must have sufficient thermal resistance to withstand the service temperature range of the roof assembly
conditions: All adhesive-bonded roof membrane applications

subject: Pipe Penetration Boot / Pipe Flashing
rule: Pipe penetration boot must form a watertight seal around the pipe
conditions: pipe penetrates roof membrane

subject: Pipe Penetration Boot / Pipe Flashing
rule: Pipe penetration boot must be flashed into the roof membrane or underlying base flashing
conditions: boot is used on a sloped or flat roof assembly

subject: Pipe Penetration Boot / Pipe Flashing
rule: Pipe penetration boot material must be compatible with the roof membrane material
conditions: boot and membrane contact directly
exceptions: a compatible separation layer or slip sheet is installed between them

subject: Roof Drain / Drain Flashing Assembly
rule: Roof drain / drain flashing assembly must create a watertight seal at the roof penetration point
conditions: installed on a roof membrane assembly
penetrates the roof deck or membrane
exceptions: temporary/test installations where water ingress is acceptable

subject: Roof Drain / Drain Flashing Assembly
rule: Roof drain / drain flashing assembly must maintain a continuous positive slope (minimum 1/4 inch per foot) from low points of the roof surface toward the drain inlet
conditions: installed on a low-slope or flat roof
exceptions: roofs with internal sump/tapered insulation systems specifically designed to achieve positive drainage through insulation build-up around the drain

subject: Roof Drain / Drain Flashing Assembly
rule: Roof drain flashing must be mechanically fastened or fully adhered such that it cannot separate from the roof membrane under anticipated wind uplift pressures
conditions: installed in regions with design wind speeds over 100 mph
installed on roofs with wind exposure category B or greater

subject: Expansion Joint Cover (Roof)
rule: expansion joint cover must accommodate thermal movement of the roof deck
conditions: roof has thermal exposure
expansion joint is present between roof deck sections

subject: Expansion Joint Cover (Roof)
rule: expansion joint cover must be watertight at its connections to the roof membrane
conditions: roof is designed as a waterproofing assembly
exceptions: unconditioned interior roof with no weather exposure

subject: Expansion Joint Cover (Roof)
rule: expansion joint cover must not be rigidly fixed on both sides of the joint
conditions: cover has sliding or bellows-type mechanism

subject: Acoustic Panel Perimeter Frame
rule: Acoustic panel perimeter frame must be rigid enough to support the acoustic panels without excessive deflection under self-weight and handling loads
conditions: When used as a load-bearing frame for acoustic panels

subject: Acoustic Panel Perimeter Frame
rule: Acoustic panel perimeter frame must be made of material that does not introduce unacceptable flanking noise or vibration transmission
conditions: When the frame is part of an acoustic separation system
exceptions: If the frame is intentionally designed as a tuned vibration element for acoustic purposes

subject: Acoustic Panel Suspension Cable
rule: acoustic panel suspension cable must have a minimum breaking strength sufficient to support the suspended panel load including a safety factor
conditions: when used to suspend acoustic panels overhead

subject: Acoustic Panel Suspension Cable
rule: acoustic panel suspension cable must not have visible damage such as fraying, kinking, corrosion, or cuts
conditions: when installed and in service

subject: Acoustic Panel Suspension Cable
rule: acoustic panel suspension cable must be secured with a rated end termination (e.g., swage, clamp, or crimp) appropriate for the cable diameter and material
conditions: at each end of the cable

subject: Acoustic Panel Suspension Cable
rule: acoustic panel suspension cable must be installed with a maximum allowable vertical deviation from plumb of no more than 1:100 (or manufacturer specification) to avoid eccentric loading on the panel
conditions: when supporting rigid acoustic panels

subject: Acoustic Wall Panel System
rule: acoustic wall panel system must be attached to structurally capable backing wall or framing
exceptions: free-standing acoustic panel systems that are self-supporting

subject: Acoustic Wall Panel System
rule: acoustic wall panel system must not bridge building fire-rated compartment walls without an equivalent fire-rated assembly or firestop
conditions: when the wall is part of a fire-rated separation
exceptions: panel systems tested and rated for the required fire-resistance period

subject: Acoustic Wall Panel System
rule: acoustic wall panel system must have an acoustically rated backing material or air gap depth that matches the specified acoustic performance target
conditions: when the system is specified for sound transmission class (STC) or noise reduction coefficient (NRC) performance
exceptions: decorative-only panels with no acoustic performance requirement

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
rule: Acoustic ceiling tiles must be installed with sufficient perimeter gap and/or relief cuts to accommodate thermal and acoustic expansion
conditions: continuous runs exceeding 50 linear feet
environments with temperature swings exceeding 15°F
exceptions: tiles cut to individual exact-fit sizes with no continuous grid runs
installations using proprietary expansion-joint grid systems

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
rule: Acoustic ceiling tiles must not be installed in exterior or unconditioned spaces subject to direct rain or standing water
conditions: outdoor soffits without waterproofing above
unconditioned porches or canopies
exceptions: tiles specifically rated and certified for exterior or high-humidity use with water-resistant coatings and framing

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
rule: Acoustic ceiling tiles must be installed with the factory-finished face oriented downward
conditions: non-reversible tile designs with one finished face
exceptions: tiles specifically designed as reversible (identical finish both sides)

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
rule: Acoustic ceiling tile must not be used as a structural diaphragm, shear panel, or load-bearing element
conditions: any installation where tiles span between grid members

subject: Bass Trap
rule: bass trap must be placed at a boundary where low-frequency sound pressure is maximum to function effectively
conditions: used as a resonant absorber
porous absorber

subject: Bass Trap
rule: bass trap must not be fully sealed with a non-porous, rigid facing on the side facing the room air
conditions: porous absorber type
exceptions: membrane/panel absorbers that rely on a sealed facing as part of their tuned mass-spring mechanism

subject: Tile Flooring
rule: tile flooring must be installed over a flat, stable, and clean substrate
conditions: tile is ceramic
tile is porcelain
tile is stone

subject: Tile Flooring
rule: tile flooring must have expansion joints or movement accommodation at perimeters and transitions
conditions: continuous installation area exceeds 8 meters in any direction
installation over radiant heating
exceptions: small mosaic tile installations under 2 meters in both directions

subject: Tile Flooring
rule: tile flooring must not be installed over a waterproof membrane that traps moisture below the tile
conditions: substrate is a wooden subfloor
substrate is gypsum-based underlayment
exceptions: application is a wet-area shower floor with a sloped mortar bed and proper weep system

subject: Plank Flooring
rule: Plank flooring must be installed with expansion gaps around the perimeter and at fixed intervals
conditions: plank flooring material is wood
wood-based
or laminate
exceptions: engineered flooring with integrated expansion system specifically designed to not require gaps

subject: Plank Flooring
rule: Plank flooring must be installed over a structurally sound, flat subfloor

subject: Plank Flooring
rule: Plank flooring must not be installed in continuously wet or flood-prone areas unless specifically rated for wet locations
exceptions: marine-grade polymer plank or porcelain plank specifically rated for continuous wet exposure

subject: Plank Flooring
rule: Plank flooring must not be installed over radiant heating without manufacturer-approved product and installation method
exceptions: flooring system explicitly certified by manufacturer for radiant heat application

subject: Seamless/Resinous Flooring
rule: Seamless/resinous flooring must be installed over a substrate that is clean, dry, structurally sound, and free of contaminants such as oils, waxes, or curing compounds
conditions: Applies to all seamless epoxy, polyurethane, polyaspartic, and MMA resin flooring systems
exceptions: Substrates that are intentionally bonded via a manufacturer-approved primer designed for contaminated surfaces

subject: Seamless/Resinous Flooring
rule: Seamless/resinous flooring must be installed only when ambient and substrate temperatures are within the manufacturer's specified range, typically above the dew point by at least 3°C
conditions: Applies to all liquid-applied resinous flooring systems
exceptions: Some low-temperature-cure formulations allow installation down to -10°C per manufacturer specifications

subject: Seamless/Resinous Flooring
rule: Seamless/resinous flooring must be installed in a single continuous application per coat to avoid cold joints, lap marks, or incomplete bonding at pour stops
conditions: Applies to self-levelling, broadcast, and trowel-applied seamless resin flooring systems
exceptions: Pre-planned construction joints or expansion joints that are designed and cut after curing

subject: Seamless/Resinous Flooring
rule: Seamless/resinous flooring must not be applied over substrates with rising moisture vapor emission rates exceeding the product's maximum allowable limit (typically >3 kg per 24 h per 100 m² for standard systems)
conditions: Applies to resinous flooring over concrete slabs on grade or below grade
exceptions: Vapor-retarding epoxy or moisture-tolerant systems specifically rated for higher MVER may be acceptable per manufacturer data

subject: Terrazzo Flooring
rule: Terrazzo flooring must be installed over a properly prepared, stable, and crack-free substrate
conditions: applies to all terrazzo installation

subject: Terrazzo Flooring
rule: Terrazzo flooring must not be installed where the ambient temperature during curing falls below 10°C (50°F)
conditions: applies to cementitious and epoxy terrazzo

subject: Terrazzo Flooring
rule: Terrazzo flooring must be installed with expansion/control joints at intervals specified by manufacturer or engineer
conditions: applies to large-area or continuous terrazzo installations

subject: Floor Underlayment
rule: floor underlayment must be installed over a structurally adequate subfloor substrate
conditions: all installations
exceptions: direct ground contact applications where the underlayment itself is the structural base

subject: Floor Underlayment
rule: floor underlayment must be installed with gaps or expansion spaces at perimeters and at transitions between adjacent sheets
conditions: any underlayment material that expands or contracts with humidity or temperature changes (e.g., plywood, OSB, cement board)
exceptions: thin foam or felt underlayments used exclusively for sound abatement under floating floors, where the finished flooring provides the expansion accommodation

subject: Floor Underlayment
rule: floor underlayment must not be directly exposed to standing water or continuous moisture without appropriate waterproofing treatment
conditions: underlayment materials that are not inherently waterproof (plywood, OSB, particleboard, gypsum-based boards)
exceptions: underlayments specifically rated for wet areas (e.g., cementitious backerboard under tile in showers) or treated with a fully bonded waterproof membrane

subject: Floor Base & Transition Strip
rule: Floor base must provide continuous bearing surface for finished flooring to prevent point loads that cause cracking or failure
conditions: when installed under rigid finished flooring such as tile, stone, or hardwood
exceptions: when flooring system is designed for point-load bearing (e.g., resilient flooring over structural subfloor only)

subject: Floor Base & Transition Strip
rule: Transition strip must accommodate the differential movement between adjacent flooring materials
conditions: when joining two different flooring materials with different coefficients of thermal expansion or moisture movement
exceptions: when both flooring materials have identical movement characteristics and are installed in climate-controlled environment with no expected differential movement

subject: Floor Base & Transition Strip
rule: Transition strip must not create a trip hazard at floor level changes
conditions: when installed at doorways or between rooms in accessible paths of travel

subject: Access Floor System
rule: Access floor system panels must be capable of supporting the specified live load without deflection exceeding manufacturer limits
conditions: when used as a structural walking surface
in areas designated for equipment or personnel access

subject: Access Floor System
rule: Access floor system pedestals must be installed on a level structural subfloor with tolerance within manufacturer specification

subject: Access Floor System
rule: Access floor system must not be used as a primary seismic bracing system unless specifically designed and certified for that purpose
conditions: in seismic design categories D, E, or F
exceptions: when the system includes certified seismic bracing components and engineering approval

subject: Slip-Resistant Flooring
rule: Slip-resistant flooring must have a surface coefficient of friction (COF) of at least 0.5 when wet and dry, as measured by a standardized test (e.g., ANSI A137.1/A326.3 or equivalent)
conditions: flooring is installed in areas expected to become wet or contaminated during normal use
exceptions: flooring in areas with purpose-specific low-friction requirements (e.g., dance floors, ice rinks, bowling approaches) that are explicitly signed and designed for that use

subject: Slip-Resistant Flooring
rule: Slip-resistant flooring must not have a surface texture that traps or harbors biological contaminants in healthcare or food-preparation environments
conditions: flooring is installed in healthcare facilities, commercial kitchens, or food-processing areas
exceptions: floors that undergo periodic sterilizing or deep-cleaning protocols sufficient to eliminate harboring risk are verified

subject: Slip-Resistant Flooring
rule: Slip-resistant flooring must be installed with a substrate and adhesive system rated for the expected static and dynamic loads without delamination or deformation
conditions: flooring receives heavy foot traffic, wheeled equipment loads, or point loads exceeding 500 psi

subject: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring
rule: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring must have a continuous electrical path to a verified ground connection
conditions: When installed in a flammable or explosive environment
When required by electrical safety code for static-sensitive areas (e.g., server rooms, cleanrooms, munitions handling)

subject: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring
rule: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring must_not have an insulating layer (e.g., non-conductive adhesive, paint, sealant, or underlayment) between its conductive surface and the grounding system
conditions: When installed as a static-dissipative or conductive flooring system
exceptions: If the insulating layer is intentionally designed with embedded conductive paths that maintain continuity to ground as specified by the flooring manufacturer

subject: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring
rule: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring must have a surface electrical resistance within the design-specified range (typically 2.5×10^4 to 1.0×10^6 ohms for conductive flooring, or 1.0×10^6 to 1.0×10^9 ohms for static-dissipative flooring)
conditions: When installed in a static-controlled area

subject: Waterstops
rule: waterstops must be placed at all construction joints in concrete water-retaining structures
conditions: waterstops are used in concrete structures designed to retain or exclude water
exceptions: joints sealed by alternative continuous waterproofing membranes that encapsulate the joint entirely

subject: Waterstops
rule: waterstops must be continuous across the entire joint length with properly formed splice connections
conditions: waterstops are installed in any water-excluding or water-retaining joint
exceptions: none — a gap or improper splice constitutes a direct leakage path

subject: Waterstops
rule: waterstops must be centered within the joint and must not be displaced during concrete placement
conditions: waterstops are embedded in a cast-in-place concrete joint
exceptions: none — displacement off-centre can shorten the water path length below the design requirement

subject: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
rule: joint sealant must be compatible with adjacent building materials (substrates)
conditions: when joint sealant is applied between two different substrate materials
exceptions: when a bond-breaker or compatible primer is used to isolate incompatible materials

subject: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
rule: expansion joint must accommodate full calculated thermal movement range
conditions: where expansion joints separate sections of a building envelope or structure
exceptions: none — this is a fundamental requirement for any expansion joint to function

subject: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
rule: sealant must not be applied to a wet, frozen, or contaminated joint surface
conditions: during field application of curing-type sealants (e.g., silicone, polyurethane)
exceptions: factory-applied pre-cured sealant tapes and gaskets are not subject to this constraint

subject: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
rule: expansion joint must not be installed without a waterstop or drainage provision in below-grade or wet-area applications
conditions: when the expansion joint is located below grade, in a retaining wall, or in a continuously wet interior area (e.g., parking ramp, pool)
exceptions: when joint is designed as a deliberately drained joint system with a collection gutter

subject: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
rule: joint sealant must have movement capability equal to or greater than the anticipated joint movement
conditions: for all sealed joints subject to cyclic movement
exceptions: none — sealant movement capacity is a fundamental selection criterion

subject: Drainage Boards & Cavity Drain Membranes
rule: Drainage boards and cavity drain membranes must be installed with a continuous drainage path to a suitable outlet or drainage system
conditions: When used as part of a below-ground or basement waterproofing system
When installed on walls or floors subject to hydrostatic pressure or groundwater ingress
exceptions: When used solely as an adhered vapour control layer without drainage function (e.g., surface membranes not forming a drained cavity)

subject: Drainage Boards & Cavity Drain Membranes
rule: Cavity drain membranes must not be installed in a manner that blocks or obstructs the intended drainage path
conditions: Where the membrane forms part of a drained cavity system
exceptions: Where the membrane is specifically designed as a sealed vapour barrier with no drainage function

subject: Drainage Boards & Cavity Drain Membranes
rule: Drainage boards must have their studs/dimples oriented to allow gravity drainage toward the perimeter drainage system or sump
conditions: When installed in vertical wall applications
exceptions: When used as horizontal insulation boards not serving a drainage function

subject: Drainage Boards & Cavity Drain Membranes
rule: Cavity drain membranes used in below-grade applications must be connected to a perimeter drainage system (e.g., French drain, sump pump, or gravity outlet)
conditions: In below-grade or basement wall/floor applications where groundwater ingress is anticipated
exceptions: In dry-site conditions where geotechnical investigation confirms no groundwater will ever reach the membrane level
Where the membrane is part of a Type A (barrier) system, not a Type C (drained cavity) system

subject: Flashing
rule: Flashing must form a continuous watertight seal at roof-wall intersections
conditions: Where flashing is used at roof-to-wall intersections

subject: Flashing
rule: Flashing must be lapped shingle-fashion (upper over lower) to direct water flow outward
conditions: Where multiple flashing pieces or flashing layers overlap

subject: Flashing
rule: Flashing must not be installed without proper adhesion or mechanical fastening at all edges

subject: Waterproofing Membrane Protection Board
rule: Waterproofing membrane protection board must be installed directly over the waterproofing membrane
conditions: when used as a protective layer over membrane
exceptions: when the membrane is designed to be self-protected or exposed

subject: Waterproofing Membrane Protection Board
rule: Waterproofing membrane protection board must be installed in a manner that does not impede drainage of the roof/wall system
conditions: when installed on a roof or below-grade wall requiring drainage
exceptions: when the drainage system is integrated into the protection board itself (drainage board products)

subject: Waterproofing Membrane Protection Board
rule: Waterproofing membrane protection board must be resistant to the intended backfill or traffic loading without crushing or puncturing
conditions: when used in buried or trafficked applications (e.g., plaza decks, green roofs, below-grade walls)
exceptions: when a separate load-distribution layer (e.g., concrete slab) is provided above the board

subject: Wall Formwork
rule: wall formwork must withstand the full lateral pressure of fresh concrete during pouring
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete walls

subject: Wall Formwork
rule: wall formwork must have a minimum safe anchorage or bracing to prevent overturning or sliding
conditions: when used in vertical wall applications

subject: Wall Formwork
rule: wall formwork must not have gaps larger than the maximum permissible concrete leakage (grout loss) threshold
conditions: during concrete placement

subject: Wall Formwork
rule: wall formwork panels must be sufficiently stiff to limit deflection to within the structural tolerance (typically span/270 or tighter)
conditions: during concrete pour and curing

subject: Beam Formwork
rule: beam formwork must be adequately braced and tied to resist lateral and vertical loads during concrete placement
conditions: during concrete pouring and before concrete reaches sufficient strength
exceptions: precast/prestressed beam formwork systems designed to be self-stabilizing without temporary bracing

subject: Beam Formwork
rule: beam formwork must have tight joints to prevent leakage of cementitious grout
conditions: when using liquid/flowable concrete mixes

subject: Beam Formwork
rule: beam formwork must not be stripped before the concrete has reached adequate compressive strength
conditions: for structural cast-in-place beams
exceptions: when reshoring/propping is installed to support the beam during early curing

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must provide a minimum concrete cover of 50 mm to the nearest reinforcing bar
conditions: formwork is cast-in-place reinforced concrete

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must be erected with a minimum slope of 1:2 (rise:run) and maximum slope of 1:1
conditions: formwork is for a means of egress stair

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must maintain a minimum headroom clearance of 2.0 m (6 ft 7 in) above the nosing line

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must not have a riser height exceeding 178 mm (7 in) for means of egress stairs
conditions: formwork is for a means of egress stair

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must provide a minimum tread depth of 280 mm (11 in) for means of egress stairs
conditions: formwork is for a means of egress stair

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must be designed to support the wet concrete load plus a construction live load of at least 2.4 kPa (50 psf)
conditions: formwork is for cast-in-place concrete stairs

subject: Stair Formwork
rule: stair formwork must not have a landing width less than the width of the stair flight it serves

subject: Foundation Formwork
rule: foundation formwork must be adequately braced and aligned to resist hydrostatic pressure and fresh concrete loads without deformation
conditions: during concrete placement and curing
when foundation depth exceeds 1.5 meters
exceptions: when formwork is specifically designed as flexible or sacrificial and this is accounted for in structural analysis

subject: Foundation Formwork
rule: foundation formwork must not contain gaps or openings that allow loss of cement paste or fine aggregates
conditions: for cast-in-place concrete foundations
exceptions: intentionally designed construction joints or tie-rod holes that are subsequently sealed

subject: Foundation Formwork
rule: foundation formwork must be capable of supporting its own weight plus the full dead load of wet concrete until the concrete achieves sufficient strength
conditions: during construction stage before formwork removal

subject: Foundation Formwork
rule: foundation formwork must not react chemically with concrete in a way that degrades the concrete surface or inhibits proper curing
conditions: when using steel formwork
when using treated timber formwork
exceptions: when a tested and approved release agent or barrier is applied

subject: Table Formwork
rule: Table formwork must have sufficient load-bearing capacity to support the wet concrete weight plus construction live loads
conditions: during concrete placement and curing

subject: Table Formwork
rule: Table formwork must not be stripped (removed) before the concrete has reached adequate strength
conditions: during stripping/de-shuttering

subject: Table Formwork
rule: Table formwork must be designed so that all vertical loads are transferred to the supporting structure without unacceptable settlement
conditions: during all phases of construction

subject: Table Formwork
rule: Table formwork panels must not exceed the dimensional tolerances specified for the finished concrete element

subject: Climbing Formwork
rule: Climbing formwork must be mechanically secured to the concrete structure being poured
conditions: during concrete placement
when formwork is in lifted position

subject: Climbing Formwork
rule: Climbing formwork must not be raised until the concrete in the supporting wall/slab has achieved sufficient curing strength
conditions: during climbing operation
exceptions: if supplemental temporary supports are provided independent of concrete strength gain

subject: Climbing Formwork
rule: Climbing formwork must have an evenly distributed concrete pour rate that does not exceed the form's rated lateral pressure capacity
conditions: during concrete placement

subject: Tunnel Formwork
rule: Tunnel formwork must have sufficient concrete cover between reinforcement and the form face
conditions: When steel reinforcement is used in the concrete tunnel element

subject: Tunnel Formwork
rule: Tunnel formwork must be able to withstand the full hydrostatic pressure of wet concrete without bursting or excessive deflection
conditions: During concrete placement and curing

subject: Tunnel Formwork
rule: Tunnel formwork must not be stripped before the concrete has reached adequate strength to be self-supporting under its own weight
conditions: During formwork removal (striking)

subject: Gang Formwork
rule: Gang formwork panels must be aligned and connected with positive fasteners (e.g., bolts or wedges) at all panel joints
conditions: when using modular steel or aluminum gang formwork systems
exceptions: custom fabricated one-piece gang forms that have no joints

subject: Gang Formwork
rule: Gang formwork must be adequately braced and tied to resist lateral concrete pressure without deflection exceeding the specified tolerance
conditions: during concrete placement and curing

subject: Gang Formwork
rule: Gang formwork must not be stripped (removed) before concrete has reached the required minimum strength specified in the structural design
conditions: for vertical gang forms supporting fresh concrete
exceptions: when engineered falsework or reshoring is in place to carry loads prematurely

subject: Gang Formwork
rule: Panel-to-panel tolerances (gap and flushness) on gang formwork faces must be within the manufacturer's specified limits (typically 1-2 mm)
conditions: for architectural concrete finishes exposed to view
exceptions: for rough/formwork-quality finishes where tighter tolerances are not specified

subject: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
rule: formwork shoring systems must support all design loads (dead, live, construction, wind) without excessive deflection or failure
conditions: during concrete placement and curing

subject: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
rule: scaffolding must have guardrails and toeboards on all open sides and ends where work platforms are more than 2 meters above the ground or floor
conditions: working platform height > 2 m

subject: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
rule: shoring and scaffolding must not be erected on unstable ground or surfaces that cannot bear the imposed loads

subject: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
rule: formwork must be designed to resist lateral pressure of fresh concrete without bursting or excessive deflection
conditions: when casting walls or columns

subject: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
rule: scaffolding must not be loaded beyond its rated load capacity

subject: Formwork Safety Netting & Guardrails
rule: Formwork safety netting must be attached to structural supports capable of withstanding the design fall arrest load
conditions: when used as fall arrest system
when installed on formwork structures

subject: Formwork Safety Netting & Guardrails
rule: Formwork safety netting must not have gaps or openings larger than the maximum permitted mesh opening dimension
conditions: when used for edge protection or fall arrest

subject: Formwork Safety Netting & Guardrails
rule: Formwork guardrails must have a top rail height not less than the minimum required height above the work surface
conditions: when used as perimeter edge protection on formwork decks

subject: Formwork Safety Netting & Guardrails
rule: Formwork safety netting must be installed with sufficient sag/deflection to absorb fall energy without tearing
conditions: when used for collective fall arrest (horizontal netting)

subject: Temporary Propping During Striking
rule: temporary props must remain in place and adequately support the structure until the struck element has gained sufficient strength to be self-supporting
conditions: during striking of formwork or falsework
where the structural element (e.g., concrete slab, beam) requires curing or has not yet reached design strength
exceptions: where a sequence analysis demonstrates that early removal is safe and the structure can redistribute loads without propping

subject: Temporary Propping During Striking
rule: props must not be removed until back-propping or re-propping has been installed where the design requires it for load transfer
conditions: when striking in multi-storey construction where floors above are still being poured or loaded
exceptions: where a engineered striking sequence specifically omits the need for back-propping by alternative load paths

subject: Temporary Propping During Striking
rule: temporary props must bear on a stable, level base capable of distributing the design loads without excessive settlement
conditions: any temporary propping installation

subject: Striking Tools and Equipment
rule: striking tool striking face must be harder than the workpiece material
conditions: tool is used for striking

subject: Striking Tools and Equipment
rule: striking tool handle must not have cracks or splinters in the gripping area
conditions: tool has a handle

subject: Striking Tools and Equipment
rule: striking tool head must be securely attached to the handle
conditions: tool has a separate head and handle assembly

subject: Concrete Anchor Bolts & Embeds
rule: concrete anchor bolts and embeds must be embedded to the depth specified by structural design calculations
conditions: when used as structural connections
when specified in engineering drawings
exceptions: bolts used for temporary construction or formwork that are removed before final assembly

subject: Concrete Anchor Bolts & Embeds
rule: concrete anchor bolts must not be installed in uncured concrete
conditions: unless specifically designed as early-age anchors per manufacturer specification
exceptions: post-installed adhesive anchors installed into hardened concrete

subject: Concrete Anchor Bolts & Embeds
rule: concrete anchor bolts and embeds must have minimum edge distance and spacing as per design or applicable code
conditions: when anchors are loaded in tension or shear
exceptions: designs specifically engineered for reduced spacing with verified pullout and breakout calculations

subject: Glazing Panel
rule: glazing panel must be structurally supported by an adjacent frame or structural member
conditions: when used as a vertical or overhead infill panel
exceptions: when the glazing panel is a structural glass assembly (e.g., structural silicone glazing or fin-supported) where the glass itself carries load

subject: Glazing Panel
rule: glazing panel must have an edge clearance (rebate gap) to accommodate thermal expansion and building movement
conditions: when installed in a curtain wall, window frame, or storefront system
exceptions: structural glass systems where panels are bonded and movement is accommodated by the sealant itself

subject: Glazing Panel
rule: glazing panel must not contact the frame or any hard material directly without a gasket or setting block
conditions: when the panel is annealed, heat-strengthened, or tempered glass

subject: Moisture Retaining Cover
rule: A moisture retaining cover must be underlain by a waterproof membrane to prevent water intrusion into the building assembly
conditions: when used as part of a building enclosure assembly
on low-slope or flat roofs
on decks or terraces
exceptions: when the moisture retaining cover is itself a fully waterproof and root-impermeable system (e.g., inverted roof membrane assembly with protection layer)

subject: Moisture Retaining Cover
rule: A moisture retaining cover must have a controlled drainage path (e.g., drainage layer, weeps, or slope) to prevent excessive hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: when installed on a horizontal or near-horizontal surface
when the cover retains water by design (e.g., green roof growing medium, gravel ballast)
exceptions: when the assembly is designed as a permanent water-retention cistern or pond with engineered structural and waterproofing provisions

subject: Moisture Retaining Cover
rule: A moisture retaining cover must not exceed the structural load capacity of the supporting deck or structure under saturated conditions
conditions: when the cover is designed to hold water (e.g., extensive or intensive green roof, blue roof, or detention system)
exceptions: when the structure is specifically designed and certified for the saturated load of the intended assembly

subject: Moisture Retaining Cover
rule: A moisture retaining cover must not allow direct contact between retained moisture and the building's primary structure or thermal insulation unless those materials are moisture-tolerant
conditions: when the underlying materials are moisture-sensitive (e.g., wood-based sheathing, batt insulation, gypsum board)
exceptions: when the cover is separated by a waterproof membrane and a drainage/ventilation layer

subject: Laminated Glazing
rule: laminated glazing must maintain integrity of its interlayer bond under design temperatures
conditions: when exposed to direct sunlight
when used in exterior applications
exceptions: when interlayer material is specifically rated for higher temperature ranges

subject: Laminated Glazing
rule: laminated glazing must not have exposed edges in exterior applications without edge sealing
conditions: when used in exterior applications
when exposed to moisture
exceptions: when edge sealant is integrated into frame system

subject: Laminated Glazing
rule: laminated glazing must have its constituent glass plies compatible in thermal expansion coefficient
conditions: when combining different glass types (e.g., annealed and tempered) in a single laminate

subject: Insulated Glazing Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU must have a sealed air or gas-filled cavity between at least two glass panes
conditions: used as a window or curtain wall component
designed for thermal insulation

subject: Insulated Glazing Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU edge seal must maintain a continuous gas-tight barrier around the entire perimeter

subject: Insulated Glazing Unit (IGU)
rule: IGU glass panes must not be in direct structural contact with each other within the cavity

subject: Low-E Coated Glazing
rule: Low-E coated glazing must have the low-emissivity coating facing the interior (or the appropriate cavity in an insulated glazing unit) to function correctly
conditions: When used in insulating glass units (IGUs)
When installed in climate-controlled buildings
exceptions: When specifically designed for exterior application in certain climates (e.g., warm-climate solar-control coatings on surface #1)

subject: Low-E Coated Glazing
rule: Low-E coated glazing must not have the coating applied on an exposed surface that will be subject to mechanical abrasion, cleaning, or weathering unless specifically designed as a hard-coat product for that position
conditions: When coating is a soft-coat (sputter-coated) type
When used in single glazing or surface #1 of an IGU
exceptions: Hard-coat (pyrolytic) low-E coatings are more durable and may be acceptable on exposed surfaces

subject: Tempered Glazing
rule: tempered glazing must be heat-treated to at least 600°C and then rapidly cooled to create surface compression
conditions: when used as safety glazing
when used in any building application

subject: Tempered Glazing
rule: tempered glazing must not be cut, drilled, or edge-worked after tempering

subject: Tempered Glazing
rule: tempered glazing must meet minimum thickness requirements per applicable building code when used as safety glazing
conditions: when installed in hazardous locations such as doors, sidelights, shower enclosures, or near-floor glazing
exceptions: where laminated glass or other code-approved safety glazing alternatives are used instead

subject: Tempered Glazing
rule: tempered glazing must not have surface damage including chips, cracks, or deep scratches exceeding code limits

subject: Self-Cleaning Glazing
rule: Self-cleaning glazing must be installed with the photocatalytic coating on the exterior-facing surface
conditions: Self-cleaning glazing relies on photocatalytic or hydrophilic coatings
exceptions: If the product is specifically designed as a dual-sided self-cleaning glazing

subject: Self-Cleaning Glazing
rule: Self-cleaning glazing must not be installed in locations permanently sheltered from rain
conditions: The self-cleaning mechanism relies on rainwater to wash away loosened dirt
exceptions: If an integrated artificial water-spray system is provided

subject: Self-Cleaning Glazing
rule: Self-cleaning glazing must not be installed where it will be permanently shaded from UV light
conditions: The self-cleaning coating is photocatalytically activated by UV radiation
exceptions: If the product uses a non-UV-dependent self-cleaning mechanism (e.g., superhydrophilic without photocatalytic activation)

subject: Reflective Glazing
rule: reflective glazing must have a visible light reflectance (VLR) no greater than the maximum allowed by local building code to prevent glare hazards to adjacent buildings and traffic
conditions: when installed on building facades
where adjacent to public rights-of-way or neighboring buildings
exceptions: when building code specifically exempts the zoning district or building type

subject: Reflective Glazing
rule: reflective glazing must not be installed in locations where concentrated reflected solar radiation could cause combustion or thermal damage to adjacent materials
conditions: when the glazing geometry creates a concave focusing effect
when adjacent surfaces are combustible or heat-sensitive

subject: Reflective Glazing
rule: reflective glazing must meet the minimum rated dead load and wind load resistance specified by applicable structural standards for its installed location
conditions: when used as a structural or semi-structural cladding component
exceptions: when the glazing is purely decorative with independent structural backup verified by an engineer

subject: Electrochromic Glazing
rule: Electrochromic glazing must have a continuous electrical power supply to switch between tint states
conditions: when automatic or manually controlled tint switching is required
exceptions: self-powered electrochromic devices that incorporate integrated energy harvesting

subject: Electrochromic Glazing
rule: Electrochromic glazing must not be subjected to sustained temperatures exceeding its rated operational range
conditions: when installed in locations exposed to direct solar radiation or adjacent heat sources
exceptions: products specifically rated and tested for extended high-temperature exposure

subject: Electrochromic Glazing
rule: Electrochromic glazing must be sealed against moisture ingress at all edges
conditions: when installed in an exterior façade or in any humid environment

subject: Fire-Rated Glazing
rule: Fire-rated glazing must have a certified fire-resistance rating (in minutes) that meets or exceeds the rating required by building code for the specific fire-resistance-rated assembly in which it is installed
conditions: Installed in any fire-resistance-rated wall, door, or partition

subject: Fire-Rated Glazing
rule: Fire-rated glazing must be tested and labeled to the applicable standard (e.g., ASTM E119, UL 263, or NFPA 252 for doors) for the specific fire exposure and hose stream test
conditions: Used in any fire-resistance-rated assembly requiring hose stream testing

subject: Fire-Rated Glazing
rule: Fire-rated glazing must not have its surface coated or painted after installation unless the coating/paint is specifically approved as part of the tested assembly
conditions: Field-applied after installation
exceptions: Factory-applied coatings that are part of the tested and listed assembly

subject: Bullet-Resistant Glazing
rule: Bullet-resistant glazing must be installed within a structurally rated frame capable of supporting its weight and withstanding the same threat level
conditions: When used in any ballistic-rated opening

subject: Bullet-Resistant Glazing
rule: Bullet-resistant glazing must be edge-supported on all four sides within a frame that provides continuous perimeter support
conditions: When installed as a vision panel in a wall or door

subject: Bullet-Resistant Glazing
rule: Bullet-resistant glazing must not be cut, drilled, notched, or altered in the field after fabrication
conditions: For any installation

subject: Bullet-Resistant Glazing
rule: Bullet-resistant glazing must achieve the specified ballistic resistance level (e.g., UL 752 or NIJ standard) across the entire visible surface area when tested per the applicable standard
conditions: When specified to meet a particular ballistic threat level

subject: Spandrel Glazing
rule: spandrel glazing must be structurally supported by the building frame or curtain wall mullions at all four edges
conditions: when used as a non-load-bearing infill panel
exceptions: when specifically designed as a structurally glazed unit with point-fixed attachments allowing edge-free support

subject: Spandrel Glazing
rule: spandrel glazing must be made of tempered, laminated, or otherwise safety-rated glass when located within 2 meters of a walking surface or occupancy area
conditions: when the spandrel glazing material is glass
when located within 2 meters of a walking surface or occupancy area
exceptions: if the spandrel area is permanently inaccessible and guarded by a barrier

subject: Spandrel Glazing
rule: spandrel glazing must not have penetrations or openings that allow air or water infiltration into the building interior
conditions: when the spandrel is part of the building envelope moisture barrier
exceptions: when penetrations are sealed with code-compliant weatherproof gaskets or flashings that maintain the barrier integrity

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing System
rule: curtain wall glazing system must be designed to resist lateral wind loads and transfer them to the building structure
conditions: system is used as an exterior building enclosure
exceptions: interior non-loadbearing glazing systems

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing System
rule: curtain wall glazing system must accommodate differential movement between the building structure and the cladding
conditions: system is attached to a structure subject to thermal expansion
seismic movement
or deflection

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing System
rule: curtain wall glazing system must not allow uncontrolled water penetration through the glazing or framing joints
conditions: system is exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: intentional weeps and drainage openings designed to collect and expel water

subject: Curtain Wall Glazing System
rule: curtain wall glazing system must have structural anchors or connections that are capable of supporting the system's dead load
conditions: system is attached to the building structure

subject: Storefront Glazing System
rule: Storefront glazing system must have structurally glazed or structurally supported panels that can resist wind loads without additional bracing
conditions: When used as a curtain wall or storefront system in exterior applications
exceptions: Interior non-load-bearing storefront partitions

subject: Storefront Glazing System
rule: Storefront glazing system must have a continuous drainage path for condensation and rainwater infiltration
conditions: When used in exterior vertical glazing applications

subject: Storefront Glazing System
rule: Storefront glazing system must not have glass-to-metal contact without a gasket or setting block
conditions: Where glass is captured in a metal frame

subject: Storefront Glazing System
rule: Storefront glazing system must have glass panels of sufficient thickness to withstand the design wind pressure without breaking
conditions: When used in exterior applications subject to wind loads
exceptions: Panels protected by an exterior rain screen or secondary barrier rated for the full wind load

subject: Window Glazing System
rule: window glazing system must resist wind load pressures specified for the building's location and height
conditions: building is in a wind zone
glazing is part of the building envelope
exceptions: interior non-load-bearing partitions with no exterior exposure

subject: Window Glazing System
rule: window glazing system must have a minimum thickness and strength to prevent breakage under normal service loads
conditions: glazing is accessible to occupants
glazing is at floor level or in doors
exceptions: laminated or tempered glass already meeting safety standards
glazing in fully restricted areas

subject: Window Glazing System
rule: window glazing system must not allow water penetration through the glazing-to-frame interface under design rainfall conditions
conditions: glazing is part of the exterior building envelope
exceptions: fully interior glazing systems with no weather exposure

subject: Skylight Glazing System
rule: skylight glazing system must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: located on a roof with flat or low-slope geometry
exposed to precipitation
exceptions: system is purely vertical or on a slope ≥ designed water-shedding threshold
system is in an interior/conditioned space with no weather exposure

subject: Skylight Glazing System
rule: skylight glazing system must have glass panels rated for the imposed design loads (dead, live, wind, snow, impact)
conditions: installed in a building enclosure
exceptions: system serves only as decorative interior laylight with no weather or load exposure

subject: Skylight Glazing System
rule: skylight glazing system must not allow direct water ingress at any joint, seal, or interface under design wind and rain conditions
conditions: system is part of the building envelope
exceptions: system is purely decorative and backs to conditioned space with secondary water management

subject: Skylight Glazing System
rule: skylight glazing system must be secured against uplift from negative wind pressure
conditions: system is mounted on a roof exposed to wind
exceptions: system is located in a fully enclosed interior well with no wind access

subject: Skylight Glazing System
rule: skylight glazing system must have a condensation management strategy (drainage or thermal control) when installed in climates where interior humidity can condense on the glazing
conditions: system separates conditioned interior space from exterior
climate or interior humidity conditions produce dew point below glazing surface temperature
exceptions: glazing is in an unconditioned attic or vented space where condensate can drain harmlessly

subject: Sloped Glazing System
rule: Sloped glazing system must have structural support capable of withstanding dead load, live load, wind load, and snow load
conditions: when used as a roof or skylight

subject: Sloped Glazing System
rule: Sloped glazing system must use laminated or tempered glass that meets safety glazing requirements
conditions: when installed overhead (slope less than 60 degrees from horizontal)
when located in areas accessible to occupants
exceptions: when protected by a wire mesh or equivalent fall-protection barrier below the glazing

subject: Sloped Glazing System
rule: Sloped glazing system must have condensation management provisions
conditions: when installed in climate zones with interior humidity levels that can lead to condensation
exceptions: when the system is designed for a non-conditioned or unoccupied space where condensation is acceptable

subject: Sloped Glazing System
rule: Sloped glazing system must not allow water penetration at sloped joints and interfaces

subject: Sloped Glazing System
rule: Sloped glazing system must provide a thermal break between interior and exterior metal framing components
conditions: when building is in a climate requiring thermal insulation (heating or cooling dominated)
exceptions: when the system serves an unconditioned space such as a covered walkway or unheated greenhouse

subject: Structural Glazing System
rule: Structural glazing system glass panes must be structurally bonded to the supporting frame using a structural silicone sealant that transfers all wind and gravity loads
conditions: The system is used as an exterior building envelope component
The system supports its own weight and resists wind loads
exceptions: Mechanical fixing (bolts, clips) systems that do not rely primarily on adhesive bonding

subject: Structural Glazing System
rule: Structural glazing system must accommodate differential thermal movement between glass and frame without transferring stress that would cause glass breakage
conditions: The system is exposed to direct sunlight or significant exterior temperature variation
exceptions: Systems installed in fully climate-controlled interior environments with no temperature fluctuation

subject: Structural Glazing System
rule: Structural glazing silicone sealant must not be subjected to tensile stress exceeding the sealant's design tensile capacity
conditions: The system is in service under design wind loads

subject: Point-Supported Glazing System
rule: Point-supported glazing system must have structural silicone or gasket seals at all glass-to-metal contact points to prevent stress concentration and glass breakage
conditions: System uses bolts or point fixings that penetrate or clamp the glass
exceptions: Fully captured frame systems where glass is not point-supported

subject: Point-Supported Glazing System
rule: Point-supported glazing system must not exceed the glass panel's edge-distance-to-thickness ratio limits specified by the manufacturer
conditions: System uses bolted or countersunk point fixings near glass edges

subject: Point-Supported Glazing System
rule: Point-supported glazing system must have tempered or heat-strengthened glass in all panels, not annealed glass
conditions: System is structural (load-bearing) and uses point fixings
exceptions: Non-structural interior partitions with small panels and no safety/impact risk

subject: Protective Coating
rule: protective coating must be compatible with the substrate material to which it is applied
conditions: when applied to any substrate

subject: Protective Coating
rule: protective coating must be applied within the manufacturer's specified environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, surface preparation)
conditions: when manufacturer specifications exist

subject: Protective Coating
rule: protective coating must not exceed its maximum service temperature
conditions: when the coating is in service under thermal exposure

subject: Protective Coating
rule: protective coating must achieve a continuous, defect-free film over the entire protected surface
conditions: when the coating is intended to provide barrier protection against moisture, chemicals, or corrosion

subject: Steel Reinforcement Bars (Rebar)
rule: Steel reinforcement bars (rebar) must have a minimum concrete cover to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: When used in reinforced concrete structures exposed to environmental conditions
When fire resistance rating is required
exceptions: When alternative corrosion protection is provided (e.g., epoxy coating, galvanizing, stainless steel)

subject: Steel Reinforcement Bars (Rebar)
rule: Steel reinforcement bars (rebar) must be embedded with sufficient development length or mechanical anchorage to develop their yield strength
conditions: At all tension lap splices
At all bar termination points in tension zones
exceptions: When headed bars or mechanical couplers are used and proven equivalent by testing

subject: Steel Reinforcement Bars (Rebar)
rule: Steel reinforcement bars (rebar) must not be placed with less than the minimum clear spacing between parallel bars
conditions: In cast-in-place concrete members
exceptions: When bundled bars are used per code provisions for bundling

subject: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
rule: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF) must have a minimum tensile strength as specified by the applicable material standard (e.g., ASTM A1064) to resist design loads
conditions: When used as primary reinforcement in concrete

subject: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
rule: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF) must have welded intersections that are adequately bonded (weld shear strength per ASTM A1064) to ensure the grid acts compositely

subject: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
rule: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF) must_not have wire diameters below the minimum specified in the design standard for the intended structural application
conditions: When used as structural reinforcement

subject: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
rule: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF) must be placed with proper concrete cover (minimum depth per ACI 318 or applicable code) to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: When embedded in concrete exposed to environment or fire

subject: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
rule: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF) must_not have a yield strength lower than the design yield strength assumed in the structural calculations
conditions: When used as tension reinforcement in reinforced concrete

subject: Rebar Supports/Chairs
rule: Rebar supports/chairs must have a minimum concrete cover as specified by structural design codes to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: When used in reinforced concrete elements exposed to environment or fire
exceptions: When stainless steel or epoxy-coated rebar is used
When alternative corrosion protection is specified in design

subject: Rebar Supports/Chairs
rule: Rebar supports/chairs must not reduce the effective structural depth of the reinforced concrete element beyond what is specified in the structural design
conditions: When installed in slabs, beams, or footing elements where rebar position determines structural capacity
exceptions: When the reduced depth is explicitly accounted for in structural calculations

subject: Rebar Supports/Chairs
rule: Rebar supports/chairs must withstand the construction loads (wet concrete weight, placement impact, worker foot traffic) without collapse or excessive deflection
conditions: During concrete placement and finishing operations

subject: Starter Bars/Dowel Bars
rule: Starter bars / dowel bars must have minimum embedment length into both the existing concrete and the new concrete pour as specified by engineering design
