conditions: Where dowel bars are used for concrete-to-concrete connections
exceptions: Non-structural applications where bars serve only as alignment guides

subject: Starter Bars/Dowel Bars
rule: Starter bars / dowel bars must be clean and free of rust scale, oil, grease, or other bond-breaking contaminants at the time of concrete placement
conditions: Always when bars are embedded in concrete
exceptions: Epoxy-coated or galvanized bars manufactured with factory-applied coating

subject: Starter Bars/Dowel Bars
rule: Starter bars / dowel bars must not be placed with less than the specified concrete cover as required by code for corrosion protection and fire resistance
conditions: Where bars are exposed to exterior environment or in corrosive conditions
exceptions: Temporary construction where bars will be encased before exposure

subject: Starter Bars/Dowel Bars
rule: Starter bars / dowel bars must be aligned straight and parallel to the direction of intended load transfer
conditions: Where bars are designed for shear transfer across a construction joint
exceptions: Purpose-bent bars designed as moment connectors with explicit engineering approval

subject: Shear Reinforcement (Stirrups/Links)
rule: shear reinforcement (stirrups/links) must be adequately anchored into the compression zone of the concrete section to develop its full yield strength
conditions: reinforced concrete beam or column subjected to shear forces exceeding the concrete's shear capacity without shear reinforcement
exceptions: members where design shear force is less than half the concrete shear capacity and minimum shear reinforcement is not required per code

subject: Shear Reinforcement (Stirrups/Links)
rule: shear reinforcement must not have a spacing that exceeds the maximum permitted by structural code for the member geometry and shear demand
conditions: any concrete beam, column, or wall with required shear reinforcement
exceptions: members where calculated shear force is negligible and no shear reinforcement is required by code

subject: Shear Reinforcement (Stirrups/Links)
rule: shear reinforcement must be closed (i.e., fully enclosed hoops or ties) in seismic lateral-force-resisting systems
conditions: members designated as part of the seismic lateral-force-resisting system in high-seismicity regions
exceptions: members in non-seismic regions or low-seismicity zones where open stirrups with standard hooks are permitted

subject: Mortar types
rule: mortar must have sufficient compressive strength to support the loads imposed by the masonry units above
conditions: mortar is used in load-bearing masonry walls

subject: Mortar types
rule: mortar must not have a lime content that causes it to be weaker than the adjacent masonry units in a load-bearing context
conditions: mortar used in load-bearing walls
exceptions: sacrificial or repointing mortars where deliberate softness is intended to protect historic masonry

subject: Tensioning Tendons/Strands
rule: tensioning tendons/strands must remain in tension under all service load conditions
conditions: when used in prestressed or post-tensioned concrete structures
during service life after prestressing force has been applied
exceptions: intentional detensioning operations during demolition or decommissioning

subject: Tensioning Tendons/Strands
rule: tensioning tendons/strands must not be overstressed beyond their specified ultimate tensile strength
conditions: during stressing operations
at any point during construction or service life

subject: Tensioning Tendons/Strands
rule: tensioning tendons/strands must be fully encapsulated or properly protected against corrosion at all exposed surfaces
conditions: when used in exterior or corrosive environments
when embedded in concrete without permanent bond
exceptions: temporary exposure during construction before grouting or encapsulation is completed

subject: Tensioning Tendons/Strands
rule: tensioning tendons/strands must not be subjected to significant bending or kinking
conditions: at any point along the tendon profile
during handling, installation, or stressing
exceptions: intentional curvature as designed in draped tendon profiles within allowable bend radii

subject: Bond patterns
rule: bond pattern must ensure adequate lap length for load transfer
conditions: when adjacent masonry units meet at a vertical joint
exceptions: continuous vertical reinforcement replaces mechanical bond

subject: Bond patterns
rule: bond pattern must not create continuous vertical joints aligned through more than one course
conditions: in loadbearing or unreinforced masonry walls
exceptions: when wall is fully reinforced and designed as a structural frame infill

subject: Bond patterns
rule: bond pattern must interlock wythes at regular intervals
conditions: in multi-wythe masonry walls without cavity
exceptions: when metal ties or ladder reinforcement are provided at designed spacing

subject: Bond patterns
rule: bond pattern must not leave head joints unfilled when mortar is the only bonding agent
conditions: in structural masonry where the bond pattern relies on mortar alone
exceptions: when perpend joints are deliberately left open for drainage in rainscreen walls

subject: Reinforced masonry
rule: reinforced masonry must have proper reinforcement placement within the masonry to resist tensile and shear stresses
conditions: when used as a structural load-bearing component

subject: Reinforced masonry
rule: reinforced masonry must have all reinforcement fully embedded in grout or mortar
conditions: when reinforcement is present

subject: Reinforced masonry
rule: reinforced masonry must not have unreinforced openings that exceed the lintel or bond beam capacity without supplementary reinforcement
conditions: when openings are present in a structural wall
exceptions: openings fully within non-load-bearing infill panels

subject: Masonry veneer
rule: Masonry veneer must be anchored to the structural backing with corrosion-resistant ties
conditions: When used as an exterior cladding on framed walls

subject: Masonry veneer
rule: Masonry veneer must have a minimum air gap (cavity) between the veneer and the structural sheathing
conditions: When installed over wood- or steel-frame walls

subject: Masonry veneer
rule: Masonry veneer must not be relied upon as the primary lateral or vertical load-resisting system

subject: Masonry veneer
rule: Masonry veneer must include weeps and flashings at the base of the veneer
conditions: When installed as a drained cladding system

subject: Cavity wall construction
rule: Cavity wall must have wall ties connecting the inner and outer leaves
conditions: Cavity wall construction with masonry inner and outer leaves

subject: Cavity wall construction
rule: Cavity wall must have a minimum cavity width of at least 50mm
conditions: Cavity wall with masonry leaves

subject: Cavity wall construction
rule: Cavity wall must not have cavity bridged by mortar droppings or debris
conditions: Cavity wall construction

subject: Cavity wall construction
rule: Cavity wall must have weep holes at the base of the cavity to allow drainage
conditions: Cavity wall above ground
Cavity wall exposed to rain

subject: Cavity wall construction
rule: Cavity wall must have cavity insulation that does not bridge the cavity and create a moisture path
conditions: Cavity wall with insulation in the cavity
exceptions: Full-fill cavity insulation systems specifically designed and tested to prevent moisture transfer

subject: Masonry lintels and arches
rule: A masonry lintel must have a bearing length of at least 100 mm (4 inches) on each supporting side
conditions: The lintel spans an opening in a load-bearing masonry wall
exceptions: Lintels cast monolithically with reinforced concrete frames where the frame itself provides the bearing

subject: Masonry lintels and arches
rule: A masonry arch must have its voussoir joint lines radiate from a single center of curvature (i.e., joints must be normal to the intrados)
conditions: The arch is a true voussoir arch (not a concealed lintel or reinforced arch)
exceptions: Modern reinforced concrete arches or jack arches with non-radial bed joints designed through engineered reinforcement

subject: Masonry lintels and arches
rule: A masonry arch must have its horizontal thrust resisted by adequate abutments or tie-rods
conditions: The arch spans a clear opening and is not part of a continuous vault or dome system that provides mutual thrust restraint

subject: Masonry lintels and arches
rule: The depth of a masonry lintel (height of the lintel section in the wall plane) must be sufficient to keep maximum tensile stress within the masonry's tensile capacity, or reinforcement must be provided
conditions: The lintel is unreinforced masonry
exceptions: Reinforced masonry lintels or pre-stressed concrete lintels specifically designed for the span and load

subject: Movement joints
rule: Movement joints must be located at all structural and material transitions where differential movement can occur
conditions: Where building includes multiple structural systems
Where dissimilar materials meet
Where building geometry changes abruptly
exceptions: Very small structures with uniform materials and stable foundations

subject: Movement joints
rule: Movement joints must not be bridged by rigid finishes, cladding, or attachments
conditions: Where movement joints are installed in floors, walls, or ceilings
Where continuous rigid materials are applied over joints
exceptions: Intentional structural connections designed as moment-resisting connections that allow joint movement

subject: Movement joints
rule: Movement joints must extend fully through the building element (not partially cut)
conditions: Where movement joints are specified in concrete slabs, masonry walls, or continuous floor decks
exceptions: Control joints (score cuts) which are intentionally partial-depth

subject: Movement joints
rule: Movement joint width must accommodate the calculated differential movement without closing entirely or opening beyond sealant capacity
conditions: Where joints are designed with sealants or gaskets
exceptions: Unsealed open joints where full closure is structurally acceptable

subject: Movement joints
rule: Movement joints must be water-sealed in weather-exposed locations
conditions: Joints located in exterior walls
Joints in roofs
Joints in waterproofed decks
Joints below grade
exceptions: Interior joints not subject to moisture exposure

subject: Masonry chimneys and flues
rule: Masonry chimney must extend at least 2 feet above any portion of the roof within 10 feet
conditions: chimney is located on a sloped roof
building is in a jurisdiction following standard fire codes
exceptions: chimney is terminated with an approved spark arrestor and local code permits reduced height

subject: Masonry chimneys and flues
rule: Masonry chimney flue must be lined with a listed flue liner material
conditions: flue is used for solid-fuel or oil-fired appliance
exceptions: flue is a factory-built metal chimney system listed as a complete assembly

subject: Masonry chimneys and flues
rule: Masonry chimney must have a minimum wall thickness of 4 inches of solid masonry when lined
conditions: chimney serves a solid-fuel or oil-burning appliance

subject: Masonry chimneys and flues
rule: Masonry chimney must not be corbeled more than 6 inches from the chimney face
conditions: chimney is corbeled above the roof
exceptions: corbeling is fully supported by reinforced masonry or steel angles designed by a structural engineer

subject: Masonry chimneys and flues
rule: Masonry chimney must have a non-combustible spark arrestor or screen at the top opening
conditions: chimney serves a solid-fuel burning appliance
exceptions: local fire authority expressly waives requirement due to non-combustible roof covering and lot conditions

subject: Damp-proof courses
rule: Damp-proof course must form a continuous barrier across the entire wall thickness, including all leaves of a cavity wall
conditions: new building work
wall construction
exceptions: walls of fully tanked basement construction where external waterproofing is used instead

subject: Damp-proof courses
rule: Damp-proof course must be located a minimum of 150 mm above finished external ground level
conditions: external walls
solid floor adjacent
exceptions: sites where ground level is permanently below internal floor level with no splash-zone risk

subject: Damp-proof courses
rule: Damp-proof course must not be bridged by external render, earth, paving, or other materials on the outside face
conditions: any wall with a DPC
exceptions: where a continuous cavity tray and weep vents provide an alternative drainage path

subject: Damp-proof courses
rule: Damp-proof course must be of a material that is impervious to moisture and durable under the service conditions
conditions: any installation

subject: Damp-proof courses
rule: Damp-proof course in a cavity wall must be lapped and sealed at all joints, and at intersections with openings and other DPCs
conditions: cavity wall construction
exceptions: proprietary interlocking DPC systems designed to not require sealing at specific joint details

subject: Retaining walls
rule: Retaining wall must be provided with a drainage system (e.g., weep holes, perforated pipe, or gravel blanket) to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: wall retains soil
exceptions: wall is designed as a waterproof basement wall with full waterproofing and positive-side drainage that meets equivalent performance

subject: Retaining walls
rule: Retaining wall must not be constructed without a geotechnical analysis of the retained soil and groundwater conditions
conditions: wall height exceeds 1.2 m
exceptions: wall is a small landscape wall on a site with previously documented soil conditions allowing prescriptive design per local code

subject: Retaining walls
rule: Retaining wall must have a foundation depth below the frost line
conditions: wall is located in a climate zone subject to seasonal freezing
wall supports a permanent structure or surcharge
exceptions: wall is a free-standing landscape wall with no surcharge and is founded on well-drained granular soil with demonstrated non-frost-susceptible conditions

subject: Retaining walls
rule: Retaining wall must not have unreinforced masonry as the sole structural element when height exceeds 1.0 m
conditions: wall is a gravity or cantilever type
height exceeds 1.0 m
exceptions: wall uses a reinforced concrete or reinforced masonry design per structural calculations
wall is a mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) system designed by a geotechnical engineer

subject: Plaster Render (External)
rule: Plaster render (external) must not be applied in freezing temperatures
conditions: during application
during curing period (typically 24-48 hours)

subject: Plaster Render (External)
rule: Plaster render (external) must be applied to a substrate that has adequate suction control (e.g., pre-wetting or bonding agent)
conditions: applied onto porous substrates such as concrete block, brick, or stone
exceptions: proprietary polymer-modified renders designed for non-porous substrates

subject: Plaster Render (External)
rule: Plaster render (external) must not be applied over surfaces contaminated with dust, oil, grease, or efflorescence
conditions: any application

subject: Plaster Render (External)
rule: Plaster render (external) must be applied in coats not exceeding the manufacturer's maximum thickness per coat
conditions: multi-coat application

subject: Plaster Render (External)
rule: Plaster render (external) must not be applied to continuously wet or saturated substrates
conditions: any application

subject: Gypsum Plaster
rule: gypsum plaster must not be used in exterior or continuously wet applications
conditions: exterior exposure
continuous moisture
high humidity environments
outdoor applications
exceptions: when protected by a waterproof coating and drainage plane with vapour barrier in non-freeze-thaw climates

subject: Gypsum Plaster
rule: gypsum plaster must be applied over a compatible substrate or lath that provides mechanical key
conditions: direct application of plaster
exceptions: prefabricated gypsum boards where adhesion is factory-bonded

subject: Gypsum Plaster
rule: gypsum plaster must not be applied when ambient or substrate temperature is below 5°C (40°F)
conditions: field application of wet plaster

subject: Lime Plaster
rule: lime plaster must not be used in exterior applications exposed to continuous liquid water or freeze-thaw cycling
conditions: exterior application
continuous liquid water exposure
freeze-thaw cycling
exceptions: sheltered locations with effective drainage and breathable weather barrier systems
lime plaster formulated with appropriate hydraulic additives for wet conditions

subject: Lime Plaster
rule: lime plaster must be applied over a compatible, breathable substrate or base coat that is less rigid than the plaster itself
conditions: application over any substrate
exceptions: lime plaster applied over lime-based substrates such as lime mortar, lime concrete, or existing sound lime plaster

subject: Lime Plaster
rule: lime plaster must be kept damp during curing for a minimum of 3 days and must not be allowed to dry rapidly
conditions: during initial curing period
exceptions: factory-prehydrated lime plaster with documented reduced curing requirements

subject: Plaster Key (on Lath)
rule: Plaster key (on lath) must have sufficient mechanical key to the plaster to resist delamination under self-weight and normal service loads
conditions: Plaster is applied to metal or wood lath

subject: Plaster Key (on Lath)
rule: Plaster key (on lath) must not be formed on lath that is excessively corroded, rotted, or degraded to the point that the lath cannot retain the key
conditions: Existing lath is reused or inspected in situ

subject: Plaster Bead / Trim
rule: plaster bead/trim must be installed at the intersection of dissimilar materials or at termination points of plaster to provide a clean edge and prevent cracking
conditions: when plaster finish is applied
where plaster meets another material or terminates
exceptions: when using a different method of edge termination such as a casing bead or reveal that is designed for the specific condition

subject: Metal Lath
rule: Metal lath must be mechanically fastened to structural supports (studs, joists, or furring) at intervals specified by the lath manufacturer and relevant building code
conditions: When used as a base for cement plaster or stucco
When used as a base for portland cement-based render
exceptions: When lath is self-furring and specifically designed for adhesive attachment per manufacturer's approved alternate method
When used exclusively as a reinforcement layer within a bonded cementitious overlay system

subject: Metal Lath
rule: Metal lath must have galvanized or other corrosion-resistant coating when used in exterior applications or in contact with Portland cement materials
conditions: When exposed to moisture either directly (exterior) or indirectly (cement contact)
exceptions: Stainless steel lath does not require coating

subject: Metal Lath
rule: Metal lath must have its self-furring dimples or equivalent standoff oriented correctly so that the lath does not lie flat against the backing surface
conditions: When used as a plaster base over a solid backing surface (e.g., sheathing, masonry)
exceptions: When lath is used over open framing where keys can form behind the lath without requiring standoff

subject: Metal Lath
rule: Metal lath must not be installed with the cut edges oriented such that sharp wire ends protrude outward into the finished plaster surface
conditions: At splice joints and termination edges
exceptions: When cut edges are covered by accessory trim or casing beads

subject: Ceramic and Porcelain Tile
rule: Ceramic and porcelain tiles must be installed on a stable, rigid substrate that minimizes deflection
conditions: tile installation

subject: Ceramic and Porcelain Tile
rule: Ceramic and porcelain tiles must not be installed where they will be subjected to repeated freeze-thaw cycles unless they are specifically rated as frost-resistant
conditions: exterior installation
unconditioned spaces
exceptions: tiles rated and tested as frost-resistant per ASTM C1026 or equivalent

subject: Ceramic and Porcelain Tile
rule: Ceramic and porcelain tiles must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot (2% slope) toward drains in wet-area floor installations
conditions: wet-area floor installation
showers
saunas
commercial kitchens
pool decks

subject: Tile Spacers and Leveling Systems
rule: Tile spacers and leveling systems must be compatible with the tile thickness and size they are supporting
conditions: When used to set tile spacing and levelness during installation

subject: Tile Spacers and Leveling Systems
rule: Tile spacers and leveling systems must be removed before the tile adhesive fully cures (hardens) if they are not designed to be left in place
conditions: When using reusable or non-embedded spacers/leveling clips
exceptions: Some leveling systems are specifically designed to be snapped off above the tile surface leaving a removable piece — in that case the base piece may remain embedded but the top piece must still be removed before full cure.

subject: Tile Spacers and Leveling Systems
rule: Tile leveling system clips must not exceed the tile's breaking strength when tensioned
conditions: When using a clip-and-wedge leveling system that applies vertical tension

subject: Tile Crack Isolation Membrane
rule: Tile crack isolation membrane must be installed directly over a clean, sound substrate free of cracks, voids, or debris
conditions: when used as a crack isolation layer under tile flooring

subject: Tile Crack Isolation Membrane
rule: Tile crack isolation membrane must achieve full coverage (100% bond) with no air pockets, unbonded areas, or fish-mouth seams
conditions: for all sheet-type crack isolation membranes

subject: Tile Crack Isolation Membrane
rule: Tile crack isolation membrane must not be installed over wet, frozen, or outgassing concrete without proper moisture testing
conditions: when substrate is concrete
exceptions: products specifically rated for green concrete with documented vapor-perm properties

subject: Tile Crack Isolation Membrane
rule: Tile crack isolation membrane must not be used as a primary waterproofing membrane in wet areas (shower pans, pools)
conditions: unless product is dual-rated by manufacturer for both crack isolation and waterproofing
exceptions: products explicitly listed as waterproof membranes that also provide crack isolation

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU) Ductwork Connection
rule: AHU ductwork connection must be sealed airtight
conditions: connection is within conditioned space
duct serves occupied zone
exceptions: intentional outdoor ventilation intakes where code allows controlled leakage

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU) Ductwork Connection
rule: AHU ductwork connection must not create a rigid bridge that transmits vibration from AHU to ductwork
conditions: AHU is mechanically powered (fan operating)
exceptions: connection uses a listed flexible vibration isolator (e.g., canvas/fabric connector)

subject: Air Handling Unit (AHU) Ductwork Connection
rule: AHU ductwork connection must be sized to match the AHU's supply/discharge collar dimensions within allowable tolerance
conditions: connection is at the immediate AHU outlet or inlet
exceptions: transition piece designed by a qualified engineer is installed between mismatched sizes

subject: Fresh Air Intake Ductwork
rule: fresh air intake ductwork must be sloped toward an appropriate drain point or back toward the air handling unit
conditions: ductwork is exposed to condensation risk
ductwork carries air that is cooled below the dew point of surrounding air
exceptions: ductwork is explicitly designed and rated for standing water (e.g., fully watertight, corrosion-resistant, with structural support)

subject: Fresh Air Intake Ductwork
rule: fresh air intake ductwork must not have low points or traps where condensate can accumulate without a drain
conditions: duct is installed with a cooling coil or dehumidification upstream
duct operates in a humid climate region
exceptions: low points are explicitly provided with a dedicated condensate drain line and trap

subject: Fresh Air Intake Ductwork
rule: fresh air intake ductwork connecting to a plenum or AHU must maintain a minimum separation distance from exhaust or contaminated air intake openings
conditions: the adjacent exhaust outlet or contaminated source is within 30 ft (10 m)
exceptions: a physical barrier or baffle with demonstrated effectiveness is installed between the intake and the source

subject: Exhaust Ductwork
rule: Exhaust ductwork must terminate at a safe location away from air intakes and occupied openings
conditions: building has any air intake openings within the vicinity
exhaust contains potentially hazardous or odorous contaminants
exceptions: exhaust is filtered/scrubbed to remove hazardous/odorous contaminants before discharge

subject: Exhaust Ductwork
rule: Exhaust ductwork must not share a common shaft with supply air ductwork unless specifically designed for shaft pressurization and compartmentation
conditions: ducts are located within a common vertical shaft or chase
exceptions: shaft is designed with smoke-rated separation and positive pressurization per applicable fire code

subject: Exhaust Ductwork
rule: Exhaust ductwork must be constructed of non-combustible materials
conditions: ductwork penetrates fire-rated assemblies
duct system serves kitchen exhaust, laboratory exhaust, or hazardous fume exhaust
exceptions: ductwork serving general bathroom exhaust in a non-combustible building where local code allows metal or UL-listed combustible duct via exception

subject: Exhaust Ductwork
rule: Exhaust ductwork must maintain a minimum clearance to combustible materials
conditions: duct carries high-temperature exhaust (e.g., kitchen, boiler, industrial process)
exceptions: duct is insulated with a listed thermal barrier system

subject: Exhaust Ductwork
rule: Exhaust ductwork must not be directly connected to a natural draft chimney or vent serving combustion appliances
conditions: building contains combustion appliances vented by natural draft
exceptions: appliance is direct-vent or power-vented with a dedicated exhaust system

subject: Spiral Round Duct
rule: Spiral round duct must maintain a minimum gauge (sheet metal thickness) to withstand internal pressure without collapsing or rupturing
conditions: when used for HVAC air distribution
when fabricated from sheet metal

subject: Spiral Round Duct
rule: Spiral round duct must not be installed without proper hanger supports at maximum intervals specified by SMACNA standards
conditions: when installed in a ceiling or overhead location

subject: Spiral Round Duct
rule: Spiral round duct joints must be sealed to prevent air leakage
conditions: when duct is part of a conditioned air system

subject: Rectangular Sheet Metal Duct
rule: rectangular sheet metal duct must maintain a minimum gauge thickness to withstand internal static pressure without excessive deflection or rupture
conditions: duct is under positive pressure
duct is fabricated from sheet metal
exceptions: duct is externally reinforced to compensate for thinner gauge

subject: Rectangular Sheet Metal Duct
rule: rectangular sheet metal duct must have all transverse joints and seams sealed to prevent air leakage
conditions: duct conveys conditioned air
duct operates under pressure differential
exceptions: duct is explicitly designed as a leaky return plenum

subject: Rectangular Sheet Metal Duct
rule: rectangular sheet metal duct must not have aspect ratio (width-to-height) exceeding 4:1 without internal bracing or tie-rod reinforcement
conditions: duct is installed in a HVAC system
exceptions: duct is externally braced by structure or continuous support

subject: Rectangular Sheet Metal Duct
rule: rectangular sheet metal duct must be installed with clearances that allow for thermal expansion and contraction
conditions: duct carries air that differs in temperature from ambient
duct runs exceed 30 feet in length
exceptions: expansion joints or bellows are incorporated at intervals

subject: Flexible Duct
rule: Flexible duct must not have sharp bends that exceed its minimum bend radius
conditions: when installed in HVAC systems
exceptions: when specifically manufactured as a pre-formed rigid elbow section

subject: Flexible Duct
rule: Flexible duct must be supported at maximum intervals specified by manufacturer or building code
conditions: when installed in horizontal or vertical runs
exceptions: continuous rigid duct sections

subject: Flexible Duct
rule: Flexible duct must not be compressed or crushed by surrounding construction or fasteners
conditions: during installation or after enclosure in walls/ceilings

subject: Duct Liner
rule: duct liner must be installed with the airstream surface facing the airflow
conditions: duct liner is used in an HVAC air distribution system
exceptions: duct liner used as an external wrap where airflow direction is irrelevant

subject: Duct Liner
rule: duct liner must not be exposed to standing water or continuous moisture
conditions: duct liner is installed in any HVAC ductwork application
exceptions: duct liner specifically rated and labeled for continuous wet service (rare, special-order products only)

subject: Duct Liner
rule: duct liner must be secured with mechanical fasteners and/or adhesive rated for the operating temperature range
conditions: duct liner is applied to interior of sheet metal ducts

subject: Volume Control Damper
rule: Volume control damper blades must not bind or stick against the frame during operation
conditions: damper is used for modulating airflow

subject: Volume Control Damper
rule: Volume control damper must have a means of blade position indication or external actuator attachment
conditions: damper is installed in an inaccessible location without visual line of sight
exceptions: damper is purely manual with a handle that protrudes through the duct

subject: Volume Control Damper
rule: Volume control damper must not have a blade-to-blade or blade-to-frame gap that exceeds the leakage class specified for its application
conditions: damper is specified with a leakage class (e.g., Class I, II, III per AMCA or SMACNA)

subject: Ductwork Hangers & Supports
rule: Ductwork hangers and supports must be attached to structural building elements (e.g., beams, joists, slabs), not to non-structural elements such as ceiling grid or light fixtures
conditions: All ductwork installations
exceptions: When hanger wires are specifically designed as seismic bracing and are independently tied to structure above a suspended ceiling

subject: Ductwork Hangers & Supports
rule: Ductwork hangers and supports must not transmit vibration or load to occupied spaces or sensitive equipment through rigid contact
conditions: When ductwork is located above occupied spaces or near vibration-sensitive equipment
exceptions: When vibration isolation devices (spring isolators, neoprene pads) are installed at all support points

subject: Ductwork Hangers & Supports
rule: Ductwork supports must be spaced at intervals not exceeding the maximum specified in applicable mechanical codes (e.g., SMACNA standards) based on duct gauge and size
conditions: All ductwork installations
exceptions: When engineered calculations demonstrate that alternative spacing provides equivalent structural performance and are approved by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Ductwork Hangers & Supports
rule: Ductwork hangers must be fabricated from materials compatible with the duct material and environment to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: When dissimilar metals are in contact in the hanger assembly
exceptions: When dielectric isolation materials are placed between dissimilar metals

subject: Smoke Damper
rule: smoke damper must close fully and seal against its frame when activated
conditions: damper is installed in a smoke control system
damper is in the closed position during fire/smoke event

subject: Smoke Damper
rule: smoke damper must not be installed in a location where it will be blocked from closing by ducts, cables, pipes, or other obstructions
conditions: damper is installed in any duct or wall penetration

subject: Smoke Damper
rule: smoke damper must be accessible for manual reset after activation
conditions: damper is of the type requiring manual reset
exceptions: dampers with remote reset capability that is tested and listed

subject: Motorized Fire Damper
rule: Motorized fire damper must be installed with the actuator and motor assembly located outside the duct (in the accessible space)
conditions: damper is installed in a duct system
exceptions: manufacturer explicitly approves in-duct actuator installation and local code permits it

subject: Motorized Fire Damper
rule: Motorized fire damper must be provided with a fire-resistive enclosure or be installed in a fire-resistance-rated barrier equal to the rating of the damper
conditions: damper penetrates a fire-resistance-rated wall, floor, or partition

subject: Motorized Fire Damper
rule: Motorized fire damper must close fully upon loss of power to the actuator (fail-closed)
exceptions: if the damper is specifically rated and listed for fail-in-place operation by a recognized testing agency and approved by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Motorized Fire Damper
rule: Motorized fire damper must not have the motor shaft or linkage blocked by duct insulation, duct liner, or construction debris

subject: Backdraft Damper
rule: backdraft damper must be installed with proper airflow directional orientation
conditions: damper is installed in an HVAC duct system

subject: Backdraft Damper
rule: backdraft damper blades must be free to pivot or move without obstruction
conditions: damper is installed and operational

subject: Backdraft Damper
rule: backdraft damper must not be installed where the airstream temperature exceeds the damper's rated temperature limit
conditions: damper is installed in a high-temperature HVAC or exhaust application
exceptions: damper is explicitly rated for the service temperature

subject: Duct-Mounted Access Door
rule: Duct-mounted access door must be openable without tools from the access side
conditions: The duct is in a location that requires routine or emergency access
exceptions: Sealed systems that are never accessed after commissioning

subject: Duct-Mounted Access Door
rule: Duct-mounted access door must not leak air at a rate exceeding the duct's leakage class when closed and latched
conditions: The duct system is rated for a specific leakage class per SMACNA or ASHRAE
exceptions: Doors in negative-pressure smoke-control systems where intentional leakage is part of design

subject: Duct-Mounted Access Door
rule: Duct-mounted access door must have a minimum clearance equal to the door opening dimension on the access side to allow full swing or removal
conditions: The door is hinged and swings open
The door is a removable panel type
exceptions: Ducts in confined spaces where a smaller door is specifically designed for inspection only, not component removal

subject: Duct Takeoff Fitting
rule: duct takeoff fitting must maintain minimum straight duct length upstream and downstream per SMACNA/ASHRAE standards
conditions: fitting is used for flow measurement or balancing damper installation
exceptions: manufacturer-certified flow straighteners or vanes are installed upstream within the minimum distance

subject: Duct Takeoff Fitting
rule: duct takeoff fitting must be airtight at all seams and joints per SMACNA seal class requirements
conditions: fitting is installed in a duct system operating above 0.5 in. w.g. static pressure

subject: Duct Takeoff Fitting
rule: duct takeoff fitting must not have a branch duct cross-sectional area exceeding the main duct cross-sectional area at the point of connection
exceptions: engineered systems with splitter dampers or vortex diffusers specifically designed for equal-pressure分流

subject: Duct Takeoff Fitting
rule: duct takeoff fitting must be installed with the branch duct orientation not opposing the main duct airflow direction at greater than 90 degrees

subject: Duct Elbow
rule: duct elbow must maintain minimum centerline radius of 1.5 times duct diameter
conditions: for rectangular ducts
for round ducts
exceptions: when manufacturer specifies a different minimum radius

subject: Duct Elbow
rule: duct elbow must not have sharp inner corners (turning vanes must be installed if radius-to-diameter ratio is below 1.0)
conditions: when airflow velocity exceeds 600 fpm (3 m/s)
exceptions: for low-velocity residential systems below 600 fpm where pressure drop is tolerable

subject: Duct Elbow
rule: duct elbow must have an aspect ratio (width/height) no greater than 4:1
conditions: for rectangular duct elbows

subject: Duct Elbow
rule: duct elbow gauge (sheet metal thickness) must meet SMACNA minimum for the specified duct dimension and static pressure class
conditions: for metal duct systems
exceptions: when using alternative materials with equivalent structural strength per engineering analysis

subject: Duct Transition & Reducer
rule: Duct transition or reducer must maintain cross-sectional area continuity (or follow area-preserving ratio) between connected duct segments to prevent excessive velocity change or static pressure loss that renders the system inoperable
conditions: When connecting two duct sections of different sizes
exceptions: When the transition is specifically designed as an intentional flow-restricting device with documented pressure drop acceptance

subject: Duct Transition & Reducer
rule: Duct transition or reducer must have an acceptable aspect ratio (width-to-depth) to prevent excessive pressure drop and structural instability
conditions: When the transition connects rectangular ducts
exceptions: When special low-velocity or equal-friction system design explicitly accounts for high aspect ratio performance

subject: Duct Transition & Reducer
rule: Duct transition or reducer must not create a sudden sharp edge or abrupt offset (i.e., improper turning vanes or lack thereof) that causes flow separation and system unbalance
conditions: When the transition includes a change in direction immediately adjacent to the size change

subject: Duct-Mounted Reheat Coil
rule: Duct-mounted reheat coil must have a heating fluid (hot water, steam, or electric) supply connected to function
conditions: when installed as an active reheat component
exceptions: uninstalled spare or future-use coil with capped connections

subject: Duct-Mounted Reheat Coil
rule: Duct-mounted reheat coil must not be installed where the leaving air temperature exceeds the maximum rated temperature of downstream duct materials or components
conditions: when the reheat coil is active and heating
exceptions: when downstream duct and components are rated for the expected temperature rise

subject: Duct-Mounted Reheat Coil
rule: Duct-mounted reheat coil condensate drain pan must have a gravity drainage path or a working condensate pump to remove collected moisture
conditions: when the coil is a cooling-and-reheat type that can dehumidify (chilled-water or DX coil upstream) and produce condensation
exceptions: dry-coil design with no condensation expected (e.g., electric resistance only, no upstream cooling)

subject: Duct-Mounted Reheat Coil
rule: Duct-mounted reheat coil must not be energized (electric coil) or receive hot fluid (hydronic coil) when airflow across the coil is below the minimum required face velocity
conditions: when the system is operating and duct airflow is present
exceptions: designs with integral airflow proving switches that interlock the heating source

subject: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
rule: Duct-mounted humidifier must be installed with its airflow direction arrow aligned with the actual airflow in the duct
conditions: unit has directional airflow markings

subject: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
rule: Duct-mounted humidifier must not be installed where duct static pressure exceeds the unit's maximum rated static pressure

subject: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
rule: Duct-mounted humidifier's water supply line must not be connected before the evaporator pad or water distribution tray is properly installed

subject: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
rule: Duct-mounted humidifier must have an overflow drain or water-level safety shutoff if connected to a permanent water supply
conditions: unit is connected to a continuous/pressurized water supply rather than manual filling

subject: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
rule: Duct-mounted humidifier must not be mounted on a duct that serves a cooling-only system without appropriate high-limit or airflow proving switch
conditions: duct serves a cooling-only air handler or heat pump without a call-for-heat interlock

subject: VAV Box Duct Connection
rule: VAV box duct connection must be airtight between the VAV box and the ductwork
conditions: For all VAV box installations with mechanical duct connections
exceptions: Intentional relief openings designed for pressure control

subject: VAV Box Duct Connection
rule: VAV box duct connection must not have unsealed gaps larger than the duct leakage class specified by applicable standards (e.g., SMACNA, ASHRAE)
conditions: For duct connections serving conditioned spaces

subject: VAV Box Duct Connection
rule: VAV box duct connection must be rigidly secured to prevent disconnection under operating pressure
conditions: All VAV box installations

subject: VAV Box Duct Connection
rule: VAV box inlet duct connection diameter must not be smaller than the VAV box inlet collar diameter
conditions: For ductwork connecting to the inlet of a VAV box
exceptions: Factory-provided transition fittings designed and certified for the specific VAV box model

subject: Plenum Box
rule: a plenum box must be located within the ceiling plenum space (the area between the structural ceiling and a dropped ceiling)
conditions: when serving as an HVAC air distribution component
when installed in a commercial building with suspended ceiling
exceptions: when installed in a plenum-rated open ceiling design where the plenum box is itself the visible terminal unit

subject: Plenum Box
rule: a plenum box must have airtight connections to both the supply duct upstream and the downstream branch ducts or diffuser boots
conditions: when the plenum box is acting as an air distribution junction

subject: Plenum Box
rule: a plenum box must not be installed in a location that is inaccessible for maintenance and filter replacement
conditions: when the plenum box contains internal components such as dampers, coils, or filters requiring periodic service
exceptions: when the plenum box is a mixing-only box with no serviceable components inside

subject: Laboratory Exhaust Duct
rule: laboratory exhaust duct must be constructed of corrosion-resistant material (e.g., stainless steel, FRP, or PVC)
conditions: duct conveys corrosive fumes
duct conveys acidic or alkaline vapors

subject: Laboratory Exhaust Duct
rule: laboratory exhaust duct must maintain negative pressure relative to surrounding occupied spaces
conditions: duct is located within or passes through occupied building areas

subject: Laboratory Exhaust Duct
rule: laboratory exhaust duct must not share common ductwork with general building exhaust or return air systems

subject: Laboratory Exhaust Duct
rule: laboratory exhaust duct discharge point must be located above the building roof and sufficiently high to prevent re-entrainment of exhaust into building air intakes
exceptions: exhaust is treated by HEPA filtration and chemical scrubbers to render effluent non-hazardous, and dispersion modeling demonstrates safe re-entry concentrations below threshold limits

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must terminate to the exterior of the building
conditions: The duct conveys greasy cooking exhaust
exceptions: Recirculating range hoods that filter and return air to the kitchen (though these are not true exhaust ducts)

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must be constructed of non-combustible material (steel, stainless steel, or equivalent)
conditions: The duct is connected to commercial cooking equipment
The duct carries exhaust at temperatures above ambient
exceptions: Residential kitchen exhaust ducts serving domestic cooking appliances may use aluminum or galvanized steel which are still non-combustible but have different thickness requirements

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must not have internal baffles, filters, or grease extraction devices made of combustible materials
conditions: The duct contains in-line grease removal components

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must maintain a minimum clearance to combustible construction (typically 18 inches or as specified by local code)
conditions: The duct passes through or near combustible building elements (wood framing, insulation, etc.)
exceptions: Clearance may be reduced if the duct is protected by an approved thermal barrier or fire-rated enclosure

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must be sealed (airtight) along its entire length

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must slope toward the cooking appliance or toward a drainage point
conditions: The duct has horizontal runs

subject: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
rule: Kitchen exhaust duct must not terminate directly above a walkway or public area at low level
conditions: The exhaust outlet is at or near grade (ground level)
exceptions: The outlet is specifically designed with grease traps, directional louvres, and sufficient height to protect passersby

subject: Pipework Supports and Hangers
rule: pipework supports and hangers must be capable of supporting the full dead weight of the filled pipe under all operating conditions
conditions: pipework is installed
system is in operation

subject: Pipework Supports and Hangers
rule: pipework supports and hangers must not impose point loads that exceed the allowable stress of the pipe wall
conditions: pipe wall thickness is standard or reduced
support type is a rigid cradle or U-bolt
exceptions: when a load-distributing saddle or wear pad is installed at the contact point

subject: Pipework Supports and Hangers
rule: pipework supports and hangers must accommodate expected thermal expansion and contraction of the supported pipe
conditions: pipe operates at a temperature different from ambient installation temperature
pipe material has a non-zero coefficient of thermal expansion

subject: Pipework Valves and Fittings
rule: Pipework valves must be installed with the flow direction arrow aligned with the actual direction of flow
conditions: valve has a directional flow indicator (e.g., arrow cast into body)
valve type is a check valve, gate valve, globe valve, or butterfly valve with directional marking
exceptions: valve body has no directional marking (e.g., some full-port ball valves are bidirectional)

subject: Pipework Valves and Fittings
rule: Pipework valves and fittings must not be installed in a position that prevents full stem travel or handle operation
conditions: valve has a rising stem, lever, handwheel, or actuated operator
exceptions: valve is designed for buried or enclosed service with remote operator

subject: Pipework Valves and Fittings
rule: Threaded pipe fittings must not be cross-threaded during assembly
conditions: fitting uses NPT, BSP, or other tapered pipe threads
joint is intended to be leak-tight

subject: Cold Water Pipework
rule: cold water pipework must be protected against freezing
conditions: pipework located in unheated areas or external to the building thermal envelope
exceptions: pipework is part of a system designed to drain down automatically when not in use
pipework is self-trace-heated and insulated to maintain temperature above freezing

subject: Cold Water Pipework
rule: cold water pipework must not be directly connected to a sewer or drainage pipe without an air gap or backflow prevention device
conditions: pipework terminates at or connects to any drainage, waste, or sewer system

subject: Cold Water Pipework
rule: cold water pipework must be rated for the maximum static pressure that can be exerted at the point of use
conditions: system is connected to a municipal supply or pumped system that can produce pressure exceeding the pipe rating
exceptions: pressure-reducing valves are installed upstream and set below the pipe rating

subject: Cold Water Pipework
rule: cold water pipework must not be installed in direct contact with aggressive materials that cause galvanic or chemical corrosion
conditions: dissimilar metals are in contact in the presence of water
pipe material is susceptible to corrosion by surrounding construction materials (e.g., copper in contact with steel, or ferrous pipes embedded in certain concretes)
exceptions: suitable dielectric unions, isolators, or protective coatings separate the dissimilar materials

subject: Hot Water Pipework
rule: hot water pipework must be insulated to prevent heat loss and protect against contact burns
conditions: where pipework carries water above 60°C
where pipework is accessible to occupants
exceptions: short uninsulated sections at connections to equipment where insulation would impede maintenance or valve operation

subject: Hot Water Pipework
rule: hot water pipework must have a minimum gradient or be fitted with automatic air vents at high points to prevent air locking
conditions: where pipework is part of a pumped circulation system
exceptions: systems with dedicated automatic air-elimination devices at every high point

subject: Hot Water Pipework
rule: hot water pipework must be rated for the maximum operating temperature and pressure of the system

subject: Hot Water Pipework
rule: hot water pipework must not be directly embedded in incompatible materials (e.g., uncoated copper in concrete containing sulfates) without protective wrapping
conditions: where pipes contact concrete, mortar, or corrosive soils
exceptions: pipes with manufacturer-approved corrosion-resistant coating or sleeving

subject: Hot Water Pipework
rule: hot water pipework must be supported at intervals that prevent sagging and thermal expansion stress

subject: Heating Pipework
rule: heating pipework must be installed with adequate thermal insulation on all exposed pipe runs
conditions: pipework is located in unheated spaces (e.g. loft, basement, outside)
pipework carries hot water or steam
exceptions: pipework located entirely within conditioned/heated zones where heat loss is not a concern
pipework that is part of a deliberately uninsulated heat-emitter system (e.g. bare radiators)

subject: Heating Pipework
rule: heating pipework must not be installed in direct contact with combustible materials without adequate clearance or shielding
conditions: pipework conveys fluids above 60 °C
adjacent building elements are combustible (e.g. timber framing, insulation with low fire rating)
exceptions: pipes that are part of a listed or heritage system where alternative protection is accepted by building control

subject: Heating Pipework
rule: heating pipework must be provided with means of expansion compensation (e.g. expansion loops, bellows, or sliding anchors) on long straight runs
conditions: pipe length exceeds 20 m between changes of direction
temperature differential exceeds 30 °C between installation and operating conditions
exceptions: short branch runs that are inherently flexible (e.g. copper microbore < 10 m)

subject: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
rule: Sanitary drainage pipework must have a minimum slope (fall) in the direction of flow to ensure self-cleansing velocity
conditions: gravity-flow drainage system
exceptions: pressurized/positive-displacement drainage systems (e.g., pumped systems)

subject: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
rule: Sanitary drainage pipework must be vented to prevent siphonage and trap seal loss
conditions: building drainage system connected to sanitary fixtures with water traps

subject: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
rule: Sanitary drainage pipework must not be directly connected to a stormwater drainage system without appropriate separation or treatment
exceptions: systems designed with approved combined sewer overflow arrangements in jurisdictions where permitted

subject: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
rule: Sanitary drainage pipework must not have sharp 90-degree changes in direction without a cleanout or access point
conditions: horizontal or near-horizontal pipe runs
exceptions: vertical-to-horizontal transitions with long-sweep fittings (≥ 45° bends)

subject: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
rule: Sanitary drainage pipework must be watertight and leak-free at all joints and connections

subject: Stormwater Drainage Pipework
rule: stormwater drainage pipework must have continuous positive slope toward the outlet point
conditions: gravity drainage system
non-pressure pipework
exceptions: siphonic drainage systems
pumped systems

subject: Stormwater Drainage Pipework
rule: stormwater drainage pipework must be sized to convey the design storm event runoff without surcharging above pipe obvert level at the design flow
conditions: pipe network designed for a specific return-period rainfall event
exceptions: where overland flood path is explicitly designed and approved for surcharge above obvert

subject: Stormwater Drainage Pipework
rule: stormwater drainage pipework must not have trapped sections where water cannot drain out without maintenance intervention
conditions: non-siphonic gravity system
exceptions: siphonic systems designed to prime and purge
inlet structures that are intentionally sumped with cleanout access

subject: Stormwater Drainage Pipework
rule: stormwater drainage pipework must have access points (cleanouts/inspection openings) at all changes of direction greater than 45 degrees and at maximum spacing per code
conditions: buried or enclosed pipework
diameter less than 600 mm
exceptions: pipe runs with rodding access from both ends where total run length is within code maximum

subject: Vented and Overflow Pipework
rule: vented and overflow pipework must discharge in a visible location where flow can be observed
conditions: system is configured as a warning or tell-tale overflow
exceptions: buried or concealed drainage systems with remote monitoring

subject: Vented and Overflow Pipework
rule: vented and overflow pipework must not be directly connected to a sanitary drainage system without an air gap or backflow prevention
conditions: pipework terminates into a sewer or drain line

subject: Vented and Overflow Pipework
rule: the overflow pipe invert must be set below the lowest controlled water inlet to the vessel
conditions: system serves a tank, cistern, or vessel with a controlled fill inlet

subject: Vented and Overflow Pipework
rule: vented and overflow pipework must have no valves or shutoff devices in the flow path
exceptions: lockshield valves permitted on vented pipework where explicitly allowed by code for maintenance isolation, provided they remain in the open position and are incapable of being inadvertently closed

subject: Vented and Overflow Pipework
rule: vented pipework must be sized to carry the full design flow without surcharging at the vent outlet
conditions: pipework functions as a combined vent and overflow

subject: Gas Pipework
rule: gas pipework must be positively sealed at all joints and connections
conditions: where gas is combustible or toxic
exceptions: systems designed for intentional controlled venting under continuous monitoring

subject: Gas Pipework
rule: gas pipework must have a means of isolation (shut-off valve) upstream of any point of use
conditions: in any building or facility with multiple gas appliances or outlets
exceptions: single-appliance installations where the appliance itself has an integral shut-off valve and the supply is immediately adjacent

subject: Gas Pipework
rule: gas pipework must not be embedded in solid concrete or masonry without a corrosion-protective sleeve or duct
conditions: where pipe material is carbon steel or other corrodible metal
exceptions: pipework made of stainless steel specifically certified for direct embedment
pipework passing through a purpose-designed ventilated duct

subject: Gas Pipework
rule: gas pipework must be bonded to the building's equipotential bonding system
conditions: where the gas pipework is metallic and enters a building
exceptions: entirely non-metallic (e.g. PE) pipework with no metallic components

subject: Fire Suppression Pipework
rule: Fire suppression pipework must be connected to a reliable water supply or suppression agent source
conditions: where fire suppression system is required by code or design intent
exceptions: standalone systems with integrated pressurized agent supplies that are self-contained and pre-charged

subject: Fire Suppression Pipework
rule: Fire suppression pipework must not be routed through areas where ambient temperatures fall below the freezing point of the contained suppression medium
conditions: where the suppression medium is water or water-based solution
exceptions: where pipework is trace-heated and insulated per applicable standards
where the system uses a dry-pipe or pre-action configuration that drains water from exposed sections

subject: Fire Suppression Pipework
rule: Fire suppression pipework must be sized to deliver the required flow and pressure at the most hydraulically remote sprinkler or nozzle
conditions: when the system is a hydraulically calculated sprinkler or spray system

subject: Fire Suppression Pipework
rule: Fire suppression pipework must be supported and braced to withstand seismic forces where required by applicable building code
conditions: in seismic design categories where code mandates seismic bracing of fire suppression systems
exceptions: buildings exempted from seismic design per governing code

subject: Cable Trays and Ladder Racks
rule: Cable trays and ladder racks must be supported at intervals that prevent excessive deflection under their own weight plus the weight of installed cables
conditions: When supporting any cables

subject: Cable Trays and Ladder Racks
rule: Cable trays and ladder racks must be electrically bonded and grounded
conditions: When part of an electrical installation where metallic cable trays are used
exceptions: Non-metallic (e.g., fiberglass) cable trays are not required to be bonded/grounded

subject: Cable Trays and Ladder Racks
rule: Cable trays and ladder racks must not have sharp edges or burrs that could damage cable insulation

subject: Cable Trays and Ladder Racks
rule: Cable trays installed outdoors must be rated for the environmental conditions (UV, rain, temperature range)
conditions: When installed outdoors or in exposed locations

subject: Refrigerant Pipework
rule: refrigerant pipework must be thermally insulated to prevent condensation and maintain system efficiency
conditions: where pipe operating temperature is below ambient dew point
where pipe carries saturated or two-phase refrigerant
exceptions: short uninsulated sections at service valves or equipment connections where condensation risk is mitigated by location or secondary drainage

subject: Refrigerant Pipework
rule: refrigerant pipework must be of material and wall thickness compatible with the refrigerant type and system operating pressure

subject: Refrigerant Pipework
rule: refrigerant pipework must not have undocumented field-brazed joints in concealed locations without access provisions
conditions: where joints are enclosed within walls, ceilings, or chases
exceptions: pre-fabricated joints tested and approved per code

subject: Refrigerant Pipework
rule: refrigerant pipework must be sloped to allow oil return to the compressor
conditions: in systems where oil is miscible with refrigerant and compressor relies on positive oil return
exceptions: systems with dedicated oil return pumps
vertical risers where engineered oil traps are provided

subject: Cable Trunking and Raceways
rule: cable trunking and raceways must not be installed where they will be subjected to physical damage unless adequately protected
conditions: locations subject to impact, crushing, or abrasion
areas with vehicular traffic
exceptions: when protective barriers, conduits, or armored constructions are used

subject: Cable Trunking and Raceways
rule: cable trunking and raceways must be installed so that internal drainage and moisture egress is ensured at all low points
conditions: outdoor or damp location installation
exposed to condensation or ingress risk
exceptions: systems entirely within controlled indoor environments with no moisture risk

subject: Cable Trunking and Raceways
rule: cable trunking and raceways must have a maximum fill ratio that does not exceed the manufacturer's rated cable fill capacity or code-prescribed limit
conditions: any installation containing multiple cables

subject: Conduit Systems (EMT/IMC/RMC/PVC)
rule: EMT, IMC, RMC, and PVC conduit must not be directly embedded in concrete without proper protection (e.g., corrosion-resistant coating for metallic types, or minimum concrete cover per code)
conditions: conduit embedded in concrete
exceptions: conduit listed and labeled for direct concrete embedment
PVC schedule 80 may be directly embedded per code

subject: Conduit Systems (EMT/IMC/RMC/PVC)
rule: Conduit systems must be installed with proper supports at intervals not exceeding code-specified maximums (e.g., EMT: 10 ft, IMC/RMC: 12 ft, PVC: 3–5 ft depending on trade size)
conditions: conduit installed in exposed or concealed locations
exceptions: conduit used as a listed manufactured assembly with integral support

subject: Conduit Systems (EMT/IMC/RMC/PVC)
rule: Conduit bends must not exceed the maximum number of 90-degree bends (typically 360 degrees total) between pull points
conditions: any conduit run
exceptions: approved junction boxes or pull boxes installed to break the run

subject: Conduit Systems (EMT/IMC/RMC/PVC)
rule: PVC conduit must not be used where ambient temperatures exceed the manufacturer's rated maximum service temperature (typically 122°F / 50°C)
conditions: PVC conduit exposed to high ambient temperatures
exceptions: PVC conduit rated for higher temperature (e.g., Schedule 80 H.T. listed for higher use)

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rule: Cable basket and mesh systems must be supported at intervals not exceeding manufacturer specifications to prevent sagging and mechanical failure
conditions: When installed as a horizontal or sloped cable support system
exceptions: Temporary installations during construction

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rule: Cable basket and mesh systems must not have sharp edges or burrs that can damage cable jackets at points of contact
conditions: At all cut ends, joints, and penetration points
exceptions: When edge protection fittings (grommets, edge strips) are installed

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rule: Cable basket and mesh systems must be fabricated from or coated with corrosion-resistant material when installed in environments with high humidity, chemical exposure, or outdoors
conditions: When installed outdoors, in wet locations, or in areas with corrosive agents
exceptions: Where sacrificial corrosion is accepted and periodic replacement is scheduled

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rule: Cable basket and mesh systems must be electrically bonded and grounded in accordance with applicable electrical codes
conditions: When used as an equipment grounding conductor per code or when metallic and part of an electrical raceway system
exceptions: Non-metallic cable basket systems do not require grounding; isolated sections not serving as grounding path

subject: Underfloor Duct and Cellular Floor Systems
rule: Underfloor duct and cellular floor systems must provide a continuous, uninterrupted pathway for cabling and airflow across the entire floor plate
conditions: when used for cable distribution
when used for air distribution
exceptions: when structural columns or shear walls physically penetrate the floor system at that location

subject: Underfloor Duct and Cellular Floor Systems
rule: Cellular floor deck cells used for electrical distribution must not be used simultaneously for both power and data cabling in the same continuous cell without a properly rated divider
conditions: when the cell carries both power (≥50V) and low-voltage data cabling
exceptions: when a listed metallic divider is factory-installed and maintains required separation per NEC/CEC

subject: Underfloor Duct and Cellular Floor Systems
rule: Underfloor duct systems must have a finished floor surface that is structurally adequate to support the design live load without transferring load through the duct covers alone
conditions: when ducts are installed in a slab-on-grade or suspended slab configuration
when duct covers are exposed to foot or equipment traffic
exceptions: when the floor finish is a separate structural topping slab that bridges across ducts

subject: Underfloor Duct and Cellular Floor Systems
rule: In cellular floor systems, the top (concrete fill) must have minimum depth sufficient to provide fire-resistance rating required by the building code for the floor assembly
conditions: when the cellular floor assembly is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: when an approved sprayed fire-resistive material or intumescent coating is applied to the underside

subject: Cable Glands and Entry Fittings
rule: cable gland must provide an environmental seal (IP rating) at the point where the cable enters the enclosure
conditions: gland is used in an outdoor or wet location
gland is used in a hazardous area requiring ingress protection
exceptions: gland installed in a completely indoor, dry, non-hazardous equipment room where no seal is specified

subject: Cable Glands and Entry Fittings
rule: cable gland entry thread must match the enclosure knock-out thread form and size (e.g., NPT, metric, PG)
conditions: gland is threaded into an enclosure port
exceptions: gland uses an adapter fitting that converts thread types

subject: Cable Glands and Entry Fittings
rule: cable gland must not be installed without the correct ferrule or insert sized to the cable outer diameter
conditions: gland is of the compression or multi-part type requiring an internal ferrule/insert
exceptions: gland is a one-piece non-compression type that seals directly on the cable jacket

subject: Cable Glands and Entry Fittings
rule: cable gland armour clamping mechanism must positively engage the cable armour (wire/tape) when used with armoured cable
conditions: gland is used with steel-wire-armoured (SWA) or similarly armoured cable
exceptions: cable is unarmoured
gland is a non-armour type intentionally used with unarmoured cable only

subject: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
rule: Firestopping and cable transit seals must be tested and classified in accordance with the relevant fire resistance standard (e.g. EN 1366-3, ASTM E814, UL 1479) to the required fire rating of the barrier being penetrated
conditions: When used to seal penetrations through fire-resistance-rated walls, floors, or ceilings

subject: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
rule: Firestopping and cable transit seals must not have gaps, voids, or unsealed spaces between the sealant material and the penetrating item or the edge of the opening
conditions: In any fire-resistance-rated barrier penetration

subject: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
rule: The annular space between a penetrating cable or pipe and the opening must be completely filled with the firestop seal to the full depth of the assembly
conditions: When sealing single or multiple penetrations through a fire-rated barrier

subject: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
rule: Firestopping and cable transit seals must remain in place and intact under the expected service conditions (vibration, thermal movement, ageing) without cracking, shrinking, or detaching
conditions: In all installations where the seal is relied upon for fire containment

subject: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
rule: Firestopping materials must not be used beyond their manufacturer-specified maximum service temperature or in fire-resistance-rated assemblies for which they have not been tested
conditions: When selecting firestop products for a given fire-rated barrier and penetrating service

subject: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
rule: conductor ampacity must not exceed the rated value for its AWG size and insulation type as specified in NEC Table 310.16 (or applicable standard)
conditions: electrical power circuit
copper or aluminum conductor
exceptions: when all terminals and devices are rated for the higher temperature
when using 90°C column for derating purposes only if final ampacity does not exceed lower temperature column ratings at the termination

subject: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
rule: wire bending space at terminals and panels must comply with NEC Table 312.6(A) and (B) minimum dimensions based on AWG size
conditions: conductor terminated at panelboard
switchboard
or control cabinet
exceptions: listed manufactured assemblies with pre-approved bending space

subject: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
rule: conductor must be protected by an overcurrent device rated at or below its ampacity (per NEC 240.4)
conditions: power and lighting circuits
exceptions: motor circuits with overload protection per Article 430
transformer primary protection per Article 450
tap conductors per 240.21

subject: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
rule: grounded (neutral) conductor must not be smaller than required by NEC Table 250.102(C)(1) or 250.122 based on phase conductor AWG size and system
conditions: grounded conductor in service
feeder
or branch circuit
exceptions: if the grounded conductor only carries unbalanced current and the phase conductors are sized larger than required

subject: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
rule: minimum AWG size for branch circuit conductors must not be smaller than 14 AWG copper (or 12 AWG aluminum) per NEC 210.19
conditions: branch circuit supplying general lighting or receptacle loads
exceptions: control circuits
Class 2 circuits
communications circuits governed by other code sections

subject: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
rule: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable must be secured and supported at intervals not exceeding 4.5 feet (1.4 m) and within 12 inches (300 mm) of every outlet box, junction box, cabinet, or fitting
conditions: Cable is installed exposed on the surface of a wall or ceiling
Cable is run through bored holes in framing members
exceptions: Cables fished through existing walls or ceilings in concealed spaces where access is limited need not be secured at the 4.5 ft interval

subject: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
rule: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable must not be used in structures exceeding three floors above grade
conditions: Building is of Type I, II, III, or IV construction
exceptions: One- and two-family dwellings and their attached or detached garages are exempt from this restriction

subject: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
rule: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable must not be installed in plenum air-handling spaces
conditions: The space is used as a plenum for environmental air return or supply

subject: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
rule: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable must not be installed where subject to physical damage
conditions: Cable is run within 1.25 inches (32 mm) of the edge of a framing member
Cable is installed below 8 feet in an unprotected location such as a garage, basement, or crawlspace where mechanical impact is possible
exceptions: Cable protected by guard strips, conduit, or installed in a location where the building finish provides equivalent protection

subject: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
rule: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable must not be used in wet or damp locations
conditions: Location is classified as a wet or damp location per NEC Article 100 definitions
exceptions: NM-B cable is rated for use in damp locations (such as masonry block walls) but not in wet locations

subject: Low-Voltage and Data Cabling (Cat 6/6A/Coax/Fiber)
rule: Low-voltage and data cabling must not be installed in the same conduit or raceway as power conductors above 50V unless separated by a continuous and bonded metallic barrier or divider
conditions: When installed in same conduit/raceway as power conductors >50V
exceptions: When separated by a continuous and bonded metallic barrier or divider meeting code requirements

subject: Low-Voltage and Data Cabling (Cat 6/6A/Coax/Fiber)
rule: Low-voltage and data cabling must maintain minimum separation distances from electrical power circuits of 50V or greater
conditions: Cabling runs parallel to power wiring for extended distances (typically >2 ft / 0.6 m)
exceptions: When separated by a continuous bonded metallic barrier or when using shielded cable in compliance with applicable codes

subject: Low-Voltage and Data Cabling (Cat 6/6A/Coax/Fiber)
rule: Low-voltage and data cabling must have a minimum bend radius not less than 4 times the cable outer diameter (for unsupported) or 8 times (for supported/bundled)
conditions: During installation and at final termination points
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified bend radius supersedes when more restrictive or explicitly tested for tighter radii

subject: Low-Voltage and Data Cabling (Cat 6/6A/Coax/Fiber)
rule: Low-voltage and data cabling must not be installed where ambient temperature exceeds the cable's rated temperature range
conditions: Cable is installed in plenums, attics, near HVAC equipment, or outdoor environments
exceptions: Use of cable with higher temperature rating (e.g., plenum-rated) that matches the installed environment

subject: Mineral-Insulated (MI) Cable
rule: MI cable must be supported at intervals not exceeding the manufacturer's specifications to prevent mechanical stress on the sheath
conditions: installed in horizontal or vertical runs
exposed (not continuously enclosed in conduit or tray)
exceptions: when installed in dedicated cable tray with continuous support

subject: Mineral-Insulated (MI) Cable
rule: MI cable terminations must be sealed against moisture ingress
conditions: any installation where cable ends are exposed to ambient air or humidity

subject: Mineral-Insulated (MI) Cable
rule: MI cable must not be bent to a radius smaller than the manufacturer's minimum bending radius
conditions: during installation or permanent placement

subject: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
rule: Service entrance and feeder cabling must be protected against physical damage
conditions: Cable is installed in areas subject to mechanical impact or abrasion
Cable is installed at grade, in a trench, or within 2m of finished grade
exceptions: Cable is installed entirely in metallic conduit or approved raceway
Cable is Type MC or Type AC with listed fittings

subject: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
rule: Service entrance conductors must not be spliced within the service raceway or service cable
conditions: Cable is used as service entrance conductors between the service point and the service disconnecting means
exceptions: Splicing is done within an approved junction box or in accordance with 230.33 and 230.46

subject: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
rule: Service entrance and feeder cable ampacity must be at least 100% of the calculated load served
conditions: Cable supplies a continuous or non-continuous load
exceptions: Ampacity is adjusted for ambient temperature and bundling per NEC 310.15; 100% applies to non-continuous load plus 125% of continuous load

subject: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
rule: Feeder cabling must have a dedicated equipment grounding conductor or be contained in metal raceway that serves as the equipment ground
conditions: The feeder supplies branch circuits that require an equipment ground
The feeder is part of a non-service installation
exceptions: Installations compliant with NEC 250.32 for existing grounded systems where an alternate path exists

subject: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
rule: Service entrance conductors must be sized not smaller than 8 AWG copper or 6 AWG aluminum
conditions: Conductors supply a one-family or two-family dwelling service of 120/240 V
exceptions: Larger services or commercial installations use different minimums per NEC 230.42 and Table 310.12

subject: Fire Sprinkler Piping
rule: fire sprinkler piping must be installed in environments maintained above 40°F (4°C) or be protected from freezing
conditions: system contains water as extinguishing agent
exceptions: dry-pipe sprinkler systems where piping is normally dry and water only enters upon activation

subject: Fire Sprinkler Piping
rule: fire sprinkler piping must not have threaded fittings in pipe sizes 8 inches (DN200) and larger
conditions: pipe diameter is 8 inches or greater

subject: Fire Sprinkler Piping
rule: fire sprinkler piping must have a minimum working pressure rating that meets or exceeds the system design pressure

subject: Fire Sprinkler Piping
rule: fire sprinkler piping must not be used as a support for any other building element, equipment, or non-sprinkler piping
exceptions: support of other fire sprinkler system components such as branch lines or sprinkler heads

subject: Fire Sprinkler Piping
rule: fire sprinkler piping must be installed with a minimum clearance of 1 inch (25 mm) from structural members and other building services

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rule: Sprinkler control valve must be installed in a location that is accessible for manual operation and maintenance
conditions: Where the valve is part of a fire sprinkler system
Where the valve requires manual operation or testing

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rule: Sprinkler control valve must not be installed in a location subject to freezing temperatures unless appropriately protected
conditions: Where the sprinkler system is a wet-pipe system
exceptions: Valve is located in a heated enclosure
Valve is a dry-pattern or freeze-protected type rated for the expected temperature

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rule: Sprinkler control valve must be visibly identified with a sign indicating its function and the portion of the system it controls

subject: Fire Sprinkler Pump
rule: Fire sprinkler pump must be connected to a reliable water supply

subject: Fire Sprinkler Pump
rule: Fire sprinkler pump must have a dedicated electrical power supply appropriate to its motor rating

subject: Fire Sprinkler Pump
rule: Fire sprinkler pump must not be installed in a location subject to freezing temperatures unless freeze protection is provided
conditions: pump and associated piping are in an unheated space
ambient temperature can drop below 4°C (40°F)
exceptions: freeze protection (e.g., heat tracing, insulation, heated enclosure) is provided

subject: Fire Sprinkler Pump
rule: Fire sprinkler pump must be listed/labeled for fire protection service by a recognized testing laboratory

subject: Fire Sprinkler Pump
rule: Fire sprinkler pump suction pipe must be sized to prevent cavitation at rated flow

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rule: Sprinkler water supply connection must have a minimum water flow and pressure capacity as specified by the hazard classification of the protected area
