conditions: where sprinkler system is installed

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rule: Sprinkler water supply connection must be protected against freezing where exposed to temperatures below 4°C
conditions: in climates where ambient temperature can drop below 4°C
exceptions: where the connection and all downstream piping are designed as dry-pipe or pre-action systems that drain fully

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rule: Sprinkler water supply connection must not be shut off or isolated from the water source by any valve that can be inadvertently closed
conditions: during normal system operation
exceptions: during maintenance or repair, provided valves are supervised (tamper switches) and the system is returned to service immediately after

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rule: sprinkler system riser must be installed in a vertical orientation
conditions: riser is part of an automatic fire sprinkler system

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rule: sprinkler system riser must have a shutoff valve (OS&Y or similar) installed in the supply line upstream of the riser
conditions: system is configured for wet-pipe or dry-pipe operation

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rule: sprinkler system riser must not be located where ambient temperature can fall below 40°F (4°C) unless the riser is part of a dry-pipe or preaction system
conditions: riser is part of a wet-pipe sprinkler system
exceptions: riser assembly is installed within a conditioned enclosure that maintains minimum 40°F

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rule: sprinkler system riser must have a check valve or backflow preventer installed immediately downstream of the main shutoff valve
conditions: system is connected to a potable water supply

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rule: sprinkler system riser must be provided with a drain valve at its lowest point
conditions: riser is part of a wet-pipe or dry-pipe system that can contain water

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rule: Sprinkler flow switch must be installed in a vertical orientation on the sprinkler riser or main
conditions: wet pipe sprinkler system
exceptions: manufacturer explicitly allows horizontal mounting

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rule: Sprinkler flow switch must not be installed downstream of a check valve that would prevent reverse flow detection
conditions: system uses a single flow switch for bidirectional flow detection
exceptions: multiple flow switches are provided for each flow direction

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rule: Sprinkler flow switch must be located at least 24 inches from any sprinkler head or branch line tee
conditions: wet pipe system

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rule: Sprinkler flow switch must not be installed where ambient temperature exceeds the device's rated temperature range
exceptions: device is specifically rated for the elevated temperature

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rule: Sprinkler tamper switch must be installed on the branch line valve of a fire sprinkler system
conditions: when the tamper switch is used to monitor a sprinkler water supply valve

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rule: Sprinkler tamper switch wiring must be supervised (Class 2) and connected to a fire alarm control panel
conditions: when the tamper switch is part of a fire sprinkler supervisory system
exceptions: wireless tamper switches that use supervised RF communication to the panel

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rule: Sprinkler tamper switch must not be bypassed or have its valve closed during a fire condition
conditions: when the building fire alarm system is in alarm or the sprinkler system is active

subject: Sprinkler Drain Valve
rule: sprinkler drain valve must be installed at the lowest point of the sprinkler system piping or at a location that allows complete drainage of the system
conditions: sprinkler system is located in a region subject to freezing temperatures
sprinkler system requires maintenance draining
exceptions: systems with listed anti-freeze solutions that remain liquid at expected minimum temperatures
dry-pipe systems where the drain valve is part of the dry-pipe valve trim

subject: Sprinkler Drain Valve
rule: sprinkler drain valve must not be installed in a location where its discharge will cause water damage or create a slipping hazard
conditions: valve is used for system testing or draining
exceptions: discharge is piped to an approved point of disposal

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rule: Sprinkler escutcheon must be concentrically aligned with the sprinkler head orifice
conditions: Escutcheon is mounted on ceiling or wall
Escutcheon surrounds a sprinkler head
exceptions: Adjustable escutcheons specifically designed for off-center mounting with listed clearance

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rule: Sprinkler escutcheon must not impede sprinkler head activation or spray pattern
conditions: Escutcheon is installed on a ceiling or wall-covering sprinkler head
exceptions: Escutcheons specifically listed as part of a concealed sprinkler assembly designed to drop or open upon activation

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rule: Sprinkler escutcheon must be secured to prevent falling from ceiling
conditions: Escutcheon is installed in an occupied space above finished ceiling

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rule: Sprinkler escutcheon must not exceed the maximum annular gap specified by the sprinkler manufacturer
conditions: Escutcheon is used with a recessed or concealed sprinkler

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rule: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports must be fabricated from ferrous materials or other approved materials that are compatible with the sprinkler system piping and resistant to corrosion in the intended service environment
conditions: When supporting metallic sprinkler piping
exceptions: Non-ferrous hangers listed specifically for sprinkler system use

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rule: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports must be capable of supporting five times the weight of the water-filled pipe plus 250 lb (113.6 kg) applied at the point of hanging
conditions: For all sprinkler piping installations

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rule: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports must not be attached directly to the sprinkler system piping by welding or drilling
conditions: When using standard malleable iron or steel hanger components
exceptions: Hangers specifically designed for welded attachment and listed as such

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rule: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports must be installed at maximum intervals as specified by pipe material and nominal diameter
conditions: For all sprinkler piping
exceptions: Where engineered calculations demonstrate equivalent support performance

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rule: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports must restrain the pipe against lateral movement at intervals not exceeding 30 ft (9.1 m)
conditions: For pipe sizes 1 inch (25 mm) and larger
In earthquake-prone areas or where seismic design is required

subject: Sprinkler Head Guard
rule: Sprinkler head guard must not obstruct the sprinkler's spray pattern
conditions: When installed over a sprinkler head

subject: Sprinkler Head Guard
rule: Sprinkler head guard must have openings or slots that allow free passage of sprinkler discharge
conditions: When installed over a sprinkler head

subject: Sprinkler Head Guard
rule: Sprinkler head guard must not be installed on sprinkler heads where prohibited by local fire code
conditions: Where local jurisdiction or fire code authority specifies restrictions
exceptions: When approved in writing by the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ)

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must be compatible with the building's occupancy classification

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must have a reliable water supply of adequate pressure and flow

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must not be designed such that its activation temperature conflicts with ambient environmental conditions
conditions: when the system uses thermally activated sprinkler heads

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must not use wet pipe configuration in areas subject to freezing temperatures
conditions: when ambient temperature can drop below 40°F (4°C)
exceptions: when the system is protected with antifreeze or listed freeze-protection methods per NFPA 13

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must be selected such that spacing and coverage area comply with the system's listing and design density requirements

subject: Fire Sprinkler System Type
rule: fire sprinkler system type must not obstruct or be obstructed by structural elements, ducts, or lighting to the point that spray pattern is compromised

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rule: Sprinkler system room must have a floor drain
conditions: Sprinkler system contains wet-pipe components
Room is located in a habitable or occupied building level
exceptions: Room is in a basement with an approved sump pump system that does not require gravity drainage

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rule: Sprinkler system room must not be used as storage for combustible materials
conditions: Room serves as the primary fire sprinkler riser/valve room
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified spare sprinkler heads and a sprinkler wrench stored in a dedicated cabinet

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rule: Sprinkler system room must have direct access from a corridor or exterior without passing through another room
conditions: Room contains fire protection valves, risers, or pumps serving multiple floors or zones

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rule: Sprinkler system room must have a minimum clearance of 36 inches in front of all valves and equipment
conditions: Room contains valves, pressure gauges, or alarm devices

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rule: Sprinkler system room must be maintained at a temperature above 40°F (4°C)
conditions: System is a wet-pipe sprinkler system
exceptions: Room is for a dry-pipe or pre-action system only

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Insulation
rule: Sprinkler pipe insulation must maintain a minimum temperature above freezing (40°F / 4°C) to prevent ice formation and pipe burst in wet-pipe sprinkler systems
conditions: Wet-pipe sprinkler system
Pipe located in area subject to freezing temperatures
exceptions: Dry-pipe or pre-action sprinkler systems where pipes are not normally water-filled

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Insulation
rule: Sprinkler pipe insulation must not obstruct sprinkler head spray patterns or heat collection
conditions: Insulation is installed on pipes near sprinkler heads
exceptions: Insulation is terminated at least 6-12 inches away from sprinkler heads per NFPA standards

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Insulation
rule: Sprinkler pipe insulation must be fire-rated or listed for use on fire protection systems
conditions: Insulation is applied to sprinkler system piping

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Insulation
rule: Sprinkler pipe insulation must not prevent pipe hangers and supports from maintaining the fire-resistance rating of the structure
conditions: Insulation wraps around or covers hanger attachments at rated penetrations
exceptions: Insulation material itself is part of a listed firestop system

subject: Gypsum Board Panels
rule: Gypsum board panels must not be installed in direct contact with concrete or masonry without a vapor barrier or moisture-protective coating
conditions: when gypsum board is used in basements, crawlspaces, or other locations where it may contact concrete or masonry
exceptions: when gypsum board is specifically rated/treated for direct concrete contact and the assembly is designed to manage moisture

subject: Gypsum Board Panels
rule: Gypsum board panels must be installed with manufacturer-specified fastener spacing and edge distance
conditions: when gypsum board is attached to framing members
exceptions: when an engineered alternative fastening pattern is approved by a design professional for the specific loading condition

subject: Gypsum Board Panels
rule: Gypsum board panels must not be installed in exterior exposed locations without proper weather-resistant cladding or covering
conditions: when gypsum board is used in exterior wall assemblies
exceptions: when the gypsum board product is specifically manufactured and rated for exterior exposure (e.g., exterior gypsum sheathing)

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rule: Metal stud framing must have properly sized and spaced lateral bracing (bridging/blocking) to prevent stud buckling under axial load
conditions: when studs are load-bearing
when stud height exceeds code-prescribed unbraced length limits
exceptions: non-structural partitions that carry no axial load and are not subject to lateral buckling requirements

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rule: Metal stud framing must not have a bearing wall stud slenderness ratio (kl/r) exceeding the code-prescribed maximum
conditions: when studs are in load-bearing walls

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rule: Metal studs must be attached to top and bottom tracks with fasteners of minimum specified type, size, and spacing
conditions: in all metal stud framing applications

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rule: Metal stud punch-outs (cripple studs) used above or below openings must not be left unattached — each end must be connected to a structural header or sill
conditions: when framing openings (doors, windows)

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rule: Metal stud track flanges must face the same direction as the stud web (not opposite) at framed openings
conditions: at door and window openings

subject: Drywall Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: drywall fasteners (screws/nails) must be corrosion-resistant when used in moisture-prone environments (e.g., bathrooms, basements, exterior-rated assemblies)
conditions: assembly is located in a wet or high-humidity area
fastener is exposed to periodic or continuous moisture
exceptions: temporary construction (non-permanent installation)
fastener is fully encapsulated in water-resistant barrier and never exposed to moisture during service life

subject: Drywall Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: drywall fasteners must not over-drive the fastener head below the paper face of the drywall
conditions: fastener is used for attaching gypsum board to framing

subject: Drywall Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
rule: drywall fasteners must be spaced at maximum 8 inches on center along edges and 12 inches on center in the field for ceiling installations
conditions: fastener is attaching gypsum board to ceiling framing
exceptions: engineered design specifying different spacing per structural calculation or fire-rating assembly

subject: Water-Resistant (Greenboard) Drywall
rule: Water-resistant (greenboard) drywall must not be used in areas subject to continuous or direct water exposure (e.g., shower interiors, soaking tub surrounds, outdoors)
conditions: Installation in wet areas
Application in showers, tub surrounds, or exterior walls
exceptions: May be used as a substrate in tile backer applications if additional waterproofing membrane is applied

subject: Water-Resistant (Greenboard) Drywall
rule: Water-resistant (greenboard) drywall must have all cut edges and fastener penetrations sealed with a moisture-resistant primer or coating before tiling or finishing
conditions: When installed in high-moisture areas such as bathrooms or kitchens
When used as backing for tile

subject: Water-Resistant (Greenboard) Drywall
rule: Water-resistant (greenboard) drywall must not be installed in unventilated enclosed spaces where relative humidity consistently exceeds 90%
conditions: Continuous occupancy or closed environment without HVAC dehumidification

subject: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall
rule: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall must have a minimum thickness of 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) to maintain its fire-resistance rating
conditions: When used in fire-resistance-rated assemblies
When used in assemblies requiring a fire-resistance rating per building code

subject: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall
rule: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall must contain glass fibers in its core to achieve its fire-resistive properties
conditions: When the assembly requires a UL or ASTM fire-resistance-rated designation

subject: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall
rule: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall must not be installed on both faces of a wall assembly without staggered joints meeting code requirements for fire-rated separation
conditions: When the assembly is used as a fire separation wall with a required fire-resistance rating
exceptions: When specifically tested and listed in an approved assembly design

subject: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall
rule: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall must be fastened with screws or nails at the spacing specified by the approved assembly design
conditions: When installed in fire-resistance-rated assemblies

subject: Mold-Resistant Drywall
rule: Mold-resistant drywall must not be used in continuously wet or submerged applications
conditions: Application involves standing water
Application involves continuous water immersion

subject: Mold-Resistant Drywall
rule: Mold-resistant drywall must be installed with a minimum 1/2-inch gap above finished floor level
conditions: Installation in areas subject to moisture exposure (bathrooms, basements, kitchens)

subject: Mold-Resistant Drywall
rule: Mold-resistant drywall must not be used as a direct substrate for ceramic tile in wet areas
conditions: Wet-area shower or tub surround application

subject: Exterior Gypsum Sheathing
rule: Exterior gypsum sheathing must not be used in exterior applications where it will be exposed to direct moisture or weather
conditions: Exterior gypsum sheathing is used as an exterior sheathing material
No vapor-permeable weather barrier is installed to protect it
exceptions: When fully protected by a continuous water-resistive barrier (WRB) and siding/cladding that prevents moisture ingress

subject: Exterior Gypsum Sheathing
rule: Exterior gypsum sheathing must be installed with a minimum 1/8-inch gap at all edges and ends
conditions: Used as exterior sheathing on framed walls

subject: Exterior Gypsum Sheathing
rule: Exterior gypsum sheathing must not be used as a structural diaphragm or shear wall without explicit engineering design
conditions: Used as the primary lateral load-resisting element
exceptions: When specifically designed and detailed for shear resistance with appropriate fasteners and blocking per engineering specification

subject: Exterior Gypsum Sheathing
rule: Exterior gypsum sheathing must be stored off the ground and protected from moisture before installation
conditions: Material is delivered to the job site prior to installation

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rule: Access panels and hatches must have a locking or latching mechanism to prevent unintended opening
conditions: when installed in accessible areas
when serving as roof access
exceptions: temporary access panels under constant supervision

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rule: Access panels and hatches must be weather-sealed when installed in exterior or weather-exposed locations
conditions: when installed on exterior walls
when installed on roofs
when installed in unenclosed spaces
exceptions: panels located entirely inside conditioned spaces with no exterior exposure

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rule: Access hatches used for roof egress must not be located directly above electrical equipment
conditions: when the hatch is intended for personnel access to the roof
exceptions: when protective shielding or drip pans are installed between the hatch and equipment

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rule: Access panel doors must open a minimum of 90 degrees or be removable to provide full access to the equipment behind them
conditions: when the panel provides access to mechanical, electrical, or plumbing equipment requiring maintenance
exceptions: panels serving only inspection/viewing windows where no service work is performed through the opening

subject: Insulated Sheathing
rule: Insulated sheathing must provide a continuous thermal barrier across the building envelope without gaps or compression
conditions: when used as part of a continuous insulation (ci) system
when installed on exterior walls or roofs
exceptions: when intentionally detailed for structural bridge elements such as clip or z-girt attachments

subject: Insulated Sheathing
rule: Insulated sheathing must not be load-bearing for vertical structural loads from floors or roof above
conditions: when used as continuous insulation over structural framing
exceptions: when specifically rated and designed as structural insulated sheathing (e.g., OSB-based insulation panels with structural capacity)

subject: Insulated Sheathing
rule: Insulated sheathing must maintain a vapor permeability appropriate for the climate zone and wall assembly to prevent moisture trapping
conditions: when installed on the exterior side of a wall assembly
exceptions: when the assembly is designed as a vapor-permeable or vented drainage system

subject: Insulated Metal Panel
rule: Insulated metal panels must have their joints properly sealed and lapped to prevent water infiltration
conditions: when used as exterior wall or roof cladding

subject: Insulated Metal Panel
rule: Insulated metal panels must not be subjected to temperatures exceeding their foam core's fire rating or service temperature limit
conditions: in fire-rated assemblies or near heat sources
exceptions: panels specifically rated for higher temperature exposure (e.g., mineral-wool core panels)

subject: Insulated Metal Panel
rule: Insulated metal panels must include thermal break materials at all through-fastener penetrations
conditions: when installed in conditioned building enclosures

subject: Insulated Metal Panel
rule: Insulated metal panels must be installed with appropriate gravity load paths that transfer panel weight to the building structure, not relying on panel-to-panel connections alone
conditions: in vertical (wall) applications

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rule: insulation fastening and accessories must be compatible with the substrate material and insulation type
conditions: when fastening insulation to any building surface
exceptions: adhesive-based systems that do not rely on mechanical fasteners

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rule: mechanical fasteners for insulation must not create a thermal bridge that compromises the insulation R-value
conditions: when using thermally conductive metal fasteners through the insulation layer
exceptions: fasteners that incorporate thermal break washers or caps
systems where the fastener penetration is accounted for in the overall thermal design

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rule: insulation fasteners must be rated for the wind uplift or lateral loads applicable to the building envelope location
conditions: when installed in exterior walls or roofs exposed to wind forces
exceptions: interior insulation applications not subject to wind loading

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rule: insulation fastening and accessories must not damage the vapor retarder or air barrier membrane during installation
conditions: when fastening through or adjacent to vapor retarder or air barrier layers
exceptions: systems specifically designed to integrate fastening with barrier penetration seals

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rule: Insulation vapor retarder / air barrier must be installed on the warm side of the building envelope (interior side in cold climates, exterior side in hot-humid climates) relative to the insulation
conditions: Building is in a climate with significant heating or cooling seasons
exceptions: When used in a vented roof assembly where code allows placement as part of a designed drying strategy

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rule: Vapor retarder / air barrier must not have two layers of impermeable material with no drying path between them (i.e., must not create a double-vapor-retarder assembly that traps moisture)
conditions: Multiple vapor-retarding layers are present in the same assembly
exceptions: When engineered design explicitly models and manages moisture accumulation (e.g., fully adhered roofing systems with documented drying capacity)

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rule: Vapor retarder / air barrier must be continuous and sealed at all penetrations, laps, and transitions

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rule: Vapor retarder permeability must be compatible with the assembly's drying potential (i.e., must not be Class I (impermeable) on both sides of cavity insulation)
conditions: Cavity insulation is present between two sheathing layers
exceptions: In assemblies specifically designed as 'perfect barriers' with controlled interior humidity (e.g., some cold-climate commercial roofs with verified vapor pressure analysis)

subject: Exterior Insulation and Finish System (EIFS)
rule: EIFS must include a drained or pressure-equalized cavity behind the insulation board to allow moisture that penetrates the cladding to exit
conditions: when used as exterior cladding on walls
exceptions: when installed over a continuous fully-adhered water-resistive barrier with no penetrations and the system is designed as a barrier-type EIFS in a climate zone with very low rainfall

subject: Exterior Insulation and Finish System (EIFS)
rule: EIFS must not have rigid foam insulation boards installed without proper gaps or without compatible sealants at joints and terminations
conditions: when the system includes continuous foam insulation board layers
exceptions: factory-assembled panels where joint movement is accommodated by panel-to-panel connections

subject: Exterior Insulation and Finish System (EIFS)
rule: EIFS must terminate at least 6 inches above finished grade and at least 2 inches above roof/deck surfaces
conditions: when installed at the base of exterior walls

subject: Cementitious Screed
rule: Cementitious screed must have a minimum thickness of 25 mm when bonded to a concrete substrate
conditions: When bonded to a concrete substrate
exceptions: When used as a floating screed over insulation, minimum thickness is typically 40-50 mm depending on specification

subject: Cementitious Screed
rule: Cementitious screed must be allowed to cure for a minimum of 7 days before receiving floor finishes
conditions: When subsequent floor finishes (tiles, timber, vinyl) are to be applied
exceptions: Rapid-dry screed formulations may have reduced curing periods per manufacturer specification

subject: Cementitious Screed
rule: Cementitious screed must not be used where it will be exposed to continuous freeze-thaw cycles
conditions: In external or unheated environments subject to freezing temperatures and moisture
exceptions: When the screed is formulated with air-entrainment and appropriate waterproofing additives specifically designed for freeze-thaw resistance

subject: Cementitious Screed
rule: Cementitious screed must be applied over a suitable primer or bonding agent when applied to a non-absorbent substrate
conditions: When applied to a non-absorbent substrate such as existing tiles, power-floated concrete, or steel

subject: Cementitious Screed
rule: Cementitious screed must have movement joints installed at maximum 4.5 m intervals in both directions
conditions: For screed areas larger than 4.5 m in any direction, or when incorporating underfloor heating
exceptions: When the screed is a fibre-reinforced 'uncracked' system specifically designed to allow longer spans per manufacturer specification

subject: Floating Screed
rule: Floating screed must be laid over a continuous, resilient isolation layer (e.g., acoustic underlay) to prevent rigid contact with the substrate or structural slab
conditions: When used for acoustic insulation
When laid over a concrete or timber structural substrate
exceptions: If the screed is bonded directly to the substrate as a bonded screed (not a floating screed)

subject: Floating Screed
rule: Floating screed must be separated from all vertical elements (walls, columns, partitions) by a perimeter expansion joint or edge strip
conditions: Where perimeter walls or columns exist

subject: Floating Screed
rule: Floating screed must have a minimum thickness as specified by the manufacturer or relevant standard (typically ≥ 50 mm for sand/cement screed)
conditions: For cementitious or anhydrite floating screeds
exceptions: Proprietary thin floating screed systems with documented performance may have lower minimum thickness

subject: Floating Screed
rule: Floating screed must not bridge across structural movement joints in the substrate
conditions: Where structural movement joints exist in the supporting slab or deck

subject: Unbonded Screed
rule: Unbonded screed must be installed over a suitable separating layer (e.g., slip membrane or bonded underlayment) to prevent bonding to the substrate
conditions: When installed over a concrete or existing substrate
exceptions: When the screed is intentionally designed as a bonded screed through mechanical or chemical keying

subject: Unbonded Screed
rule: Unbonded screed must incorporate movement joints (e.g., expansion joints) at perimeters and at regular intervals
conditions: For any unbonded screed area exceeding 40 m² or with side lengths over 6 m
exceptions: Very small areas where thermal/acoustic movement is negligible

subject: Unbonded Screed
rule: Unbonded screed minimum thickness must not be less than 65 mm for floor-finish applications
conditions: When used as a floating floor screed over a separating layer and insulation
exceptions: Proprietary thin-layer unbonded screeds with specific manufacturer approval

subject: Unbonded Screed
rule: Unbonded screed must not be subjected to point loads exceeding its design compressive strength before achieving full cure
conditions: During the first 7 days after installation

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rule: Heated floor screed must have a minimum thickness to fully encase heating pipes/cables
conditions: heating elements are embedded within the screed

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rule: Heated floor screed must not contain air voids or delamination in the zone surrounding heating pipes/cables
conditions: screed is in service and subjected to thermal cycling

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rule: Heated floor screed must be compatible with the coefficient of thermal expansion of the embedded heating elements
conditions: screed will experience temperature changes during operation

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rule: Heated floor screed must not be installed over construction joints that are expected to move
conditions: screed is continuous across a structural movement joint

subject: Fast-Drying Screed
rule: Fast-Drying Screed must be applied at a minimum thickness specified by the manufacturer
conditions: Screed is used as a floor finish or base for floor coverings

subject: Fast-Drying Screed
rule: Fast-Drying Screed must not be applied over substrates with moisture content exceeding the screed manufacturer's limit
conditions: Screed is applied onto a concrete or cementitious substrate

subject: Fast-Drying Screed
rule: Fast-Drying Screed must be protected from rapid water loss (e.g., wind, direct sun, high temperature) during the initial setting period
conditions: Application environment is exposed to external conditions or forced air movement

subject: Polymer-Modified Screed
rule: Polymer-modified screed must be applied over a sound, clean, and properly prepared substrate
conditions: When used as a floor or roof screed
exceptions: Manufacturer-approved self-priming systems that chemically bond to unsound substrates

subject: Polymer-Modified Screed
rule: Polymer-modified screed must be allowed to cure for the minimum time specified by the manufacturer before trafficking or applying subsequent layers
conditions: After installation
exceptions: Rapid-cure formulations explicitly rated for early trafficking per manufacturer data

subject: Polymer-Modified Screed
rule: Polymer-modified screed must not be applied when ambient or substrate temperature is below the manufacturer's minimum (typically 5°C) or expected to fall below that within 24 hours
conditions: During installation and initial cure period
exceptions: Systems specifically formulated and certified for low-temperature application

subject: Polymer-Modified Screed
rule: Polymer-modified screed thickness must not fall below the manufacturer's stated minimum (typically 10–15 mm for bonded systems)
conditions: When bonded directly to substrate
exceptions: Self-levelling polymer screeds with documented thin-film approval from manufacturer

subject: Self-Levelling Underlayment
rule: self-levelling underlayment must be applied over a structurally sound, clean, and properly prepared substrate
conditions: substrate is existing concrete
substrate is plywood or timber

subject: Self-Levelling Underlayment
rule: self-levelling underlayment must not be applied over a damp or moisture-emitting substrate without an appropriate moisture vapour barrier
conditions: substrate is concrete on or below grade
exceptions: concrete with verified low moisture emission (per ASTM F2170 or equivalent)

subject: Self-Levelling Underlayment
rule: self-levelling underlayment must be poured at a minimum thickness specified by the manufacturer for the intended application
exceptions: product specifically certified for feathered-edge (zero-thickness) applications

subject: Self-Levelling Underlayment
rule: self-levelling underlayment must not be applied over a substrate temperature below the manufacturer's minimum
conditions: cold-weather installation conditions

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rule: Screed reinforcement mesh must be fully embedded within the screed layer
conditions: When used in a cementitious screed application

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rule: Screed reinforcement mesh must not be placed directly on the substrate or insulation without adequate spacing/nest supports
conditions: When used in a bonded or unbonded screed over insulation or a substrate

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rule: Screed reinforcement mesh joints/laps must overlap by at least one full mesh spacing
conditions: When multiple sheets of mesh are used in the same screed pour

subject: Liquid Waterproof Membrane Under Screed
rule: Liquid waterproof membrane under screed must be fully continuous and unbroken across the entire substrate surface
conditions: when installed beneath a bonded screed layer
in any wet area or continuously wet environment
exceptions: where a dedicated drainage layer is integrated between membrane and screed

subject: Liquid Waterproof Membrane Under Screed
rule: Liquid waterproof membrane under screed must not be applied over a contaminated or unprimed substrate
conditions: when the substrate is concrete, cementitious screed, or existing ceramic tile
exceptions: where the membrane manufacturer explicitly certifies direct application to the specific uncleaned substrate type

subject: Liquid Waterproof Membrane Under Screed
rule: Liquid waterproof membrane under screed must be fully cured before screed placement
conditions: in all installations
exceptions: where the membrane system is specifically formulated for 'green' or uncured overlay application and certified by the manufacturer

subject: Air Barrier
rule: Air barrier must be continuous across all building envelope joints, seams, and penetrations
conditions: Building has a conditioned interior space
Building envelope separates conditioned from unconditioned space
exceptions: Buildings with no conditioned spaces

subject: Air Barrier
rule: Air barrier must be rigidly attached or supported to resist design wind loads without tearing, detachment, or excessive deflection
conditions: Building is exposed to wind loads
exceptions: Temporary structures not subject to wind design requirements

subject: Air Barrier
rule: Air barrier must not have holes, gaps, or tears larger than the allowable leakage rate specified by code or design standard
conditions: Air barrier is required by applicable building code or performance specification
exceptions: Intentional ventilation openings designed with controlled airflow (e.g., intentional openings with dampers)

subject: Roof Deck
rule: roof deck must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: roof deck is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: roof deck is an indoor/covered space not exposed to rain or snow

subject: Roof Deck
rule: roof deck must be designed for the design live load specified by building code for occupiable roof surfaces
conditions: roof deck is accessible/occupiable
exceptions: roof deck is designated as non-occupiable and clearly marked as such with restricted access

subject: Roof Deck
rule: roof deck must not have unprotected fall hazards at the perimeter
conditions: roof deck is accessible to people and elevated above grade
exceptions: roof deck is at grade level with no fall distance

subject: Roof Deck
rule: roof deck must have a waterproof membrane system
conditions: roof deck is exposed to weather and has occupied space below
exceptions: roof deck is over an unoccupied space such as an open carport or has a drained rain-screen assembly that achieves equivalent water shedding

subject: Roof Membrane
rule: roof membrane must be installed in a continuous plane without gaps at seams
conditions: membrane is single-ply or built-up roofing
roof is low-slope or flat
exceptions: intentional gaps for expansion or drainage are designed with flashing details

subject: Roof Membrane
rule: roof membrane must not be installed upside down (wrong orientation of plies or layers)
conditions: membrane is an asphalt-based built-up roof or modified bitumen sheet with a factory-applied granular surface

subject: Roof Membrane
rule: roof membrane must have a continuous drainage path to prevent ponding water
conditions: roof slope is less than 1/4 inch per foot
exceptions: roof is designed as a 'green roof' or 'blue roof' with intentional detained water storage

subject: Roof Covering / Ballast
rule: Roof ballast must have a minimum weight per unit area sufficient to resist design wind uplift pressures
conditions: Ballasted roof assembly on low-slope roof
Wind speed zone requiring uplift resistance
exceptions: Mechanically attached or adhered roof systems

subject: Roof Covering / Ballast
rule: Roof ballast must consist of clean, hard, durable particles free of fines and organic material
conditions: Stone ballast for membrane protection
exceptions: Engineered paver systems with factory-controlled composition

subject: Roof Covering / Ballast
rule: Ballast aggregate must not be large enough to puncture or damage the roof membrane
conditions: Loose stone ballast applied over single-ply membrane
Aggregate ballast size not controlled by manufacturer specification
exceptions: Protection mats or fabric layers installed between ballast and membrane

subject: Roof Covering / Ballast
rule: Ballast must be uniformly distributed across the roof surface to maintain design weight distribution
conditions: Any ballasted roof assembly
exceptions: Non-ballasted roof systems

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rule: roof edge flashing/trim must be lapped in the direction of water flow (i.e., with the higher piece overlapping the lower piece)
conditions: flashing/trim is installed on a sloped roof
flashing/trim consists of multiple overlapping sections
exceptions: single-piece continuous flashing/trim with no joints

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rule: roof edge flashing/trim must extend at least 25 mm (1 in.) above the finished roofing surface (or above the anticipated standing water/ice dam height) at the vertical leg
conditions: edge flashing/trim has a vertical back leg that terminates against a wall or parapet
exceptions: flashing/trim designed with a fully sealed curb or with a dedicated membrane upturn that replaces the vertical leg function

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rule: roof edge flashing/trim must not be installed with fasteners placed closer than 3 mm from the free edge of the metal
conditions: flashing/trim is metal (steel, aluminum, copper, etc.)
fasteners are exposed (not hidden behind a seam or cleat)
exceptions: fasteners are factory-set into a hemmed edge with the parent material thickness already accounted for in the edge distance

subject: Penetration Flashing
rule: Penetration flashing must be lapped under the roofing membrane above and over the membrane below (shingle-fashion) to ensure continuous water shedding
conditions: When used on sloped roofs with overlapping membrane layers
exceptions: Single-ply membrane systems with factory-fabricated flashing boots designed for monolithic integration

subject: Penetration Flashing
rule: Penetration flashing must create a watertight seal at the penetration-to-roof interface
conditions: All applications
exceptions: Non-weather-exposed interior penetrations (e.g., within a conditioned attic space with secondary drainage)

subject: Penetration Flashing
rule: Penetration flashing must not be installed without a backer rod or structural support that prevents the flashing from sagging or deforming under thermal or load cycles
conditions: When used as a flexible flashing (e.g., lead, rubber, or peel-and-stick membrane)
exceptions: Rigid metal counter-flashings directly fastened to a solid substrate that provides continuous support

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rule: Expansion joint assembly must allow for free thermal movement of adjacent building elements without causing stress or damage to the structure
conditions: When installed between two building sections or structural elements
exceptions: When the joint is a cosmetic/sealant-only joint not tied to structural expansion

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rule: Expansion joint assembly must be located coincident with a structural separation line (full separation of the building structure)
conditions: For structural expansion joints that accommodate building-wide movement

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rule: Expansion joint assembly must not be bridged by rigid structural elements (beams, slabs, or columns) that would prevent relative movement
conditions: Where the joint is intended to accommodate differential movement between building sections
exceptions: When a designed mechanical connection or shear key is engineered to allow controlled movement while transferring lateral loads

subject: Roof Curb
rule: roof curb must be water-sealed at all perimeter seams and joints
conditions: curb is exposed to weather
curb supports roofing membrane
exceptions: curb is purely decorative interior element not exposed to weather

subject: Roof Curb
rule: roof curb must have structural capacity to support the equipment or component mounted on it
conditions: curb supports HVAC equipment, skylight, or other rooftop component
exceptions: curb is a non-structural aesthetic cap only

subject: Roof Curb
rule: roof curb must be positively fastened to the roof structural deck
conditions: curb is located on structural roof

subject: Roof Curb
rule: roof curb must not create a ponding condition on the roof surface
conditions: curb is installed on a low-slope or flat roof
exceptions: curb is on a steep-slope roof where ponding cannot occur

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rule: roof walkway pads must be load-rated for anticipated service loads (live load + dead load)
conditions: when walkway is accessible to maintenance personnel
when walkway provides access to roof-mounted equipment
exceptions: temporary walkway pads used during construction only (if rated for worker loads)

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rule: roof walkway pads must not be placed directly over incompatible roofing membranes that could be damaged by the pad material
conditions: when pad material is not chemically compatible with the underlying roof membrane
when pad has sharp edges or abrasive underside
exceptions: when a protective separation layer (slip sheet, geotextile) is installed between pad and membrane

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rule: roof walkway pads must be secured or weighted to resist wind uplift forces
conditions: when installed on a building in a wind zone with design wind speed exceeding 100 mph
when walkway is on a roof edge or corner zone where uplift pressures are highest
exceptions: where walkway is ballasted with gravel or pavers of sufficient weight per manufacturer's wind uplift rating
when walkway is mechanically fastened through to the roof deck

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rule: roof walkway pads must provide a slip-resistant walking surface with a coefficient of friction meeting code minimums
conditions: when walkway is on a sloped roof surface
when walkway is exposed to rain, ice, or condensation
exceptions: when walkway is in a climate-controlled interior rooftop space not exposed to moisture

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rule: roof walkway pads must not create a trip hazard at transitions between pad sections or between pad and adjacent roof surface
conditions: when pad sections are butted end-to-end or side-to-side
exceptions: where a tapered transition ramp is provided at height discontinuities

subject: Green Roof Assembly
rule: green roof assembly must have a waterproof membrane layer
conditions: any green roof system

subject: Green Roof Assembly
rule: green roof assembly must maintain a minimum roof slope for drainage
conditions: extensive or intensive green roof
exceptions: roofs specifically designed with active drainage systems or detention layers that manage water on a flat deck

subject: Green Roof Assembly
rule: green roof assembly must have a root barrier layer between substrate and waterproofing
conditions: roof with vegetative growth medium directly above the waterproof membrane

subject: Green Roof Assembly
rule: green roof assembly must not have soil depth exceeding structural load capacity
conditions: any green roof

subject: Green Roof Assembly
rule: green roof assembly must have a drainage layer that conveys water to roof outlets
conditions: green roof over occupied space

subject: Roof Hatch
rule: roof hatch must have a positive locking mechanism to prevent accidental opening
conditions: hatch is accessible to building occupants
hatch is located on occupied roof
exceptions: hatch is only accessible via locked ladder with separate access control

subject: Roof Hatch
rule: roof hatch must be weather-sealed when closed to prevent water intrusion
conditions: hatch is exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: hatch is located in a conditioned interior space only

subject: Roof Hatch
rule: roof hatch must not be located within the required clear zone of a fire escape or egress path
conditions: building has a fire escape or designated egress path on the roof

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rule: skylight/roof window assembly must maintain a watertight seal against roof penetration
conditions: when installed as a penetration through the roof membrane
when exposed to precipitation
exceptions: non-penetrating tubular skylight systems that use curbs above the roof plane

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rule: skylight/roof window must be sloped or flashings must provide positive drainage away from the opening
conditions: when installed on a roof with slope less than the skylight manufacturer's minimum recommended pitch
exceptions: skylights designed and listed for flat-roof installation with built-in upturned curbs and positive drainage flashing systems

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rule: skylight/roof window must not be installed in a roof location that creates a snow dam or ice dam collection area above the unit
conditions: in climate zones with sustained freezing temperatures and snow accumulation
exceptions: when a dedicated ice-and-water shield membrane is installed extending at least 24 inches upslope and the skylight is designed for snow-load conditions

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rule: skylight must have a condensation management system (thermal break, drip gutter, or insulated frame) when installed in humid interior environments
conditions: when interior relative humidity regularly exceeds 60%
when installed in bathrooms, indoor pools, or commercial kitchens
exceptions: skylights with warm-edge spacers and low-U-value glazing that keep interior surface temperature above dew point

subject: Photovoltaic Roof Integration
rule: photovoltaic panels must not create shaded zones on other panels within the same array
conditions: roof-mounted PV array with multiple panels in same row or plane
exceptions: systems specifically designed for partial shading tolerance with bypass diodes and module-level power electronics that maintain operability

subject: Photovoltaic Roof Integration
rule: photovoltaic panels must maintain a minimum clearance above the roof surface for airflow cooling
conditions: building-integrated or rack-mounted photovoltaic roof system
exceptions: building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) modules designed as direct roof replacement materials that are certified for elevated temperature operation

subject: Photovoltaic Roof Integration
rule: roof structure must support the additional dead load of photovoltaic panels, mounting system, and ballast or attachment hardware
conditions: retrofitting PV on existing roof
exceptions: new construction where roof was designed from the outset to accommodate PV loading

subject: Photovoltaic Roof Integration
rule: photovoltaic roof penetrations must be flashed and sealed to prevent water ingress
conditions: roof-mounted PV requiring attachment penetrations through the roof membrane
exceptions: non-penetrating ballasted mounting systems that meet wind uplift requirements without roof penetrations

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rule: window frame must accommodate the thickness of the glazing unit within its rebate
conditions: when designed to hold glass or infill panels
exceptions: decorative or non-operable dummy frames with no glazing intended

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rule: window frame must be dimensionally compatible with the rough opening (allowance for shimming and sealing)
conditions: when installed into a building wall opening
exceptions: factory-glazed curtain wall units where frame and opening are fabricated as matched sets

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rule: window frame must not have unsealed joints between frame members when intended to be weathertight
conditions: when the frame is part of an exterior building envelope
exceptions: internal (non-weather-exposed) partitions where air and water sealing is not required

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rule: window frame must be self-supporting or adequately braced against wind loads
conditions: when installed in a vertical exterior wall

subject: Window Sealant / Caulking
rule: Window sealant/caulking must be compatible with the materials it contacts (e.g., window frame, glass, and adjacent wall cladding)
conditions: When applied at interfaces between dissimilar materials
exceptions: Manufacturer-tested compatibility charts confirm full adhesion and no chemical reaction

subject: Window Sealant / Caulking
rule: Window sealant/caulking must be applied within its specified temperature and humidity range
conditions: During installation
exceptions: Use of manufacturer-approved primer or surface conditioning extends acceptable range

subject: Window Sealant / Caulking
rule: Window sealant/caulking must not be applied over a wet or contaminated surface
conditions: At the time of installation

subject: Window Sealant / Caulking
rule: Window sealant/caulking joint depth-to-width ratio must not exceed manufacturer's specified maximum
conditions: When sealing gaps wider than the minimum recommended
exceptions: Use of closed-cell backer rod reduces required sealant depth

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing must be securely fixed to the frame or surrounding structure to prevent falling out
conditions: applicable to all glazed window openings
exceptions: temporary openings during construction or maintenance

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing must resist the design wind load specified for the building's location without breaking or becoming dislodged
conditions: when the window is part of the building envelope exposed to exterior wind pressures
exceptions: interior glazing not exposed to exterior wind loads

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing must not have sharp exposed edges within reachable area of building occupants
conditions: where edges are accessible to occupants (below 2m height or where people can come into contact)
exceptions: edges that are fully guarded by protective capping or framing

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing in doors, side panels, and low-level windows must be safety-glazed (toughened or laminated) to resist impact
conditions: glazing below 800mm from floor level
glazing in doors (including side panels within 300mm of door edge)
glazing within 300mm of a door opening edge
exceptions: glazing where a fixed permanent barrier protects the glass from impact

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing must not allow water ingress between the glass and frame under standard weather exposure
conditions: exterior windows and glazed openings in exterior walls
exceptions: deliberate weep-hole drainage provision that manages water egress

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: window glazing must be of a thickness and construction that prevents falling through under occupant load
conditions: glazing that forms part of a floor, roof, balcony, ramp, or stair guard
exceptions: glazing where a secondary barrier (guardrail) fully prevents occupant loading on the glass

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rule: door casing / architrave must maintain a minimum clearance from the door opening to allow the door to swing freely without binding
conditions: door is hinged and swings through the opening
exceptions: sliding or pocket doors where casing is not adjacent to the swing path

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rule: door casing / architrave must be securely fastened to the wall framing
conditions: casing is installed as a finished trim component

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rule: door casing / architrave must not obstruct the latch or strike plate area
conditions: casing is installed around a door that has a latching mechanism

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rule: Door leaf / door slab must have a thickness that fits within the door frame rebate and gap allowances
conditions: Door is hinged or pivoted
Frame is pre-installed
exceptions: Sliding door leaves where the slab is not contained within a rebated frame

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rule: Door leaf / door slab must not warp or twist beyond the plane tolerance that prevents latching
conditions: Door is side-hinged with a latch or lock
exceptions: Doors held only by friction or gravity (e.g., some pivot doors without latches)

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rule: Door leaf / door slab must have a maximum weight within the hinge or track load rating
conditions: Hinges or sliding hardware are specified
exceptions: Doors that are frameless or pivot on floor springs where load is transferred directly to floor

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rule: Door leaf / door slab must have a free edge (non-hinge edge) that does not obstruct the frame or adjacent wall during its swing arc
conditions: Door swings through an arc
Adjacent wall, frame, or obstruction exists within the swing path
exceptions: Pocket doors or sliding doors with no swing arc

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rule: Door leaf / door slab made of glass must be safety-glazed (tempered or laminated) if within a hazardous location
conditions: Door leaf contains glass panel
Door is within a hazardous location per building code (e.g., near floor level, adjacent to bath/shower, in a door opening)
exceptions: Glass panels more than 1.5 m above finished floor where breakage risk is mitigated

subject: Weatherstripping (Door)
rule: weatherstripping must form a continuous seal around the door perimeter when the door is closed
conditions: door is in closed position

subject: Weatherstripping (Door)
rule: weatherstripping must be compressible enough to allow door to close fully without excessive force

subject: Weatherstripping (Door)
rule: weatherstripping must not be installed in a location that prevents the door from swinging or sliding through its intended arc of travel

subject: Weatherstripping (Door)
rule: weatherstripping material must be compatible with the door and frame contact surfaces to avoid chemical degradation that compromises the seal

subject: Door Sealant / Caulking
rule: Door sealant/caulking must be applied to fill gaps between the door frame and the rough opening to prevent air and water infiltration
conditions: The door is an exterior door
The door is installed in a wall assembly exposed to weather
exceptions: The gap is designed to be left intentionally open for drainage (e.g., bottom weep gap on some door systems)

subject: Door Sealant / Caulking
rule: Door sealant/caulking must be compatible with both the door frame material and the adjacent wall material to avoid chemical reaction or bond failure
conditions: The door assembly uses materials that can chemically react (e.g., certain plastics, metals, or factory finishes)

subject: Door Sealant / Caulking
rule: Door sealant/caulking must not bridge across intended movement joints or expansion gaps in the door assembly
conditions: The door system is designed with control joints, expansion joints, or other intentional movement gaps
exceptions: The sealant is specifically formulated as a movement-capable sealant (e.g., silicone or polyurethane designed for dynamic joints) and is detailed to accommodate the expected movement range

subject: Window Assembly
rule: window assembly must be weather-sealed against air and water infiltration at all perimeter joints
conditions: window is installed in an exterior wall
window assembly includes frame and operable or fixed glazing
exceptions: temporary construction openings

subject: Window Assembly
rule: window assembly must have a condensation-resistant thermal break or insulated frame when installed in conditioned spaces in cold climates
conditions: window assembly is installed in a conditioned building envelope
climate zone experiences below-freezing temperatures

subject: Window Assembly
rule: window assembly must not allow sashes or panels to dislodge from their tracks or hinges under normal operating conditions
conditions: window is operable type (sliding, casement, awning, hung, etc.)

subject: Window Assembly
rule: window assembly must have a means of emergency egress or rescue in sleeping rooms
conditions: window serves a sleeping room as defined by building code
room has no other approved means of egress
exceptions: sprinklered buildings where code allows alternatives

subject: Door Assembly
rule: a door assembly must have a functioning latching or locking mechanism to remain closed under expected loads
conditions: door assembly is intended to be closed and secured
exceptions: decorative door assemblies that are never meant to be closed
fixed door assemblies (non-operable panels)

subject: Door Assembly
rule: a door assembly must not have hinge or pivot failures that allow the door to detach from the frame under normal operation
conditions: door is operable (swings or slides)

subject: Door Assembly
rule: a door assembly must have a means of egress (openable from the inside without special knowledge or tools) when serving as an exit in an occupied space
conditions: door assembly is located on a means of egress path
building is occupied by people
exceptions: security doors in high-security facilities where egress is intentionally restricted (e.g., prison cells)

subject: Door Assembly
rule: a door assembly must have a fire-resistance rating appropriate to its location when installed in a fire-rated wall assembly
conditions: door assembly is installed in a fire-rated wall or partition

subject: Door Assembly
rule: a door assembly must not have a bottom gap or perimeter clearance that exceeds the allowable limit for its intended use (e.g., smoke seal, acoustic seal, pest barrier)
conditions: door assembly is intended to provide a seal (smoke, acoustic, air, or pest)
exceptions: doors where intentional ventilation gap is part of the design (e.g., mechanical room louvers)

subject: Window Screen
rule: window screen mesh openings must be smaller than the smallest expected insect or pest to exclude them
conditions: when used as an insect barrier
exceptions: when used only for solar control or light diffusion with no pest exclusion requirement

subject: Window Screen
rule: window screen must allow adequate airflow for natural ventilation under expected wind pressures
conditions: when natural ventilation is required
exceptions: when building uses only mechanical ventilation and screen serves only solar/light purposes

subject: Window Screen
rule: window screen frame must not obstruct the emergency egress opening of the window
conditions: when window is designated as an emergency escape and rescue opening
exceptions: when screen is designed with a quick-release mechanism that meets egress code requirements

subject: Window Screen
rule: window screen material must not corrode or degrade when exposed to expected environmental conditions (rain, UV, humidity)
conditions: when installed in exterior applications
exceptions: when screen is designed as a temporary or seasonal installation with planned replacement

subject: Window Screen
rule: window screen must be securely attached to the window frame to prevent dislodgement under design wind loads
conditions: when installed in locations subject to wind
exceptions: when screen is intentionally removable and stored during high-wind events

subject: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must not be cut, drilled, or edge-worked after heat treatment
conditions: glass has been fully tempered
exceptions: CNC waterjet cutting is possible but extremely limited and risky

subject: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass used as safety glazing must be fully tempered (not heat-strengthened) when installed in hazardous locations
conditions: glass is used in doors
glass is used in sidelites adjacent to doors
glass is used in shower enclosures
glass is used in balustrades
glass is used in areas within 18 inches of floor
exceptions: laminated glass meeting safety glazing ratings may substitute
wired glass in fire-rated assemblies where code permits

subject: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass edges must be seamed or polished before tempering

subject: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must not be used in applications where it will be exposed to nickel sulfide inclusions at elevated temperatures exceeding 200°C
conditions: glass is continuously exposed to temperatures above 200°C
exceptions: heat-soak tested glass (e.g., EN 14179) significantly reduces risk but does not eliminate it

subject: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
rule: tempered glass must not be re-annealed or re-tempered

subject: Window Flashing
rule: Window flashing must be integrated with the building's weather-resistive barrier (WRB) or drainage plane to prevent water intrusion behind the cladding
conditions: when window is installed in an exterior wall assembly
exceptions: windows in fully interior, non-weather-exposed partitions

subject: Window Flashing
rule: Window flashing must not be installed with reverse lap (i.e., head flashing must lap over side flashing, side flashing over sill flashing, and sill flashing must extend beyond the cladding face)
conditions: for all stacked or sequenced flashing components on a window

subject: Window Flashing
rule: Window sill pan flashing must have positive slope (minimum 5 degrees) away from the window frame toward the exterior
conditions: for any operable or fixed window in a vertical wall

subject: Window Flashing
rule: Window flashing must not rely solely on sealant/adhesive for water-tightness at terminations and end dams
conditions: at all end dams, corners, and splice joints of continuous flashing

subject: Door Flashing
rule: door flashing must create a continuous seal around the door opening to prevent water intrusion
conditions: door flashing is installed as part of a door assembly exposed to weather
exceptions: interior doors not exposed to exterior moisture

subject: Door Flashing
rule: door flashing must slope away from the door opening
conditions: door flashing is installed at the head (top) of the door

subject: Door Flashing
rule: door flashing must not terminate inside the wall cavity
conditions: sill or head flashing is integrated into the wall assembly

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rule: Vision panel / door lite must be glazed with a safety-rated material (tempered, laminated, or wired glass) where the panel is within a door or within 18 inches of the floor
conditions: Vision panel is installed in a door
Panel bottom is within 18 inches of finished floor
exceptions: Panel is fully above 18 inches from floor and not part of a door assembly

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rule: Vision panel / door lite must have a maximum size limited by the fire rating of the door assembly when used in a fire-rated opening
conditions: Door assembly has a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Vision panel is listed as part of a UL-classified fire door assembly with tested glazing

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rule: Vision panel / door lite must not reduce the door stile/rail width below the minimum required for structural integrity and hardware mounting
exceptions: Panel is factory-engineered as part of a complete door assembly with tested structural performance

subject: Sliding Door Track & Hardware
rule: Sliding door track must be mounted level to within specified tolerance
conditions: Track is installed horizontally

subject: Sliding Door Track & Hardware
rule: Sliding door track must be rated to support the full weight of the door panels

subject: Sliding Door Track & Hardware
rule: Sliding door hardware must include a positive stop or restraint to prevent the door from derailing at end of travel

subject: Sliding Door Track & Hardware
rule: Sliding door track must not have sharp burrs or edges at the rolling surface

subject: Folding Door System
rule: folding door system must have a clear egress path width that meets local building code minimum when fully open
conditions: when used as a means of egress
in buildings subject to occupancy permits
exceptions: when the door is not part of a required means of egress path

subject: Folding Door System
rule: folding door system must not obstruct required clear floor space when in the open or partially open position
conditions: at points of entry or exit
in areas requiring unobstructed maneuvering clearance per accessibility standards
exceptions: when the door is designed to fold flush into a pocket or recess that maintains clear space

subject: Folding Door System
rule: folding door system must have a locking or latching mechanism that prevents inadvertent unfolding
conditions: when installed in a vertical (overhead or side-folding) orientation
exceptions: when the door is non-latching and gravity alone is sufficient to hold the closed position

subject: Bay/Bow Window Assembly
rule: Bay/bow window assembly must be structurally supported at its base by the building frame or foundation
conditions: Assembly projects outward from the main building wall
exceptions: Temporary installations during construction

subject: Bay/Bow Window Assembly
rule: Bay/bow window assembly must have a weather-tested flashing and sealing system at all junctions with the exterior wall and roof
conditions: Assembly is exposed to exterior weather conditions

subject: Bay/Bow Window Assembly
rule: Bay/bow window assembly must not have glass-to-frame gaps that exceed the manufacturer's specified tolerance

subject: Bay/Bow Window Assembly
rule: Bay/bow window assembly must have adequate support for its roof (if the assembly includes a roof element)
conditions: Assembly includes an integrated roof element (e.g., a copper or asphalt shingle top)

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rule: window opening restrictor must not prevent the window from achieving its minimum required egress opening dimensions
conditions: applicable to windows serving as emergency egress or rescue openings
exceptions: windows not required to serve as egress openings

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rule: window opening restrictor must allow the window to close fully and latch securely
conditions: all installations

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rule: window opening restrictor must not allow the window to open beyond the maximum safe opening distance specified by applicable regulations
conditions: installations in buildings with fall risk, e.g., window located above ground floor in residential or institutional occupancies
exceptions: windows with fixed screens or other physical barriers that independently prevent falls
windows not subject to fall-protection regulations

subject: Fire-Rated Door Assembly
rule: Fire-rated door assembly must have a self-closing device
conditions: Door is not held open by automatic release device
exceptions: Doors in smoke partitions that are not required to be self-closing by code

subject: Fire-Rated Door Assembly
rule: Fire-rated door assembly must not have the fire-resistance rating reduced by field modifications (e.g., cutting, notching, or drilling)
exceptions: Modifications specifically permitted by the door manufacturer's listing and labeled assembly

subject: Fire-Rated Door Assembly
rule: Fire-rated door assembly must have positive-latching hardware
conditions: Door is side-hinged and swinging
exceptions: Doors in smoke barriers where positive latching is not required by applicable code

subject: Intumescent Seal
rule: Intumescent seal must be in direct contact with the material it is protecting to expand and form a char barrier when exposed to fire
conditions: When used for passive fire protection
When installed in a fire-rated assembly
exceptions: When used as a gap filler in oversized openings where backing materials are required per code

subject: Intumescent Seal
rule: Intumescent seal must not be painted over or coated with non-intumescent materials
conditions: After installation in a fire-rated application

subject: Intumescent Seal
rule: Intumescent seal must be installed within the ambient temperature range specified by the manufacturer
conditions: During installation

subject: Lift Car
rule: lift car must have a structurally sound floor capable of supporting the rated load plus a safety factor

subject: Lift Car
rule: lift car must have a door that prevents opening when the car is not at a landing or is moving between floors
conditions: car is in normal passenger operation
exceptions: emergency rescue mode with authorized override

subject: Lift Car
rule: lift car must not have sharp protrusions or edges inside the car that could injure occupants

subject: Lift Car
rule: lift car must have adequate ventilation openings to prevent asphyxiation of trapped occupants
conditions: car is enclosed and occupied by passengers

subject: Lift Car
rule: lift car must have a braking or safety gear system capable of stopping and holding the car under overload and at rated speed

subject: Lift Shaft
rule: lift shaft must be continuous from top to bottom without horizontal offsets or changes in alignment
conditions: building has more than one floor
lift serves multiple levels
exceptions: lift shaft for inclined/zigzag lifts specifically designed for such geometry (rare)

subject: Lift Shaft
rule: lift shaft must be enclosed by fire-resisting construction on all sides
conditions: building is subject to fire safety regulations
exceptions: shaft open to external air on one side where local codes permit (e.g., observation lifts in atria with sprinkler protection)

subject: Lift Shaft
rule: lift shaft must not contain any pipework or ducts unrelated to the lift operation
exceptions: fire mains or sprinkler piping if specifically permitted by local codes and isolated within a separate fire-rated duct within the shaft

subject: Lift Shaft
rule: lift shaft pit must be dry and waterproof

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room must have adequate ventilation to prevent overheating of lift equipment

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room must have a fire-rated enclosure (minimum fire resistance rating as per local code)
conditions: building code requires fire separation between lift machine room and adjacent spaces

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room must have a lockable door with restricted access
exceptions: unlocked access permitted if room is in a continuously supervised/security-controlled zone

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room must have a minimum clear working space around lift equipment (typically 600-1000mm)
conditions: as specified by lift manufacturer and local safety regulations

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room floor must be level and capable of supporting the static and dynamic loads of lift equipment

subject: Lift Machine Room
rule: Lift machine room must not contain pipes or services unrelated to the lift operation
exceptions: fire suppression sprinklers serving the room itself

subject: Lift Pit
rule: lift pit base must be waterproof and structurally sealed against groundwater ingress
conditions: pit extends below the water table or in a zone with high groundwater level

subject: Lift Pit
rule: lift pit must have a positive drainage system (e.g., sump pump or gravity drain)
conditions: pit is located in a zone prone to water accumulation or below the building's sewer level

subject: Lift Pit
rule: lift pit depth must not exceed the maximum buffer zone required for hydraulic lift cylinder overtravel
conditions: hydraulic lift is installed in the pit
exceptions: screw-driven or machine-room-less traction lifts with no cylinder overtravel requirement

subject: Lift Pit
rule: lift pit must be provided with a fixed ladder or access steps if pit depth exceeds 1.0 m
conditions: pit depth > 1.0 m

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rule: Lift guide rails must be vertically straight and aligned within manufacturer-specified tolerances
conditions: guide rails are installed for a passenger or freight lift

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rule: Lift guide rails must be securely fixed to the building structure at all bracket points
conditions: guide rails are installed

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rule: Lift guide rails must have a smooth, continuous running surface free of burrs, weld spatter, or protrusions
conditions: guide rails are installed

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rule: Lift guide rail joints must not introduce a step or offset greater than the manufacturer-specified tolerance
conditions: rails are joined end-to-end in a multi-story installation

subject: Lift Counterweight
rule: lift counterweight must have a total mass that is at least equal to the mass of the lift car plus its rated load capacity when fully loaded
conditions: traction or roped hydraulic elevator installation
exceptions: hydraulic elevators without counterweights
elevators with compensating ropes that alter the balance ratio

subject: Lift Counterweight
rule: lift counterweight mass must not exceed the mass of the lift car plus the rated load capacity when unloaded by more than the overbalance ratio defined in the elevator design
conditions: traction elevator installation
exceptions: elevator designs specifically engineered for a different overbalance ratio

subject: Lift Counterweight
rule: lift counterweight must be guided within its travel path by rigid guide rails with defined clearances
conditions: any counterweighted elevator installation

subject: Lift Counterweight
rule: lift counterweight must travel within a dedicated counterweight buffer or striking plate at the base of the hoistway
conditions: any counterweighted elevator installation with bottom clearance less than counterweight stroke
exceptions: counterweights that are over-slung and do not reach the pit at full compression

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rule: Lift hoisting ropes or belts must have a safety factor compliant with applicable elevator codes (e.g., ASME A17.1/CSA B44)
conditions: All traction elevators using ropes or belts for suspension

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rule: Lift hoisting ropes or belts must not have visible broken wires, corrosion, or wear beyond allowed rejection criteria
conditions: In-service ropes or belts

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rule: Lift hoisting ropes must not be undersized for the maximum static load including car weight, rated load, and counterweight
conditions: All rope-based suspension systems

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rule: Lift hoisting belts must have end terminations that are mechanically locked and cannot slip under full load
conditions: Flat-belt or polyurethane-belt suspension systems

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rule: Lift traction machine must be located in a dedicated machine room (or enclosed machine space) that is accessible only to authorized personnel
conditions: For buildings with traction elevators where the machine is not mounted inside the hoistway
exceptions: Machine-room-less (MRL) elevator designs where the traction machine is compact enough to fit within the hoistway or overhead space

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rule: Lift traction machine must be installed on a structural support capable of bearing its static and dynamic loads

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rule: Lift traction machine must not be installed in a location exposed to water leakage or flooding

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rule: Lift traction machine must have a working braking system that engages automatically upon power loss

subject: Lift Controller
rule: lift controller must receive electrical power within its rated voltage and frequency range
conditions: when installed and operational

subject: Lift Controller
rule: lift controller must have its safety-related inputs (e.g., door lock, overspeed governor, limit switches) electrically connected and functional before allowing car motion
conditions: during normal automatic operation
exceptions: during authorised maintenance mode with bypass keyswitch engaged

subject: Lift Controller
rule: lift controller must not be subjected to ambient temperature outside its rated operating range
conditions: during any operating mode

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rule: lift landing doors must withstand the rated landing load without deformation that prevents door operation
conditions: door is in closed position
lift car is not at the landing

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rule: lift landing doors must be interlocked such that the lift car cannot move away from the landing while the doors are not fully closed and locked
exceptions: during maintenance or inspection mode with bypass key

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rule: lift landing doors must not have gaps large enough to allow a child or object to pass through when closed and locked
exceptions: purpose-designed ventilation openings that comply with code size limits

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rule: lift landing doors must be self-closing and self-locking upon release of the landing operating device
