exceptions: power-operated doors with reopening devices as permitted by code

subject: Lift Car Doors
rule: lift car doors must be able to open fully to allow passenger entry and exit
conditions: when lift is at a landing with the car level within the landing zone
exceptions: emergency lockdown modes where doors are intentionally locked shut

subject: Lift Car Doors
rule: lift car doors must not open when the car is not at a landing or is moving between floors
exceptions: specifically designed emergency egress sequences where controlled opening at reduced speed is permitted

subject: Lift Car Doors
rule: lift car doors must close fully before the lift car is permitted to move

subject: Lift Car Doors
rule: lift car doors must provide a mechanical barrier that prevents a passenger from falling into the hoistway when the car is absent

subject: Lift Car Doors
rule: lift car doors must withstand a lateral impact force without dislodging from their guides or tracks
conditions: under normal passenger crowding conditions inside the car

subject: Lift Buffers
rule: lift buffer must have adequate structural capacity to support the rated load of the lift
conditions: when the lift is in operation
when the buffer is installed as a load-bearing component

subject: Lift Buffers
rule: lift buffer must not compress below its fully compressed height under the rated impact load

subject: Lift Buffers
rule: lift buffer must be made of a material with sufficient energy absorption capacity for the lift's stopping distance and speed
conditions: when the buffer type is energy-absorbing (e.g., oil, spring, or polyurethane)

subject: Lift Buffers
rule: lift buffer must be securely anchored to the pit floor or supporting structure

subject: Lift Buffers
rule: lift buffer must be positioned such that it is aligned with the lift car or counterweight striking plate

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rule: Lift safety gear must be capable of stopping and holding the elevator car (with rated load) in the event of overspeed or free fall
conditions: elevator car is in service
rated load is applied

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rule: Lift safety gear must engage the guide rails symmetrically to prevent car binding or derailment
conditions: safety gear is activated

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rule: Lift safety gear must not activate under normal operating conditions (e.g., during routine braking or power fluctuations)
conditions: elevator is operating within normal speed and acceleration limits
no governor overspeed signal is present

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rule: Lift safety gear wedge/roller surfaces must have a coefficient of friction within a specified range (not too low causing ineffective braking, not too high causing jamming)

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rule: Lift safety gear must be mechanically independent of the normal service brake

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rule: Lift overhead beam must be designed to carry the combined dead load (self-weight + permanently attached equipment) plus the full rated live load of the lift (including dynamic factor, typically 1.25x rated capacity) without exceeding allowable stress limits
conditions: Lift is installed and operational

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rule: Lift overhead beam must have a safety factor (against yielding) of at least the minimum required by the applicable design code (e.g., BS EN 1990, AS 1418, or local equivalent)
conditions: Lift is installed and operational

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rule: Lift overhead beam must not have any visible cracks, notches, or sharp discontinuities in load-bearing zones
conditions: Beam is in service
exceptions: Minor surface imperfections within fabrication tolerance limits defined by the applicable standard

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rule: Lift overhead beam must be fabricated from material with documented traceability and mechanical properties meeting or exceeding the design specification (grade, yield strength, toughness, weldability)
conditions: Beam is part of a permanent lift installation

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rule: Lift traveling cable must be properly supported and guided within the hoistway
conditions: Cable travels vertically in a lift hoistway

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rule: Lift traveling cable must not be subjected to tension exceeding its rated breaking strength
conditions: Cable is installed and operational

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rule: Lift traveling cable bend radius must not be less than the manufacturer-specified minimum
conditions: Cable is flexed during lift travel

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rule: Lift traveling cable must be fire-resistant to the applicable code standard

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rule: hydraulic cylinder working fluid must be clean and free of contaminants
conditions: cylinder is in operation
exceptions: during initial assembly before first use

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rule: cylinder pressure rating must not exceed the manufacturer's rated maximum operating pressure
conditions: system is pressurized

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rule: piston rod surface must be free of scoring, nicks, or corrosion damage
conditions: cylinder is assembled and in use

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rule: hydraulic fluid must be compatible with the seal material
conditions: cylinder is assembled with seals

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rule: cylinder mounting alignment must not induce side loading on the piston rod
conditions: cylinder is mounted and actuated
exceptions: systems designed with guided rods that compensate for misalignment

subject: MRL (Machine-Room-Less) Lift System
rule: MRL lift system must have a functional braking mechanism that engages automatically upon power loss
conditions: electric power supply is present

subject: MRL (Machine-Room-Less) Lift System
rule: MRL lift system must_not have its controller positioned such that it is inaccessible for maintenance and emergency rescue operations

subject: MRL (Machine-Room-Less) Lift System
rule: MRL lift system must have a means of emergency manual lowering and raising of the car

subject: MRL (Machine-Room-Less) Lift System
rule: MRL lift system must_not have the machine-sheave or rope contact surface subjected to lubricant contamination that reduces traction below the design coefficient

subject: Scenic / Panoramic Lift
rule: scenic/panoramic lift cab must be fully enclosed with safety glazing or robust guarding
conditions: lift is accessible to passengers
lift operates at height
exceptions: temporary maintenance with restricted access

subject: Scenic / Panoramic Lift
rule: scenic/panoramic lift must have anti-glare or UV protection on transparent surfaces
conditions: transparent glazing is used for scenic viewing
exceptions: lift is fully interior with no direct sunlight exposure

subject: Scenic / Panoramic Lift
rule: scenic/panoramic lift must not have structural obstructions that block the designated viewing direction
conditions: lift is marketed or designated as scenic/panoramic
exceptions: obstructions are required for structural safety and are clearly unavoidable

subject: Scenic / Panoramic Lift
rule: scenic/panoramic lift must have rated impact-resistant glazing on all exterior-facing transparent surfaces
conditions: glazing is at ground level or within reach of public
lift is externally visible
exceptions: none — public safety requirement

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift car must have load-bearing rated suspension (cables, chains, or hydraulic mechanism) capable of supporting the rated capacity plus safety margin
conditions: The lift is in service

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift must have overspeed governor or fall-arrest safety device that engages if descent velocity exceeds rated speed by a defined threshold
conditions: The lift travels vertically more than a few metres
The lift is in service

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift car must have braking or locking mechanism that holds the car stationary at a landing when parked
conditions: The lift is in service

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift must not have a door or gate that can be opened from the hoistway side when the car is not present at that landing
conditions: The lift serves multiple landings

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift car floor must be level with the landing floor at each stop within a tolerance that prevents tripping or equipment roll-away
conditions: The lift serves landings for loading/unloading

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift must have a rated load capacity plate visibly affixed inside the car
conditions: The lift is in service

subject: Goods / Freight Lift
rule: Goods/freight lift must not be operated with a load exceeding the manufacturer's rated capacity
conditions: The lift is in service

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rule: EMI shielding for a lift shaft must form a continuous conductive enclosure around the entire shaft
conditions: When electromagnetic interference shielding is required for the lift shaft

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rule: EMI shielding for a lift shaft must be electrically bonded to the building's grounding/earthing system
conditions: When electromagnetic interference shielding is installed for a lift shaft

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rule: EMI shielding material for a lift shaft must not have gaps at joints, seams, or penetrations larger than the maximum allowable aperture size specified for the target shielding frequency
conditions: When electromagnetic interference shielding is used for the lift shaft

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rule: Penetrations through the EMI shield of a lift shaft (e.g., for cables, ventilation, doors) must be treated with conductive gaskets, waveguides, or other continuous shielding measures
conditions: When electromagnetic interference shielding is installed for a lift shaft
When there are penetrations through the shielding boundary

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rule: Lift shaft doors within an EMI shielded shaft must themselves be shielded and maintain continuous electrical contact with the surrounding shield when closed
conditions: When electromagnetic interference shielding is required for the lift shaft
When lift shaft doors are present

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rule: lift car emergency phone or intercom must provide two-way hands-free communication to a constantly attended off-site location or building management office
conditions: lift is installed and used for passenger transport

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rule: lift emergency phone or intercom must function during mains power failure
conditions: lift is installed and used for passenger transport

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rule: lift emergency phone or intercom must not require the user to dial a number or press a button other than a single activation (e.g., push-to-talk or auto-connect)
conditions: lift is installed and used for passenger transport

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rule: lift emergency phone or intercom connection point in the building must be capable of identifying the specific lift car from which a call originates
conditions: multiple lift cars are served or the building management receives calls remotely

subject: Lift Smoke Detection and Fireman's Recall System
rule: smoke detection in lift lobby, lift machine room, and lift shaft must initiate fireman's recall of all lifts in the bank
conditions: building is equipped with a fireman's recall system
smoke detector is installed in lift-related spaces

subject: Lift Smoke Detection and Fireman's Recall System
rule: the fireman's recall system must override all normal lift car and landing calls upon activation
conditions: fireman's recall system is activated by smoke detection or manual switch

subject: Lift Smoke Detection and Fireman's Recall System
rule: the fireman's recall switch at the nominated recall level must be accessible only to fire services and must not be operable by the general public
conditions: building has a nominated fireman's recall level

subject: Lift Smoke Detection and Fireman's Recall System
rule: smoke detectors in lift shafts must not be of a type that requires routine entry into the shaft for resetting
conditions: smoke detector is located inside the lift shaft

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must have a minimum rated load capacity sufficient to carry a stretcher with a patient and two attendants
conditions: when intended for patient transport with accompanying staff

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must have a clear internal depth of at least 2100 mm (or applicable local code minimum) to accommodate a standard stretcher length
conditions: when designed for horizontal stretcher entry

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must have a clear internal door opening width of at least 1100 mm (or applicable local code minimum) to allow stretcher passage
conditions: when stretcher width exceeds standard wheelchair width

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must not have any internal column, handrail, or obstruction that reduces the clear usable stretcher area below minimum dimensions
conditions: when the car interior contains fixed protrusions within stretcher zone

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift car must have a minimum clear floor-to-ceiling height of at least 2300 mm (or applicable local code minimum) to allow standing attendants beside a raised stretcher
conditions: when attendants need to stand upright beside the stretcher

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must have a door that remains open if obstructed (safety edge or sensor) to prevent injury during stretcher loading/unloading
conditions: when automatic power-operated doors are fitted

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must be able to level accurately at each landing floor within applicable tolerance (typically ±6 mm)
conditions: when serving more than one floor

subject: Stretcher / Ambulance Lift
rule: stretcher/ambulance lift must have emergency communication (alarm/intercom) accessible from stretcher level
conditions: when the lift is intended for emergency/patient transport

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rule: All seating rows must provide a clear, unobstructed line of sight to the presentation/performance area
conditions: seating is tiered/raked
fixed seating is installed

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rule: Each tier/row must have sufficient step height to allow safe egress and must not create trip hazards between tiers
conditions: tiered seating is present
occupant load exceeds 50 persons

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rule: Tiered seating structure must be designed to support the live load of seated occupants plus dynamic loads from crowd movement
conditions: seating is fixed/tiered
occupant load is defined

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rule: Handrails or guardrails must be provided at the open edge of any tier where the vertical drop exceeds 30 inches (760 mm)
conditions: tier/row elevation change exceeds 30 inches
exceptions: if the tier is accessible only from the front and the drop is fully within the seating zone with no walkway alongside

subject: Fixed Bench Seating
rule: Fixed bench seating must be anchored to the floor or ground
conditions: When located indoors
When located outdoors on a hard surface
exceptions: When the bench is intentionally designed as movable/freestanding furniture

subject: Fixed Bench Seating
rule: Fixed bench seating must have a seating surface height between 400 mm and 480 mm from the finished floor
conditions: When intended for adult use in public or commercial spaces
exceptions: When designed specifically for children (lower height range acceptable)

subject: Fixed Bench Seating
rule: Fixed bench seating must provide a clear leg space depth of at least 300 mm from the front edge of the seat to any obstruction
conditions: When located against a wall, partition, or other vertical obstruction at the rear

subject: Fixed Bench Seating
rule: Fixed bench seating must not have sharp edges or corners on surfaces that contact users

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rule: Bleacher/grandstand seating rows must have a minimum tread depth (seat width) of at least 300 mm (12 in) to allow safe occupant egress and seating.
conditions: Seating is fixed in place
Seating is used for public occupancy

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rule: Bleacher/grandstand seating must have a maximum riser height (vertical step between rows) of no more than 500 mm (20 in) to prevent falls and enable safe circulation.
conditions: Seating is tiered with more than two rows

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rule: Bleacher/grandstand seating must have handrails or guardrails at any open side where the drop exceeds 760 mm (30 in) to prevent falls.
conditions: Seating is elevated above adjacent floor/ground level by more than 760 mm

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rule: Bleacher/grandstand seating rows must not have gaps between adjacent seat platforms or between the seating surface and the riser face that exceed 100 mm (4 in) to prevent entrapment of limbs or objects.
conditions: Seating is constructed from separate modular sections or planks

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rule: Bleacher/grandstand seating must have a means of egress capacity sufficient for the occupant load, calculated at a minimum width of 7.6 mm (0.3 in) per occupant for stairs and 5.1 mm (0.2 in) per occupant for ramps.
conditions: Seating is used for public occupancy events

subject: Fixed Individual Seat
rule: seat must have a stable base or mounting method that prevents tipping under expected lateral loads
conditions: when occupied by a user
when subjected to lateral forces such as leaning or shifting weight

subject: Fixed Individual Seat
rule: seat must have a horizontal seating surface that supports the user
conditions: when intended for sitting

subject: Fixed Individual Seat
rule: seat must be fixedly attached to a supporting structure with connections capable of sustaining occupant weight

subject: Reception Desk / Welcome Counter
rule: reception desk / welcome counter must have a clear, unobstructed front face for staff-guest interaction
conditions: when designed as a staffed counter
exceptions: when the desk is purely decorative or not intended for active service

subject: Reception Desk / Welcome Counter
rule: reception desk / welcome counter must not have sharp or hazardous edges at user contact height
conditions: when located in areas accessible to the public, including children or people with disabilities

subject: Reception Desk / Welcome Counter
rule: reception desk / welcome counter must have a minimum clear knee space of at least 27 inches high, 30 inches wide, and 19 inches deep at service positions
conditions: when designed for seated staff use
when required to comply with accessibility standards
exceptions: when the counter is purely self-service with no staff workstation

subject: Reception Desk / Welcome Counter
rule: reception desk / welcome counter must have a work surface height between 28 and 34 inches for seated use and between 36 and 42 inches for standing use
conditions: when designed as a functional workspace for staff

subject: Stadium Seat with Armrest
rule: stadium seat with armrest must have a minimum width between armrests to accommodate the intended occupant
conditions: seat is designed for individual occupancy

subject: Stadium Seat with Armrest
rule: stadium seat with armrest must not have armrests that protrude into adjacent seat's required clear width zone
conditions: seats are installed side-by-side in a row
exceptions: seats are standalone with gap on both sides

subject: Stadium Seat with Armrest
rule: stadium seat with armrest must have a seat surface that can support the static load of a seated adult without collapse

subject: Stadium Seat with Armrest
rule: stadium seat with armrest must be attached to the stadium structure (riser or floor) with sufficient connection to prevent detachment under expected live loads

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must have a structurally adequate attachment to floor or adjacent structure
conditions: installed in a fixed position
exceptions: freestanding units that rely solely on self-weight for stability

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must provide a minimum clear aisle width in front of or behind the seats for egress
conditions: located in a means of egress path or assembly area
exceptions: seating with unobstructed access on all sides not forming part of a required egress path

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must not obstruct emergency exit access or fire extinguisher/equipment access
conditions: located near exits or fire safety equipment

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must have seating surfaces that withstand expected static and dynamic loads without failure

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must not create sharp edges or protrusions at head or limb height in circulation zones
conditions: located within an accessible or circulation route

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rule: Fixed booth seating must not block required clear floor area for accessible seating where required
conditions: part of a public accommodation or commercial facility required to comply with accessibility standards
exceptions: facilities exempt from accessibility code requirements

subject: Fixed Seat Anchoring System
rule: fixed seat anchoring system must be structurally connected to the primary building structure (e.g., floor slab, supporting beam) capable of withstanding design loads
conditions: when the anchoring system is load-bearing and intended to resist seismic or gravity-induced lateral forces
exceptions: when the fixed seat is a non-structural element and the anchoring system serves only as positional restraint with no structural load path requirement

subject: Fixed Seat Anchoring System
rule: fixed seat anchoring system must not rely solely on friction or gravity to resist uplift or overturning forces
conditions: when the installed seat orientation creates a potential for overturning or uplift under design loading (e.g., cantilevered or high-back seating)
exceptions: when analysis demonstrates that the seat's self-weight and friction alone provide a factor of safety of at least 1.5 against overturning

subject: Built-in Waiting Area Seating
rule: seating must be anchored or secured to prevent tipping or movement under expected live loads
conditions: built-in fixed seating exposed to public use

subject: Built-in Waiting Area Seating
rule: seat surface must be slip-resistant or have drainage to prevent pooling of water
conditions: installed in exterior or semi-exposed location

subject: Built-in Waiting Area Seating
rule: clearance in front of seating must be sufficient for wheelchair access and circulation paths
conditions: seating is part of a public or accessible waiting area

subject: Built-in Waiting Area Seating
rule: edge of seat must not have sharp corners or projecting elements that could cause laceration or snagging

subject: Fixed Seating Framing and Support Structure
rule: Fixed seating framing and support structure must support the design dead load plus live load per applicable building code without exceeding allowable stress or deflection limits
conditions: Fixed seating is installed in a commercial or public assembly occupancy
exceptions: Temporary seating not fixed to the structure

subject: Fixed Seating Framing and Support Structure
rule: Fixed seating framing and support structure must not have a load path that bypasses or is discontinuous from the primary building structure
conditions: The seating is cantilevered or bracket-mounted to walls or slabs

subject: Fixed Seating Framing and Support Structure
rule: Fixed seating framing and support structure must be positively anchored to prevent lateral or overturning displacement under design lateral loads (seismic or wind)
conditions: The seating is located in a Seismic Design Category B, C, D, E, or F region
OR the seating is at grade exposed to wind
exceptions: Seating that is self-stabilizing with a width-to-height ratio exceeding 3:1 and resting on friction alone, but only where code permits

subject: Fixed Seating Framing and Support Structure
rule: Fixed seating framing and support structure must not obstruct means of egress from any seat row to the exit
conditions: The seating is arranged in rows serving an assembly occupancy

subject: Custom Cabinetry
rule: Custom cabinetry must be constructed from materials that can withstand the moisture, temperature, and humidity conditions of its intended environment (e.g., kitchen, bathroom) without warping, delaminating, or degrading.
exceptions: Cabinetry installed exclusively in climate-controlled interior spaces not subject to moisture (e.g., a study, bedroom closet) may use standard interior-grade materials

subject: Custom Cabinetry
rule: Custom cabinetry must have a structural frame or carcass that can support the weight of its doors, drawers, shelves, and stored contents without failure or dangerous deformation.

subject: Custom Cabinetry
rule: Custom cabinetry doors and drawers must not open unintentionally under gravity or normal vibration (e.g., they require latches, catches, self-closing hinges, or friction sufficient to prevent self-opening).
conditions: where cabinet is mounted on a moving vehicle or vessel
where cabinet is subject to seismic forces
exceptions: Cabinetry designed with deliberate friction-free push-to-open mechanisms where the design intent allows gravity opening

subject: Custom Cabinetry
rule: Custom cabinetry must be anchored or secured against tipping when the cabinet is tall or top-heavy (e.g., tall pantry cabinets, wall-hung upper cabinets).
conditions: cabinet height exceeds 36 inches
cabinet is wall-mounted
cabinet depth-to-height ratio exceeds 1:3
exceptions: Cabinets that are floor-supported and have a wide base making them inherently stable (e.g., low base cabinets under 36 inches)

subject: Kitchen Base Cabinets
rule: Kitchen base cabinets must be installed on a level, structurally adequate floor

subject: Kitchen Base Cabinets
rule: Kitchen base cabinets must be securely fastened to the wall structure (studs or equivalent anchorage)

subject: Kitchen Base Cabinets
rule: Kitchen base cabinet doors and drawers must not be obstructed by the countertop overhang or adjacent elements such that they cannot fully open
exceptions: Cases where doors/drawers use lift-up or pull-out mechanisms that intentionally clear the obstruction

subject: Kitchen Base Cabinets
rule: Kitchen base cabinets must not be placed directly against an uncovered heat source (cooktop, oven, radiator) without a rated thermal barrier or minimum clearance
exceptions: Cabinets designed and rated for proximity to heat sources with integral thermal protection

subject: Kitchen Wall Cabinets
rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must be securely attached to wall studs or a suitable structural backing
conditions: Cabinets will bear load of stored items

subject: Kitchen Wall Cabinets
rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must not obstruct ventilation hood exhaust paths or required clearances
conditions: Range hood or exhaust system is present above the cooking appliance

subject: Kitchen Wall Cabinets
rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must be installed with bottom edge at least 18 inches above cooktop surface
conditions: Cabinets are located directly above a cooking appliance
exceptions: Cabinets are explicitly rated and listed for zero-clearance installation above cooking appliances

subject: Kitchen Wall Cabinets
rule: Kitchen wall cabinet doors and hardware must not protrude into required clear walkway space as defined by applicable accessibility codes
conditions: Cabinets are adjacent to a passageway or work aisle that requires unobstructed movement

subject: Tall/Utility Cabinets
rule: Tall/Utility cabinets must be anchored or fastened to prevent tip-over
conditions: Free-standing tall/utility cabinet over 600mm in height
Located in a seismic region or accessible to children
exceptions: Cabinet is integrally built into a wall structure

subject: Tall/Utility Cabinets
rule: Tall/Utility cabinet doors must not obstruct adjacent circulation or equipment swing clearances when fully open
conditions: Cabinet is located adjacent to a doorway, walkway, or operable equipment
exceptions: Adjacent area is designated as non-circulation space

subject: Tall/Utility Cabinets
rule: Tall/Utility cabinets housing mechanical or electrical equipment must have adequate ventilation to prevent heat buildup
conditions: Cabinet contains heat-producing equipment (e.g., water heater, electrical panel, HVAC components)
exceptions: Equipment is rated for enclosed installation with zero clearance ventilation requirements met by cabinet design itself

subject: Vanity Cabinets
rule: vanity cabinets must be made of moisture-resistant materials
conditions: installed in bathroom or humid environment
exceptions: cabinets installed in fully dry locations such as powder rooms with no plumbing

subject: Vanity Cabinets
rule: vanity cabinet countertop must have a backsplash that seals the joint between countertop and wall
conditions: countertop is installed against a wall

subject: Vanity Cabinets
rule: vanity cabinet doors must not obstruct each other or nearby fixtures when opened
conditions: cabinet is in a confined space or adjacent to other fixtures
exceptions: doors are designed as sliding/pocket doors or removable

subject: Closet Organization Systems
rule: Closet organization systems must be attached to load-bearing wall studs, not to drywall alone
conditions: when supporting significant weight (e.g., hanging rods with clothing)
when wall-mounted
exceptions: freestanding systems not attached to walls
systems using specialized toggle anchors rated for the full design load

subject: Closet Organization Systems
rule: Closet organization systems must not block HVAC supply or return vents
conditions: when installed in closets containing HVAC registers or returns
exceptions: vents that have been properly relocated or sealed per building code

subject: Closet Organization Systems
rule: Hanging rods must be level within manufacturer-specified tolerance
conditions: when rod is installed for hanging garments

subject: Closet Organization Systems
rule: Closet organization systems must maintain minimum clearance around electrical panels or junction boxes if present inside the closet
conditions: when electrical panel or junction box is located within the closet space
exceptions: panels relocated to comply with clearance before system installation

subject: Entertainment Center Cabinetry
rule: entertainment center cabinetry must be structurally stable and securely anchored to wall or floor structure
conditions: free-standing cabinet exceeds 48 inches in height
exceptions: cabinet is designed as a low console under 30 inches tall and not subject to tip-over risk

subject: Entertainment Center Cabinetry
rule: entertainment center cabinetry must not have shelves or enclosed compartments that lack ventilation when housing heat-generating electronic equipment
conditions: cabinetry encloses AV receivers, amplifiers, game consoles, or other equipment that produces heat during normal operation

subject: Entertainment Center Cabinetry
rule: entertainment center cabinetry must support the static vertical load of all installed equipment, shelving, and stored media without structural failure

subject: Built-in Window Seats
rule: built-in window seat must have a minimum clear seat depth of at least 400 mm (approximately 16 in) from the inner face of the window to the backrest or wall
conditions: seat is intended for sitting by an adult or child over age 3
exceptions: seat is purely decorative and not intended for occupancy

subject: Built-in Window Seats
rule: built-in window seat must have a clear seat width of at least 600 mm (approximately 24 in) per intended occupant
conditions: seat is intended for occupancy by one or more persons

subject: Built-in Window Seats
rule: built-in window seat must have a seat height between 400 mm and 500 mm (approximately 16-20 in) above finished floor
conditions: seat is intended for sitting by adults or children
exceptions: seat is a custom accessible design with documented clear floor space for wheelchair transfer at other heights

subject: Built-in Window Seats
rule: built-in window seat must not have sharp or protruding edges or corners at seated occupant head height between 700 mm and 1200 mm above the seat surface
conditions: seat is located in a circulation path where a seated person could be bumped by passing persons

subject: Mudroom/Locker Cabinetry
rule: mudroom/locker cabinetry must have a minimum of 4 inches (102 mm) of clearance above the floor
conditions: cabinetry is constructed of wood or engineered wood products
cabinetry is not suspended from wall
exceptions: cabinetry is specifically designed as floor-mounted base units with integral toe-kick

subject: Mudroom/Locker Cabinetry
rule: mudroom/locker cabinetry must_not obstruct the swing path of the room's entry door
conditions: cabinetry is located within the door swing zone of the primary mudroom entry
exceptions: the entry door is a sliding or pocket door

subject: Mudroom/Locker Cabinetry
rule: mudroom/locker cabinetry containing electrical outlets or USB charging ports must be at least 6 inches (152 mm) away from any plumbing drain or supply line within the same wall cavity
conditions: cabinetry includes integrated electrical devices
exceptions: electrical and plumbing rough-ins are separated by a vapor barrier or metal shield

subject: Mudroom/Locker Cabinetry
rule: mudroom/locker cabinetry must have a clear floor space of at least 30 inches (762 mm) in front of each locker compartment
conditions: cabinetry includes individual partitioned locker compartments intended for occupant use
exceptions: cabinetry is only storage shelving without seating or changing function

subject: Laboratory Casework
rule: Laboratory casework benchtop surfaces must be non-porous and chemically resistant
conditions: applicable to all laboratory casework benchtops

subject: Laboratory Casework
rule: Laboratory casework must not have exposed unsealed wood surfaces in wet or chemical-use zones
conditions: when casework is located in wet lab areas or zones where chemical handling occurs

subject: Laboratory Casework
rule: Laboratory casework must incorporate edge banding or seamless construction on all exposed laminate edges in active lab zones
conditions: when using laminate-faced casework in active laboratory areas

subject: Laboratory Casework
rule: Laboratory casework must support a minimum distributed live load of 300 lb per linear foot of counter
conditions: when casework is intended to support laboratory equipment or heavy materials

subject: Built-in Banquette Seating
rule: must allow at least 450 mm (18 in) of clear floor space in front of banquette seating for egress and accessibility
conditions: when the banquette is fixed in position
when the banquette is located in a path of egress or accessible route
exceptions: when seating is removable or not fixed
when the space in front is unobstructed and serves only circulation to the banquette row

subject: Built-in Banquette Seating
rule: seat height must be between 400 mm and 480 mm (16 in to 19 in) above finished floor
conditions: when designed for adult users in commercial or public occupancy
exceptions: when the banquette is in a children's area or in a residential setting with explicit non-commercial use

subject: Built-in Banquette Seating
rule: seat depth must not exceed 610 mm (24 in)
conditions: when the banquette has no backrest or lumbar support
exceptions: when the banquette includes a fixed backrest that supports the lower back at a depth greater than 610 mm

subject: Millwork Trim & Moldings
rule: Millwork trim and moldings must be installed with proper fastening to the substrate (nailing, screwing, or adhesive as per code)
conditions: when installed as finish carpentry

subject: Millwork Trim & Moldings
rule: Millwork trim and moldings must be made from materials that are dimensionally stable under expected environmental conditions (temperature and humidity ranges of the installation location)
conditions: when installed in conditioned interior spaces
when installed in exterior applications
exceptions: temporary decorative installations where dimensional movement is acceptable

subject: Millwork Trim & Moldings
rule: Millwork trim and moldings must not bridge or block required fire-rated assemblies (e.g., fire doors, fire-rated walls) in a way that compromises the fire-resistance rating
conditions: when installed in buildings subject to fire code requirements
when crossing or abutting fire-rated construction
exceptions: where the trim itself is certified as part of a listed fire-rated assembly (e.g., approved intumescent-coated trim)

subject: Millwork Trim & Moldings
rule: Millwork trim and moldings installed as grasping/pulling elements (e.g., handrails, grab bars) must meet structural load requirements for their intended use
conditions: when the trim is intended to function as a handrail or grab bar

subject: Excavation Support / Shoring
rule: excavation support/shoring must be structurally continuous from top of wall to below excavation subgrade
conditions: when soldier piles or sheet piles are used as shoring system
exceptions: when tieback anchors provide equivalent load transfer at multiple levels

subject: Excavation Support / Shoring
rule: excavation support/shoring must not have unbraced wall height exceeding the allowable span per structural design
conditions: when the shoring is cantilevered or has one level of bracing
exceptions: if soil conditions allow increased cantilever height per calibrated observational method

subject: Excavation Support / Shoring
rule: excavation support/shoring must provide positive drainage at the base of the excavation
conditions: when groundwater or surface water infiltration is anticipated
exceptions: where dewatering wells keep the excavation dry without collection at the shoring face

subject: Excavation Support / Shoring
rule: excavation support/shoring must be positively connected to the waler/brace system at each support level
conditions: when wales or cross-lot braces are part of the shoring system
exceptions: when the shoring elements derive lateral stability entirely from soil embedment without rakers

subject: Excavation Support / Shoring
rule: excavation support/shoring must not have soldier pile or sheet pile tip elevation above the required embedment depth
conditions: when the shoring system relies on toe embedment for stability
exceptions: when the shoring is a gravity or anchored system that does not require embedment

subject: Granular Backfill Material
rule: granular backfill material must be free-draining to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: when used behind retaining walls
when used in foundation drainage systems
when placed against building substructures
exceptions: when explicitly designed as part of a water-retaining system (e.g., engineered wet backfill)

subject: Granular Backfill Material
rule: granular backfill material must not contain more than 5% fines passing the No. 200 sieve
conditions: when specified for structural drainage applications
when used as sub-slab base course
exceptions: when material is specifically designed as a filtration layer with controlled fines content per geotechnical specification

subject: Granular Backfill Material
rule: granular backfill material must be compacted in lifts not exceeding the maximum specified thickness
conditions: during placement against structures
when specified compaction density is required

subject: Geotextile Separation Layer
rule: Geotextile separation layer must have sufficient permittivity to allow water flow perpendicular to the plane
conditions: when used in drainage applications
when placed between granular and fine-grained soils
exceptions: when used solely as a filtration barrier in non-drainage applications

subject: Geotextile Separation Layer
rule: Geotextile separation layer must have an opening size (AOS) smaller than the particle size of the finer soil it is separating
conditions: when used to separate fine-grained soil from coarse aggregate
exceptions: when the geotextile is designed specifically as a drainage geocomposite core rather than a separator

subject: Geotextile Separation Layer
rule: Geotextile separation layer must not have an opening size so small that it causes clogging by soil particles
conditions: when in contact with silty or clayey soils
exceptions: when a biological or chemical filter cake is intended as part of design

subject: Geotextile Separation Layer
rule: Geotextile separation layer must have minimum grab tensile strength sufficient to survive installation stresses without tearing
conditions: during construction/installation
when subjected to construction equipment loading
exceptions: when installed by hand and not trafficked during construction

subject: Drainage Backfill (French Drain)
rule: drainage backfill (french drain) must have a continuous outlet path that gravity-drains daylight or connects to an approved discharge point
conditions: system is installed to collect groundwater or surface water
exceptions: system is designed as a completely closed-loop with pumped discharge to an approved location

subject: Drainage Backfill (French Drain)
rule: drainage backfill (french drain) must not have the perforated pipe invert below the outlet invert elevation
conditions: system relies on gravity flow to an outlet
exceptions: system includes a sump pump or mechanical lift station downstream of the pipe

subject: Drainage Backfill (French Drain)
rule: drainage backfill (french drain) must have granular backfill material (e.g., clean gravel or crushed stone) surrounding the perforated pipe

subject: Drainage Backfill (French Drain)
rule: drainage backfill (french drain) must not allow fine soil particles to enter and clog the perforated pipe or granular fill
exceptions: system is wrapped in a properly designed geotextile filter fabric selected for the site soil gradation

subject: Scaffold Tubes
rule: Scaffold tubes must have a minimum wall thickness sufficient to carry the design load without buckling
conditions: When used as vertical load-bearing members (standards)

subject: Scaffold Tubes
rule: Scaffold tubes must not have visible cracks, corrosion pits deeper than 10% of wall thickness, or bends exceeding the straightness tolerance
conditions: Prior to each use or erection

subject: Scaffold Tubes
rule: Scaffold tubes must be made of steel or aluminum with a specified minimum yield strength appropriate for the scaffold class
conditions: When used in load-bearing scaffold structures

subject: Scaffold Couplers/Fittings
rule: scaffold coupler must achieve a secure mechanical interlock preventing unintended separation under design loads
conditions: when used to connect scaffold tubes
under all intended loading conditions including wind, worker, and material loads
exceptions: temporary slack allowed during initial assembly before final tightening

subject: Scaffold Couplers/Fittings
rule: scaffold coupler must not have sharp edges or projections in areas contacted by workers during normal use or handling
conditions: when installed and in service
exceptions: manufacturing identification marks or minor surface imperfections below 0.5mm radius

subject: Scaffold Couplers/Fittings
rule: scaffold coupler must be dimensionally compatible with the nominal tube outer diameter it is designed to fit
conditions: for each standard tube size the coupler is rated for (e.g., 48.3mm OD for steel tube per EN 39)
exceptions: adjustable or variable-diameter couplers as explicitly designed and rated for multiple sizes

subject: Scaffold Couplers/Fittings
rule: scaffold coupler forging/metal body must not contain cracks, porosity, or other material discontinuities that reduce load capacity below rated value
conditions: after manufacturing
before and during service life
exceptions: cosmetic surface flaws not affecting minimum cross-section or stress concentration factors

subject: Scaffold Boards/Planks
rule: scaffold boards/planks must have a minimum width-to-thickness ratio to prevent lateral instability under load
conditions: when used as load-bearing walking surfaces
when spanning between supports
exceptions: boards designed as part of a fully-braced deck system where lateral restraint is provided continuously by adjacent structure

subject: Scaffold Boards/Planks
rule: scaffold boards/planks must not have through-thickness cracks or splits that reduce effective cross-section by more than 10%
conditions: under any service condition
exceptions: hairline surface checks that do not penetrate more than 10% of thickness

subject: Scaffold Boards/Planks
rule: scaffold boards/planks must not exceed maximum allowable deflection under design load
conditions: when used as a work platform

subject: Scaffold Boards/Planks
rule: scaffold boards/planks must overhang their supports by at least a minimum distance to prevent kick-out
conditions: when simply supported at ends
exceptions: boards continuously restrained against lateral movement at supports by positive fastening

subject: Scaffold Base Plates
rule: scaffold base plates must distribute load to a firm, level bearing surface
conditions: scaffold is erected on ground or floor surface
exceptions: scaffold is suspended (e.g., hanging scaffold) where base plates are not used

subject: Scaffold Base Plates
rule: scaffold base plates must not be used directly on unstable or uncompacted fill without additional load-distributing measures
conditions: scaffold base plates are placed on soil or fill material
exceptions: a concrete pad, timber sole plate, or engineered ground-treatment system is provided to achieve adequate bearing capacity

subject: Scaffold Base Plates
rule: scaffold base plate dimensions (length and width) must equal or exceed the minimum specified in the scaffold design standard for the given load and soil condition
conditions: scaffold is supporting design loads above negligible/light-duty thresholds
exceptions: engineered alternative with documented bearing-capacity verification is used

subject: Scaffold Sole Plates/Timbers
rule: Scaffold sole plates/timbers must be positioned on firm, level ground capable of supporting the imposed loads without settlement
conditions: scaffold is freestanding or supported on ground

subject: Scaffold Sole Plates/Timbers
rule: Scaffold sole plates/timbers must have a minimum thickness adequate to prevent punch-through or crushing under the standard load

subject: Scaffold Sole Plates/Timbers
rule: Scaffold sole plates/timbers must not be fabricated from materials that are rotten, split, or otherwise structurally compromised

subject: Scaffold Sole Plates/Timbers
rule: Scaffold sole plates must extend a minimum length sufficient to span any soft spots or uneven ground conditions directly beneath the leg
conditions: ground condition is variable or uneven

subject: Scaffold Transoms
rule: scaffold transoms must be positioned perpendicular to scaffold standards (uprights)
conditions: when used in traditional tube-and-clamp scaffolding

subject: Scaffold Transoms
rule: scaffold transoms must be secured at both ends to scaffold standards or ledger connections
conditions: when assembled as part of a scaffold structure

subject: Scaffold Transoms
rule: scaffold transom material must not be damaged beyond allowable service limits
conditions: in load-bearing use

subject: Scaffold Standards (Uprights)
rule: Scaffold standards (uprights) must be supported on a firm, level foundation or base plates capable of distributing the load without excessive settlement
conditions: when scaffold is erected on ground
when scaffold is in use
exceptions: scaffold designed by a chartered engineer with alternative foundation details

subject: Scaffold Standards (Uprights)
rule: Scaffold standards (uprights) must have a maximum vertical spacing (lift height) that does not exceed the manufacturer's rated capacity or the limit specified in the design calculation for the given loading
conditions: when supporting working platforms
exceptions: where a specific engineered design demonstrates safe capacity beyond standard limits

subject: Scaffold Standards (Uprights)
rule: Scaffold standards (uprights) must not be removed or disconnected from the scaffold structure before the loads they carry are safely redistributed to adjacent standards
conditions: during erection, alteration or dismantling
when the scaffold is loaded

subject: Scaffold Standards (Uprights)
rule: Scaffold standards (uprights) must be aligned vertically (within tolerances) and plumb within the allowable deviation (typically no more than 1:200 out-of-plumb)
conditions: during erection
during use

subject: Scaffold Standards (Uprights)
rule: Scaffold standards (uprights) must be spaced such that the imposed load does not exceed the safe working load of each standard
conditions: under design load conditions

subject: Scaffold Toe Boards
rule: Scaffold toe boards must be at least 100 mm (4 inches) in height
conditions: scaffold platforms are used as a work surface above ground level

subject: Scaffold Toe Boards
rule: Scaffold toe boards must not have gaps exceeding 6 mm (1/4 inch) between the bottom of the toe board and the platform surface
conditions: scaffold platforms are used as a work surface above ground level

subject: Scaffold Toe Boards
rule: Scaffold toe boards must be securely attached to the scaffold structure
conditions: scaffold platforms are used as a work surface above ground level

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrails must have a top rail height between 900 mm and 1100 mm above the working platform
conditions: scaffold is used for construction work
working platform height exceeds 2 meters
exceptions: scaffolds designed specifically for maintenance access where risk assessment permits alternative height

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrails must be capable of withstanding a minimum concentrated load of 0.3 kN applied in any direction
conditions: scaffold is in use with personnel present
exceptions: temporary guardrails for non-personnel loads only, within demarcated exclusion zone

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrails must have intermediate rails or infill such that the gap between rails does not exceed 470 mm
conditions: scaffold working platform height exceeds 2 meters
exceptions: scaffolds with mesh or solid infill panels that prevent passage of a person

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrails must not be removed from any working platform that is in use
conditions: scaffold platform is occupied or accessed by personnel
exceptions: temporary removal permitted only when a fall protection system (harness and lanyard) is actively used by all personnel on the platform

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrails must be installed on all open sides and ends of every working platform
conditions: working platform height exceeds 2 meters
side or end is not protected by a permanent structure within 150 mm
exceptions: side used exclusively for material loading/unloading with controlled access and alternative fall protection

subject: Scaffold Guardrails
rule: Scaffold guardrail toeboards must be at least 150 mm high
conditions: scaffold working platform height exceeds 2 meters
there is risk of materials or tools falling from the platform
exceptions: scaffold is used exclusively for personnel access with no materials above

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal/Lateral)
rule: Scaffold bracing (diagonal/lateral) must be installed in both the longitudinal and transverse planes at each lift of the scaffold frame
conditions: When using frame or tube-and-coupler scaffolding
exceptions: Systems certified by the manufacturer as self-bracing without diagonal/lateral bracing

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal/Lateral)
rule: Scaffold bracing (diagonal/lateral) must not be removed from any level while the scaffold is under load or in use
conditions: When scaffold supports workers, materials, or equipment
exceptions: When scaffold is completely unloaded and scheduled for systematic dismantling progressing from top to bottom

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal/Lateral)
rule: Diagonal bracing for scaffolds must be fixed to the scaffold at nodes (connections of ledgers and standards) and not at mid-span of members
conditions: All tube-and-coupler and frame scaffold types

subject: Scaffold Ladders/Stair Towers
rule: Scaffold ladder/stair tower must have a firm, level base or foundation capable of supporting the design load without settlement or displacement
conditions: when erected on any surface

subject: Scaffold Ladders/Stair Towers
rule: Scaffold ladder/stair tower must be secured against overturning at intervals specified by the manufacturer or engineer
conditions: when tower height exceeds 4 times the minimum base dimension
or when tower is in a wind-exposed or unbraced location
exceptions: when tower is designed as freestanding with a certified engineered base width to height ratio that eliminates overturning risk

subject: Scaffold Ladders/Stair Towers
rule: Scaffold ladder/stair tower must have guardrails and toeboards on all open sides and ends of each platform
conditions: when platform elevation exceeds 2 m (6 ft) above the lower level

subject: Scaffold Ladders/Stair Towers
rule: Scaffold ladder/stair tower must not be loaded beyond its rated design capacity (safe working load)
conditions: during any use condition

subject: Scaffold Ladders/Stair Towers
rule: Scaffold ladder/stair tower must have continuous handrails on both sides of the ladder or stairway
conditions: when ladder or stairway is used for access between levels

subject: Scaffold Sheeting/Netting
rule: Scaffold sheeting/netting must be securely fastened to the scaffold structure at all attachment points
conditions: when used as wind/debris containment
when installed on working scaffolds

subject: Scaffold Sheeting/Netting
rule: Scaffold sheeting/netting must not fully enclose the scaffold in a way that blocks emergency egress or access for fire rescue
conditions: when the scaffold provides primary worker access
when the scaffold is attached to an occupied building
exceptions: when dedicated emergency access panels or cut-outs are provided and clearly marked

subject: Scaffold Sheeting/Netting
rule: Scaffold sheeting/netting must be made of fire-retardant material that meets relevant flammability standards
conditions: when used on construction sites with welding, grinding, or other ignition sources nearby
when required by local building code

subject: Scaffold Sheeting/Netting
rule: Scaffold sheeting/netting must not impose wind loads exceeding the scaffold design capacity
conditions: when installed as solid sheeting (not mesh) on tall or exposed scaffolds
when wind region is classified as high-wind or cyclonic

subject: Scaffold Ties (Anchors)
rule: scaffold ties (anchors) must be capable of transferring the design loads from the scaffold to the supporting structure without failure
conditions: scaffold is erected and in use
scaffold is of a type that requires tying (e.g. independent tied scaffold)
exceptions: freestanding scaffolds that do not require ties

subject: Scaffold Ties (Anchors)
rule: scaffold ties (anchors) must not be fastened to brittle or frangible building elements (e.g. single-leaf brickwork, cladding panels, or insulation) that cannot resist the pull-out or shear forces
conditions: tie is being installed into the building fabric
exceptions: where the tie is specifically designed and tested for such a substrate and the substrate is verified as adequate

subject: Scaffold Ties (Anchors)
rule: scaffold ties (anchors) must be fixed to structurally adequate parts of the building (e.g. concrete floors, steel columns, loadbearing masonry) that can resist the imposed tie forces
conditions: scaffold tie is being designed and installed

subject: Scaffold Ties (Anchors)
rule: scaffold ties (anchors) must not be removed or loosened during scaffold use unless the scaffold is otherwise stabilised and a competent person has assessed the condition as safe
conditions: scaffold is in service or loaded
exceptions: during planned, controlled alterations to the scaffold ties performed under a method statement and supervision

subject: Scaffold Hoist Bracket
rule: Scaffold hoist bracket must be capable of supporting the maximum rated working load (SWL) plus a safety factor without permanent deformation or failure
conditions: When used for lifting materials on a construction scaffold

subject: Scaffold Hoist Bracket
rule: Scaffold hoist bracket must be positively secured or interlocked to the scaffold structure to prevent dislodgement during operation
conditions: When mounted on a scaffold for hoisting operations

subject: Scaffold Hoist Bracket
rule: Scaffold hoist bracket must not have sharp edges, burrs, or projections that could sever or abrade the hoist rope/cable during normal operation
conditions: In any area where the hoist rope/cable passes over or contacts the bracket

subject: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck
rule: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck must withstand its self-weight plus the design live load (e.g., debris, workers, materials) without collapse or excessive deflection
conditions: When used as a protection deck or working platform

subject: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck
rule: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck must have positive attachment (latching/pinning) to its supporting structure at all connection points
conditions: When installed at height

subject: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck
rule: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck must not have gaps exceeding local code limits (typically 25 mm or 1 inch) between adjacent deck panels or between deck and building face
conditions: When used as a debris/safety shield

subject: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck
rule: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck must be sloped or provided with a drainage path (e.g., weep holes, gaps) to prevent water ponding
conditions: When exposed to rainfall/weather

subject: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck
rule: Scaffold Fan/Shield Deck must not have a net uplift resistance less than the design wind uplift pressure
conditions: When installed at height and exposed to wind

subject: Putlog Scaffold System
rule: Putlog scaffold tubes must be supported on the putlog blade/end resting securely against the structure face
conditions: When used in traditional putlog scaffolding

subject: Putlog Scaffold System
rule: Putlog scaffold must not be used as an independent (free-standing) scaffold without additional bracing and tie-in design
conditions: When configured as a standard putlog system without independent scaffold ties
exceptions: If converted to an independent scaffold by adding full ledger ties and bracing on both faces

subject: Putlog Scaffold System
rule: Putlog scaffold working platform must have a minimum width to allow safe worker passage and material handling
conditions: When used as a working platform for personnel

subject: Independent Tied Scaffold System
rule: Independent tied scaffold system must have all ties securely connected to both the scaffold and the supporting structure
conditions: scaffold is in use
scaffold height exceeds 4 times the minimum base dimension

subject: Independent Tied Scaffold System
rule: Independent tied scaffold system must have a fully planked working platform at each lift level where work is performed
conditions: workers access the platform
exceptions: during initial erection or dismantling by trained personnel

subject: Independent Tied Scaffold System
rule: Independent tied scaffold system must have all base plates and sole plates bearing on adequate ground or a structural surface capable of supporting the design load
exceptions: scaffold is suspended from above rather than bearing on ground

subject: Independent Tied Scaffold System
rule: Independent tied scaffold system must not exceed its manufacturer's or engineer-designated maximum safe working load

subject: Independent Tied Scaffold System
rule: Independent tied scaffold system must have guardrails and toe boards on all open sides and ends of platforms where a person could fall 2 meters or more
conditions: platform height is 2 meters or greater above the adjacent surface
exceptions: during active erection or dismantling by trained personnel

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: Birdcage scaffold must be erected on a stable, level base
conditions: All configurations

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: Vertical load from birdcage scaffold must be distributed such that ground-bearing capacity is not exceeded
conditions: When supporting heavy loads such as wet concrete or formwork

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: Birdcage scaffold must not exceed its manufacturer-specified maximum height without additional stability measures
conditions: When freestanding and unbraced to a building

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: All vertical standards in a birdcage scaffold must be connected to a full system of longitudinal and transverse bracing at each lift
conditions: When erected to occupied height (typically above 2 m)

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: Birdcage scaffold must have a full working platform or decking if personnel access the top level
conditions: When used as a working platform for personnel

subject: Birdcage Scaffold System
rule: Base plates and sole boards must be used under every standard of a birdcage scaffold
conditions: All configurations

subject: Cantilever/Hanging Scaffold System
rule: cantilever/hanging scaffold system must have its suspension wire ropes or chains secured to independent support points that are structurally capable of bearing the intended load
conditions: when used as a suspended access system
when supporting workers or materials

subject: Cantilever/Hanging Scaffold System
rule: cantilever/hanging scaffold system must not exceed the manufacturer-rated maximum load capacity including combined dead load, live load, and dynamic/impact forces

subject: Cantilever/Hanging Scaffold System
rule: cantilever/hanging scaffold system must have a positive anti-sway or tie-back mechanism that prevents uncontrolled horizontal oscillation
conditions: when the scaffold is suspended at a height exceeding 5 meters above the lower support level
when wind loads or worker movement could induce sway
exceptions: fully guided systems with rigid vertical tracks

subject: Cantilever/Hanging Scaffold System
rule: cantilever/hanging scaffold system must not use a single-point suspension for a working platform unless a secondary independent safety line is provided for each occupant
conditions: when used as a working platform for personnel

subject: Cantilever/Hanging Scaffold System
rule: cantilever/hanging scaffold system must have counterweights or structural anchors that resist the overturning moment from the cantilevered portion with a minimum factor of safety of 2:1 against uplift
conditions: when configured as a cantilevered outrigger scaffold (not a pure hanging system)

subject: System Scaffold (Modular Frame)
rule: modular frame system scaffold must comply with applicable scaffold design codes and load ratings
conditions: when used for construction access or structural support
exceptions: non-load-bearing decorative scaffold replicas

subject: System Scaffold (Modular Frame)
rule: modular frame system scaffold must not exceed its rated load capacity
conditions: when in service with workers, materials, or equipment
exceptions: purpose-engineered overload test under controlled conditions

subject: System Scaffold (Modular Frame)
rule: modular frame system scaffold must have all locking mechanisms fully engaged at every connection before loading
conditions: when erected and prior to use

subject: System Scaffold (Modular Frame)
rule: modular frame system scaffold must be erected on a stable, level base with adequate bearing capacity
exceptions: purpose-designed suspended scaffolds where the frame is hung from overhead supports

subject: System Scaffold (Modular Frame)
rule: modular frame system scaffold must be restrained against lateral movement using ties or guys at intervals specified by engineering design
conditions: when the scaffold height exceeds four times its minimum base dimension
or when exposed to wind loading
exceptions: free-standing scaffolds designed specifically as self-supporting towers within a defined height limit per code

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: Mobile scaffold tower must have a base-to-height ratio that keeps the overall centre of gravity within the base footprint (typically 1:3 for outdoor use, 1:3.5 for indoor use) or be secured with outriggers/tie-ins
conditions: when erected on a level surface
exceptions: When the tower is tied to an adjacent permanent structure

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: All working platforms on a mobile scaffold tower must be fully decked with guardrails and toeboards on every open side
conditions: when platform height exceeds 2 metres

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: Mobile scaffold tower must not be moved while any person or material is on the platform

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: Mobile scaffold tower must be erected on a firm, level surface capable of supporting the design load without settlement
exceptions: When the tower is equipped with screw jacks or base plates on a prepared sub-base that compensates for unevenness

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: Mobile scaffold tower castor wheels must be equipped with effective brakes that are engaged whenever the tower is stationary and occupied

subject: Mobile Scaffold Tower
rule: The height-to-minimum-base-dimension ratio of a freestanding mobile scaffold tower must not exceed the manufacturer's specified limit (typically between 3:1 and 4:1)
conditions: when used without outriggers or tie-ins

subject: Suspended Access Scaffold (Cradle/Gondola)
rule: suspended access scaffold (cradle/gondola) must be supported by wire ropes or suspension cables attached to a roof-top anchorage or counterweight system
conditions: installed on building facade for access
exceptions: tied to building structure directly without roof anchorage

subject: Suspended Access Scaffold (Cradle/Gondola)
rule: suspended access scaffold (cradle/gondola) must not exceed the safe working load (SWL) specified by the manufacturer
conditions: during operation with personnel, tools, and materials

subject: Suspended Access Scaffold (Cradle/Gondola)
rule: suspended access scaffold (cradle/gondola) must have a secondary safety rope (independent fall-arrest line) attached to the cradle and to a separate anchorage
conditions: when personnel occupy the cradle

subject: Suspended Access Scaffold (Cradle/Gondola)
rule: suspended access scaffold (cradle/gondola) must not be operated in wind speeds exceeding the manufacturer's rated limit
conditions: during outdoor use on building exterior

subject: Suspended Access Scaffold (Cradle/Gondola)
rule: roof-top anchorage or counterweight system for the suspended access scaffold must have a safety factor of at least 4:1 against overturning or uplift
conditions: when scaffold is installed and loaded

subject: Shoring/Falsework Scaffold
rule: shoring/falsework scaffold must be designed to support all anticipated construction loads (dead, live, wind, seismic, concrete placement, equipment, personnel) without instability or collapse
conditions: during construction

subject: Shoring/Falsework Scaffold
rule: shoring/falsework scaffold must not be removed until the permanent structure has gained sufficient strength to be self-supporting
exceptions: if engineered sequential stripping is explicitly designed and approved

subject: Shoring/Falsework Scaffold
rule: shoring/falsework scaffold must bear on stable ground or a structural base capable of supporting the imposed loads without excessive settlement

subject: Shoring/Falsework Scaffold
rule: shoring/falsework scaffold must not be subjected to lateral loads for which it was not designed

subject: Shoring/Falsework Scaffold
rule: shoring/falsework scaffold must be designed with adequate bracing to prevent buckling of individual members and overall system instability

subject: Scaffold Base Plates & Jacks
rule: base plates must distribute scaffold load to a minimum bearing area sufficient to prevent soil or surface failure
conditions: scaffold is erected on compressible ground or non-structural surface
exceptions: scaffold is supported on a structural slab designed to take the point loads without a plate

subject: Scaffold Base Plates & Jacks
rule: adjustment jacks must not be extended beyond their maximum rated extension length
conditions: scaffold is in use under design loads

subject: Scaffold Base Plates & Jacks
rule: base plate and jack assembly must be concentric with the vertical scaffold standard
conditions: scaffold supports load-bearing vertical members

subject: Scaffold Base Plates & Jacks
rule: base jack threads must not be visibly damaged, bent, or corroded beyond serviceability limits
conditions: scaffold is in use

subject: Scaffold Couplers & Clamps
rule: scaffold coupler or clamp must develop and sustain its rated load capacity without slip, deformation, or fracture under rated working load
conditions: when used in a scaffold structure
under rated load conditions

subject: Scaffold Couplers & Clamps
rule: scaffold coupler or clamp must not permit disengagement or loosening under cyclic or dynamic loading unless mechanically locked
conditions: during scaffold erection, use, or dismantling
exceptions: intentional adjustment by a competent person with a tool

subject: Scaffold Couplers & Clamps
rule: scaffold coupler or clamp must be made of material with documented yield strength and ductility suitable for the intended load and environmental exposure
conditions: when used in load-bearing scaffold applications

subject: Scaffold Couplers & Clamps
rule: scaffold coupler or clamp geometry must provide a secure fit on the nominal tube diameter it is designed for, without excessive play or the need for shims
conditions: when assembled on standard scaffold tube

subject: Scaffold Ledgers & Transoms
rule: scaffold ledgers and transoms must be horizontal when installed
conditions: when used in tubular scaffolding systems

subject: Scaffold Ledgers & Transoms
rule: scaffold ledgers and transoms must not be removed from a bay while the platform above is in use or loaded
conditions: where a working platform is erected on the scaffold
exceptions: during controlled progressive dismantling sequenced from top to bottom

subject: Scaffold Ledgers & Transoms
rule: scaffold ledgers and transoms must be secured against lateral displacement at each end
conditions: when used in tube-and-coupler scaffolding

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: guardrails must have a top rail height between 900 mm and 1100 mm above the working platform
conditions: when used as fall protection on scaffolding

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: guardrails must have a mid-rail or equivalent intermediate barrier
conditions: when guardrail height exceeds 900 mm

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: toe boards must be at least 150 mm in height
conditions: when installed on scaffold platforms

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: guardrails must not have openings through which a person could fall
conditions: when used as fall protection

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: guardrails and toe boards must be attached to scaffolding standards or ledgers
conditions: when installed on tubular steel scaffolding

subject: Scaffold Guardrails & Toe Boards
rule: toe boards must be installed along all open sides of the scaffold platform
conditions: where there is a risk of falling objects

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal & Cross)
rule: Diagonal and cross bracing must be installed in both tension and compression to provide lateral stability to the scaffold structure
conditions: scaffold height exceeds 4 times its minimum base dimension
scaffold is freestanding (not tied to a structure)

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal & Cross)
rule: Cross bracing must extend from ledger-to-ledger and standard-to-standard to form a rigid triangulated panel
conditions: scaffold is of frame or tube-and-coupler type

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal & Cross)
rule: Diagonal bracing must not be omitted on any lift where the scaffold platform height exceeds 20 feet (6 m)
conditions: scaffold platform height exceeds 20 feet (6 m)

subject: Scaffold Bracing (Diagonal & Cross)
rule: Bracing members must be securely fastened at each intersection with a coupler or equivalent connection rated for the load

subject: Scaffold Ladders / Stairs
rule: scaffold ladders must have rungs or steps that are evenly spaced and slip-resistant
conditions: ladder-type access
exceptions: engineered stair systems with closed treads

subject: Scaffold Ladders / Stairs
rule: scaffold stairs must have handrails on both sides
conditions: stair-type access with a rise greater than 2 feet

subject: Scaffold Ladders / Stairs
rule: scaffold ladder rungs must not be damaged, bent, or missing

subject: Scaffold Ladders / Stairs
rule: scaffold ladder must be secured against lateral movement at the top and bottom
conditions: free-standing ladder without an integrated scaffold frame attachment
exceptions: ladder permanently built into scaffold tower as part of the frame

subject: Scaffold Ladders / Stairs
rule: scaffold stairs must have a clear width of at least 18 inches between handrails
conditions: stair-type access

subject: Scaffold Debris Netting / Fans
rule: Scaffold debris netting must be securely attached to the scaffold structure at all connection points
conditions: when debris netting is installed on a scaffold

subject: Scaffold Debris Netting / Fans
rule: Scaffold debris netting must not have gaps exceeding the mesh rating of the netting material
conditions: when used for debris containment

subject: Scaffold Debris Netting / Fans
rule: Scaffold fans (debris catch platforms) must be designed to withstand the anticipated debris loading without collapse
conditions: when installed as a debris catch fan

subject: Scaffold Hoist / Gin Wheel
rule: Scaffold hoist / gin wheel must be securely anchored or tied to a structurally sound part of the building or scaffolding
conditions: when used for lifting loads on a construction site
exceptions: if the hoist is designed as a free-standing unit with a sufficiently ballasted base per manufacturer specifications

subject: Scaffold Hoist / Gin Wheel
rule: Scaffold hoist / gin wheel must not be loaded beyond its rated safe working load (SWL)
conditions: during any lifting operation

subject: Scaffold Hoist / Gin Wheel
rule: The rope or chain of a scaffold hoist / gin wheel must run freely through the wheel without rubbing against adjacent structure or sharp edges
conditions: during operation

subject: Controlled Descent / Chute System
rule: controlled descent / chute system must have a load path that transfers all operational forces (gravity, wind, deceleration) into the building structure
conditions: when installed as a permanent system
when used for human occupants or heavy cargo

subject: Controlled Descent / Chute System
rule: controlled descent / chute system must maintain continuous structural integrity along its entire length
conditions: when the chute is a fixed, enclosed shaft or tube

subject: Controlled Descent / Chute System
rule: controlled descent / chute system must not have any openings or gaps large enough for a person to fall through
conditions: when designed for human egress

subject: Controlled Descent / Chute System
rule: controlled descent / chute system must have a deceleration mechanism (e.g., brake, speed governor, friction control) that limits descent velocity to a survivable value
conditions: when used for human occupants

subject: Controlled Descent / Chute System
rule: controlled descent / chute system must be fire-rated or fire-resistant to match the building's egress pathway requirements
conditions: when the chute serves as a means of egress
when installed in a building requiring fire-rated exit enclosures

subject: Scaffold Tag & Inspection System
rule: Scaffold tag must be physically affixed to the scaffold structure at all times when the scaffold is erected and in use
conditions: scaffold is erected
scaffold is in use
exceptions: scaffold is being erected or dismantled under supervised work-in-progress conditions where a tag is temporarily removed to affix the next-stage tag

subject: Scaffold Tag & Inspection System
rule: Scaffold tag must be weather-resistant and legible under expected site conditions
conditions: scaffold is exposed to outdoor weather

subject: Scaffold Tag & Inspection System
rule: Scaffold tag must clearly display at minimum: inspection date, inspector identifier, and load rating

subject: Scaffold Tag & Inspection System
rule: Scaffold tag must not show a 'safe/approved' status when the scaffold has unresolved critical defects
conditions: scaffold has unresolved critical defects

subject: Living Wall System
rule: living wall system must have a waterproof barrier between the growing medium and the building structure
conditions: system is installed on an exterior building wall

subject: Living Wall System
rule: living wall system must not allow standing water to accumulate within the growing medium or drainage layer for more than 24 hours
conditions: system is actively planted and irrigated

subject: Living Wall System
rule: living wall system must have an irrigation system that distributes water evenly across the entire planted surface
conditions: system contains live plants requiring hydration

subject: Living Wall System
rule: living wall system must have structural attachment rated to support the fully saturated weight of the system including growing medium, plants, and retained water
conditions: system is mounted on a vertical surface

subject: Bioretention Planter
rule: Bioretention planter must have a functional drainage outlet (e.g., underdrain or connection to storm sewer) to prevent prolonged saturation and root suffocation
conditions: planter is lined or has low-permeability native soils
planter receives runoff from impervious surfaces
exceptions: planter is designed as an unlined infiltration basin in high-permeability native soils with no underdrain needed

subject: Bioretention Planter
rule: Bioretention planter must not be completely sealed at the bottom with an impermeable liner without an overflow or underdrain system
conditions: planter is enclosed on all sides and bottom by impervious material (e.g., concrete vault)
exceptions: planter is designed as a self-contained planter with integrated water storage and sub-irrigation system that allows controlled drainage

subject: Bioretention Planter
