rule: must have a powered ventilation or air exchange system
conditions: booth is fully enclosed with a door
occupant will be inside for more than 2 minutes
exceptions: booth has open top or grille providing passive airflow

subject: Acoustic Phone Booth
rule: interior surfaces must not create standing acoustic waves or flutter echo
conditions: interior is substantially parallel-walled

subject: Acoustic Phone Booth
rule: door must be openable from the inside without tools
conditions: booth has a door that closes fully
exceptions: booth is less than 0.5m deep and used only for standing quick calls with door ajar

subject: Acoustic Phone Booth
rule: must not have materials that produce significant volatile organic compound (VOC) off-gassing
conditions: booth is enclosed and lacks active fresh air ventilation

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Cloud
rule: acoustic ceiling cloud must be suspended from an overhead structural support (slab, beam, or roof deck)
conditions: when installed as a suspended acoustic element

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Cloud
rule: acoustic ceiling cloud must not be directly attached to a finished ceiling finish below (i.e., it must be independently suspended)
conditions: when intended to function as a free-hanging acoustic cloud

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Cloud
rule: acoustic ceiling cloud must have a maximum weight that does not exceed the load capacity of its suspension system and the supporting structure

subject: City Magic Entrance Canopy
rule: canopy must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot for positive drainage
conditions: if canopy has a solid roof surface
if canopy is not a fabric/stretch membrane structure
exceptions: canopy is designed as a green/living roof with engineered drainage layer

subject: City Magic Entrance Canopy
rule: canopy must be designed for local wind uplift loads per ASCE 7
conditions: canopy is attached to a building facade or freestanding
exceptions: canopy is entirely enclosed within a conditioned interior space

subject: City Magic Entrance Canopy
rule: canopy attachment to building structure must not compromise building envelope watertightness
conditions: canopy is attached to an exterior wall of a conditioned building
exceptions: attachment occurs at a non-weather-exposed interface

subject: City Magic Entrance Canopy
rule: canopy structural framing must not obstruct required emergency egress paths below
conditions: canopy is located above a pedestrian pathway
canopy is located above a means of egress

subject: City Magic Entrance Canopy
rule: canopy must have a minimum clearance of 7 feet 6 inches above pedestrian walkways
conditions: canopy overhangs a public or occupiable pedestrian path
exceptions: canopy structural depth can encroach if it maintains 80 inches minimum clear height at any point

subject: Urban Magic Atrium
rule: atrium roof must provide natural daylight penetration to occupied spaces below
conditions: space is classified as an atrium
roof is the primary overhead enclosure
exceptions: atrium is entirely artificially lit and certified for occupant wellbeing

subject: Urban Magic Atrium
rule: atrium roof and skylight assembly must resist wind uplift loads per code
conditions: roof contains glazed or skylight elements
building is located in a region subject to wind design requirements
exceptions: roof is a fully opaque non-structural membrane with no glazed openings

subject: Urban Magic Atrium
rule: atrium must not have unprotected openings connecting to adjacent floors that lack fire-resistance-rated enclosure
conditions: atrium connects three or more stories
adjacent spaces are occupied floor areas
exceptions: atrium and all adjoining spaces are protected throughout by an engineered smoke control system and automatic sprinklers per IBC §404

subject: Urban Magic Atrium
rule: atrium roof drainage system must be capable of handling the local 100-year storm event without internal overflow
conditions: roof area exceeds 200 sq ft

subject: Urban Magic Atrium
rule: atrium must have a means of egress path from the atrium floor level that does not require travel through the atrium itself to reach an exit
conditions: atrium floor is occupied by occupants not continuously supervised
exceptions: atrium floor area is less than the threshold requiring a second exit (per local code)

subject: Illuminated Facade System
rule: illuminated facade system must be electrically safe with proper grounding, IP-rated enclosures, and earth leakage protection
conditions: system is powered by mains electricity
exceptions: system operates solely on extra-low voltage (SELV/PELV) below 60V DC with no external conductive parts

subject: Illuminated Facade System
rule: illuminated facade system must not create glare hazardous to pedestrians or drivers
conditions: facade is adjacent to public walkways, roads, or vehicle routes
exceptions: glare is fully shielded by louvers or optical controls and luminance is below local regulatory thresholds

subject: Illuminated Facade System
rule: illuminated facade system must not exceed maximum allowable heat dissipation of the building envelope
conditions: luminaire housing is in direct contact with or embedded within combustible cladding material
exceptions: thermal modeling shows surface temperature remains below ignition point of adjacent materials with adequate safety factor

subject: City-Scape Rooftop Terrace
rule: rooftop terrace must have a structural load capacity rated for expected occupancy and equipment
conditions: used as occupiable space
includes furniture or fixtures

subject: City-Scape Rooftop Terrace
rule: rooftop terrace must provide a safe perimeter barrier (guardrail or parapet) at minimum code height
conditions: terrace is accessible to occupants
edge is at a height above grade where a fall could cause injury

subject: City-Scape Rooftop Terrace
rule: rooftop terrace must have a waterproof membrane system beneath the finished surface
conditions: terrace is built above habitable or conditioned space

subject: City-Scape Rooftop Terrace
rule: rooftop terrace finished surface must slope to drainage (minimum 1/4 inch per foot or as locally required)
conditions: terrace is exposed to precipitation or irrigation water

subject: Kinetic Art Installation Wall
rule: The wall must have a structurally sound mounting/framing system capable of supporting the static and dynamic loads of all kinetic components

subject: Kinetic Art Installation Wall
rule: All electrical components must be protected against moisture ingress to IP65 or equivalent rating
conditions: wall is installed outdoors or in a location exposed to weather or condensation

subject: Kinetic Art Installation Wall
rule: Moving parts must not create pinching, shearing, or trapping hazards accessible to users
conditions: wall is installed in a publicly accessible area

subject: Kinetic Art Installation Wall
rule: The kinetic mechanism must be fail-safe — it must stop or return to a safe position upon power loss or control signal failure

subject: Kinetic Art Installation Wall
rule: Wall fixings to the building structure must be rated for the maximum dynamic load including any wind-induced forces on moving elements
conditions: wall is attached to an exterior (façade) or interior structural wall

subject: Digital Street-Facing Display
rule: digital street-facing display must have a minimum brightness sufficient to remain legible under direct sunlight
conditions: display is installed outdoors
display faces direct sunlight exposure

subject: Digital Street-Facing Display
rule: digital street-facing display must be weather-sealed to at least IP65 ingress protection rating
conditions: display is installed outdoors
exceptions: display is installed in a covered, fully weather-protected alcove

subject: Digital Street-Facing Display
rule: digital street-facing display must not produce glare that impairs driver or pedestrian visibility
conditions: display is located near a roadway
display is within line-of-sight of vehicular traffic

subject: Urban Living Wall System
rule: Urban Living Wall System must have an integrated irrigation system that delivers water uniformly to all planted wall sections
conditions: when the system includes living plants
exceptions: when the system is designed as a modular tray system with capillary wicking that replaces active irrigation

subject: Urban Living Wall System
rule: Urban Living Wall System must not have continuous impermeable backing that traps water against the building envelope
conditions: when the system is attached to an occupied building exterior wall
exceptions: when the system includes an engineered waterproofing membrane and drainage cavity independently verified for moisture management

subject: Urban Living Wall System
rule: Urban Living Wall System must have structural attachment rated for the fully saturated weight of the planted wall
conditions: when the system is mounted on a vertical surface above grade

subject: Urban Living Wall System
rule: Urban Living Wall System must maintain a minimum air gap between the planted modules and the building facade
conditions: when the system is installed on an occupied building's exterior wall
exceptions: when the system uses a fully sealed insulated panel system with integrated drainage that prohibits moisture transfer

subject: Magic Lantern Light Wells
rule: light well must maintain a clear vertical path to the sky (no obstructions that block daylight entry from above)
conditions: when functioning as a primary daylight source for adjacent spaces

subject: Magic Lantern Light Wells
rule: light well must not have a fully opaque roof or cover that eliminates all daylight transmission
conditions: if the well is intended to admit daylight
exceptions: temporary shading devices that can be opened or removed

subject: Magic Lantern Light Wells
rule: light well interior surfaces must be finished with light-reflective (non-absorbent dark) materials to enable daylight penetration to lower levels
conditions: when the well serves spaces below the topmost occupied level

subject: City Fabric Curtain Wall
rule: curtain wall must be structurally anchored to the building's primary structure at each floor level
conditions: when spanning more than one story

subject: City Fabric Curtain Wall
rule: curtain wall must accommodate differential movement between the curtain wall frame and the building structure

subject: City Fabric Curtain Wall
rule: curtain wall must not obstruct required means of egress or fire escape openings

subject: Bus Bay
rule: bus bay floor surface must be level (slope ≤ 1%) to prevent bus tipping and passenger tripping
conditions: bus bay is used for passenger boarding/alighting
exceptions: temporary portable bus bays

subject: Bus Bay
rule: bus bay must have a minimum vertical clearance of at least 4.3 m (14 ft) to accommodate standard transit buses
conditions: bus bay is covered or has an overhead structure

subject: Bus Bay
rule: bus bay must not have a loading dock or raised platform that obstructs bus access
conditions: bus bay is at-grade for bus entry
exceptions: bus bays designed specifically for kneeling-bus loading systems

subject: Drop-off / Pick-up Zone
rule: drop-off / pick-up zone must have a vehicular access point connecting to a drivable roadway or circulation path
exceptions: zone designated exclusively for pedestrian or bicycle use

subject: Drop-off / Pick-up Zone
rule: drop-off / pick-up zone surface must be paved or hard-surfaced
exceptions: temporary or seasonal drop-off zones on compacted gravel where local code permits

subject: Drop-off / Pick-up Zone
rule: drop-off / pick-up zone must not block emergency vehicle access lanes or fire apparatus access roads

subject: Drop-off / Pick-up Zone
rule: drop-off / pick-up zone must have a minimum clear width of at least 2.4 m (8 ft) for a single vehicle lane
conditions: zone is designed for motor-vehicle use
exceptions: zones serving only bicycles or micromobility devices

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock floor must be sloped (typically 1-2%) away from the building to prevent water entry
conditions: outdoor or semi-enclosed loading dock
exceptions: docks with sealed lip seals and active drainage channels at the door threshold

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock must have sufficient vertical clearance for the tallest vehicle expected to use it

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock level must match the typical truck bed height of vehicles servicing the facility (typically 48-52 inches)
exceptions: docks equipped with adjustable hydraulic levelers that span the full height range

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock door must not open directly into an unconditioned exterior space without a seal or weather protection
conditions: dock located in climate zone with freezing temperatures or significant precipitation
exceptions: docks in temperate climates where goods are not sensitive to temperature or moisture

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock must have a minimum load capacity (floor rating) that exceeds the maximum axle weight of any vehicle using the dock

subject: Loading Dock
rule: Loading dock approach/pavement must be designed to support the fully loaded weight of the heaviest vehicle

subject: Delivery Bay
rule: delivery bay must have a vehicle-accessible opening (door or gate) large enough for delivery vehicles to enter
conditions: used for vehicular deliveries
exceptions: parcel locker / mail-only delivery room where only hand-carried packages are dropped off

subject: Delivery Bay
rule: delivery bay floor must be level with or ramped to match the typical delivery vehicle cargo bed height at the loading position
conditions: designed for loading/unloading from vehicles
exceptions: bays that use adjustable dock levellers or lift tables to bridge any height gap

subject: Delivery Bay
rule: delivery bay must be positioned on a building perimeter with direct external vehicle access

subject: Pedestrian Concourse
rule: pedestrian concourse floor surface must be slip-resistant
conditions: when the concourse is exposed to weather
or when it serves as a primary egress path
exceptions: temporary construction phases where barricades and alternative paths are provided

subject: Pedestrian Concourse
rule: pedestrian concourse must have a minimum clear width that accommodates emergency egress capacity
conditions: when the concourse serves as a means of egress as defined by applicable building code

subject: Pedestrian Concourse
rule: pedestrian concourse must not have a change in level that exceeds the allowable ramp slope without an intermediate landing
conditions: when the concourse is accessible to the public
exceptions: historic structures where equivalent facilitation is provided

subject: Bicycle Parking Area
rule: Bicycle parking area must have a minimum clear height of 2.1 m to allow user access and bicycle maneuvering
conditions: covered bicycle parking
exceptions: uncovered open racks

subject: Bicycle Parking Area
rule: Bicycle parking area must have a hard, stable, drained surface

subject: Bicycle Parking Area
rule: Bicycle parking area must not have steps or stairs on the direct access path from the public way to the racks
exceptions: where a ramp or lift of equivalent capacity is provided

subject: Bicycle Parking Area
rule: Bicycle parking area must have a minimum clear aisle width of 1.2 m between rows of racks for bicycle maneuvering
conditions: two-sided racks
racks arranged in rows
exceptions: single-row installation against a wall with access from one side only

subject: Bicycle Parking Area
rule: Bicycle parking area that is enclosed or located within a building must have unobstructed egress path width of at least 0.9 m to the nearest exit
conditions: enclosed
indoor location

subject: Waiting Area / Shelter
rule: roof must provide overhead weather protection (rain, sun)
conditions: the shelter is open on at least one side
the shelter is not a fully enclosed building
exceptions: structure is entirely below grade

subject: Waiting Area / Shelter
rule: floor must be elevated above adjacent grade or have a drainage system to prevent standing water
conditions: shelter is located outdoors
shelter is located in a region with measurable rainfall or snowmelt
exceptions: shelter is on a porous surface (e.g., gravel, decking gaps) that naturally drains
shelter floor is designed as a drainage surface with positive slope

subject: Waiting Area / Shelter
rule: must_not have unguarded drop-offs at circulation edges where floor level differs by more than 600 mm
conditions: shelter is accessible to the general public
shelter floor is raised more than 600 mm above surrounding grade
exceptions: edge is at a loading dock or service area not intended for waiting occupants

subject: Kerb and Bumper System
rule: kerb and bumper system must absorb low-speed impact without transferring damaging forces to vehicle structure
conditions: vehicle is in motion
impact speed is within design range (typically 5-15 km/h)

subject: Kerb and Bumper System
rule: kerb and bumper system must not exceed the vehicle's geometric envelope defined by regulatory body
conditions: vehicle is in standard operating configuration

subject: Kerb and Bumper System
rule: kerb height and location must not obstruct suspension articulation or steering lock
conditions: vehicle is a passenger car or light truck
exceptions: off-road vehicles with explicitly designed high-clearance bumpers

subject: Canopy / Weather Protection
rule: canopy / weather protection must resist wind uplift forces
conditions: when installed as permanent structure
when exposed to open wind conditions
exceptions: temporary or removable canopies not designed for wind resistance

subject: Canopy / Weather Protection
rule: canopy / weather protection must shed water away from building entry or occupied area
conditions: when positioned over an entrance
when positioned over an occupied exterior area
exceptions: canopy designed as decorative feature with no weather protection function and no occupied space beneath

subject: Canopy / Weather Protection
rule: canopy / weather protection structure must not accumulate snow load beyond design capacity
conditions: in climate zones with snowfall
exceptions: canopies with active snow-melt systems designed for snow removal
non-load-bearing membrane canopies designed to shed snow passively

subject: Vehicle Barrier / Guardrail
rule: Vehicle barrier / guardrail must have a minimum height to prevent vehicle override
conditions: when installed at a drop-off, roadway edge, or other location where vehicle containment is required
exceptions: temporary barriers used in low-speed, non-critical areas

subject: Vehicle Barrier / Guardrail
rule: Vehicle barrier / guardrail must be structurally continuous or properly anchored at each end
conditions: when used as a longitudinal barrier system

subject: Vehicle Barrier / Guardrail
rule: Vehicle barrier / guardrail must not have exposed blunt edges or protruding ends facing oncoming traffic
conditions: in any permanent roadside installation
exceptions: when end terminals or crash cushions are fitted to treat the blunt end

subject: Vehicle Barrier / Guardrail
rule: Vehicle barrier / guardrail must have a working width (lateral deflection under impact) that stays clear of any fixed hazard behind it
conditions: when installed in front of a rigid obstacle such as a bridge pier, sign support, or steep slope

subject: Residential Units
rule: Residential units must have an egress path to a public way or safe area
conditions: when occupied as dwelling spaces
when constructed as habitable rooms
exceptions: jail cells under direct supervision

subject: Residential Units
rule: Residential units must have at least one operable window or mechanical ventilation providing minimum air changes per hour
conditions: when the unit is enclosed and intended for sleeping or prolonged occupancy
exceptions: units with approved balanced mechanical ventilation meeting code

subject: Residential Units
rule: Residential units must not be located in a space with no natural or artificial lighting to safe circulation levels
conditions: when the unit is intended for occupancy during nighttime hours

subject: Residential Units
rule: Residential units must have a minimum ceiling height of 2.1 m (approx. 7 ft) over at least 50% of the floor area
conditions: when the space is designated as a habitable room per building code
exceptions: existing buildings where non-conforming height is legally grandfathered

subject: Common Amenity Spaces
rule: Common amenity spaces must have at least one means of egress (door or opening) that leads directly to a corridor, exit stair, or exterior.
conditions: Space is occupied by people
Space is enclosed by walls
exceptions: Spaces with floor area less than 50 sq ft (e.g., small phone rooms)

subject: Common Amenity Spaces
rule: Common amenity spaces must have a minimum ceiling height of 7 feet 6 inches (2.29 m) in habitable areas.
conditions: Space is designated as habitable (not storage or mechanical)
exceptions: Beams, ducts, or other obstructions projecting below the ceiling may reduce clear height locally, provided the reduced area does not exceed 50% of the room

subject: Common Amenity Spaces
rule: Common amenity spaces must have a floor that is structurally capable of supporting the intended live load (minimum 40 psf for assembly/social areas, 100 psf for fitness/weight rooms).
conditions: Space is located above grade
Space is intended for assembly, social gathering, or exercise use

subject: Common Amenity Spaces
rule: Common amenity spaces must have mechanical ventilation or operable windows providing minimum outdoor air delivery per building code.
conditions: Space is fully enclosed (no open sides to exterior)
exceptions: Spaces with all four sides open to outdoors (e.g., rooftop terrace without roof structure)

subject: Common Amenity Spaces
rule: Common amenity spaces must not have floor drains that discharge directly to the exterior grade without a trap or connection to the sanitary drainage system.
conditions: Space contains a floor drain
exceptions: Drains connected to an approved storm-water system

subject: Laundry Facilities
rule: laundry facilities must have a dedicated drainage system connected to sanitary sewer or approved greywater system
conditions: any laundry facility with washing machines or water-based equipment
exceptions: dry-clean-only facilities with no water discharge

subject: Laundry Facilities
rule: laundry facilities must have a floor drain or sloped floor to drain
conditions: floor is subject to water spills from machine loading/unloading or leaks
exceptions: facilities where all machines are on drip pans with dedicated pumped drains and no floor-level water exposure

subject: Laundry Facilities
rule: laundry facilities must have hot and cold water supply lines
conditions: facility contains washing machines that require both hot and cold water connections
exceptions: facility designed exclusively for cold-water-only commercial washers

subject: Laundry Facilities
rule: laundry facilities must not have electrical outlets or fixtures within the splash zone of washing machines or wash basins
conditions: any laundry facility with water-source equipment
exceptions: GFCI-protected outlets located per code-minimum horizontal and vertical distances from water sources

subject: Laundry Facilities
rule: laundry facilities must have adequate ventilation (mechanical or natural) to prevent humidity buildup
conditions: facility is enclosed and contains washing machines or dryers that emit heat and moisture
exceptions: outdoor or unconditioned laundry areas where moisture dissipates naturally

subject: Mail and Package Rooms
rule: Mail and package rooms must have a fire-rated enclosure with self-closing doors when opening directly onto a means of egress corridor
conditions: The room opens directly onto an egress corridor
The building is subject to IBC or equivalent life-safety code
exceptions: A sprinkler system throughout the building may reduce the required fire-rating in some codes (check local amendments)

subject: Mail and Package Rooms
rule: Mail and package rooms must have a minimum of one dedicated electrical receptacle for sorting/work surface area per local electrical code
conditions: The room contains any counter or sorting table

subject: Mail and Package Rooms
rule: Mail and package rooms must have a floor drain or a waterproofed floor if located above finished spaces and containing plumbing fixtures or ice-melt drip zones
conditions: The room is located above a finished occupied space
The room contains a sink, ice machine, or other potential water source

subject: Mail and Package Rooms
rule: Mail and package rooms must not have mail slots or package drops that bypass the building's fire-resistance-rated envelope
conditions: The building envelope has a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Approved through-penetration firestop systems listed for mail-drop applications

subject: Corridors and Circulation
rule: Corridors and circulation paths must have a minimum clear width of 0.9 m (36 inches) for accessibility
conditions: Applicable to all interior circulation spaces
exceptions: Single-family residential dwellings may have narrower corridors

subject: Corridors and Circulation
rule: Corridors must have a clear height of at least 2.1 m (7 feet)
conditions: Applicable to all interior circulation paths used for egress
exceptions: Existing structures with grandfathered lower heights under specific building code variances

subject: Corridors and Circulation
rule: Corridors serving as means of egress must be continuous and unobstructed to an exit
conditions: Corridor is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: Temporary obstructions during construction with approved alternative egress paths

subject: Corridors and Circulation
rule: Corridor doors must not reduce the required egress width when opened
conditions: Doors are located within the corridor and swing into it
exceptions: Doors in smoke barriers where building code specifically permits projection up to 50% of required width

subject: Corridors and Circulation
rule: Corridors must have a maximum travel distance to an exit as specified by building code
conditions: Corridor is in a building requiring fire-rated egress paths
exceptions: Buildings with NFPA 13-compliant sprinkler systems may have extended travel distances per code

subject: Building Core and Shell
rule: The building core and shell roof must have a drainage path
conditions: building has a roof
exceptions: buildings in arid climates where precipitation is virtually zero and roof design intentionally captures no water

subject: Building Core and Shell
rule: The building core and shell must be capable of transferring all vertical gravity loads (dead, live, snow) continuously to the foundation

subject: Building Core and Shell
rule: The building core and shell must be capable of resisting lateral loads (wind, seismic) and transferring them to the foundation

subject: Building Core and Shell
rule: The building core and shell must not have an unbroken thermal bridge that bypasses the insulation layer across the entire envelope
conditions: building is intended to be conditioned (heated or cooled)
exceptions: buildings with no interior conditioning requirements (e.g., unconditioned storage shells)

subject: Building Core and Shell
rule: The building core and shell must maintain structural integrity and stability under all design load combinations without progressive collapse beyond allowable limits

subject: Residential Unit Interior Finishes
rule: interior wall and ceiling finishes must have a flame spread index of Class C (0-200) or better per IBC/IRC requirements
conditions: applies to all residential unit interior finishes
applies to wall and ceiling surfaces
exceptions: finishes protected by an automatic sprinkler system throughout

subject: Residential Unit Interior Finishes
rule: interior floor finishes in exit access paths must be Class I or Class II per ASTM E648 (critical radiant flux >= 0.45 W/cm²)
conditions: floor finish is located in a corridor or path serving as an exit access within the residential unit

subject: Residential Unit Interior Finishes
rule: interior finishes must not emit VOCs exceeding regulatory thresholds (e.g., CDPH Standard Method v1.2) in occupiable spaces
conditions: finish is applied within an occupiable interior space
exceptions: unoccupied mechanical or service rooms

subject: Residential Unit Interior Finishes
rule: wet-area wall and floor finishes must be smooth, non-absorbent, and cleanable to prevent moisture intrusion and mold growth
conditions: finish is in a bathroom, shower, or similar wet area within the residential unit

subject: Residential Unit Interior Finishes
rule: interior floor finishes in kitchens and bathrooms must be slip-resistant with a dynamic coefficient of friction >= 0.50 per ANSI A137.1/A326.3
conditions: floor finish is in a kitchen or bathroom

subject: Unit Kitchen Systems
rule: Unit kitchen systems must include a means of safely containing and draining wastewater
conditions: system includes a sink or washbasin

subject: Unit Kitchen Systems
rule: Unit kitchen systems must have electrical systems rated for the wet/damp location conditions typical of a kitchen environment
conditions: system includes electrical outlets, switches, or appliances

subject: Unit Kitchen Systems
rule: Unit kitchen systems must not have gas appliances or gas supply lines in an unventilated enclosed space
conditions: system includes gas-powered cooking equipment or gas supply connections

subject: Unit Kitchen Systems
rule: Unit kitchen systems must have all food-contact surfaces made of materials that are non-toxic, non-absorbent, and cleanable
conditions: system includes countertops, sinks, or food-prep surfaces

subject: Unit Bathroom Systems
rule: Unit bathroom system must have a dedicated drainage connection to the building's waste plumbing stack
conditions: when the unit bathroom is installed as a prefabricated pod
when the unit contains a toilet, shower, or sink
exceptions: temporary or portable units that discharge to a holding tank

subject: Unit Bathroom Systems
rule: Unit bathroom system must have a water supply connection capable of delivering potable water at required flow rates
conditions: when the unit contains fixtures requiring water (toilet, shower, sink)
exceptions: units designed exclusively as dry toilets with no water-fed fixtures

subject: Unit Bathroom Systems
rule: Unit bathroom system must have waterproof wall and floor surfaces in wet areas
conditions: where surfaces are exposed to direct water spray or pooling (shower area, around sink, floor)

subject: Unit Bathroom Systems
rule: Unit bathroom system must not have electrical outlets or switches located within the defined splash zone of water fixtures unless properly rated (IPX4 or higher)
conditions: when electrical fixtures are present in the bathroom unit
exceptions: outlets rated for wet locations (GFCI protected and weatherproof cover) installed per code

subject: Common Kitchen and Dining Systems
rule: kitchen and dining exhaust systems must have a dedicated grease-removal path (hood, duct, and fire-suppression assembly) before connecting to any shared building ventilation
conditions: the system includes cooking equipment that produces grease-laden vapors
the system is connected to a building-wide HVAC or exhaust riser
exceptions: systems serving cold-food-only preparation (no frying, grilling, or broiling) where local code exempts grease ductwork

subject: Common Kitchen and Dining Systems
rule: kitchen grease ducts must not pass through fire-rated barriers without a listed fire-resistive enclosure or approved fire damper assembly
conditions: the duct penetrates a floor, wall, or shaft enclosure that is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: the duct is fully enclosed in a 2-hour fire-resistive shaft constructed per governing code

subject: Common Kitchen and Dining Systems
rule: common dining-area floor surfaces must be slip-resistant and cleanable, with floor drains pitched to drain, in any location where wet cleaning or spillage is routine
conditions: the dining area is used for sit-down or self-serve meals
the floor is subject to routine wet mopping or spill potential
exceptions: carpeted dining areas in low-spill settings (e.g., dry-crumb-only service) where local health code permits carpet

subject: Common Kitchen and Dining Systems
rule: common kitchen hot-water supply must deliver water at a minimum temperature of 110°F at every handwash sink and at least 120°F at the dishwashing machine supply line
conditions: the kitchen is used for food preparation and utensil/plate washing
exceptions: temporary or mobile food-service units that use point-of-use water heaters and are permitted under alternative health authority provisions

subject: Common Kitchen and Dining Systems
rule: fire-suppression systems for commercial cooking equipment must not share control or supply lines with non-fire-protection building systems
conditions: the system includes a hood-integrated or duct-mounted fire-suppression system (wet-chemical, dry-chemical, or water-mist)
exceptions: monitoring or alarm tie-ins to the building fire-alarm system that do not affect suppression-agent delivery or control

subject: HVAC Systems
rule: HVAC system must have a minimum clearance around outdoor condensing units for adequate airflow
conditions: mechanical equipment is located outdoors
system uses air-cooled condensers
exceptions: water-cooled systems with remote heat rejection

subject: HVAC Systems
rule: HVAC system must not have refrigerant lines that exceed manufacturer's maximum equivalent length
conditions: split-system configuration is used
refrigerant lines connect indoor and outdoor units
exceptions: systems specifically designed with oversized line sets and additional oil traps as approved by manufacturer

subject: HVAC Systems
rule: HVAC duct system must maintain minimum cross-sectional area proportional to airflow to prevent static pressure exceeding fan capability
conditions: ducted air distribution is used

subject: HVAC Systems
rule: HVAC system must not have return air plenums that are shared with combustion appliance spaces without sealed separation
conditions: building contains combustion appliances (furnaces, water heaters, boilers)
return air plenum is open to appliance room
exceptions: combustion appliances are direct-vent/sealed-combustion type with dedicated outdoor combustion air

subject: HVAC Systems
rule: HVAC system must have condensate drain line with adequate slope to prevent water accumulation in the drain pan
conditions: system produces condensate (cooling operation with dehumidification)
exceptions: condensate pump is installed with proper safety float switch

subject: Electrical and Lighting Systems
rule: All electrical wiring and connections must be properly insulated and rated for their intended voltage and current
conditions: For all electrical and lighting systems in any building

subject: Electrical and Lighting Systems
rule: Electrical systems must include overcurrent protection devices (fuses or circuit breakers)
conditions: For all branch circuits supplying power

subject: Electrical and Lighting Systems
rule: Lighting fixtures must not be installed in direct contact with combustible materials unless rated for such contact
conditions: Where combustible materials are present in ceilings, walls, or adjacent surfaces
exceptions: Fixtures explicitly rated and listed for contact with insulation or combustible materials (e.g., IC-rated recessed fixtures)

subject: Electrical and Lighting Systems
rule: Electrical systems must provide a low-impedance path to ground for fault currents
conditions: For all electrical systems connected to a power source

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: drainage piping must maintain a minimum slope of 1/8 inch per foot (1% grade) for waste and 1/4 inch per foot (2% grade) for soil lines
conditions: piping is gravity-fed
piping conveys wastewater or sewage
exceptions: piping uses an approved mechanical lift or ejector system
piping is a horizontal branch less than 6 feet serving a single fixture

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: drainage piping must be vented to prevent siphoning of trap seals
conditions: drainage system includes traps serving fixtures
exceptions: fixtures with integral trap-seal protection (e.g., some self-siphoning designs)

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: sanitary drainage system must not be directly connected to the stormwater drainage system
conditions: both systems are present on the site
exceptions: combined sewer systems explicitly designed and approved by local authority

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: drainage piping must be sized to handle the peak fixture unit load without surcharging
conditions: new design or modification of drainage system

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: drainage piping material must be corrosion-resistant for the intended waste type
conditions: piping conveys acidic, alkaline, or otherwise chemically aggressive waste
exceptions: piping is sacrificial and regularly inspected/replaced

subject: Plumbing and Drainage Systems
rule: cleanouts must be installed at every change of direction greater than 45 degrees in horizontal drainage piping
conditions: horizontal drainage piping is concealed or inaccessible
exceptions: temporary or non-permanent installations

subject: Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems
rule: Fire protection and life safety systems must comply with applicable building codes and fire codes (e.g., IBC, NFPA) governing their design, installation, and testing
conditions: system is installed in a jurisdiction that adopts or references such codes
exceptions: jurisdictions with no adopted fire or building codes

subject: Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems
rule: Fire protection and life safety systems must not be obstructed by other building elements that would prevent their intended operation
conditions: sprinkler heads, fire alarms, smoke detectors, or egress signage are present

subject: Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems
rule: Fire alarm and detection systems must have a backup power source to maintain operation during a primary power failure
conditions: system is required by code to provide emergency functionality

subject: Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems
rule: Automatic sprinkler systems must have a reliable water supply (municipal connection, tank, or pump) capable of supplying design demand
conditions: system is wet-pipe, dry-pipe, or pre-action sprinkler system

subject: Security and Access Control Systems
rule: security and access control systems must have a dedicated and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or backup power source
conditions: system includes any electronic locks, readers, controllers, or network-connected devices
exceptions: system is fully mechanical (e.g., key-operated locks only with no electronic components)

subject: Security and Access Control Systems
rule: security and access control systems must not be installed in locations where electromagnetic interference (EMI) from nearby equipment exceeds the system's specified immunity threshold
conditions: system includes electronic card readers, biometric scanners, or wireless communication components

subject: Security and Access Control Systems
rule: security and access control systems must have all exterior cables and wiring protected from physical tampering and environmental damage (e.g., in conduit or armored cable)
conditions: any wiring is run outdoors or in accessible/unsecured areas
exceptions: wireless-only systems with no external cabling

subject: Data and Telecommunications Infrastructure
rule: data and telecommunications infrastructure must have a dedicated grounding and bonding system per electrical code
conditions: when infrastructure includes metallic components
when serving as part of a structured cabling system
exceptions: fully non-metallic (e.g., all-dielectric) fiber-optic systems with no metallic pathways

subject: Data and Telecommunications Infrastructure
rule: data and telecommunications pathways must not be routed within 12 inches of parallel electrical power conductors rated over 480V unless separated by a grounded metal barrier
conditions: when cabling contains metallic conductors
when pathway runs parallel for more than 24 inches
exceptions: when both power and data cables are enclosed in separate continuous grounded metal conduit

subject: Data and Telecommunications Infrastructure
rule: data and telecommunications infrastructure must not create a flammable firestop breach when penetrating a fire-rated assembly
conditions: when cables, conduits, or pathways pass through any fire-rated wall, floor, or ceiling
exceptions: when penetration is sealed with a listed through-penetration firestop system rated to the same fire resistance as the assembly

subject: Loading and Service Areas
rule: Loading and service areas must have a minimum vertical clearance of 4.5 m (15 ft) to accommodate delivery trucks
conditions: area is used by trucks or large delivery vehicles
exceptions: area is designated exclusively for small vans or service vehicles with known lower height requirements

subject: Loading and Service Areas
rule: Loading dock floor must be level with or within ±2.5 cm (±1 inch) of the truck bed height when the truck is fully loaded
conditions: loading dock is present and designed for truck loading/unloading
exceptions: facility uses adjustable dock levelers that can compensate for greater height differences

subject: Loading and Service Areas
rule: Loading and service areas must not have step changes or level breaks in the path between truck parking and the building entry
conditions: area is designed for roll-in cargo or forklift access
exceptions: step is bridged by a permanently installed ramp or dock leveler rated for the equipment load

subject: Structural Frame and Floor Systems
rule: structural frame must resist all gravity loads (dead, live, snow) without exceeding allowable stress or deflection limits
conditions: building is occupied
building is subject to snow loads

subject: Structural Frame and Floor Systems
rule: structural frame must transfer lateral loads (wind, seismic) to the foundation without collapse
conditions: building is located in a seismically active zone
building is subject to significant wind loads

subject: Structural Frame and Floor Systems
rule: floor system must support its design live load without exceeding deflection limits that cause damage to finishes or components below
conditions: floor is accessible to occupants

subject: Structural Frame and Floor Systems
rule: structural frame and floor systems must not have discontinuities in load path (e.g., missing connections, unbraced members) that prevent load transfer

subject: Structural Frame and Floor Systems
rule: structural frame members must have adequate fire resistance rating per applicable building code
conditions: building is subject to fire-resistance rating requirements

subject: Foundation and Substructure
rule: foundation must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill capable of supporting design loads without excessive settlement
conditions: all buildings with foundations
exceptions: piles or deep foundations transferring load to competent strata

subject: Foundation and Substructure
rule: foundation bottom (footing base) must be placed below the frost penetration depth
conditions: buildings in climates where seasonal ground freezing occurs
exceptions: foundations designed with frost-protected shallow foundation methods per engineered thermal analysis

subject: Foundation and Substructure
rule: substructure drainage system must prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup against foundation walls
conditions: foundation walls retaining earth (below-grade basements or crawlspaces)
exceptions: foundations in free-draining granular soils where code allows omission of perimeter drainage

subject: Foundation and Substructure
rule: foundation must not be constructed on uncompacted fill or organic soil without complete removal or engineered stabilization
conditions: all buildings
exceptions: sites where geotechnical engineer designs a deep foundation system that penetrates through poor soil to bearing strata

subject: Foundation and Substructure
rule: reinforced concrete foundation elements must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement as specified by structural code for soil exposure
conditions: cast-in-place or precast concrete foundations in contact with soil

subject: Exterior Wall and Cladding System
rule: exterior wall and cladding system must resist wind loads

subject: Exterior Wall and Cladding System
rule: exterior wall and cladding system must provide a continuous water barrier

subject: Exterior Wall and Cladding System
rule: exterior wall and cladding system must allow for thermal expansion and contraction

subject: Exterior Wall and Cladding System
rule: exterior wall and cladding system must not trap moisture within the wall assembly

subject: Exterior Wall and Cladding System
rule: exterior wall cladding must be securely fastened to resist gravity loads (self-weight)

subject: Roofing and Weatherproofing
rule: roof assembly must have a continuous water-shedding surface
conditions: all roof assemblies
exceptions: green/vegetated roofs designed for water retention have controlled drainage rather than full shedding

subject: Roofing and Weatherproofing
rule: roof must provide a continuous air barrier at the building envelope
conditions: conditioned buildings
exceptions: unconditioned structures such as open shelters

subject: Roofing and Weatherproofing
rule: roof must not allow ponding water to exceed the structural design load
conditions: low-slope roofs with parapets or internal drains
exceptions: roofs specifically designed for intended ponding (e.g., certain green roofs with controlled drainage)

subject: Roofing and Weatherproofing
rule: roof membrane must be compatible with adjacent materials to prevent chemical degradation
conditions: all roof assemblies using sheet membranes
exceptions: systems where an appropriate separation layer is installed

subject: Roofing and Weatherproofing
rule: roof must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: roofs designed as sloped drainage surfaces
exceptions: roofs designed as cisterns/catchment systems where intentional water retention is the design goal

subject: Subculture Boundary Wall
rule: Subculture boundary wall must be structurally stable under its own weight and lateral earth/water pressures
conditions: When the wall retains soil or water on one side
exceptions: If the wall is purely decorative and not load-bearing on a site with no grade change

subject: Subculture Boundary Wall
rule: Subculture boundary wall must not be undermined by excavation or erosion at its base
conditions: When the wall is located adjacent to sloped terrain, water flow paths, or future excavation zones

subject: Subculture Boundary Wall
rule: Subculture boundary wall must have adequate drainage (weep holes or drainage aggregate) when retaining soil
conditions: When the wall functions as a retaining wall with soil backfill

subject: Subculture Boundary Wall
rule: Subculture boundary wall must not exceed its material's allowable bearing or lateral load capacity
conditions: Under all load conditions including wind, seismic, and soil pressure

subject: Exterior Canopies and Walkway Covers
rule: Exterior canopies and walkway covers must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot to ensure positive drainage
conditions: The canopy or walkway cover has a solid (non-perforated) roof surface
exceptions: The canopy or walkway cover is designed with a perforated/openslat roof that allows water to pass through

subject: Exterior Canopies and Walkway Covers
rule: Exterior canopies and walkway covers must be designed to resist wind uplift pressures per ASCE 7

subject: Exterior Canopies and Walkway Covers
rule: Exterior canopies and walkway covers must not trap snow or ice in a manner that creates lateral loads on supporting structure
conditions: The canopy is located in a region with design snow loads per the applicable building code
exceptions: The canopy is designed with a steep slope (≥ 45 degrees) or a low-friction surface that prevents snow/ice accumulation

subject: Exterior Canopies and Walkway Covers
rule: Exterior canopies and walkway covers must have a fire-resistance rating compliant with the building code when they are part of a means of egress or when they bridge between buildings
conditions: The canopy or walkway cover serves as a required means of egress path or connects two separate buildings
exceptions: Local building code provides an exception for open-sided walkway covers that meet specific area and distance criteria

subject: Subculture Boundary Ceiling
rule: Subculture Boundary Ceiling must be structurally capable of supporting its own weight and any imposed live loads without collapse
conditions: when installed as a finished ceiling component

subject: Subculture Boundary Ceiling
rule: Subculture Boundary Ceiling must have a fire-resistance rating meeting the applicable building code requirements for fire separation between subculture spaces
conditions: when the subculture boundary ceiling serves as a fire-rated separation between adjacent occupancies or compartments

subject: Subculture Boundary Ceiling
rule: Subculture Boundary Ceiling must not contain materials that shed hazardous fibers or particulates into occupied spaces below
conditions: when the ceiling is exposed to the occupied interior environment

subject: Subculture Boundary Partition System
rule: subculture boundary partition system must provide a continuous physical separation between distinct subculture zones
conditions: when used to separate distinct subculture or functional zones
exceptions: when designed as a permeable marker system specifically allowing cultural exchange

subject: Subculture Boundary Partition System
rule: subculture boundary partition system must not collapse under its own weight or imposed lateral loads
conditions: when installed in any occupied condition

subject: Subculture Boundary Partition System
rule: subculture boundary partition system must be constructed from materials that are compatible in thermal and moisture expansion
conditions: when comprising multiple material types at joints or interfaces

subject: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint
rule: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint must maintain continuous contact with both adjoining substrate surfaces along the full intended bond line
conditions: When installed as a sealant joint between different building materials or assemblies
exceptions: Joints designed as intentional separation gaps with no bond requirement

subject: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint
rule: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint must not be installed over a bond-breaking surface or contaminated substrate without proper surface preparation
conditions: When substrate is concrete, masonry, metal, or other common construction material
exceptions: Joints specifically designed as non-bonding or expansion-only sealant applications where bond is intentionally prevented

subject: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint
rule: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint must accommodate the full range of differential movement between the two subculture zones
conditions: Where the joint spans a boundary between two distinct construction assemblies or material types with different thermal or moisture movement characteristics
exceptions: Joints in strictly controlled interior environments with negligible differential movement

subject: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint
rule: Subculture Boundary Sealant Joint must not exceed its maximum designed joint width during service
conditions: Under any expected thermal, moisture, or structural loading condition

subject: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly
rule: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly must achieve a fire-resistance rating (FRR) compliant with applicable building code (e.g., IBC, NFPA 5000) for the specific occupancy and construction type
conditions: The assembly serves as a fire-rated separation between different occupancies, tenancies, or fire areas
The assembly is part of a means of egress or required fire barrier/enclosure
exceptions: When the building code allows alternative means of protection (e.g., automatic sprinklers reduce rating requirements) — but this is a code-permitted reduction, not an exception to the binary requirement of some rating

subject: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly
rule: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly must be constructed entirely from materials and in a configuration listed in an approved fire-resistance design (e.g., UL, Intertek, ASTM E119 listings)
conditions: The assembly is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: When engineered alternative designs are approved through a registered design professional and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction based on full-scale fire test evidence — this replaces the listing requirement with equivalent proof

subject: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly
rule: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly must not have unprotected penetrations, joints, or openings that exceed the allowable size or lack the required firestopping material
conditions: The assembly contains any through-penetration, membrane penetration, joint, or opening for utilities, ducts, or structural elements
exceptions: When penetration is protected by a listed through-penetration firestop system that maintains the required FRR
When the opening is part of a listed fire door or fire damper assembly also rated for the required FRR

subject: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly
rule: Subculture Boundary Fire-Rated Assembly must be continuous from the top of the foundation or floor below to the underside of the roof deck or floor above, including continuity through concealed spaces such as ceiling plenums
conditions: The assembly serves as a fire barrier, fire wall, or fire partition as defined by building code
exceptions: Where code explicitly permits terminating at the underside of a fire-rated floor/roof assembly that itself provides equivalent continuity

subject: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder
rule: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder must be installed on the warm side of the building envelope (interior side in heating-dominated climates, exterior side in cooling-dominated climates)
conditions: The assembly includes a vapor retarder layer
The climate zone is defined as heating-dominated or cooling-dominated
exceptions: In climates with very low humidity year-round, placement may be less critical

subject: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder
rule: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder must have a permeance rating of 0.1 perm (US) or less when tested per ASTM E96 (desiccant method)
conditions: The material is classified as a Class I vapor retarder
It serves as the primary vapor control layer
exceptions: Materials labeled as vapor barriers but meeting Class II or III thresholds are not subject to the 0.1 perm threshold

subject: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder
rule: Subculture Boundary Vapor Retarder must not be installed in locations where it creates a double vapor barrier (i.e., two low-perm layers on opposite sides of an assembly)
conditions: The building assembly is in a climate with significant seasonal moisture drive reversals
There is already another vapor retarder layer on the opposite side of the same cavity
exceptions: Assemblies specifically designed to accommodate or manage moisture between two vapor barriers (e.g., ventilated roof decks)

subject: Subculture Boundary Glazing System
rule: subculture boundary glazing system must maintain continuous separation between interior and exterior environments
conditions: when installed as part of building envelope
exceptions: intentional open-air designs where boundary is deliberately omitted

subject: Subculture Boundary Glazing System
rule: subculture boundary glazing system must have all glass panes fully captured within framing members under design loads
conditions: when glazed panels are present

subject: Subculture Boundary Glazing System
rule: subculture boundary glazing system must not permit water penetration under rated pressure differential
conditions: when rated for weather-exposed application
exceptions: intentionally drained systems that collect and redirect water are acceptable — the rule prohibits uncontrolled penetration

subject: Neighborhood Identifier Signage
rule: Neighborhood Identifier Signage must be structurally stable under expected wind loads
conditions: when installed outdoors
when elevation exceeds 1m above grade

subject: Neighborhood Identifier Signage
rule: Neighborhood Identifier Signage must have its primary information legible from the intended viewing approach

subject: Neighborhood Identifier Signage
rule: Neighborhood Identifier Signage must not obstruct required sight lines at vehicular or pedestrian junctions
conditions: when located near a street intersection
when located near a pedestrian crossing

subject: Neighborhood Identifier Signage
rule: Neighborhood Identifier Signage must not contain sharp protrusions or edges at accessible heights that could cause injury
conditions: when any part of the sign is below 2.1m above ground

subject: Neighborhood Street/Aisle
rule: Neighborhood Street/Aisle must have a minimum clear width to allow emergency vehicle access
conditions: where emergency vehicle access is required by code
exceptions: gated communities with alternative emergency access agreements
pedestrian-only streets with bollards that can be removed by emergency services

subject: Neighborhood Street/Aisle
rule: Neighborhood Street/Aisle must have a continuous path to a public right-of-way or equivalent egress route
exceptions: cul-de-sacs that terminate in an approved turnaround area with secondary emergency access

subject: Neighborhood Street/Aisle
rule: Neighborhood Street/Aisle must not have a gradient exceeding the maximum allowable slope for the design vehicle type
exceptions: short ramps less than the code-defined length that are explicitly designed as exceptions

subject: Neighborhood Street/Aisle
rule: Neighborhood Street/Aisle must have a surface that supports the design vehicle load without structural failure

subject: Neighborhood Anchor Element
rule: neighborhood anchor element must have structural connection to at least one primary load-bearing element of the building
conditions: when the element supports other components
when the element is part of the main structural system
exceptions: freestanding landscape anchor elements that are solely decorative and carry no structural load

subject: Neighborhood Anchor Element
rule: neighborhood anchor element must not block required egress paths or fire access routes
conditions: when located near building exits
when located along exterior circulation paths
exceptions: when temporary and removable per local fire code

subject: Neighborhood Anchor Element
rule: neighborhood anchor element must have a minimum setback from property lines as required by zoning
conditions: when located at or near the perimeter of the building site
exceptions: when a variance or zero-lot-line provision is legally granted

subject: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub
rule: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub must have a fully accessible path of travel from the public right-of-way to all primary entry points
conditions: located within a jurisdiction that adopts accessibility codes such as ADA or local equivalent

subject: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub
rule: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub must have a minimum clear floor area ratio for occupant load based on egress capacity
conditions: enclosed or partially enclosed space intended to accommodate assembly occupancy

subject: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub
rule: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub must not have a single means of egress when occupant load exceeds code-specified threshold
conditions: occupant load exceeds threshold defined by applicable building code for the occupancy classification
space is not sprinklered throughout

subject: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub
rule: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub must have a floor surface that is slip-resistant under expected wet conditions at entry and circulation paths
conditions: accessible to the public and exposed to weather or pedestrian traffic that may introduce water, mud, or debris

subject: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub
rule: Neighborhood Plaza/Hub must not have protruding objects that create a head-strike hazard in circulation paths below 80 inches
conditions: path is designated for pedestrian use

subject: Neighborhood Subzone
rule: Neighborhood subzone must be contiguous (non-disjoint) land area
conditions: When defined as a spatial zone within a neighborhood
exceptions: When explicitly defined as a distributed or non-contiguous zone (e.g., special overlay district with separated parcels)

subject: Neighborhood Subzone
rule: Neighborhood subzone must not extend beyond the boundary of its parent neighborhood
conditions: When the subzone is hierarchically nested within a defined neighborhood boundary

subject: Neighborhood Subzone
rule: Neighborhood subzone must not overlap with another distinct subzone of the same parent neighborhood
conditions: When multiple subzones are defined under a single neighborhood
exceptions: When overlapping subzones are explicitly allowed as part of a hybrid/mixed-use overlay designation

subject: Neighborhood Acoustic Separation
rule: Neighboring buildings must maintain a minimum separation distance determined by local noise ordinances and acoustic attenuation requirements
conditions: Buildings are in a mixed-use or residential zone
Local noise ordinances specify minimum separation distances
exceptions: When a continuous noise barrier of sufficient height and mass is installed between buildings
When buildings are designed with mechanical ventilation allowing full-time sealed windows

subject: Neighborhood Acoustic Separation
rule: Outdoor mechanical equipment must not be positioned such that its noise emissions directly face neighboring residential habitable spaces within the acoustic shadow zone
conditions: Site contains rooftop or ground-level mechanical equipment
Neighboring buildings have residential habitable spaces within 30 meters
exceptions: When equipment is enclosed in a sound-rated enclosure achieving at least STC 50

subject: Neighborhood Acoustic Separation
rule: A party wall or demising assembly between attached dwelling units must achieve a minimum sound transmission class (STC) rating per applicable building code
conditions: Buildings share a common wall (attached/townhouse configuration)

subject: Adjacent Road Right-of-Way Edge
rule: Adjacent Road Right-of-Way Edge must have a minimum setback dimension from the building face as specified by local zoning code
conditions: when the building is located on a lot fronting a public right-of-way
exceptions: if a variance or special permit has been granted by the zoning authority

subject: Adjacent Road Right-of-Way Edge
rule: Adjacent Road Right-of-Way Edge must not be obstructed by permanent structures or grade changes that block emergency vehicle access
conditions: when the edge is adjacent to a public road used for emergency response

subject: Building Envelope Line
rule: Building envelope line must be continuous (unbroken) to maintain thermal, air, and moisture barrier integrity
conditions: Where envelope line serves as a thermal/air/moisture barrier
exceptions: Joints designed with approved sealant systems and expansion joints that maintain equivalent performance

subject: Building Envelope Line
rule: Building envelope line must not have penetrations that bypass all barrier layers without a sealed assembly
conditions: Where envelope includes all barrier layers (air, vapor, water, thermal)
exceptions: Purpose-designed penetrations with listed through-wall flashing, seals, and thermal break assemblies rated for the specific condition

subject: Building Envelope Line
rule: Building envelope line must maintain structural continuity such that wind and seismic loads can be transferred across it without rupture
conditions: Where the envelope also serves a structural diaphragm or shear wall function
exceptions: Curtain wall systems where loads are transferred through connections to primary structure, not through the envelope plane itself

subject: Boundary Marker / Survey Monument
rule: Boundary marker / survey monument must be physically stable in its installed position
conditions: installed in ground or fixed location
exceptions: temporary markers used during active survey work where continuous monitoring is present

subject: Boundary Marker / Survey Monument
rule: Boundary marker must be durably identifiable as a monument (not ambiguous with natural debris or unmarked objects)
conditions: used for permanent boundary demarcation

subject: Fence or Wall Foundation
rule: fence or wall foundation must transfer loads to soil of adequate bearing capacity
conditions: foundation supports a loadbearing wall or fence

subject: Fence or Wall Foundation
rule: fence or wall foundation must have its bottom below the frost line
conditions: foundation is located in a climate with seasonal freezing
foundation supports a solid wall or privacy fence that could be damaged by frost heave
exceptions: foundation is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation techniques per code

subject: Fence or Wall Foundation
rule: fence or wall foundation must not be placed on uncompacted fill
exceptions: fill has been engineered and compacted to specified density and tested

subject: Train Station Platform
rule: platform surface must have a minimum slip resistance coefficient (e.g., wet Pendulum Test Value ≥ 40) to prevent passenger slipping
conditions: platform is exposed to rain or moisture

subject: Train Station Platform
rule: platform edge must be at least 305 mm (12 inches) from the nearest running rail face to maintain kinematic gauge clearance
conditions: platform is adjacent to an active railway track
exceptions: platforms with an approved on-track warning system or speed-restricted zone may have reduced clearance under engineering assessment

subject: Train Station Platform
rule: platform surface must not be more than 30 mm higher than train car floor entry height for level boarding
conditions: platform serves passenger trains with level-boarding design
exceptions: platforms at heritage or mixed-traffic stations where rolling stock is non-uniform may permit a greater step-up gap under operational control

subject: Train Station Platform
rule: platform must have a continuous even surface free of trip hazards exceeding 6 mm in height variation
exceptions: expansion joints and drainage channels are permitted if profiled to be traversable by wheeled mobility aids

subject: Bus Terminal / Transit Hub
rule: passenger queuing and waiting areas must have direct weather protection (roof/canopy) for at least 80% of the footprint
conditions: bus terminal serves regions with annual rainfall > 500 mm or snow climate
exceptions: terminal is entirely climate-controlled indoor facility with enclosed passenger holding areas

subject: Bus Terminal / Transit Hub
rule: bus berths and passenger boarding areas must have a vertical clearance of at least 4.0 m (13 ft) for the full length of the berth
conditions: terminal serves standard 12 m transit buses or larger intercity coaches
exceptions: terminal is dedicated exclusively to minibuses/vans with known max height < 3.0 m

subject: Bus Terminal / Transit Hub
rule: bus circulation roadways within the terminal must have a minimum centreline turning radius of at least 12 m (40 ft) for standard 12 m buses
conditions: terminal accommodates articulated or 12 m+ buses
exceptions: terminal uses only shuttle vans under 8 m length

subject: Bus Terminal / Transit Hub
rule: diesel or CNG bus refueling areas must have a fixed gas-detection and ventilation system interlocked with fuel supply shutoff
conditions: terminal includes on-site fuel dispensing for CNG or diesel buses
exceptions: terminal uses only electric buses with no on-site combustible fuel storage

subject: Bus Terminal / Transit Hub
rule: bus terminal passenger platforms adjacent to moving bus lanes must have a physical barrier or minimum 1.0 m setback from the edge of the bus lane
conditions: platform is at same grade as bus travel lane, with buses passing within 3 m of the platform edge
exceptions: platform uses a full-height wall or fence that separates passengers from the bus lane completely

subject: Light Rail / Tram Stop
rule: platform edge must maintain a minimum clearance from moving trains
conditions: platform serves boarding/alighting passengers
exceptions: station with platform screen doors where clearance is zero

subject: Light Rail / Tram Stop
rule: platform must not have a slope exceeding 2% in the boarding area
conditions: wheelchair accessible boarding zone

subject: Light Rail / Tram Stop
rule: overhead wire contact height must be between the minimum and maximum specified for the tram pantograph
conditions: overhead catenary power supply is used

subject: Light Rail / Tram Stop
rule: platform height must be within the vertical tolerance band specified for the tram fleet's step or floor height
conditions: platform is intended for level boarding
exceptions: retractable step systems on trams compensate for platform height variation

subject: Subway / Metro Entrance
rule: The entrance must not obstruct the public sidewalk or pedestrian right-of-way
conditions: entrance is located on a public street
exceptions: temporary construction with permits and approved pedestrian detour

subject: Subway / Metro Entrance
rule: The stair treads and landings must have a non-slip surface
conditions: entrance includes stairs

subject: Subway / Metro Entrance
rule: The entrance canopy or overhead structure must have a minimum clearance of 2.1 m (7 ft) above the walking surface
conditions: entrance has a canopy, portal roof, or overhead structure

subject: Taxi Stand / Ride-Share Pick-up Zone
rule: Taxi stand / ride-share pick-up zone must have a vehicular access point connecting to a public roadway or drop-off/pick-up lane
conditions: When designated as an active pick-up/drop-off zone

subject: Taxi Stand / Ride-Share Pick-up Zone
rule: Taxi stand / ride-share pick-up zone must have an accessible passenger loading area (curb or platform) adjacent to vehicle stopping position

subject: Taxi Stand / Ride-Share Pick-up Zone
rule: Taxi stand / ride-share pick-up zone must not have a roof or canopy that is lower than the minimum vehicular clearance height
conditions: When a roof or canopy is present over the zone

subject: Taxi Stand / Ride-Share Pick-up Zone
rule: Taxi stand / ride-share pick-up zone must be located such that vehicles can queue or stand without blocking through traffic lanes
exceptions: When the zone is designed as a purely dynamic 'kiss-and-ride' with no standing/queuing

subject: Bicycle Parking Facility
rule: bicycle parking facility must have a surface that is firm, stable, and level to prevent bicycles from tipping over
conditions: facility is intended for bicycle parking
exceptions: temporary/event-based parking on unpaved surfaces where bicycles are attended

subject: Bicycle Parking Facility
rule: bicycle parking facility must have each rack or stand that supports the bicycle frame at two points of contact
conditions: facility includes racks for long-term or overnight parking
exceptions: short-term/visitor racks where wheel-only support is acceptable for parking durations under 2 hours

subject: Bicycle Parking Facility
rule: bicycle parking facility must not have racks that support the bicycle only by the front wheel
conditions: facility is intended for public or multi-user bicycle parking
exceptions: none — wheel-only racks are universally discouraged by bicycle parking standards

subject: Bicycle Parking Facility
rule: bicycle parking facility must have a minimum aisle width of 1.2 m (4 ft) between rows of parked bicycles to allow access
conditions: facility has two-sided racks or parallel rows of parking
exceptions: single-row parking against a wall where access is from the opposite side only

subject: Bicycle Parking Facility
rule: bicycle parking facility must have a clear path from the street or building entrance to the parking area with minimum width of 1.0 m
conditions: facility serves as the primary bicycle parking for a building or site
exceptions: none — access path is required for the facility to be usable

subject: Pedestrian Bridge / Skywalk Connection
rule: pedestrian bridge / skywalk connection must have a minimum clear width to accommodate pedestrian flow and emergency egress
conditions: publicly accessible
exceptions: private maintenance-only connections

subject: Pedestrian Bridge / Skywalk Connection
rule: pedestrian bridge / skywalk connection must have a minimum vertical clearance (headroom) along its entire length

subject: Pedestrian Bridge / Skywalk Connection
rule: pedestrian bridge / skywalk connection must have handrails or guardrails on any open side where a drop of 30 inches or more exists
conditions: elevated above grade by 30 inches or more
exceptions: side that is fully enclosed by a wall to at least 42 inches height

subject: Pedestrian Bridge / Skywalk Connection
rule: pedestrian bridge / skywalk connection must have a slip-resistant walking surface
conditions: exposed to weather or moisture
exceptions: fully enclosed climate-controlled interior bridges with dry walking surface under all conditions

subject: Pedestrian Bridge / Skywalk Connection
rule: pedestrian bridge / skywalk connection must_not have a slope that exceeds the maximum ramp slope allowed by building code for accessible means of egress
conditions: intended for public or accessible use
exceptions: inclined walkways serving only maintenance personnel and not required to be ADA accessible

subject: Transit Information Display System
rule: The display system must be weather-sealed to IP65 or higher when installed in outdoor or semi-outdoor locations
conditions: installed in outdoor or semi-outdoor location
exceptions: installed exclusively in fully climate-controlled indoor environment

subject: Transit Information Display System
rule: The display system must not generate surface temperatures exceeding 60°C at any externally accessible point during normal operation
conditions: installed within reachable distance of transit passengers

subject: Transit Information Display System
rule: The display system's power supply must be protected by a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) when connected to a mains supply
conditions: connected to mains AC power supply
exceptions: system is low-voltage DC powered (e.g., Power over Ethernet or battery)

subject: Fare Gate / Turnstile Assembly
rule: fare gate / turnstile assembly must have a minimum clear passage width that accommodates the design's intended wheelchair-accessible path (typically ≥ 32 inches / 815 mm clear between barriers)
conditions: when the assembly is installed in a location required to be ADA compliant or equivalent accessibility standard
exceptions: when installed in a non-public, secured staff-only egress path not subject to accessibility codes

subject: Fare Gate / Turnstile Assembly
rule: fare gate / turnstile assembly must not have a rotating arm or barrier that can trap a person between the moving element and a fixed structure (crush/shear hazard)
conditions: when the assembly includes any powered or spring-return rotating barrier element

subject: Fare Gate / Turnstile Assembly
rule: fare gate / turnstile assembly must have a fail-safe unlock or break-away mode in the direction of egress upon power loss or fire alarm
conditions: when the assembly is installed along a means of egress path
exceptions: when the gate is not on a required egress path and building code permits secured egress with special locking arrangements

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: roof must have a drainage path
conditions: shelter has a roof
exceptions: roof surface is permeable to the extent that water passes through without pooling

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: shelter must resist wind uplift forces
conditions: shelter is freestanding or roofed

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: glazing or transparent panels must be safety-rated or shielded from impact
conditions: shelter incorporates glass or rigid transparent panels at levels reachable by the public
exceptions: panels are fully guarded by a structural barrier that prevents any human contact or impact

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: shelter must not have unvented gas or combustion appliance enclosures without combustion air supply
conditions: shelter encloses any gas-fired or combustion equipment
exceptions: no combustion equipment is present in the shelter

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: shelter foundation or base must prevent overturning under design wind and live loads
conditions: shelter is permanently installed on a foundation or pad
exceptions: shelter is intentionally temporary and anchored by ballast only on a flat surface with no uplift risk

subject: Public Transportation Shelter / Canopy
rule: shelter must have a means to prevent entrapment or pinch points in moving or folding components
conditions: shelter includes any movable panels, folding doors, or adjustable louvers

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must have direct pedestrian access to at least one transit station or stop

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must have a hardscape surface capable of supporting pedestrian and bicycle traffic in all weather conditions

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must not have permanent vehicular traffic lanes crossing the primary pedestrian pathway between the plaza and the transit entrance
exceptions: if the crossing is controlled by a signalized crosswalk with pedestrian phase and curb extensions that reduce crossing distance to less than 6 meters

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must provide a minimum clear width of 1.8 meters on all accessible routes through the plaza

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must have a surface slope not exceeding 5% (1:20) in any direction along accessible paths
exceptions: where a ramp is provided as an alternative accessible route meeting all applicable accessibility code requirements

subject: Transit-Oriented Plaza
rule: transit-oriented plaza must not have unenclosed drop-offs or level changes exceeding 0.3 meters without guardrails or barriers
exceptions: where the drop-off is at the edge of a planted bioswale or water feature with a maximum depth of 0.45 meters and a bottom surface that prevents injury on impact

subject: Elevated Guideway Support Structure
rule: Elevated guideway support structure must transfer all vertical loads from the guideway to the foundation without exceeding allowable bearing capacity or causing differential settlement
conditions: guideway is in service

subject: Elevated Guideway Support Structure
rule: Elevated guideway support structure must maintain a minimum clearance envelope below the guideway for the intended passage of road vehicles, pedestrians, or rail traffic
