conditions: guideway crosses over another transportation corridor or public space

subject: Elevated Guideway Support Structure
rule: Elevated guideway support structure must resist overturning and sliding under the most critical combination of wind, seismic, and service loads without reliance on passive soil resistance beyond what is reliably mobilizable

subject: Elevated Guideway Support Structure
rule: Elevated guideway support structure must not have any component that fails in fatigue under the design cyclic loading within the specified design life
conditions: structure is of steel or has welded connections
structure is subject to repeated traffic or wind loading cycles
exceptions: components designed as sacrificial or replaceable with inspection intervals that detect cracks before critical size

subject: Elevated Guideway Support Structure
rule: Elevated guideway support structure must be laterally braced against buckling of slender compression members under all design load combinations
conditions: structure uses slender columns, struts, or truss members in compression

subject: Transit Signal Priority System Interface
rule: Transit Signal Priority System Interface must use a standardized communication protocol (e.g., NTCIP 1211 or equivalent) to interface with traffic signal controllers
conditions: when deployed in a signalized corridor with existing traffic management infrastructure
exceptions: proprietary protocols may be used if the traffic signal controller manufacturer explicitly supports no other protocol and a protocol converter is physically impossible to integrate

subject: Transit Signal Priority System Interface
rule: Transit Signal Priority System Interface must not inject a priority request that conflicts with the traffic signal controller's safety-critical timing functions
conditions: when the traffic signal controller is actively serving a pedestrian clearance interval
when the traffic signal controller is in a preemption state (e.g., emergency vehicle preemption)
when the phase being requested has a minimum green time that has not yet been satisfied

subject: Multi-Modal Wayfinding Signage
rule: Multi-modal wayfinding signage must be legible under all expected ambient lighting conditions
conditions: when signage is installed in publicly accessible areas

subject: Multi-Modal Wayfinding Signage
rule: Multi-modal wayfinding signage must not use only color to convey critical information
conditions: when used in contexts where color vision deficiency (CVD) is prevalent among users

subject: Multi-Modal Wayfinding Signage
rule: Multi-modal wayfinding signage must have tactile and high-contrast visual elements for accessibility
conditions: when signage serves as a permanent directional identifier

subject: Multi-Modal Wayfinding Signage
rule: Multi-modal wayfinding signage must be placed at consistent decision points along a path
conditions: when signage is part of a coordinated wayfinding system
exceptions: single-building unidirectional corridors where destination is directly visible

subject: Multi-Modal Wayfinding Signage
rule: Multi-modal wayfinding signage must not have protruding elements that create a head-strike or trip hazard
conditions: when mounted in egress paths or corridors with less than 80 inches (2032 mm) clearance

subject: Transit Operator Staff Booth
rule: staff booth must have a means of egress to a safe area outside transit tracks
conditions: booth is located on or adjacent to transit tracks
exceptions: booth is directly accessible to a station exit without crossing tracks

subject: Transit Operator Staff Booth
rule: staff booth must have a door that opens outward or is sliding to avoid obstructing the interior path in an emergency
conditions: booth is occupied by a single person
booth interior floor area is less than 15 sq ft

subject: Transit Operator Staff Booth
rule: staff booth must not have any unguarded opening facing active transit tracks within 3 ft of the track centerline
conditions: booth is located on a platform adjacent to tracks

rule: pit walls must have structural shoring or reinforced sides to prevent collapse
conditions: pit depth exceeds 1.2 meters
exceptions: pit is cut into stable bedrock and geotechnically certified

subject: Mini-bus maintenance pit
rule: pit opening must have a physical barrier or cover when not in use
conditions: pit is located in a vehicle or pedestrian traffic area

subject: Mini-bus maintenance pit
rule: pit must not have an enclosed confined-space configuration without ventilation and rescue provisions
conditions: pit has only one means of entry/exit
pit depth exceeds 1.5 meters
exceptions: pit is fitted with mechanical ventilation and a standby rescue system meeting confined-space standards

subject: Bus charging station (mini-bus)
rule: charging cable must be rated for the vehicle's charging power and current
conditions: electric bus charging
exceptions: wireless/inductive charging systems

subject: Bus charging station (mini-bus)
rule: protective earthing (grounding) must be provided at the charging point
conditions: conductive charging system

subject: Bus charging station (mini-bus)
rule: charging connector must be compatible with the bus inlet receptacle
conditions: plug-in charging configuration

subject: Bus charging station (mini-bus)
rule: station must not be sited where surface water routinely accumulates or floods
conditions: outdoor installation
exceptions: station designed to IPX6 or higher water ingress rating and all electrical components elevated above known flood level

subject: Mini-bus wash bay
rule: The wash bay floor must be sealed and waterproof to contain wastewater and cleaning chemicals

subject: Mini-bus wash bay
rule: The wash bay must have a properly sloped floor (minimum 1-2% gradient) directing water to a drainage system

subject: Mini-bus wash bay
rule: The wash bay roof must have a drainage path with appropriate capacity for local rainfall intensity
conditions: covered wash bay

subject: Mini-bus wash bay
rule: The wash bay must not have electrical outlets, switches, or fixtures within reach of water spray (minimum 1.5-2m horizontal distance from any wash zone)
exceptions: weatherproof/waterproof rated electrical fixtures (IP65 or higher) properly installed

subject: Bus bay floor drainage
rule: Bus bay floor drainage must have a continuous slope toward drainage outlets
conditions: Floor is designed to drain surface water
exceptions: Floor is designed with a pump-assisted drainage system

subject: Bus bay floor drainage
rule: Bus bay floor drainage must not have drainage gratings or covers that create a trip hazard for pedestrians
conditions: Pedestrian access or walkway crosses the bus bay floor area
exceptions: Area is strictly vehicle-only with no pedestrian traffic

subject: Bus bay floor drainage
rule: Bus bay floor drainage must be sized to handle the design storm runoff from the entire contributing catchment area
conditions: Drainage system discharges to a stormwater network or receiving environment

subject: Bus bay floor drainage
rule: Bus bay floor drainage must not discharge oil or hydrocarbon-laden water directly to the environment without treatment
conditions: Bus bay is used for fuelling, servicing, or parking of buses with potential for oil/hydrocarbon leaks
exceptions: Discharge is to a sanitary sewer with appropriate trade waste approval

subject: Mini-bus bay exhaust extraction system
rule: exhaust extraction system must be directly connected to the mini-bus bay exhaust outlet
conditions: when mini-bus is stationary within the bay
during engine idling or testing
exceptions: when bay is not in use

subject: Mini-bus bay exhaust extraction system
rule: exhaust extraction system must maintain negative pressure relative to the occupied space at all connection points
conditions: when system is operating

subject: Mini-bus bay exhaust extraction system
rule: exhaust extraction system ductwork must not have any openings or leaks between the vehicle connection point and the discharge point
exceptions: access doors that seal when closed

subject: Mini-bus bay exhaust extraction system
rule: exhaust extraction system must discharge to a safe outdoor location away from building air intakes, doors, and operable windows

subject: Mini-bus bay lighting
rule: lighting fixtures must be rated for exterior/damp location use
conditions: the mini-bus bay is an uncovered outdoor area
or covered but open on sides
exceptions: bay is fully enclosed and conditioned

subject: Mini-bus bay lighting
rule: lighting must not produce glare that impairs driver vision into or out of the bay
conditions: bay is adjacent to a roadway or vehicle circulation path

subject: Mini-bus bay lighting
rule: luminaires must be mounted at a height that prevents collision with buses

subject: Mini-bus bay fire suppression system
rule: fire suppression system must have a dedicated water supply or fire suppressant reservoir
conditions: mini-bus bay is enclosed or roofed
system is configured for automatic or manual activation

subject: Mini-bus bay fire suppression system
rule: fire suppression system must not rely on a utility water supply that can be turned off independently of the bay
conditions: system is a wet-pipe sprinkler or water-based deluge type
exceptions: system has a backup dedicated tank that provides full design flow for the required duration

subject: Mini-bus bay fire suppression system
rule: mini-bus bay fire suppression system must detect fire condition before or simultaneously with agent discharge
conditions: system is automatic or pre-action type
exceptions: system is purely manual (e.g., hose reel or portable extinguisher) and requires human judgment

subject: Bus bay rolling door
rule: Bus bay rolling door must have a clear sweep path free of permanent obstructions (e.g., columns, walls, kerbs) for its full travel length
conditions: The door is a sliding or roll-up type that moves horizontally or vertically along a track
exceptions: Doors designed as removable/barrier-type panels that are manually lifted out entirely

subject: Bus bay rolling door
rule: Bus bay rolling door must not reduce the functional clearance width or height below the minimum required for the design bus to enter or exit
conditions: The door is installed at the bay entrance/exit and closes off the bay opening

subject: Bus bay rolling door
rule: Bus bay rolling door in the closed position must be lockable/securable against unauthorised entry
conditions: The bay houses equipment or serves a space requiring security or access control
exceptions: Bays in fully supervised/continuously attended locations where physical locking is redundant

subject: Bus bay bumper rail
rule: Bus bay bumper rail must be positioned to prevent a bus from overrunning the boarding/alighting area
conditions: bus bay is in active use for passenger boarding/alighting

subject: Bus bay bumper rail
rule: Bus bay bumper rail must withstand the design impact load from a bus without structural failure
conditions: bus bay is designed for full-size transit buses
exceptions: temporary/light-duty installation with explicit speed and vehicle size restrictions posted

subject: Bus bay bumper rail
rule: Bus bay bumper rail must not protrude into the bus path or vehicle swept path envelope
conditions: bus bay has defined swept path for the design vehicle

subject: Bus bay bumper rail
rule: Bus bay bumper rail must have a continuous, snag-free surface without exposed sharp edges or projections
conditions: rail is at pedestrian-accessible height (typically < 2 m above ground)

subject: High-rise exemption threshold
rule: building height must be at or above the local jurisdiction's high-rise exemption threshold to qualify as a high-rise building
conditions: local building code defines a specific height threshold for high-rise exemption
exceptions: jurisdictions that do not define a high-rise exemption threshold

subject: Floor count (storeys)
rule: Floor count must be a positive integer

subject: Floor count (storeys)
rule: Floor count must not exceed the maximum structurally feasible storeys for the given structural system and site conditions
conditions: structural system is defined
site seismic/wind/soil conditions are known

subject: Floor count (storeys)
rule: Floor count must comply with the maximum storey height allowed by local building code for the occupancy type
conditions: local building code is applicable
occupancy type is defined
exceptions: building has special engineering justification and is granted a code variance or performance-based design approval

subject: Floor count (storeys)
rule: Floor count must be consistent with the means of egress design (sufficient stair/exit capacity for the occupant load at each floor)
conditions: building has more than one storey

subject: Sprinkler system requirement zone
rule: sprinkler system requirement zone must have unobstructed vertical clearance for sprinkler discharge
conditions: where sprinkler heads are installed

subject: Sprinkler system requirement zone
rule: sprinkler system requirement zone must not be enclosed by fire-resistance-rated construction that prevents sprinkler activation or water distribution
conditions: unless the enclosure is specifically designed as a sprinklered compartment

subject: Sprinkler system requirement zone
rule: sprinkler system requirement zone must maintain ambient temperature above 4°C (40°F) to prevent freezing
conditions: in locations subject to freezing temperatures
exceptions: dry-pipe or pre-action systems designed for freezing conditions

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress path must have a minimum clear width of 44 inches (1.12 m) for occupancy loads requiring two or more exits
conditions: stairwell serves occupancy loads requiring two or more exits
exceptions: buildings with sprinkler systems may reduce to 36 inches (0.91 m) per some codes, though this is jurisdiction-dependent and not universally accepted as physically valid

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress door must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: door serves an occupant load of 50 or more
exceptions: doors in dwelling units or serving fewer than 50 occupants in some low-hazard occupancies

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress door must not be locked from the egress side when the building is occupied
conditions: building is occupied
exceptions: doors equipped with panic hardware or fire-rated exit hardware that releases upon pressure

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress path must be illuminated to a minimum of 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux) at the walking surface
conditions: stairwell is part of a required means of egress

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: handrail must be continuous on both sides of the stairwell egress stair
conditions: stair has a total rise of more than 30 inches (0.76 m)
exceptions: private stairways in some residential occupancies

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress stair treads must have a minimum depth of 11 inches (280 mm)
conditions: stair is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: existing non-conforming stairs in historic buildings when approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress stair risers must have a maximum height of 7 inches (180 mm)
conditions: stair is part of a required means of egress

subject: Stairwell egress configuration
rule: stairwell egress walkway must be free of any obstruction reducing clear width below the minimum required
exceptions: temporary obstructions during construction with alternate egress path provided

subject: Building height measurement
rule: Building height measurement must be taken from the average grade plane to the highest point of the building
conditions: building height is being measured for code compliance or zoning
exceptions: buildings with sloped roofs where height is measured to the midpoint of the roof slope

subject: Building height measurement
rule: Building height measurement must not exceed the maximum allowable height established by the applicable zoning or building code
conditions: the building is subject to a zoning or building code with a maximum height limit
exceptions: height exemptions are explicitly granted for specific building features such as spires, chimneys, or mechanical equipment where the code permits

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must have a minimum width that accommodates the required egress capacity for the floor area served
conditions: building is served by the core
core contains stairs
exceptions: buildings with sprinkler systems may have reduced egress width per code

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must have doors that swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: core door serves an occupied space
door leads to an exit stair or exit passageway
exceptions: doors in dwelling units
doors serving fewer than 50 occupants

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must be enclosed with fire-resistance-rated construction
conditions: core connects more than two stories
building is of Type I, II, III, or IV construction
exceptions: open stairways complying with IBC Section 1011.12 for small buildings or spaces with sprinkler systems

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must not have any unenclosed penetrations that bypass the fire-rated enclosure
conditions: core is required to be fire-resistance-rated
exceptions: penetrations that are properly firestopped with approved materials

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must have landing areas at each floor level that are level and free of obstructions
conditions: core contains stairs

subject: Vertical circulation core
rule: vertical circulation core must have handrails on both sides of the stairway
conditions: stair width exceeds 44 inches (1120 mm)
core contains stairs
exceptions: residential dwelling units where one handrail may be acceptable if stair width is less than specified threshold per code

subject: Structural load path for mid-rise
rule: The load path from any structural element must ultimately transfer forces to the foundation without interruption
conditions: The structure is a mid-rise building (typically 4–12 stories)
Structural elements include gravity and lateral load-resisting systems

subject: Structural load path for mid-rise
rule: All lateral load-resisting elements (shear walls, braced frames, moment frames) must be adequately interconnected with diaphragms at each floor level to distribute horizontal forces
conditions: The building is subject to wind or seismic lateral loads
The mid-rise height range means significant lateral load accumulation

subject: Structural load path for mid-rise
rule: The load path must not contain a structural element with a capacity lower than the demand transmitted to it from elements above
conditions: Any element that is part of the primary vertical or lateral load path

subject: Structural load path for mid-rise
rule: Overturning forces in the lateral load path must be resisted by an interconnected foundation system capable of developing the required tension and compression reactions
conditions: The mid-rise building has a height-to-width ratio sufficient to generate net uplift at the foundation under lateral loads

subject: Mezzanine exclusion zone
rule: mezzanine exclusion zone must maintain clear vertical space free of permanent obstructions from finished floor to overhead structure
conditions: Where mezzanine exclusion zone is defined on floor plans
exceptions: Temporary decorative elements less than 300mm in projection

subject: Mezzanine exclusion zone
rule: mezzanine exclusion zone must not contain structural columns or load-bearing elements
conditions: When the zone is designated as part of a future mezzanine installation area

subject: Mezzanine exclusion zone
rule: mezzanine exclusion zone must have minimum floor area of 9 m²
conditions: Where building code requires a minimum area for a mezzanine to be classified as such
exceptions: Areas governed by alternative local codes with different minimum thresholds

subject: Floor-to-floor height
rule: Floor-to-floor height must provide minimum clear headroom of 2.4 m (8 ft) for habitable spaces
conditions: When the floor is part of a habitable room
Under typical building codes (e.g., IBC, IRC)
exceptions: Uninhabitable attics or crawl spaces may have lower clearance
Mechanical equipment rooms may have exceptions per code

subject: Floor-to-floor height
rule: Floor-to-floor height must accommodate the required structural depth between floors
conditions: When structural systems (slabs, beams, joists) are placed within the floor-ceiling assembly

subject: Floor-to-floor height
rule: Floor-to-floor height must not be less than the sum of minimum required ceiling height, structural depth, and floor/ceiling finish thickness
conditions: In any occupied building floor plate

subject: Floor-to-floor height
rule: Floor-to-floor height must be consistent within a single occupancy group or fire compartment to maintain compartmentation integrity
conditions: Where fire-resistance-rated floor assemblies are required by code

subject: Compact Parking Stall
rule: compact parking stall must have minimum width of 2.2 m and minimum length of 4.8 m (or local equivalent, e.g., 7.5 ft × 16 ft)
conditions: when designated for standard passenger vehicles
exceptions: when explicitly designated as a 'small car only' stall with lower minimum dimensions (e.g., 2.1 m × 4.5 m) per local code

subject: Compact Parking Stall
rule: compact parking stall must have a vertical clearance of at least 2.1 m (or local equivalent) if located within a structured parking facility
conditions: when part of a multi-level parking structure or covered parking area

subject: Compact Parking Stall
rule: compact parking stall must not have any fixed obstruction (column, wall, equipment) within its required clear zone
conditions: when measuring the stall's usable parking area
exceptions: wheel stops or curbs at the front edge are permitted

subject: Parking Space Markings
rule: Parking space markings must have a minimum width of 2.4 meters (standard parking space) for accessible perpendicular/angled parking
conditions: Applicable to standard perpendicular or angled parking layouts in jurisdictions following typical dimensional codes
exceptions: Parallel parking spaces
Compact car spaces where local codes explicitly allow reduced width
Motorcycle parking spaces

subject: Parking Space Markings
rule: Parking space markings must provide a minimum clear length of 4.8 meters for standard parking spaces
conditions: Applicable to standard perpendicular, angled, and parallel parking spaces for passenger vehicles
exceptions: Compact car spaces where local codes explicitly allow shorter length
Handicapped-accessible spaces which may require longer length per code

subject: Parking Space Markings
rule: Parking space markings must be at least 2.4 meters wide for accessible (handicapped) parking spaces
conditions: Applicable to designated accessible/disabled parking spaces
exceptions: Jurisdictions specifying larger minimum widths (e.g., 3.6m for van-accessible)

subject: Parking Space Markings
rule: Parking space markings must not overlap with fire lane markings or fire hydrant clearance zones
conditions: Applicable to any parking lot layout
exceptions: Temporary event parking with fire marshal approval

subject: Parking Space Markings
rule: Parking space markings must be visible (adequate contrast against pavement surface)
conditions: Applicable to all parking space markings

subject: Parking Barrier / Wheel Stop
rule: Parking barrier / wheel stop must be securely anchored to the ground or substrate to prevent displacement under vehicle impact
conditions: Installed in vehicular traffic areas
Expected to resist vehicle contact
exceptions: Temporary/portable wheel stops designed for repositioning

subject: Parking Barrier / Wheel Stop
rule: Parking barrier / wheel stop must not create a tripping hazard that exceeds allowable height above the finished pavement surface
conditions: Pedestrian access is present adjacent to or across the parking area
exceptions: Designs with chamfered/tapered edges that comply with accessibility codes

subject: Parking Barrier / Wheel Stop
rule: Parking barrier / wheel stop must be made of material durable enough to withstand repeated vehicle tire contact, weather exposure, and UV radiation without cracking or disintegrating
conditions: Installed outdoors or in unconditioned parking garages

subject: Parking Barrier / Wheel Stop
rule: Parking barrier / wheel stop must not impede required drainage flow across the parking surface
conditions: Installed on a sloped parking surface with surface drainage
exceptions: Wheel stops designed with drainage channels or gaps that maintain flow capacity

subject: Parking Aisle
rule: Parking aisle width must be at least 2.4 m (8 ft) for one-way traffic
conditions: standard vehicle access required

subject: Parking Aisle
rule: Parking aisle width must be at least 6.7 m (22 ft) for two-way traffic
conditions: two-way vehicle traffic allowed

subject: Parking Aisle
rule: Parking aisle must have a clear height of at least 2.1 m (7 ft)
conditions: indoor or covered parking aisle

subject: Parking Aisle
rule: Parking aisle must have a maximum gradient no steeper than 1:20 (5%) for the primary travel path
conditions: aisle is on a slope
exceptions: short ramps serving level changes may exceed this where explicitly designed as a ramp, not an aisle

subject: Parking Aisle
rule: Parking aisle must not have any obstruction protruding into the minimum clearance envelope

subject: Parking Surface Pavement
rule: Parking surface pavement must have a minimum cross-slope of 1% (1/8 inch per foot) for drainage
conditions: pavement is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: pavement is in an arid climate where drainage is managed by adjacent systems

subject: Parking Surface Pavement
rule: Parking surface pavement must have a minimum thickness adequate for the design vehicle load
conditions: pavement supports vehicular traffic
exceptions: pedestrian-only parking surfaces

subject: Parking Surface Pavement
rule: Parking surface pavement must not have standing water within 48 hours of a rain event
conditions: pavement is in a region with regular precipitation

subject: Parking Surface Pavement
rule: Parking surface pavement must be compacted to at least 95% of maximum dry density (Modified Proctor) for asphalt or 98% for concrete subbase
conditions: pavement is asphalt or concrete
exceptions: permeable pavement systems designed with different structural requirements

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station (Compact Bay)
rule: electrical supply cable must be rated for the charging station's maximum current draw
conditions: station has a fixed power rating

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station (Compact Bay)
rule: charging connector must be compatible with the vehicle inlet standard (e.g., CCS, CHAdeMO, Type 2)
conditions: station is intended for public or multi-vehicle use

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station (Compact Bay)
rule: grounding conductor must be continuous and bonded to the station chassis

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station (Compact Bay)
rule: charging station must not be installed in a location where standing water can accumulate around the base

subject: Parking Area Drainage System
rule: parking area drainage system must have a positive slope toward collection points or outlets
conditions: surface is paved
surface is impervious

subject: Parking Area Drainage System
rule: parking area drainage system must have collection inlets (catch basins or trench drains) at low points and intervals that capture design storm runoff
exceptions: parking area is designed as permeable pavement with full-depth subsurface storage and no surface runoff is permitted

subject: Parking Area Drainage System
rule: parking area drainage system must convey collected water to a lawful point of discharge (storm sewer, detention basin, or approved outfall)
exceptions: site is designed for complete on-site infiltration with no discharge

subject: Parking Area Drainage System
rule: parking area drainage system must not direct concentrated runoff onto adjacent properties or public rights-of-way in an erosive or flooding manner
exceptions: downstream conveyance is designed and approved to receive the flow

subject: Parking Area Drainage System
rule: parking area drainage system must have sufficient capacity to convey the design storm runoff without surface flooding exceeding allowable depth

subject: Roadway Pavement Layers
rule: Roadway pavement layers must be designed to prevent water infiltration into the subgrade
conditions: where pavement is subject to precipitation or groundwater
for flexible or rigid pavement systems
exceptions: permeable pavement systems designed for water infiltration

subject: Roadway Pavement Layers
rule: Roadway pavement layers must not have layer interfaces that trap water
conditions: between adjacent pavement layers
for any pavement structure with more than one layer

subject: Roadway Pavement Layers
rule: Roadway pavement layers must provide sufficient load distribution to protect the subgrade from overstress
conditions: for any roadway designed for vehicular traffic
exceptions: temporary unpaved roads

subject: Roadway Pavement Layers
rule: Roadway pavement surface layer must not have a cross-slope below the minimum drainage gradient
conditions: for paved roadways exposed to precipitation

subject: Roadway Base Subgrade
rule: Roadway base subgrade must have a California Bearing Ratio (CBR) of at least 3 for light traffic or 5 for moderate traffic
conditions: subgrade is in-service for vehicular traffic
exceptions: subgrade is replaced with a stabilized or engineered fill layer

subject: Roadway Base Subgrade
rule: Roadway base subgrade must be compacted to at least 95% of standard Proctor maximum dry density
conditions: subgrade is constructed from compacted earth materials
exceptions: site-specific geotechnical analysis demonstrates adequate performance at lower density

subject: Roadway Base Subgrade
rule: Roadway base subgrade must be free of organic matter exceeding 1% by volume in the top 300 mm
conditions: subgrade is natural soil used directly as a pavement foundation
exceptions: organic layer is removed and replaced with suitable fill

subject: Roadway Base Subgrade
rule: Roadway base subgrade must be provided with adequate drainage to prevent water saturation within 600 mm of the pavement surface
conditions: subgrade is in a region with an average annual rainfall exceeding 500 mm or with a water table within 1.5 m of the surface
exceptions: subgrade material is non-frost-susceptible granular material with permeability greater than 10^-4 m/s

subject: Roadway Gutters
rule: Roadway gutters must have continuous positive slope toward the outlet point to prevent standing water
conditions: Gutter is installed on a roadway
Gutter is intended to convey stormwater runoff
exceptions: Gutter is part of a level spreader or bioretention system designed to pond water intentionally

subject: Roadway Gutters
rule: Roadway gutters must not have a flow capacity less than the design storm runoff they are intended to convey
conditions: Gutter is designed to a specified storm recurrence interval (e.g., 10-year or 25-year event)

subject: Roadway Gutters
rule: Roadway gutters must not discharge concentrated flow onto an unprotected slope at a velocity that causes erosion
conditions: Outlet discharges onto soil or vegetated slope
Slope is not armored or stabilized
exceptions: Outlet discharges into a designed energy dissipator or stabilized channel

subject: Roadway Gutters
rule: Roadway gutters must be free of obstructions that block flow and cause localized ponding
conditions: Gutter is in service and expected to convey stormwater
exceptions: Temporary obstruction during planned maintenance with traffic control in place

subject: Roadway Curbs
rule: Roadway curb height must be between 4 and 8 inches above the pavement surface
conditions: Used in standard vehicular roadway applications
Poured-in-place concrete curb construction
exceptions: Mountable curbs used in low-speed residential or parking areas where vehicles must cross the curb

subject: Roadway Curbs
rule: Roadway curb must not have a vertical face height exceeding 8 inches without an appropriate transition or warning
conditions: Adjacent to pedestrian walkways or crosswalks
Vehicle travel speeds above 25 mph
exceptions: Protected medians with no pedestrian crossing
Areas with physical barriers between curb and travel lanes

subject: Roadway Curbs
rule: Roadway curb must provide a minimum 6-inch reveal at the gutter line to ensure positive drainage
conditions: Curb and gutter combined section
exceptions: Curb-only sections with separate drainage systems
Zero-reveal mountable curbs designed for sheet flow

subject: Roadway Curbs
rule: Roadway curb at driveway openings must be depressed or have a tapered transition no steeper than 1:4 slope
conditions: Residential or commercial driveway crossing
Curb type is barrier or standard curb
exceptions: Mountable curb designed for vehicle crossing
Alleys or service drives with designated low-speed access

subject: Roadway Drainage Inlets
rule: roadway drainage inlet must have a positive hydraulic gradient (downward slope) from the inlet to the outlet/discharge point
conditions: gravity-flow drainage system
exceptions: systems utilizing active pumping or siphoning mechanisms

subject: Roadway Drainage Inlets
rule: roadway drainage inlet grate must have openings sized to prevent pedestrian heel/tire ingress while allowing water entry
conditions: pedestrian-accessible location
vehicular traffic area
exceptions: non-traffic, fenced-off areas with no pedestrian access

subject: Roadway Drainage Inlets
rule: roadway drainage inlet must not be installed with the grate slope opposing the roadway cross-slope or longitudinal grade

subject: Roadway Drainage Inlets
rule: roadway drainage inlet must have structural capacity to withstand H-20 or HS-20 (or equivalent) vehicle loading without collapse
conditions: inlet located in vehicular travel lane or shoulder
exceptions: inlets in non-traffic areas such as medians inaccessible to vehicles

subject: Roadway Drainage Inlets
rule: roadway drainage inlet sump (catch basin) must have a watertight seal between the grate frame and the basin structure

subject: Roadway Stormwater Pipes
rule: roadway stormwater pipes must have continuous gravity flow path to discharge point
conditions: pipe system is designed for gravity drainage
exceptions: system uses pumped force main instead of gravity flow

subject: Roadway Stormwater Pipes
rule: roadway stormwater pipes must be sized to convey the design storm runoff without surcharging above the pipe crown
conditions: pipe is part of a minor storm drainage system
exceptions: pipe is explicitly designed as a surcharge-approved storm sewer with controlled pressurization

subject: Roadway Stormwater Pipes
rule: roadway stormwater pipes must not have standing water in sags or low points under dry-weather baseflow conditions
conditions: pipe is designed for dry-weather flow
system is intended to be self-cleaning
exceptions: low point is a designed sediment trap or sump with maintenance access

subject: Roadway Stormwater Pipes
rule: roadway stormwater pipes must have positive connection at every joint to prevent soil infiltration
conditions: pipe joints are below the groundwater table
pipe joints are in uncompacted fill
exceptions: joints are designed with flexible waterstop that does not require rigid connection

subject: Roadway Stormwater Pipes
rule: roadway stormwater pipes must not cross beneath the roadway at depths that compromise structural load capacity
conditions: pipe is installed under a vehicular roadway
exceptions: pipe is encased in a reinforced concrete protective structure or placed in a structural culvert

subject: Roadway Catch Basins
rule: Roadway catch basin must have a minimum 2-inch (50 mm) sump depth below the outlet pipe invert
conditions: Catch basin receives sediment-laden stormwater runoff

subject: Roadway Catch Basins
rule: Roadway catch basin grate must have an opening size no larger than the maximum allowable by local standards for pedestrian and bicycle safety
conditions: Catch basin is located in a pedestrian-accessible or bicycle-accessible area
exceptions: Catch basin is in a location with no pedestrian or bicycle traffic and is protected by barriers

subject: Roadway Catch Basins
rule: Roadway catch basin must not be placed such that its rim is above the surrounding pavement grade

subject: Roadway Catch Basins
rule: Roadway catch basin must have a minimum 0.5% slope on all connecting lateral pipes to the main storm drain
conditions: Catch basin connects to a storm drain system via lateral pipes

subject: Roadway Manholes
rule: manhole cover must be rated for traffic loading (e.g., H-20 or equivalent) when located in a roadway
conditions: manhole is located in a vehicular roadway
exceptions: manhole is in a pedestrian-only or non-traffic area

subject: Roadway Manholes
rule: manhole cover must be flush with the finished road pavement surface
conditions: manhole is in a paved roadway

subject: Roadway Manholes
rule: manhole must not be located at the low point (sag) of a roadway vertical curve
conditions: roadway has a vertical sag curve
exceptions: stormwater drainage is designed to prevent ponding and the cover is watertight rated for submerged conditions

subject: Roadway Utility Trenches
rule: utility trench cover must withstand roadway traffic loads
conditions: trench is located under a roadway or vehicular travel lane
exceptions: trench is entirely within pedestrian-only zone or roadside verge

subject: Roadway Utility Trenches
rule: utility trench must not create an open excavation across an active roadway lane without temporary bridging or backfill
conditions: trench intersects a roadway used by vehicular traffic

subject: Roadway Utility Trenches
rule: utility trench bedding must prevent differential settlement that damages adjacent roadway pavement
conditions: trench is within the roadway right-of-way and parallel or perpendicular to pavement edge

subject: Roadway Utility Trenches
rule: trench side slopes or shoring must protect against cave-in under roadway vibration loads
conditions: trench is open during construction
trench is in or adjacent to a roadway subject to traffic vibrations
exceptions: trench depth is less than 1.2 m in stable soil and no personnel entry is required

subject: Roadway Subsurface Utility Vaults
rule: vault structure must withstand full AASHTO HS-20 or HS-25 vehicular live load plus earth cover dead load without collapse or excessive deflection
conditions: vault is located within roadway or travel lanes
vault is subject to traffic loading
exceptions: vault is located in non-traffic area such as sidewalk or greenway with no vehicular access

subject: Roadway Subsurface Utility Vaults
rule: vault must have a watertight seal at all access openings (lid, hatch, cable entry ports) preventing groundwater and surface water ingress
conditions: vault is located below grade or in areas subject to groundwater or surface water runoff

subject: Roadway Subsurface Utility Vaults
rule: vault must not block or compromise existing subsurface utilities (storm drains, sanitary sewers, gas lines, water mains, electrical conduits)
conditions: vault is installed in an existing roadway with pre-existing subsurface infrastructure
exceptions: utilities are successfully relocated per approved engineering plans prior to vault installation

subject: Roadway Pavement Markings
rule: Roadway pavement markings must be retroreflective to ensure nighttime visibility
conditions: markings are installed on roads with nighttime traffic
exceptions: temporary markings for construction zones with daytime-only operations
markings on roads not open to public vehicular traffic

subject: Roadway Pavement Markings
rule: Pavement markings must not create a skid hazard for vehicles or bicycles
conditions: markings are applied to travel surfaces used by moving vehicles or bicycles

subject: Roadway Pavement Markings

Non-rock conditions

rule: shopping street ceiling must be fire-rated to maintain the required fire-resistance rating of the street as a means of egress
