exceptions: each cubicle has an independent ventilation duct not shared with other cubicles

subject: Sleeping Area Floor Finish
rule: Sleeping area floor finish must be slip-resistant
conditions: when finish is wet or polished
in areas accessible to barefoot occupants
exceptions: when floor finish is carpet

subject: Sleeping Area Floor Finish
rule: Sleeping area floor finish must not have sharp edges or protruding fasteners

subject: Sleeping Area Floor Finish
rule: Sleeping area floor finish must be cleanable and not harbor moisture or biological growth

subject: Day-Night Lighting Control
rule: day-night lighting control must maintain proper isolation between daylight sensing circuits and electrical lighting control circuits
conditions: when system combines both daylight harvesting and electric lighting control functions

subject: Day-Night Lighting Control
rule: day-night lighting control must not allow electric lighting to energize when daylight sensor indicates sufficient ambient light level
conditions: during occupied daytime periods
exceptions: override for emergency egress lighting

subject: Day-Night Lighting Control
rule: day-night lighting control must have a fail-safe state that defaults to minimum egress lighting level upon sensor or controller failure

subject: Structural System
rule: structural system must transfer all gravity loads to the ground through a continuous load path
conditions: any building

subject: Structural System
rule: structural system must resist lateral loads (wind, seismic) through a stable bracing or moment-resisting system
conditions: any building

subject: Structural System
rule: structural system must not have a horizontal span without a load-resisting element capable of supporting the intended design loads
conditions: any building

subject: Structural System
rule: structural system must maintain static equilibrium under all design load combinations
conditions: any building

subject: Structural System
rule: structural system must not have a tension-only element connected in a manner that cannot develop tension capacity
conditions: building with cables, rods, or other tension-only members

subject: Main Building Core
rule: The Main Building Core must have a means of egress (exit path) that leads directly to a public way or safe dispersal area
conditions: building is occupied by people
exceptions: building is under construction and not yet occupied

subject: Main Building Core
rule: The Main Building Core must be separated from adjacent spaces by fire-resistance-rated assemblies
conditions: building exceeds local code threshold for floor area or occupant load
exceptions: sprinklered throughout with code-permitted trade-offs

subject: Main Building Core
rule: The Main Building Core must not have penetrations in its vertical enclosure that bypass fire or smoke barriers
conditions: enclosure serves as a fire or smoke barrier
exceptions: penetrations are properly firestopped with approved materials

subject: Annex or Wing
rule: An annex or wing must have a direct means of egress to a public way or to an exit that leads to a public way
conditions: Building is classified as an assembly, educational, institutional, residential, or hazardous occupancy
Floor area exceeds allowable travel distance limits per building code
exceptions: When the annex or wing has no occupied spaces (e.g., purely mechanical or storage with limited access)

subject: Annex or Wing
rule: Structural connection between the annex/wing and the main building must accommodate differential movement (settlement, thermal expansion, seismic displacement)
conditions: Annex or wing shares a structural connection (expansion joint, common wall, or roof) with the main building
exceptions: Annex or wing is structurally independent with a full separation gap and no shared structural elements

subject: Annex or Wing
rule: An annex or wing connected to an existing building must not block or reduce existing required openings for light, ventilation, or egress
conditions: Annex or wing is attached along a wall that contains existing required windows, vents, or exit openings
exceptions: Existing openings are relocated or resized to meet code requirements elsewhere
The existing openings are no longer required because the space use or occupancy classification changes

subject: Annex or Wing
rule: Fire-resistance-rated wall or separation assembly must be maintained where an annex or wing adjoins an existing building
conditions: Annex or wing creates a new opening or connection through an existing fire wall, fire barrier, or fire partition
exceptions: Opening is protected with a rated fire door or fire damper assembly that matches the required fire-resistance rating

subject: Annex or Wing
rule: An annex or wing must have a continuous load path from the roof to the foundation
conditions: Annex or wing has its own roof and self-supporting structure (not fully cantilevered or hung from main building)

subject: Below-Grade Parking Garage
rule: below-grade parking garage must have active or passive waterproofing system on all below-grade walls and slab
conditions: garage is fully or partially below grade
occupied or used for vehicle storage
exceptions: garage in extremely arid climate with no water table and no soil moisture
free-standing above-grade structure with no below-grade portions

subject: Below-Grade Parking Garage
rule: below-grade parking garage must have mechanical ventilation system providing continuous air changes
conditions: garage is fully enclosed below grade with no natural ventilation openings to exterior
exceptions: small single-car garage with direct vehicle ramp open to exterior on one full side such that natural ventilation is achieved

subject: Below-Grade Parking Garage
rule: below-grade parking garage must have a drainage system to remove groundwater, stormwater, and wash-water from the lowest floor level
conditions: garage floor is below the surrounding water table or below grade where water can accumulate
exceptions: garage in arid region with zero water table and no precipitation drainage path to garage floor

subject: Below-Grade Parking Garage
rule: below-grade parking garage must not have habitable dwelling units or sleeping quarters
conditions: garage is classified as a parking structure under building code
exceptions: none under parking garage classification

subject: Below-Grade Parking Garage
rule: below-grade parking garage ramp or vehicle entrance must not have a slope exceeding 20% (approximately 1:5)
conditions: garage serves standard passenger vehicles, SUVs, and light trucks
exceptions: facility designed exclusively for small electric carts or golf carts with manufacturer-specified ramp tolerance

subject: Above-Grade Parking Structure
rule: Above-grade parking structure ramp slopes must not exceed 1:6.67 (15%) for passenger vehicles
conditions: Ramp serves passenger vehicle traffic
Ramp is part of required vehicular circulation within the structure

subject: Above-Grade Parking Structure
rule: Above-grade parking structure floor-to-floor height must be at least 7.0 feet (2.13 m) clear
conditions: Floor is designated for passenger vehicle parking
exceptions: Structures designed exclusively for compact cars may reduce to 6.5 feet (2.0 m) where local code permits

subject: Above-Grade Parking Structure
rule: Above-grade parking structure ventilation openings must provide minimum 5% of the total floor area distributed on at least two sides
conditions: Structure is open-air (not enclosed mechanical ventilation)
exceptions: Fully enclosed parking structures with engineered mechanical ventilation systems may substitute
Structures with approved smoke control systems per local fire code

subject: Above-Grade Parking Structure
rule: The driving surface of each parking level must have a minimum cross-slope of 1% for drainage
conditions: Surface is exposed to precipitation (open-air or semi-enclosed design)
exceptions: Fully enclosed conditioned structures with roof drainage only

subject: Central Plant / Utility Building
rule: Central plant / utility building must have a roof drainage system (e.g., scuppers, roof drains, gutters, or controlled overflow paths) to prevent ponding that could lead to structural overload or leakage into sensitive equipment spaces.
conditions: If the building has a roof with any slope or flat roof membrane
exceptions: None — all such buildings have a roof requiring positive drainage per code and operational safety

subject: Central Plant / Utility Building
rule: Central plant / utility building must not have floor drains or trench drains located directly above or immediately adjacent to critical electrical equipment (switchgear, MCCs, VFDs, controls panels) without a liquid-tight barrier interposed.
conditions: If the building contains exposed electrical equipment at or below the drain elevation
exceptions: If all electrical equipment is rated for wet locations and the drain is part of a designed wash-down system with sealed conduits and listed enclosures

subject: Plaza / Courtyard
rule: a plaza or courtyard must have a minimum slope of 1% (1:100) for surface drainage to prevent ponding
conditions: outdoor plaza/courtyard
uncovered plaza/courtyard
exceptions: covered plaza/courtyard with a separate drainage system below grade

subject: Plaza / Courtyard
rule: a plaza or courtyard must not have an elevation that causes stormwater to drain into adjacent building entrances or interior spaces
conditions: plaza/courtyard adjacent to building entrances
plaza/courtyard at a higher elevation than adjacent finished floor levels
exceptions: when a positive drainage swale, trench drain, or curb redirects water away from the building opening

subject: Plaza / Courtyard
rule: a sunken plaza or courtyard must have a mechanical drainage system (pumps or gravity drains) to remove accumulated rainwater
conditions: sunken plaza/courtyard
plaza/courtyard below the surrounding grade
exceptions: when the sunken area is covered
when the sunken area connects to a positive gravity outfall at its lowest point

subject: Landscape and Sitework
rule: site grading must provide positive drainage away from all building foundations
conditions: building is present on site
exceptions: engineered retaining walls and subsurface drainage systems are used that achieve equivalent waterproofing and structural protection

subject: Landscape and Sitework
rule: surface water (stormwater runoff) must not flow onto adjacent properties in a manner that causes erosion, flooding, or damage
conditions: site is developed with impervious surfaces (roof, pavement) that alter natural drainage
exceptions: a legal stormwater easement or shared drainage agreement is recorded and approved by local authority

subject: Landscape and Sitework
rule: landscape vegetation must not be planted within utility easements or directly over buried utilities
conditions: utility easements or buried utilities exist on the site
exceptions: plant species with root systems proven non-invasive and shallow are specifically approved by utility authority

subject: Landscape and Sitework
rule: finished site grade around building perimeters must slope away at a minimum of 2% (1/4 in per ft) for a minimum of 10 ft
conditions: building has a foundation that extends below finished grade
exceptions: site is constrained and approved engineered drainage swales, gutters, and waterproofing systems are designed to achieve equivalent foundation protection

subject: Plumbing and Sanitary System
rule: plumbing and sanitary system must have adequate pipe slope for drainage
conditions: system serves gravity-flow drainage
system includes horizontal drainage piping
exceptions: pressurized drainage systems (e.g., sewage ejectors) where flow is mechanically forced

subject: Plumbing and Sanitary System
rule: plumbing and sanitary system must have vent piping to maintain trap seals
conditions: system includes trapped fixtures
system connects to a building drainage system
exceptions: self-scenting or specially designed trap-priming systems
certain isolated fixtures in unoccupied industrial settings where sewer gas entry is not a hazard

subject: Plumbing and Sanitary System
rule: plumbing and sanitary system must not have cross-connections between potable water and non-potable or contaminated sources
conditions: system includes a potable water supply connection
exceptions: approved backflow prevention devices are installed at the point of cross-connection

subject: Roof System
rule: roof must have a drainage path (slope, gutters, scuppers, or internal drains) to prevent ponding water
conditions: roof is flat or low-slope (< 2% slope)
roof is located in a climate with precipitation
exceptions: roof is strictly an architectural canopy with no weather-exposed surface
roof is a temporary structure not intended to shed water

subject: Roof System
rule: roof must resist uplift forces from wind
conditions: roof is attached to a building in a wind-prone region
roof is not a ground-supported independent structure
exceptions: roof is a temporary shade structure designed to fail before its supports

subject: Roof System
rule: roof must not have unsealed penetrations larger than its waterproofing membrane can bridge
conditions: roof serves as a weather barrier
exceptions: roof is intentionally open (e.g., operable louvered roof, pergola)

subject: Lighting and Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting system must have a backup power source (battery, generator, or equivalent) that automatically activates within 10 seconds of utility power failure
conditions: applicable to emergency lighting as defined by building codes (e.g., IBC, NFPA 101)
exceptions: none — this is a life-safety requirement with no waiver

subject: Lighting and Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting system must provide illumination of at least 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux) along the path of egress at the floor level
conditions: applicable to means-of-egress paths in buildings covered by IBC/NFPA 101
exceptions: none — minimum illuminance is a hard code requirement for safe egress

subject: Lighting and Emergency Lighting System
rule: lighting system must not exceed the maximum allowable wattage or load specified for the branch circuit and overcurrent protection device
conditions: applies to all permanently installed lighting circuits
exceptions: none — exceeding branch-circuit ratings is a fire and shock hazard prohibited by NEC

subject: Lighting and Emergency Lighting System
rule: emergency lighting luminaires must not share the same branch circuit as general lighting unless specifically permitted by code (e.g., a dedicated circuit serving only emergency fixtures)
conditions: where emergency lighting is required per applicable building code
exceptions: code-permitted configurations where emergency and normal lighting share a circuit only if that circuit serves no other load and is protected against inadvertent shutoff

subject: Lighting and Emergency Lighting System
rule: lighting fixtures must have a minimum clearance from combustible materials as specified by the fixture's listing and marking
conditions: applies to recessed, surface-mounted, and track lighting
exceptions: fixtures specifically marked and listed for zero clearance (e.g., IC-rated recessed fixtures)

subject: Interior Finishes
rule: interior finishes must have fire-resistance ratings compliant with applicable building code requirements
conditions: building is classified as non-combustible construction
finish is on a required fire-resistance-rated wall, floor, or ceiling assembly
exceptions: finishes in single-family dwellings of limited size where code permits untreated materials
finishes protected by an automatic sprinkler system throughout where code allows reduction

subject: Interior Finishes
rule: interior finishes must not emit hazardous levels of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in occupied indoor environments
conditions: space is mechanically ventilated or naturally ventilated occupied indoor space
finish is applied to interior surfaces within the conditioned envelope
exceptions: unoccupied utility rooms or mechanical spaces with no human occupancy

subject: Exterior Cladding and Finish System
rule: exterior cladding and finish system must provide a continuous water-resistive barrier
conditions: building is enclosed
cladding system is of the type that requires a water-resistive barrier (e.g., non-load-bearing curtain wall, rainscreen, or adhered veneer)
exceptions: building is designed as an unconditioned open structure where weathertightness is not required

subject: Exterior Cladding and Finish System
rule: exterior cladding and finish system must not trap moisture behind the cladding surface
conditions: cladding is installed over a substrate or insulation layer
system is not designed as a direct-adhered single-layer finish
exceptions: system is specifically designed as a drainage plane with intentional vented cavities to allow drying

subject: Exterior Cladding and Finish System
rule: exterior cladding and finish system must be anchored to resist wind uplift and lateral loads
conditions: cladding is located in a wind-exposed zone (above ground level or in a region with design wind speeds exceeding 85 mph)
cladding panels or elements have significant surface area
exceptions: cladding is a low-rise single-story system in a sheltered location where code-wind loads are negligible (rare)

subject: Waste and Recycling Rooms
rule: waste and recycling room floor must be sloped to a floor drain
conditions: room contains wet waste or wash-down activities

subject: Waste and Recycling Rooms
rule: waste and recycling room must have a fire-rated enclosure with self-closing doors
conditions: building is served by an automatic fire sprinkler system
exceptions: room is in an open-air or unconditioned structure with no adjacent occupancies

subject: Waste and Recycling Rooms
rule: waste and recycling room must not have habitable spaces directly above unless floor is liquid-tight and fire-resistance rated
conditions: room contains compactors, wet waste, or recyclable storage

subject: Waste and Recycling Rooms
rule: waste and recycling room must have a ventilation system with a minimum outdoor air change rate
conditions: room is enclosed and indoors

subject: Waste and Recycling Rooms
rule: waste and recycling room must have a sealed, slip-resistant floor surface

subject: Common Corridor and Circulation Zone
rule: common corridor and circulation zone must have a minimum clear width of at least 900 mm (or per local code) to allow safe occupant egress and passage
conditions: served occupancy exceeds one dwelling unit
building is for public or commercial use
exceptions: single-family dwelling unit corridors where local code permits narrower width

subject: Common Corridor and Circulation Zone
rule: common corridor and circulation zone must be free of fixed obstructions that reduce the clear passage width below the required minimum
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress
exceptions: fire hose cabinets or standpipes recessed so they do not project into required clear width

subject: Common Corridor and Circulation Zone
rule: common corridor and circulation zone floor surface must not have a change in level exceeding 6 mm without a ramp or beveled edge
conditions: corridor is accessible to the public or required to be accessible under ADA or equivalent
exceptions: historic buildings where alteration would threaten heritage character and equivalent facilitation is provided

subject: Common Corridor and Circulation Zone
rule: common corridor and circulation zone must provide a clear path of travel to at least two separate exits when the common corridor serves a floor area above a certain threshold
conditions: floor area served exceeds the maximum allowable for a single exit per applicable building code
corridor is on a floor above or below grade
exceptions: dead-end corridors permitted in certain sprinklered buildings where code specifically allows

subject: Sheltered Drop-Off Canopy
rule: drop-off canopy roof must have a positive slope for water runoff
conditions: canopy is exposed to weather
canopy has a solid roof
exceptions: canopy roof is designed with an internal drainage system such as gutters and downspouts that collect and redirect water

subject: Sheltered Drop-Off Canopy
rule: drop-off canopy must maintain a minimum vertical clearance above the vehicular drive lane
conditions: canopy is located over a roadway or drop-off lane used by vehicles

subject: Sheltered Drop-Off Canopy
rule: drop-off canopy must not obstruct sight lines between drivers and pedestrians
conditions: canopy columns or screens are placed within the drop-off zone near crosswalks or pedestrian paths
exceptions: sight-line analysis demonstrates that visual obstruction does not exceed the acceptable threshold defined by applicable traffic safety standards

subject: Sheltered Drop-Off Canopy
rule: canopy structural support columns must be placed outside the vehicle travel path or be protected by impact barriers
conditions: canopy has vertical support columns
canopy is located over an active vehicular drop-off lane

subject: Partial / Mezzanine Stories
rule: partial / mezzanine stories must have a minimum clear height of 2.0 m (or as required by local building code) to be occupiable
conditions: if the mezzanine is intended for occupancy
if the mezzanine is not used exclusively for storage or mechanical equipment
exceptions: mezzanines used solely for storage with no regular human occupancy may have reduced clear height per applicable building code

subject: Partial / Mezzanine Stories
rule: partial / mezzanine stories must not exceed 33% of the floor area of the room or space in which they are located (or the applicable jurisdictional limit)
conditions: under typical building code definitions (e.g., IBC) that treat it as a mezzanine rather than a full story
exceptions: some jurisdictions allow up to 40% or define by other metrics; the specific local code limit supersedes

subject: Partial / Mezzanine Stories
rule: partial / mezzanine stories must have direct access to a means of egress (exit access stairway or ramp) that leads to an exit
conditions: if the mezzanine is occupied by more than a de minimis number of occupants
exceptions: very small mezzanines with limited occupant load as permitted by applicable code may have a single means of egress path

subject: Partial / Mezzanine Stories
rule: partial / mezzanine stories must have an open connection to the floor below (i.e., not fully enclosed) to retain mezzanine classification
conditions: when the space is required to be classified as a mezzanine rather than a separate story
exceptions: local code variances may allow partial enclosure with large openings

subject: Below-Grade Stories
rule: below-grade stories must have a waterproofing system on exterior walls and slabs
conditions: building contains below-grade occupied or habitable spaces
water table is at or above the lowest floor level
exceptions: structure is temporary with less than 6-month design life
below-grade space is unoccupied and non-mechanical (e.g., void space)

subject: Below-Grade Stories
rule: below-grade stories must be designed to resist hydrostatic uplift forces
conditions: water table is above the lowest floor elevation
soil type permits groundwater accumulation
exceptions: site has permanent dewatering systems that maintain groundwater below slab level throughout design life
structure is anchored to bedrock with verified tensile capacity exceeding uplift forces

subject: Below-Grade Stories
rule: below-grade stories must have gravity drainage or mechanical sump pumping to remove water that bypasses the waterproofing system
conditions: below-grade floor slab is below the local groundwater table or in a soil type with poor natural drainage (clay, loam)
exceptions: the waterproofing system is redundant and tested 100% impermeable (e.g., welded steel bathtub structure)
space is designed for periodic flooding (e.g., intentional floodable basement)

subject: Below-Grade Stories
rule: below-grade stories must not have habitable rooms without at least one means of egress that leads directly to the exterior or to an above-grade exit
conditions: below-grade story contains sleeping rooms, offices, or other occupied spaces intended for human occupancy
exceptions: building is fully sprinklered with NFPA 13 system and occupancy is less than 50 people per floor
below-grade story is served by two remote means of egress, one of which leads directly to outside via an areaway or stair
local building code explicitly permits scuppers or other alternative egress for the specific occupancy type

subject: Below-Grade Stories
rule: below-grade stories must not depend on gravity-only venting for combustion appliance exhaust — appliances must have power venting or direct exhaust to exterior
conditions: below-grade story contains fuel-burning appliances (furnaces, water heaters, boilers)
appliance relies on natural draft for exhaust
exceptions: appliance is sealed-combustion with direct intake and direct exhaust to exterior through a flue that rises above grade

subject: Ground Floor / First Story
rule: ground floor / first story floor structure must be designed to support all imposed dead and live loads from the spaces above it
conditions: building has more than one story
exceptions: building is a single-story structure

subject: Ground Floor / First Story
rule: ground floor / first story must be at or above the design flood elevation or incorporate approved floodproofing measures
conditions: site is located in a regulatory flood hazard area

subject: Ground Floor / First Story
rule: ground floor / first story must have at least one operable means of egress to the exterior at grade
conditions: space is occupied by people

subject: Ground Floor / First Story
rule: ground floor / first story slab-on-grade must be separated from the ground by a vapor retarder or capillary break
conditions: floor construction is slab-on-grade
space is conditioned or finished

subject: Basement Stories
rule: basement stories must have at least one means of egress to the exterior or a protected path to an exit at grade
conditions: when occupied by people
when the basement depth exceeds 200 sq ft or has sleeping quarters
exceptions: if the basement has a direct door to the outside at grade level

subject: Basement Stories
rule: basement stories must not have habitable spaces below the groundwater table without a permanent waterproofing and drainage system
conditions: when the basement is used for sleeping, living, or working areas
exceptions: temporary/seasonal floodable spaces such as crawl spaces or storage-only areas

subject: Basement Stories
rule: basement stories must have a minimum ceiling height of 7 feet for habitable spaces
conditions: when the space is designated as habitable (living, sleeping, eating, cooking)
exceptions: unfinished storage, mechanical rooms, or crawl spaces

subject: Roof / Penthouse Level
rule: roof / penthouse level must have a drainage path to prevent water accumulation and structural overload
conditions: if the roof is flat or low-slope
if the roof is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: enclosed penthouse levels that are fully sheltered by an upper roof or canopy and have no exposed horizontal surfaces collecting water

subject: Roof / Penthouse Level
rule: roof / penthouse level must not have unprotected penetrations that allow water ingress into the building envelope
conditions: when mechanical, electrical, or structural penetrations pass through the roof membrane
exceptions: penetrations that are properly flashed, sealed, and detailed per roofing standards

subject: Roof / Penthouse Level
rule: roof / penthouse level must have fall protection for personnel accessing the roof surface
conditions: if the roof is accessible for maintenance or occupancy
if the roof edge has a drop greater than the applicable building code threshold (typically 30 inches / 762 mm)
exceptions: roofs designed as unoccupiable and not requiring any personnel access during building operation

subject: Blast Ventilation Dampers
rule: blast ventilation dampers must be rated to withstand the peak overpressure and impulse from the design blast load without failing or prematurely releasing
conditions: the building is in a blast-resistant design category
a design-basis threat has been defined
exceptions: the damper is located in a non-blast-rated partition or envelope where failure is permitted for venting

subject: Blast Ventilation Dampers
rule: blast ventilation dampers must not have a net free area that is less than the minimum required for the protected space's emergency ventilation or exhaust airflow
conditions: the damper serves a space with emergency ventilation or exhaust requirements
exceptions: supplemental dampers or alternative pathways provide the required airflow

subject: Blast Ventilation Dampers
rule: blast ventilation dampers must remain closed during a blast event unless specifically designed for automatic opening on blast detection
conditions: the damper is intended to isolate a protected space from external blast effects
exceptions: the damper is a blast-actuated pressure-relief damper designed to open at a set overpressure

subject: Shielded Parking Structural Slab
rule: Shielded Parking Structural Slab must have adequate structural capacity to support its self-weight plus superimposed parking live loads and earth cover
conditions: When used as a load-bearing structural element
exceptions: If the slab is designed only as a non-structural fill or separation layer

subject: Shielded Parking Structural Slab
rule: Shielded Parking Structural Slab must not have uncontrolled water ponding on its surface
conditions: When the slab is exposed to precipitation or drainage flow
exceptions: If the slab is intentionally designed as a water-retention structure

subject: Shielded Parking Structural Slab
rule: Shielded Parking Structural Slab must provide a fire-resistance rating consistent with its occupancy separation function
conditions: When the slab forms part of a fire-rated horizontal assembly between parking and occupied spaces above
exceptions: If no fire separation is required by code due to building classification

subject: Vehicle Blast Containment Walls
rule: Vehicle blast containment walls must be structurally continuous and anchored to a reinforced foundation
conditions: Wall is load-bearing or blast-rated
exceptions: Temporary or non-structural barriers used only for traffic routing

subject: Vehicle Blast Containment Walls
rule: Vehicle blast containment walls must not have openings or penetrations larger than 0.1% of wall face area unless fitted with blast-rated closures
conditions: Wall is designed to contain a vehicle-borne explosive event
exceptions: Non-blast-rated openings in walls that are secondary and not part of the primary containment envelope

subject: Vehicle Blast Containment Walls
rule: Vehicle blast containment walls must resist the design-basis vehicle impact load without progressive collapse
conditions: Wall is located where vehicle approach is possible up to the design speed
exceptions: Walls with separate dedicated vehicle barrier systems that absorb impact energy independently

subject: Blast-Resistant Parking Entry Doors
rule: Blast-resistant parking entry doors must achieve a certified blast resistance rating (e.g., ASTM F2248 or equivalent) for the specified design pressure and impulse
conditions: Door is located in a facility with a defined blast threat level
exceptions: Facility blast assessment determines no blast requirement

subject: Blast-Resistant Parking Entry Doors
rule: Blast-resistant parking entry doors must be positively anchored to the surrounding wall or frame with engineered blast-rated hardware and embedments capable of transmitting the full design reaction loads

subject: Blast-Resistant Parking Entry Doors
rule: Blast-resistant parking entry doors must not incorporate standard annealed glass; any glazing must be blast-rated laminated or polycarbonate systems
conditions: Door contains vision panels or glazing

subject: Blast-Resistant Parking Entry Doors
rule: Blast-resistant parking entry doors must have a door-to-frame gap that does not exceed the maximum clearance specified in the door's blast test certification

subject: Hardened Parking Column Encasement
rule: hardened parking column encasement must provide minimum 4-hour fire resistance rating
conditions: when used in fire-rated structure parking facilities
exceptions: when separate active fire suppression system provides equivalent protection

subject: Hardened Parking Column Encasement
rule: hardened parking column encasement must have minimum steel reinforcement ratio to resist blast loading
conditions: when the column is part of a blast-resistant perimeter or standoff zone
exceptions: when structural analysis demonstrates ductile failure mode without minimum ratio

subject: Hardened Parking Column Encasement
rule: hardened parking column encasement must not have unreinforced masonry or plain concrete construction
conditions: when the encasement is designed for blast or impact resistance

subject: Vehicle Access Control System
rule: Vehicle Access Control System must physically prevent unauthorized vehicle entry while allowing authorized passage
conditions: system is installed at a vehicle entry/exit point
exceptions: temporary override for emergency vehicle access

subject: Vehicle Access Control System
rule: Vehicle Access Control System barrier arm/gate must not lower or close onto a vehicle that is partially within the path of travel
conditions: system uses a descending barrier such as a gate arm, bollard, or wedge

subject: Vehicle Access Control System
rule: Vehicle Access Control System must detect vehicle presence in the detection zone before initiating a close command
conditions: system is automated and uses inductive loop, radar, or optical sensors for vehicle detection
exceptions: manually operated systems where an attendant visually confirms clear path

subject: Shielded Parking Exhaust System
rule: Shielded Parking Exhaust System exhaust discharge must be located at least 3 meters above grade or above adjacent pedestrian-accessible surfaces
conditions: system is providing ventilation for an enclosed parking structure
discharge is within 10 meters of publicly accessible sidewalks, entrances, or outdoor gathering areas
exceptions: discharge is directly ducted to a dedicated vertical stack extending above the roof of any adjacent occupied building

subject: Shielded Parking Exhaust System
rule: Shielded Parking Exhaust System must not have exhaust discharge openings facing building air intakes, operable windows, or building entries within 15 meters horizontally
conditions: the system includes mechanical exhaust fans
there are any building fresh air intakes or occupied openings on the same facade or adjacent facades within 15 m
exceptions: discharge velocity exceeds 10 m/s and is directed vertically upward at 45 degrees or steeper

subject: Shielded Parking Exhaust System
rule: Shielded Parking Exhaust System must maintain a minimum exhaust flow rate of 0.5 cfm per square foot of parking area when carbon monoxide concentration exceeds 25 ppm
conditions: system serves an enclosed parking garage
continuous CO monitoring is installed
exceptions: local code explicitly permits a lower minimum rate with engineered dilution modeling

subject: Shielded Parking Exhaust System
rule: Shielded Parking Exhaust System must be physically separated from building general exhaust or return-air ducts to prevent cross-contamination
conditions: building has non-parking occupied zones sharing a mechanical system
exceptions: a dedicated energy-recovery device with pressure-relief and fail-closed dampers provides isolation

subject: Shielded Parking Space Layout
rule: shielded parking space must have a clear vehicular access path to a public right-of-way or internal circulation road
exceptions: temporary event parking with separate egress plan

subject: Shielded Parking Space Layout
rule: shielded parking space must have a minimum overhead clearance of at least 2.1 m (or local code minimum) along the entire access route and within the space

subject: Shielded Parking Space Layout
rule: shielded parking space must not be located within a fire lane or block required fire apparatus access
conditions: when fire lane is marked and enforced per local fire code

subject: Shielded Parking Space Layout
rule: shielded parking space must have a structural shield (wall, berm, or barrier) between the parked vehicle and any adjacent traffic lane or hazard
conditions: when the parking space is adjacent to a travel lane with speed limit above 15 mph

subject: Shielded Parking Space Layout
rule: parking space surface must be capable of supporting the design vehicle's wheel loads without failure

subject: Parking Security Lighting
rule: Parking security lighting must be positioned to avoid glare that impairs driver vision or security camera performance
conditions: when located adjacent to vehicle circulation paths
when located near security cameras
exceptions: where glare shields or directed optics eliminate line-of-sight impact

subject: Parking Security Lighting
rule: Parking security lighting luminaires must not be mounted within reach of ground-level vehicle impact without protective bollards or crash-rated barriers
conditions: when pole or base is located within 1.5 m of a vehicular travel lane or parking stall
exceptions: when luminaire mounting height exceeds 4.5 m and pole is slip-base or frangible

subject: Parking Security Lighting
rule: Parking security lighting must produce minimum 1.0 foot-candle (10.8 lux) uniformly across the parking surface as required by security and life-safety standards
conditions: for active parking areas intended for pedestrian use after dark
exceptions: for decorative or entry monument lighting not relied upon for security illumination

subject: Emergency Egress from Shielded Parking
rule: emergency egress path from shielded parking must provide a continuously unobstructed route to a public way or safe dispersal area
conditions: space is classified as shielded parking
space requires emergency egress
exceptions: none

subject: Emergency Egress from Shielded Parking
rule: emergency egress doors from shielded parking must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: door serves an egress path from shielded parking
occupant load of the space exceeds 50 persons
exceptions: none

subject: Emergency Egress from Shielded Parking
rule: egress travel distance from any point in shielded parking to the nearest exit must not exceed the maximum permitted by applicable building code
conditions: space is shielded parking with emergency egress requirement
exceptions: none

subject: Emergency Egress from Shielded Parking
rule: shielded parking egress path must not pass through a hazardous area (e.g., mechanical room, electrical vault, fuel storage)
conditions: egress path is designated from shielded parking
exceptions: none

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths (corridors, hallways, passageways) must have a minimum clear width that accommodates egress requirements and accessibility standards
conditions: occupied building
path serves as means of egress
exceptions: single-occupancy structures
unoccupied service tunnels

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths must maintain a minimum clear headroom height throughout
conditions: path intended for human occupancy
exceptions: mechanical/utility catwalks with restricted access and signage

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths must not have abrupt changes in level without a ramp or lift where accessibility is required
conditions: path is part of an accessible route required by code
exceptions: single steps of limited height where code specifically permits (e.g., historic structures with variance)

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths serving as means of egress must have doors that swing in the direction of travel
conditions: path is part of a required means of egress
door serves an occupant load of 50 or more or is in a high-hazard occupancy
exceptions: doors in dwelling units
doors opening into a corridor from a room with fewer than 50 occupants may swing inward

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths must be free of obstructions that reduce the required clear width below code minimum at any point
conditions: path is a required means of egress or accessible route
exceptions: temporary obstructions allowed only if they maintain minimum clear width per fire code

subject: Horizontal Circulation
rule: horizontal circulation paths must have a walking surface that is slip-resistant, stable, and free of tripping hazards
conditions: path is intended for pedestrian use
exceptions: construction-phase temporary paths with warning signage

subject: Vertical Circulation
rule: Vertical circulation elements (stairs, ramps, ladders) must have a clear width sufficient for intended occupant load and egress requirements
conditions: When serving as a means of egress
When occupied by more than incidental number of people
exceptions: Private stairways in single-family dwellings not serving as required egress

subject: Vertical Circulation
rule: Vertical circulation elements must not have a riser height that creates a tripping hazard or violates code maximum step rise
conditions: For stairs serving as required means of egress or regular occupant use
exceptions: Fixed industrial ladders or ship stairs where code specifically permits steeper riser geometries under restricted-access conditions

subject: Vertical Circulation
rule: Vertical circulation elements must have handrails on at least one side where a drop exists
conditions: When the stair or ramp run has a total rise exceeding 12 inches
When serving occupant use or egress
exceptions: Aisle stairs in assembly occupancies where handrails would obstruct sightlines, provided guardrails are provided

subject: Vertical Circulation
rule: Vertical circulation must not have a tread depth insufficient for safe foot placement
conditions: For stairs serving occupant use or egress
exceptions: Industrial ladders, ship stairs, or alternating tread devices where code explicitly permits reduced tread dimensions under restricted access

subject: Vertical Circulation
rule: Vertical circulation elements must have a landing at the top and bottom of each stair or ramp run
conditions: For stairs serving occupant use or egress
exceptions: Continuous spiral stairs where code permits single top and bottom landing
Single riser step changes that meet code exception criteria

subject: Entrance Zones
rule: entrance zone must provide a clear egress path to the building exterior
conditions: the space is classified as an exit or means of egress
exceptions: the entrance zone is a non-egress decorative entry that does not lead to an occupied area

subject: Entrance Zones
rule: entrance zone must have a minimum clear width of not less than 32 inches (813 mm) when serving as a means of egress
conditions: the entrance zone is part of a means of egress and serves an occupant load
exceptions: existing buildings under certain retroactive code provisions may have reduced widths

subject: Entrance Zones
rule: entrance zone must not have a door that swings against the direction of egress travel when serving more than 50 occupants
conditions: the entrance zone contains a door
the door serves an occupant load greater than 50
exceptions: doors in dwelling units or guest rooms

subject: Entrance Zones
rule: entrance zone must have a floor surface that is slip-resistant when wet
conditions: the entrance zone is exposed to exterior weather (e.g., directly adjacent to the outdoors)
exceptions: interior-only entrance zones not subject to moisture from outdoors

subject: Entrance Zones
rule: entrance zone must provide a level landing immediately inside and outside each door, with a slope not exceeding 1:48
conditions: the entrance zone contains an exterior door
exceptions: thresholds up to 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) at door openings are permitted

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress routes must have a minimum clear width of 0.9 m (approx. 36 in) for door openings and 1.1 m (approx. 44 in) for corridors serving more than one dwelling unit
conditions: building classification requires egress paths
path serves more than one dwelling unit or has an occupant load ≥ 50
exceptions: existing buildings undergoing minor renovation where local code permits reduced widths

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress routes must not be obstructed by furniture, storage, or any movable objects that reduce the required clear width
conditions: path is designated as a required means of egress
exceptions: none — any obstruction in the required clear width is a code violation regardless of circumstances

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress routes must have a minimum clear headroom of 1.98 m (approx. 6 ft 6 in) throughout
conditions: path is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: door frames — door height may be 2.03 m (80 in) with a minimum frame height of 1.98 m measured from the finished floor

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress routes must terminate at a public way or an open exterior space at grade level
conditions: path is the terminal segment of a required means of egress
exceptions: an interior exit stair or ramp that leads to a street floor discharge in accordance with local code

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress doors must swing in the direction of egress travel when serving an occupant load of 50 or more
conditions: door serves a room, area, or space with an occupant load ≥ 50
exceptions: doors in dwelling units and guestrooms serving fewer than 10 occupants

subject: Egress Routes
rule: egress routes must not pass through adjacent rooms or spaces that require passing through one room to reach another unless those spaces are accessory to the area served
conditions: occupant load of the intervening space exceeds 30
path is the sole means of egress from a space
exceptions: one intervening room is permitted if it is a lobby, foyer, or reception area not classified as a high-hazard space

subject: Atria and Interior Streets
rule: atria and interior streets must have continuous accessible egress paths to building exits
conditions: publicly accessible atrium
occupied space connects to atrium
exceptions: very small atria less than 55m² where separate egress is provided

subject: Atria and Interior Streets
rule: atria must not have unprotected vertical openings that connect more than three stories without smoke control
conditions: atrium connects multiple floors vertically
exceptions: atrium equipped with approved engineered smoke control system

subject: Atria and Interior Streets
rule: glass roofs over atria and interior streets must use laminated or tempered safety glazing
conditions: overhead glazing present
occupants can walk beneath the glazing

subject: Atria and Interior Streets
rule: interior streets must not be narrower than required minimum egress width
conditions: interior street serves as an exit access corridor

subject: Escalator and Moving Walk
rule: escalator or moving walk must have a braking system capable of stopping under full load within specified distance
conditions: when carrying passengers
in operation

subject: Escalator and Moving Walk
rule: escalator or moving walk must have a handrail that moves synchronously with the step or pallet belt

subject: Escalator and Moving Walk
rule: escalator step or moving walk pallet must not have a vertical gap between adjacent steps/pallets exceeding code limit

subject: Escalator and Moving Walk
rule: escalator or moving walk must have a comb plate at entry and exit that meshes correctly with step/pallet grooves

subject: Escalator and Moving Walk
rule: escalator truss or moving walk structure must be designed to support dead load plus full passenger live load without yielding

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must have continuous handrails on at least one side
conditions: Vertical rise exceeds 600mm
More than 3 risers
exceptions: Private stairways within individual dwelling units in some jurisdictions

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must have tread depth and riser height that are uniform within a single flight

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must have a minimum headroom clearance of 2.0 m (approx. 6'-8")
exceptions: Existing structures where reduction to 1.95 m is permitted under certain codes

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must have a landing at the top and bottom of each flight
conditions: Flight contains more than 16 risers

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must not have a rise (individual riser height) exceeding 200 mm (approx. 7-3/4")

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must not have a tread depth less than 250 mm (approx. 10") for occupiable spaces
exceptions: Service stairs (e.g., access to mechanical equipment) may have reduced tread depth under some codes

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must have a maximum riser-to-tread relationship that satisfies the formula: (2 × riser) + tread ≥ 550 mm and ≤ 700 mm

subject: Staircase System
rule: Staircase system must not have open risers with a gap greater than 100 mm
conditions: Open-riser stair design is used

subject: Railing and Guard System
rule: railing and guard system must resist horizontal loads (e.g., 0.5 kN/m at top rail) as specified by building code
conditions: when used as a guard along open edges of floors, balconies, or stairs
when required by applicable building code
exceptions: areas not accessible to occupants

subject: Railing and Guard System
rule: railing and guard system must have infill openings not wide enough to allow passage of a 100 mm (or 4 inch) sphere
conditions: when functioning as a guard to prevent falls

subject: Railing and Guard System
rule: guard height must meet minimum required height (typically 1.07 m / 42 inches above walking surface)
conditions: when installed as a protective guard at a drop-off

subject: Railing and Guard System
rule: railing and guard handrail must have an ergonomic graspable cross-section (typically not less than 30 mm and not more than 50 mm in diameter, or equivalent shape)
conditions: when the railing also serves as a handrail required for stair or ramp egress
exceptions: guards not required to be graspable if separate handrail is provided

subject: Railing and Guard System
rule: railing and guard system must not have any sharp edges, burrs, or projections that could cause injury

subject: Wayfinding and Signage Elements
rule: Wayfinding and signage elements must provide clear directional information to support safe egress and emergency evacuation
conditions: building requires emergency egress paths
signage is installed in a means of egress
exceptions: buildings not occupied by the public or employees

subject: Wayfinding and Signage Elements
rule: Wayfinding and signage elements must not use conflicting or ambiguous symbols that could mislead occupants during an emergency
conditions: signage is part of the emergency egress or life-safety system

subject: Wayfinding and Signage Elements
rule: Wayfinding and signage elements must be visible and legible under all lighting conditions, including power failure
conditions: signage is required for life safety or egress

subject: Wayfinding and Signage Elements
rule: Wayfinding and signage elements must not obstruct fire suppression systems or emergency equipment
conditions: signage is mounted in proximity to sprinkler heads, fire alarms, extinguishers, or emergency equipment

subject: Building Structure
rule: Building structure must have a continuous load path from roof to foundation
conditions: For all buildings
exceptions: Temporary structures not intended for human occupancy

subject: Building Structure
rule: Building structure must resist all anticipated loads without exceeding allowable stress or deformation limits
conditions: For all buildings

subject: Building Structure
rule: Building structure must not have a fundamental frequency that coincides with resonance-inducing excitation frequencies
conditions: For buildings subject to dynamic loads such as wind, seismic activity, or mechanical vibrations

subject: Building Structure
rule: Building structure must not rely on tensile capacity of unreinforced masonry or plain concrete
conditions: For structural elements made of masonry or concrete
exceptions: Properly reinforced masonry or concrete designed in accordance with material-specific codes

subject: Interior Spaces
rule: interior spaces must have adequate ventilation to prevent mold growth and maintain air quality
conditions: enclosed space with limited natural ventilation
space occupied by people
space with moisture sources
exceptions: utility closets or small service spaces not intended for occupancy
temporary structures with planned limited duration

subject: Interior Spaces
rule: interior spaces must have a means of egress that meets minimum clear width and travel distance requirements
conditions: space designed for occupancy
exceptions: maintenance-only crawl spaces where no occupancy is intended

subject: Interior Spaces
rule: interior spaces must not have a floor-to-ceiling height below the minimum required for human occupancy
conditions: space intended for human occupancy
exceptions: mechanical penthouses
attic storage spaces
crawl spaces

subject: Interior Spaces
rule: interior spaces must have artificial lighting providing minimum illuminance levels for the intended use
conditions: space without adequate daylighting
space intended for occupied use during all hours
exceptions: spaces used exclusively during daytime with sufficient daylight
unoccupied storage rooms

subject: Structural Slab
rule: A structural slab must be designed to carry its specified dead and live loads without exceeding allowable stresses or deflections
conditions: When the slab is in service

subject: Structural Slab
rule: A structural slab must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement as specified by code for fire resistance and corrosion protection
conditions: When reinforced concrete slab

subject: Structural Slab
rule: A structural slab must not have a span-to-depth ratio exceeding the maximum permitted by code for the given support conditions and concrete type
conditions: One-way or two-way slab spanning between supports
exceptions: When detailed deflection analysis demonstrates adequacy

subject: Structural Slab
rule: A structural slab must be provided with adequate reinforcement in both principal directions to resist tensile stresses
conditions: When the slab is a two-way slab or subjected to bending in multiple directions

subject: Exterior Cladding
rule: exterior cladding must be attached to the building structure with adequate connections to resist wind loads
conditions: any building with cladding
exceptions: temporary structures not designed for wind resistance

subject: Exterior Cladding
rule: exterior cladding must not create a vapor barrier on the wrong side of the wall assembly that traps moisture within the structure
conditions: where the cladding system includes a vapor retarder layer
in climates where interior vapor drive exceeds exterior vapor drive
exceptions: cladding systems with engineered drainage and ventilation that manage moisture regardless of vapor profile

subject: Exterior Cladding
rule: exterior cladding must provide a continuous water-shedding surface or be backed by a drained cavity that prevents bulk water entry into the structure
conditions: any building expected to remain dry inside
exceptions: unoccupied structures where water entry is acceptable

subject: Partition Walls
rule: partition wall must be braced or connected to the building structure (floor, ceiling, or adjacent walls) to resist lateral loads
conditions: wall height exceeds 2.4 m
wall is not a freestanding screen shorter than 1.2 m
exceptions: temporary demountable partitions in seismic zone 0

subject: Partition Walls
rule: partition wall must not bear vertical loads from floors, roofs, or other structural elements above
conditions: wall is a non-loadbearing partition (the typical case)
exceptions: wall is explicitly designed and detailed as a loadbearing wall with appropriate footing and reinforcement

subject: Partition Walls
rule: partition wall must be laterally restrained at head and base to prevent rotation under out-of-plane forces
conditions: wall is a full-height partition (floor-to-slab or floor-to-deck)
exceptions: freestanding low-height partitions (e.g., below 1.0 m) used as space dividers only

subject: Ceiling System
rule: ceiling system must be securely attached to the structure above
conditions: all ceiling installations
exceptions: suspended ceilings designed for seismic or intentional displacement

subject: Ceiling System
rule: ceiling system must not trap moisture within the assembly
conditions: ceiling installed in a space with moisture sources or vapour drive
exceptions: systems specifically rated for continuous moisture exposure and designed with drainage

subject: Ceiling System
rule: ceiling system must not rely on ceiling finish for structural bracing of the building frame
conditions: ceiling is not a rated structural diaphragm

subject: Ceiling System
rule: ceiling system must have a fire-resistance rating consistent with the rated assembly of which it is part
conditions: ceiling forms part of a fire-rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assembly

subject: Structural Columns
rule: structural column must be vertically continuous from foundation to supported element without lateral offsets that transfer load through bending
conditions: column is a primary gravity load path member
exceptions: column is designed as a deliberately eccentric column with explicit bending moment capacity verified

subject: Structural Columns
rule: structural column must not have a slenderness ratio (effective length / least radius of gyration) exceeding the code-prescribed limit for its material
conditions: column is classified as slender or long per applicable design code
exceptions: second-order (P-Delta) effects are explicitly accounted for in the design

subject: Structural Columns
rule: structural column must have sufficient end restraint or bracing to prevent buckling in its weakest direction
conditions: column is not continuously braced along its length
column is in compression
exceptions: column is designed as a tension-only member

subject: Structural Columns
rule: structural column's load-bearing capacity must equal or exceed the factored design load applied to it

subject: Structural Columns
rule: structural column must not be placed on unconsolidated fill or uncompacted soil without proper foundation design addressing settlement
conditions: column transfers load to ground through a footing or foundation
exceptions: geotechnical investigation confirms soil bearing capacity is adequate and differential settlement is within tolerable limits

subject: Structural Beams
rule: structural beams must be designed to carry their self-weight plus specified live and dead loads without exceeding allowable stress limits
conditions: beam is part of a load-bearing structure

subject: Structural Beams
rule: structural beams must not have a span-to-depth ratio that exceeds the code-prescribed maximum for the given material and loading condition
conditions: beam is in bending
beam spans between supports
exceptions: beam is designed with pre-stressing or post-tensioning that explicitly accounts for greater deflection

subject: Structural Beams
rule: structural beams must have adequate lateral bracing or torsional restraint to prevent lateral-torsional buckling at design loads
conditions: beam is made of steel or other slender section
beam is not continuously embedded in concrete or similar lateral-restraining material
exceptions: beam cross-section is such that its lateral buckling moment exceeds the required moment capacity without bracing (e.g., stocky sections)

subject: Structural Beams
rule: structural beams must not have connections that are incapable of developing the required moment, shear, or axial strength at the connection interface
conditions: beam is connected to other structural members at its ends or along its span
exceptions: beam is seated on a bearing that is designed for pure gravity transfer and the connection is explicitly detailed for that condition

subject: Pedestrian Street Pavement
rule: pedestrian street pavement surface must have a minimum cross-slope of 1.5% to 2% for drainage
conditions: pavement is located in an area with precipitation

subject: Pedestrian Street Pavement
rule: pedestrian street pavement surface must not have trip hazards exceeding 6 mm (1/4 inch) vertical displacement at joints or cracks

subject: Pedestrian Street Pavement
rule: pedestrian street pavement must have a slip-resistant surface with a minimum coefficient of friction of 0.5 when wet

subject: Pedestrian Street Pavement
rule: pedestrian street pavement must support a minimum live load of 5 kPa (100 psf) for pedestrian traffic

subject: Pedestrian Street Pavement
rule: pedestrian street pavement base and subgrade must be compacted to at least 95% of maximum dry density (Standard Proctor)

subject: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab
rule: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab must be designed for live load appropriate to pedestrian traffic

subject: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab
rule: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab must have a minimum slip resistance surface appropriate for pedestrian use
conditions: when exposed to weather or expected wet conditions
exceptions: interior covered decks not subject to moisture

subject: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab
rule: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab must have a continuous load path to supporting structure

subject: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab
rule: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab must not exceed allowable deflection under design loads

subject: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab
rule: Pedestrian Street Deck/Base Slab must have a minimum fire resistance rating as required by building code for the occupancy beneath
conditions: when the slab forms a floor/ceiling assembly above an occupied space

subject: Pedestrian Street Lighting System
rule: luminaire mounting height must be at least 3.5 meters above pedestrian walking surface
conditions: system is installed in a public pedestrian walkway or street
exceptions: low-level bollard lighting specifically designed for ground-level illumination

subject: Pedestrian Street Lighting System
rule: lamp housing must be sealed against moisture ingress to minimum IP65 rating
conditions: system is installed outdoors and exposed to weather

subject: Pedestrian Street Lighting System
rule: luminous intensity must not exceed 6500 candela at any angle above 90 degrees from vertical
conditions: system is located in a zone with nighttime pedestrian traffic

subject: Pedestrian Street Drainage System
rule: pedestrian street drainage system must have continuous longitudinal slope to convey stormwater to collection inlets or outfalls
conditions: pedestrian street is designed to be paved or impervious
exceptions: street design incorporates a completely pervious pavement system that allows all rainfall to infiltrate in situ with no surface runoff

subject: Pedestrian Street Drainage System
rule: catch basins or grate inlets must be positioned at low points and spaced to limit surface flow width within allowable spread for pedestrian safety
conditions: pedestrian street is served by curb-and-gutter or surface drainage inlets

subject: Pedestrian Street Drainage System
rule: pedestrian street drainage system must not discharge stormwater onto adjacent private property or building entries in an uncontrolled manner
exceptions: adjacent site has a recorded drainage easement and engineered receiving swale specifically designed to accept the discharge

subject: Pedestrian Street Street Furniture
rule: Street furniture must not obstruct the minimum clear pedestrian pathway width
conditions: when located in a pedestrian street or footpath area
exceptions: temporarily placed furniture for approved events

subject: Pedestrian Street Street Furniture
rule: Street furniture must be stable against overturning under wind load

subject: Pedestrian Street Street Furniture
rule: Street furniture must not have sharp edges or protruding elements at pedestrian impact height
conditions: within pedestrian circulation zones

subject: Pedestrian Street Canopy/Awning
rule: canopy/awning overhead surface must have a minimum slope for water drainage
conditions: canopy/awning is exposed to weather (not fully enclosed)
exceptions: canopy/awning is intentionally designed as a water-collection feature with controlled drainage system

subject: Pedestrian Street Canopy/Awning
rule: canopy/awning must resist downward snow load and live load to prevent collapse onto pedestrians
conditions: canopy/awning is located in a climate with snow accumulation
canopy/awning is over a publicly accessible path

subject: Pedestrian Street Canopy/Awning
rule: canopy/awning must not obstruct required emergency egress or fire apparatus access
conditions: canopy/awning projects over a public sidewalk or egress path

subject: Pedestrian Street Canopy/Awning
rule: canopy/awning must have a minimum clearance height above pedestrian walkway (typically 7-8 ft minimum)
conditions: canopy/awning overhangs a pedestrian path

subject: Pedestrian Street Hardscape Planters
rule: Pedestrian street hardscape planters must have drainage holes or a drainage layer to prevent standing water from killing plant roots
conditions: planter is intended to support live plants
planter is exposed to precipitation or irrigation
exceptions: planter contains only artificial plants
planter is a purely decorative shell with no soil medium

subject: Pedestrian Street Hardscape Planters
rule: Pedestrian street hardscape planters must not block required pedestrian clear path widths (typically minimum 1.2–1.8 m depending on local code)
conditions: planter is located within a public pedestrian right-of-way or accessible route
exceptions: planter is placed in a furnishing zone or setback outside the required clear path

subject: Pedestrian Street Hardscape Planters
rule: Pedestrian street hardscape planters must be structurally stable against overturning due to wind or accidental impact
conditions: planter is freestanding (not permanently fixed to the ground)

subject: Pedestrian Street Hardscape Planters
rule: Pedestrian street hardscape planter materials must be frost-resistant in climates where freeze-thaw cycling occurs
conditions: planter is located in a climate with regular freeze-thaw cycles (mean winter minimum below 0 °C)

subject: Pedestrian Street Retaining Walls
rule: retaining wall must resist active lateral earth pressure without overturning or sliding
conditions: wall retains soil on one side
wall is vertical or near-vertical
exceptions: wall is designed as a gravity wall with sufficient self-weight
wall is mechanically anchored/tiedback

subject: Pedestrian Street Retaining Walls
rule: retaining wall must have a drainage system (weep holes or granular backfill) to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: wall retains earth that can accumulate water
wall is impermeable (e.g., concrete, masonry)
exceptions: wall is designed for full hydrostatic pressure
backfill material is freely draining with no water source

subject: Pedestrian Street Retaining Walls
rule: retaining wall on a pedestrian street must not have loose or protruding elements at head height that could injure pedestrians
conditions: wall is adjacent to pedestrian circulation area
exceptions: wall is behind a barrier or railing preventing pedestrian contact

subject: Pedestrian Street Retaining Walls
rule: retaining wall must not exceed its maximum unsupported height without structural reinforcement or tiering
conditions: wall is a cantilever or gravity type without lateral bracing at top
exceptions: wall is designed per geotechnical analysis for a specific greater height

subject: Pedestrian Street Signage System
rule: signage system must be structurally stable under wind loads
conditions: when installed outdoors
when exceeding 1.5m in height
exceptions: temporary signage for events of less than 72 hours duration

subject: Pedestrian Street Signage System
rule: signage system must not obstruct minimum pedestrian clear width on footpath
conditions: when placed on public pedestrian pathways

subject: Pedestrian Street Signage System
rule: signage system must have impact-resistant construction at vulnerable heights
conditions: when installed below 2.1 m above ground level
when located near vehicle traffic areas

subject: Pedestrian Street Signage System
rule: signage system must not create a trip hazard from base or ground fixings
conditions: when mounted at or near ground level

subject: Pedestrian Street Bollards
rule: bollard must be spaced such that wheelchair users, prams, and bicycles can pass through
conditions: bollards are used to restrict vehicle access while allowing pedestrian and micromobility access
exceptions: location is a vehicle-only zone with alternative accessible routes nearby

subject: Pedestrian Street Bollards
rule: bollard must have a minimum height and visibility treatment (e.g. reflective band, contrasting colour) so it is clearly visible to all users
conditions: bollard is installed in a pedestrian zone shared with cyclists or vehicles, or at night-time use area

subject: Pedestrian Street Bollards
rule: bollard must not have sharp edges or protrusions at pedestrian contact height (0–1.5 m)
conditions: bollard is located in a publicly accessible pedestrian area

subject: Pedestrian Street Bollards
rule: bollard must be anchored to withstand an impact force equivalent to the design vehicle for the zone
conditions: bollard is intended to stop or deter vehicles
exceptions: bollard is purely decorative with no vehicle-stopping role and is clearly marked as non-structural

subject: Pedestrian Street Bollards
rule: bollard must not create a tripping hazard at its base (e.g., base projection above 6 mm or abrupt change in level)
conditions: bollard is installed on a pedestrian walking surface
exceptions: bollard base is ramped or chamfered to meet ADA/accessibility compliance

subject: Covered Arcade
rule: covered arcade must have a continuous weatherproof roof covering

subject: Covered Arcade
rule: covered arcade roof must be structurally self-supporting over the full covered path

subject: Covered Arcade
rule: covered arcade must not have unguarded edges where the floor drops more than 600mm adjacent to the path
exceptions: where a balustrade, wall, or railing of at least 1.0m height is provided

subject: Covered Arcade
rule: covered arcade floor surface must be slip-resistant under wet conditions
conditions: where the arcade is exposed to rain or moisture ingress

subject: Pedestrian Plaza
rule: pedestrian plaza surface must be slip-resistant
conditions: surface is paved
exceptions: temporary plaza with permeable/grass surface

subject: Pedestrian Plaza
rule: pedestrian plaza must not have unguarded drop-offs or changes in level exceeding 0.5m

subject: Pedestrian Plaza
rule: pedestrian plaza surface must be free of protruding tripping hazards
exceptions: temporary construction or events with barriers and warning markings

subject: Pedestrian Plaza
rule: pedestrian plaza must have a minimum clear width of 1.2m for accessible passage
conditions: plaza is intended for public access

subject: Shared Street (Woonerf)
rule: Shared street (woonerf) must have a continuous level surface with no raised curbs separating vehicular and pedestrian areas
exceptions: Where a grade change is required for accessibility ramps at boundaries with adjacent sidewalks

subject: Shared Street (Woonerf)
rule: Shared street (woonerf) must have a vehicular speed limit not exceeding walking pace (typically 15-20 km/h or 10 mph)
conditions: When motor vehicle access is permitted

subject: Shared Street (Woonerf)
rule: Shared street (woonerf) must not have separate pedestrian-only and vehicle-only traffic signal phases

subject: Shared Street (Woonerf)
rule: Shared street (woonerf) must provide vehicular access to all abutting properties
conditions: When properties fronting the woonerf have no alternative vehicular access

subject: Pedestrian Mall
rule: pedestrian mall ground surface must be slip-resistant
conditions: surface is exposed to weather
surface is walking area
exceptions: temporary surfaces for special events

subject: Pedestrian Mall
rule: pedestrian mall must be accessible to emergency vehicles via a clear path
conditions: mall length exceeds 30 m from any public street access point

subject: Pedestrian Mall
rule: pedestrian mall must not have level changes that exceed barrier-free maximum without an accessible alternative route

subject: Pedestrian Street Edge Zone
rule: pedestrian street edge zone must maintain a minimum clear width of obstruction-free path
conditions: zone is adjacent to vehicular traffic lanes
exceptions: temporary street furniture during permitted events

subject: Pedestrian Street Edge Zone
rule: pedestrian street edge zone must not have a longitudinal slope exceeding the maximum accessible gradient
conditions: zone is intended for pedestrian access

subject: Pedestrian Street Edge Zone
rule: pedestrian street edge zone must have a slip-resistant walking surface
conditions: zone is exposed to weather or moisture

subject: Thoroughfare Exit
rule: thoroughfare exit door must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: door serves an occupant load greater than 50
door is in an assembly occupancy
exceptions: door is located in a health care facility where swinging into the corridor would reduce corridor width below required minimum

subject: Thoroughfare Exit
rule: thoroughfare exit must not be concealed or obstructed in a way that makes it unrecognizable as an exit

subject: Thoroughfare Exit
rule: thoroughfare exit door must have a clear opening width of at least 32 inches
conditions: door serves as a required means of egress
exceptions: existing buildings under certain historic preservation allowances where 28 inches minimum is permitted with authority having jurisdiction approval

subject: Thoroughfare Exit
rule: thoroughfare exit door must be openable from the egress side without the use of a key, tool, or special knowledge
exceptions: egress doors in hazardous areas where delayed egress locking systems are permitted with fire alarm integration

subject: Thoroughfare Exit
rule: thoroughfare exit must not terminate in a dead-end corridor that requires travel back toward the hazard

subject: Thoroughfare Lighting
rule: thoroughfare lighting must have a minimum mounting height above roadway surface to prevent vehicle collision
conditions: lighting poles are located within vehicle impact zone adjacent to roadway
exceptions: lighting is mounted on existing building facades or structures above collision height
use of breakaway or frangible pole bases that comply with impact safety standards

subject: Thoroughfare Lighting
rule: thoroughfare lighting must not direct excessive glare into the travel lanes of vehicular traffic
conditions: lighting installation includes luminaires that emit light upwards or laterally toward driver eye level

subject: Thoroughfare Lighting
rule: thoroughfare lighting luminaires and electrical components must be rated for outdoor/wet location exposure
conditions: lighting is installed in exterior, uncovered locations

subject: Thoroughfare Signage
rule: Thoroughfare signage must be vertically oriented and mounted with its primary face perpendicular to the direction of travel
conditions: signage is installed on a public right-of-way
signage is intended for vehicular traffic

subject: Thoroughfare Signage
rule: Thoroughfare signage must have retroreflective or illuminated lettering on a contrasting background
conditions: signage is installed for nighttime visibility
exceptions: signage is located in a fully pedestrian-only zone with ambient lighting

subject: Thoroughfare Signage
rule: Thoroughfare signage must not be obstructed by vegetation, structures, or other signage within its sight triangle
conditions: signage is intended for approaching vehicular or pedestrian traffic

subject: Thoroughfare Signage
rule: Thoroughfare signage must be securely fastened to a rigid support structure rated for local wind loads
conditions: signage is installed outdoors

subject: Thoroughfare Handrail
rule: Thoroughfare handrail must have a height between 900mm and 1100mm
conditions: Applicable to stairs, ramps, and level thoroughfares
exceptions: Private single-family dwellings may have different requirements per local code

subject: Thoroughfare Handrail
rule: Thoroughfare handrail must withstand a uniformly distributed load of at least 0.36 kN/m and a concentrated load of at least 0.9 kN
conditions: Handrail installed in public or commercial buildings

subject: Thoroughfare Handrail
rule: Thoroughfare handrail must not have openings that permit passage of a 100mm sphere
conditions: Handrail with balusters or horizontal rails within the guardrail zone

subject: Thoroughfare Handrail
rule: Thoroughfare handrail must provide a continuous grasping surface without obstruction
conditions: Handrail serving egress stairs or accessible routes
exceptions: Where brackets or supports are permitted to interrupt the surface at intervals if they do not reduce the effective clear width

subject: Thoroughfare Fire Door
rule: A thoroughfare fire door must be self-closing and latching
conditions: when installed in a means of egress path
in any wall required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: where specifically permitted by the authority having jurisdiction for continuous operations

subject: Thoroughfare Fire Door
rule: A thoroughfare fire door must not be obstructed or blocked in the open position
conditions: at any time the building is occupied
exceptions: when held open by an approved automatic release device that closes the door upon fire/smoke detection

subject: Thoroughfare Fire Door
rule: A thoroughfare fire door must have a fire-protection rating equal to or greater than the required fire-resistance rating of the wall in which it is installed

subject: Thoroughfare Smoke Control Damper
rule: Thoroughfare smoke control damper must maintain a minimum leakage class rating when in the closed position
conditions: When installed in a smoke control system
When the damper is in the closed position

subject: Thoroughfare Smoke Control Damper
rule: Thoroughfare smoke control damper must not be installed where ambient temperature exceeds the damper's rated temperature range
conditions: For dampers with standard temperature ratings
exceptions: Unless the damper is specifically rated for elevated temperature service (e.g., high-temperature rated damper)

subject: Thoroughfare Expansion Joint
rule: Thoroughfare expansion joint must accommodate differential movement between adjacent building sections
conditions: when connecting two separate building structures or structural bays

subject: Thoroughfare Expansion Joint
rule: Thoroughfare expansion joint must not create a trip hazard for pedestrians
