conditions: when the thoroughfare is intended for pedestrian use

subject: Thoroughfare Expansion Joint
rule: Thoroughfare expansion joint must maintain continuity of the waterproofing membrane across the joint
conditions: when the thoroughfare is exposed to weather or moisture

subject: Thoroughfare Floor Drain
rule: thoroughfare floor drain must be located at a low point in the floor surface to allow gravitational water flow
conditions: drain serves a sloped or flat floor area where water accumulates
exceptions: drain is part of a mechanically pumped collection system that does not rely on gravity

subject: Thoroughfare Floor Drain
rule: thoroughfare floor drain must have a trap seal to prevent sewer gas ingress
conditions: drain is connected to a sanitary sewer or combined sewer system
exceptions: drain discharges to a dedicated stormwater system with no sewer gas source
drain is a trench drain with an external trap installed separately

subject: Thoroughfare Floor Drain
rule: thoroughfare floor drain must not have a grate opening larger than the maximum allowable by local code for pedestrian or vehicular traffic
conditions: drain is located in an area subject to pedestrian foot traffic or vehicular wheel loads
exceptions: drain is in a restricted-access mechanical room with no foot or vehicle traffic

subject: Thoroughfare Floor Drain
rule: thoroughfare floor drain body must be watertight to the surrounding floor slab
conditions: drain is cast into a concrete floor slab
exceptions: drain is a surface-mounted retrofit unit with external waterproofing membrane lapped over the flange

subject: Thoroughfare Reception Counter
rule: A thoroughfare reception counter must provide a clear, unobstructed path for wheelchair users to approach and access the counter surface
conditions: The counter serves a public or employee thoroughfare where accessibility regulations apply

subject: Thoroughfare Reception Counter
rule: The counter surface must be at a height allowing service interaction from both seated and standing positions, or have a lowered section
conditions: The counter is staffed and used for direct service transactions

subject: Thoroughfare Gate or Turnstile
rule: thoroughfare gate or turnstile must allow passage of a person of standard anthropometric dimensions
conditions: when used for pedestrian access control
exceptions: specially designated staff-only gates with restricted clearance

subject: Thoroughfare Gate or Turnstile
rule: thoroughfare gate or turnstile must not obstruct emergency egress when fail-safe or panic mode is activated
conditions: when installed in an egress path subject to life-safety codes
exceptions: turnstiles with drop-arm or breakaway mechanisms that automatically release on power loss or panic force

subject: Thoroughfare Gate or Turnstile
rule: thoroughfare gate or turnstile must not have pinch points or shear hazards within the normal passage envelope
conditions: when the gate or turnstile has moving components (swinging, sliding, or rotating arms)
exceptions: guarded or interlocked designs where motion stops upon contact detection

subject: Entrance Lobby
rule: entrance lobby floor must be level or have a maximum slope of 1:50 (2%) for accessibility
conditions: lobby serves as a building entrance
lobby is accessible to the public
exceptions: historic building where accessibility compliance is exempted by code

subject: Entrance Lobby
rule: entrance lobby must have at least one means of egress door that opens in the direction of exit travel
conditions: lobby serves an occupancy load greater than 50 people
lobby is a required egress component

subject: Entrance Lobby
rule: entrance lobby must not have a door that swings into the path of egress without a landing or recess
conditions: door serves as an exit from the lobby
exceptions: door serves an occupancy of fewer than 10 people and is not on a required egress path

subject: Entry Door
rule: entry door must have a clear opening width of at least 32 inches (813 mm) when in the open position
conditions: applies to doors serving accessible routes
applies to commercial buildings and multi-family residential under ADA/ICC A117.1
exceptions: existing construction where compliance is technically infeasible and allowed by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Entry Door
rule: entry door must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: applies to doors serving a room or area with an occupant load of 50 or more
applies to doors in hazardous areas such as high-hazard occupancy groups
exceptions: residential one- and two-family dwellings
doors in dwelling units within larger buildings where occupant load is below threshold

subject: Entry Door
rule: entry door must have a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the wall in which it is installed
conditions: applies to doors in fire-resistance-rated walls (e.g., stairwell enclosures, corridor partitions, shaft enclosures)
exceptions: non-rated openings in non-rated walls

subject: Entry Door
rule: entry door must not have a lock that requires a key, tool, or special knowledge to exit from the egress side
conditions: applies to all egress doors in buildings other than detention/ correctional occupancies
exceptions: egress-controlled doors in high-security areas where alternative panic hardware is provided and code permits

subject: Door Hardware Set
rule: door hardware set must be compatible with the door's lock preparation type (e.g., cylindrical, mortise, or bored)

subject: Door Hardware Set
rule: door hardware set must have a fire-rating equal to or greater than the fire-rating of the door assembly when installed in a fire-rated opening
conditions: door is in a fire-rated wall assembly

subject: Door Hardware Set
rule: door hardware set must not have latch projection that prevents the door from fully closing and latching

subject: Door Hardware Set
rule: door hardware set must include a functioning locking mechanism where required by code for means of egress doors
conditions: door is on an exit route or means of egress
exceptions: egress doors that must use panic hardware instead of a key-operated lock in certain occupancy types (e.g., assembly, educational)

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy must have a minimum slope to prevent water pooling
conditions: canopy has a flat or nearly flat roof surface
canopy is exposed to rain or snow
exceptions: canopy uses a fully sealed, non-draining system (e.g., completely glazed with internal drainage gutters that still require slope)

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy must be structurally capable of supporting its self-weight plus design live loads (snow, rain, maintenance personnel)
conditions: canopy is attached to a building facade or freestanding above an entrance

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy must not obstruct required egress pathways or emergency access
conditions: canopy is located over or adjacent to a building entrance used for egress

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy must have a minimum clearance height above the walking surface to accommodate pedestrian and vehicle passage
conditions: canopy is located above a walkway, driveway, or entrance path

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy must be securely anchored to the building structure to resist wind uplift forces
conditions: canopy is attached to a building facade or supported by columns

subject: Entrance Canopy
rule: entrance canopy glass (if present) must be made of safety-rated laminated or tempered glass
conditions: canopy includes glass panels overhead
exceptions: canopy is at ground level with no overhead occupancy and local code permits annealed glass with protective mesh

subject: Weather Stripping
rule: weather stripping must form a continuous seal around the entire perimeter of the operable element (door or window) it is applied to
conditions: weather stripping is installed on an operable door or window
exceptions: weather stripping used only as a temporary dust seal during construction

subject: Weather Stripping
rule: weather stripping must not be installed where it will be crushed beyond its recovery thickness during normal operation of the door or window
conditions: weather stripping is of a compressible type (foam, tubular rubber, bulb, etc.)

subject: Weather Stripping
rule: weather stripping must maintain dimensional stability across the full service temperature range of its installation location
conditions: weather stripping is installed on an exterior door or window subject to outdoor temperature extremes

subject: Entrance Mat/Grid
rule: Entrance mat/grid must be flush with or recessed below the surrounding finished floor surface
conditions: When installed as a permanent building component at an entrance

subject: Entrance Mat/Grid
rule: Entrance mat/grid must be securely anchored or restrained against horizontal movement
conditions: When installed in a location subject to foot traffic

subject: Entrance Mat/Grid
rule: Entrance mat/grid must not create a vertical change that exceeds accessibility threshold limits at the door swing path
conditions: When installed at an egress door or accessible entrance

subject: Entrance Mat/Grid
rule: Entrance mat/grid must have adequate drainage or weep paths to prevent standing water accumulation
conditions: When installed in an exterior or covered entrance exposed to moisture

subject: Entrance Mat/Grid
rule: Entrance mat/grid must be fabricated from materials with sufficient load-bearing capacity for the anticipated traffic and point loads (e.g., heels, cart wheels)
exceptions: Temporary lightweight mats not intended for heavy traffic

subject: Intercom/Entry Phone
rule: Intercom/Entry Phone must be connected to the building's electrical power supply
conditions: when installed as a hardwired unit
exceptions: battery-powered wireless units

subject: Intercom/Entry Phone
rule: Intercom/Entry Phone must be installed within reach of its wiring or wireless range to the door/gate it controls

subject: Intercom/Entry Phone
rule: Intercom/Entry Phone must not be installed in a fully enclosed space with no means of dissipating heat if it generates heat during operation
conditions: when the unit has active electronics that generate heat
exceptions: units rated for enclosed/waterproof installation with passive cooling design

subject: Entrance Threshold
rule: Entrance threshold must have a slip-resistant surface
conditions: when threshold is exposed to weather
when threshold is in a public or accessible route
exceptions: temporary thresholds used only during construction

subject: Entrance Threshold
rule: Entrance threshold must not create a trip hazard exceeding allowable height differential
conditions: where building code (e.g., ADA, IBC) applies
exceptions: existing historical buildings where full compliance is exempted by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Entrance Threshold
rule: Entrance threshold must be weather-sealed against water intrusion
conditions: when threshold separates exterior from conditioned interior space
exceptions: fully sheltered entrances not exposed to rain or snowmelt

subject: Paving Surface
rule: paving surface must have a cross-fall or gradient (typically 1–2%) to ensure positive drainage
conditions: paving surface is exposed to rainfall
paving surface is outdoors
exceptions: paving surface is an internal/indoor floor finish
paving surface is designed as a level retention/passive water storage system

subject: Paving Surface
rule: paving surface must not have a slope steeper than the material's maximum safe gradient (typically 1:12 for pedestrian, 1:20 for wheelchair accessible)
conditions: paving surface is intended for pedestrian or wheelchair use
exceptions: paving surface is specifically designed as a stepped ramp (e.g., in landscape architecture)

subject: Paving Surface
rule: paving surface must have a minimum thickness adequate for its intended load (e.g., concrete pavers ≥ 60 mm for vehicular traffic, ≥ 40 mm for pedestrian)
conditions: paving surface is load-bearing for vehicular or pedestrian traffic
exceptions: paving surface is purely decorative / non-traffic

subject: Paving Surface
rule: paving surface must not have abrupt level changes or trip hazards exceeding 6 mm (1/4 inch) in pedestrian areas
conditions: paving surface is in a publicly accessible pedestrian route
exceptions: paving surface at construction joints designed with chamfered edges ≤ 1:2 slope

subject: Parking Stall Striping
rule: Parking stall striping must have a minimum stripe width of 4 inches (100 mm) for standard parking stalls
conditions: Applies to standard automobile parking stalls in asphalt or concrete pavement
exceptions: Compact car stalls may use 3-inch minimum width stripes

subject: Parking Stall Striping
rule: Parking stall striping must contrast with the pavement surface
conditions: Applies to all painted or taped parking stall markings on any paved surface
exceptions: N/A

subject: Parking Stall Striping
rule: Parking stall striping must be slip-resistant when wet
conditions: Applies to all striping materials applied to vehicular traffic surfaces
exceptions: N/A

subject: Parking Stall Striping
rule: Parking stall striping must not contain raised or protruding elements that exceed 0.25 inches above the pavement surface
conditions: Applies to all striping methods including paint, thermoplastic, tape, and raised pavement markers used for stall delineation
exceptions: Detectable warning surfaces at pedestrian crossings are not considered striping and are excluded

subject: Wheel Stop
rule: wheel stop must prevent vehicle from contacting the building or structure beyond it
conditions: when installed as a parking or barrier element

subject: Wheel Stop
rule: wheel stop must be anchored to the ground/pavement to resist horizontal impact forces without displacement
conditions: when installed in vehicular traffic areas

subject: Wheel Stop
rule: wheel stop must not exceed maximum allowable height as specified by accessibility codes
conditions: when installed in pedestrian-accessible areas such as parking lots

subject: Curb and Gutter
rule: Curb and gutter must maintain a continuous positive slope toward the inlet or drainage point
conditions: When designed for stormwater conveyance
exceptions: When gutter is designed as a level or sump condition with a dedicated drainage system

subject: Curb and Gutter
rule: Curb and gutter must have a minimum height differential between the flow line and the top of curb to contain design storm runoff
conditions: When curb acts as a barrier to vehicular overtopping of stormwater
exceptions: Mountable curb designs for driveway crossings or specific low-speed urban contexts

subject: Curb and Gutter
rule: Curb and gutter must not have a reverse grade or sag that creates a closed depression without an overflow path
conditions: Along any continuous run of curb and gutter
exceptions: When designed as a deliberate detention/sump inlet with engineered overflow

subject: Parking Lot Signage
rule: parking lot signage must be clearly visible from approaching vehicles under all lighting conditions (day, night, and adverse weather)
conditions: signage is intended to guide or regulate vehicular traffic

subject: Parking Lot Signage
rule: parking lot signage must not obstruct the sight lines of drivers or pedestrians at intersections, crosswalks, or access aisles

subject: Parking Lot Signage
rule: parking lot signage must be mounted at a height that does not create a head-strike hazard for pedestrians
conditions: signage is located in pedestrian-accessible areas
exceptions: sign is protected by a physical barrier or guard that prevents pedestrian contact

subject: Parking Lot Signage
rule: parking lot signage must comply with minimum reflectivity/retroreflectivity standards for night-time legibility
conditions: signage is used for regulatory or wayfinding purposes and is intended to be read at night

subject: Entry and Exit Driveways
rule: Entry and exit driveways must have a minimum width of 3.0 meters (10 feet) for one-way traffic
exceptions: Narrower widths may be permitted for single residential driveways serving one dwelling unit where local zoning allows

subject: Entry and Exit Driveways
rule: Entry and exit driveways must not have a slope exceeding 15% (1:6.67) for paved driveways
conditions: applies to paved residential and commercial driveways
exceptions: Steeper slopes may be permitted for very short ramp segments with speed control measures

subject: Entry and Exit Driveways
rule: Entry and exit driveways must have a clear sight distance at the intersection with the public roadway
conditions: applies where driveway meets a public street or road
exceptions: Properties with permanent traffic control devices (signals, stop signs) at the driveway entrance may have modified requirements

subject: Entry and Exit Driveways
rule: Entry and exit driveways must not cross or be located within the clear zone of fire hydrants

subject: Entry and Exit Driveways
rule: Entry and exit driveways must have a maximum grade change without transition of no more than 8% difference between adjacent segments
conditions: applies to paved driveways with vertical curves

subject: Parking Lot Landscaping
rule: parking lot landscaping must not block sight lines for vehicular and pedestrian traffic at driveways, intersections, and pedestrian crossings
conditions: landscaping elements are taller than 0.6 m (2 ft) within sight triangles
exceptions: landscaping consists solely of trees with canopies trimmed to maintain visibility below 2.4 m (8 ft) and trunks less than 0.15 m (6 in) diameter

subject: Parking Lot Landscaping
rule: parking lot landscaping must not obstruct fire apparatus access lanes and turnaround areas
conditions: landscaping is located within a designated fire lane or fire apparatus access route

subject: Parking Lot Landscaping
rule: parking lot landscaping stormwater management features (e.g., bioretention cells, rain gardens) must have an overflow outlet that conveys runoff to a lawful point of discharge without flooding adjacent property
conditions: landscaping includes stormwater management or low-impact development (LID) facilities
exceptions: the facility is designed to fully contain and infiltrate the 100-year, 24-hour storm event on site

subject: Parking Lot Landscaping
rule: parking lot landscaping trees must not be planted directly above or within the root zone of underground utilities (water, sewer, gas, electric, communications)
conditions: trees are part of the parking lot landscaping
exceptions: root barriers and utility-protection measures approved by the utility authority are installed

subject: Parking Barrier or Gate
rule: a parking barrier or gate must withstand the design wind load for its location
conditions: Permanent installation
Outdoor location

subject: Parking Barrier or Gate
rule: a parking barrier or gate must not obstruct required emergency egress paths or fire lanes when in the open position
conditions: Installed across a path designated for egress or fire access

subject: Parking Barrier or Gate
rule: a powered parking barrier or gate must have a manual release mechanism that functions without electrical power
conditions: Gate or barrier is powered (electric/hydraulic)

subject: Parking Barrier or Gate
rule: a parking barrier or gate must not descend or close on a vehicle or pedestrian during normal operation
exceptions: Controlled descent with obstacle detection and automatic reversal per safety standards (e.g., UL 325)

subject: Parking Lot Bicycle Rack
rule: bicycle rack must be securely anchored to the ground or supporting structure
conditions: rack is freestanding
rack is exposed to wind or incidental contact
exceptions: temporary/portable racks used during special events where anchoring would damage pavement

subject: Parking Lot Bicycle Rack
rule: bicycle rack must accommodate the frame of a standard adult bicycle without wheel-only support
conditions: rack is intended for permanent public or commercial installation

subject: Parking Lot Bicycle Rack
rule: bicycle rack must not obstruct minimum pathway clearance of 1.2 m (48 in)
conditions: rack is placed adjacent to pedestrian walkways or building entrances

subject: Parking Lot Bicycle Rack
rule: bicycle rack must not have sharp edges, protruding bolts, or pinch points at user contact height
conditions: rack is intended for public or employee use

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
rule: EV charging station must have a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) for each output connector
conditions: station is grid-connected
output is AC or DC

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
rule: EV charging station must not be installed in a location where charging cable can be driven over by vehicles not intended to charge
conditions: station is at-grade or in a parking area shared with moving traffic
exceptions: cable is routed in a protective conduit or trench that prevents vehicle contact

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
rule: EV charging station must have a ventilation system if using lead-acid or nickel-cadmium batteries for onboard energy storage
conditions: station includes internal battery storage
battery chemistry is lead-acid or NiCd
exceptions: storage is Li-ion or other sealed chemistry that does not vent hydrogen

subject: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
rule: EV charging station must have an enclosure rated for the intended outdoor environment (minimum NEMA 3R)
conditions: station is installed outdoors

subject: Parking Lot Base and Sub-base
rule: parking lot base and sub-base must provide adequate load-bearing capacity for the intended vehicle load (passenger cars, trucks, or buses)

subject: Parking Lot Base and Sub-base
rule: parking lot base and sub-base must have a minimum thickness to prevent frost heave in frost-susceptible soils
conditions: location is in a climate with seasonal freezing temperatures
subgrade soils are frost-susceptible
exceptions: subgrade is non-frost-susceptible
location has no freezing conditions

subject: Parking Lot Base and Sub-base
rule: parking lot base and sub-base must be compacted to the specified density to prevent excessive settlement

subject: Parking Lot Base and Sub-base
rule: parking lot base and sub-base must provide positive drainage to prevent water accumulation within the pavement structure

subject: Accessible Parking Space Compliance
rule: Accessible parking spaces must have a minimum width of 96 inches (8 ft) and an adjacent access aisle of at least 60 inches (5 ft) width
conditions: For van-accessible spaces, access aisle must be on passenger side

subject: Accessible Parking Space Compliance
rule: Accessible parking spaces must have a surface that is stable, firm, and slip-resistant
conditions: Applies to all accessible parking spaces

subject: Accessible Parking Space Compliance
rule: Accessible parking space surface slope must not exceed 1:48 (2.08%) in any direction
conditions: Measured in both the parking space and the adjacent access aisle

subject: Accessible Parking Space Compliance
rule: Accessible parking spaces must be identified by a sign with the International Symbol of Accessibility mounted at least 60 inches above the ground
conditions: Van-accessible spaces require an additional 'Van-Accessible' sign

subject: Erosion and Sediment Control
rule: erosion and sediment control measures must be installed before land-disturbing activities begin
conditions: site involves earth disturbance
construction or grading activities
exceptions: emergency situations where immediate action is needed to prevent greater harm

subject: Erosion and Sediment Control
rule: erosion and sediment control measures must remain in place and functional until the disturbed area is permanently stabilized
conditions: sediment basin
silt fence
inlet protection
or other temporary control is installed
exceptions: area has achieved final stabilization and vegetation is established per regulatory criteria

subject: Erosion and Sediment Control
rule: stormwater runoff must not bypass sediment control measures
conditions: concentrated flow paths exist on site

subject: Erosion and Sediment Control
rule: sediment basin outlet structures must have adequate capacity to convey the design storm without overtopping
conditions: sediment basin is used as primary control

subject: Site Drainage and Grading
rule: The site must have a positive drainage slope away from all building foundations
conditions: Where a building is present on the site
exceptions: Sites where engineered waterproofing and drainage systems (e.g., French drains, sump pumps) are designed to handle neutral or negative slope

subject: Site Drainage and Grading
rule: The finished grade must not create ponding or standing water within the site's habitable or useable areas
conditions: Within areas designated for occupation, circulation, or parking
exceptions: Intentionally designed stormwater management features such as detention basins, rain gardens, or retention ponds

subject: Site Drainage and Grading
rule: The site must have a continuous, unobstructed drainage path to a lawful point of discharge
conditions: For all impervious surfaces (roofs, paved areas, terraces)
exceptions: Sites where all runoff is captured in a closed system (cistern, closed-loop stormwater tank) for reuse or controlled release

subject: Site Drainage and Grading
rule: The finish grade elevation at the building perimeter must not be higher than the finished floor elevation
conditions: At any point within 300 mm (12 inches) of exterior walls with habitable space
exceptions: Where a secondary drainage system (area drain, trench drain) and waterproof barrier system is installed with redundant capacity

subject: Geotextile and Geogrid
rule: geotextile or geogrid must not be placed directly on an unprepared or uncompacted subgrade
conditions: when used as a separation or stabilization layer in pavement or earthwork applications

subject: Geotextile and Geogrid
rule: geotextile or geogrid must have a minimum overlap at joints/seams when placed in successive rolls
conditions: when multiple rolls are installed adjacent to each other in a reinforcement or separation application
exceptions: factory-bonded or mechanically joined seams that are tested to equivalent strength

subject: Geotextile and Geogrid
rule: geotextile must be protected from direct UV exposure beyond the material's rated duration
conditions: when the geotextile is left exposed before covering in construction staging
exceptions: UV-stabilized geotextile products specifically rated for extended exposure

subject: South-Facing Terrace
rule: a South-Facing Terrace must have a minimum depth of at least 1.5 m to be usable as an occupiable outdoor space
conditions: terrace is intended for occupancy or outdoor amenity use

subject: South-Facing Terrace
rule: a South-Facing Terrace must have a slip-resistant walking surface with a slip resistance value (e.g., COF ≥ 0.6 when wet) to prevent fall injuries
conditions: terrace is accessible to occupants
exceptions: temporary construction or maintenance-only terraces not open to occupancy

subject: South-Facing Terrace
rule: a South-Facing Terrace must not have ponding water; the finished surface must slope away from the building at minimum 1:48 (2%) to ensure positive drainage

subject: South-Facing Terrace
rule: a South-Facing Terrace must have a guardrail or parapet at least 1.07 m (42 inches) high where the drop exceeds 0.6 m (24 inches)
conditions: terrace is elevated more than 0.6 m above adjacent grade or surface

subject: South-Facing Balcony
rule: south-facing balcony must have a minimum depth to be usable
conditions: balcony is intended for occupation or use
exceptions: balcony is purely decorative/ornamental

subject: South-Facing Balcony
rule: south-facing balcony must have a waterproof deck surface and proper drainage away from the building envelope
conditions: balcony is exposed to rain or precipitation
exceptions: balcony is fully enclosed and weatherproofed as an internal space

subject: South-Facing Balcony
rule: south-facing balcony must have a guardrail or balustrade if elevated more than 600 mm above grade
conditions: balcony floor is more than 600 mm above adjacent ground or surface

subject: South-Facing Balcony
rule: south-facing balcony must not have a solid parapet or overhang that fully blocks direct sunlight during the intended use period
conditions: balcony is intended for solar access, passive heating, or daylighting
exceptions: shading is intentionally designed for overheating control in hot climates

subject: South-Facing Roof Terrace
rule: A south-facing roof terrace must have a drainage system that directs water away from the building envelope and prevents ponding
conditions: Located at roof level
Outdoor or semi-outdoor space
exceptions: Terrace is covered by an impermeable canopy with separate drainage that sheds water away from the terrace surface

subject: South-Facing Roof Terrace
rule: The terrace surface must have a minimum slope (typically 1-2%) toward drainage points to prevent standing water
conditions: Terrace is exposed to rain or snow melt
Drainage relies on gravity flow
exceptions: Terrace uses a siphonic or pumped drainage system that can remove water from a flat surface

subject: South-Facing Roof Terrace
rule: A south-facing roof terrace must not have drainage outlets that discharge onto pedestrian areas or public right-of-way below without proper diversion
conditions: Terrace is at a height above ground level
Discharge point is above pedestrian zones
exceptions: Discharge is directed through downspouts or scuppers routed to an enclosed stormwater system
Discharge is onto a vegetated area designed to absorb the runoff

subject: South-Facing Courtyard
rule: south-facing courtyard must have an unobstructed southern exposure to receive direct sunlight
conditions: courtyard is intended for passive solar gain
courtyard is located in a climate where winter heating is beneficial
exceptions: site topography or legal easements permanently block southern light

subject: South-Facing Courtyard
rule: courtyard must provide a minimum clear floor area of 2m in any horizontal dimension to be usable as outdoor space
conditions: courtyard is intended for human occupancy or passage
exceptions: courtyard is purely decorative and not accessible

subject: South-Facing Courtyard
rule: courtyard must not have a roof or overhead enclosure that fully covers it
conditions: space is classified as a courtyard rather than an atrium or interior court
exceptions: partial overhead shading structures (pergolas, trellises) that leave more than 50% of the area open to the sky

subject: South-Facing Veranda
rule: a south-facing veranda must have a roof or canopy providing overhead weather protection
conditions: veranda is open to the sky
veranda is attached to habitable interior spaces
exceptions: veranda is purely decorative/non-functional and not meant for occupancy

subject: South-Facing Veranda
rule: south-facing veranda roof or canopy must have a drainage path that directs water away from the building foundation
conditions: veranda has a solid roof or canopy
exceptions: roof is permeable/grille-type with no water collection surface

subject: South-Facing Veranda
rule: veranda floor surface must not slope toward the adjacent interior wall
conditions: veranda is adjacent to a habitable interior space
veranda is uncovered or partially covered
exceptions: a physical threshold or drainage channel separates veranda from interior

subject: South-Facing Veranda
rule: south-facing veranda in northern hemisphere climates with freeze-thaw cycles must have a minimum roof overhang depth adequate to protect the veranda floor from snow accumulation and ice damming
conditions: climate zone experiences below-freezing temperatures
veranda is attached to a heated building
exceptions: veranda roof is designed as a cold roof with separate snow shedding strategy

subject: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure
rule: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure must be positioned to the south of the building elements it shades
conditions: structure is intended to provide shading

subject: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure
rule: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure must be designed to allow rainwater drainage so water does not pond or collect

subject: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure
rule: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure must be structurally attached or supported such that it can resist wind uplift and gravity loads

subject: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure
rule: South-Facing Sun Shade Structure must not block required egress paths or emergency access
conditions: structure is located near openings, walkways, or fire access routes

subject: South-Facing Glazed Screen
rule: south-facing glazed screen must have a solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC) appropriate to the climate zone and building use, or include external shading to prevent overheating
conditions: the screen is part of a conditioned space envelope
the screen has direct solar exposure
exceptions: the screen is secondary (non-envelope) and does not separate conditioned from unconditioned space

subject: South-Facing Glazed Screen
rule: south-facing glazed screen must not cause dangerous glare or reflective concentration onto adjacent buildings, pedestrians, or traffic
conditions: the screen uses highly reflective or mirrored glazing
the screen is at a height and angle that can reflect sunlight to ground level or neighboring occupied spaces
exceptions: the screen is located where no adjacent publicly accessible areas or traffic routes exist within the reflection zone

subject: South-Facing Glazed Screen
rule: south-facing glazed screen must withstand wind loads calculated for its location and exposure
conditions: the screen is part of the building envelope or a freestanding structure above grade

subject: South-Facing Glazed Screen
rule: south-facing glazed screen must not use annealed glass in locations where human impact is possible unless it is fully protected by a guardrail or located out of reach
conditions: the screen is installed at heights accessible to building occupants or the public
the glazing is vertical or near-vertical and within 900 mm of a walking surface
exceptions: the glass is laminated and designed to remain in place if broken
a permanent protective barrier prevents human contact

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must be structurally anchored to a load-bearing surface (deck, balcony, or foundation)
conditions: installed on any building surface

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must have a minimum height of 36 inches (0.91 m) above the walking surface
conditions: serving as a guardrail on a residential deck or balcony with a drop greater than 30 inches
exceptions: commercial/industrial applications may require 42 inches

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must have balusters or infill spaced such that a 4-inch (102 mm) sphere cannot pass through
conditions: used as a guardrail with vertical balusters or infill panels

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must not have horizontal rails or climbing aids on the guardrail face that could be used as a ladder
conditions: installed as a guardrail on a surface with a drop greater than 30 inches
exceptions: if the railing is purely decorative and not required as a guardrail

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must be capable of resisting a concentrated load of 200 lbs (0.89 kN) applied at any point
conditions: used as a guardrail

subject: South-Facing Railing System
rule: south-facing railing system must not obstruct required egress paths or emergency access from the south-facing side
conditions: installed in front of doors, windows, or pathways that serve as egress points on the south facade
exceptions: if the railing incorporates a self-opening gate of sufficient width

subject: South-Facing Outdoor Drainage System
rule: drainage system must have a continuous gravity-driven flow path from collection points to outlet
conditions: system is installed on a sloped site
system relies on gravity flow
exceptions: system includes active pumping components that override gravity

subject: South-Facing Outdoor Drainage System
rule: drainage system must not terminate discharge within the building's foundation zone or against the building envelope
conditions: system discharges onto or near the ground surface
exceptions: discharge is into a sealed, code-compliant drywell or approved stormwater management structure designed to safely handle volumes away from foundations

subject: South-Facing Outdoor Drainage System
rule: surface drainage system must be graded at a minimum slope of 1% (1/8 inch per foot) away from all adjacent structures
conditions: system is a surface swale or overland flow path
adjacent to any habitable building structure
exceptions: site is entirely flat and positive drainage is achieved through subsurface drains or mechanical means

subject: Roof Terrace
rule: roof terrace must have a drainage path to prevent water accumulation and structural overload
conditions: terrace is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: terrace is fully enclosed by a waterproof roof structure above

subject: Roof Terrace
rule: roof terrace must have a fall-protection barrier at any open edge where the drop height exceeds 600 mm
conditions: terrace has an unguarded perimeter edge
adjacent surface is more than 600 mm below
exceptions: terrace is only accessible for maintenance via ladder and not intended as an occupiable space

subject: Roof Terrace
rule: roof terrace must not have a surface slope steeper than the drainage gradient required by the roofing membrane manufacturer
conditions: terrace surface is finished with a walking membrane or pavers

subject: Loggia
rule: loggia floor must have a minimum slope for drainage away from the adjacent building facade
conditions: loggia is uncovered or exposed to rain
exceptions: loggia is fully enclosed and weatherproofed

subject: Loggia
rule: loggia must have a minimum clear depth to allow functional egress or passage
conditions: loggia serves as a required means of egress or exit path
exceptions: loggia is decorative/unoccupiable and not part of egress

subject: Loggia
rule: loggia floor structure must be designed for the design live load per occupancy classification
conditions: loggia is occupiable

subject: Patio
rule: patio surface must slope away from the building foundation
conditions: patio is adjacent to a building
exceptions: patio has a drainage channel/gutter system at the building edge
patio has a waterproof membrane transition at the foundation

subject: Patio
rule: patio surface must have a minimum cross-slope of 1% (1/8 inch per foot) for drainage
conditions: patio is uncovered (no roof/awning above)
exceptions: patio is designed with a sloped structural deck and positive drainage system

subject: Patio
rule: patio must not be located over a septic tank or leach field
conditions: site has a septic system

subject: Deck
rule: deck must have a minimum live load capacity of 40 psf (1.92 kN/m²) for residential use (or 100 psf for assembly/occupancy) per building code
conditions: deck is accessible for occupancy
exceptions: decks designed for storage-only or ornamental use with restricted access

subject: Deck
rule: deck must have guardrails if the deck surface is more than 30 inches above adjacent grade
conditions: deck is elevated more than 30 inches above grade

subject: Deck
rule: deck guardrail balusters must not allow passage of a 4-inch diameter sphere
conditions: deck has guardrails
deck is more than 30 inches above grade

subject: Deck
rule: deck must have a means of egress that does not require passing through another dwelling unit
conditions: deck serves as required egress path
deck is part of a multi-unit building
exceptions: decks serving only one dwelling unit with direct exit to exterior

subject: Deck
rule: deck ledger attachment to building structure must be capable of resisting full lateral and gravity loads
conditions: deck is attached to a building wall
exceptions: freestanding decks with independent support system

subject: Veranda
rule: veranda floor must have a minimum slope away from the building for drainage
conditions: veranda is exposed to rain
veranda has a solid floor surface
exceptions: veranda is fully enclosed and weatherproofed

subject: Veranda
rule: veranda roof must have a positive drainage path to clear rainwater
conditions: veranda has a roof
exceptions: veranda roof is designed as a living green roof with controlled drainage system
veranda is fully interior/atrium condition and not exposed to weather

subject: Veranda
rule: veranda must not have an enclosed ceiling without ventilation or access to roof drainage
conditions: veranda has a solid roof with an enclosed soffit or ceiling below
exceptions: veranda roof assembly includes accessible gutters and overflow drains

subject: Outdoor Walkway
rule: outdoor walkway surface must be slip-resistant when wet
conditions: location is in climate region with precipitation
walkway is exposed to rain or snow
exceptions: walkway is covered by an opaque roof that prevents any moisture reaching the surface

subject: Outdoor Walkway
rule: outdoor walkway must have a minimum width of 36 inches (915 mm)
conditions: walkway is intended for pedestrian access
exceptions: walkway serves maintenance-only access with no public or occupant use

subject: Outdoor Walkway
rule: outdoor walkway must not have a cross-slope exceeding 2%
conditions: walkway is intended for pedestrian use
walkway is not designed as a ramp
exceptions: walkway is specifically designed as an accessible ramp complying with maximum slope requirements

subject: Outdoor Walkway
rule: outdoor walkway must have a running slope of 5% or less if not designed as a ramp
conditions: walkway is intended for pedestrian use
exceptions: walkway is designed and signed as an accessible ramp with handrails

subject: Outdoor Walkway
rule: outdoor walkway must be free of protruding objects in the path of travel below 80 inches (2030 mm)
conditions: walkway is intended for pedestrian use
exceptions: objects are cane-detectable (extend to within 15 inches of the ground) or are mounted with clear headroom

subject: Green Roof
rule: green roof must have a waterproof membrane beneath the growing medium
conditions: intensive green roof
extensive green roof

subject: Green Roof
rule: green roof must have a root barrier layer
conditions: intensive green roof
extensive green roof

subject: Green Roof
rule: green roof must have a drainage layer
conditions: intensive green roof
extensive green roof

subject: Green Roof
rule: green roof slope must not exceed the maximum allowable slope for the selected green roof system
exceptions: slopes exceeding system limits may be possible with additional stabilization measures such as battens, cross-slope retention, or terraced systems

subject: Green Roof
rule: green roof growing medium depth must be sufficient to support the specified plant species

subject: Outdoor Drainage System
rule: outdoor drainage system must have a continuous gravity-flow path from catchment area to discharge point
conditions: system relies on gravity drainage
drainage is surface- or shallow-sub-surface
exceptions: system uses active pumping for all flow

subject: Outdoor Drainage System
rule: outdoor drainage system must not discharge onto adjacent property in a manner that causes concentrated flow or erosion
conditions: system outlet is within the property boundary
adjacent property is not designed to receive the flow
exceptions: an established drainage easement or shared stormwater agreement exists with the neighbour

subject: Outdoor Drainage System
rule: outdoor drainage system must have inlet capacity equal to or greater than the design storm runoff at each collection point
conditions: system is designed for a specified storm return period

subject: Outdoor Drainage System
rule: outdoor drainage system must not have trapped sections where water cannot drain by gravity and cannot be flushed
conditions: system includes enclosed pipe runs
system does not include active pumping
exceptions: trapped sections are provided with cleanouts and positive means of evacuation (e.g., sump pump)

subject: Rain Screen Cladding
rule: rain screen cladding must provide a ventilated and drained cavity behind the cladding panel to allow moisture that penetrates the outer surface to drain out and dry
conditions: building envelope designed to manage moisture penetration

subject: Rain Screen Cladding
rule: rain screen cladding must not rely solely on sealant or gaskets at all panel joints as the primary water barrier
conditions: system is classified as a pressure-equalized rain screen
exceptions: compartmentalized systems where each panel is individually sealed and drained

subject: Rain Screen Cladding
rule: rain screen cladding must include continuous air barrier and water-resistive barrier on the inner layer (sheathing/structural wall) behind the drained cavity
conditions: system separates exterior cladding from interior conditioned space

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixtures
rule: Outdoor lighting fixtures must be rated for wet or damp locations (IP65 minimum for damp, IP66+ for direct wet exposure)
conditions: Fixture is installed outdoors
Fixture is exposed to rain, snow, or moisture
exceptions: Fixture is mounted under a fully covered, fully enclosed weatherproof overhang that keeps it completely dry at all times

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixtures
rule: Outdoor lighting fixtures must not have exposed live electrical parts or unsealed connections accessible to touch
conditions: Fixture is installed in a location reachable by people or animals
Fixture is at or below 8 ft (2.4 m) mounting height
exceptions: Fixture is within a locked/secure enclosure not accessible without tools

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixtures
rule: Outdoor lighting fixtures must be grounded (earth-bonded) to the building's electrical grounding system
conditions: Fixture operates at line voltage (>50 V AC or >120 V DC)
Fixture has a metallic enclosure or exposed conductive parts
exceptions: Fixture is Class II (double-insulated) with no exposed metal and is certified as such

subject: Railing and Balustrade
rule: railing and balustrade must have a top rail with a minimum height to prevent falls
conditions: when serving as a fall protection barrier
when located at a drop-off edge
when adjacent to stairs, landings, balconies, or mezzanines
exceptions: handrail-only configurations not serving as guardrails
guards in industrial areas with different safety codes

subject: Railing and Balustrade
rule: railing and balustrade must have infill elements spaced to prevent passage of a sphere of specified diameter
conditions: when used as a guardrail or fall barrier
exceptions: certain industrial or agricultural applications with different spacing requirements

subject: Railing and Balustrade
rule: railing and balustrade must be capable of resisting the design live load without failure
conditions: when installed as a guardrail or barrier
exceptions: decorative non-structural railings that do not serve as barriers

subject: Railing and Balustrade
rule: railing and balustrade must not have discontinuous or protruding elements at the top rail that could catch clothing or cause injury
conditions: when located in a means of egress
when accessible to the public
exceptions: historically protected installations where full compliance is infeasible

subject: Outdoor Paving
rule: outdoor paving must have a minimum slope of 1% (1:100) for drainage
conditions: paving is exposed to rain or precipitation
paving is installed on grade or on a drainage plane
exceptions: paving is designed as permeable/porous where water infiltrates directly into subgrade and standing water is acceptable

subject: Outdoor Paving
rule: outdoor paving must not create a tripping hazard at transitions
conditions: paving abuts another surface (e.g., turf, walkway, curb, building threshold)
paving is intended for pedestrian use
exceptions: paving is designed with a deliberate level change that is clearly marked and compliant with accessibility codes

subject: Outdoor Paving
rule: outdoor paving must have a base/subbase capable of supporting design loads without excessive settlement
conditions: paving supports vehicular loads OR heavy pedestrian traffic
exceptions: paving is purely decorative and not intended to bear traffic loads

subject: Trellis and Pergola Structure
rule: trellis or pergola structure must be self-supporting or attached to a stable structure
conditions: standalone installation
wall-mounted installation

subject: Trellis and Pergola Structure
rule: pergola roof slats or louvered members must not create ponding water risk
conditions: pergola has a solid or close-spaced roof covering
exceptions: structure designed specifically for rainwater harvesting with controlled drainage

subject: Trellis and Pergola Structure
rule: trellis must not exceed its structural load capacity for climbing plants or attached objects
conditions: trellis is intended to support climbing plants, vines, or hung planters

subject: Trellis and Pergola Structure
rule: pergola structure must have sufficient ground anchorage or ballast to resist overturning from wind uplift
conditions: freestanding pergola in an open location
exceptions: pergola that is fully enclosed and engineered to a different lateral system

subject: Built-in Bench
rule: built-in bench must have a horizontal seating surface with a minimum depth of 300 mm (12 in) for sit-ability
conditions: intended for sitting use

subject: Built-in Bench
rule: built-in bench must not have sharp edges or exposed corners on seating surface within reachable ergonomic zone
conditions: accessible to occupants
exceptions: decorative feature zones clearly marked as non-seating

subject: Built-in Bench
rule: built-in bench must be supported by a structural substrate capable of carrying the minimum live load of 1.5 kN/m² (approx 30 psf) for residential seating
conditions: serving as permanent seating

subject: Built-in Bench
rule: built-in bench must have a minimum clear height of 400 mm (16 in) from finished floor to top of seat
conditions: intended for standard adult seating
exceptions: children's areas where lower height is intentional and specified

subject: Fixed Canopy
rule: fixed canopy must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: canopy is flat or near-flat
exceptions: canopy is designed as a 'green roof' with integrated drainage layer

subject: Fixed Canopy
rule: fixed canopy structural frame must not deflect under design snow or wind load beyond allowable limit
conditions: canopy is located in a climate region with code-defined snow or wind loads

subject: Fixed Canopy
rule: fixed canopy attachment to main building must resist uplift forces
conditions: canopy is attached to a building wall or structure
exceptions: freestanding canopy with independent foundation designed for uplift

subject: Fixed Canopy
rule: fixed canopy glazing or panels must not be susceptible to thermal stress fracture
conditions: canopy includes glass or other brittle panel materials
canopy is exposed to direct solar radiation

subject: Fixed Canopy
rule: fixed canopy must not collect debris that blocks drainage
conditions: canopy is located near trees or in environments with airborne debris

subject: Light-Transmitting Roof Structure
rule: light-transmitting roof structure must have a drainage path

subject: Light-Transmitting Roof Structure
rule: light-transmitting roof structure must be capable of supporting its own weight plus live loads (snow, rain, maintenance) without collapse

subject: Light-Transmitting Roof Structure
rule: light-transmitting roof structure must not allow uncontrolled water ingress at joints and seals

subject: Structural Wing Canopy
rule: structural wing canopy must be securely attached to the main building structure at its root connection
conditions: cantilevered design
side-attached canopy
exceptions: freestanding canopy not attached to a building

subject: Structural Wing Canopy
rule: structural wing canopy must have a minimum of 2 points of lateral restraint to prevent flutter or wind-induced oscillation
conditions: span-to-depth ratio exceeds 10
located in wind zone with basic wind speed > 40 m/s

subject: Structural Wing Canopy
rule: structural wing canopy surface must not collect standing water
exceptions: intentionally designed as a water feature with waterproofed structure

subject: Structural Wing Canopy
rule: structural wing canopy must provide a fall protection barrier or comply with building code edge protection requirements where the open edge is more than 600 mm above accessible grade
conditions: canopy is accessible to people
edge height exceeds 600 mm above adjacent walking surface
exceptions: canopy is solely decorative and has no accessible surface area

subject: Integrated Daylight Control Louvers
rule: Integrated daylight control louvers must be mounted at an angle that prevents direct water ingress into the building interior through the louver assembly
conditions: when used in a building envelope assembly
when located on a facade or roof exposed to precipitation
exceptions: when the louvers are part of a fully sealed, gasketed curtain wall system rated for water penetration resistance

subject: Integrated Daylight Control Louvers
rule: Integrated daylight control louvers must not obstruct required means of egress or emergency exit pathways
conditions: when louvers are installed in or adjacent to egress paths
when the louver assembly projects into a required clear width or height of an exit corridor, door, or stair
exceptions: when code explicitly allows fixed or operable louvers within a defined encroachment zone, such as up to 4 inches from the wall face per IBC

subject: Integrated Daylight Control Louvers
rule: The louver blade profile and spacing must prevent the passage of birds or large debris that could block drainage or accumulate within the louver cavity
conditions: when louvers are installed in an exterior wall or roof opening without bird screen or debris mesh
exceptions: when a dedicated bird screen or debris filter is installed separately upstream of the louver

subject: Light Shelf Assembly
rule: light shelf assembly must be mounted at a vertical angle that allows both direct sun rejection (summer) and daylight redirection (winter) without exceeding the assembly's structural load capacity
conditions: when used as part of a daylighting system with seasonal solar control requirements

subject: Light Shelf Assembly
rule: light shelf assembly must not be installed lower than the top of the window opening it serves
conditions: when configured as an interior or exterior horizontal light shelf for daylight harvesting

subject: Light Shelf Assembly
rule: light shelf assembly must be rated for the expected wind uplift/suction load at its mounting location when installed externally
conditions: when mounted on an exterior façade in a wind-exposed zone

subject: Glazed Curtain Wall System
rule: A glazed curtain wall must be structurally anchored to the building's main structural frame at each floor level or at intervals specified by structural engineering
conditions: System is used as an exterior building enclosure
System spans multiple stories
exceptions: Structural silicone glazed (SSG) systems where the mullions are designed as continuous spanning members from foundation to roof

subject: Glazed Curtain Wall System
rule: A glazed curtain wall must accommodate inter-story drift and differential movement between floors without glass breakage or loss of seal integrity
conditions: Building is subject to wind loads, seismic loads, or thermal expansion cycles

subject: Glazed Curtain Wall System
rule: A glazed curtain wall must be designed with a continuous air barrier and water barrier system that prevents uncontrolled air leakage and water penetration under a specified pressure differential
conditions: System serves as the building envelope
exceptions: Interior non-envelope applications such as atrium partitions within conditioned space

subject: Glazed Curtain Wall System
rule: A glazed curtain wall must not allow condensation within the sealed insulating glass unit (IGU) cavity under normal occupancy conditions
conditions: System uses sealed insulating glass units
exceptions: Deliberately ventilated glazing systems with engineered condensation drainage channels

subject: Etched or Fritted Glass Panels
rule: Etched or fritted glass panels must be heat-soaked to mitigate nickel-sulfide inclusion risk
conditions: when used in overhead glazing or spandrel applications where panel failure could cause injury
when glass is heat-strengthened or fully tempered
exceptions: when panels are fully laminated and the interlayer is structural enough to retain broken glass

subject: Etched or Fritted Glass Panels
rule: Etched or fritted glass panels must have the frit or etch pattern on the non-structural face or be compatible with structural sealant bond
conditions: when panels are used in structurally-glazed curtain walls

subject: Etched or Fritted Glass Panels
rule: Etched or fritted glass panels must not be used as a walking surface without anti-slip treatment
conditions: when used as a floor, stair tread, or ramp
exceptions: when a tested slip-resistant coating or surface treatment is applied that meets applicable slip-resistance standards

subject: Automated Shading Blind System
rule: Automated Shading Blind System must have a power supply or energy source to operate
conditions: System is motorized
exceptions: Manually operated shading blinds are excluded

subject: Automated Shading Blind System
rule: Automated Shading Blind System must not have moving parts that pinch or entrap users or occupants
conditions: System is installed in an occupied space within reach of occupants
exceptions: Systems with certified safety mechanisms (e.g., pinch guards, torque-limiting motors) that prevent entrapment

subject: Automated Shading Blind System
rule: Automated Shading Blind System must be rated for the environmental conditions of its installation location
conditions: System is installed outdoors or in unconditioned spaces (e.g., exterior blinds between glazing layers)
exceptions: Systems installed solely in conditioned indoor spaces

subject: Rainwater Drainage Channel
rule: rainwater drainage channel must have a continuous slope of at least 0.5% towards the outlet or collection point
conditions: gravity-flow system
exceptions: pressurized/closed conduit drainage systems

subject: Rainwater Drainage Channel
rule: rainwater drainage channel must not have a cross-section area smaller than the upstream contributing catchment's design runoff flow area
conditions: channel sized by rational method or similar hydraulic design

subject: Rainwater Drainage Channel
rule: rainwater drainage channel invert must be at or below the lowest roof outlet or surface inlet it serves
conditions: gravity-flow system
exceptions: where a sump pump or lift station is installed

subject: Rainwater Drainage Channel
rule: rainwater drainage channel must not have internal obstructions that block hydraulic flow capacity
conditions: any drainage channel
exceptions: designed debris screens or sediment traps with overflow provisions

subject: Skybridge
rule: Skybridge must have a minimum structural load capacity to support its own weight plus anticipated live loads (pedestrian traffic, wind, snow where applicable)
conditions: Used for pedestrian circulation

subject: Skybridge
rule: Skybridge must have a means of egress (emergency exit path) at both ends or otherwise comply with fire and life safety codes
conditions: Enclosed or covered, longer than minimum egress distance thresholds

subject: Skybridge
rule: Skybridge must not have a floor slope that exceeds accessibility ramp standards (typically 1:12 maximum)
conditions: Designed for public pedestrian access

subject: Skybridge
rule: Skybridge structural connections to adjoining buildings must accommodate differential movement (thermal expansion, settlement, seismic drift)

subject: Skybridge
rule: Skybridge must not block required fire-access zones or emergency vehicle clearances on the ground below

subject: Underground Tunnel
rule: underground tunnel must have a waterproofing system on all exterior surfaces
conditions: tunnel is below the water table
tunnel is in soil with measurable moisture content
exceptions: tunnel constructed entirely within dry, stable rock above the water table with negligible groundwater inflow

subject: Underground Tunnel
rule: underground tunnel must have a minimum of two independent means of egress
conditions: tunnel exceeds 25 m in length
exceptions: tunnel is a utility chase not intended for human occupancy

subject: Underground Tunnel
rule: underground tunnel must have mechanical ventilation providing positive pressure airflow
conditions: tunnel exceeds 15 m in length
tunnel is used for human occupancy
exceptions: tunnel is passively ventilated via open ends and natural stack effect is verified to meet air quality standards

subject: Underground Tunnel
rule: underground tunnel must have a drainage system that prevents water accumulation
conditions: tunnel floor is below the surrounding water table
tunnel is subject to groundwater infiltration
exceptions: tunnel is designed to allow controlled flooding (e.g., stormwater tunnel)

subject: Atrium Link
rule: an atrium link (enclosed bridge or link between buildings) must have fire-rated construction and automatic fire/smoke detection
conditions: when the link connects two or more buildings
when the link exceeds certain length thresholds defined by local building code
exceptions: if the link is an open walkway (not enclosed)
if the entire building is covered by a single fire suppression system spanning both sides

subject: Atrium Link
rule: an atrium link must not have a floor area or occupant load that reclassifies it as a habitable space without meeting egress and ventilation requirements
conditions: when the link is designated purely as a circulation/connector space
exceptions: when the link is designed and permitted as occupied programmable space with its own separate egress and ventilation

subject: Expansion Joint
rule: expansion joint must allow for differential movement between adjacent building sections
conditions: when used between structurally independent building segments
in large or long buildings
exceptions: monolithic structures without planned movement joints

subject: Expansion Joint
rule: expansion joint must be continuous through the building envelope including structure, finishes, roof membrane, and cladding
conditions: when installed as a through-building joint
exceptions: non-continuous control joints that stop at slab edges

subject: Expansion Joint
rule: expansion joint must not be blocked or filled with rigid material that prevents movement
conditions: after installation and throughout building service life
exceptions: temporary bridging during construction that is removed prior to completion

subject: Expansion Joint
rule: expansion joint must maintain a minimum gap width adequate for the expected thermal movement range
conditions: for every expansion joint designed in regions with temperature variation
exceptions: joints in strictly controlled interior environments with no thermal cycling

subject: Expansion Joint
rule: expansion joint cover or sealant must be weathertight and water-resistant when located on exterior faces or roof
conditions: when the joint is exposed to exterior conditions
exceptions: interior-only joints in dry conditioned spaces

subject: Shared Service Core
rule: Shared Service Core must provide independent, dedicated egress paths (exit stairs or doors) that discharge directly to the exterior or to a safe area, sized for the occupant load served
conditions: core contains stairs
building is more than one story
core serves occupied floors
exceptions: single-story building where core serves only ground floor with direct exit

subject: Shared Service Core
rule: Shared Service Core must maintain a minimum fire-resistance rating (typically 1–2 hours) for its enclosing walls, floors, and shaft enclosures
conditions: core contains vertical shafts (elevator, stair, mechanical)
core penetrates floor slabs
exceptions: one-story buildings without floor penetrations

subject: Shared Service Core
rule: Shared Service Core must not have unprotected openings (doors, louvers, penetrations) that breach the rated shaft enclosure on multiple floors without proper fire/smoke dampers or rated assemblies
conditions: core enclosure is fire-rated
core contains vertical penetrations
exceptions: openings protected by listed fire doors with self-closers and smoke gaskets
openings equipped with fire/smoke dampers rated per code

subject: Shared Service Core
rule: Shared Service Core must provide a minimum clear width of at least 44 inches (1120 mm) for each required stairway within the core
conditions: core contains egress stairways
stair serves more than two stories
exceptions: stair serving occupant load less than 50 per floor where building official may allow narrower width

subject: Interconnecting Corridor
rule: interconnecting corridor must have a minimum clear width of at least the building code required egress width for its occupant load
conditions: when the corridor serves as a means of egress
exceptions: when not required for egress by code

subject: Interconnecting Corridor
rule: interconnecting corridor must have a fire-resistance rating meeting the building code for the type of connection and occupancy it bridges
conditions: when it connects two separate buildings or fire compartments
exceptions: when local code exempts small or one-story interconnections

subject: Interconnecting Corridor
rule: interconnecting corridor must not have a floor level that creates a trip hazard at transitions unless ramped or level
conditions: when the corridor is accessible to pedestrians

subject: Interconnecting Corridor
rule: interconnecting corridor must be enclosed with weather-tight construction where exposed to exterior environmental conditions
conditions: when the corridor is an enclosed, conditioned space bridging between buildings
exceptions: when the corridor is deliberately designed as an open-air breezeway

subject: Shared Utility Trench
rule: Shared Utility Trench must maintain minimum separation distances from other underground utilities and structures
conditions: Where multiple utilities share a common trench
Per local code or utility coordination requirements
exceptions: Where engineered shielding or encasement is provided to prevent interference

subject: Shared Utility Trench
rule: Shared Utility Trench must be deep enough to protect utilities from surface loads and frost penetration
conditions: Trench is located in a region with freeze-thaw cycles
Trench is subject to vehicular or other surface loading
exceptions: Where utilities are frost-resistant by design
Where trench is protected by structural slab or other load-distributing system

subject: Shared Utility Trench
rule: Shared Utility Trench must not contain incompatible utility types in the same trench without proper separation or shielding
conditions: Trench contains both high-temperature utilities (e.g., steam, hot water) and temperature-sensitive utilities (e.g., chilled water, telecom, electrical)
exceptions: Where adequate insulation, shielding, or physical separation is provided per engineering analysis

subject: Shared Utility Trench
rule: Shared Utility Trench must be sloped or provided with drainage to prevent standing water accumulation
conditions: Trench is below grade and not fully sealed/waterproofed
exceptions: Trench is designed as a watertight structure with active dewatering

subject: Shared Utility Trench
rule: Shared Utility Trench must have adequate access points (manholes, handholes, pull boxes) for installation, inspection, and maintenance of all utilities within
conditions: Trench length exceeds maximum pull distance for the longest utility run within it
exceptions: Where utilities are installed via directional boring with no need for intermediate access

subject: Joint Foundation/Mat Slab
rule: mat slab thickness must be sufficient to distribute building loads without exceeding soil bearing capacity
conditions: building constructed on soil with finite bearing capacity
exceptions: building founded on solid rock with no soil layer

subject: Joint Foundation/Mat Slab
rule: mat slab reinforcement must provide continuity across construction joints
conditions: mat slab is larger than a single pour, requiring construction joints
exceptions: joint is designed as a movement/isolation joint that intentionally breaks continuity

subject: Joint Foundation/Mat Slab
rule: mat slab must not be placed directly on frost-susceptible soil without frost protection
conditions: climate zone experiences freezing temperatures
soil type is frost-susceptible (e.g., silt, clay)
exceptions: foundation is heated year-round and heat loss prevents freezing beneath slab
frost-protected shallow foundation design with perimeter insulation per code

subject: Joint Foundation/Mat Slab
rule: mat slab concrete must have adequate water-cement ratio and curing to achieve design strength before full load application
conditions: slab is designed to support full building loads
exceptions: none — concrete strength gain follows known time-temperature relationships

subject: Joint Foundation/Mat Slab
rule: joint foundation must not be constructed on expansive clay without moisture control or soil treatment measures
conditions: subgrade soil is expansive clay (high plasticity index)
exceptions: soil has been chemically treated (e.g., lime stabilization) to reduce swell potential
moisture barrier system and drainage prevent volume change under slab

subject: Common Plant Room
rule: Common Plant Room must have a minimum ceiling height of 2.4m to accommodate mechanical equipment
conditions: Room contains mechanical equipment requiring vertical clearance
Room is for active plant operation (not storage-only)

subject: Common Plant Room
rule: Common Plant Room must have a fire resistance rating of at least 90 minutes for walls and floor/ceiling assemblies
conditions: Room contains fuel-burning equipment
Room is located within a building containing occupied spaces

subject: Common Plant Room
rule: Common Plant Room must not have floor drains located directly beneath electrical equipment
conditions: Room contains electrical switchgear, panels, or motors
exceptions: Floor drain is equipped with a cover that prevents splash and is approved for such location by electrical code

subject: Common Plant Room
rule: Common Plant Room must be provided with mechanical ventilation that maintains temperature below 40°C
conditions: Room contains heat-generating mechanical equipment
exceptions: Room is a dedicated geothermal or ground-source plant room where equipment operates at lower temperatures

subject: Structural Tie Beam
rule: Structural tie beam must have continuous reinforcement through beam-column joints
conditions: beam is part of a moment-resisting frame
beam spans between columns
exceptions: non-seismic non-structural applications where tie beam is not required to resist moment

subject: Structural Tie Beam
rule: Structural tie beam must have minimum cross-sectional dimensions as specified by structural code for the span
conditions: beam is structural (load-bearing)

subject: Structural Tie Beam
rule: Structural tie beam must be connected monolithically to supporting columns
conditions: beam is cast-in-place reinforced concrete
exceptions: precast connections designed with equivalent structural capacity

subject: Narrow Rectangular Floor Plate
rule: A narrow rectangular floor plate must have egress paths (e.g., doors, stairs) within the maximum travel distance required by applicable building codes at both ends or along its length
conditions: Floor plate length exceeds the maximum allowable dead-end corridor length per code
Occupancy type requires two means of egress
exceptions: Single-occupancy very small spaces (e.g., storage closets) where a single exit is permitted by code

subject: Narrow Rectangular Floor Plate
rule: The floor plate width must be sufficient to accommodate the required corridor width plus occupiable depth on at least one side of the corridor
conditions: The space is designed for occupiable use (not solely a circulation passage)

subject: Narrow Rectangular Floor Plate
rule: The floor plate must not have a slenderness ratio (length/width) so extreme that lateral structural stability cannot be achieved with conventional framing
conditions: Building height is more than one story
Location is in a seismically active or high-wind region
exceptions: Single-story structures where lateral loads are minimal

subject: Linear Structural Frame
rule: linear structural frame must maintain static equilibrium under all design loads
conditions: when acting as primary load-bearing structure

subject: Linear Structural Frame
rule: linear structural frame members must not exceed their material yield or ultimate strength under factored design loads

subject: Linear Structural Frame
rule: linear structural frame must have continuous load paths from points of load application to foundations
conditions: when transferring gravity or lateral loads

subject: Linear Structural Frame
rule: linear structural frame connections must not fail (slip, rupture, or excessive deformation) before connected members reach their design capacity

subject: Linear Structural Frame
rule: linear structural frame must not experience lateral instability (buckling) in any compression member under design loads

subject: Continuous Ridge Beam
rule: continuous ridge beam must be continuous over at least two supports
conditions: when used as a primary structural element
exceptions: when designed as a simply supported beam with pinned connections at ends

subject: Continuous Ridge Beam
rule: continuous ridge beam must not have abrupt changes in cross-section along its span
conditions: unless specifically designed for stepped or tapered sections
exceptions: when the change is detailed with proper structural connections and stress analysis

subject: End Wall Glazing
rule: End wall glazing must be structurally supported by a frame or curtain wall system capable of transferring wind loads to the building structure
conditions: End wall is exposed to exterior wind loads

subject: End Wall Glazing
rule: End wall glazing must be rated for the design wind load pressure at the building site
conditions: End wall is part of the building envelope exposed to wind
exceptions: Glazing that is entirely interior (not part of the building envelope)

subject: End Wall Glazing
rule: End wall glazing must not be installed in a location where it would be the primary lateral load-resisting element without an engineered frame system
conditions: Glazing is load-bearing or serves as a shear wall
exceptions: Specially engineered structural glass systems designed and tested for such loads

subject: End Wall Glazing
rule: End wall glazing must have tempered or laminated glass where human impact risk exists within 900 mm of floor level
conditions: End wall glazing is in an occupiable area with pedestrian traffic within 900 mm of the glass
exceptions: Glazing separated by permanent barriers or railings preventing human contact

subject: Linear Roof Form
rule: Linear roof form must have a continuous drainage path along its length to prevent ponding
conditions: roof pitch is less than 1/4:12
roof is located in a region with measurable precipitation
exceptions: roof is designed as a water-retaining feature (e.g., blue roof or intentional detention)

subject: Linear Roof Form
rule: Linear roof form must not have an uninterrupted cross-section that allows lateral water entry at its open ends under wind-driven rain
conditions: roof ends are unenclosed or open to prevailing winds
roof is not designed as a sheltered internal feature
exceptions: ends are fully sealed with weatherproof cladding or glazing
roof is an internal atrium element not exposed to exterior weather

subject: Slot Courtyard
rule: Slot Courtyard must have an unobstructed path for emergency egress from the courtyard to a public way or safe area
conditions: If the courtyard is used as an occupied space
If the courtyard is accessible to building occupants
exceptions: If the courtyard is a lightwell or service void not intended for occupancy

subject: Slot Courtyard
rule: Slot Courtyard must not be fully enclosed on all sides by combustible construction without fire-rated separations
conditions: If the courtyard is bounded by multiple building walls
If the walls enclosing the courtyard are load-bearing or part of the primary structure
exceptions: If all enclosing walls are constructed of non-combustible materials with appropriate fire-resistance ratings

subject: Slot Courtyard
rule: Slot Courtyard must have a minimum width-to-height ratio to ensure adequate daylight access and prevent oppressive spatial conditions
conditions: If the courtyard depth exceeds one story (≥3m)
If the courtyard is intended for human occupancy or habitable room adjacency
exceptions: If the courtyard serves exclusively as a lightwell or ventilation shaft and is not occupied

subject: Linear Circulation Spine
rule: linear circulation spine must maintain a minimum clear width for safe egress
conditions: occupied spaces served by the spine
applicable building code occupancy classification
exceptions: non-egress circulation spines such as purely service or utility corridors with restricted access

subject: Linear Circulation Spine
rule: linear circulation spine must have a maximum travel distance to an exit
conditions: serves as a means of egress
building over one story or with high occupant load
exceptions: spines in single-story buildings with sprinkler systems may have extended distances per code

subject: Linear Circulation Spine
rule: linear circulation spine must be free of obstructions below the required headroom height
conditions: used for pedestrian circulation

subject: Linear Circulation Spine
rule: linear circulation spine must_not have a slope exceeding the maximum permitted for accessible means of egress
conditions: serves as an accessible path of travel
must comply with ADA or equivalent accessibility codes
exceptions: ramped portions designed as accessible ramps with handrails and landings are permitted

subject: Thermally Massive Slab-on-Grade
rule: Thermally massive slab-on-grade must have continuous insulation beneath and/or around its perimeter to decouple it from the ground
conditions: slab is intended to provide thermal storage mass for passive solar or radiant conditioning
exceptions: slab is in a climate where ground temperature is always within the occupied comfort range

subject: Thermally Massive Slab-on-Grade
rule: Thermally massive slab-on-grade must not be covered with thick carpet or other high-R-value floor finishes that would thermally isolate the mass from the occupied space
conditions: slab is intended to serve as exposed thermal mass for passive heating or cooling
exceptions: a thin, thermally conductive covering such as tile or thin stone is used

subject: Thermally Massive Slab-on-Grade
