rule: Layered door assembly must not allow inter-layer delamination under normal operating loads
conditions: Assembly consists of bonded or laminated layers
exceptions: Mechanically fastened layers where partial separation is intentional (e.g., sliding layers)

subject: Layered Door Assembly
rule: Layered door assembly must have all layers constrained to move together as a rigid body when the door is actuated
conditions: Door is a single-panel design where layers are permanently joined
exceptions: Multi-panel or sectional doors where layers intentionally move relative to each other

subject: Glazing Opacity Gradient
rule: Glazing opacity must change monotonically (continuously increase or decrease) across the building facade to create a coherent visual gradient
conditions: when a gradient is explicitly designed as part of the architectural expression
exceptions: when the glazing is purely functional with no aesthetic gradient intent
when multiple independent gradient zones are separated by non-glazed partitions or structural mullions

subject: Glazing Opacity Gradient
rule: Glazing opacity gradient must not produce a sudden material discontinuity that violates structural load path continuity
conditions: where the gradient involves changes in glass thickness or lamination type that affect structural capacity
exceptions: when structural discontinuities are independently resolved by the supporting frame system

subject: Glazing Opacity Gradient
rule: Glazing must have a minimum visible light transmittance (VLT) at any point to meet egress or life-safety visibility requirements
conditions: when the glazing is on an egress path or required means of escape
exceptions: when the area is sprinklered or alternative egress lighting is provided

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: window openings must include a weather-resistant barrier or seal between the window frame and the rough opening
conditions: window is installed in an exterior wall

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: glazing in doors or sidelites within a certain zone of the floor must be safety glazing (tempered or laminated)
conditions: glazing is in a door
glazing is in a sidelite within 24 inches of a door swing
glazing is within 18 inches of the floor and larger than 9 inches in any dimension
glazing is in a shower or bathtub enclosure
exceptions: glazing is fully obscured by permanent decorative grilles or munins that prevent a 9-inch sphere from passing through

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: window openings must have a minimum clear opening area and dimensions for emergency egress and rescue
conditions: window serves a sleeping room
window serves a habitable basement
window is in a residential dwelling unit
exceptions: building is fully sprinklered where code permits alternative

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: window glazing must not be installed directly against the ground or a walking surface where it presents a tripping or impact hazard
conditions: glazing is in a wall adjacent to a walking surface
glazing bottom edge is within 36 inches of the walking surface
exceptions: glazing is safety-tempered or laminated and meets impact resistance standards

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: window glazing must provide a minimum thermal resistance (U-factor) appropriate for the climate zone
conditions: window is in a conditioned space
building is subject to energy code (IECC or equivalent)
exceptions: historic preservation exceptions where code permits
unenclosed unconditioned structures

subject: Window Openings & Glazing
rule: operable window openings must not allow a 4-inch sphere to pass through when the window is in the closed position
conditions: window is operable
exceptions: exterior decorative grilles or screens are present that block the opening

subject: Skylights & Roof Glazing
rule: skylight and roof glazing assembly must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot (2%) for drainage
conditions: flat roof application
curb-mounted skylight
exceptions: factory-sealed structural glass systems designed for zero-slope
unit skylights rated for low-slope installation per manufacturer's listing

subject: Skylights & Roof Glazing
rule: skylight glazing must be laminated or have a protective layer below when located in the plane of the roof
conditions: skylight is within 12 feet of walking surface on the roof
or skylight is in a roof area designated for occupancy
exceptions: skylights with wire glass in industrial buildings where impact is unlikely

subject: Skylights & Roof Glazing
rule: skylight curb must be at least 4 inches higher than the finished roof surface on low-slope roofs
conditions: roof slope is less than 2:12
skylight is curb-mounted
exceptions: unit skylights listed with lower curbs per manufacturer's tested assembly

subject: Skylights & Roof Glazing
rule: skylight and roof glazing must not be installed directly over an unprotected opening in the roof deck without a structural curb or frame
exceptions: structural glass systems designed and tested as roof deck assemblies

subject: Skylights & Roof Glazing
rule: skylight glass must be safety glazing (tempered or laminated) if the skylight is walk-on type or if the roof area above is subject to maintenance traffic
conditions: roof has permanent maintenance access
or skylight is rated for foot traffic
exceptions: skylights with protective grilles or screens rated for walk-on loading

subject: Light Tubes & Solar Tunnels
rule: light tube must have a continuous, highly reflective interior surface with reflectance ≥ 99%
conditions: the system is a tubular daylighting device (TDD) relying on passive light transmission
exceptions: fiber-optic solar collection systems that use cables instead of reflective tubes

subject: Light Tubes & Solar Tunnels
rule: solar tunnel must maintain a sealed, water-vapor-tight enclosure between roof penetration and interior ceiling
conditions: the device penetrates the building envelope

subject: Light Tubes & Solar Tunnels
rule: light tube must not have a total turning angle exceeding 90 degrees between roof aperture and ceiling diffuser
conditions: the tube uses passive specular reflection without active tracking or booster mirrors
exceptions: systems with dual-axis tracking mirrors or active light-redirecting lenses that compensate for angle losses

subject: Light Tubes & Solar Tunnels
rule: solar tunnel roof penetration must be flashed and weather-sealed to prevent leakage
conditions: the tunnel penetrates the roof

subject: Light Tubes & Solar Tunnels
rule: light tube diffuser must be located in a conditioned space (not directly exposed to exterior)

subject: Atria & Light Wells
rule: Atria and light wells must provide a means of natural ventilation and smoke exhaust at the top
conditions: atrium is enclosed
atrium exceeds 2 stories in height
exceptions: mechanical smoke exhaust system is designed and approved

subject: Atria & Light Wells
rule: Atria and light wells must maintain a minimum 1-hour fire-resistance-rated separation from adjacent occupied spaces
conditions: atrium connects three or more stories

subject: Atria & Light Wells
rule: Atria and light wells must not allow rainwater to collect or pond at the base or on intermediate ledges
conditions: atrium has a glazed or open roof
exceptions: dedicated drainage systems are provided at all collection points

subject: Atria & Light Wells
rule: Atria and light wells must have a fully sprinklered interior volume when the height exceeds 55 feet
conditions: atrium height exceeds 55 feet (approx. 17 m)

subject: Glazing Coatings & Films
rule: glazing coatings and films must be compatible with the substrate and adhesive system to which they are applied
conditions: when applied as a retrofit film
when applied during manufacturing

subject: Glazing Coatings & Films
rule: glazing coatings and films must not significantly reduce the visible light transmittance below applicable building code minimums for egress areas
conditions: when applied to windows in spaces requiring natural light for egress or emergency escape
exceptions: where artificial lighting is permanently provided as an alternative

subject: Glazing Coatings & Films
rule: glazing coatings and films must not introduce excessive solar heat gain that causes thermal stress fracture of the glass substrate
conditions: when applied to fully tempered or heat-strengthened glass
when applied to glass with edge damage or pre-existing stress
exceptions: films specifically rated and tested for the given glass type and solar exposure

subject: Light Shelves & Reflectors
rule: Light shelves and reflectors must have a minimum reflectance of at least 80% for their upper surface to function as effective daylighting devices
conditions: when used for interior daylight redirection
when upper surface is the primary reflective element
exceptions: when used exclusively as shading devices with no daylight redirection intent

subject: Light Shelves & Reflectors
rule: Light shelves and reflectors must be positioned outside the regular maintenance and cleaning path of windows and glazing
conditions: when installed on building facades above or below windows

subject: Light Shelves & Reflectors
rule: Light shelves and reflectors must not obstruct required emergency egress or natural ventilation openings
conditions: when installed on operable windows or near emergency exits
exceptions: when the openings are designed with alternative egress paths or mechanical ventilation

subject: Light Shelves & Reflectors
rule: The reflective surface of exterior light shelves must be self-draining and must not allow water ponding
conditions: when installed on exterior building facades exposed to rain

subject: Sunspace & Conservatory
rule: glazing must be impact-resistant or protected by screens where subject to wind-borne debris
conditions: located in regions subject to hurricanes, tornadoes, or severe storms
exceptions: glazing fully protected by permanent structural shutters meeting impact standards

subject: Sunspace & Conservatory
rule: glass panels must be tempered or laminated safety glass where located within reachable height or subject to human impact
conditions: glazing is within 18 inches of floor or doorways
glazing area exceeds 9 square feet per panel
exceptions: glazing is fully screened by fixed bars or guardrails preventing human contact

subject: Sunspace & Conservatory
rule: glazed areas must not exceed structural load limits for wind and snow without adequate framing and anchorage
conditions: conservatory or sunspace is in a snow-prone or high-wind region

subject: Sunspace & Conservatory
rule: roof glazing must be sloped at a minimum pitch to allow water runoff
conditions: roof is glazed
roof is not a fully sealed structural glass system with internal drainage
exceptions: curtain-wall systems with continuous interior gutter drainage and redundant waterproofing

subject: Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) Rating
rule: SHGC rating must be between 0 and 1 inclusive

subject: Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) Rating
rule: SHGC rating must be measured under standardized test conditions (e.g., NFRC 200 or ISO 9050)
conditions: when used for regulatory compliance or product certification in North America or international markets

subject: Photovoltaic Glazing & BIPV
rule: Photovoltaic glazing and BIPV modules must be structural-grade (load-bearing) when serving as building envelope (roof, façade, or canopy) to withstand design dead, live, wind, snow, and seismic loads without collapse or unsafe deflection.
conditions: When the BIPV product replaces a conventional building envelope element (roof, façade, window, or canopy) rather than being an add-on/cladding-only system.
exceptions: When the BIPV is a non-structural add-on installed over an already-rated structural substrate — in that case only the substrate must be load-bearing.

subject: Photovoltaic Glazing & BIPV
rule: Photovoltaic glazing must not be installed in a position where it is fully shaded for more than 70% of peak sun hours by fixed architectural elements (parapets, overhangs, adjacent walls) unless the system includes per-cell bypass diodes or module-level power electronics that prevent hot-spot damage.
conditions: Applicable to any BIPV glazing installation (curtain wall, skylight, window-integrated PV).
exceptions: Systems with integrated microinverters or optimizers that isolate shaded cells can tolerate shading patterns without creating reverse-bias hot spots.

subject: Photovoltaic Glazing & BIPV
rule: BIPV laminated glass units must use heat-strengthened or fully tempered glass when installed in overhead (skylight/canopy) applications, with interlayer adhesion rated for the expected thermal cycling and impact loads.
conditions: Applies to translucent or semi-transparent BIPV modules used in overhead glazing (skylights, canopies, walkway covers) at any height above occupied space.
exceptions: None — safety glazing codes universally require tempered/heat-strengthened glass with retained post-breakage adhesion for overhead applications (IBC 2406, EN 14449).

subject: Daylight Autonomy & Illuminance Sensors
rule: illuminance sensors must be placed in locations that receive the daylight conditions they are intended to measure
conditions: sensors are used for daylight autonomy assessment

subject: Daylight Autonomy & Illuminance Sensors
rule: daylight sensors must not be mounted in direct contact with artificial light sources that alter the daylight reading
conditions: sensors are used for daylight autonomy verification
exceptions: sensors specifically designed and calibrated to subtract electric light contribution

subject: Lobby/Atrium
rule: Lobby/Atrium must have a minimum clear floor area to accommodate occupant egress and circulation
conditions: Occupied space
Building code jurisdiction applies
exceptions: If the lobby/atrium is designed solely as a decorative or unoccupied void with restricted access

subject: Lobby/Atrium
rule: Lobby/Atrium must have at least one exit access leading directly to an exit or exit discharge
conditions: Lobby/atrium is on a floor level requiring egress
exceptions: Single-story building with direct outdoor access at multiple points

subject: Lobby/Atrium
rule: Lobby/Atrium must have a smoke control or exhaust system when the atrium exceeds specified height thresholds
conditions: Atrium exceeds building code height limit for open interconnected spaces (e.g., >55 ft in IBC)
exceptions: Where an engineered alternative performance-based design demonstrates equivalent safety

subject: Lobby/Atrium
rule: Lobby/Atrium must not have floor openings that create an unprotected vertical smoke migration path exceeding code limits
conditions: Building is sprinklered and atrium exceeds height triggers per code
exceptions: When compliant smoke barriers or enclosures are provided at each floor level

subject: Lobby/Atrium
rule: Lobby/Atrium must provide accessible means of egress compliant with ADA and local accessibility codes
conditions: Building is subject to accessibility regulations
exceptions: Historic buildings with special accessibility waivers

subject: Break Room / Pantry
rule: Break room / pantry must have at least one sink connected to potable water supply and drainage
conditions: Space is classified as a break room or pantry
Space is intended for food preparation or cleanup
exceptions: Vending-machine-only pantry with no sink required by local code

subject: Break Room / Pantry
rule: Break room / pantry must have at least one electrical outlet capable of serving a microwave or similar appliance
conditions: Space is intended for food storage, reheating, or beverage preparation

subject: Break Room / Pantry
rule: Break room / pantry must not have a floor drain that can emit sewer gas without a trap
conditions: Floor drain is present in the space
exceptions: Drains are not present at all

subject: Break Room / Pantry
rule: Break room / pantry must have a means of natural or mechanical ventilation
conditions: Space contains cooking or odor-producing equipment (e.g., microwave, toaster oven)
exceptions: Space has no cooking or odor-producing equipment beyond a refrigerator

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must have at least one toilet fixture

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must have a handwashing sink
exceptions: mobile or temporary portable toilet units without plumbing (e.g., portable chemical toilets)

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must have a means of ventilation

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must have a water supply connection to toilet and sink fixtures
exceptions: portable chemical toilets that use holding tanks and do not require plumbing connections

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must have a sanitary waste drainage connection for toilet and sink
exceptions: portable chemical toilets that use sealed holding tanks and are serviced externally

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must be accessible from a publicly accessible circulation space

subject: Public Toilet / Restroom
rule: public toilet / restroom must not be located where sewage or waste can backflow into the space
conditions: when below-grade or in a flood-prone area
exceptions: when equipped with a code-compliant backflow prevention system and sewage ejector pump

subject: Built-in Reception Seating
rule: Built-in reception seating must have a minimum seat depth of 400 mm
conditions: seating is intended for adult users
exceptions: seat is purely decorative and not intended for sitting

subject: Built-in Reception Seating
rule: Built-in reception seating must have a seat height between 400 mm and 480 mm
conditions: seating is intended for typical adult use
exceptions: seating is specifically designed for children or alternate user group with different anthropometrics

subject: Built-in Reception Seating
rule: Built-in reception seating must_not have sharp edges or corners at seated occupant contact points

subject: Directory / Wayfinding Signage
rule: Directory / wayfinding signage must be legible from intended viewing distance under expected lighting conditions
conditions: installed in publicly accessible areas
used for navigation

subject: Directory / Wayfinding Signage
rule: Directory / wayfinding signage must be mounted at a height and location that does not create an obstruction or hazard
conditions: installed in circulation paths
egress routes
corridors
exceptions: signs recessed into alcoves or wall pockets that maintain clear width

subject: Directory / Wayfinding Signage
rule: Directory / wayfinding signage must have text and symbols that contrast sufficiently with the background for readability
conditions: any installation

subject: Fire-rated Doorset
rule: Fire-rated doorset must have a fire-resistance rating (e.g., FD30, FD60, FD90, FD120) that matches or exceeds the fire-resistance rating of the wall assembly in which it is installed
conditions: Doorset installed in a fire-resistance-rated wall
Doorset installed in a fire compartment wall or enclosure
exceptions: Doorset installed solely as a non-rated interior door with no fire separation function

subject: Fire-rated Doorset
rule: Fire-rated doorset must be self-closing and positive-latching
conditions: Doorset is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Doorset serving an area where self-closing would create a life-safety hazard (e.g., stairwell in some specific egress configurations where hold-open devices are permitted and tied to fire alarm)

subject: Fire-rated Doorset
rule: Fire-rated doorset must not have its fire-resistance rating compromised by field modifications such as cutting, drilling, or installing hardware not listed for that door assembly
conditions: Doorset is installed and in use
exceptions: Modifications explicitly permitted by the door manufacturer's listing and labeling

subject: Fire-rated Doorset
rule: Fire-rated doorset must maintain the required clearance gaps (typically 3/4 inch to 1 inch at bottom, and 1/8 inch along sides and top, per listing) and must not have through-openings or holes in the door leaf or frame
conditions: Doorset is installed and closed

subject: Stair Handrail
rule: Stair handrail must have a gripping surface that is continuous along the full length of the stair flight
conditions: handrail is provided on a staircase
exceptions: handrail terminates at a newel post or wall return

subject: Stair Handrail
rule: Stair handrail must be at a consistent height measured from the stair nosing line
conditions: handrail is provided on a staircase
exceptions: switchback or landing segments where handrail height may transition within code-allowed range

subject: Stair Handrail
rule: Stair handrail must withstand a minimum of 200 pounds of concentrated load applied in any direction
conditions: handrail is mounted for building occupancy use

subject: Stair Handrail
rule: Stair handrail must not have projections or obstructions that can catch loose clothing or cause injury

subject: Stair Handrail
rule: Stair handrail must have a cross-section diameter that fits the average adult hand grip
exceptions: specialized handrails for children or accessibility devices where alternate grip dimensions are intentional

subject: Corridor Ceiling System
rule: Corridor ceiling system must provide a minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating
conditions: when corridor serves as a means of egress
when corridor connects more than two adjacent occupancies
exceptions: when building is fully sprinklered and local code permits reduction

subject: Corridor Ceiling System
rule: Corridor ceiling system must have a maximum flame spread index of 25
conditions: when corridor ceiling is part of a means of egress

subject: Corridor Ceiling System
rule: Corridor ceiling system must not sag or deflect more than L/240 under dead load
conditions: when supporting any finish or tile material

subject: Elevator Door Operator
rule: Elevator door operator must detect door zone position within specified tolerance before initiating door movement
conditions: During automatic operation mode
During power-up sequence
exceptions: Manual inspection/service mode with qualified personnel

subject: Elevator Door Operator
rule: Elevator door operator must not apply door-closing force exceeding regulatory limit (typically 135 N static force per EN 81-20 / ASME A17.1)
conditions: During passenger door closing operation
exceptions: Firefighter emergency override mode

subject: Elevator Door Operator
rule: Elevator door operator must include a functional mechanical or electronic reversing edge / obstruction detection system that triggers reversal upon contact with an obstacle
conditions: Automatic sliding door operation
exceptions: Manual swing doors without automatic operation

subject: Elevator Door Operator
rule: Elevator door operator motor and control electronics must be rated for the temperature range of the hoistway environment (typically 0°C to 40°C for indoor, or wider if exposed)
conditions: All operating environments
exceptions: Custom environmental package specified for extreme conditions

subject: Stairwell Pressurization Fan
rule: Stairwell pressurization fan must be powered by a listed emergency or standby power source (e.g., generator, uninterruptible power supply)
conditions: Building is equipped with an automatic sprinkler system
Building height exceeds limits for code exception
exceptions: Buildings with fewer than 3 stories and no sprinkler system where local code permits

subject: Stairwell Pressurization Fan
rule: Stairwell pressurization fan must pressurize the stairwell to a minimum of 0.05 in. w.g. (12.5 Pa) above the adjacent floor level while keeping door-closing forces within 30 lbf (133 N)
conditions: Stairwell is designated as a means of egress
System is designed to comply with IBC or NFPA 92
exceptions: Alternative performance-based design approved by the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ)

subject: Stairwell Pressurization Fan
rule: Stairwell pressurization fan must not be located in an area where it can intake smoke or contaminated air from the fire floor or exterior smoke sources
conditions: Fan intake is outdoors or within a mechanical room that is not smoke-protected

subject: Stairwell Pressurization Fan
rule: Stairwell pressurization fan must be interlocked with the fire alarm system to activate upon detection of a fire signal
conditions: Building is equipped with an automatic fire alarm system
exceptions: Manually activated systems with approved alternative sequence

subject: Stairwell Pressurization Fan
rule: Stairwell pressurization fan supply duct must be constructed of minimum 26-gauge galvanized steel or equivalent noncombustible material
conditions: Duct penetrates any fire-resistance-rated assembly

subject: Reception Desk / Counter
rule: Reception desk/counter must have a clear user-facing surface at an accessible height
conditions: The reception desk serves the general public or building occupants
exceptions: The desk is designed exclusively as a behind-the-scenes administrative work surface with no public interaction

subject: Reception Desk / Counter
rule: Reception desk/counter must have a minimum clear workspace depth behind the counter for a seated or standing staff person
conditions: Staff are expected to work at the desk
exceptions: The desk is purely a drop-off or self-service station with no staff positioned behind it

subject: Reception Desk / Counter
rule: Reception desk/counter must not have sharp edges or corners on the public-facing side at reachable height
conditions: The desk is in a location accessible to the public

subject: Entry Vestibule
rule: Entry vestibule must have two doors separating it from exterior and interior spaces
conditions: Vestibule is present as an entry space
Building has conditioned interior space
exceptions: Building with unconditioned interior (e.g., unheated storage)

subject: Entry Vestibule
rule: Entry vestibule must have a minimum floor area that accommodates door swing clearance and occupant queuing
conditions: Vestibule is required by building code for occupancy type

subject: Entry Vestibule
rule: Entry vestibule must not have a single set of doors that opens directly to both exterior and interior without an intermediate space
conditions: Vestibule is required by energy code or accessibility code

subject: Entry Vestibule
rule: Entry vestibule floor must be non-absorbent and sloped for drainage at exterior door
conditions: Vestibule is at a grade-level entrance exposed to rain or snow
exceptions: Vestibule is fully covered by a canopy or overhang that prevents rainwater entry

subject: Entry Floor Finish
rule: Entry floor finish must be slip-resistant when wet
conditions: entry is exterior or semi-enclosed
entry is exposed to rain or moisture
exceptions: entry is fully interior with no moisture exposure from occupants or cleaning

subject: Entry Floor Finish
rule: Entry floor finish must be at least as hard as the adjacent exterior paving material
conditions: entry is at grade and connects directly to exterior walkways
exceptions: a transition mat or threshold strip of harder material is installed between surfaces

subject: Signage / Directory Board
rule: signage or directory board must be securely fixed to its supporting structure to prevent falling
conditions: the board is installed in a location accessible to the public
the board is mounted overhead or on a wall
exceptions: freestanding boards placed on level ground that rely on gravity and broad base are exempt from mechanical fixing

subject: Signage / Directory Board
rule: signage or directory board must not project into an accessible path of travel below headroom clearance
conditions: the board is wall-mounted or suspended at a height where it could be struck by pedestrians
the board is located along a circulation route
exceptions: signs mounted flush on a wall with no protrusion beyond the wall face

subject: Signage / Directory Board
rule: directory board text and symbols must be legible under expected lighting conditions
conditions: the board is used for wayfinding or identification

subject: Entrance Canopy / Portico
rule: an entrance canopy / portico must have a minimum 1/4 inch per foot slope for drainage
conditions: the canopy has a solid roof surface
exceptions: the canopy is designed with a green/vegetated roof with integrated drainage

subject: Entrance Canopy / Portico
rule: an entrance canopy / portico must not have unprotected snow/ice accumulation zones above building entrances
conditions: the canopy or portico is located in a climate zone with measurable snowfall
the canopy is above or adjacent to an egress path or public entry
exceptions: the canopy is designed for snow retention with engineered structural capacity for full snow load and dedicated melt/diversion systems

subject: Entrance Canopy / Portico
rule: an entrance canopy / portico must be laterally braced to resist wind uplift forces
conditions: the canopy is freestanding or cantilevered
the canopy roof area exceeds 50 square feet
exceptions: the canopy is an integral structural extension of the main building frame with continuous load path verified by structural analysis

subject: Entrance Canopy / Portico
rule: an entrance canopy / portico's structural supports must not obstruct the required clear width of the accessible route below
conditions: the canopy spans over a pedestrian pathway or building entrance serving accessible means of egress
exceptions: the supports are placed outside the required accessible route clear width per code

subject: Partition Wall
rule: partition wall must be laterally supported at top and bottom to prevent out-of-plane instability
conditions: when spanning full floor-to-ceiling height
in any occupancy
exceptions: free-standing partition walls designed as cantilevers with adequate base fixity

subject: Partition Wall
rule: partition wall must not bear vertical load from the structure above unless specifically designed as a load-bearing wall
conditions: when classified as non-load-bearing partition

subject: Partition Wall
rule: partition wall must have a maximum height-to-thickness ratio not exceeding that specified by the applicable material code to prevent buckling
conditions: for masonry partitions
for stud-framed partitions the slenderness limit applies instead

subject: Room Finish - Wall
rule: wall finish must not trap moisture against the wall substrate
conditions: applies to any wall finish applied to interior or exterior walls
exceptions: vapor-permeable finishes specifically designed to allow moisture transmission
finishes applied over drainage mats or ventilated cavity systems

subject: Room Finish - Wall
rule: wall finish must have a fire-resistance rating compatible with the occupancy and fire separation requirements of the wall assembly
conditions: applies where local building codes require fire-rated assemblies (e.g., exit corridors, stairwells, shaft walls, occupancy separations)
exceptions: finishes applied to non-rated walls in single-family dwellings where code permits unrated finishes

subject: Room Finish - Wall
rule: wall finish must be securely attached to prevent detachment under expected loads
conditions: applies to all wall finishes regardless of material or location
exceptions: temporary finishes or display installations explicitly designed for periodic removal

subject: Room Finish - Wall
rule: wall finish must not block required ventilation paths or air gaps in the wall assembly
conditions: applies where the wall assembly design incorporates intentional ventilation paths, drainage cavities, or air gaps for moisture or thermal performance
exceptions: finishes that are specifically designed to be part of a sealed (non-ventilated) assembly

subject: Baseboard / Skirting
rule: Baseboard / skirting must be installed with a gap between its bottom edge and finished flooring to allow for thermal expansion of the flooring material
conditions: When installed over floating floor systems (e.g., laminate, engineered wood, LVP)
When flooring material has known thermal expansion coefficient
exceptions: When flooring is tile set in thinset (no lateral expansion)
When skirting is installed before flooring and flooring butts against it without floating

subject: Baseboard / Skirting
rule: Baseboard / skirting must be fastened at intervals that prevent warping or detachment under normal building movement
conditions: When wall construction is standard framed drywall or plaster
exceptions: When adhesive-only system is specified and wall movement is negligible (e.g., interior partition walls in stable climate)

subject: Baseboard / Skirting
rule: Baseboard / skirting must not block required ventilation openings at the base of a wall cavity
conditions: When the wall assembly includes a ventilated crawlspace or basement
When building code requires weep screed or foundation vent clearance
exceptions: When ventilation is provided through other means (e.g., through-floor vents, mechanical system)

subject: Electrical Outlet / Switch
rule: Electrical outlet must be mounted in an accessible location that is not obstructed by permanent fixtures
conditions: when installed in habitable spaces
when required for intended use

subject: Electrical Outlet / Switch
rule: Electrical outlet must have a ground path (grounding connection)
conditions: when installed in any building with grounded electrical system
exceptions: ungrounded outlets permitted only in buildings built before grounding requirements where GFCI protection is provided

subject: Electrical Outlet / Switch
rule: Electrical outlet must not be installed in a location exposed to direct spray of water unless it is a weather-resistant (WR) type with appropriate cover
conditions: in outdoor locations
in bathrooms
in kitchens within 6 feet of sink
near water sources
exceptions: if properly rated weather-resistant outlet with in-use weatherproof cover is used

subject: Electrical Outlet / Switch
rule: Electrical outlet must not have reversed polarity (hot and neutral conductors must be correctly connected)
conditions: always

subject: Electrical Outlet / Switch
rule: Electrical outlet box must be securely fastened to a structural element
conditions: when installed
exceptions: old-work boxes with approved clamping mechanisms in existing walls

subject: Interior Door Hardware
rule: Interior door hardware must have a latching mechanism that engages with the strike plate when the door is closed
conditions: Door is of swinging type
Hardware includes a latch or lock
exceptions: Doors that are intentionally non-latching (e.g., certain pivot or sliding doors with separate locking mechanisms)

subject: Interior Door Hardware
rule: Interior door hardware must not prevent the door from swinging through its full intended arc of operation
conditions: Hardware projects beyond the door face (e.g., lever handles, knobs, or plates)
exceptions: Hardware designed for sliding or pocket doors that have no swing arc

subject: Interior Door Hardware
rule: Interior door hardware must have a return-to-center spring mechanism for lever handles on fire-rated doors
conditions: Door is fire-rated
Hardware is a lever handle (not a knob)

subject: Built-in Storage / Cabinet
rule: Built-in storage / cabinet must have adequate structural attachment to the wall, floor, or adjacent structure to prevent tipping or collapse under intended load
conditions: When unit is freestanding and taller than its base width
When unit is wall-mounted

subject: Built-in Storage / Cabinet
rule: Built-in storage / cabinet must not block egress paths or required clearances when in the open position
conditions: When located adjacent to doors, corridors, or means of egress

subject: Built-in Storage / Cabinet
rule: Built-in storage / cabinet must not obstruct HVAC supply or return registers
conditions: When installed in front of or directly adjacent to HVAC diffusers, grilles, or returns

subject: Built-in Storage / Cabinet
rule: Built-in storage / cabinet must have a minimum clearance to combustible materials if housing heat-producing equipment
conditions: When cabinet encloses a water heater, boiler, furnace, or other heat-producing appliance

subject: Room Signage
rule: Room signage must be legible from the intended viewing distance under expected lighting conditions
conditions: signage is installed

subject: Room Signage
rule: Room signage must not be obstructed by other building elements, furniture, or equipment
conditions: signage is mounted on walls, doors, or ceiling

subject: Room Signage
rule: Room signage must maintain a minimum color contrast ratio between text and background
conditions: signage includes textual or numeric content

subject: Threshold / Saddle
rule: Threshold / saddle must be sloped to drain water away from the door opening
conditions: threshold/saddle is exposed to exterior or weather
exceptions: threshold/saddle is located fully under a covered, drained canopy that eliminates rainwater exposure

subject: Threshold / Saddle
rule: Threshold / saddle must have a height differential (step-down) or positive barrier to prevent water from entering the interior under normal conditions
conditions: threshold/saddle is at an exterior doorway
exceptions: doorway is designed for accessibility (e.g., ADA zero-threshold) AND a secondary drainage system handles water at the opening

subject: Threshold / Saddle
rule: Threshold / saddle must not create a trip hazard exceeding applicable code limits
conditions: threshold/saddle is at an occupant-accessible doorway
exceptions: historic building with documented exemption

subject: Wall Penetration Sleeve
rule: wall penetration sleeve must maintain a minimum clearance from structural elements (e.g., rebar, studs, beams) to avoid compromising structural integrity
conditions: sleeve passes through a structural wall or load-bearing member
exceptions: sleeve diameter is engineered to be cast-in-place with structural reinforcement designed around it

subject: Wall Penetration Sleeve
rule: wall penetration sleeve must be water-sealed or waterproofed at the exterior face to prevent moisture ingress
conditions: sleeve penetrates an exterior wall or below-grade wall assembly

subject: Wall Penetration Sleeve
rule: wall penetration sleeve must not deform or collapse under the imposed backfill or wall load
conditions: sleeve is installed in a below-grade wall or retaining wall subject to soil load
exceptions: sleeve is a structural-grade sleeve specifically rated for the expected load

subject: Wall Penetration Sleeve
rule: wall penetration sleeve must accommodate differential movement between the pipe/conduit and the wall without leakage or breakage
conditions: sleeve carries a pipe or conduit through a wall subject to differential settlement or thermal movement
exceptions: sleeve is rigidly cast into both sides of a movement joint without a flexible coupling — in which case a different failure mode applies

subject: Wall Penetration Sleeve
rule: wall penetration sleeve must not create a fire-rated assembly breach without being fire-stopped with an approved firestop system
conditions: sleeve penetrates a fire-rated wall assembly
exceptions: sleeve is part of a listed firestop system with intumescent material tested for the specific wall rating

subject: Passageway Connector
rule: A passageway connector must have a minimum clear width for emergency egress
conditions: Occupied or intended for occupant use
exceptions: When solely designated as a service/support tunnel with no public access

subject: Passageway Connector
rule: A passageway connector must not have a slope that exceeds the maximum allowable ramp gradient
conditions: Intended for pedestrian use

subject: Passageway Connector
rule: A passageway connector must have fire-rated construction at any junction with a building it connects
conditions: The connector provides a pedestrian passage between two separate buildings
exceptions: When both connected buildings are under the same ownership and the local fire code does not require separation

subject: Hallway
rule: hallway must have a minimum clear width of at least the applicable building code minimum for egress and accessibility
conditions: hallway serves as a means of egress
hallway provides access to building occupants
exceptions: hallways in residential dwelling units serving only one bedroom

subject: Hallway
rule: hallway must have a minimum clear height as required by building code for occupied spaces
conditions: hallway is an occupied path of travel

subject: Hallway
rule: hallway must not have a step or change in level unless a ramp or lift is provided
conditions: hallway is accessible to building occupants
exceptions: steps serving a single dwelling unit where grade change is unavoidable and no accessible route is required

subject: Hallway
rule: hallway must provide a clear path to an exit in accordance with maximum travel distance requirements
conditions: hallway is part of a means of egress

subject: Hallway
rule: hallway must not be narrower at any point than the required egress width based on occupant load served
conditions: hallway serves as part of an egress path

subject: Breezeway
rule: breezeway roof must have a continuous slope or drainage path to prevent standing water
conditions: breezeway has a roof

subject: Breezeway
rule: breezeway must have a minimum clear width of at least 36 inches (0.91 m) for safe pedestrian passage
conditions: breezeway is intended for pedestrian access or egress

subject: Breezeway
rule: breezeway must not have a floor level change exceeding 1/2 inch without a ramp or step
conditions: breezeway is part of an accessible path of travel

subject: Corridor Ceiling
rule: corridor ceiling must have a minimum fire resistance rating as required by applicable building code
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress
building code requires fire-resistance-rated construction
exceptions: corridor is in a sprinklered building with code-allowed reduction

subject: Corridor Ceiling
rule: corridor ceiling must not have exposed combustible materials that violate flame spread and smoke development index limits
conditions: ceiling is part of a means of egress corridor
local code specifies interior finish requirements
exceptions: materials are tested and certified to meet the required Class A/Class I rating

subject: Corridor Ceiling
rule: corridor ceiling must provide minimum clear height as required by accessibility and building codes
conditions: corridor is accessible to the public or occupants
exceptions: existing buildings with grandfathered reduced heights per code

subject: Corridor Floor Finish
rule: Corridor floor finish must be slip-resistant under foreseeable wet or dry conditions
conditions: corridor is a means of egress
corridor serves occupied spaces
exceptions: corridor is not intended for occupant use (e.g., service/mechanical corridor with restricted access)

subject: Corridor Floor Finish
rule: Corridor floor finish must have a flame-spread index not exceeding applicable code limits for the occupancy type
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress
exceptions: finish is part of an approved fire-resistive assembly tested as a whole

subject: Corridor Floor Finish
rule: Corridor floor finish must not produce smoke that exceeds the code-specified smoke-developed index in a corridor serving as a means of egress
conditions: corridor serves as a means of egress

subject: Passage Fire Door
rule: Passage fire door must be self-closing and self-latching
conditions: Door is installed in a fire-rated wall assembly
Door serves as a means of egress
exceptions: Doors in health care facilities where automatic-closing devices are permitted to be held open and release upon fire alarm signal

subject: Passage Fire Door
rule: Passage fire door must have a fire-resistance rating equal to or greater than the fire rating of the wall assembly in which it is installed
conditions: Door is installed in a fire-resistance-rated wall
exceptions: Doors in smoke barriers rated for 20-minute protection may have different rating equivalencies per code

subject: Passage Fire Door
rule: Passage fire door must not have field-applied rated glazing that exceeds the tested rating of the door assembly
conditions: Glazing is being field-installed into an existing fire door

subject: Passage Fire Door
rule: Passage fire door must have positive-latching hardware
conditions: Door is rated for 20 minutes or more
Door is in a means of egress

subject: Passage Ductwork
rule: passage ductwork must maintain a minimum cross-sectional airflow area as specified by design
conditions: where serving occupied spaces
where required for ventilation or exhaust air movement

subject: Passage Ductwork
rule: passage ductwork must not have internal obstructions that reduce net free area below the design minimum
conditions: at any cross-section along the duct run
exceptions: turning vanes and dampers explicitly designed and scheduled for the duct

subject: Passage Ductwork
rule: passage ductwork must be airtight within the leakage class specified by the applicable standard (e.g., SMACNA or equivalent)
conditions: for ductwork located within conditioned spaces
for ductwork carrying hazardous or high-temperature air

subject: Passage Ductwork
rule: passage ductwork must not be constructed of materials with a flame spread or smoke-developed index exceeding the limits of the applicable building code

subject: Aisle
rule: aisle width must meet minimum egress code requirements
conditions: aisle serves as a means of egress
occupant load exceeds threshold requiring two exits
exceptions: buildings with sprinkler systems may allow reduced widths under some codes

subject: Aisle
rule: aisle must be free of permanent obstructions below the required clear height
conditions: aisle is designated as an accessible route
aisle is an egress path
exceptions: temporary movable objects that do not reduce clear width below minimum

subject: Aisle
rule: aisle must not have a step or change in level without a ramp or stair
conditions: aisle is on an accessible path of travel
exceptions: changes in level up to 1/2 inch may be beveled; up to 3/4 inch with sloped edge

subject: Passage Emergency Exit Route
rule: Passage emergency exit route must be free of all obstructions including furniture, stored materials, and debris
conditions: When designated as a means of egress
exceptions: Temporary obstructions during immediate emergency response activities

subject: Passage Emergency Exit Route
rule: Passage emergency exit route must have a clear width of at least 0.91 m (36 in) at all points
conditions: When serving an occupant load of 50 or more per story

subject: Passage Emergency Exit Route
rule: Passage emergency exit route must not terminate in a dead-end corridor longer than 6.1 m (20 ft)
conditions: When the exit route is a corridor serving as a means of egress

subject: Passage Emergency Exit Route
rule: Passage emergency exit route doors must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: When the door serves an occupant load of 50 or more
exceptions: Doors in private dwelling units

subject: Passage Emergency Exit Route
rule: Passage emergency exit route must be illuminated to at least 10 lux (1 ft-candle) at all times when the building is occupied

subject: Runway
rule: runway must have a minimum length based on aircraft performance requirements
conditions: operational runway

subject: Runway
rule: runway must have a load-bearing pavement structure capable of supporting design aircraft wheel loads
conditions: paved runway
exceptions: unpaved/grass runways for light aircraft where subgrade natural bearing capacity is sufficient

subject: Runway
rule: runway must maintain a longitudinal slope within acceptable limits for safe aircraft operations
conditions: operational runway

subject: Runway
rule: runway must have a clear obstacle-free approach and departure surface (obstacle limitation surfaces)
conditions: operational runway with instrument or non-instrument approaches

subject: Runway
rule: runway markings and lighting must comply with applicable aviation authority standards for the runway's type of operation
conditions: operational runway used for night or low-visibility operations
exceptions: runways used exclusively for daytime VFR operations with no night use

subject: Runway
rule: runway must not have ungrooved pavement surface when used by aircraft in wet conditions above a threshold traffic level
conditions: paved runway in region with significant rainfall
runway serving commercial or high-performance aircraft
exceptions: low-traffic runways in arid climates
runways with alternative friction-enhancing surface treatment

subject: Stage Handrail/Balustrade
rule: Stage handrail/balustrade must have a top rail that can sustain a minimum horizontal load of 0.74 kN/m applied at the top rail height
conditions: handrail is required by code
stage edge is accessible to performers or crew
exceptions: temporary/low-height stages where applicable local codes exempt handrails

subject: Stage Handrail/Balustrade
rule: Stage handrail/balustrade must not have openings between balusters or between the bottom rail and the stage floor that permit passage of a 100 mm (4 in) sphere
conditions: guardrail/balustrade serves as fall protection at an open side of a stage
exceptions: stage areas not accessible to the public or where a different infill standard is permitted by code

subject: Stage Handrail/Balustrade
rule: Stage handrail/balustrade must have a minimum height of 865 mm measured from the stage floor to the top of the handrail
conditions: handrail/balustrade is required as a guard at a drop-off on stage
exceptions: local code amendments that specify a different minimum height (e.g., 900 mm or 1100 mm in some jurisdictions)

subject: Stage Handrail/Balustrade
rule: Stage handrail/balustrade must not have sharp edges or projections that could catch clothing or injure performers
conditions: handrail is within reach of performers during stage activity
exceptions: purely decorative balustrade separated from performance area by a physical barrier

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must have a slip-resistant walking surface on all treads and aisles
conditions: used for public assembly
occupant egress path
exceptions: temporary seating structures used for single event where slip testing is performed before each use

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must have a handrail where the rise between adjacent tiers exceeds 30 inches
conditions: seating capacity exceeds 50 occupants
used in assembly occupancy
exceptions: locations with only performer/backstage access and no public circulation between tiers

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must not have more than 14 riser steps in an unsloped aisle without a landing
conditions: aisle serves as means of egress
steps are continuous without intermediate landing
exceptions: existing historic theater installations with variance approval from authority having jurisdiction

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must have a minimum clear width of 23 inches between rows for egress
conditions: seating has back-to-back or back-to-seat spacing
exceptions: seating with folding seat pans that automatically retract to provide clear width when unoccupied

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must have a maximum riser step height of 12 inches
conditions: step serves as part of a means of egress aisle

subject: Tiered Seating Risers
rule: Tiered seating risers must not have a rise-to-run ratio that permits a sphere 4 inches in diameter to pass through the opening between the seat and the riser face
conditions: seats are fixed
riser face is open behind the seat row

subject: Backstage/Back-of-House Access
rule: Backstage/back-of-house access routes must be separated from public/audience circulation paths
conditions: In performance venues
In facilities with simultaneous public and backstage operations
exceptions: Where a single shared corridor is explicitly approved by fire marshal and accessibility authority having jurisdiction

subject: Backstage/Back-of-House Access
rule: Backstage/back-of-house access must provide a minimum clear width of 44 inches (1118 mm) for equipment and scenery movement
conditions: In venues hosting theatrical or live event productions that require moving set pieces, lighting trusses, or large equipment
exceptions: Existing buildings with documented dimensional limitations where a formal variance has been granted by the authority having jurisdiction

subject: Backstage/Back-of-House Access
rule: Backstage/back-of-house access must have a minimum overhead clearance of 8 feet (2440 mm) in all travel paths
conditions: Where the path accommodates flown scenery, lighting rigs, or standing crew transport
exceptions: Under structural beams or ductwork where alternate routes exist and restricted-height zones are clearly marked

subject: Backstage/Back-of-House Access
rule: Backstage/back-of-house access must not have steps or level changes without an adjacent ramp or lift
conditions: On primary equipment transport paths and wheelchair-accessible routes
exceptions: Steps may exist on secondary crew-only paths that are not part of the accessible egress path and where equipment is hand-carried

subject: Stage Trap Door
rule: Stage trap door must be flush with the surrounding stage floor when closed
conditions: When installed in a performance stage
exceptions: If specifically designed for a raised/decorative aesthetic effect

subject: Stage Trap Door
rule: Stage trap door must support the same live load rating as the surrounding stage floor
conditions: When used as part of the walking/performance surface

subject: Stage Trap Door
rule: Stage trap door must not open unexpectedly during a performance
conditions: When occupied or walked upon by performers
exceptions: Choreographed performance sequences where opening is part of the act, provided safety interlocks are active

subject: Stage Trap Door
rule: Stage trap door must have a handrail or barrier when in the open position and accessible from stage level
conditions: When the open trap creates a drop of more than 300 mm (12 in) below the stage floor
exceptions: When the open trap is actively being used for performer entrance/exit and a crew member is stationed to control access

subject: Concealed Rigging Points
rule: concealed rigging points must be rated for the full intended load capacity
conditions: when used for load-bearing purposes

subject: Concealed Rigging Points
rule: concealed rigging points must be securely anchored to primary structural members, not to finish materials or non-structural substrates

subject: Concealed Rigging Points
rule: concealed rigging points must not be obstructed by building services, insulation, or finish materials that prevent access or attachment
conditions: when intended for future use
exceptions: if a clear access panel or removable covering is provided and documented in the maintenance plan

subject: Concealed Rigging Points
rule: concealed rigging points must be clearly identifiable from below or from the access side after installation
conditions: when the rigging point is intended to be used after building completion

subject: Stair-Stage Acoustic Treatment
rule: stair-stage acoustic treatment must have a minimum NRC (Noise Reduction Coefficient) rating of 0.70 or higher to provide adequate sound absorption in a stair-stage configuration
conditions: when installed in enclosed stairwells or performance stages requiring acoustic control
exceptions: outdoor stair-stages where acoustic performance is not required

subject: Stair-Stage Acoustic Treatment
rule: stair-stage acoustic treatment must not create a trip hazard or obstruct egress paths
conditions: when applied to stair treads, risers, or stage walking surfaces
exceptions: areas not designated as egress paths or walking surfaces

subject: Stair-Stage Acoustic Treatment
rule: stair-stage acoustic treatment must have a Class A fire rating (flame spread index ≤ 25)
conditions: when installed in any enclosed or conditioned space
exceptions: none — fire safety is a universal physical/regulatory requirement for interior finishes

subject: Curtain Track System
rule: curtain track system must be securely fastened to a structurally adequate support surface (wall, ceiling, or header)
conditions: track is installed and in use
system supports curtain weight

subject: Curtain Track System
rule: curtain track system must allow smooth, unobstructed movement of carriers along its full intended travel path
conditions: system is operated with sliding or gliding curtains
exceptions: fixed/decorative curtain tracks not intended for operation

subject: Curtain Track System
rule: curtain track system must not have sharp edges, burrs, or protruding fasteners along the curtain travel path or at user-accessible areas
conditions: track is installed within reach of occupants
exceptions: industrial tracks in fully restricted-access areas

subject: Zen Garden View
rule: Zen Garden View must have a continuous waterproof membrane separating the garden bed from the building structure below
conditions: when the Zen Garden View is located above an occupied interior space
when the garden has an irrigation or watering system
exceptions: if the garden is installed over a drainage mat that diverts all water away before contacting the structure

subject: Zen Garden View
rule: Zen Garden View must have a minimum slope of 1% toward a primary drain to prevent standing water
conditions: when the Zen Garden View is installed as a horizontal or near-horizontal plane
when the garden has a hardscape or impermeable surface layer
exceptions: if the garden uses a capillary-break drainage layer and pump system certified for zero-standing-water design

subject: Zen Garden View
rule: Zen Garden View must not have soil depth exceeding the structural load capacity of the supporting slab or beam system
conditions: when the Zen Garden View is located on a structural deck, roof slab, or elevated platform

subject: Fire-Rated Stage Curtain
rule: Fire-rated stage curtain must be constructed of materials that have been tested and certified to meet the required fire-resistance rating (e.g., ASTM E84 Class A or local equivalent)
conditions: When installed in any theater, auditorium, or performance space requiring fire protection compliance
exceptions: When no fire-rating is required by local code for the specific occupancy type

subject: Fire-Rated Stage Curtain
rule: Fire-rated stage curtain must be suspended from a support structure (header/beam) capable of bearing the curtain's dead load plus any live loads during operation
conditions: When installed in any configuration

subject: Fire-Rated Stage Curtain
rule: Fire-rated stage curtain must be attached to a closing mechanism (e.g., gravity-drop release, motorized drive, or thermally activated closure) that ensures automatic deployment in a fire event
conditions: When the curtain is required to serve as an active fire barrier in a fire-safety scenario
exceptions: When the curtain is permanently fixed in the closed position and never retracts

subject: Fire-Rated Stage Curtain
rule: Fire-rated stage curtain must not be made of materials that produce excessive smoke or toxic byproducts when exposed to fire
conditions: When the curtain is required to comply with building fire codes for means of egress protection

subject: View-Framing Opening
rule: A view-framing opening must have a structurally adequate lintel or header spanning its full width to support the load above
conditions: opening is in a load-bearing wall
opening width exceeds the masonry or wall material's self-spanning limit
exceptions: opening is entirely within a non-load-bearing partition
opening is at the top of a wall with no load above

subject: View-Framing Opening
rule: A view-framing opening must not compromise the lateral bracing or shear resistance of the wall it penetrates
conditions: wall is designated as a shear wall or lateral-force-resisting element
exceptions: the opening is accounted for in an engineered lateral-force-resisting system with appropriate strengthening around the opening

subject: View-Framing Opening
rule: A view-framing opening must maintain a minimum edge distance from corners and adjacent openings to prevent stress concentration and cracking
conditions: opening is in a masonry or concrete wall

subject: View-Skirting Wall
rule: View-skirting wall must not block required sightlines from the viewing area
conditions: When the wall is located between a viewing position and a target scene
exceptions: When the wall itself is designed as a transparent or translucent element
When the wall height is below the minimum eye-level sightline

subject: View-Skirting Wall
rule: View-skirting wall must be structurally self-supporting or adequately braced to resist lateral loads
conditions: When the wall is freestanding (not bearing on an adjacent structure)
exceptions: When the wall is permanently tied to a primary structural frame

subject: View-Skirting Wall
rule: View-skirting wall must not create a tripping hazard at floor-level transitions
conditions: When the wall base is located in a walking path or egress route
exceptions: When the wall base is flush with the finished floor and does not project above the walking surface

subject: Zen-View Glazing Assembly
rule: glazing assembly must be structurally supported by a load-bearing frame or substructure
conditions: when used as a vertical or inclined building enclosure

subject: Zen-View Glazing Assembly
rule: glazing panes must not be placed in direct contact with incompatible materials that cause galvanic corrosion or chemical etching
conditions: when aluminum frames or dissimilar metal flashings are part of the assembly
exceptions: when an appropriate insulating barrier, gasket, or coating separates the materials

subject: Zen-View Glazing Assembly
rule: glazing assembly must accommodate thermal expansion and contraction without glass breakage or seal failure
conditions: when the assembly spans more than 1.2 m in any dimension or is exposed to direct solar radiation
exceptions: small spandrel panels fully isolated by structural silicone and designed with calculated expansion gaps

subject: Shoji-Style View Screen
rule: shoji-style view screen must have a stable, level base or mounting to prevent tipping
conditions: when installed as a freestanding architectural element
exceptions: when designed to intentionally tilt as part of its aesthetic or viewing function

subject: Shoji-Style View Screen
rule: shoji-style view screen must not obstruct required egress paths or emergency exits
conditions: when placed in a means of egress or circulation path
exceptions: when the screen is intentionally part of a fire-rated assembly that meets code requirements for opening protectives

subject: Shoji-Style View Screen
rule: shoji-style view screen must not block required natural light or ventilation openings if those are mandated by code
conditions: when the screen is placed directly in front of a required window or ventilation opening
and the local building code requires minimum natural light or ventilation
exceptions: when the screen is designed as a translucent shoji (washi/paper) that allows light transmission and some airflow

subject: View-Platform/Deck
rule: View-platform/deck surface must have a minimum slope to drain water
conditions: outdoor exposure
uncovered deck
exceptions: indoor observation deck with conditioned space and active drainage systems

subject: View-Platform/Deck
rule: View-platform/deck guardrail or balustrade must be at least 42 inches (1.07 m) in height above the walking surface
conditions: deck elevated more than 30 inches (0.76 m) above grade or floor below

subject: View-Platform/Deck
rule: View-platform/deck guardrails must have balusters or infill spaced such that a 4-inch (100 mm) sphere cannot pass through
conditions: deck elevated more than 30 inches (0.76 m) above grade or floor below

subject: View-Platform/Deck
rule: View-platform/deck must not have a concentrated point load exceeding its structural design capacity without additional reinforcement
exceptions: areas specifically designed and engineered for concentrated loads such as designated heavy equipment zones

subject: View-Platform/Deck
rule: View-platform/deck walking surface must be slip-resistant when wet
conditions: outdoor or unconditioned indoor deck exposed to moisture
exceptions: interior conditioned decks not exposed to moisture and with documented alternative fall-prevention measures

subject: Engawa (Veranda)
rule: engawa veranda must have a roof or overhead covering
conditions: the engawa is attached to a building
the engawa is exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: the engawa is located in a climate region where overhead protection is not required for usability (very rare)

subject: Engawa (Veranda)
rule: engawa veranda floor surface must be weather-resistant and allow drainage
conditions: the engawa is exposed to exterior weather

subject: Engawa (Veranda)
rule: engawa veranda must_not have a height difference that creates a tripping hazard at the transition to the interior floor
conditions: the engawa is intended for seated or walking use as a transition zone

subject: Shadow-Casting Brise-Soleil
rule: brise-soleil must be structurally attached to the building facade or frame
conditions: applies to all shadow-casting brise-soleil installations

subject: Shadow-Casting Brise-Soleil
rule: brise-soleil slats or panels must not completely block natural ventilation paths required by code
conditions: where the brise-soleil is mounted directly in front of operable windows or ventilation openings
exceptions: buildings with fully mechanical ventilation and no required natural ventilation openings

subject: Shadow-Casting Brise-Soleil
rule: brise-soleil must not shed water onto building entrance paths or public walkways in a way that creates ice hazards
conditions: in climates where freezing temperatures occur
where the brise-soleil extends beyond the building footprint

subject: Daylight-Responsive Automated Shade System
rule: Must have a dedicated power supply (wired or self-powered via integrated photovoltaics/battery)
conditions: when deployed as an automated system requiring motorized actuation

subject: Daylight-Responsive Automated Shade System
rule: Must have a continuous control loop connecting at least one photosensor input to the actuator output
conditions: when classified as 'daylight-responsive' and 'automated'

subject: Daylight-Responsive Automated Shade System
rule: Must not block required egress path or emergency exit route
conditions: when installed over or adjacent to a window or opening serving as an egress point

subject: Light Well / Atrium Void
rule: light well / atrium void must provide a clear vertical path for light transmission from top to bottom
conditions: designed as a light well or atrium for daylighting purposes
exceptions: void is entirely decorative and does not serve a daylighting function

subject: Light Well / Atrium Void
rule: light well / atrium void must be open to the exterior at the top (or have a fully transparent/translucent roof covering)
conditions: serves as the primary source of natural light to adjacent occupied spaces
exceptions: atrium is artificially lit and not intended to admit daylight

subject: Light Well / Atrium Void
rule: light well / atrium void must not have floor plates that fully block the void's cross-section at any level
conditions: void is continuous through multiple floors
exceptions: bridges and walkways that occupy less than ~20% of the cross-sectional area are permissible

subject: Light Well / Atrium Void
rule: light well / atrium void in a fire-rated building must have smoke management or be compartmentalised to prevent smoke spread between floors
conditions: building is subject to fire codes and the void connects three or more storeys
exceptions: local codes explicitly exempt small residential light wells (e.g., single-family stairwell voids)

subject: Master Bedroom
rule: master bedroom must have at least one egress window or door that provides a clear opening to the outside for emergency escape and rescue
conditions: room is used for sleeping
room is located in a residential dwelling unit
exceptions: room has a sprinkler system where local code permits

subject: Master Bedroom
rule: master bedroom must have a minimum ceiling height of at least 7 feet (2.13 m) over at least 50% of the room area
conditions: occupiable space
exceptions: rooms with sloped ceilings where the minimum height applies only to the required floor area portion

subject: Master Bedroom
rule: master bedroom must have at least one operable window providing natural ventilation equivalent to at least 4% of the floor area
conditions: room is mechanically ventilated
building code requires natural ventilation
exceptions: room is served by a mechanical ventilation system that meets code-required air changes per hour

subject: Master Bedroom
rule: master bedroom must not have a direct opening into a garage unless a self-closing fire-rated door is provided
conditions: bedroom shares a wall with an attached garage

subject: En-suite Bathroom
rule: en-suite bathroom must have a waterproof floor assembly (e.g., tile over waterproof membrane with sealed joints)

subject: En-suite Bathroom
rule: en-suite bathroom must have a ventilation path to the exterior (mechanical or natural) that removes moisture-laden air

subject: En-suite Bathroom
rule: en-suite bathroom must have a trapped sanitary drainage connection for the shower/bath waste

subject: Bidet
rule: bidet must have a water supply connection with backflow prevention
conditions: when connected to potable water supply

subject: Bidet
rule: bidet must have a drain connection to sanitary sewer or approved wastewater system

subject: Bidet
rule: bidet water spray or nozzle must not contact the toilet bowl or bidet basin rim at a height below the flood-level rim

subject: Bidet
rule: bidet electrical components (if present) must be protected from water ingress with appropriate IP rating
conditions: when bidet includes electrically powered features (heater, pump, electronic controls)

subject: Private Toilet Compartment
rule: must have a floor drain
conditions: private toilet compartment contains a toilet or shower

subject: Private Toilet Compartment
rule: must have a ventilation path to the exterior or a mechanical exhaust system
conditions: private toilet compartment is enclosed and has no operable window to the exterior

subject: Private Toilet Compartment
rule: floor surface must be waterproof and slip-resistant

subject: Private Toilet Compartment
rule: door must swing outward or be a pocket door
conditions: compartment is a single-occupancy private toilet room less than the minimum clear floor space required for inward-swinging door clearance

subject: Private Toilet Compartment
rule: must not share a light switch or exhaust fan switch with an adjacent compartment that could be confused
conditions: private toilet compartment is in a multi-compartment restroom arrangement

subject: Built-in Wardrobe System
rule: built-in wardrobe system must have a minimum interior depth to accommodate standard hanging garments
conditions: when designed for hanging clothes storage
exceptions: when designed exclusively for folded storage or shelving only

subject: Built-in Wardrobe System
rule: built-in wardrobe system doors must not obstruct adjacent room circulation when opened
conditions: when sliding doors are not used
when wardrobe is located in a circulation path or room with limited clear floor area
exceptions: when sliding doors are specified

subject: Master Suite Sitting Area
rule: master suite sitting area must provide a minimum clear floor area of 4 feet by 4 feet (1.2 m x 1.2 m) to accommodate seating furniture and occupant egress
conditions: if the space is designated as a sitting area within a dwelling unit
exceptions: when the space is used exclusively as a passage/aisle and not for stationary seating

subject: Master Suite Sitting Area
rule: master suite sitting area must not be located such that its only means of egress passes through a bathroom
conditions: if the sitting area is part of a dwelling unit required to comply with life safety egress paths
exceptions: if the sitting area has a second independent means of egress (e.g., direct door to corridor or exterior)

subject: Jewelry Safe / In-Room Safe
rule: Jewelry safe must have a locking mechanism that can be securely locked and unlocked

subject: Jewelry Safe / In-Room Safe
rule: Jewelry safe must have physical walls, a door, and an enclosure that are structurally continuous (no open sides or gaps large enough to reach through)

subject: Jewelry Safe / In-Room Safe
rule: Jewelry safe must_not have a door that can be opened without defeating the locking mechanism or without proper credentials

subject: Acoustic Insulation Layer
rule: Acoustic insulation layer must remain continuous across building enclosure assemblies to prevent flanking paths
conditions: When installed in walls, roofs, or floor-ceiling assemblies
exceptions: Joints sealed with acoustic sealant to match STC rating of the assembly

subject: Acoustic Insulation Layer
rule: Acoustic insulation layer must not be compressed beyond its designed thickness during installation
conditions: When using fibrous or porous acoustic insulation materials such as mineral wool or fiberglass batts
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified slight compression for friction-fit installation that does not exceed 5-10% thickness reduction

subject: Acoustic Insulation Layer
rule: Acoustic insulation layer must be separated from both sides of the assembly by an air gap or resilient decoupling when used in high-STC-rated assemblies
conditions: When the assembly requires STC 50 or higher performance in wood-frame or steel-frame construction
exceptions: When using insulation with integrated resilient channels or decoupling clips that maintain the separation

subject: Underfloor Heating System
rule: underfloor heating system must not be installed beneath fixed heavy fixtures (e.g., bathtubs, kitchen islands, built-in cabinets, or load-bearing walls)
conditions: system is embedded in a concrete screed or timber subfloor
exceptions: fixture is designed with removable access panels and the manufacturer explicitly approves underfloor heating beneath it

subject: Underfloor Heating System
rule: underfloor heating system must have a maximum surface temperature limit to prevent flooring damage or burn injury
conditions: system is installed in habitable spaces
floor covering is wood, laminate, vinyl, or carpet
exceptions: system is installed in non-habitable spaces (e.g., garage, workshop) with appropriate warnings

subject: Underfloor Heating System
rule: underfloor heating system must have a minimum insulation layer beneath it when installed over an unheated space or on-grade slab
conditions: system is installed above an unheated basement, crawlspace, or exterior-grade slab
exceptions: the subfloor assembly is designed as a thermally broken system (e.g., structural insulated panels) that meets equivalent thermal resistance

subject: Underfloor Heating System
rule: underfloor heating system must not have pipes or cables crossing movement joints in the subfloor without an expansion loop or protective sleeve
conditions: subfloor contains construction, expansion, or seismic movement joints
exceptions: system is designed with flexible connections that can accommodate the joint movement and is manufacturer-approved for such use

subject: Exhaust Ventilation Duct
rule: exhaust ventilation duct must be connected to a fan or mechanical ventilation system to create airflow

subject: Exhaust Ventilation Duct
rule: exhaust ventilation duct must terminate to the outdoors or to a permitted exhaust system discharge point
exceptions: recirculating range hoods that filter and return air to the space

subject: Exhaust Ventilation Duct
rule: exhaust ventilation duct must not have sharp reductions in cross-sectional area or severe bends that prevent airflow

subject: Exhaust Ventilation Duct
rule: exhaust ventilation duct must be constructed of material rated for the temperature of the exhaust airstream

subject: Towel Warming Rack
rule: Towel warming rack must have a method of heat dissipation that prevents surface temperatures from exceeding safe touch limits (typically 60°C / 140°F) in areas accessible to users
conditions: rack is installed in a bathroom or living space
rack is accessible to bare skin contact
exceptions: rack is installed in a locked mechanical room or other inaccessible location
rack is explicitly designed and labeled as a high-temperature industrial unit with safety barriers

subject: Towel Warming Rack
rule: Towel warming rack must not have ungrounded electrical components in contact with or capable of contacting water
conditions: rack is electrically powered
rack is installed in a bathroom, laundry, or other wet or damp location
exceptions: rack is powered by low-voltage DC (≤ 12V) with isolated power supply outside wet zone
rack is a purely hydronic (hot water) type with no electrical components

subject: Child-Safe Flooring
rule: Child-safe flooring must have a slip-resistant surface finish
conditions: when used in wet areas such as bathrooms or kitchens
when used in high-traffic play areas

subject: Child-Safe Flooring
rule: Child-safe flooring must be free of toxic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and hazardous chemicals

subject: Child-Safe Flooring
rule: Child-safe flooring must have a minimum impact-absorbing/cushioning property meeting safety standards for fall attenuation
conditions: when installed in areas with play equipment above 0.5m fall height
when specified for early childhood education centers

subject: Child-Safe Flooring
rule: Child-safe flooring must_not have sharp edges, splinters, or protruding fasteners

subject: Child-Safe Flooring
rule: Child-safe flooring must have a closed, non-porous surface that is resistant to bacterial and fungal growth
conditions: when used in childcare facilities or healthcare pediatric wards

subject: Child-Height Worktops
rule: A child-height worktop must have a minimum clear knee space underneath of at least 24 inches (610 mm) deep, 30 inches (762 mm) wide, and 27 inches (686 mm) high to allow wheelchair access
conditions: When the worktop is intended for use by a child in a wheelchair
When the worktop is installed in a facility covered by ADA or similar accessibility standards
exceptions: Worktops that are not fixed in place (e.g., portable/collapsible tables)

subject: Child-Height Worktops
rule: The worktop surface must not have sharp edges or corners at child head/eye height
conditions: When the worktop is installed at a height reachable by standing children (typically 20-30 inches from floor)

subject: Child-Height Worktops
rule: The worktop must be stable against tip-over under a lateral force of at least 20% of its own weight applied at the front edge
conditions: When the worktop is freestanding (not fixed to wall or floor)
exceptions: Worktops that are permanently anchored to a structural wall or floor

subject: Child-Height Worktops
rule: The worktop height must not exceed 34 inches (864 mm) from the finished floor
