rule: insulation must not be compressed when installed between framing or within cavities
conditions: fibrous insulation (e.g., fiberglass, mineral wool) is used
exceptions: rigid board or spray foam insulation where compression is not a failure mode

subject: Workshop Insulation and Vapor Barrier
rule: vapor barrier must be located on the warm-in-winter side of the insulation assembly
conditions: workshop is in a heating-dominated climate zone
exceptions: cooling-dominated climate zones where vapor barrier should be on the warm-in-summer side (outside of insulation)
climate zones where vapor-permeable assemblies are code-compliant

subject: Tread
rule: tread depth must be sufficient to provide adequate friction and safe foot placement
conditions: component is used as a stair tread
component is used as a ladder tread

subject: Tread
rule: tread must have a non-slip surface or treatment
conditions: tread is exposed to pedestrian traffic
exceptions: tread is a purely decorative non-walkable element

subject: Tread
rule: tread must not have a vertical rise greater than the allowable maximum for the stair run
conditions: tread is part of a stair system

subject: Tread
rule: tread run (horizontal depth) must not be less than the code minimum for the intended occupancy
conditions: tread is part of a stair system serving occupied spaces

subject: Stringer
rule: stringer must be designed to resist buckling under compressive loads
conditions: when the stringer is subjected to compressive axial forces
exceptions: if the stringer is only in tension

subject: Stringer
rule: stringer must not exceed its yield strength under any design load combination

subject: Stringer
rule: stringer must have sufficient cross-section to carry the applied axial load without exceeding allowable stress

subject: Balustrade Assembly
rule: balustrade assembly must have a minimum height of 1100 mm above the finished floor level for fall protection
conditions: where the balustrade is adjacent to a change in level exceeding 600 mm
where the balustrade is serving as a guardrail
exceptions: industrial contexts or maintenance-only areas where local codes permit lower heights

subject: Balustrade Assembly
rule: balustrade assembly must not have gaps or openings that allow passage of a 100 mm sphere
conditions: where the balustrade is serving as a guardrail for fall protection
where children may be present (e.g., residential, schools, public buildings)
exceptions: balustrades in areas inaccessible to children (some industrial mezzanines)

subject: Balustrade Assembly
rule: balustrade assembly must be capable of resisting a uniformly distributed horizontal load of at least 0.74 kN/m applied at the top rail
conditions: where the balustrade is serving as a guardrail for occupancy Category A (domestic/residential)
exceptions: higher occupancy categories (assembly, institutional) require greater load resistance per code

subject: Balustrade Assembly
rule: balustrade assembly must not have sharp edges or projections capable of causing injury on handrails and exposed surfaces
conditions: where the balustrade is accessible to building occupants

subject: Stair Support Structure
rule: Stair support structure must be capable of carrying the design dead load plus the specified live load (occupancy, snow, etc.) without exceeding allowable stress or deflection limits
conditions: When the stair is intended for general building access
When the structure is designed for any occupancy load
exceptions: Stairs not intended for occupancy (e.g., purely decorative stairs with no load requirement)

subject: Stair Support Structure
rule: Stair support structure must not have a fire-resistance rating lower than the minimum required by building code for the stair enclosure or egress path
conditions: When the stair serves as a required means of egress
exceptions: Stairs that are not part of the required egress (e.g., private interior stairs in very small buildings may have lower requirements depending on jurisdiction)

subject: Stair Support Structure
rule: Stair support structure must provide a minimum live load capacity of 100 psf (4.79 kN/m²) for stairs within buildings with public or assembly occupancy
conditions: When the stair is part of a public building, assembly space, or egress route subject to high-density occupancy
exceptions: One- and two-family dwellings where codes typically permit 40 psf (1.92 kN/m²) residential loading

subject: Monolithic Concrete Open Stair
rule: monolithic concrete open stair must have a minimum clear width of at least the value required by applicable building code for egress
conditions: stair serves as means of egress
stair is part of a building subject to building code

subject: Monolithic Concrete Open Stair
rule: monolithic concrete open stair must have treads and risers that comply with the maximum riser height and minimum tread depth required by applicable building code
conditions: stair is intended for regular occupant use

subject: Monolithic Concrete Open Stair
rule: monolithic concrete open stair must have handrails on at least one side if the stair width exceeds the threshold in applicable building code
conditions: stair has more than a minimum number of risers (typically 3-4) as defined by code

subject: Monolithic Concrete Open Stair
rule: monolithic concrete open stair must have structural reinforcement adequate to support the design live load plus dead load without failure

subject: Monolithic Concrete Open Stair
rule: monolithic concrete open stair must not have open risers that exceed the maximum opening dimension permitted by building code (typically to prevent a 4-inch sphere from passing through)
conditions: stair serves children or is in a building where guardrail/riser opening limits apply
exceptions: stair is not part of a building type subject to child-safety opening limits

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must have treads capable of supporting a minimum live load of 100 psf (4.79 kN/m²) per IBC/OSHA requirements
conditions: stair is intended for occupant egress
stair is part of a building subject to IBC or OSHA

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must have slip-resistant tread surfaces
conditions: used in any environment where wet or oily conditions may occur

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must have handrails on both sides when width exceeds 44 inches
conditions: stair width is greater than 44 inches

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must not have a riser height exceeding 7 inches or less than 4 inches
conditions: stair is used for general occupant egress

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must have landing at top and bottom with depth at least equal to stair width
conditions: stair serves as a required means of egress

subject: Prefabricated Steel Open Stair
rule: Prefabricated steel open stair must have all structural steel connections designed for the full factored load path

subject: Timber Open Stair
rule: timber open stair tread must have a minimum depth of 200 mm (or local code minimum) to safely accommodate a human foot
exceptions: private residential stairs with specific local building code exceptions

subject: Timber Open Stair
rule: timber open stair riser height must not exceed 200 mm (or local code maximum)
exceptions: private residential stairs where local code allows up to 220 mm in some jurisdictions

subject: Timber Open Stair
rule: timber open stair must have a handrail on at least one side if the total rise exceeds 600 mm
conditions: total stair rise exceeds 600 mm

subject: Timber Open Stair
rule: open gap between adjacent treads on a timber open stair must not exceed 100 mm (or local code limit) to prevent a child's body from passing through
exceptions: stair is not accessible to children under 5 years old and local code explicitly exempts

subject: Glass Tread Stair
rule: glass tread stair must have anti-slip surface treatment
conditions: installed in commercial or public building
wet or high-moisture environment
exceptions: stair is intended for decorative use only and not meant for regular foot traffic

subject: Glass Tread Stair
rule: glass tread stair must be constructed of tempered or laminated safety glass
conditions: stair is load-bearing and used for human occupancy

subject: Glass Tread Stair
rule: glass tread stair must_not have visible surface cracks, chips, or edge defects
conditions: stair is in use

subject: Glass Tread Stair
rule: glass tread stair span must_not exceed the manufacturer's certified maximum unsupported length

subject: Cantilevered Open Stair
rule: cantilevered open stair must have a minimum tread depth that supports safe foot placement
conditions: intended for occupiable use

subject: Cantilevered Open Stair
rule: cantilevered open stair must have a maximum riser height to prevent tripping
conditions: intended for occupiable use
stairs are not exempt egress elements
exceptions: private stairs within a single dwelling unit where local code allows greater variation

subject: Cantilevered Open Stair
rule: cantilevered open stair must have handrails on at least one side
conditions: open side exists
total rise exceeds 600 mm
exceptions: stairs serving only a single non-occupiable platform where local code excludes handrail requirement

subject: Cantilevered Open Stair
rule: cantilevered open stair must_not have tread-to-tread gap that exceeds a child's head passage limit
conditions: guard or handrail balusters are present
the stair is accessible to children under 5
exceptions: private residence with no children occupants and local code exempts

subject: Cantilevered Open Stair
rule: cantilevered open stair treads must be designed to resist the full live load without relying on riser support
conditions: treads are cantilevered from a supporting wall or stringer

subject: Under-Stair Enclosure
rule: Under-stair enclosure must have a minimum headroom clearance of at least 6 ft 8 in (2030 mm) at the stair side opening to allow safe passage
conditions: used as a habitable space
or used as an egress path
exceptions: if only used for storage and not on any egress path, local codes may permit reduced headroom (e.g., 6 ft 4 in)

subject: Under-Stair Enclosure
rule: Under-stair enclosure must be enclosed with fire-rated construction (typically 1-hour fire-resistance rating) if the stair serves more than two stories or is part of a required means of egress
conditions: stair is part of a building with more than two stories
or stair is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: one- and two-family dwellings typically exempt

subject: Under-Stair Enclosure
rule: Under-stair enclosure must not contain mechanical, electrical, or plumbing equipment that requires maintenance access unless the enclosure provides adequate access panel or door
conditions: mechanical, electrical, or plumbing equipment is present within the enclosure
exceptions: no equipment present — no constraint applies

subject: Under-Stair Enclosure
rule: Under-stair enclosure must not have a finished ceiling height less than the code-minimum habitable space height (7 ft 6 in typical) if it is designed as a habitable room
conditions: enclosure is designed as a habitable room (e.g., bathroom, closet counts as habitable in some codes)
exceptions: non-habitable storage only — no constraint

subject: Stair Opening (Stairwell)
rule: stair opening (stairwell) must be enclosed by fire-resistance-rated construction
conditions: building has more than one story
stairwell connects multiple floors
exceptions: single-story buildings
open stairs in buildings with sprinkler systems where local code permits

subject: Stair Opening (Stairwell)
rule: stair opening must have a minimum clear width of at least 44 inches (1118 mm) for means of egress
conditions: stair is part of a required means of egress
stair serves more than 50 occupants on a floor
exceptions: stairs serving less than 50 occupants may reduce to 36 inches (914 mm)

subject: Stair Opening (Stairwell)
rule: stair opening must not have any dimension that reduces the headroom clearance below 6 feet 8 inches (2032 mm)

subject: Stair Opening (Stairwell)
rule: stair opening must not allow direct opening into the stair enclosure from spaces with hazardous contents (e.g., storage rooms, boiler rooms)
conditions: the space is classified as high-hazard or containing flammable/combustible materials
exceptions: vestibules or airlocks with fire-rated doors may be used as intervening spaces

subject: Stair Opening (Stairwell)
rule: stair opening landing at each floor level must be at least as wide as the stair width

subject: Perimeter Glazing
rule: perimeter glazing must be protected by a structurally adequate guardrail or fall-protection system where the glazing is at a height that creates a fall risk
conditions: glazing is located at a floor or balcony edge
drop height exceeds applicable building code threshold (typically 30 inches or more)
exceptions: glazing is fully tempered and meets CPSC 16 CFR 1201 or equivalent impact/fall-out safety standards accepted by local code as a substitute for a guardrail

subject: Perimeter Glazing
rule: perimeter glazing must resist the design wind load for its location without failure or unsafe deflection
conditions: glazing is part of the building envelope (exterior wall)
exceptions: interior perimeter glazing not exposed to wind

subject: Perimeter Glazing
rule: perimeter glazing must not create an unsafe condition where a person can fall through or be entrapped between the glazing and an adjacent fixed element
conditions: glazing is operable (awning, casement, sliding, etc.) or has large openable panels
exceptions: openings are protected by guards or screens that prevent passage of a 4-inch sphere
openings are limited by code-required restrictors to less than 4 inches

subject: Perimeter Glazing
rule: perimeter glazing must be glazed with safety-rated glass (tempered or laminated) where the glazing is in a hazardous location as defined by building code
conditions: glazing is within 18 inches of the floor
glazing is within 24 inches of a door opening
glazing is in a shower or bath enclosure
glazing is in a sidelight adjacent to a door
exceptions: glazing is fully laminated and meets impact safety criteria without tempering where code permits

subject: Light Shelves
rule: Light shelves must have a minimum tilt angle to prevent water pooling
conditions: installed in exterior/outdoor application
exposed to precipitation
exceptions: interior-only light shelves
light shelves with active drainage systems

subject: Light Shelves
rule: Light shelves must not block required egress or emergency ventilation openings
conditions: installed on facades that contain emergency exits or operable windows required by code
exceptions: building designs where all egress is provided via other means (e.g., alternate facade)

subject: Light Shelves
rule: Light shelves must have a smooth, cleanable upper surface
conditions: installed in locations with limited access for cleaning
exposed to dust, pollen, or bird debris
exceptions: light shelves with automated cleaning systems
light shelves in hermetically sealed cavity applications

subject: Reflective Interior Surfaces
rule: reflective interior surfaces must not create concentrated solar glare that could ignite materials or cause thermal damage
conditions: surface is positioned opposite windows or other daylight openings
surface has high specular reflectivity (e.g., polished metal, mirror)
exceptions: surface is intentionally designed as part of a daylighting system with fire-rated glazing and thermal break controls

subject: Reflective Interior Surfaces
rule: reflective interior surfaces must maintain a minimum fire performance rating per applicable building code
conditions: surface is installed in an egress path or occupied space

subject: Reflective Interior Surfaces
rule: reflective interior surfaces must_not produce specular glare directed at occupant eye level in critical task areas
conditions: surface is located in a workspace, classroom, or healthcare treatment area
surface angle relative to light source is between 20 and 70 degrees
exceptions: area is designated as a controlled lighting environment where occupants use personal protective eyewear

subject: Automatic Shading Devices
rule: Automatic shading devices must be structurally supported by the building facade or frame
conditions: When mounted externally on the building envelope
exceptions: When shading device is freestanding/ground-mounted and not attached to the building

subject: Automatic Shading Devices
rule: Automatic shading devices must have a power supply or energy source to enable automated operation
conditions: For any motorized or automated actuation mechanism
exceptions: Manually operated shading devices are not automatic

subject: Automatic Shading Devices
rule: Automatic shading devices must not obstruct required means of egress or emergency exit pathways
conditions: When installed over or adjacent to doors, windows, or paths designated as fire egress routes
exceptions: When device retracts fully and automatically upon fire alarm or power loss, leaving clear egress path

subject: Automatic Shading Devices
rule: Automatic shading device control systems must not create a single-point electrical hazard when wet
conditions: When installed in locations exposed to rain, condensation, or irrigation spray
exceptions: Devices rated for wet locations with proper ingress protection (IP rating)

subject: Double-Loaded Corridor Layout
rule: Corridor width must accommodate two-way pedestrian flow and emergency egress (minimum clear width typically 1.8–2.4 m).
conditions: Occupied on both sides by habitable rooms or offices
exceptions: Single-loaded corridors are exempt because one side is open or exterior

subject: Double-Loaded Corridor Layout
rule: Corridor must be fire-rated (typically 1-hour fire-resistance rating) when serving as the sole egress path from rooms on both sides.
conditions: Building height exceeds two storeys or local code requires rated corridors
exceptions: Buildings with sprinkler systems throughout may allow reduced ratings per some codes

subject: Double-Loaded Corridor Layout
rule: Corridor must not have dead-end travel distance exceeding code maximum (typically 6–15 m depending on occupancy and sprinkler presence).
conditions: Corridor has a dead-end configuration
exceptions: Buildings fully sprinklered and with smoke control may be permitted longer dead-ends per some codes

subject: Double-Loaded Corridor Layout
rule: Corridor must have doors swinging into rooms (not into corridor) when occupant load exceeds 50 people per room.
conditions: Rooms served have occupant load > 50
exceptions: Doors may swing into corridor if corridor width is increased per code

subject: Window Wall Assembly
rule: window wall assembly must have continuous air barrier sealing at all perimeter joints, penetrations, and transitions
conditions: when used as exterior envelope
when building is conditioned
exceptions: assembly is intentionally designed as a non-pressure-boundary sunscreen

subject: Window Wall Assembly
rule: window wall assembly must be structurally anchored to the building's primary structure at each floor level
conditions: when spanning multiple stories
exceptions: single-story applications where continuous spandrel anchoring is used

subject: Window Wall Assembly
rule: window wall assembly must not permit water penetration under a static pressure differential of 300 Pa or greater
conditions: when tested in accordance with ASTM E1105

subject: Window Wall Assembly
rule: window wall assembly must accommodate differential movement between the assembly frame and the building structure
conditions: when building structure is steel or concrete frame
exceptions: structureless buildings or structures with identical coefficient of thermal expansion

subject: Glare Control Louvers
rule: Glare control louvers must be oriented to block direct sun paths
conditions: installed in overhead or clerestory glazing
targeting solar heat gain or glare reduction

subject: Glare Control Louvers
rule: Glare control louvers must have an opaque or sufficiently reflective surface finish on the sun-facing side
conditions: operating in visible light spectrum for glare control

subject: Glare Control Louvers
rule: Glare control louvers must not be placed where they obstruct required emergency egress or fire/smoke exhaust paths
conditions: located in a means of egress path
or within a smoke-control zone requiring automatic exhaust
exceptions: if louvers are designed to automatically retract or break away under fire/smoke conditions

subject: Building Edge Foundation
rule: building edge foundation must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: site has soil
exceptions: foundation is piled or caisson-supported to competent strata

subject: Building Edge Foundation
rule: building edge foundation must extend below frost depth
conditions: climate zone experiences seasonal freezing
exceptions: foundation is on non-frost-susceptible soil with slab-on-grade or frost-protected shallow foundation design per code

subject: Building Edge Foundation
rule: building edge foundation must not rest on organic topsoil, uncompacted fill, or debris
exceptions: material is removed and replaced with engineered fill prior to founding

subject: Drip Edge
rule: drip edge must be installed at roof edges to direct water away from the fascia and into the gutter
conditions: roof has a sloped roofing system
roof has a gutter system
exceptions: roof with integrated edge metal that serves the same function without a separate drip edge component

subject: Drip Edge
rule: drip edge must extend at least 2 inches up the roof deck and be installed under the underlayment on the roof deck side
conditions: asphalt shingle roof assembly with underlayment
exceptions: metal roof systems where drip edge is installed over the underlayment per manufacturer instructions

subject: Drip Edge
rule: drip edge must not be omitted at eaves and rakes in roof assemblies
conditions: roof is a pitched roof
local building code requires drip edge per IRC or IBC
exceptions: buildings where code exempts drip edge (e.g., certain accessory structures)
roof assemblies designed with a self-flashing edge condition that replaces drip edge function

subject: Perimeter Drainage System
rule: perimeter drainage system must have continuous positive slope (minimum 0.5%) along its entire length
conditions: system is gravity-fed
system is not under pressurized flow
exceptions: system includes pump-assisted lift stations at low points

subject: Perimeter Drainage System
rule: perimeter drainage system must not discharge directly onto a public sidewalk or pedestrian walkway
conditions: system outlet is at grade level
exceptions: outlet is equipped with a splash block or diffuse outlet that directs flow away from pedestrian zone

subject: Perimeter Drainage System
rule: perimeter drainage system must have a minimum 2-foot horizontal separation from building foundation wall
conditions: system is a French drain or perforated pipe type
system is located below grade
exceptions: system is a surface swale with impermeable liner directing water away

subject: Perimeter Drainage System
rule: perimeter drainage system must not outlet into a sanitary sewer system
conditions: jurisdiction has separate storm and sanitary sewers
exceptions: jurisdiction explicitly permits combined sewer connections and system includes backflow prevention

subject: Building Edge Sealant
rule: Building edge sealant must be compatible with the adjacent building materials to prevent chemical degradation or adhesion failure
conditions: When sealant contacts dissimilar materials (e.g., metal, concrete, glass, masonry)
exceptions: When a compatible primer or bond-breaker layer is used that has been tested and approved for the specific material combination

subject: Building Edge Sealant
rule: Building edge sealant must remain flexible enough to accommodate the expected thermal and structural movement of the building envelope without cohesive or adhesive failure
conditions: For sealants installed in joints or interfaces subject to cyclic movement from thermal expansion, contraction, wind load, or building settlement
exceptions: When the edge sealant is specified as a rigid, non-moving seal (e.g., certain glazing tapes designed for zero-movement applications)

subject: Building Edge Sealant
rule: Building edge sealant must not be applied to wet, frost-covered, or contaminated surfaces that prevent proper adhesion
conditions: During installation on any substrate
exceptions: When the sealant manufacturer explicitly certifies application on damp surfaces with a specific surface preparation protocol

subject: Edge of Slab
rule: edge of slab must be provided with a continuous load-bearing support beneath its entire length
conditions: where slab edge is not cantilevered
where slab transfers load to walls or beams
exceptions: when edge of slab is specifically designed as a cantilever with approved engineering detailing

subject: Edge of Slab
rule: edge of slab must have minimum concrete cover to reinforcement as required by exposure class and fire rating
conditions: for reinforced concrete slabs
exceptions: when protected by an additional permanent topping or cladding system that provides equivalent cover

subject: Edge of Slab
rule: edge of slab must not terminate without an edge form or bulkhead at a construction joint
conditions: during concrete placement
where slab is not a free edge in the final structure
exceptions: when slab edge is designed as a free architectural edge with no subsequent pour abutting it

subject: Copings and Parapet Caps
rule: copings and parapet caps must be securely anchored to the wall or roof structure to prevent wind uplift or displacement

subject: Copings and Parapet Caps
rule: parapet caps must have a continuous slope (minimum 1:4 or as specified) to direct water away from the parapet wall

subject: Copings and Parapet Caps
rule: metal copings must have expansion joints at intervals no greater than the manufacturer's specified maximum
conditions: metal coping

subject: Copings and Parapet Caps
rule: parapet caps and copings must not be installed without a continuous underlying membrane or flashing where required by the wall assembly type

subject: Perimeter Flashing
rule: perimeter flashing must be installed at all roof edges, parapets, and penetrations where the roofing membrane terminates
conditions: where roofing membrane terminates at an edge, parapet, curb, or penetration
exceptions: fully adhered single-ply membranes mechanically fastened at the perimeter may use alternate termination detail

subject: Perimeter Flashing
rule: perimeter flashing must extend at least 8 inches (200 mm) above the finished roof surface
conditions: on low-slope roofs
exceptions: ballasted roof systems with engineered paver details may use lower height

subject: Perimeter Flashing
rule: perimeter flashing must be positively secured to the building structure with corrosion-resistant fasteners at maximum 24-inch (600 mm) on-center spacing
conditions: where wind-uplift resistance is required by code
exceptions: fully adhered flashing systems with tested wind-uplift rating may use adhesive attachment per manufacturer specification

subject: Perimeter Flashing
rule: perimeter flashing must not be installed with incompatible metals in contact (galvanic corrosion)
conditions: when metal flashing is used
exceptions: metals separated by an approved dielectric barrier or in the same galvanic series group

subject: Perimeter Flashing
rule: perimeter flashing counterflashing (reglet) must be embedded a minimum of 1.5 inches (38 mm) into the masonry joint or substrate
conditions: where counterflashing is used against masonry walls
exceptions: surface-mounted counterflashing systems specifically tested and approved for the application

subject: Sun-Facing Glazing Assembly
rule: sun-facing glazing assembly must have adequate solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC) rating to prevent overheating in conditioned spaces
conditions: assembly is part of a conditioned building space
assembly receives direct solar exposure during occupied hours
exceptions: assembly is protected by external shading devices that fully intercept direct solar radiation
assembly is part of a passive solar heating system where heat gain is intentionally utilized

subject: Sun-Facing Glazing Assembly
rule: sun-facing glazing assembly must not have glass-to-frame thermal stress differential exceeding the design limits of the assembly
conditions: assembly incorporates glass panels with metallic frames
assembly is exposed to direct sunlight

subject: Sun-Facing Glazing Assembly
rule: sun-facing glazing assembly must have safety-rated glazing (tempered or laminated) where occupant impact risk exists
conditions: assembly is located within 18 inches of floor level
assembly is in a door or sidelight configuration
assembly is in a location where human impact is foreseeable (e.g., near walkways, play areas)
exceptions: assembly height prevents any reasonable human contact

subject: Exterior Solar Shading Device
rule: exterior solar shading device must be securely attached to the building structure

subject: Exterior Solar Shading Device
rule: exterior solar shading device must not block required egress paths or emergency access
conditions: when located near doors, windows, or egress routes

subject: Exterior Solar Shading Device
rule: exterior solar shading device must not accumulate water in a way that causes ponding or structural overloading
conditions: when device has horizontal or near-horizontal surfaces
exceptions: devices designed with integrated drainage

subject: Interior Solar Shading Device
rule: interior solar shading device must be installed with clear access for manual operation or maintenance
conditions: device is manually operated
exceptions: device is fully automated and does not require manual intervention

subject: Interior Solar Shading Device
rule: interior solar shading device must not obstruct emergency egress paths or fire safety equipment
conditions: device is located near a door, window, or corridor designated as an egress route

subject: Sunspace / Solar Conservatory
rule: glazing must be solar control / low-E coated to prevent overheating
conditions: space is used for passive solar heating
glazing area exceeds 30% of south-facing wall

subject: Sunspace / Solar Conservatory
rule: thermal mass must be present in the space to absorb and store solar heat gain
conditions: space is intended for year-round occupancy or passive heating

subject: Sunspace / Solar Conservatory
rule: operable vents or automated exhaust must be provided to prevent lethal temperature buildup
exceptions: space is unconditioned and used only for seasonal plant overwintering with no human occupancy

subject: Sunspace / Solar Conservatory
rule: glazing must not face within 45 degrees of north in the northern hemisphere (or south in the southern hemisphere) for passive heating performance
conditions: primary design purpose is passive solar heat collection

subject: Trombe Wall Assembly
rule: Trombe wall must have a south-facing (equator-facing in the northern hemisphere) glazing surface to capture solar radiation
conditions: Building is located in the northern hemisphere
Building is intended for passive solar heating
exceptions: Building is located in the southern hemisphere — then must face north

subject: Trombe Wall Assembly
rule: Trombe wall must include a thermal mass layer (e.g., concrete, masonry, stone) with adequate thickness for diurnal heat storage

subject: Trombe Wall Assembly
rule: Trombe wall must have an air gap between the glazing and the thermal mass to allow convective air circulation

subject: Trombe Wall Assembly
rule: Trombe wall glazing must not be fully shaded by adjacent structures, overhangs, or vegetation during the heating season
conditions: System is relied upon for space heating
exceptions: System is used only for night-time radiative cooling rather than heating

subject: Trombe Wall Assembly
rule: Trombe wall must have operable vents at both top and bottom of the wall to enable convective heat transfer into the occupied space
conditions: System is designed as a ventilated (circulating) Trombe wall rather than a sealed direct-gain wall

subject: Solar Thermal Collector Array
rule: Solar thermal collector array must be oriented within ±45° of true south in the northern hemisphere (or true north in the southern hemisphere) to maintain adequate solar exposure
conditions: Collector is installed at latitude above 15°
exceptions: Facility uses tracking mounts that automatically adjust orientation throughout the day
Site has documented shading analysis showing acceptable annual performance at a different orientation

subject: Solar Thermal Collector Array
rule: Solar thermal collector array must be installed at a tilt angle that prevents fluid stagnation temperatures from exceeding the maximum safe operating temperature of the collector and system components
conditions: System uses liquid heat-transfer fluid and includes no active drain-back mechanism
exceptions: System is designed with stagnation-safe components rated for the calculated stagnation temperature

subject: Solar Thermal Collector Array
rule: Solar thermal collector array must not be installed on a roof structure that cannot support the dead load of the collectors plus live loads (snow, wind, maintenance personnel) as specified by applicable building codes
conditions: Collectors are roof-mounted
exceptions: Installation is ground-mounted or wall-mounted instead of roof-mounted

subject: Phase-Change Material (PCM) Thermal Storage
rule: PCM must be encapsulated or contained within a leak-proof barrier
conditions: PCM is in liquid state during operation
PCM undergoes solid-liquid phase change
exceptions: PCM that remains solid throughout all operating conditions

subject: Phase-Change Material (PCM) Thermal Storage
rule: PCM must not exceed its maximum operating temperature threshold
conditions: PCM is integrated into a building thermal storage system
exceptions: PCM specifically formulated for higher temperature ranges that match the application

subject: Phase-Change Material (PCM) Thermal Storage
rule: PCM thermal storage must not be installed in direct contact with materials that chemically react with the PCM
conditions: PCM is exposed to or in contact with other building materials
exceptions: When a compatible barrier or liner separates the PCM from reactive materials

subject: Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) System
rule: BIPV system must be electrically isolated from the building structure to prevent electric shock hazards
conditions: system is grid-connected
system operates at voltages above safety extra-low voltage (SELV)
exceptions: systems designed with double or reinforced insulation in accordance with IEC 61730

subject: Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) System
rule: BIPV system must not create a single point of water ingress failure at roof or façade penetrations
conditions: system is installed in a weather-exposed envelope position
exceptions: systems with a redundant secondary waterproofing layer fully independent of the PV laminate

subject: Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) System
rule: BIPV system must have a documented thermal management path that prevents cell temperature from exceeding the module's rated maximum operating temperature
conditions: installation is on a roof or façade with limited rear ventilation (e.g., fully integrated, no air gap)
exceptions: modules certified to operate at the predicted stagnation temperature with no derating required

subject: Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) System
rule: BIPV system must not structurally overload the host building element
conditions: system replaces or is bonded to existing roof, façade, or glazing structure
exceptions: building structure has been verified by a structural engineer to have reserve capacity for the added dead and live loads

subject: Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) System
rule: BIPV system must comply with the same fire-resistance rating as the building element it replaces
conditions: system is installed on a fire-rated assembly (e.g., roof with Class A rating, façade with fire-resistance rating)
exceptions: building code permits an alternative engineered solution with equivalent performance

subject: North-facing wall assembly
rule: North-facing wall assembly in the northern hemisphere must incorporate sufficient thermal insulation to prevent condensation within the wall cavity
conditions: located in the northern hemisphere
conditioned interior space on the south side of the assembly
exceptions: unconditioned spaces that are vented to the exterior

subject: North-facing wall assembly
rule: North-facing wall assembly must be designed to resist wind-driven rain penetration
conditions: climate zone with significant wind-driven rain exposure
exceptions: protected by a full rain-screen over-cladding system

subject: North-facing wall assembly
rule: North-facing wall assembly must not have vapor barrier placed on the cold (exterior) side of the insulation in heating-dominated climates
conditions: heating-dominated climate (more annual heating degree days than cooling degree days)
vapor barrier is used in the assembly
exceptions: assemblies with ventilated drainage cavities that allow outward drying

subject: North-facing glazing system
rule: North-facing glazing system must be installed with a proper weather seal to prevent water infiltration
conditions: glazing is operable (openable)
glazing is exposed to exterior
exceptions: glazing is permanently sealed and interior-facing only

subject: North-facing glazing system
rule: North-facing glazing system must have a minimum insulating glass unit (double or triple glazing) in climates with heating degree days
conditions: building is located in a climate zone with significant heating load (HDD > 3000)
exceptions: glazing is part of a conditioned buffer space (e.g., sunspace not affecting occupied thermal zone)

subject: North-facing glazing system
rule: North-facing glazing system must not be structurally undersized for its span and wind load
conditions: glazing spans more than 1.2 m in any dimension
building is in a wind zone with design wind speed > 40 m/s

subject: North-facing shading devices
rule: North-facing shading devices must have a minimum projection angle sufficient to block direct solar radiation during the cooling season
conditions: Building is located in a climate zone with significant cooling loads
Shading is intended for passive solar control
exceptions: Device is designed as a light-shelf for daylight redirection rather than solar blocking

subject: North-facing shading devices
rule: North-facing shading devices must not block required daylight access or emergency egress paths
conditions: Device is installed at or below window sill level
Device is located near egress openings
exceptions: Device is retractable or movable such that it can be cleared during egress

subject: North-facing shading devices
rule: North-facing shading devices must be structurally anchored to resist wind uplift and dead loads without detachment
conditions: Device is permanently fixed (not temporary or seasonal)

subject: North entrance / lobby
rule: North entrance / lobby must have a minimum clear width of 1.2 m for wheelchair accessibility
conditions: building is publicly accessible
building has a main public entrance
exceptions: building is a single-family dwelling not open to the public

subject: North entrance / lobby
rule: North entrance / lobby must have a level landing or threshold that does not exceed 13 mm vertical rise
conditions: entrance serves as an accessible means of egress
exceptions: existing buildings with structural constraints where a ramp is provided

subject: North entrance / lobby
rule: North entrance / lobby must not have a step or stair as the only means of access
conditions: entrance is intended as a primary public entry
exceptions: building is exempt from accessibility requirements

subject: North entrance / lobby
rule: North entrance / lobby must have an illuminated exit sign visible from any point in the lobby
conditions: lobby is part of a means of egress path
floor area exceeds 20 m²
exceptions: lobby has direct exit to exterior within sight line without signage

subject: North roof edge / parapet
rule: North roof edge / parapet must resist wind uplift forces to prevent detachment
conditions: building is located in a region with design wind speeds exceeding 100 mph
parapet height exceeds 12 inches above the roof surface

subject: North roof edge / parapet
rule: North roof edge / parapet must have a continuous drainage path that prevents ponding at the roof-to-parapet intersection
conditions: roof is designed as a low-slope or flat roof

subject: North face rainwater drainage
rule: The north face rainwater drainage system must have continuous positive slope (minimum 1% for pipes, minimum 1/8 inch per foot for gutters) toward outlet points
conditions: Gravity-fed drainage system without mechanical pumping
exceptions: System uses siphonic roof drainage designed for flat roofs with zero-slope piping

subject: North face rainwater drainage
rule: The north face rainwater drainage system must not discharge onto pedestrian walkways, building entrances, or adjacent property in an uncontrolled manner
conditions: Rainwater outlet is at or near ground level
exceptions: Outlets are specifically designed as controlled splash pads or rain gardens with erosion protection and public safety measures

subject: North face rainwater drainage
rule: The north face rainwater drainage system must be sized to handle the design rainfall event (typically 100-year, 1-hour storm for the geographic location)
conditions: System serves any occupied building structure
exceptions: Temporary or ancillary structures where local code permits reduced design storm

subject: North face exterior insulation and finish system (EIFS)
rule: North face EIFS must have a water-resistive barrier (WRB) behind the insulation layer
conditions: Applied to exterior wall assembly
EIFS is installed over sheathing
exceptions: When the EIFS assembly is tested and certified as an integrated barrier system that eliminates the need for a separate WRB per code

subject: North face exterior insulation and finish system (EIFS)
rule: North face EIFS must_not be installed directly over absorbent substrate without a drainage plane
conditions: Applied on north (shaded, wetter) elevation
Substrate is gypsum sheathing or wood-based panel

subject: North face exterior insulation and finish system (EIFS)
rule: North face EIFS must include a termination flashing at all penetrations, joints, and base of wall

subject: North face snow/ice management system
rule: snow/ice management system on a north face must be designed to prevent uncontrolled ice fall or snow sliding onto occupied areas or egress paths
conditions: building has occupied areas or egress paths below the north face
exceptions: the area below is permanently barricaded and unoccupied

subject: North face snow/ice management system
rule: snow/ice management system must not impede required roof drainage
conditions: system is installed on a roof with a drainage system
exceptions: drainage is provided through or around the system with equivalent capacity

subject: North face snow/ice management system
rule: snow/ice management system on a north-facing slope must be rated for the full design snow load at that location
conditions: system supports or retains snow

subject: Terrace
rule: Terrace must have a minimum slope for water drainage away from the building envelope
conditions: terrace is exposed to precipitation
terrace is not fully covered by an impermeable membrane with active drainage
exceptions: terrace is entirely enclosed and climate-controlled

subject: Terrace
rule: Terrace must have a waterproof membrane or waterproofing layer protecting the structure below
conditions: terrace is located above habitable or occupiable space
terrace is exposed to precipitation or irrigation
exceptions: terrace is a structural slab with integral waterstop detailing and no occupied space beneath

subject: Terrace
rule: Terrace must have a load-bearing capacity sufficient for its intended occupancy load

subject: Terrace
rule: Terrace must not have ponding water that exceeds structural design limits
conditions: terrace is flat or low-slope (less than 1/4 inch per foot)
exceptions: terrace is specifically designed as a water-retention feature (e.g., green roof detention)

subject: Lanai
rule: Lanai must have a floor surface that is weather-resistant and sloped for water drainage away from the building
conditions: when the lanai is uncovered or partially covered
when the lanai is at grade or on a slab
exceptions: when the lanai is fully enclosed and conditioned as interior space

subject: Lanai
rule: Lanai must have a minimum 5-foot clear width in the primary egress path if it serves as an exit discharge path from the building
conditions: when the lanai is the only means of egress from any occupied space
when the lanai is part of a required exit discharge path
exceptions: when the lanai is not part of any required means of egress
when sprinklered and alternative code path permits reduced width

subject: Lanai
rule: Lanai must not have an open flame or cooking appliance within 36 inches of combustible materials if the lanai is not protected by an automatic sprinkler system
conditions: when the lanai contains a grill, fire pit, or outdoor kitchen equipment
exceptions: when non-combustible construction and clearance per manufacturer specification is provided

subject: Lanai
rule: Lanai roof structure must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot if covered
conditions: when the lanai has a solid roof covering
exceptions: when the roof is a green roof with engineered drainage and waterproofing

subject: Outdoor Stair
rule: an outdoor stair must have slip-resistant tread surfaces
conditions: exposed to weather
wet conditions possible

subject: Outdoor Stair
rule: an outdoor stair must have a handrail on at least one side
conditions: stair has more than 3 risers
rise height exceeds 600mm

subject: Outdoor Stair
rule: an outdoor stair must have drainage (gap or slope) to prevent water pooling on treads

subject: Outdoor Stair
rule: an outdoor stair tread must have a minimum depth of 255mm (10 inches) and maximum riser height of 200mm (8 inches)

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must have a maximum slope of 1:12 (8.33%) for accessibility
conditions: ramp serves as an accessible route
ramp is for pedestrian use
exceptions: existing ramps where compliance is structurally infeasible and documented

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must have a minimum clear width of 36 inches (915 mm) between handrails
conditions: ramp serves as an accessible route
ramp serves pedestrian use

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must have slip-resistant walking surface

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must have handrails on both sides when rise exceeds 6 inches
conditions: ramp rise is greater than 6 inches (150 mm)

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must have landings at top and bottom with dimensions at least as wide as ramp and minimum 60 inches in length

subject: Outdoor Ramp
rule: Outdoor ramp must not have a cross slope exceeding 1:50 (2%)
conditions: ramp serves as an accessible route

subject: Outdoor Balustrade
rule: outdoor balustrade must have a minimum height of 1.0 m (approx. 1000 mm) measured from the finished floor level to the top of the handrail
conditions: where the balustrade is adjacent to a change in level exceeding 600 mm
where the balustrade serves as a fall-protection barrier
exceptions: guardrails in residential single-family dwellings where local codes permit lower heights (e.g., 900 mm)

subject: Outdoor Balustrade
rule: outdoor balustrade must have baluster or infill spacing that prevents passage of a 100 mm diameter sphere
conditions: where the balustrade is used as a fall-protection barrier with open infill (e.g., vertical balusters, cable, glass)
exceptions: balustrades with solid panels or non-open infill

subject: Outdoor Balustrade
rule: outdoor balustrade must not have horizontal elements that can be used as a ladder or climbing aid
conditions: where the balustrade is required to serve as an anti-climb barrier for safety
where the balustrade has open rails (not solid panels)
exceptions: balustrades fully enclosed with solid panels
decorative horizontal rails that do not form a climbable pattern (rare, typically disallowed in most codes)

subject: Outdoor Balustrade
rule: outdoor balustrade handrail must have a cross-section diameter or width that is graspable, typically between 30 mm and 50 mm for circular sections
conditions: where the balustrade includes a handrail that serves as a gripping surface
exceptions: non-circular profiles that provide equivalent graspability per code

subject: Outdoor Balustrade
rule: outdoor balustrade must be self-supporting or continuously supported by a structure capable of resisting the design loads (minimum 0.74 kN/m live load at rail level, or 1.5 kN concentrated load)
conditions: where the balustrade is a structural barrier
exceptions: non-structural decorative balustrades not serving as barriers

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must have a minimum height of 900 mm (36 inches) measured from the stair nosing or ramp surface
conditions: when adjacent to stairs
when adjacent to ramps
when drop exceeds 600 mm

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must have a maximum opening size of 100 mm (4 inches) between balusters or between the bottom rail and tread
conditions: when guardrail includes balusters or infill

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must be graspable with a cross-section diameter between 30 mm and 50 mm (or equivalent perimeter)
conditions: when handrail is intended to be gripped by users
exceptions: handrails not required to be graspable per local code (e.g.,某些 country-specific exceptions)

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must have a minimum clearance of 50 mm (2 inches) between the handrail and any adjacent wall or surface
conditions: when mounted on or adjacent to a wall

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must not have sharp edges or protruding elements that could cause injury

subject: Outdoor Handrail
rule: Outdoor handrail must extend at least 300 mm (12 inches) horizontally beyond the top and bottom of stairs or ramp
conditions: at stair or ramp landings
exceptions: where local code permits lesser extensions for specific occupancy types

subject: Outdoor Floor Paving
rule: outdoor floor paving must have a minimum cross slope of 1% (1:100) for drainage away from building structures
conditions: paving is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: paving is designed with an integrated permeable surface system that handles drainage sub-grade

subject: Outdoor Floor Paving
rule: outdoor floor paving materials must have a coefficient of friction (COF) of at least 0.5 when wet
conditions: paving is in a pedestrian-accessible area exposed to rain or moisture
exceptions: area is permanently barricaded from pedestrian access

subject: Outdoor Floor Paving
rule: outdoor floor paving must have a minimum compressive strength adequate for its anticipated load
conditions: paving supports vehicular traffic or heavy equipment loads

subject: Outdoor Floor Paving
rule: outdoor floor paving must not create a trip hazard at transitions
conditions: paving is adjacent to another surface or changes level
exceptions: change in level is clearly marked and compliant with accessible design codes (e.g., beveled edge ≤ 1:2 slope)

subject: Outdoor Decking Board
rule: Outdoor decking board must be rated for exterior/outdoor use (e.g., treated wood, composite, or tropical hardwood)

subject: Outdoor Decking Board
rule: Outdoor decking board must be installed with sufficient gap between adjacent boards for drainage and ventilation
conditions: The decking boards are laid side by side in a standard deck surface

subject: Outdoor Decking Board
rule: Outdoor decking board must not be installed in direct ground contact unless specifically rated for ground-contact use
conditions: The decking boards are used at grade level or below
exceptions: Boards explicitly labeled for ground-contact (e.g., certain pressure-treated lumber)

subject: Outdoor Decking Board
rule: Outdoor decking board must be fastened with corrosion-resistant fasteners suitable for exterior exposure

subject: Outdoor Wall Cladding
rule: Outdoor wall cladding must provide a weather-resistant barrier to prevent moisture ingress into the building envelope
conditions: applied to exterior walls of conditioned spaces
exceptions: decorative cladding on freestanding non-enclosed structures (e.g., garden walls, fences) where no interior space is protected

subject: Outdoor Wall Cladding
rule: Outdoor wall cladding must be ventilated or drained to prevent moisture accumulation behind the cladding
conditions: installed over a substrate that is not a fully sealed waterproof membrane
cladding material is absorptive (e.g., wood, brick, stone, fiber cement)
exceptions: cladding applied directly to a waterproofed concrete wall with no cavity (e.g., thin stone veneer on concrete)
cladding system that is itself a fully bonded waterproof membrane (e.g., some EIFS with drained assembly)

subject: Outdoor Wall Cladding
rule: Outdoor wall cladding must be fastened to resist design wind loads without detachment
conditions: building is in any wind-exposed region

subject: Pergola
rule: pergola roof structure must be open to allow natural light penetration (typically lath, rafters, or slats with spacing)
conditions: when described as a pergola in architectural context
exceptions: modern pergola designs with operable louvers or retractable canopy covers that can close fully

subject: Pergola
rule: pergola must be structurally self-supporting or attached to a primary building for lateral stability
conditions: free-standing pergola
exceptions: pergolas attached directly to a house wall gain lateral support from that wall

subject: Pergola
rule: pergola posts must be embedded in or anchored to a foundation sufficient to resist overturning
conditions: any permanent pergola
exceptions: very small/lightweight temporary pergolas not intended for wind resistance

subject: Outdoor Ceiling
rule: outdoor ceiling must be sloped for water runoff
conditions: subject to direct rain exposure
exceptions: ceiling has a sealed/waterproof membrane and positive drainage elsewhere

subject: Outdoor Ceiling
rule: outdoor ceiling must not trap moisture between its layers
conditions: constructed with multiple layers (e.g., soffit, insulation, decking)
exceptions: assembly is designed as a ventilated rainscreen with drainage cavities

subject: Outdoor Ceiling
rule: outdoor ceiling must resist wind uplift forces
conditions: located in region with design wind speed exceeding 110 mph per ASCE 7

subject: Weatherproof Electrical Outlet
rule: Weatherproof electrical outlet must have a weather-resistant cover (e.g., spring-loaded lid, gasket, or gasketed flap) that remains closed when not in use
conditions: outlet is installed in a location exposed to rain, snow, or moisture
exceptions: outlet is installed in a fully enclosed, conditioned indoor space with no moisture exposure

subject: Weatherproof Electrical Outlet
rule: Weatherproof electrical outlet must be rated for the voltage and current of the connected circuit

subject: Weatherproof Electrical Outlet
rule: Weatherproof electrical outlet must not have exposed live conductors when the cover is closed or when the plug is partially inserted

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixture
rule: outdoor lighting fixture must have a minimum IP (Ingress Protection) rating of IP65 for exterior exposure
conditions: fixture is installed in an uncovered outdoor location exposed to rain and dust
exceptions: fixture is installed in a fully sheltered/covered outdoor location not exposed to direct rain

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixture
rule: outdoor lighting fixture must have a grounded metallic enclosure or be double-insulated (Class II)
conditions: fixture is connected to mains voltage (120V–277V AC)
exceptions: fixture is low-voltage (e.g., 12V/24V) with a listed Class 2 power supply

subject: Outdoor Lighting Fixture
rule: outdoor lighting fixture must not have exposed energized terminals or bare conductors accessible without tools
exceptions: terminals are within a weatherproof junction box with a rated cover

subject: Exterior Ceiling Fan
rule: exterior ceiling fan must be listed/rated for outdoor/damp/wet location use

subject: Exterior Ceiling Fan
rule: exterior ceiling fan must be securely mounted to a structural ceiling or support capable of withstanding dynamic and static loads

subject: Exterior Ceiling Fan
rule: exterior ceiling fan must not be installed where the blade path is within 1.5 m (5 ft) of any obstruction or occupant reach zone
conditions: when blades are exposed and rotating

subject: Exterior Ceiling Fan
rule: exterior ceiling fan must have a minimum 1.5 m (5 ft) clearance from grade/floor to blade bottom
conditions: when fan is accessible to pedestrians

subject: Outdoor Heater Mount
rule: Outdoor Heater Mount must be securely attached to a structural surface capable of supporting the heater's weight and wind loads
conditions: mounted on wall
mounted on roof
mounted on ground

subject: Outdoor Heater Mount
rule: Outdoor Heater Mount must not be positioned where it interferes with overhead obstructions or combustibles
conditions: mounted under eaves
mounted near combustible materials

subject: Outdoor Heater Mount
rule: Outdoor Heater Mount must provide electrical bonding/grounding continuity if the heater requires electrical connection
conditions: heater has electrical components
exceptions: heater is fully self-contained battery-powered with no line-voltage connection

subject: Exterior Drainage Channel
rule: Exterior drainage channel must have a continuous slope toward the discharge point
conditions: channel is intended to convey water by gravity flow
exceptions: channel is designed as a level-gutter system with built-in sump and pump

subject: Exterior Drainage Channel
rule: Exterior drainage channel must not have a cross-sectional area smaller than the design flow requires
conditions: channel is sized to handle a specific rainfall event or runoff volume
exceptions: upstream flow-control devices intentionally restrict inflow below design capacity

subject: Exterior Drainage Channel
rule: Exterior drainage channel must be free of obstructions that block the full flow path
conditions: channel is in operation
exceptions: temporary blockage during maintenance is allowed if flow is safely diverted or the channel is deactivated

subject: Exterior Drainage Channel
rule: Exterior drainage channel must discharge to a legally compliant outfall location
conditions: channel is connected to a municipal stormwater system or natural watercourse
exceptions: channel terminates at an on-site retention/detention facility designed for zero off-site discharge

subject: Privacy Screen
rule: privacy screen must not block required emergency egress windows or doors
conditions: if privacy screen is attached to a building containing occupiable spaces
exceptions: if local building code explicitly permits screens over egress openings with quick-release mechanisms

subject: Privacy Screen
rule: privacy screen structural attachments must be capable of resisting design wind loads
conditions: if privacy screen is installed outdoors or on a building exterior

subject: Privacy Screen
rule: privacy screen must not create a fire spread hazard by being constructed of combustible materials where fire-rated construction is required
conditions: if privacy screen is located within the fire-resistance-rated exterior wall assembly or within the required fire separation distance of a property line
exceptions: if the screen material is fire-retardant-treated and code-compliant for that location

subject: Outdoor Shade Louver
rule: outdoor shade louver must be angled to shed water and prevent pooling
conditions: installed in a location exposed to rain
exceptions: louver is purely decorative and fully sealed against moisture ingress

subject: Outdoor Shade Louver
rule: outdoor shade louver must be structurally self-supporting or secured to an adequate structure

subject: Outdoor Shade Louver
rule: outdoor shade louver must not block required egress or emergency access paths
conditions: installed near doors, windows, or escape routes
exceptions: louver is designed to break away or retract under emergency force per code

subject: Outdoor Shade Louver
rule: outdoor shade louver must have gaps or openings sized to prevent accumulation of debris that causes ponding or blockage
conditions: louver is installed horizontally or near grade
exceptions: louver is regularly maintained and cleaned per schedule

subject: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount
rule: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount must be attached to a structurally adequate support (wall, post, or structure) capable of resisting the combined dead and wind loads
conditions: All installations

subject: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount
rule: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount must not be installed where the sail cannot achieve the minimum required tension (sag angle) for drainage
conditions: Any shade sail installation intended to shed water or prevent ponding
exceptions: Decorative-only sails not expected to shed water

subject: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount
rule: Outdoor Shade Sail Mount must have corrosion protection suitable for its exposure environment (e.g., stainless steel, galvanized, or powder-coated steel)
conditions: Installation in outdoor, uncovered location exposed to weather
exceptions: Temporary/seasonal installations that are removed during wet seasons

subject: Outdoor Planter Wall
rule: Outdoor planter wall must have a drainage path at its base to prevent water accumulation
conditions: wall retains soil on one or both sides
wall is exposed to rainfall or irrigation overspray
exceptions: wall is purely decorative and does not retain any soil volume
wall is designed with fully permeable construction (e.g., spaced blocks) that drains freely through the assembly

subject: Outdoor Planter Wall
rule: Outdoor planter wall must be structurally stable under saturated soil loading
conditions: wall retains soil that can become waterlogged
exceptions: wall height is less than 300 mm and soil volume is negligible

subject: Outdoor Planter Wall
rule: Outdoor planter wall must not have a continuous impervious barrier that traps water against adjacent building wall surfaces
conditions: planter wall is installed directly against a building exterior wall
exceptions: a properly detailed waterproofing and drainage plane exists between planter wall and building wall

subject: Outdoor Fireplace
rule: outdoor fireplace must have non-combustible materials in all heat-affected surfaces
conditions: gas or wood-burning outdoor fireplace

subject: Outdoor Fireplace
rule: outdoor fireplace chimney or flue must terminate above the highest point of any adjacent combustible structure within a specified horizontal distance
conditions: outdoor fireplace is attached to or within 10 feet of a combustible structure (e.g., a wood deck, house eaves)

subject: Outdoor Fireplace
rule: outdoor fireplace must not be placed directly on a combustible deck without an approved non-combustible fire-rated base or ember shield
conditions: outdoor fireplace is wood-burning or uses solid fuel
exceptions: prefabricated listed units whose listing explicitly permits direct deck placement with no additional protection

subject: Outdoor Fire Pit
rule: outdoor fire pit must be surrounded by non-combustible material on all sides within a minimum horizontal clearance distance
conditions: fire pit is installed on a deck or combustible surface
exceptions: fire pit is a portable unit placed on concrete, stone, or bare ground without surrounding combustibles

subject: Outdoor Fire Pit
rule: outdoor fire pit must have a spark arrestor or screen cover when in use
conditions: fire pit burns solid fuel (wood or charcoal)
exceptions: fire pit is a gas-fired model with no exposed flame above the burner level

subject: Outdoor Fire Pit
rule: outdoor fire pit must be located at a minimum distance from any building structure or property line

subject: Outdoor Fire Pit
rule: outdoor fire pit must not be placed directly under any overhanging tree branches, eaves, or combustible overhead elements

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Counter
rule: outdoor kitchen counter must be made of weather-resistant materials
conditions: counter is permanently installed outdoors

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Counter
rule: outdoor kitchen counter must have a minimum slope for water runoff
conditions: counter surface is solid and exposed directly to rain

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Counter
rule: outdoor kitchen counter must be structurally stable under its own weight and typical live loads

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Counter
rule: outdoor kitchen counter must not have unprotected electrical outlets or fixtures exposed to weather
conditions: counter includes electrical receptacles or integrated lighting

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Counter
rule: outdoor kitchen counter must not have combustible materials in direct contact with a heat source or open flame
conditions: counter is adjacent to or integrated with a grill, cooktop, or fire feature

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Sink
rule: Outdoor kitchen sink must be connected to a potable water supply and wastewater drainage system
conditions: permanently installed
exceptions: temporary or mobile outdoor kitchen setups that use self-contained water tanks and capture wastewater

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Sink
rule: Outdoor kitchen sink must have freeze protection for water supply lines
conditions: installed in a climate where ambient temperatures drop below freezing (0°C / 32°F)
exceptions: sink is drained and winterized before each freeze event
sink uses a self-draining valve system that fully empties exposed pipes

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Sink
rule: Outdoor kitchen sink must not be installed where electrical wiring or fixtures create an electrocution hazard in wet conditions
conditions: sink area includes or is adjacent to electrical outlets, switches, or appliances
exceptions: all electrical components are GFCI-protected, weatherproof, and installed per code at safe distances

subject: Outdoor Shower
rule: Outdoor shower must have a floor or ground surface that slopes away from the building to prevent water pooling near the foundation
conditions: When the outdoor shower is attached to or adjacent to a building
exceptions: When the outdoor shower has a fully sealed drain system connected to municipal sewer or septic

subject: Outdoor Shower
rule: Outdoor shower must not have electrical fixtures or outlets within reach of the water spray zone
conditions: When the outdoor shower includes any electrical components such as lighting, controls, or outlets
exceptions: When electrical fixtures are rated for wet locations and installed with GFCI protection at a safe distance per electrical code

subject: Outdoor Shower
rule: Outdoor shower floor or standing surface must be slip-resistant

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Island
rule: outdoor kitchen island must have a non-combustible countertop surface
conditions: is used for cooking with live fire or high-heat appliances (e.g., grill, pizza oven)
exceptions: is used exclusively as a prep/serving station with no heat source

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Island
rule: outdoor kitchen island must not have an enclosed, roofed gas grill alcove without a minimum 6-inch clearance on all sides for ventilation
conditions: contains a built-in gas grill
grill is installed in an alcove with a roof or overhead obstruction
exceptions: grill is fully open on at least three sides with no roof above it

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Island
rule: outdoor kitchen island must have a drain or drainage path for the sink compartment
conditions: includes a sink

subject: Outdoor Kitchen Island
rule: outdoor kitchen island base and cabinetry must not be constructed of untreated particleboard or MDF exposed to weather
conditions: is permanently installed outdoors without a weatherproof enclosure
exceptions: cabinetry is rated marine-grade or specifically manufactured for outdoor exposure

subject: Retractable Awning
rule: retractable awning retraction mechanism must fully retract fabric into protective housing
conditions: awning is retractable type
awning has fabric canopy

subject: Retractable Awning
rule: retractable awning must not have pinch points or shear hazards accessible to users during normal operation
conditions: awning is manually operated or within reach of users
exceptions: commercial/industrial awnings with locked-out maintenance-only access

subject: Exterior Water Feature Basin
rule: exterior water feature basin must contain a waterproof lining or sealed basin structure
conditions: basin is intended to hold standing water

subject: Exterior Water Feature Basin
rule: exterior water feature basin must have a drainage outlet or overflow mechanism
conditions: basin is exposed to rainfall
basin is filled via recirculating pump system
exceptions: basin is a temporary/seasonal decorative feature that is manually drained and stored

subject: Exterior Water Feature Basin
rule: exterior water feature basin must not exceed the load-bearing capacity of its supporting substrate
conditions: basin is installed above grade on a deck, balcony, or roof structure

subject: Outdoor Floor Heating System
rule: Outdoor floor heating system must have freeze protection (antifreeze or self-regulating cable) when installed in climates where ambient temperature can drop below 0°C
conditions: System installed in climate where ambient temperature can drop below 0°C
exceptions: System is drained and decommissioned before freezing season

subject: Outdoor Floor Heating System
rule: Outdoor floor heating system must have ground moisture / water ingress protection (waterproof insulation and sealed connections)

subject: Outdoor Floor Heating System
rule: Outdoor floor heating system must not be operated without a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection
conditions: System is electric-resistance type
exceptions: Hydronic (fluid-based) systems with no electrical heating elements in the ground loop

subject: Outdoor Floor Heating System
rule: Maximum surface temperature of outdoor heated floor must not exceed 29°C (84°F) for public pedestrian areas with bare feet
conditions: Surface is accessible to barefoot pedestrians
exceptions: Area designated for footwear only and clearly marked

subject: Window Head/Lintel
rule: window head/lintel must transfer vertical loads above the opening to adjacent wall elements
conditions: when supporting masonry or other non-self-supporting wall material above
exceptions: in structures where a primary structural frame (e.g., steel or concrete) carries all vertical loads and the wall is only infill

subject: Window Head/Lintel
rule: window head/lintel must have a minimum bearing length at each end on the supporting wall or jamb
conditions: when the lintel is a discrete element resting on jambs or wall sections on both sides of the opening
exceptions: when the head is cast monolithically with a continuous concrete or steel frame

subject: Window Head/Lintel
rule: window head/lintel must be weather-sealed at its interface with the window frame and adjacent wall
conditions: when the assembly is part of the building envelope exposed to exterior conditions
exceptions: for interior non-rated openings with no weather exposure

subject: Window Head/Lintel
rule: window head/lintel must not reduce the structural capacity of the wall below minimum code-required values
conditions: when the lintel forms part of a loadbearing wall
exceptions: when all loads above are carried by an independent structural frame

subject: Window Gasket/Glazing Bead
rule: window gasket or glazing bead must create a continuous, unbroken seal around the entire perimeter of the glass or infill panel
conditions: used as a primary weather seal
exceptions: drainable glazing systems where intentional gaps are part of a controlled weep path

subject: Window Gasket/Glazing Bead
rule: window gasket or glazing bead must accommodate differential thermal movement between the frame and the glass without losing compression or seal integrity
conditions: exposed to diurnal or seasonal temperature cycles exceeding 20°C range

subject: Window Gasket/Glazing Bead
rule: window gasket or glazing bead must not be rigidly bonded to both the frame and the glass in a way that prevents independent movement
conditions: used in a framed assembly with dissimilar materials (e.g., aluminum frame with glass)
exceptions: structural glazing applications where the bond is designed as part of the structural load path

subject: Window Mullion
rule: Window mullion must have a minimum thickness to resist wind load and support glazing without deflection that breaks the glass seal
conditions: mullion is load-bearing
mullion supports operable or fixed glazing
exceptions: non-structural decorative mullion applied to the interior face of monolithic glazing

subject: Window Mullion
rule: Window mullion must not create a thermal bridge that causes condensation inside the wall assembly
conditions: mullion is part of a thermally insulated wall assembly in a climate where interior dew point can be reached
exceptions: mullion is fully enclosed within the conditioned space with no thermal gradient across it

subject: Window Mullion
rule: Window mullion must be structurally continuous from head to sill or properly spliced to transfer vertical load
conditions: mullion is vertical and supports stacked glazing panels above and below
exceptions: mullion is non-structural and attached only to a structurally independent curtain wall frame

subject: Window Transom
rule: window transom must be installed above the operable window sash or door leaf, not below it
conditions: when used in a window or door assembly

subject: Window Transom
rule: window transom must be separated from the sill or floor by a minimum height that accommodates the intended operation of the door or window below
conditions: when installed in an inhabited space where a door or operable window is placed beneath

subject: Window Transom
rule: window transom must not block required emergency egress opening dimensions when installed above an operable window
conditions: when the assembly serves as an emergency escape and rescue opening

subject: Window Transom
rule: window transom must be structurally supported at jambs or frame, not cantilevered unsupported across the span
conditions: when span exceeds the material's unsupported capacity

subject: Window Shading Device (Built-in)
rule: Built-in window shading device must not obstruct emergency egress from the window
conditions: window is used as an emergency egress opening
applicable building code requires egress
exceptions: shading device is automatically retractable upon activation of building fire alarm or manual release

subject: Window Shading Device (Built-in)
rule: Built-in window shading device must not prevent the window from fully closing and locking
exceptions: shading device is mounted independently of the window sash and does not interfere with its travel path

subject: Window Shading Device (Built-in)
rule: Built-in window shading device must allow for operation of the window opening hardware (handle, crank, lock)
conditions: window is operable (not fixed/stationary)

subject: Window Operation Mechanism
rule: window operation mechanism must allow manual override for emergency egress or rescue
conditions: applies to windows serving as required emergency egress or rescue openings per building code
exceptions: windows not designated as egress openings

subject: Window Operation Mechanism
rule: window operation mechanism must not allow unintentional opening (fall prevention)
conditions: applies to windows above ground floor or where fall risk exists
exceptions: windows designed with permanently fixed operation (non-operable)

subject: Window Operation Mechanism
rule: window operation mechanism must permit full closure and sealing against weather penetration

subject: Storefront
rule: Storefront must include a clear entrance opening (door or openable assembly) that provides means of egress
conditions: building is occupied by people
storefront serves as a primary means of entry/exit
exceptions: storefront is purely decorative and not an accessible entry point
separate dedicated entrance exists adjacent to the storefront

subject: Storefront
rule: Storefront must be structurally supported at the head (top) by a lintel or structural beam spanning the opening
conditions: storefront opening exceeds 4 feet in width
exceptions: storefront uses a structural glass fin system designed to carry vertical loads without a traditional lintel

subject: Storefront
rule: Storefront glazing must be tempered or laminated safety glass where the bottom edge is less than 18 inches above the floor
conditions: storefront contains glass panels
glass panel bottom edge is below 18 inches from finished floor
exceptions: glass is protected by a permanent guardrail system

subject: Storefront
rule: Storefront must not obstruct required means of egress width when in any open or closed position
conditions: storefront is located along a required means of egress path

subject: Entry Canopy
rule: entry canopy must have a minimum slope to shed water
conditions: canopy is exposed to rainfall
canopy has a solid roof surface
exceptions: canopy is constructed with fully permeable materials throughout
canopy is designed as a rain-screen with no solid deck

subject: Entry Canopy
rule: entry canopy must not block required egress clearance
conditions: canopy is located over a means of egress
canopy is located within egress path width

subject: Entry Canopy
rule: entry canopy must not collect debris or water in a manner that creates a falling hazard to occupants below
conditions: canopy is located above an occupied pedestrian area

subject: Entry Canopy
rule: entry canopy must be structurally stable under self-weight and design live loads

subject: Street-Facing Window Wall
rule: Street-facing window wall must have a minimum fire-resistance rating as required by local building code for exposed exterior walls
conditions: Located on a building with more than one story
Required by applicable building code
exceptions: Building is fully sprinklered and code allows reduced rating

subject: Street-Facing Window Wall
rule: Street-facing window wall must not have unprotected openings within the required fire-resistance zone unless rated assemblies are used
conditions: Fire-resistance rating is required for the wall assembly
exceptions: Fire-rated glazing assemblies are used that meet the required rating

subject: Display Window
rule: display window must have a clear glazed area for product visibility
conditions: retail/commercial function
