exceptions: window display with open front (no glazing) where security is not required

subject: Display Window
rule: display window must be recessed or protected from direct solar gain where sun exposure is significant
conditions: facade orientation receives direct sunlight for more than 4 hours daily

subject: Display Window
rule: display window must not have structural loads transferred through glass panels

subject: Display Window
rule: display window sill height must not exceed 1200 mm from finished floor level
conditions: street-facing retail display
exceptions: display window located on upper floors or non-pedestrian frontage

subject: Entry Threshold
rule: entry threshold must have a height difference of at least 15 mm (or comply with local accessibility code) to prevent water ingress into the interior
conditions: when threshold is installed at an exterior doorway exposed to rain
exceptions: when building has a covered entrance that fully shelters the threshold from precipitation
when a properly designed drainage channel is provided immediately outside the threshold

subject: Entry Threshold
rule: entry threshold must not create a trip hazard exceeding permitted step height
conditions: when threshold serves a doorway intended for general occupant/visitor access
exceptions: when threshold is part of a designated accessible route and conforms to local accessibility standards for sloped transitions

subject: Entry Threshold
rule: entry threshold must provide a continuous weather seal when the door is closed
conditions: when threshold is installed at an exterior doorway
exceptions: when the doorway is purely interior (not an exterior entry)

subject: Access Ramp
rule: access ramp slope must not exceed 1:12 (8.33%)
conditions: public use
ADA/non-discriminatory access context
exceptions: Existing sites with documented impracticality may allow up to 1:10 slope for short distances under some codes

subject: Access Ramp
rule: access ramp must have a clear width of at least 36 inches (915 mm) between handrails
conditions: public use
wheelchair accessible path

subject: Access Ramp
rule: access ramp must have landings at top and bottom
conditions: any ramp exceeding 6 inches in rise

subject: Access Ramp
rule: access ramp must have handrails on both sides when rise exceeds 6 inches
conditions: rise > 6 inches

subject: Access Ramp
rule: access ramp surface must be slip-resistant

subject: Fixed Street Canopy
rule: Fixed street canopy must have a minimum downward slope (at least 1:50) for drainage
conditions: The canopy is a solid roof type (not louvered or permeable)
The canopy is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: Canopy is designed with integrated gutter and downspout system that collects and channels water without requiring slope

subject: Fixed Street Canopy
rule: Fixed street canopy must be structurally capable of supporting its own weight plus imposed loads (snow, wind, maintenance)

subject: Fixed Street Canopy
rule: Fixed street canopy must not obstruct emergency vehicle access or fire egress routes below it
conditions: Canopy projects over a public right-of-way or designated access route
exceptions: Local authority grants a specific variance with alternate emergency access provisions

subject: Fixed Street Canopy
rule: Fixed street canopy must have a minimum clearance height above pedestrian walkway (typically 2.4 m / 8 ft)
conditions: Canopy is located above a pedestrian accessible area

subject: Door Closer & Panic Hardware
rule: door closer must be installed on the interior side of the door
conditions: door closer is surface-mounted
door is inward-swinging
exceptions: fire-rated doors where local codes require closer on exterior side for egress

subject: Door Closer & Panic Hardware
rule: panic hardware must not require more than 15 lbf (67 N) force to actuate the push pad or crossbar
conditions: door is on an egress path
occupant load exceeds 50

subject: Door Closer & Panic Hardware
rule: door closer must return the door to the fully closed and latched position from any open position
conditions: door is self-closing per code requirement
door serves a fire-rated opening
exceptions: hold-open devices connected to fire alarm system where permitted

subject: Door Closer & Panic Hardware
rule: panic hardware must be operable with a single pushing or pulling motion on the crossbar or push pad
conditions: hardware is mortise-type panic device

subject: Door Closer & Panic Hardware
rule: door closer must not generate more than 30 lbf (133 N) closing force at the door edge
conditions: door is on an accessible route

subject: Entry Mat/Grid System
rule: Entry mat/grid system must be recessed flush with, or slightly below, the finished floor surface to create a safe walking surface and prevent trip hazards
conditions: Where installed in a walking path or entryway
exceptions: Temporary or portable mats that are clearly visible and marked as temporary, used in construction or event contexts where flush installation is not feasible

subject: Entry Mat/Grid System
rule: Entry mat/grid system must not trap or pool water on its surface such that standing water remains after normal drainage
conditions: Where installed in exterior entries or covered entries exposed to moisture
exceptions: Mat systems explicitly designed and rated for water retention (e.g., absorbent entry mats) where drainage is not expected

subject: Entry Mat/Grid System
rule: Entry mat/grid system must be securely anchored or restrained to prevent lateral movement/displacement under foot traffic
conditions: Where installed as a permanent or semi-permanent fixture in a public or high-traffic entry
exceptions: Lightweight loose-lay mats used in low-traffic residential interiors where intentional removal for cleaning is frequent and displacement risk is minimal

subject: Street-Facing Entrance Door
rule: door leaf must swing in the direction of egress (outward) when serving an occupancy of more than 50 people or a high-hazard occupancy
conditions: occupancy > 50 people
high-hazard occupancy
exceptions: door serves a dwelling unit with occupancy ≤ 50 and is not high-hazard

subject: Street-Facing Entrance Door
rule: street-facing entrance door must have a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm)
conditions: required means of egress door
exceptions: existing buildings undergoing limited alteration where strict compliance is infeasible and alternative is accepted by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Street-Facing Entrance Door
rule: door threshold must not exceed 1/2 inch (13 mm) in height at a street-facing entrance
conditions: required accessible entrance
exceptions: existing thresholds up to 3/4 inch with beveled edges are permitted if alteration is limited

subject: Street-Facing Entrance Door
rule: bottom of door undercuts or gaps must not exceed 3/4 inch (19 mm) at a street-facing entrance exposed to weather
conditions: door exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: doors with covered canopies providing full weather protection

subject: Street-Facing Entrance Door
rule: street-facing entrance door must be side-hinged or pivoted when serving as a required means of egress
conditions: door is part of required means of egress
exceptions: sliding doors or revolving doors are permitted when they are not the sole means of egress
doors in dwelling units with direct exit

subject: Gallery Surround Balustrade
rule: gallery surround balustrade must have a handrail that can be grasped continuously along the entire walking surface
conditions: when the balustrade is adjacent to a walking surface
when the gallery surround is accessible to occupants

subject: Gallery Surround Balustrade
rule: gallery surround balustrade must resist a minimum horizontal live load of 50 pounds per linear foot applied at the top rail
conditions: when the balustrade functions as a guardrail with a fall height greater than 30 inches

subject: Gallery Surround Balustrade
rule: gallery surround balustrade must not have openings that permit passage of a 4-inch diameter sphere
conditions: when the balustrade serves as a guardrail

subject: Gallery Surround Balustrade
rule: balustrade top rail height must be at least 42 inches above the walking surface
conditions: when the balustrade serves as a guardrail adjacent to a drop-off
when the gallery surround is in a commercial or multi-family building
exceptions: residential occupancies may require 36 inches minimum instead of 42

subject: Gallery Surround Structural Beam
rule: gallery surround structural beam must be capable of supporting its own self-weight plus any superimposed dead and live loads without exceeding allowable stress limits

subject: Gallery Surround Structural Beam
rule: gallery surround structural beam must not have a bending moment or shear force that exceeds its moment or shear capacity at any section

subject: Gallery Surround Structural Beam
rule: gallery surround structural beam must have adequate deflection control such that maximum deflection under service loads does not exceed span/240 (or other code-specified limit)

subject: Gallery Surround Structural Beam
rule: gallery surround structural beam must be laterally braced at intervals not exceeding the maximum unbraced length to prevent lateral-torsional buckling
conditions: for steel or other slender beams where the beam is not continuously laterally restrained
exceptions: if the beam has a section that is compact and the unbraced length is within code limits such that LTB does not govern

subject: Balcony Slab
rule: balcony slab must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: slab is exposed to weather
slab is not covered by an additional waterproofed layer
exceptions: slab is designed as a plant-on waterproofed finish with integrated drainage membrane

subject: Balcony Slab
rule: balcony slab must have adequate structural capacity for its design live load

subject: Balcony Slab
rule: balcony slab must have a continuous waterproof membrane or be constructed of waterproof material
conditions: slab is exposed to exterior weather conditions
exceptions: slab is entirely indoors or fully protected from precipitation

subject: Balcony Slab
rule: balcony slab must not have a parapet height below minimum code-specified guard height
conditions: balcony is at an elevation above grade where guardrails are required by building code
exceptions: balcony is at grade level with no fall hazard

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly must have a minimum height of 1060 mm (42 inches) above the finished floor for multi-story residential buildings
conditions: building is multi-story residential
balcony is accessible
exceptions: single-family dwellings with no rental units
guarded areas where the drop is less than 600 mm

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly must prevent passage of a 100 mm (4 inch) sphere through any opening in the infill
conditions: guardrail is required for fall protection
infill has openings
exceptions: triangular openings at the tread/riser of stairs where a 150 mm sphere is used instead

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly must not have any horizontal or near-horizontal elements that could act as a climbing ladder within the guarded area
conditions: guardrail is on an accessible balcony
children under 6 years old have access
exceptions: railings where the horizontal members are not within 150 mm of each other
interior side of handrails on stairs

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly must withstand a minimum uniformly distributed live load of 0.74 kN/m (50 lb/ft) applied at the top rail
conditions: guardrail is located on a balcony
exceptions: handrails attached to walls (not part of guardrail system)
industrial/warehouse applications with different load standards

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly top rail must have a graspable profile (hand-sized cross-section, typically 32-50 mm diameter equivalent)
conditions: top rail also serves as a handrail
exceptions: handrail is provided separately on the wall
barrier top is used as a shelf or planter surface and a separate handrail exists

subject: Balcony Guardrail/Handrail Assembly
rule: balcony guardrail/handrail assembly must be at least 900 mm (36 inches) in height above the finished floor for all other occupancies
conditions: building is not multi-story residential
building occupancy is commercial, industrial, or assembly
drop height exceeds 600 mm
exceptions: raised platforms for performance stages
loading docks with vehicle barriers

subject: Balcony Balusters
rule: Balcony balusters must have vertical spacing between elements no greater than 100 mm (4 inches)
conditions: guard is intended to prevent children from passing through
guard is required by building code for life-safety fall protection
exceptions: decorative non-guard elements not serving as fall protection

subject: Balcony Balusters
rule: Balcony balusters must resist a concentrated horizontal load of at least 0.5 kN (≈ 50 kg force) applied at any point
conditions: balusters form part of a guard system protecting a walking surface elevated more than 300 mm above adjacent grade
exceptions: balusters that are purely ornamental and structurally independent from the guard system

subject: Balcony Deck Drainage
rule: balcony deck drainage must have a minimum slope of 1:50 (2%) toward drainage outlets
conditions: balcony deck is exposed to rain or other precipitation
exceptions: deck uses a fully integrated linear drain system designed for zero-slope application

subject: Balcony Deck Drainage
rule: balcony deck drainage system must not discharge onto lower balconies, walkways, or public areas
conditions: drainage system has any outflow

subject: Balcony Deck Drainage
rule: balcony deck drainage must prevent backflow of water into the building interior
conditions: drainage system connects to building drainage network

subject: Balcony Deck Drainage
rule: balcony deck drainage outlets must be protected by debris screens or strainers
conditions: drainage system has open outlets
exceptions: outlets are designed as self-cleaning siphonic drains

subject: Balcony Deck Drainage
rule: balcony deck surface must not be sloped toward the building wall
conditions: balcony deck is adjacent to a building wall
exceptions: a waterproof cove base and continuous membrane at the wall junction is designed to handle water at the interface

subject: Balcony Door Assembly
rule: balcony door assembly must have a weatherstripped seal between the door frame and the door leaf
conditions: when the assembly is installed in an exterior wall
exceptions: none

subject: Balcony Door Assembly
rule: balcony door assembly must have a functioning locking mechanism that engages the door leaf to the frame
conditions: when the assembly is required to be operable and securable
exceptions: fixed (non-operable) door assemblies

subject: Balcony Door Assembly
rule: balcony door assembly must not have a door sill height that creates a tripping hazard exceeding code-prescribed limits at the balcony threshold
conditions: when the door opens to an occupied balcony deck
exceptions: accessible/barrier-free designs with tapered transition permitted by code

subject: Balcony Door Assembly
rule: balcony door assembly must have a tempered or laminated glazing panel if the glass area is within the hazardous location zone as defined by building code
conditions: when the door contains glazing
when the glazing is within 60 inches of the floor or within 24 inches of a door opening
exceptions: glass block assemblies
fire-rated glazing with alternative tested assembly

subject: Balcony Soffit
rule: Balcony soffit must be ventilated to prevent moisture accumulation and rot in the concealed deck structure above
conditions: when balcony is enclosed or has a solid waterproof membrane above
when the balcony soffit is not exposed to open air on all sides
exceptions: when the balcony deck above is designed with a cold-roof ventilated cavity that makes soffit ventilation redundant
when the entire assembly is designed as a hot-roof (unventilated) system with approved moisture control analysis

subject: Balcony Soffit
rule: Balcony soffit must have a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the building's fire-resistance-rated floor/ceiling assembly when the balcony is part of the means of egress or the soffit provides fire separation
conditions: when the balcony serves as an exit passageway or egress component
when the soffit assembly forms part of a fire separation between dwelling units or between a dwelling unit and a common area
exceptions: when local building code exempts exterior balconies from fire-rating requirements
when the building is of Type V (combustible) construction and the soffit is protected by an automatic sprinkler system per code exception

subject: Balcony Soffit
rule: Balcony soffit must not trap water or allow capillary water entry at joints between soffit panels and at the soffit-to-wall interface
conditions: when the soffit is constructed from multiple panels or boards
when the soffit abuts a vertical wall surface
exceptions: when all joints are fully sealed with a waterproof, flexible sealant and a secondary drainage plane is provided behind the soffit

subject: Balcony Structure Anchorage
rule: Balcony structure anchorage must resist both lateral and vertical loads as specified by design codes
conditions: When balcony is cantilevered from the main structure

subject: Balcony Structure Anchorage
rule: Balcony structure anchorage must not rely solely on masonry or unreinforced infill walls for structural support
conditions: When balcony is load-bearing and attached to a masonry wall

subject: Balcony Structure Anchorage
rule: Balcony structure anchorage connections must be designed for corrosion resistance appropriate to the exposure environment
conditions: When balcony is exposed to exterior weather conditions

subject: Balcony Structure Anchorage
rule: Balcony structure anchorage must not be embedded in a manner that creates a thermal bridge causing condensation within the building envelope
conditions: When anchorage penetrates the building thermal envelope

subject: Earth Continuity Conductor
rule: Earth Continuity Conductor must be electrically continuous along its entire length
conditions: When installed as part of electrical earthing system

subject: Earth Continuity Conductor
rule: Earth Continuity Conductor must not have any disconnecting links or switches inserted in it
conditions: When used as a protective bonding conductor
exceptions: When specifically designed test links are installed for testing purposes, provided they maintain continuity when closed

subject: Earth Continuity Conductor
rule: Earth Continuity Conductor must have a cross-sectional area not less than required by the connected circuit protective conductor
conditions: When connecting electrical equipment to the earthing system

subject: Earthing Electrode
rule: earthing electrode must be in direct contact with soil or electrolyte
conditions: when used as a ground electrode
exceptions: electrodes embedded in concrete (Ufer ground) where concrete provides ionic coupling

subject: Earthing Electrode
rule: earthing electrode must be made of corrosion-resistant material or have corrosion protection
exceptions: sacrificial electrodes intended to corrode (e.g., galvanic anodes) where controlled corrosion is the design purpose

subject: Earthing Electrode
rule: earthing electrode must not be painted or coated with non-conductive material at the soil-contact surface
exceptions: electrodes encased in conductive concrete or specified conductive backfill

subject: Earthing Electrode
rule: earthing electrode must have a cross-sectional area sufficient to carry the maximum fault current without fusing
conditions: when the electrode is part of a fault-current return path

subject: Earth Termination Bar
rule: An Earth Termination Bar must be bonded to the grounding electrode system via a properly rated conductor
conditions: When used as part of a lightning protection system per NFPA 780 or UL 96A

subject: Earth Termination Bar
rule: An Earth Termination Bar must not be installed where it can be submerged or subject to standing water unless specifically rated for wet locations
conditions: When installed outdoors or below grade
exceptions: If the bar and all connections are specifically listed and rated for continuous submersion (e.g., direct-burial rated) and the installation complies with applicable codes

subject: Earth Termination Bar
rule: An Earth Termination Bar must be electrically continuous with all connected lightning protection down conductors

subject: Earth Pit / Inspection Pit
rule: Earth pit / inspection pit must have an openable cover (lid) that provides safe access for inspection and maintenance
conditions: pit is installed below finished ground level
pit is intended for periodic inspection or maintenance access

subject: Earth Pit / Inspection Pit
rule: Earth pit / inspection pit must have structural integrity to withstand expected surface loads (e.g., pedestrian, vehicular) without collapsing
conditions: pit is installed in a trafficked or load-bearing area
exceptions: pit is located in a non-trafficked area with no anticipated surface load

subject: Earth Pit / Inspection Pit
rule: Earth pit / inspection pit must not allow ingress of groundwater or surface water that would submerge the internal services
conditions: pit houses electrical connections, cable joints, or equipment sensitive to water
exceptions: pit is designed as a watertight/sealed unit or includes a sump pump system that actively removes water

subject: Earth Pit / Inspection Pit
rule: Earth pit / inspection pit must have a minimum internal dimension sufficient for a person (or tool) to perform the required inspection/maintenance task
conditions: pit is classified as a man-entry pit requiring personnel access
exceptions: pit is a small hand-access pit (e.g., telecom finger pit) where only tool/manual arm access is needed

subject: Foundation Earth Electrode
rule: Foundation earth electrode must be in direct and permanent contact with soil (or a permanent conductive medium embedded in soil)
conditions: applicable to all permanent building or structure earthing systems
exceptions: rock sites where equivalent grounding performance is achieved via deep-driven rods or chemical treatment with engineering verification

subject: Foundation Earth Electrode
rule: Foundation earth electrode must be a continuous conductor (welded or approved clamp) with no interruptions along its loop
conditions: when configured as a ring or loop electrode within or under the foundation
exceptions: bonding points intentionally left accessible for testing are not considered interruptions if conductivity is restorable via a test link

subject: Foundation Earth Electrode
rule: Foundation earth electrode must not be coated with paint, enamel, or other insulating material on its burial surfaces
conditions: applies to all embedded metalwork serving as the electrode
exceptions: factory-applied corrosion protection that remains sufficiently conductive (e.g. galvanizing, bituminous coating with conductive filler) is acceptable if proven by test

subject: Foundation Earth Electrode
rule: Foundation earth electrode must be buried at a depth that remains below the local frost line or otherwise protected against frost heave displacement
conditions: in climates where seasonal ground freezing occurs
exceptions: locations where the soil type and building thermal load prevent freezing at electrode depth

subject: Lightning Protection Down Conductor
rule: Lightning protection down conductor must be electrically continuous from roof to ground
conditions: building has lightning protection system
down conductor is installed
exceptions: conductors with engineered spark gaps or isolated sections for testing purposes

subject: Lightning Protection Down Conductor
rule: Lightning protection down conductor must have a cross-sectional area and material type meeting the applicable standard (e.g., NFPA 780, IEC 62305 minimum 50 mm² copper or equivalent)
conditions: down conductor is part of a lightning protection system

subject: Lightning Protection Down Conductor
rule: Lightning protection down conductor must not be installed in direct contact with combustible materials along its entire length
conditions: down conductor is routed through or adjacent to building fabric containing combustible materials
exceptions: conductors encased in non-combustible conduit or thermal barrier rated for lightning current

subject: Lightning Protection Down Conductor
rule: Lightning protection down conductor must be bonded to the building's grounding electrode system
conditions: down conductor terminates at ground level
building has a grounding electrode system
exceptions: systems using a separate dedicated grounding electrode that is bonded to the main system at a single point

subject: Lightning Protection Down Conductor
rule: Lightning protection down conductor must not have sharp bends (bend radius must meet code minimum, typically not less than 200 mm or 8 inches)
conditions: down conductor is routed with directional changes

subject: Bonding Conductor
rule: Bonding conductor must be electrically continuous from the bonding point to the grounding electrode system
conditions: When used for electrical safety bonding
exceptions: Intentional disconnects for testing purposes as permitted by code

subject: Bonding Conductor
rule: Bonding conductor must not be smaller than the minimum size specified by applicable electrical code (typically Table 250.66 of NEC)
conditions: When used for grounding electrode system bonding

subject: Bonding Conductor
rule: Bonding conductor must not have any splice or connection that is not listed for the purpose
conditions: Per NEC 250.64(C)
exceptions: Irreversible compression-type connectors listed for the purpose are permitted

subject: Backfill Material for Earth Pit
rule: Backfill material for earth pit must be granular, non-cohesive soil (e.g., sand, gravel, or crushed stone) with low clay/silt content
conditions: Earth pit is used for electrical earthing/grounding system
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified backfill designed for the specific grounding system

subject: Backfill Material for Earth Pit
rule: Backfill material must be free of large rocks, debris, and organic matter
conditions: Earth pit is used for electrical earthing/grounding system

subject: Backfill Material for Earth Pit
rule: Backfill material must be compacted in layers to achieve specified density

subject: Backfill Material for Earth Pit
rule: Backfill material must not contain corrosive substances such as chlorides, sulfates, or acidic compounds above allowable limits
conditions: Earth pit contains metallic grounding electrodes
exceptions: Corrosion-inhibiting backfill compounds specifically designed for grounding systems

subject: Main Earth Busbar
rule: Main Earth Busbar must be directly connected to the earth electrode via a conductor of appropriate cross-sectional area
conditions: In any electrical installation requiring earthing
exceptions: Where the Main Earth Busbar is not the primary means of earthing connection, such as in TT systems where each circuit has its own earth electrode

subject: Main Earth Busbar
rule: Main Earth Busbar must be bonded to the main water pipe, gas pipe, and other incoming metallic services within the building
conditions: Where such metallic services enter the building and are part of the equipotential bonding zone
exceptions: Where services are entirely plastic/non-metallic and do not require bonding
Where bonding is achieved via a separate bonding bar that is itself connected to the main earth busbar

subject: Main Earth Busbar
rule: Main Earth Busbar must be accessible for inspection and testing
conditions: In any permanent electrical installation
exceptions: Temporary or mobile installations where the busbar is integrated into sealed factory-assembled equipment

subject: Main Earth Busbar
rule: Main Earth Busbar must not be used as a neutral conductor
conditions: In any AC electrical system

subject: Main Earth Busbar
rule: Main Earth Busbar must be electrically continuous (no switch or overcurrent device interrupting the earthing conductor path)
conditions: In any protective earthing system

subject: Equipotential Bonding Grid
rule: equipotential bonding grid must be electrically connected to all exposed conductive surfaces within the zone it protects
conditions: when used for lightning protection or electrical safety
exceptions: surfaces that are intentionally isolated for functional reasons and are within a zone that is not subject to lightning risk

subject: Equipotential Bonding Grid
rule: equipotential bonding grid must form a closed-loop conductive path with no unintentional breaks or open circuits
exceptions: temporary test disconnects that are designed to be closed during normal operation

subject: Equipotential Bonding Grid
rule: equipotential bonding grid must not be installed in series with overcurrent protective devices that could interrupt continuity
exceptions: where a specifically designed spark gap or surge protective device is used that maintains bonding under fault conditions

subject: Equipotential Bonding Grid
rule: equipotential bonding grid must have a resistance-to-earth value that does not exceed the maximum specified by applicable electrical safety standards for the installation type
conditions: when the grid is also used as a grounding electrode system
exceptions: where the bonding grid is purely for equipotential equalization and not relied upon for earth fault current return path

subject: Equipotential Bonding Grid
rule: equipotential bonding grid conductors must be sized to withstand the maximum prospective fault current without thermal damage

subject: Terraced Slope Structure
rule: A terraced slope structure must maintain inter-terrace drainage continuity to prevent water accumulation and slope failure
conditions: multi-terrace configuration
exposed to precipitation or surface water flow
exceptions: fully enclosed terraced structure with internal drainage system

subject: Terraced Slope Structure
rule: Each terrace retaining wall must have adequate weep holes or drainage outlets at the base
conditions: retaining walls are present
wall height exceeds 0.5 m
exceptions: wall designed as a waterproof barrier with engineered sub-surface drainage behind it

subject: Terraced Slope Structure
rule: The overall slope angle of a terraced structure must not exceed the angle of repose of the underlying soil or fill material
conditions: structure is earth-retaining
found on granular or cohesive soil
exceptions: rock-cut terraces in competent bedrock with engineered stabilization

subject: Tiered Treads
rule: Each tread tier must have a minimum tread depth (run) of at least 280 mm (11 inches) for exterior stairs and 260 mm (10 inches) for interior stairs in a tiered tread configuration
conditions: Tiered treads are used as a stair component
exceptions: Private dwelling interior stairs may reduce to 220 mm (8.5 inches) under some residential codes

subject: Tiered Treads
rule: The maximum riser height between consecutive tread tiers must not exceed 200 mm (8 inches) for exterior stairs and 190 mm (7.5 inches) for interior stairs
conditions: Tiered treads form a stair run

subject: Tiered Treads
rule: Each tiered tread must have a minimum noshing projection of 15 mm (0.5 inches) if the tread has an open riser
conditions: Tiered tread has an open riser below it
exceptions: Enclosed risers do not require nosing projection

subject: Tiered Treads
rule: Tiered treads must not have a vertical gap between successive tread surfaces exceeding 100 mm (4 inches) when used as accessible egress
conditions: Tiered treads are part of an accessible egress path
exceptions: Private non-accessible dwellings are exempt

subject: Terraced Retaining Wall
rule: terraced retaining wall must be designed to resist sliding failure
conditions: wall retains soil
wall is on a sloped site
exceptions: if bedrock is encountered at the base providing sufficient friction

subject: Terraced Retaining Wall
rule: terraced retaining wall must be designed to resist overturning
conditions: wall retains soil
wall is not anchored or tied back
exceptions: if wall is mechanically anchored into stable bedrock

subject: Terraced Retaining Wall
rule: terraced retaining wall must include a drainage system to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: wall retains soil that can hold water
wall height exceeds 1 meter
exceptions: if the retained soil is free-draining granular material with proven drainage

subject: Terraced Retaining Wall
rule: terraced retaining wall must have structural capacity to bear vertical loads from upper terraces
conditions: wall supports loads from a terrace above

subject: Terraced Retaining Wall
rule: terraced retaining wall must not be built on uncompacted or unstable fill material
conditions: foundation soil is known to be fill or disturbed
exceptions: if fill is engineered and compacted to geotechnical specification

subject: Geogrid Soil Reinforcement
rule: Geogrid tensile strength must not be less than the maximum design tensile force in the soil
conditions: when used as primary reinforcement in reinforced soil structures

subject: Geogrid Soil Reinforcement
rule: Geogrid must have an aperture size compatible with the soil grain size to ensure adequate interlock
conditions: when used for soil confinement or reinforcement
exceptions: geotextile-type geogrids used primarily for separation rather than interlock

subject: Geogrid Soil Reinforcement
rule: Geogrid must be installed with the principal tensile direction aligned with the primary direction of tensile strain in the soil
conditions: when used in slopes, retaining walls, or embankments with a defined failure plane

subject: Slope Drainage System
rule: Slope drainage system must have a continuous positive gradient (fall) toward the outlet to prevent ponding and ensure flow
conditions: gravity-driven flow is used
system is designed for liquid water removal
exceptions: siphonic drainage systems where negative pressure drives flow

subject: Slope Drainage System
rule: Slope drainage system must not have a gradient less than the minimum fall required by applicable building code for the roof/ surface type
conditions: system is part of a building subject to code jurisdiction
exceptions: engineered systems with verified hydraulic design demonstrating adequate drainage at lower slopes through specific gutter/pipe sizing or scuppers

subject: Slope Drainage System
rule: Slope drainage system must not allow drainage across an expansion joint or structural separation without a dedicated drainage break or collector
conditions: building has structural expansion joints or seismic separations

subject: Slope Drainage System
rule: Slope drainage system must be sized to handle the design rainfall intensity for the geographic location, accounting for tributary area

subject: Terraced Planting Pockets
rule: Terraced Planting Pockets must have a continuous waterproof membrane below all soil/planting layers
conditions: When installed above occupiable spaces
When installed above interior spaces
exceptions: When planting pockets are ground-level and drain directly into earth

subject: Terraced Planting Pockets
rule: Terraced Planting Pockets must have an irrigation drainage outlet at the lowest point of each pocket
exceptions: Pockets that are fully self-contained and manually drained

subject: Terraced Planting Pockets
rule: Terraced Planting Pockets must not exceed the structural load capacity of the supporting wall or frame

subject: Integrated Terrace Bench Seating
rule: Integrated terrace bench seating must be structurally supported to bear expected live loads (people sitting/standing)
conditions: seating is intended for occupant use
seating projects from building face without independent ground support
exceptions: decorative-only seating not intended for occupancy

subject: Integrated Terrace Bench Seating
rule: Integrated terrace bench seating must have a slip-resistant walking surface on any portion serving as a walking/standing area
conditions: seating includes a terrace surface accessible to occupants
surface is exposed to weather/moisture

subject: Integrated Terrace Bench Seating
rule: Integrated terrace bench seating must not block required egress paths or reduce required exit width
conditions: seating is located along or adjacent to means of egress
exceptions: where local code permits encroachment up to a specific width (e.g., 18" projection above 27" height)

subject: Integrated Terrace Bench Seating
rule: Integrated terrace bench seating must have a guardrail or parapet where the fall height from the seating surface exceeds the code threshold (typically 762 mm / 30")
conditions: seating surface elevation is 30" or more above adjacent grade or floor
exceptions: Where bench backrest itself meets guard height requirements (typically 42") and can resist design loads

subject: Integrated Terrace Bench Seating
rule: Integrated terrace bench seating must be detailed to prevent water ponding on the seating surface
conditions: seating surface is horizontal or nearly horizontal
surface is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: perforated or slatted surfaces that allow free drainage

subject: Terraced Amphitheater Layout
rule: Terraced amphitheater layout must have continuous, unobstructed egress paths (aisles/steps) from every seating row to exits
conditions: Occupant load exceeds 50 persons
exceptions: One-story amphitheaters with direct ground-level exit from each row

subject: Terraced Amphitheater Layout
rule: Terraced amphitheater layout must have a minimum tread depth on stepped seating rows that prevents forward toppling and supports stable standing/sitting

subject: Terraced Amphitheater Layout
rule: Terraced amphitheater layout must not have a vertical riser height between adjacent seating rows that exceeds a safe stepping height
exceptions: Rows accessible only via handrail-equipped stairs adjacent to the terrace rather than direct stepping between rows

subject: Terraced Amphitheater Layout
rule: Terraced amphitheater layout must have each terrace level structurally capable of supporting its design live load (seated/standing occupants)

subject: Built-in Terrace Lighting Installation
rule: Built-in terrace lighting installation must be IP-rated for outdoor exposure
conditions: Lighting is installed in an exposed outdoor terrace area
exceptions: Terrace is fully enclosed and weather-protected

subject: Built-in Terrace Lighting Installation
rule: Built-in terrace lighting installation must be connected to a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protected circuit
conditions: Lighting is line-voltage (not low-voltage Class 2)
exceptions: Low-voltage lighting system with isolated transformer

subject: Built-in Terrace Lighting Installation
rule: Built-in terrace lighting must not be installed in a location where its housing traps standing water
conditions: Fixture is surface-mounted or recessed in a horizontal or upward-facing orientation
exceptions: Fixture is specifically rated and designed for wet locations with drainage channels

subject: Handrail and Guardrail System
rule: handrail or guardrail system must have a top rail capable of withstanding the required design loads (e.g., concentrated load of 200 lbf minimum for handrails, 50 plf distributed load for guardrails under typical building codes)
conditions: when used as a handrail serving stairs, ramps, or walkways
when used as a guardrail to prevent falls from elevated surfaces
exceptions: low-rise residential applications where local code permits reduced loading

subject: Handrail and Guardrail System
rule: handrail and guardrail system must not have openings that allow passage of a 4-inch (102 mm) sphere (for guardrails) or a 6-inch (152 mm) sphere (for handrails on stairs)
conditions: when the system serves as a guardrail at the open side of a walking surface with a drop of 30 inches or more
exceptions: triangular openings at the tread/riser intersection of stairs are typically exempted up to a specific dimension

subject: Handrail and Guardrail System
rule: handrail gripping surface must have a cross-section dimension between 1.25 inches and 2 inches (32-51 mm) or equivalent ergonomic profile
conditions: when the handrail is required for accessible means of egress per ADA / ANSI A117.1
exceptions: handrails not required for accessibility, such as in industrial or non-public areas where local code may allow alternate profiles

subject: Handrail and Guardrail System
rule: guardrail system must have a minimum height of 42 inches (1067 mm) measured from the walking surface
conditions: when the guardrail is on the open side of a walking surface with a vertical drop of 30 inches or more
commercial or multi-family residential buildings per IBC
exceptions: residential occupancies where minimum height is 36 inches (914 mm) per IRC

subject: Handrail and Guardrail System
rule: handrail must be continuously graspable along its entire length without obstruction by newel posts, brackets, or other elements
conditions: when the handrail serves an accessible route or is required per ADA / building code
exceptions: temporary interruptions allowed at intermediate newel posts where the handrail returns to the wall or continues on an alternate path

subject: Orchard
rule: orchard must have a drainage system to prevent waterlogging of tree roots
conditions: orchard is on a site with any precipitation
exceptions: orchard is on land with naturally perfect drainage (e.g., pure sand over deep gravel) and no risk of standing water

subject: Orchard
rule: orchard must have frost protection measures in low-lying areas prone to frost pockets
conditions: orchard is located in a region where frost occurs
orchard is sited in a topographic depression or valley floor where cold air drains
exceptions: orchard consists entirely of frost-tolerant species (e.g., certain cider apple varieties)
orchard is on a slope with unobstructed cold-air drainage away from trees

subject: Orchard
rule: orchard must have pollinator access during bloom period
conditions: orchard contains tree varieties that are not self-fertile
exceptions: orchard contains only self-fertile varieties (e.g., certain peach, apricot, or self-fertile apple cultivars)
orchard is small enough for hand-pollination as primary strategy

subject: Orchard
rule: orchard must not be sited on land with a hardpan or impervious layer within the effective root zone without remediation
conditions: soil survey or test shows a compacted layer, claypan, or bedrock within 1 m of the surface
exceptions: hardpan is broken by deep ripping or tile drainage prior to planting
orchard uses raised beds or mounds that provide sufficient root depth above the impervious layer

subject: Fruit Tree Planting Pit
rule: Fruit tree planting pit must have at least one open side or drainage outlet to prevent waterlogging
conditions: pit is excavated in soil with clay content > 20%
pit is in region with annual rainfall > 600mm
exceptions: pit is lined with impermeable membrane and designed as a water-retention feature

subject: Fruit Tree Planting Pit
rule: Fruit tree planting pit must_not be located directly above buried utilities (gas, water, power, sewage)
exceptions: utility has been rerouted or protected with a structural sleeve approved by the relevant authority

subject: Fruit Tree Planting Pit
rule: Fruit tree planting pit dimensions must accommodate the root ball of the selected fruit tree species with at least 30 cm clearance on all sides
exceptions: pit is a temporary nursery pot

subject: Fruit Tree Planting Pit
rule: Fruit tree planting pit must have a minimum depth of 50 cm (or depth sufficient for the species' rootstock, whichever is greater)
exceptions: tree species is a dwarf variety with documented shallower root requirements

subject: Fruit Tree Root Barrier
rule: Fruit tree root barrier must be installed vertically in the trench, extending from just below the soil surface to at least the expected rooting depth of the tree
conditions: When installed for a fruit tree

subject: Fruit Tree Root Barrier
rule: Fruit tree root barrier must be made of a material that is impermeable to roots and resistant to soil-borne decay

subject: Fruit Tree Root Barrier
rule: Fruit tree root barrier must not have gaps, holes, or seams that exceed the diameter of fine root hairs

subject: Fruit Tree Support Structure
rule: Fruit tree support structure must be rigidly anchored to prevent toppling under fruit load
conditions: tree supports heavy fruit crop
structure is freestanding
exceptions: structure is temporary and manually stabilized during fruiting season

subject: Fruit Tree Support Structure
rule: Fruit tree support structure must not damage tree bark or branches at contact points
conditions: support members contact living tree tissue

subject: Fruit Tree Support Structure
rule: Fruit tree support structure must be constructed from weather-resistant or treated materials
conditions: structure is installed outdoors permanently or for more than one growing season
exceptions: structure is single-season disposable (e.g., bamboo stakes removed after harvest)

subject: Fruit Tree Irrigation System
rule: irrigation water must not contain contaminants (e.g., pathogens, heavy metals, oils) that can harm fruit trees or accumulate in fruit

subject: Fruit Tree Irrigation System
rule: water delivery pressure at the emitter must be within the range specified by the emitter manufacturer
conditions: system uses drip emitters, micro-sprinklers, or other pressure-sensitive emission devices

subject: Fruit Tree Irrigation System
rule: piping and fittings must be rated for the maximum expected water pressure in the system

subject: Fruit Tree Irrigation System
rule: the system must be protected against backflow to prevent contamination of the potable water supply
conditions: system is connected to a potable water supply

subject: Tree Pit Grate
rule: Tree pit grate must be able to support pedestrian and occasional vehicular live loads without breaking or deforming
conditions: installed in sidewalk or paved area
subject to foot traffic
exceptions: decorative-only grates in non-traffic areas with explicit pedestrian exclusion

subject: Tree Pit Grate
rule: Tree pit grate must have openings large enough to allow water and air to reach the tree root zone
conditions: installed around a living tree

subject: Tree Pit Grate
rule: Tree pit grate must not have openings large enough for a pedestrian's foot or heel to become trapped
conditions: installed in pedestrian-accessible area

subject: Tree Pit Grate
rule: Tree pit grate must be secured against uplift or displacement by wind, traffic, or vandalism
exceptions: temporary/removable grates that are clearly marked and supervised

subject: Tree Pit Grate
rule: Tree pit grate must be compatible with the tree trunk diameter allowing for future trunk expansion without girdling the tree
conditions: installed around a living tree
exceptions: grates with expandable/cut-out collars designed to be adjusted over time

subject: Espalier Trellis System
rule: the espalier trellis system must be structurally self-supporting or securely attached to a supporting wall/foundation
conditions: when used as a standalone structure
when attached to a building wall
exceptions: temporary training stakes that are manually held or lightly inserted into soft ground without permanent attachment

subject: Espalier Trellis System
rule: the espalier trellis system must not have horizontal wires or rails spaced wider than the maximum reach of the target plant species' lateral branches
conditions: when training fruit trees or woody ornamentals in espalier form

subject: Espalier Trellis System
rule: the espalier trellis system's support posts or wall anchors must be embedded or fastened to resist overturning and lateral forces without relying solely on the plant for stability
conditions: when the trellis is taller than 1.5 meters
when located in regions with wind speeds exceeding 80 km/h
exceptions: lightweight temporary trellises used for annuals that are fully removed each season

subject: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain
rule: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain must be positioned downhill from the fruit tree(s) it serves
conditions: drain serves one or more fruit trees
site has topographic slope
exceptions: site is perfectly flat with engineered subsurface flow control

subject: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain
rule: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain outlet must not be blocked by root growth or soil compaction
conditions: drain is installed with a permeable outlet or weep hole
exceptions: outlet is fitted with a root-proof geotextile filter sock that is regularly maintained

subject: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain
rule: Fruit Tree Soakaway Drain invert must be at least 300 mm above the seasonal high groundwater table
conditions: site has a measurable seasonal high groundwater table

subject: Interior Courtyard
rule: Interior courtyard must have a means of water drainage (e.g., drains, sloping, or hydraulic connection to a storm system)
conditions: courtyard is open to the sky
courtyard is located in a climate with precipitation
exceptions: courtyard is fully roofed (i.e., is an atrium rather than an open courtyard)

subject: Interior Courtyard
rule: Interior courtyard must have adequate emergency egress or fire-engine access if surrounded by occupied spaces on multiple sides
conditions: courtyard is enclosed by occupied floors on two or more sides
courtyard is the only means of escape for adjacent spaces
exceptions: adjacent spaces have alternative egress paths that do not rely on the courtyard

subject: Interior Courtyard
rule: Interior courtyard must not have a fully enclosed floor area that collects and traps hazardous gas or smoke without ventilation
conditions: courtyard is open to the sky but has high surrounding walls that impede natural air movement
exceptions: mechanical smoke exhaust system is provided
courtyard is designed as a pressurised safe zone

subject: Tree Atrium
rule: Tree Atrium space must be open to the sky or have a transparent roof to allow tree growth and natural light penetration
conditions: space is designated as an atrium
space contains live trees
exceptions: artificial trees are used instead of live trees

subject: Tree Atrium
rule: Tree Atrium must have a minimum floor-to-roof/ceiling height sufficient to accommodate the mature height of the tree species planted
conditions: space contains live trees

subject: Tree Atrium
rule: Tree Atrium must not have impermeable floor surface fully covering the root zone area without an engineered drainage and aeration system
conditions: space contains live trees planted in-ground
exceptions: trees are in raised planters with integrated drainage

subject: Tree Atrium
rule: Tree Atrium must have a fire-rated separation or active fire suppression system between the tree zone and occupied floors if the tree species has high flammability
conditions: tree species has high flammable resin or foliage
building exceeds local code height threshold
exceptions: local fire code explicitly exempts interior atriums with live trees under a size threshold

subject: Green Wall / Vertical Garden (tree-adjacent)
rule: Green wall / vertical garden system must have an integrated irrigation system or be positioned within reach of a water supply
conditions: installed in climate with less than 500mm annual rainfall
or installed where supplementary watering is otherwise unavailable
exceptions: wall is planted exclusively with drought-adapted species that can survive on ambient rainfall in a humid climate

subject: Green Wall / Vertical Garden (tree-adjacent)
rule: Green wall structure must be engineered to support the total saturated weight of growing medium, plants, and retained water
conditions: mounted on any vertical surface

subject: Green Wall / Vertical Garden (tree-adjacent)
rule: Green wall / vertical garden must not be installed on a wall that cannot accommodate the required waterproofing and drainage layer
conditions: wall is interior and adjacent to habitable spaces
or wall has no existing moisture barrier
exceptions: a separate free-standing structural frame is erected in front of the wall

subject: Green Wall / Vertical Garden (tree-adjacent)
rule: Green wall / vertical garden must not create a fire propagation path across building floors
conditions: installed on an exterior facade spanning more than one story
and local fire code classifies vertical greenery as a fire-risk feature
exceptions: system uses non-combustible growing medium and plants with high moisture content that have passed a relevant fire-resistance test

subject: Tree Grate / Cover
rule: Tree grate / cover must have openings large enough to allow water and air to reach tree roots
conditions: installed over soil around a tree

subject: Tree Grate / Cover
rule: Tree grate / cover must be structurally capable of supporting pedestrian / light vehicular loads without collapsing
conditions: installed in a walkway or paved area subject to foot or occasional light vehicle traffic

subject: Tree Grate / Cover
rule: Tree grate / cover must not completely seal around the tree trunk without allowance for trunk growth
conditions: installed around an existing or future tree trunk

subject: Root Barrier System
rule: root barrier system must be continuous and unbroken across all protected surfaces
conditions: when used as a waterproofing or root-proof membrane
exceptions: intentional gaps at control joints that are specifically designed with root-resistant detailing

subject: Root Barrier System
rule: root barrier system must resist root penetration for the intended service life of the assembly
conditions: when installed in contact with soil or growing medium containing vegetation

subject: Root Barrier System
rule: root barrier must not contain plasticizers or components that are biodegradable or consumable by soil microorganisms
conditions: when installed below grade or in permanent contact with soil

subject: Drainage Layer / Sub-base
rule: Drainage layer / sub-base must provide a continuous slope toward drainage outlets to prevent water ponding
conditions: The drainage layer is installed in a flat or low-slope roof or terrace assembly
exceptions: When the drainage layer is part of a fully adhered, tapered insulation system that provides the slope separately

subject: Drainage Layer / Sub-base
rule: Drainage layer / sub-base must not be constructed of materials that degrade or clog when exposed to water
conditions: The drainage layer is below the wearing surface or directly under a permeable paving system

subject: Drainage Layer / Sub-base
rule: Drainage layer / sub-base must have sufficient compressive strength to resist the design loads without crushing that would close void spaces
conditions: The drainage layer is beneath a trafficable surface, paving, or structural fill
exceptions: When the drainage layer is only in a vertical wall drainage application with no superimposed load

subject: Bench / Seating Around Tree Pit
rule: Bench / seating around tree pit must have a minimum setback distance from the tree trunk to avoid root damage and provide soil aeration
conditions: Tree pit contains living tree
Bench is adjacent to tree pit
exceptions: Tree pit is surface-rooted with root barrier protection installed

subject: Bench / Seating Around Tree Pit
rule: Bench / seating around tree pit must not block pedestrian egress or accessibility clearance zones
conditions: Bench is located in a public walkway or plaza with pedestrian circulation
exceptions: Bench is placed on a dedicated seating island outside the clear path width

subject: Bench / Seating Around Tree Pit
rule: Bench / seating around tree pit must have a structurally stable mounting or base that prevents tipping
conditions: Bench is freestanding (not anchored to a wall or structure)

subject: Tree Support / Guying System (Temporary)
rule: Tree support/guying system must be installed with tension not exceeding the tree's structural capacity to avoid girdling or bark damage
conditions: System uses cables, straps, or wires in direct contact with tree trunk or branches

subject: Tree Support / Guying System (Temporary)
rule: Temporary tree support/guying system must be removed or loosened before the tree's trunk diameter growth contacts the hardware
conditions: System is intended for temporary installation (e.g., 1-3 growing seasons)

subject: Tree Support / Guying System (Temporary)
rule: Guying cable or strap must not be wrapped completely around the tree trunk in a closed loop without a protective buffer/spacer
conditions: Cable or strap encircles the full circumference of the trunk

subject: Tree Support / Guying System (Temporary)
rule: Anchor stake/rod must be driven to a depth sufficient to resist the design wind/snow load without pulling out of the soil
conditions: System uses ground anchors or stakes

subject: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone
rule: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone must have direct exposure to rainfall or an irrigation supply
exceptions: Zone is designed as a controlled xeriscape with drought-tolerant species that only require fog/moisture capture

subject: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone
rule: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone soil depth must be sufficient for root anchorage and seed germination (minimum 150 mm growing medium)
conditions: Zone is installed on a roof or artificial structure rather than on natural grade
exceptions: Zone uses a purpose-engineered green-roof substrate tray system with integrated shallow-cell depth certified for the specified plant palette

subject: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone
rule: Self-Seeding Groundcover Zone must not be placed where prevailing wind speeds consistently exceed the tolerance of the selected groundcover species
conditions: Zone is located on a rooftop, balcony, or open elevated plane
exceptions: Wind-mitigation measures (screens, walls, baffles) are in place to reduce wind speed at grade to within species tolerance

subject: Naturalistic Pond or Wetland Pocket
rule: Naturalistic pond or wetland pocket must have a water source (inflow) that maintains the designed water level or saturation regime
conditions: pond is intended to hold water year-round or seasonally
wetland is designed to maintain hydric soil conditions
exceptions: ephemeral pond designed to be dry for most of the year

subject: Naturalistic Pond or Wetland Pocket
rule: Naturalistic pond or wetland pocket must have an outlet or overflow path to prevent uncontrolled flooding of adjacent areas
conditions: pond or wetland receives stormwater runoff or has a continuous inflow
exceptions: self-contained basin sized to store the full design storm without overflow

subject: Naturalistic Pond or Wetland Pocket
rule: Naturalistic pond or wetland pocket must not be placed directly above underground utility tunnels, major pipelines, or building basements without an impermeable liner
conditions: water depth exceeds 0.3 m
underlying space is occupied or contains critical infrastructure
exceptions: liner or waterproof barrier of verified integrity separates water from below-grade space

subject: Naturalistic Pond or Wetland Pocket
rule: Naturalistic pond or wetland pocket must have a minimum freeboard of at least 0.15 m between the design high-water level and the lowest adjacent finished grade or building opening
conditions: pond or wetland is located within 5 m of a building or critical structure
exceptions: engineered flood wall or barrier permanently protects the building opening

subject: Overgrown Trellis or Pergola
rule: overgrown trellis or pergola must have structural load capacity for the combined weight of its own structure, any climbing plants, and anticipated environmental loads (snow, wind, rain)
conditions: when designed to support climbing plants
when located in areas with snow or wind loading
exceptions: temporary or purely decorative lightweight structures not intended to bear any plant or environmental load

subject: Overgrown Trellis or Pergola
rule: overgrown trellis or pergola must not have enclosed solid roof covering
conditions: when classified as a pergola or open trellis structure
exceptions: when designed as a fully engineered roofed structure with proper drainage, snow load, and wind resistance per building code

subject: Overgrown Trellis or Pergola
rule: overgrown trellis or pergola must have adequate ventilation gaps between roof members to prevent moisture entrapment and fungal decay of the structure and climbing plants
conditions: when made of wood or other organic material
when supporting living climbing plants
exceptions: structures made entirely of non-organic materials where moisture drainage is otherwise ensured

subject: Informal Stone or Gravel Path
rule: path surface must have a stable, compacted base layer to prevent sinking or shifting under foot traffic
conditions: when used as a primary walking surface
when supporting pedestrian loads
exceptions: decorative paths that are not intended for regular foot traffic

subject: Informal Stone or Gravel Path
rule: path must have edge restraint (e.g., edging stones, timbers, or curb) to prevent lateral spreading of gravel
conditions: when the path is surfaced with loose gravel
when the path has sloped sides or is adjacent to soft ground
exceptions: when gravel is deep enough and compacted to form a self-stable angle of repose within a defined trench

subject: Informal Stone or Gravel Path
rule: path surface must not have standing water or become a continuous mud patch after rain
conditions: when the path is intended for all-weather use

subject: Rustic Wooden Garden Bench
rule: bench must have a stable base resting on ground or solid surface to prevent tipping under seated load
conditions: when used for seating

subject: Rustic Wooden Garden Bench
rule: bench must not have sharp edges or splinters on seating and armrest surfaces
conditions: when intended for human contact during normal use
exceptions: if explicitly designed as decorative-only non-contact art piece

subject: Rustic Wooden Garden Bench
rule: bench must support at least 250 lbs static load without structural failure
conditions: when designed for typical adult seating
exceptions: if explicitly labeled as child-only or decorative-only bench

subject: Rustic Wooden Garden Bench
rule: wood must be treated or naturally resistant to outdoor rot and insect damage
conditions: when intended for continuous outdoor garden use
exceptions: if bench is designed as indoor-only or seasonal indoor-outdoor furniture brought inside when not in use

subject: Rainwater Collection Cistern
rule: cistern must be watertight
conditions: cistern is intended to store collected rainwater

subject: Rainwater Collection Cistern
rule: cistern must have an overflow outlet
conditions: cistern receives rainwater from a catchment surface
cistern has a finite storage volume

subject: Rainwater Collection Cistern
rule: cistern inlet must be screened to exclude debris and mosquitoes
conditions: cistern is open to the atmosphere at the inlet

subject: Rainwater Collection Cistern
rule: cistern must not be constructed with materials that leach contaminants into stored water
conditions: water is intended for potable or household use

subject: Rainwater Collection Cistern
rule: cistern must be structurally capable of withstanding the maximum hydrostatic pressure of its full water volume
conditions: cistern is installed above or below grade
cistern will be filled to its design capacity

subject: Dry-Laid Retaining Wall
rule: dry-laid retaining wall must have a base width at least one-third of its height
conditions: wall height exceeds 0.5 m

subject: Dry-Laid Retaining Wall
rule: dry-laid retaining wall must not be built on uncompacted or water-saturated soil without drainage provisions
conditions: wall retains soil
exceptions: wall height is less than 0.3 m and soil is well-draining gravel

subject: Dry-Laid Retaining Wall
rule: dry-laid retaining wall must have drainage openings or a granular backfill layer to relieve hydrostatic pressure
conditions: wall retains cohesive soil or is taller than 1 m
exceptions: wall retains free-draining granular material such as clean gravel

subject: Dry-Laid Retaining Wall
rule: dry-laid retaining wall must not have individual stones smaller than one-quarter the wall thickness

subject: Wild Garden Irrigation Drip Network
rule: drip line emitters must maintain pressure within manufacturer-specified operating range
conditions: system is actively delivering water
exceptions: system completely shut off and drained for maintenance or winterization

subject: Wild Garden Irrigation Drip Network
rule: drip network must not exceed maximum allowable flow rate of the supply line or backflow preventer
conditions: system is supplied from a municipal or pressurized source

subject: Wild Garden Irrigation Drip Network
rule: drip tubing must not be installed with dead-end runs that prevent flushing of sediment
conditions: system uses un-filtered or partially filtered water
tubing diameter is less than 1/2 inch
exceptions: system is equipped with automatic flushing end caps or a self-cleaning filter at each dead end

subject: Garden Wall Base Foundation
rule: Garden wall base foundation must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
exceptions: When deep foundation system (piles, piers) transfers load to competent stratum

subject: Garden Wall Base Foundation
rule: Garden wall base foundation bottom must be below frost depth
conditions: In regions subject to seasonal freezing
exceptions: When foundation is designed to accommodate frost heave (e.g., floating slab, insulated foundation)

subject: Garden Wall Base Foundation
rule: Garden wall base foundation must not bear on organic soils, peat, or uncompacted fill
exceptions: When organic soils are fully removed and replaced with engineered fill, or when deep foundation is used

subject: Garden Site Drainage Layer
rule: Garden Site Drainage Layer must have a continuous positive slope away from building foundations toward an approved discharge point
conditions: Layer is installed adjacent to building foundation
exceptions: Site is designed with an alternative engineered drainage system such as French drains or sump pumps that provides equivalent water removal

subject: Garden Site Drainage Layer
rule: Garden Site Drainage Layer must not have impermeable barriers that block the lateral flow of water through the drainage medium
conditions: Drainage layer is composed of granular material or geocomposite drain board
exceptions: The impermeable barrier is a designed component of a bioretention or rainwater harvesting system that intentionally retains water

subject: Garden Site Drainage Layer
rule: Garden Site Drainage Layer must have an outlet or overflow pathway that can handle the design storm event without backing up into the planting media
conditions: Drainage layer serves a roof garden or podium garden with limited vertical percolation
exceptions: The garden is designed as a constructed wetland or permanent water feature requiring saturation

subject: Garden Site Drainage Layer
rule: Garden Site Drainage Layer must_not release water in a manner that causes erosion of adjacent soil or landscaping
conditions: Discharge point is on or adjacent to vegetated soil slopes
exceptions: Erosion control measures (e.g., riprap, energy dissipaters, turf reinforcement) are installed at the outlet

subject: Garden Wall Facing / Cladding
rule: Garden wall facing / cladding must be applied to an existing structural wall or substrate that provides load-bearing support

subject: Garden Wall Facing / Cladding
rule: Garden wall facing / cladding must not trap moisture against the structural wall behind it

subject: Garden Wall Facing / Cladding
rule: Garden wall facing / cladding must have an appropriate drainage and ventilation cavity behind it when used on external walls in a wet climate
conditions: external wall application
wet climate or exposure to driving rain

subject: Garden Wall Facing / Cladding
rule: Garden wall facing / cladding must be mechanically fixed or adhered with a system rated for the weight and thermal movement of the material
exceptions: Stone veneer thinner than 40mm bedded in full mortar bed on a solid masonry wall may rely on adhesive bond alone

subject: Garden Wall Coping
rule: Garden wall coping must have a minimum slope to shed water
conditions: when installed as a horizontal or near-horizontal top element on a wall
exceptions: when coping is designed as a flat-surface green roof assembly with controlled drainage

subject: Garden Wall Coping
rule: Garden wall coping must overhang the wall face on both sides
conditions: when the coping caps a wall exposed to rain
exceptions: when an integrated drip kerf or groove is provided within the coping's underside

subject: Garden Wall Coping
rule: Garden wall coping must not be constructed from materials with higher porosity than the wall below
conditions: when both coping and wall are exposed to direct rainfall
exceptions: when a continuous impermeable membrane separates coping from wall

subject: Garden Wall Damp-Proof Course
rule: A garden wall damp-proof course must be continuous and unbroken across the entire wall width to prevent moisture bridging
conditions: Where a damp-proof course is specified in a garden wall construction
exceptions: Walls built entirely of moisture-resistant materials (e.g., engineering brick in full-bed mortar with no capillary path)

subject: Garden Wall Damp-Proof Course
rule: A garden wall damp-proof course must be positioned at least 150 mm above the adjacent finished ground level
conditions: Where external ground abuts the wall

subject: Garden Wall Damp-Proof Course
rule: A garden wall damp-proof course must not be bridged by external render, pointing, or backfill material across the DPC line
conditions: Where the wall has applied finishes or earth contact on either side

subject: Garden Wall Pier / Pilaster
rule: Garden wall pier / pilaster must be laterally supported at top and base to prevent buckling under vertical load
conditions: when acting as a structural pier supporting vertical loads from arches or beams
exceptions: free-standing decorative pilaster not carrying vertical load

subject: Garden Wall Pier / Pilaster
rule: Garden wall pier / pilaster must have a minimum cross-sectional dimension proportion to its height to avoid slenderness failure
conditions: when constructed in unreinforced masonry
when height exceeds 6 times the least lateral dimension
exceptions: if pier is reinforced with steel and designed to modern structural code

subject: Garden Wall Pier / Pilaster
rule: Garden wall pier / pilaster must not be built with incompatible masonry materials that cause differential movement cracking
conditions: when combining brick and stone in the same pier
exceptions: if movement joints are provided between dissimilar materials

subject: Garden Wall Expansion / Movement Joint
rule: garden wall expansion/movement joint must be located where the new garden wall abuts an existing structure or at intervals along a long wall run
conditions: When a new garden wall is built adjacent to an existing building, wall, or rigid structure
When a garden wall exceeds typical unreinforced masonry length (generally > 6m)
exceptions: When a continuous reinforced concrete or steel ring beam ties the entire wall to a deep foundation system

subject: Garden Wall Expansion / Movement Joint
rule: movement joint must extend fully through the wall section and be free of mortar or rigid filling
conditions: Where a movement joint is provided in a garden wall
exceptions: Where the joint is specifically designed as a 'parting' or 'slip' layer that only breaks the outer leaf in a cavity wall system

subject: Garden Wall Expansion / Movement Joint
rule: movement joint must not be bridged by rigid mortar, render, or rigid wall capping
conditions: Where a garden wall includes a movement joint
exceptions: Where a flexible cover strip or purpose-made compressible joint filler is installed to seal the gap while preserving movement capacity

subject: Garden Wall Drainage / Weepholes
rule: garden walls with drainage/weepholes must have a minimum clear drainage path to allow water egress
conditions: wall retains soil or is a retaining wall
weepholes are present
exceptions: wall does not retain water/soil (e.g., free-standing decorative non-retaining wall)

subject: Garden Wall Drainage / Weepholes
rule: weepholes must not be located below finished grade or submerged in backfill material
conditions: weepholes are installed in a retaining or garden wall
exceptions: weephole is connected to a subsurface drainage pipe system that keeps the outlet clear

subject: Garden Wall Drainage / Weepholes
rule: weephole openings must be at least the specified minimum diameter or cross-sectional area
conditions: weepholes are provided in garden retaining walls

subject: Garden Wall Drainage / Weepholes
rule: a permeable drainage aggregate must be placed immediately behind weepholes
conditions: weepholes are installed in a retaining wall
backfill is present
exceptions: wall uses a proprietary drained cavity system with prefabricated drainage composite that meets equivalent performance

subject: Garden Wall Mortar / Jointing
rule: Garden wall mortar / jointing must be lime-based (not Portland cement) in historic or traditional garden walls to allow vapor permeability and prevent trapped moisture from damaging masonry
conditions: wall is historic or traditional construction
wall contains soft or porous masonry units (e.g., soft brick, stone)
exceptions: wall is a modern engineered garden wall designed with sealed systems and impermeable masonry

subject: Garden Wall Mortar / Jointing
rule: Garden wall mortar / jointing must not have a compressive strength exceeding that of the masonry units
exceptions: engineered reinforced garden walls where mortar strength is specifically designed as part of a structural system

subject: Garden Wall Mortar / Jointing
rule: Garden wall mortar joints must be fully filled (no voids or honeycombing) to prevent water ingress and frost damage
exceptions: weep-hole locations intentionally left open for drainage

subject: Garden Wall Mortar / Jointing
rule: Mortar for garden walls must not be applied during freezing temperatures or when frost is expected within 24 hours

subject: Garden Wall Plaster / Render Finish
rule: plaster/render finish must be compatible with the substrate (brick, block, or stone of the garden wall)
conditions: applied to masonry garden wall substrate
exceptions: when a bonding agent or mesh is used to bridge incompatible materials

subject: Garden Wall Plaster / Render Finish
rule: plaster/render finish must be applied over stable, non-moving substrate
conditions: garden wall is subject to frost heave, vibration, or settlement
exceptions: when flexible render systems or movement joints are incorporated

subject: Garden Wall Plaster / Render Finish
rule: plaster/render finish must not trap moisture behind it
conditions: garden wall is exposed to rain or ground moisture
exceptions: when breathable (vapor-permeable) render is used in combination with a drained cavity or waterproofed substrate

subject: Garden Wall Plaster / Render Finish
rule: render finish must have adequate mechanical key or bond to the substrate
conditions: applied directly to a smooth or low-porosity surface
exceptions: when a mechanical mesh reinforcement is fixed to the substrate

subject: Garden Wall with Retaining Function
rule: garden wall with retaining function must resist overturning from lateral earth pressure
conditions: wall retains soil on one side
wall is not laterally supported at top
exceptions: soil height on both sides is equal (no net lateral pressure)

subject: Garden Wall with Retaining Function
rule: garden wall with retaining function must have adequate drainage behind the wall
conditions: wall retains soil
soil type is cohesive or has high water table potential
exceptions: wall retains free-draining granular material with proven negligible hydrostatic pressure

subject: Garden Wall with Retaining Function
rule: garden wall with retaining function must not have a height-to-base-width ratio exceeding the stability limit for the soil and wall type
conditions: wall is freestanding without tiebacks or anchors
exceptions: wall is mechanically anchored or reinforced

subject: Garden Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Garden wall insulation layer must maintain a continuous thermal barrier without gaps or compression
conditions: when installed as part of a garden wall assembly
exceptions: intentional thermal breaks for structural connections

subject: Garden Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Garden wall insulation layer must not be in direct contact with ground moisture without a proper damp-proof barrier
conditions: when the insulation is below grade or in contact with soil
exceptions: closed-cell foam insulation rated for below-grade direct contact
insulation specifically manufactured with integral moisture barrier

subject: Garden Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Garden wall insulation layer must have a fire-resistance rating compatible with the adjacent building elements and occupancy
conditions: when the garden wall is attached to or within close proximity to a habitable building
exceptions: when local building codes explicitly exempt garden walls from fire-resistance requirements

subject: Garden Wall with Pier Cap / Ball Finial
rule: pier cap must provide a weathering surface to shed water away from the wall core
conditions: pier cap is present on top of garden wall

subject: Garden Wall with Pier Cap / Ball Finial
rule: ball finial must not create a water-trapping pocket at its junction with the pier cap
conditions: ball finial is installed on top of pier cap

subject: Garden Wall with Pier Cap / Ball Finial
rule: pier cap must overlap the pier below on all sides

subject: Garden Wall Integrated Planter / Seat
rule: planter must have drainage holes or a drainage path to prevent waterlogging and root rot
conditions: when used as a planter for live plants
exceptions: when used solely as a decorative or dry-laid planter without soil or plants

subject: Garden Wall Integrated Planter / Seat
rule: planter must be waterproofed or lined on the interior surfaces that contact soil and moisture
conditions: when the planter is constructed from porous materials (e.g., concrete, brick, stone)
exceptions: when the material is naturally waterproof (e.g., glazed ceramic, metal, plastic)

subject: Garden Wall Integrated Planter / Seat
rule: planter must not create a lateral moisture bridge into the adjacent wall structure
conditions: when the planter is attached to or integrated into a building wall
exceptions: when a continuous waterproof membrane or physical gap separates planter from the wall structure

subject: Garden Wall Integrated Planter / Seat
rule: seat surface must be structurally adequate for a minimum live load of 1.5 kN (approximately 150 kg per person) concentrated on the seating area
conditions: when the integrated seat is intended for human occupancy
