rule: banquet hall must have at least one means of egress (exit) that leads directly to a public way or safe area
conditions: occupied by more than 50 persons
any occupancy
exceptions: single-story banquet hall with occupant load ≤ 49 may have a single exit if allowed by local code

subject: Banquet Hall
rule: banquet hall ceiling height must not be less than 7 feet 6 inches (2.29 m) in occupiable spaces
conditions: assembly use
new construction
exceptions: existing buildings undergoing minor alteration where code permits reduced height

subject: Banquet Hall
rule: banquet hall must have a fire alarm system if occupant load exceeds 300
conditions: occupant load > 300
exceptions: where occupant load is ≤ 300 and no other code trigger applies

subject: Banquet Hall
rule: banquet hall's floor finish in exit access corridors must have a Class I or Class II flame-spread rating
conditions: floor finish installed in means of egress
exceptions: single-family dwellings (not applicable to banquet halls)
existing compliant finishes

subject: Dining Room (Residential)
rule: dining room floor must support typical residential live loads of at least 40 psf (1.92 kN/m²)
conditions: residential occupancy

subject: Dining Room (Residential)
rule: dining room ceiling height must be at least 2.1 m (7 ft) in habitable spaces
conditions: habitable room
new construction
exceptions: existing buildings under renovation where non-conforming height is permitted by local code

subject: Dining Room (Residential)
rule: dining room must have at least one means of egress directly to a corridor or exit
conditions: dining room larger than 50 m² (540 ft²)
exceptions: if the dining room opens directly to the exterior at grade

subject: Dining Room (Residential)
rule: dining room must not have a floor drain that connects to the sanitary sewer without an air gap or trap primer
conditions: dining room contains a floor drain

subject: Dining Counter / Breakfast Bar
rule: Dining counter / breakfast bar must have a horizontal top surface that is stable under normal use loads

subject: Dining Counter / Breakfast Bar
rule: Dining counter / breakfast bar must not have sharp exposed edges or corners at seated user height that pose a laceration hazard
conditions: when accessible to users

subject: Dining Counter / Breakfast Bar
rule: Dining counter / breakfast bar surface must be cleanable and non-absorbent for food-contact use
conditions: when used for food service

subject: Outdoor Dining Patio / Terrace
rule: the outdoor dining patio/terrace must have a minimum slope of 1% away from the building structure for drainage
conditions: the patio/terrace is uncovered
the patio/terrace is adjacent to a building wall
exceptions: the patio/terrace has an integrated drainage system such as channel drains or floor drains that collect all surface water

subject: Outdoor Dining Patio / Terrace
rule: the outdoor dining patio/terrace surface must be made of slip-resistant materials
conditions: the patio/terrace is accessible to patrons
the patio/terrace can become wet from rain, sprinklers, or cleaning

subject: Outdoor Dining Patio / Terrace
rule: the outdoor dining patio/terrace must not have a drainage point that discharges toward the building foundation
exceptions: the site has a below-grade perimeter drainage system designed to capture and carry away foundation-adjacent water

subject: Built-in Dining Banquette
rule: built-in dining banquette must have a horizontal seat surface that is level (parallel to the floor plane)

subject: Built-in Dining Banquette
rule: built-in dining banquette must have a seat height within the range suitable for dining (typically 430-480 mm from finished floor to seat top)
conditions: when used for standard adult dining

subject: Built-in Dining Banquette
rule: built-in dining banquette must not have sharp or abrasive edges on surfaces exposed to occupant contact

subject: Built-in Dining Banquette
rule: built-in dining banquette must be structurally capable of supporting a distributed live load of at least 1.92 kN/m² (40 psf) for residential occupancy
conditions: when designed for residential use

subject: Dining Chair / Stool (Fixed)
rule: dining chair or fixed stool must have a minimum seat height between 420 mm and 480 mm for comfortable seated dining
conditions: designed for use at a dining table with standard table height (720–760 mm)
exceptions: children's furniture designed for lower table heights
custom accessible seating with documented user requirements

subject: Dining Chair / Stool (Fixed)
rule: dining chair or fixed stool must have a minimum seat width of 400 mm at the front
conditions: intended for adult use
exceptions: space-constrained seating such as stacked or ganging chairs with documented reduced width

subject: Dining Chair / Stool (Fixed)
rule: dining chair or fixed stool must provide a stable base such that the chair does not tip forward when a vertical load of 600 N is applied 50 mm from the front edge of the seat
exceptions: chairs specifically designed for rocking or tilting motion where instability is intentional and within a safe range

subject: Dining Chair / Stool (Fixed)
rule: seat surface must not have sharp edges or protrusions in the area contacted by the user's thighs or buttocks during normal use

subject: Sneeze Guard / Food Shield
rule: Sneeze guard / food shield must be made of transparent material (glass or clear plastic)

subject: Sneeze Guard / Food Shield
rule: Sneeze guard / food shield must have a solid, impermeable barrier panel (no mesh, slats, or open gaps in the protective zone)
exceptions: Airflow gaps at the very bottom or top that do not create a direct line-of-sight droplet path

subject: Sneeze Guard / Food Shield
rule: Sneeze guard / food shield must not have sharp edges or corners at customer-facing or food-facing surfaces

subject: Sneeze Guard / Food Shield
rule: Sneeze guard / food shield must be positioned at a height that blocks the direct mouth-to-food droplet trajectory of a standing person (typically 14-16 inches above the counter)
conditions: installed over a self-serve food counter

subject: Dining Floor Finish
rule: Dining floor finish must be slip-resistant
conditions: when floor is expected to be exposed to food or beverage spills
in dining areas where users walk
exceptions: if the finish is only used on vertical surfaces or baseboards

subject: Dining Floor Finish
rule: Dining floor finish must be cleanable and impervious to moisture and food soils
conditions: in all dining areas where food is served

subject: Dining Floor Finish
rule: Dining floor finish must not produce toxic fumes or reactions under normal cleaning conditions
conditions: when used in enclosed dining spaces

subject: Dining Area HVAC Diffuser / Vent
rule: dining area HVAC diffuser / vent must be positioned to avoid direct airflow onto diners at seating height
conditions: when installed in an occupied dining area
when seating is located within the airflow zone
exceptions: when diffuser is of a non-draft-inducing type (e.g., displacement ventilation with very low velocity)

subject: Dining Area HVAC Diffuser / Vent
rule: dining area HVAC diffuser / vent must not be located directly above a cooking or dishwashing station
conditions: when the diffuser supplies conditioned air (not dedicated exhaust)
when the dining area includes open kitchen or servery elements
exceptions: when the diffuser is specifically designed for grease-laden or humid environments (e.g., stainless steel, cleanable)

subject: Dining Area HVAC Diffuser / Vent
rule: dining area HVAC diffuser / vent must maintain minimum clearance from sprinkler heads
conditions: when fire suppression sprinklers are present in the same ceiling zone

subject: Condiment / Service Station
rule: Condiment / Service Station must have a water-resistant counter surface
conditions: when installed in a food-service area
when intended for dispensing condiments or beverages

subject: Condiment / Service Station
rule: Condiment / Service Station must not have exposed electrical outlets within 300 mm of any dispensing area that is subject to liquid splash
conditions: when the station includes electrical equipment (e.g., refrigeration, warming units)
when dispensing liquids or semi-liquids
exceptions: outlets that are GFCI-protected and fitted with a weatherproof/in-use cover may be permitted in some jurisdictions

subject: Condiment / Service Station
rule: Condiment / Service Station must provide a clear toe-kick or base clearance if the unit is freestanding and accessible to wheelchair users
conditions: when the station is in a publicly accessible space subject to accessibility codes (e.g., ADA in the US)
exceptions: when the station is wall-mounted with no floor contact
when the station is entirely behind a service counter not intended for patron access

subject: Wall Wainscot / Chair Rail (Dining)
rule: Wall wainscot / chair rail must be installed at a height that does not obstruct the wall area reserved for dining table backsplash or artwork
conditions: when a dining table is present along the wall
when the wall wainscot/chair rail is intended as a protective or decorative element in a dining area

subject: Wall Wainscot / Chair Rail (Dining)
rule: Wall wainscot / chair rail must_not be installed at a height that conflicts with electrical outlets or light switches on the same wall
conditions: when the wall contains electrical outlet or switch boxes at standard heights (typically 12–48 inches from finished floor)
exceptions: if the outlets/switches are relocated to clear the wainscot/chair rail band

subject: Wall Wainscot / Chair Rail (Dining)
rule: Wall wainscot / chair rail must be installed on a structurally sound substrate that can accept fasteners or adhesive loads
conditions: when the wainscot/chair rail is mechanically fastened or adhered to the wall
exceptions: free-standing or furred-out installations that do not rely on the existing wall substrate for support

subject: Wall Wainscot / Chair Rail (Dining)
rule: Wall wainscot / chair rail must_not be installed where it creates a tripping hazard at floor transitions
conditions: when the wainscot/chair rail projects more than 1/4 inch from the wall surface at the base
when the wainscot/chair rail extends to or near floor level (e.g., full-height wainscot)

subject: Dining Table Electrical / Data Outlet
rule: A dining table electrical/data outlet must be installed at least 150 mm above the finished floor level
conditions: The outlet is located in a region where floor washing or flooding is possible
The outlet serves a dining table area in a commercial or residential setting

subject: Dining Table Electrical / Data Outlet
rule: A dining table electrical/data outlet must not be positioned directly above a heat source such as an in-table induction cooktop or hot plate
conditions: The dining table incorporates integrated cooking appliances or warming surfaces

subject: Dining Table Electrical / Data Outlet
rule: A dining table electrical/data outlet must have a minimum separation of 75 mm from metallic table framing or structure
conditions: The outlet is integrated into the table structure itself

subject: HVAC Diffuser
rule: HVAC diffuser must be positioned such that its discharge airflow does not directly impinge on occupants in the occupied zone
conditions: diffuser serves an occupied space
diffuser is used for supply air (not exhaust or return)
exceptions: diffuser is in an unoccupied mechanical room or storage space
discharge is directed away from occupants via a directional diffuser or properly designed throw pattern

subject: HVAC Diffuser
rule: HVAC diffuser must not be installed in a location where it will be obstructed by structural elements, furniture, or architectural features that block airflow delivery
conditions: diffuser is mounted in ceiling, wall, or floor for air distribution

subject: HVAC Diffuser
rule: HVAC diffuser must be installed with a clearance distance to ceiling-mounted fire sprinklers that complies with applicable fire code spacing requirements
conditions: diffuser is ceiling-mounted
space is sprinklered
exceptions: diffuser type and layout has been specifically coordinated and approved by fire protection engineer showing adequate sprinkler coverage

subject: HVAC Diffuser
rule: HVAC diffuser must have a neck size and pressure rating compatible with the connected ductwork and system static pressure

subject: Window / Glazed Panel
rule: glazed panel must be made of a material rated for the design wind load
conditions: when the window/glazed panel is part of the building envelope
when the building is in a wind-prone region
exceptions: temporary openings protected by approved shutters rated for wind load

subject: Window / Glazed Panel
rule: window must not be positioned where it serves as an egress window unless it meets minimum clear opening dimensions
conditions: when the window is intended to serve as an emergency escape and rescue opening in a sleeping room or basement
exceptions: when the room has an alternative approved means of egress

subject: Window / Glazed Panel
rule: window must be glazed with safety glazing (tempered or laminated) when located in a hazardous location
conditions: when the window is in a door
when the window is adjacent to a walking surface where the bottom edge is less than 60 inches above the floor
when the window is in a shower or bathtub enclosure

subject: Window / Glazed Panel
rule: window/glazed panel must have a minimum sill height or protective barrier to prevent falls
conditions: when the window is in a wall above grade
when the sill is less than 24 inches above the floor
when the drop to the outside is more than 30 inches
exceptions: windows with fixed opening-limiting devices set to allow no more than 4 inches of opening

subject: Window / Glazed Panel
rule: operable window must not have a head height less than the required egress headroom
conditions: when the window is an operable egress window

subject: Data/Electrical Outlet
rule: electrical outlet must not be installed in a location exposed to direct water spray or immersion
exceptions: outlets rated and listed for wet locations (e.g., Weatherproof WR GFCI) are permitted in direct water exposure areas

subject: Data/Electrical Outlet
rule: electrical outlet must be connected to a branch circuit with appropriate overcurrent protection
conditions: when outlet is part of a permanent wiring installation

subject: Data/Electrical Outlet
rule: electrical outlet must have an enclosure that prevents unintentional contact with live parts
conditions: when outlet is installed and voltage is present

subject: Data/Electrical Outlet
rule: electrical outlet must not be wired with reverse polarity (hot/neutral swapped)

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must provide a clear opening width of at least 32 inches (815 mm) when the door is in the open position
conditions: door is part of a building egress path
door serves an accessible workspace
exceptions: existing buildings where alteration is not feasible and the door serves a space with fewer than 5 occupants

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must be operable with a single effort (one-hand operation) without tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist
conditions: door is on an accessible route
door serves a workspace accessible to the public or employees

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must swing in the direction of egress travel when serving a space with an occupant load of 50 or more
conditions: door serves a room or space with occupant load of 50 or more persons
exceptions: doors serving individual dwelling units

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must have panic hardware or fire exit hardware when serving a space with an occupant load of 50 or more and is equipped with a lock or latch
conditions: door serves a space with occupant load of 50 or more
door is equipped with any locking or latching device
exceptions: doors that are not required egress doors

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must not have a door closer or other device that requires more than 15 lbf (67 N) to operate the door
conditions: door is on an accessible route

subject: Workspace Door
rule: Workspace door must have a door leaf with a nominal thickness of at least 1-3/4 inches (44 mm) when constructed as a fire door assembly
conditions: door is part of a fire-rated assembly
door is constructed of wood or composite material

subject: Built-in Storage Unit
rule: built-in storage unit must be securely fastened to the structure (wall, floor, or ceiling) to prevent tipping or falling
conditions: unit is freestanding and not part of a continuous millwork assembly
exceptions: unit is designed as a removable modular furniture piece with no fixed attachment required by code

subject: Built-in Storage Unit
rule: built-in storage unit must not block required egress paths or emergency access
conditions: unit is located in a corridor, near an exit, or along a means of egress
exceptions: unit is recessed into a wall and does not reduce the clear egress width below code minimums

subject: Built-in Storage Unit
rule: built-in storage unit must have adequate structural support from the host building to carry its own weight plus design live load
conditions: unit is cantilevered, suspended, or unusually heavy (e.g., floor-to-ceiling library with dense contents)
exceptions: unit bears directly on a slab-on-grade or adequately designed floor structure

subject: Privacy Booth
rule: privacy booth must have at least one operable door for user access and egress
conditions: intended for human occupancy

subject: Privacy Booth
rule: privacy booth must have adequate ventilation to maintain safe CO2 and oxygen levels for an occupant
conditions: intended for human occupancy
fully enclosed
exceptions: if occupancy duration is extremely short (e.g., under 30 seconds) and volume is large enough that air exchange is not required

subject: Privacy Booth
rule: privacy booth's interior must be visually opaque from the outside when in use

subject: Privacy Booth
rule: privacy booth must not have interior surfaces that can trap or conceal a person from view during emergency inspection
conditions: installed in a location subject to safety/security sweeps

subject: Privacy Booth
rule: privacy booth must have a means for emergency exit without requiring power
conditions: door is electronically locked or latched

subject: Meeting Room
rule: meeting room must have at least one means of egress (door or unobstructed path to exit)
conditions: room is occupied
room is enclosed

subject: Meeting Room
rule: meeting room must have a minimum ceiling height of at least 2.1 m (7 ft)
conditions: room is intended for occupancy

subject: Meeting Room
rule: meeting room must not have a floor slope exceeding 1:20 (5%)
conditions: room is intended for seated occupancy or presentations
exceptions: raked seating in lecture theatres with stepped floors

subject: Meeting Room
rule: meeting room must have adequate ventilation providing minimum outdoor air supply per occupant
conditions: room is enclosed with no operable windows
exceptions: rooms with operable windows sized to meet ventilation code

subject: Meeting Room
rule: meeting room must have a floor load capacity of at least 2.4 kPa (50 psf) for occupied assembly use

subject: Breakout Space
rule: Breakout space must have at least one means of egress (door or unobstructed opening) to an adjacent circulation space or exit
conditions: Occupied by people
Enclosed by walls or partitions
exceptions: Spaces that are not occupied by people (e.g., storage-only)
Spaces open on at least one full side to a larger space (alcove condition)

subject: Breakout Space
rule: Breakout space must have a minimum clear floor area of at least the applicable building-code minimum for an occupied space of its occupant load
conditions: Intended for occupancy by more than one person
Classified as a habitable or occupied room
exceptions: Spaces classified as alcoves or open-plan adjuncts under local code

subject: Breakout Space
rule: Breakout space must not have a floor level that is below the adjacent exterior grade without adequate waterproofing and drainage
conditions: Located partially or fully below grade
exceptions: Spaces entirely above grade
Spaces that are not occupied (e.g., mechanical rooms)

subject: Kitchen island
rule: kitchen island must have a minimum clearance of at least 36 inches (914 mm) to surrounding cabinets, appliances, or walls on all accessible sides
conditions: island is installed in a residential kitchen
island is intended for food preparation and/or cooking

subject: Kitchen island
rule: kitchen island must have a grounded electrical receptacle installed on the island if the island countertop surface is 12 inches or wider in any dimension
conditions: island countertop width is 12 inches or greater
exceptions: island is purely decorative and has no countertop surface

subject: Kitchen island
rule: kitchen island must not obstruct the work triangle (sink, refrigerator, and primary cooktop) distances beyond allowable limits
conditions: kitchen is designed with a work-triangle layout
exceptions: kitchen uses an alternative layout methodology (e.g., single-wall, galley, or open-plan that does not follow work-triangle principles)

subject: Kitchen island
rule: kitchen island must have a minimum structural support capable of bearing its own weight plus a uniform live load of at least 40 psf (1.92 kN/m²)
conditions: island supports a countertop and is used as a working surface

subject: Kitchen island
rule: kitchen island must have a fire-resistant material barrier if it contains a cooktop or any heat-producing appliance
conditions: island contains a cooktop, warming drawer, or other heat-producing appliance

subject: Preparation counter
rule: preparation counter must have a horizontal work surface that is flat and level
conditions: when used as a food preparation surface
exceptions: counters with integrated cutting boards that create slight depressions

subject: Preparation counter
rule: preparation counter must be at a height suitable for standing or seated tasks without causing ergonomic strain
conditions: when intended for manual work by occupants
exceptions: adjustable-height counters are exempt from a single fixed height requirement

subject: Preparation counter
rule: preparation counter must not have sharp exposed edges or corners in areas where users stand and work
conditions: when located in a public or high-traffic food preparation area
exceptions: counters with deliberately sharp edges for specialized tasks like dough scraping, provided safety warnings are present

subject: Ventilation hood
rule: ventilation hood must be connected to a duct system that terminates outside the building envelope
conditions: when the hood is used for removing combustion products
when the hood is used for removing hazardous fumes
when the hood is installed in a conditioned space
exceptions: recirculating hoods that use charcoal/carbon filtration and are not rated for hazardous or combustion exhaust

subject: Ventilation hood
rule: ventilation hood must not have filters or grease-laden surfaces located directly above an open flame or heat source unless the filter material is non-combustible and rated for the operating temperature
conditions: when the hood is installed over a cooking appliance
when the hood is installed over any appliance with an open flame

subject: Ventilation hood
rule: ventilation hood must maintain a minimum clearance to combustible materials as specified by manufacturer and applicable fire codes
conditions: when installed over a cooking surface or heat-producing appliance

subject: Sink zone
rule: A sink zone must have a floor drain or drainage system capable of handling the maximum expected water flow
conditions: Sink zone is a wet area
Sink zone contains one or more sinks or water fixtures
exceptions: Sink zone is not connected to a potable water supply and is used only for dry activities

subject: Sink zone
rule: Sink zone floor surfaces must be slip-resistant and waterproof
conditions: Sink zone is a wet area with water fixtures
exceptions: Space is used solely as a dry storage zone with no water supply present

subject: Sink zone
rule: Sink zone must not have electrical outlets or switches within 1.8 meters horizontal reach of a sink basin or water source
conditions: Sink zone contains a sink or water fixture
exceptions: Outlets are ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protected and installed per applicable electrical code

subject: Sink zone
rule: Sink zone floor must be sloped toward the drain at a minimum gradient of 1:50
conditions: Sink zone is a commercial or industrial wet area with a floor drain
exceptions: Sink zone has a trench drain system or equivalent engineered drainage that does not rely on floor slope

subject: Cooking layout lighting
rule: cooking task lighting must be positioned to avoid casting shadows on the primary work surface from the cook's body or hands
conditions: when overhead cabinets or the cook's position could block ambient light
exceptions: if the lighting is integrated into the cooktop or hood with a downward-directed low-glare source

subject: Cooking layout lighting
rule: light fixtures over a cooking surface must not be mounted where grease vapour or steam can directly condense onto electrical components
conditions: when the fixture is directly above a gas or electric hob without a range hood interposed
exceptions: if the fixture is IP-rated for wet/grease-laden environments and accessible for cleaning

subject: Cooking layout lighting
rule: cooking layout lighting must provide a minimum of 500 lux at the primary preparation surface under normal operation
conditions: when the space is used for meal preparation
exceptions: none

subject: Cooking layout cabinetry
rule: Cooking layout cabinetry must provide a minimum clear floor space of 40 inches (1016 mm) in front of all cooking appliances
conditions: where cooking appliances are installed within cabinetry
exceptions: Galley kitchens with opposing countertops where the facing countertop itself can serve as the required clear space if it is unencumbered

subject: Cooking layout cabinetry
rule: Cooking layout cabinetry must not have combustible surfaces directly above or within 24 inches (610 mm) horizontally of a cooktop without a range hood or exhaust fan
conditions: where a cooktop is integrated into the cabinetry layout
exceptions: Cabinetry with a metal or noncombustible undersurface directly above the cooktop area

subject: Cooking layout cabinetry
rule: Cooking layout cabinetry must maintain a minimum 18-inch (457 mm) clearance between a wall-mounted microwave and the cooktop surface below
conditions: where a microwave is installed above a cooktop in the cabinetry layout
exceptions: Manufacturer specifications that explicitly allow a lesser clearance and are certified to UL/CSA standards for that configuration

subject: Cooking layout cabinetry
rule: Cooking layout cabinetry must not have a window or other penetrable surface directly behind the cooktop within the splash zone
conditions: where a cooktop is installed with a backsplash wall directly behind it
exceptions: Tempered glass windows rated for high heat and impact located at least 6 inches above the cooktop surface

subject: Cooking layout cabinetry
rule: Cooking layout cabinetry must provide a lateral landing surface of at least 15 inches (381 mm) on at least one side of a cooktop
conditions: where a cooktop is installed
exceptions: Custom accessible kitchen designs where the user transfers from a wheelchair and requires unobstructed side approach space instead

subject: Galley layout
rule: Galley layout must have a clear circulation path between workstations that is at least 36 inches (91 cm) wide
conditions: Used in commercial or institutional kitchens
Layout includes multiple parallel workstations
exceptions: Single-home residential galley kitchens where minimum clearance may be reduced to 30 inches (76 cm)

subject: Galley layout
rule: Galley layout must_not have workstations on both sides if the aisle width is less than the minimum required for safe passage
conditions: Aisle width between parallel counters is below code minimum

subject: Galley layout
rule: Galley layout must have at least one accessible egress clear path from the enclosed corridor to an exit
conditions: Galley aisle length exceeds 12 feet (3.7 m)
Both ends are closed (no through-access)
exceptions: Galley that is open at both ends to adjacent spaces

subject: U-shaped layout
rule: A U-shaped layout must have at least one continuous structural diaphragm connecting the two side wings at the base to resist lateral loads
conditions: Located in seismic or high-wind region
exceptions: Wings are structurally independent with a seismic or expansion joint separating them

subject: U-shaped layout
rule: A U-shaped layout must not have an interior courtyard width less than the height of the enclosing walls when the courtyard is occupied
conditions: Courtyard is designed for occupancy (e.g., people will stand, sit, or walk inside it)
exceptions: Courtyard is strictly a light/ventilation shaft with no occupancy and a grate or barrier preventing fall entry

subject: U-shaped layout
rule: A U-shaped layout must provide a minimum of two means of egress from the interior courtyard
conditions: Courtyard is enclosed on three sides by occupied building wings
exceptions: Courtyard has a direct opening to a public way on the open fourth side with unobstructed path width of at least 1.2 m

subject: Integrated Side/End Tables
rule: integrated side/end tables must be capable of supporting the weight of objects typically placed on them (e.g., lamps, drinks, books) without collapsing or tilting
conditions: when the table is serving its intended function as a side or end table

subject: Integrated Side/End Tables
rule: integrated side/end tables must not have sharp corners or edges that pose a laceration or impact hazard at typical table height
conditions: when accessible to occupants in normal use

subject: Integrated Side/End Tables
rule: integrated side/end tables must be stable on a level floor surface without tipping under typical lateral forces
conditions: when placed on a level floor surface

subject: Fixed Auditorium/Stadium Seating
rule: fixed auditorium/stadium seating must have a minimum clear sightline from every seat to the performance/field area, calculated from the eye position of the seated spectator
conditions: seating rows are tiered or stepped
seating is oriented toward a stage or field

subject: Fixed Auditorium/Stadium Seating
rule: fixed auditorium/stadium seating must comply with local building code minimum egress aisle width and maximum travel distance to an exit
conditions: seating capacity exceeds the threshold defined by local code

subject: Fixed Auditorium/Stadium Seating
rule: fixed auditorium/stadium seating must have a step or handrail at any change in level that exceeds the riser-height limit defined by applicable building code
conditions: seating rows are stepped or tiered

subject: Fixed Auditorium/Stadium Seating
rule: fixed auditorium/stadium seating must not have any seat whose row-access path is narrower than the minimum clear width required by code for accessible means of egress
conditions: seating is in a public assembly venue subject to accessibility regulations

subject: Fixed Auditorium/Stadium Seating
rule: fixed auditorium/stadium seating must have seats positively attached to the structure or floor to resist overturning under design lateral loads (seismic or wind)
conditions: seating is in a seismically active or high-wind region
seats are not continuous benches but individual or discrete seating units

subject: Reception/Concierge Desk
rule: reception/concierge desk must be positioned such that it has direct line-of-sight to all public entry points it is intended to monitor
conditions: desk is staffed
desk serves a security or greeting function
exceptions: building has electronic access control and CCTV monitoring covering all entry points

subject: Reception/Concierge Desk
rule: reception/concierge desk must not block required egress pathways or reduce corridor clear width below building code minimum
conditions: desk is located in a circulation path
desk is adjacent to an exit route

subject: Reception/Concierge Desk
rule: reception/concierge desk work surface height must comply with accessibility standards for a forward-approach work surface
conditions: desk is intended for public interaction with wheelchair users
exceptions: a separate accessible counter or lowered section is provided elsewhere at the same desk

subject: Modular Platform/Deck Base
rule: Modular Platform/Deck Base must have load capacity rated for the intended deck or equipment live load (e.g., 40 psf residential, 100 psf commercial, or as per local code)
conditions: When used as a structural walking/work surface
When supporting equipment or occupancy loads
exceptions: If the platform is decorative only and clearly marked as non-load-bearing

subject: Modular Platform/Deck Base
rule: Modular Platform/Deck Base must be secured against lateral movement (sliding or tipping) under design lateral loads
conditions: When installed at grade or on a roof
When subject to wind, seismic, or slope forces
exceptions: If the platform rests fully within a recessed well that prevents all lateral displacement through contact with surrounding structure

subject: Modular Platform/Deck Base
rule: Modular Platform/Deck Base must not have gaps or openings that allow a 4-inch sphere to pass through in walking areas
conditions: When intended for pedestrian access or occupancy above grade (e.g., elevated more than 12 inches)
exceptions: If the platform is at ground level and not a walking surface
If the gap is part of a designed drainage feature that cannot capture a person's foot (e.g., slotted drains with bars ≤ 4 in spacing)

subject: Sitting Circle Floor Finish
rule: sitting circle floor finish must be slip-resistant
conditions: surface is intended for pedestrian traffic
finish may be exposed to moisture or spills
exceptions: finish is a sacrificial temporary covering removed before use

subject: Sitting Circle Floor Finish
rule: sitting circle floor finish must be stable under foot traffic and seating loads

subject: Sitting Circle Floor Finish
rule: sitting circle floor finish must not generate hazardous projections or sharp edges

subject: Railing/Guardrail System
rule: railing/guardrail system must have a top rail height between 36 and 42 inches above the walking surface for residential applications, and 42 inches for commercial/industrial applications
conditions: applies to all guardrail installations where a fall hazard exists
exceptions: existing structures where code has grandfathering provisions
certain agricultural or industrial exempted areas

subject: Railing/Guardrail System
rule: railing/guardrail system must have intermediate rails or infill such that a 4-inch diameter sphere cannot pass through any opening
conditions: applies to all guardrail systems with openings

subject: Railing/Guardrail System
rule: railing/guardrail system must withstand a concentrated load of 200 pounds applied in any direction at any point on the top rail
conditions: applies to all guardrail systems

subject: Railing/Guardrail System
rule: railing/guardrail system must not have ladder-effect horizontal rails on the open side that could facilitate climbing by children
conditions: applies in child-occupied facilities such as schools, daycare centers, and residential applications typically enforced

subject: Railing/Guardrail System
rule: railing/guardrail system must have handrail gripping surface that is continuous and provides adequate graspability (circular cross-section 1.25 to 2 inches diameter, or equivalent non-circular)
conditions: applies where the top rail also serves as a handrail on stairs or ramps

subject: Step/Tread Construction
rule: each tread must have a slip-resistant surface or finish
conditions: when used as an outdoor step
when used in wet areas
when used in public buildings
exceptions: treads that are intentionally designed for drainage without slip-resistant coating but with textured surface patterns achieving equivalent slip resistance

subject: Step/Tread Construction
rule: all tread steps in a single flight must have uniform riser height
conditions: for any stair or step flight consisting of two or more risers
exceptions: the bottom or top riser may vary by no more than the tolerances specified in applicable building code (typically ≤ 3/8 inch / 9.5 mm deviation)

subject: Step/Tread Construction
rule: each tread must have a minimum tread depth
conditions: for stair treads serving occupiable spaces
exceptions: winders or spiral stairs where minimum depth is measured at the walk line per code

subject: Step/Tread Construction
rule: the nosing projection of each tread must not exceed the maximum permitted dimension
conditions: when treads have projecting nosings
exceptions: treads without projecting nosings (flush riser/tread interfaces are exempt)

subject: Sitting Circle Framing Structure
rule: Sitting Circle Framing Structure must form a complete, continuous ring to maintain structural stability
conditions: The structure is a circular sitting area

subject: Sitting Circle Framing Structure
rule: Sitting Circle Framing Structure must not have individual spans that exceed the material's bending or shear capacity
conditions: Structure is made of a material with finite bending/shear strength

subject: Sitting Circle Framing Structure
rule: Sitting Circle Framing Structure must transfer all applied loads (self-weight + live load) to its foundation or supporting structure without exceeding soil or support bearing capacity

subject: Sitting Circle Framing Structure
rule: Sitting Circle Framing Structure must have connections that resist the forces and moments demanded by the ring geometry (radial thrust, tangential shear, potential overturning)
conditions: Structure uses discrete members joined at nodes rather than a monolithic form

subject: Sitting Circle Framing Structure
rule: Sitting Circle Framing Structure must not have a slenderness ratio (in any member) that permits buckling under design loads
conditions: Members are slender relative to their cross-section

subject: Landscaped/Green Sitting Circle
rule: seating surface must be level and stable
conditions: used for sitting
exceptions: intentional rocking or moving furniture designed for dynamic seating

subject: Landscaped/Green Sitting Circle
rule: ground surface within the circle must be accessible per applicable accessibility codes
conditions: publicly accessible space

subject: Landscaped/Green Sitting Circle
rule: planted or green materials must have a means of irrigation or natural water access
conditions: contains living plantings
exceptions: use of only drought-tolerant/xeriscape species that can survive on local rainfall with no supplementary water

subject: Landscaped/Green Sitting Circle
rule: seating must not have sharp edges or protrusions at user contact points
conditions: includes built-in or fixed seating elements

subject: Fireplace/Hearth Circle
rule: A fireplace/hearth must have a non-combustible floor ember protection extending a minimum of 18 inches (460 mm) in front of the hearth opening and at least 12 inches (300 mm) beyond each side of the opening if the hearth is elevated less than 6 inches above the floor
conditions: fireplace/hearth circle is installed on a combustible floor
exceptions: hearth is elevated 6 inches or more above the floor, reducing required ember protection

subject: Fireplace/Hearth Circle
rule: A fireplace/hearth must have a chimney or flue that terminates above the roof line at a height compliant with the 10-2-3 rule (at least 2 feet higher than any portion of the building within 10 feet)
conditions: fireplace/hearth circle is a wood-burning or solid-fuel fireplace
exceptions: electric or gas fireplace that is ventless (zero-clearance sealed combustion unit certified for direct venting may have different termination requirements)

subject: Fireplace/Hearth Circle
rule: A fireplace hearth must not be constructed of combustible materials directly in contact with the fire
exceptions: factory-built zero-clearance fireplaces with listed non-combustible hearth extension assemblies

subject: Lecture/Tiered Teaching Circle
rule: Tiered seating (raked floor) must have a minimum aisle width of 900mm to meet egress/accessibility code
conditions: space has fixed tiered seating
seating capacity exceeds 50 persons
exceptions: non-fixed seating setup where seating can be reconfigured

subject: Lecture/Tiered Teaching Circle
rule: Tiered seating rows must have a maximum riser height of 200mm (approx 8 inches) between rows
conditions: fixed tiered seating is present
exceptions: handicapped-access platforms with ramp access may have alternative riser configurations as per local codes

subject: Lecture/Tiered Teaching Circle
rule: The room must have at least two separate means of egress if occupant load exceeds 49 persons
conditions: occupant load exceeds 49 persons
exceptions: sprinklered buildings may allow exceptions per local code variance

subject: Lecture/Tiered Teaching Circle
rule: The slope of any ramp serving tiered seating must not exceed 1:12 gradient
conditions: ramp provides access to or within tiered seating area
exceptions: existing structures under historical preservation may have grandfather clause allowances per local authority

subject: Dormitory Room
rule: dormitory room must have at least one operable window or mechanical ventilation that provides a minimum of 5 air changes per hour
conditions: room has no direct door to outdoors
exceptions: rooms with balanced mechanical ventilation meeting ASHRAE 62.1 minimum rates

subject: Dormitory Room
rule: dormitory room must have a door that can be opened from the inside without a key or special knowledge
conditions: room is an individual sleeping unit

subject: Dormitory Room
rule: dormitory room must not have a floor drain that connects directly to the sanitary sewer without a trap
conditions: room contains a bathroom or wet area within the unit

subject: Dormitory Room
rule: dormitory room must have a smoke alarm or smoke detector installed within the room

subject: Dormitory Room
rule: dormitory room must have a minimum ceiling height of at least 2.13 m (7 ft 0 in) over at least 50% of the floor area
exceptions: rooms that are existing and legally non-conforming under applicable code

subject: Bunk Bed System
rule: bunk bed ladder or access point must be positioned to allow safe climbing without obstruction from the bed frame above
conditions: bunk bed has a ladder or climbing aid
exceptions: bed is a loft bed with an alternative access such as stairs or a railed landing

subject: Bunk Bed System
rule: distance between the top bunk mattress surface and the ceiling or any overhead obstruction must be sufficient for a seated occupant to avoid head injury
conditions: bunk bed is installed indoors under a ceiling
exceptions: bed is specifically designed as a low-profile children's bunk where manufacturer explicitly warns against sitting up

subject: Bunk Bed System
rule: guardrail on the top bunk must extend above the mattress surface by a height that prevents a sleeping occupant from rolling off
conditions: top bunk is above lower bunk or floor
exceptions: bed is a single-story loft bed with no uppermost sleeping surface requiring a rail

subject: Bunk Bed System
rule: bunk bed must not have sharp edges or protrusions at head or knee height where an occupant could impact them during normal use

subject: Privacy Curtain Track System
rule: Privacy curtain track system must be structurally supported by a ceiling, wall, or overhead structure capable of bearing the combined weight of the track, curtains, and dynamic loading from operation
conditions: The system is installed in any building or enclosure
exceptions: Tension-based cable systems that bear loads entirely on floor-anchored endpoints with no intermediate support from overhead structure

subject: Privacy Curtain Track System
rule: Privacy curtain track must not be installed where it obstructs required fire egress paths or emergency exit access
conditions: The system is installed in a means of egress corridor, doorway, or path required by building code
exceptions: The track is designed to automatically retract or break away under minimal force in the direction of egress

subject: Privacy Curtain Track System
rule: Privacy curtain track fire barrier rating must match or exceed the fire-resistance rating of the wall or partition in which it is installed if the track penetrates the barrier
conditions: The track or its mounting penetrates a fire-rated wall or partition assembly
exceptions: The penetration is fully sealed with an approved firestop system maintaining the wall rating

subject: Communal Locker Unit
rule: communal locker unit must be located in a publicly accessible area
exceptions: if the unit serves a private residential cluster with restricted access

subject: Communal Locker Unit
rule: communal locker unit must have a minimum clear floor area in front of each locker door for user access

subject: Communal Locker Unit
rule: communal locker unit must not block emergency egress paths
conditions: when installed in a corridor
when installed near an exit door

subject: Communal Locker Unit
rule: communal locker unit must be anchored to the floor or wall to prevent tip-over
conditions: when the unit height exceeds 1.2 m

subject: Bed Frame
rule: bed frame must have a flat and level surface to support the mattress
exceptions: adjustable beds where the frame articulates

subject: Bed Frame
rule: bed frame must have a load capacity at least equal to the combined weight of the mattress and expected occupants

subject: Bed Frame
rule: bed frame must not have sharp edges or protrusions in areas accessible to occupants
conditions: at heights and locations where a person's limbs or head can contact them during normal use

subject: Bed Frame
rule: slats or mattress support must be spaced such that the mattress does not sag through the gaps
conditions: when the bed frame uses slats rather than a solid platform

subject: Bed Frame
rule: bed frame must be stable against tipping when lateral force is applied at the top edge

subject: Sleeping Platform Railing
rule: sleeping platform railing must have vertical balusters or infill spaced no more than 100mm (4 inches) apart
conditions: when the railing is in a sleeping platform intended for children under 6 years old
when the railing is in a jurisdiction that follows the 100mm sphere rule (e.g., IRC, BCA)
exceptions: if the railing uses solid sheet panels instead of balusters
if the railing is entirely at floor level with no drop hazard on the other side

subject: Sleeping Platform Railing
rule: sleeping platform railing must withstand a concentrated horizontal load of at least 0.5 kN applied at any point
conditions: when the railing is designed for residential use

subject: Sleeping Platform Railing
rule: sleeping platform railing must have a minimum height of 900mm (approx 36 inches) measured from the walking surface
conditions: when the platform floor is more than 600mm above the adjacent surface

subject: Sleeping Platform Railing
rule: sleeping platform railing must not have horizontal members that could be used as a climbing ladder by children
conditions: when the sleeping platform is intended for use by children under 10 years
when the gap between horizontal members is within a range that allows footholds
exceptions: if the horizontal members are on the interior side and the sleeping platform is only accessible to adults

subject: Footboard
rule: footboard must be securely fastened to the bed frame or wall

subject: Footboard
rule: footboard must not have sharp edges or protruding hardware at heights accessible to occupants
conditions: when used in a residential bed

subject: Footboard
rule: footboard must not reduce the clear interior length of the mattress support below the minimum required for the intended mattress size

subject: Under-bed Storage Drawers
rule: under-bed storage drawers must have a clearance gap between the drawer top and the bed frame/box spring above to prevent friction and jamming
conditions: drawers are installed under a bed with a fixed frame height
drawers are on casters or sliders requiring vertical space
exceptions: custom bed frames with integrated drawer systems where clearance is built into the frame design

subject: Under-bed Storage Drawers
rule: under-bed storage drawers must not exceed the available under-bed height minus required clearance
conditions: bed frame height is fixed

subject: Under-bed Storage Drawers
rule: under-bed storage drawers must have a mechanism to prevent the drawer from being pulled fully out and dropping
conditions: drawers are on slides or casters without a fixed track
exceptions: drawers designed to be fully removable intentionally

subject: Wall Paneling Behind Bed
rule: Wall paneling behind a bed must be securely fixed to the wall framing or solid backing
conditions: Panel material is rigid (e.g., wood, MDF, tile)
Bed is in normal residential or hospitality occupancy
exceptions: Freestanding headboard not fixed to wall

subject: Wall Paneling Behind Bed
rule: Wall paneling behind a bed must not have sharp protruding edges or corners at head height
conditions: Paneling extends into the zone within 1.0 m above mattress surface
exceptions: Edge is chamfered, rounded, or covered with a padded/soft material

subject: Wall Paneling Behind Bed
rule: Wall paneling behind a bed must not block or impede the operation of electrical outlets or light switches serving the bed area
conditions: Electrical boxes are present on the wall behind the bed position
exceptions: Outlets/switches have been relocated to an accessible adjacent surface
Paneling incorporates a flush, operable access door

subject: Sleeping Platform/Deck
rule: sleeping platform or deck must have a load-bearing structure capable of supporting at least one adult human weight (assumed 100 kg or 220 lbs) plus bedding
conditions: when used for sleeping
exceptions: decorative platforms not intended for occupancy

subject: Sleeping Platform/Deck
rule: sleeping platform or deck must have a horizontal or near-horizontal surface that prevents the occupant from rolling off during sleep
conditions: when intended for sleeping at heights above ground level
exceptions: if a restraint system (e.g., rail, guard, tiedown) is provided to prevent falls

subject: Sleeping Platform/Deck
rule: sleeping platform must not have gaps or openings larger than 120 mm (approx. 4.75 in) between decking members in the area where a sleeping person lies
conditions: when the platform is raised above ground and used for sleeping
exceptions: if a mattress or continuous covering bridges all gaps for the full sleeping area

subject: Sleeping Platform/Deck
rule: sleeping platform must be constructed from materials that are not slippery when wet if exposed to weather
conditions: when the platform is outdoors or subject to moisture
exceptions: if the platform is fully sheltered from rain or dew

subject: Bed Alcove Structure
rule: bed alcove structure must have a minimum clear opening width of at least 600 mm for emergency egress
conditions: when the alcove is used as a sleeping space
when the alcove is in a dwelling unit
exceptions: when the alcove is not a legal sleeping room

subject: Bed Alcove Structure
rule: bed alcove structure must have a minimum ceiling height of at least 2.0 m over at least 50% of the floor area
conditions: when the alcove is designated as a habitable space
exceptions: when local building code permits lower ceiling heights for alcoves under sloped roofs

subject: Bed Alcove Structure
rule: bed alcove structure must not block the path of egress from the main room it adjoins
conditions: when the alcove opens directly into a required means of egress pathway
exceptions: when a separate egress path exists from the alcove itself

subject: Bed Alcove Ceiling
rule: bed alcove ceiling must have a maximum height limit to ensure proper fire sprinkler clearance
conditions: when the bed alcove ceiling is part of a fire sprinkler-protected building
exceptions: buildings not required to have fire sprinklers

subject: Bed Alcove Ceiling
rule: bed alcove ceiling must not have a horizontal dimension that creates an enclosed space requiring emergency escape and rescue opening
conditions: when the alcove depth exceeds typical closet depth thresholds defined by code
exceptions: when the alcove is provided with an alternative means of egress or is less than the code-defined size threshold

subject: Bed Alcove Floor
rule: bed alcove floor must be level within allowable tolerances to prevent occupant rolling or discomfort
conditions: when used as a sleeping surface
exceptions: intentionally sloped designs for specific therapeutic or ergonomic purposes

subject: Bed Alcove Floor
rule: bed alcove floor must have sufficient structural load capacity to support the intended live load of a bed plus occupants

subject: Bed Alcove Floor
rule: bed alcove floor must not have unprotected openings or gaps larger than building code allowance adjacent to the sleeping area
conditions: when elevated above grade
exceptions: guardrails or barriers provided per code

subject: Built-in Bed Platform
rule: Built-in bed platform must have load-rated structural support capable of sustaining static live load of at least 40 psf (1.9 kPa) plus the weight of mattress and occupants
conditions: Used for sleeping or reclining

subject: Built-in Bed Platform
rule: Built-in bed platform must not have sharp edges, protruding hardware, or unradiused corners at head/body contact height
conditions: Accessible to occupants during sleep or rest
exceptions: Deliberate therapeutic or medical devices where risk is offset by clinical benefit

subject: Built-in Bed Platform
rule: Built-in bed platform must provide adequate ventilation or a slatted/ perforated surface to prevent moisture entrapment between mattress and platform
conditions: Solid (non-slatted) platform surface used with a standard mattress
exceptions: Mattress specifically designed for solid platforms with integrated ventilation channels

subject: Bed Alcove Electrical Outlets
rule: Bed alcove electrical outlets must be at least 6 feet (1.83m) away from the edge of any water source (e.g., sink, shower, bathtub) located within the same room or space
conditions: The bed alcove is located in a room that contains a sink, shower, or bathtub
exceptions: Outlets protected by a GFCI device may be placed closer than 6 feet but must still comply with local electrical code minimum distances

subject: Bed Alcove Electrical Outlets
rule: Bed alcove electrical outlets must be tamper-resistant (TR) type
conditions: The bed alcove is intended for occupancy by children, or the building jurisdiction requires tamper-resistant outlets in all habitable rooms per NEC 406.12
exceptions: Outlets installed above 5.5 feet from the floor in the alcove are exempt from tamper-resistance requirements

subject: Bed Alcove Electrical Outlets
rule: Bed alcove electrical outlets must not be installed behind a permanently fixed headboard or bed frame that prevents physical access to the outlet
conditions: The alcove is designed to accommodate a fixed bed installation where the headboard or frame is built-in or permanently affixed

subject: Bed Alcove Curtain Track
rule: Bed alcove curtain track must be securely fastened to a structural substrate (wall, ceiling, or framing member) capable of supporting the curtain and track load
conditions: When the curtain track is installed in a functional bed alcove
exceptions: Freestanding or tension-mounted curtain systems that do not rely on structural fastening

subject: Bed Alcove Curtain Track
rule: Bed alcove curtain track must be mounted with a minimum clearance from the bed surface to avoid interference with sleeping occupants
conditions: When the curtain is intended to close fully across the alcove opening

subject: Bed Alcove Curtain Track
rule: Bed alcove curtain track must not be installed where it obstructs required egress from the bed alcove
conditions: When the bed alcove is the only means of exit from a sleeping area
exceptions: If the track is designed to break away or retract under emergency force

subject: Alcove Bed
rule: An alcove bed must have a minimum clearance of at least 24 inches (610 mm) between the top of the mattress surface and the ceiling or soffit above
conditions: The alcove has a ceiling or soffit above the bed area

subject: Alcove Bed
rule: The alcove opening must be at least wide enough to allow a standard mattress to be inserted and removed
conditions: The bed is built into a fully enclosed alcove with fixed walls on three sides
exceptions: If the alcove bed is designed as a piece of furniture that can be disassembled or slid out

subject: Alcove Bed
rule: An alcove bed must not block required means of egress from the room
conditions: The room containing the alcove bed is a bedroom or sleeping room
exceptions: If the alcove is not in a path to the exit door

subject: Alcove Bed
rule: The alcove bed platform must be capable of supporting the design live load for sleeping areas (typically 40 psf residential)

subject: Bed Alcove Smoke Detector
rule: Bed alcove smoke detector must be located on the ceiling or on the wall within 12 inches of the ceiling
conditions: detector is installed in a bed alcove
exceptions: when manufacturer installation instructions specify a different placement that still meets code compliance

subject: Bed Alcove Smoke Detector
rule: Bed alcove smoke detector must not be installed within 36 inches of a bathroom door
conditions: bathroom is adjacent to the bed alcove
bathroom contains a shower or bathtub

subject: Bed Alcove Smoke Detector
rule: Bed alcove smoke detector must not be installed in dead air spaces such as the peak of a vaulted ceiling where air is stagnant
conditions: alcove ceiling is vaulted, cathedral, or has a peak geometry

subject: Bed Alcove Smoke Detector
rule: Bed alcove smoke detector must be wired to the building's fire alarm or dedicated smoke detection circuit with backup battery power
conditions: detector is hardwired type (not battery-only)
building is new construction or undergoing electrical renovation

subject: Bed Alcove Emergency Egress Window
rule: bed alcove emergency egress window must provide a clear opening area of at least 0.38 m² (as per building codes for sleeping room egress windows)
conditions: window serves as required emergency escape and rescue opening from a sleeping alcove
exceptions: window opens directly to a public way or to a yard/court that provides safe passage
sprinkler system installed per NFPA 13 throughout the building

subject: Bed Alcove Emergency Egress Window
rule: bed alcove emergency egress window must have a sill height no more than 1100 mm (approximately 44 inches) above the floor
conditions: window is the required egress route from a sleeping alcove
alcove floor is finished and usable for standing/crawling
exceptions: window serves as secondary egress with a fixed ladder or step beneath window sill
occupant is provided with an alternative compliant egress path

subject: Bed Alcove Emergency Egress Window
rule: bed alcove emergency egress window must have a minimum net clear opening width of at least 500 mm (approximately 20 inches)
conditions: window is used as the primary or required emergency escape opening
exceptions: alternative compliant egress opening of equivalent size is provided within the alcove

subject: Bed Alcove Emergency Egress Window
rule: bed alcove emergency egress window must not require abnormal physical effort or tools to open from the inside without key or special knowledge
conditions: window is installed in a bedroom alcove intended for sleeping occupancy
exceptions: window serves a non-egress function and a separate compliant egress window exists
building is equipped with automatic fire suppression system and alternative egress path

subject: Wardrobe/Closet
rule: wardrobe/closet must have a door or opening that provides access to the interior storage volume
conditions: when the wardrobe/closet is a built-in or freestanding enclosed unit intended for storage access
exceptions: the wardrobe/closet is purely decorative and not intended for functional storage access
the wardrobe/closet is a display-only case with sealed interior

subject: Wardrobe/Closet
rule: wardrobe/closet must have a floor or base that is structurally capable of supporting the weight of stored items
conditions: when the wardrobe/closet is intended to hold clothing, shoes, or other stored goods on its base surface
exceptions: the wardrobe/closet is wall-mounted and all stored weight is transferred through wall attachment rather than a floor panel

subject: Wardrobe/Closet
rule: wardrobe/closet must not have shelves or hanging rods placed at a vertical spacing that prevents the intended storage item from fitting
conditions: when the wardrobe/closet includes fixed shelves or hanging rods intended for specific categories of items (e.g., hanging garments, folded clothes)
exceptions: the spacing is adjustable by the user
the wardrobe/closet is designed for a specific non-standard item size

subject: Built-in Shelving
rule: built-in shelving must be structurally attached to the building structure
conditions: installed as a fixed component
not freestanding/furniture

subject: Built-in Shelving
rule: built-in shelving must have a minimum depth-to-height ratio that prevents overturning under design lateral loads
conditions: attached to wall only (not also floor- or ceiling-supported)
height exceeds 4 times depth at base

subject: Built-in Shelving
rule: built-in shelving must not block required means of egress or fire sprinkler coverage
conditions: located in a corridor
located near a required exit
located below a sprinkler head
exceptions: if sufficient clearance is maintained per applicable building code (e.g., minimum 36-inch corridor width, 18-inch sprinkler head clearance)

subject: Built-in Shelving
rule: shelving material and finish must have a flame-spread rating compliant with local building code for the occupancy type
conditions: located in a commercial, institutional, or multi-family residential building
occupancy type requires interior finish classification
exceptions: single-family detached dwellings where code does not mandate finish classification for shelving

subject: Full-Length Mirror
rule: full-length mirror must be mounted to a structurally adequate wall or support system capable of bearing its weight
conditions: mirror is wall-mounted
mirror weight exceeds what adhesive alone can support
exceptions: mirror weighs less than 5 kg and uses only adhesive mounting rated for its weight

subject: Full-Length Mirror
rule: full-length mirror must not be installed where its location creates a safety hazard such as obstructing egress paths, emergency exits, or stairway landings
conditions: mirror is installed in a circulation or egress zone
exceptions: local building codes explicitly permit mirrors adjacent to egress paths with sufficient clearance

subject: Full-Length Mirror
rule: full-length mirror must have a shatter-resistant backing or safety film if installed in a location subject to impact or in a commercial occupancy with high pedestrian traffic
conditions: mirror is located in a gymnasium, dance studio, retail fitting room, school, or other high-impact or high-traffic area
mirror glass is larger than 0.5 m²
exceptions: mirror is made of acrylic or polycarbonate instead of glass
local codes do not require safety glazing for mirrors in the specific occupancy

subject: Dressing Room Ventilation
rule: Dressing room ventilation must provide a minimum outdoor air supply rate of 5 cfm per person or meet applicable local building code requirements
conditions: dressing room is occupied by people
dressing room is enclosed/indoor space
exceptions: dressing room is designed as an unoccupied storage-only space

subject: Dressing Room Ventilation
rule: Dressing room exhaust ventilation must not be directly recirculated into the same space without sufficient filtration
conditions: ventilation system reuses or recirculates extracted air
dressing room is mechanically ventilated
exceptions: recirculation air is passed through HEPA or MERV-13+ filtration

subject: Dressing Room Ventilation
rule: Dressing room ventilation system must maintain negative pressure relative to adjacent occupied spaces
conditions: dressing room contains toilet or shower facilities

subject: His-and-Hers Split Layout
rule: The His-and-Hers Split Layout must provide separate and distinct spatial zones for each occupant that are physically partitioned or clearly delineated
conditions: The layout is intended for two occupants who require privacy from one another
exceptions: Temporary or short-duration occupancy where occupants consent to shared space

subject: His-and-Hers Split Layout
rule: Each split zone in the His-and-Hers Layout must have its own independent access or egress path that does not require passing through the other occupant's zone
conditions: The layout is intended for simultaneous occupancy by both parties
exceptions: Studio-style split layouts where the only separation is visual or partial-height partitioning

subject: His-and-Hers Split Layout
rule: The split must not create any dead-end or trapped zone where an occupant has only one exit path that is controlled by or passes through the other occupant's zone
conditions: The layout serves as a dwelling unit or occupied space subject to building code
exceptions: Non-habitable accessory spaces such as storage closets within each zone

subject: Walk-In Dressing Room
rule: Walk-In Dressing Room must have at least one means of entry/exit (doorway or open threshold) that allows a person to enter and exit without obstruction

subject: Walk-In Dressing Room
rule: Walk-In Dressing Room must have a floor that can support the static load of at least one standing adult and any stored clothing/furnishings

subject: Walk-In Dressing Room
rule: Walk-In Dressing Room must not have a ceiling height lower than the minimum required for a standing adult to enter and move within the space (typically 2.0 m minimum clear height)

subject: Walk-In Dressing Room
rule: Walk-In Dressing Room must have adequate ventilation to prevent moisture buildup and mold growth
conditions: space is enclosed on all sides
space has no direct exterior wall opening
exceptions: space is naturally ventilated via open doorway to conditioned interior space

subject: Dressing Room Partition Wall
rule: Dressing room partition wall must be self-supporting or laterally braced to prevent overturning
conditions: Used as a freestanding partition not connected to primary structure at top
exceptions: When partition wall is full-height and connected to structure at both floor and ceiling/roof diaphragm

subject: Dressing Room Partition Wall
rule: Dressing room partition wall must have a minimum thickness or material stiffness to avoid excessive deflection under expected lateral loads
conditions: Used in a public or high-traffic occupancy setting

subject: Stepped Ceiling
rule: A stepped ceiling must be structurally self-supporting or supported by an independent structural frame; it cannot rely on the ceiling finish alone for load-bearing capacity.
conditions: any stepped ceiling configuration
exceptions: If the stepped ceiling is purely decorative and suspended from a separate overhead structure that bears all loads

subject: Stepped Ceiling
rule: A stepped ceiling must not create an enclosed, unventilated void between ceiling layers that cannot be accessed for fire safety, condensation control, or maintenance.
conditions: stepped ceiling with multiple stacked or overlapped planes that produce concealed cavities
exceptions: If the void is intentionally designed as a plenum with proper fire-rated construction, ventilation, and access panels

subject: Sloped Ceiling
rule: sloped ceiling must have a minimum slope of 1:4 (14 degrees) to ensure proper drainage and prevent ponding
conditions: when the sloped ceiling is the roof
when exposed to precipitation
exceptions: when a separate roof structure provides drainage above the ceiling

subject: Sloped Ceiling
rule: sloped ceiling must not have a slope less than 1:12 (approximately 4.8 degrees) when serving as the roof
conditions: when the sloped ceiling is the roof
exceptions: when a secondary waterproof membrane and drainage system is provided

subject: Sloped Ceiling
rule: sloped ceiling finish materials must not be incompatible with the ceiling slope (e.g., loose granular finishes must not be used on slopes exceeding the material's angle of repose)
conditions: when finish materials are applied directly to the sloped surface
exceptions: when mechanical fastening or adhesive systems are designed for the specific slope

subject: Sawtooth Ceiling
rule: Sawtooth ceiling glazing must be oriented away from prevailing wind-driven rain to prevent water infiltration
conditions: sawtooth ceiling includes glazed apertures
building is located in a region with prevailing wind-driven rain
exceptions: glazing is rated for high-pressure water penetration resistance

subject: Sawtooth Ceiling
rule: Sawtooth ceiling valleys must have a positive slope toward drainage outlets with no standing water allowed
conditions: sawtooth configuration creates valley gutters between adjacent sawteeth

subject: Sawtooth Ceiling
rule: Sawtooth ceiling structural ridge must not be lower than the adjacent valley gutter

subject: Room Enclosure Surfaces
rule: room enclosure surfaces must be continuous and weathertight to prevent uncontrolled air and water infiltration
conditions: for exterior enclosure surfaces
for surfaces separating conditioned from unconditioned spaces
exceptions: intentional openings with controlled assemblies such as windows, doors, vents, and louvers

subject: Room Enclosure Surfaces
rule: room enclosure surfaces must have a continuous air barrier aligned with the thermal barrier
conditions: for exterior walls and roofs forming the building envelope

subject: Room Enclosure Surfaces
rule: room enclosure surfaces that are opaque must not have penetrations that bypass the vapor or moisture control layer
conditions: for opaque wall, roof, and floor assemblies
exceptions: sealed penetrations for services that maintain continuity of the control layers

subject: Room Enclosure Surfaces
rule: room enclosure surfaces must be structurally capable of resisting design wind loads and impact loads
conditions: for all exterior enclosure surfaces
exceptions: temporary surfaces during construction only

subject: Room Enclosure Surfaces
rule: room enclosure surfaces must not use materials that create a galvanic corrosion risk when in contact with dissimilar metals in the assembly
conditions: where metal components are part of or contact the enclosure surface assembly
exceptions: where an effective dielectric break is provided between dissimilar metals

subject: Indoor Spatial Zones
rule: indoor spatial zones must be enclosed by fire-resistance-rated assemblies (walls, floors, ceilings) that provide a barrier to fire and smoke
conditions: building is required to have fire compartmentation per applicable building code
exceptions: open-plan spaces without fire-resistance-rated partitions may be permitted where sprinklered and occupant load is low, depending on jurisdiction

subject: Indoor Spatial Zones
rule: indoor spatial zones must have a means of egress (exit path) that leads to a public way or safe area
conditions: space is intended for human occupancy
exceptions: unoccupied service closets or chases less than a certain size may be exempt

subject: Indoor Spatial Zones
rule: indoor spatial zones must have minimum ceiling height as prescribed by applicable building code for the occupancy type
conditions: space is habitable or occupiable
exceptions: mechanical rooms, crawl spaces, and attics may have reduced height requirements

subject: Indoor Spatial Zones
rule: indoor spatial zones must not have floor-to-floor heights that prevent vertical circulation (stairs, elevators, ramps) from fitting within the available vertical dimension
conditions: building has multiple stories requiring vertical circulation

subject: Indoor Spatial Zones
rule: indoor spatial zones must have minimum floor-to-ceiling clearance at all points along the egress path
conditions: space contains an egress route
exceptions: points where overhead obstructions are protected (e.g., sprinkler pipes with crash guards) may have reduced clearance per code

subject: Floor-To-Floor Height Clearance
rule: Floor-to-floor height clearance must be at least the minimum required for the building's occupancy type per applicable building code
conditions: Building is designed for human occupancy
exceptions: Structures not intended for human occupancy (e.g., certain storage or equipment areas)

subject: Floor-To-Floor Height Clearance
rule: Floor-to-floor height clearance must not be less than the vertical clearance required for the passage of firefighting and emergency rescue equipment
conditions: Building includes floors above or below grade accessible by emergency responders

subject: Floor-To-Floor Height Clearance
rule: Floor-to-floor height clearance must accommodate the combined depth of all structural and MEP systems installed between floors
conditions: Building contains suspended ceilings or interstitial mechanical/electrical/plumbing zones

subject: Floor-To-Floor Height Clearance
rule: Floor-to-floor height clearance must be sufficient to meet minimum headroom (clear height) requirements for all occupied spaces
conditions: Spaces within the floor are designated as occupied or traversable by personnel
exceptions: Mechanical rooms, crawl spaces, or attics with restricted access where codes permit lower clearances

subject: Spatial Grid & Layout
rule: grid lines must maintain consistent orthogonal alignment (90° or 45°) throughout the layout
conditions: when using rectilinear grid system
exceptions: curved or radial grids designed for specific formal/aesthetic intent

subject: Spatial Grid & Layout
rule: grid spacing must be uniform within any single zone or structural bay
conditions: where a regular grid is defined
exceptions: intentional transition zones or column-free spaces that break the grid locally

subject: Spatial Grid & Layout
rule: layout must accommodate minimum circulation path widths for egress
conditions: when the layout includes occupied spaces or means of egress

subject: Spatial Grid & Layout
rule: grid layout must not place structural columns within required clear floor areas for programmed functions
conditions: where programmatic zones with specific clear-span requirements are defined (e.g., auditoria, ballrooms, open-plan offices)
exceptions: columns allowed within zones if they are integrated into partitions or designed as deliberate architectural features with programmatic acceptance

subject: Spatial Grid & Layout
rule: grid modules must be dimensioned to fit available prefabricated or standard material lengths without excessive off-cut waste
conditions: when using standard material sizes (e.g., 4'×8' sheet goods, standard steel beam lengths)
exceptions: custom-fabricated elements or projects where material waste is not a design constraint

subject: Ceiling Geometry & Finish
rule: Ceiling finish materials must be structurally attached to prevent falling hazard
conditions: applies to all occupiable spaces
exceptions: temporary suspended rigging for events with engineered supports

subject: Ceiling Geometry & Finish
rule: Ceiling geometry must provide minimum headroom clearance as required by applicable building code
conditions: ceiling exists above occupiable floor area
exceptions: unoccupied service spaces such as attics or crawl spaces

subject: Ceiling Geometry & Finish
rule: Ceiling finish must not use materials that release toxic fumes when heated in a fire scenario
conditions: ceiling is part of a building interior

subject: Ceiling Geometry & Finish
rule: Ceiling geometry must not reduce the minimum fire-resistance rating of the floor-ceiling assembly below code-required value
conditions: ceiling is part of a rated floor-ceiling assembly

subject: Indoor-Outdoor Transition Zone
rule: Indoor-outdoor transition zone must have a physical barrier (e.g., door, gate, retractable screen, or air curtain) that can be closed to separate interior conditioned space from exterior unconditioned space
conditions: the transition zone connects a conditioned interior space directly to the exterior
the building has a mechanical HVAC system serving the adjacent interior space
exceptions: the transition zone is itself fully unconditioned and designed as an open breezeway with no adjacent conditioned space

subject: Indoor-Outdoor Transition Zone
rule: Indoor-outdoor transition zone must have a floor surface that is slip-resistant when wet
conditions: the transition zone is exposed to direct rainfall or tracked-in water from the exterior
exceptions: the transition zone is a fully enclosed mudroom with drained floor grating where standing water is routed away before foot traffic

subject: Indoor-Outdoor Transition Zone
rule: Indoor-outdoor transition zone floor must be sloped or drained to prevent water pooling inside the conditioned interior space
conditions: the transition zone is at grade or below grade
there is no continuous waterproof membrane separating the zone from the interior
exceptions: the transition zone is a fully enclosed vestibule with a raised sill and sealed threshold preventing water ingress

subject: Wall Geometry & Finish
rule: wall exterior surface must be weather-resistive (water-shedding or water-resistant cladding/coating) to prevent moisture intrusion
conditions: wall is exterior (separates interior from outside environment)
roof or other overhead element is not present above the wall to fully shield it from rain
exceptions: wall is intentionally designed as a rainscreen assembly with a drained cavity
wall is a retaining wall where the exterior face is in contact with soil and designed for waterproofing

subject: Wall Geometry & Finish
rule: wall must not have uncontrolled openings or gaps that allow continuous air infiltration between conditioned interior and exterior
conditions: wall separates a conditioned space from unconditioned space or outdoors
wall is not a purposely ventilated assembly (e.g., vented cavity)
exceptions: intentional ventilation openings designed with controlled dampers or louvers (e.g., crawlspace vents, attic gable vents) where the wall is part of a ventilated enclosure

subject: Void & Atrium Spaces
rule: void and atrium spaces must have a means of natural or mechanical smoke extraction
conditions: space is enclosed
space exceeds 400 sq m in area
space serves as an occupied floor
exceptions: space is an unoccupied lightwell with no floor plates
space is fully sprinklered and designed with smoke reservoirs per code

subject: Void & Atrium Spaces
rule: void and atrium spaces must have a fire-resistance rated enclosure or separation from adjoining occupied floors
conditions: atrium connects three or more storeys
building is of combustible construction
