exceptions: space is provided with an engineered smoke control system and sprinklers throughout the building

subject: Void & Atrium Spaces
rule: void and atrium spaces must not contain permanent occupiable floor area that blocks the full vertical opening
conditions: space is classified as an atrium under building code
exceptions: mezzanines that occupy less than one-third of the atrium floor area and comply with code limits

subject: Void & Atrium Spaces
rule: void and atrium spaces must have a minimum opening area to the exterior for natural ventilation if relying on passive smoke control
conditions: smoke management is provided by natural ventilation
space is enclosed
exceptions: space uses mechanical smoke exhaust system instead

subject: Structural Columns Within Space
rule: structural columns within space must be continuous from foundation to roof (or designated load-transfer level) without interruption
conditions: column is load-bearing
column is part of primary gravity load path
exceptions: column is intentionally discontinuous for seismic isolation or settlement joints, with engineered load-transfer detail

subject: Structural Columns Within Space
rule: structural columns within space must not have their load-bearing capacity reduced by openings or penetrations without engineered reinforcement
conditions: column is designed as a load-bearing element
exceptions: openings are pre-engineered with collars, stirrups, or additional reinforcement per structural design

subject: Structural Columns Within Space
rule: structural columns within space must be axially aligned with the load path above and below
conditions: column transfers vertical loads from structure above to structure below
exceptions: offset is explicitly designed with transfer beams, corbels, or brackets engineered for eccentricity

subject: Window Sill Plant Shelf
rule: window sill plant shelf must be securely attached to the window sill
conditions: shelf is mounted on a window sill

subject: Window Sill Plant Shelf
rule: window sill plant shelf must have drainage or a waterproof tray
conditions: shelf holds live plants in pots or soil
exceptions: shelf holds only artificial plants or sealed decorative items with no water source

subject: Window Sill Plant Shelf
rule: window sill plant shelf must not obstruct window operation
conditions: window is operable (opens/closes)
exceptions: window is permanently sealed or fixed in place

subject: Integrated Planter Box
rule: Integrated planter box must have drainage holes or a drainage layer to prevent waterlogging of plant roots
conditions: when used for live plants
exceptions: when used strictly as a decorative/fake planter with no soil or plants

subject: Integrated Planter Box
rule: Integrated planter box must not have drainage outlets that discharge onto pedestrian walkways, occupied balconies, or building entrances below
conditions: when located above occupiable outdoor spaces or building entries
exceptions: when drainage is piped directly to a downspout or rainwater conductor

subject: Integrated Planter Box
rule: Integrated planter box must be structurally capable of supporting the saturated weight of soil, water, and plants

subject: Integrated Planter Box
rule: Integrated planter box must not have soil in direct contact with building materials that are susceptible to moisture damage (e.g., unprotected wood framing, gypsum)
conditions: when built into or adjacent to building envelope assemblies
exceptions: when a continuous waterproof membrane and drainage plane separate soil from the building structure

subject: Window Box Support Bracket
rule: support bracket must be securely fastened to a load-bearing wall or structure
conditions: the bracket is used to support a window box

subject: Window Box Support Bracket
rule: support bracket must have minimum load capacity equal to the weight of the fully saturated window box plus a safety factor
conditions: the bracket is used to hold a window box

subject: Window Box Support Bracket
rule: support bracket must not visibly protrude into pedestrian pathway or usable space below the window
conditions: the bracket is installed at ground-accessible height

subject: Window Box Support Bracket
rule: support bracket must be corrosion-resistant or protected from moisture
conditions: the bracket is exposed to outdoor weather and watering from the window box
exceptions: bracket is made of a non-corrodible material such as stainless steel or aluminum

subject: Window Box Support Bracket
rule: support bracket must be designed to prevent water pooling on horizontal surfaces
conditions: the bracket has horizontal or near-horizontal surfaces

subject: Internal Green Wall Frame
rule: Internal Green Wall Frame must be structurally connected to the building's primary structure or a load-bearing wall to transfer the weight of the green wall system
conditions: green wall is installed
frame supports live vegetation and growing medium
exceptions: free-standing internal green wall with its own independent base support system

subject: Internal Green Wall Frame
rule: Internal Green Wall Frame must include a waterproof membrane or drainage collection system at its base to prevent water damage to adjacent floors and walls
conditions: irrigation system is used to water the green wall
exceptions: the green wall uses a self-contained sealed hydroponic system with no liquid runoff

subject: Internal Green Wall Frame
rule: Internal Green Wall Frame must provide adequate ventilation gap between the frame back and the building wall to prevent mold and moisture entrapment
conditions: the green wall frame is mounted directly against an existing interior wall
exceptions: the wall surface behind the frame is itself a waterproof, mold-resistant surface designed for direct contact with the green wall system

subject: Internal Green Wall Frame
rule: Internal Green Wall Frame must not impede fire egress paths or block access to fire safety equipment
conditions: the frame is installed in a corridor, egress route, or near fire extinguishers/sprinklers
exceptions: the frame is specifically designed as a fire-rated assembly tested and certified for that location

subject: Trellis or Climbing Support Frame
rule: trellis or climbing support frame must have structural connection to ground or supporting wall
conditions: installed as standalone structure
installed against building facade
exceptions: lightweight freestanding frame resting on ground via base plates without fixed connection, where stability relies solely on gravity and geometry

subject: Trellis or Climbing Support Frame
rule: trellis or climbing support frame must not exceed material stress limits under combined dead load and wind load
conditions: supporting mature climbing plants
located in wind-exposed area

subject: Trellis or Climbing Support Frame
rule: trellis or climbing support frame must have minimum ground clearance at bottom edge to prevent ground-contact rot
conditions: wood material
exceptions: frame constructed from rot-resistant material (e.g. galvanized steel, aluminum, composite, or treated timber rated for ground contact)

subject: Biophilic Window System
rule: a biophilic window system must maintain a continuous thermal break between interior and exterior surfaces
conditions: when installed in a thermal envelope assembly
exceptions: in unconditioned structures where thermal separation is not required

subject: Biophilic Window System
rule: a biophilic window system must not allow uncontrolled air leakage between the window frame and the rough opening
conditions: when installed as part of a conditioned building enclosure

subject: Self-Watering Reservoir Tray
rule: Self-watering reservoir tray must be watertight (impermeable to water) on all interior surfaces that hold water
conditions: when configured to contain a standing water reservoir
exceptions: tray with a controlled leak designed for sub-irrigation flow-through systems where water is continuously supplied

subject: Self-Watering Reservoir Tray
rule: self-watering reservoir tray must have at least one opening or wicking interface between the reservoir chamber and the growing medium above
conditions: when used as part of a self-watering planter system where capillary action delivers water to plant roots
exceptions: systems that use external drip irrigation into the tray instead of wicking

subject: Self-Watering Reservoir Tray
rule: self-watering reservoir tray must not have a continuous open path from the reservoir water surface to the outside air at a level below the maximum fill line
conditions: when designed for passive wicking and the planter is located indoors or in a location where mosquito habitat is a concern
exceptions: outdoor systems where mosquito mesh or a sealed cap is provided
systems with active water treatment (e.g., chlorine or Bti dosing)

subject: Self-Watering Reservoir Tray
rule: self-watering reservoir tray must have an overfill drain or an automatic shutoff mechanism at the maximum designed water level
conditions: when the tray is filled by an external water supply (hose, faucet, or irrigation line) rather than by the user pouring a measured amount
exceptions: hand-filled trays where the user can see and stop filling at the max line

subject: Window Overhang / Shading Louvres for Plants
rule: Window overhang or shading louvre must extend at least as far as the mature plant canopy width projected outward from the façade
conditions: Plants are placed directly below or adjacent to the window
exceptions: Plants are trained to grow vertically on a trellis and do not require horizontal shading

subject: Window Overhang / Shading Louvres for Plants
rule: Window overhang must not fully block all direct sunlight for a heliophilic (full-sun) plant species
conditions: The plant species is classified as full-sun or heliophilic requiring >6 hours direct sun daily
exceptions: The plant species is shade-tolerant or shade-requiring

subject: Window Overhang / Shading Louvres for Plants
rule: Shading louvre slat angle must be adjustable or preselected to allow at least the minimum light transmission required by the specific plant species
conditions: The louvre system has adjustable slats
The plant species has a documented minimum light requirement
exceptions: The louvre is fixed and the fixed angle was designed specifically for that plant's light tolerance

subject: Glazing with Integrated UV-Filter Coating
rule: glazing with integrated UV-filter coating must block at least 95% of UV-A and UV-B radiation
conditions: when installed in exterior building envelope applications
exceptions: when specified for interior-only or non-solar-exposed applications

subject: Glazing with Integrated UV-Filter Coating
rule: glazing with integrated UV-filter coating must not show visible degradation (delamination, peeling, cracking, or significant color shift) after accelerated weathering testing equivalent to 10 years of typical exterior exposure
conditions: when the coating is applied to the exterior-facing surface of the glazing
when the product is rated for outdoor use

subject: Glazing with Integrated UV-Filter Coating
rule: glazing with integrated UV-filter coating must have a solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC) no greater than 0.40 when the coating is spectrally selective
conditions: when the coating is marketed as a spectrally-selective low-e coating with UV-filtering properties
exceptions: when the product explicitly targets heritage/transparency-maximizing applications where higher SHGC is accepted

subject: Drainage Layer / Geotextile Mat
rule: Drainage layer / geotextile mat must be placed beneath the ballast or paving layer and above the waterproofing membrane on a green or ballasted roof
conditions: when used in a green roof assembly
when used in a ballasted roof assembly
exceptions: inverted roof membrane assemblies where drainage layer is above waterproofing by design

subject: Drainage Layer / Geotextile Mat
rule: Drainage layer / geotextile mat must not be installed on a slope exceeding its manufacturer-rated maximum
conditions: when geotextile mat has a specified maximum slope rating
exceptions: when mechanically fastened or adhered per manufacturer's steep-slope detailing

subject: Drainage Layer / Geotextile Mat
rule: Drainage layer / geotextile mat must have overlapping joints of sufficient width (typically ≥ 150 mm) and be secured to prevent separation
conditions: when multiple sheets or rolls of drainage mat are used
exceptions: when sheets are heat-welded or adhesively bonded with a continuous seam

subject: Operable Casement with Plant Access Hatch
rule: operable casement must have a clear opening area that is at least the minimum required for emergency egress
conditions: when used as an egress opening
when serving a habitable room
exceptions: when serving a non-habitable space such as a mechanical plant room where egress is not required

subject: Operable Casement with Plant Access Hatch
rule: casement sash must not obstruct the plant access hatch when simultaneously opened
conditions: when the casement and the plant access hatch are installed in the same frame or directly adjacent

subject: Operable Casement with Plant Access Hatch
rule: plant access hatch must have a minimum clear opening dimension to allow passage of the largest replaceable plant component
conditions: where the hatch provides the only access route for equipment removal or replacement

subject: Operable Casement with Plant Access Hatch
rule: hinges and hardware for the operable casement must be rated for the weight and cyclic loading of the sash
conditions: when the casement sash exceeds standard weight thresholds

subject: Half-open Wall Frame
rule: half-open wall frame must have a continuous load path from top to foundation
conditions: when serving as a primary vertical loadbearing component
when part of a structural wall system
exceptions: non-structural decorative frames

subject: Half-open Wall Frame
rule: half-open wall frame must have lateral bracing or shear-resisting elements
conditions: when the wall contributes to the building's lateral stability system
in seismic or high-wind regions
exceptions: when the frame is strictly infill and not part of the lateral load-resisting system
when adjacent solid walls provide all lateral resistance

subject: Half-open Wall Frame
rule: openings in the half-open wall frame must not compromise the minimum cross-section of structural members below safe limits
conditions: when the wall carries gravity or lateral loads

subject: Half-open Wall Frame
rule: half-open wall frame members must be connected with joints capable of transferring design forces
conditions: when the frame is structural
exceptions: non-structural partitions fixed only at base and top

subject: Half-open Wall Cladding
rule: Half-open wall cladding must be structurally attached to a supporting frame or substrate
conditions: used as exterior cladding
vertical wall application

subject: Half-open Wall Cladding
rule: Half-open wall cladding must have gaps or openings that allow air and moisture to pass through
conditions: when the term 'half-open' refers to ventilated or screen-type cladding

subject: Half-open Wall Cladding
rule: Half-open wall cladding must not create a continuous sealed barrier that traps moisture against the building envelope
conditions: used as a rainscreen or ventilated facade

subject: Half-open Wall Opening
rule: half-open wall opening must have a lintel or arch to span the opening
conditions: opening width exceeds the structural capacity of the masonry or wall material above
exceptions: opening is beneath a continuous ring beam or bond beam that provides equivalent spanning action
opening is in a non-loadbearing infill wall where the structure is independently framed

subject: Half-open Wall Opening
rule: half-open wall opening must not exceed the maximum permitted width without intermediate vertical support
conditions: wall is loadbearing and built of unreinforced masonry
exceptions: structural analysis demonstrates adequate stress distribution via deep arch or buttressing

subject: Half-open Wall Glazing
rule: Half-open wall glazing must be structurally supported by a frame or adjacent building elements at all four sides to prevent glass failure under wind or gravity loads
conditions: Where glazing panels are larger than 0.5 m²
exceptions: Point-fixed structural glazing systems using bolts and spider fittings

subject: Half-open Wall Glazing
rule: Half-open wall glazing must not create a step or drop of more than 750 mm on the interior side without guarding or safety glazing
conditions: Where the glazing is accessible to building occupants at floor level

subject: Half-open Wall Glazing
rule: Half-open wall glazing must have an openable-to-fixed ratio that prevents wind-driven rain ingress under normal exposure conditions
conditions: Where the 'half-open' designation means panels are operable (e.g., sliding or pivoting)
exceptions: Fully weather-sealed closed position when not in operation

subject: Half-open Wall Counter/Desk Top
rule: The half-open wall counter/desk top must have a minimum horizontal depth (typically ≥ 300 mm) to provide a usable work surface and prevent items from falling off the back
conditions: The counter/desk top is intended for writing, placing equipment, or similar tasks
exceptions: The counter is purely decorative and not intended to bear any items

subject: Half-open Wall Counter/Desk Top
rule: The half-open wall counter/desk top must not have a gap between its rear edge and the wall larger than 10 mm
conditions: The counter/desk top is installed against a wall
exceptions: A intentional drainage/venting gap is explicitly designed and items are prevented from falling through

subject: Half-open Wall Sill
rule: Half-open wall sill must provide a continuous weather barrier between the wall opening frame and the wall surface
conditions: When installed as part of an exterior wall assembly
exceptions: When the wall assembly uses a fully drained rainscreen system that captures and redirects water at a different plane

subject: Half-open Wall Sill
rule: Half-open wall sill must slope outward (away from the building interior) at minimum 5 degrees
conditions: When installed horizontally as part of a window or door opening

subject: Half-open Wall Sill
rule: Half-open wall sill must not be installed with the drainage opening facing upward or inward

subject: Interior Window Frame
rule: interior window frame must be rigidly attached to the surrounding wall structure
conditions: frame is load-bearing or supports window operation
exceptions: temporary or decorative non-operable mockups

subject: Interior Window Frame
rule: interior window frame must not obstruct the window's operable sash movement
conditions: window is designed to be operable
exceptions: fixed (non-operable) windows

subject: Interior Window Frame
rule: interior window frame must be continuous and closed at all joints to prevent air and water infiltration
conditions: frame is part of an exterior wall assembly
exceptions: intentional decorative gaps in interior-only partitions

subject: Interior Window Glazing
rule: interior window glazing must be made of safety glazing material (tempered, laminated, or wired glass) when located in hazardous locations such as doors, side lights within 24 inches of a door opening, and low windows where the sill is less than 18 inches above the floor
conditions: glazing is in a door
glazing is within 24 inches of a door opening
glazing sill is less than 18 inches above the floor
glazing is in a shower or bathtub enclosure

subject: Interior Window Glazing
rule: interior window glazing must have a minimum visible light transmittance (VLT) that complies with the applicable energy code
conditions: glazing is part of the building thermal envelope
local energy code specifies minimum VLT for interior glazing
exceptions: decorative or non-vision glazing

subject: Interior Window Glazing
rule: interior window glazing must not be installed in fire-resistance-rated walls unless it meets the fire-protection rating required for the wall assembly
conditions: the wall assembly containing the glazing has a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: glazing assemblies tested and listed for the required fire-protection rating

subject: Interior Window Sill
rule: interior window sill must be sloped toward the room (or have a positive drainage angle) to prevent water pooling on the sill surface
conditions: sill is installed below an operable window
sill is exposed to rainwater or condensation runoff

subject: Interior Window Sill
rule: interior window sill must be sealed at all joints between the sill and the window frame, and between the sill and the wall finish

subject: Interior Window Sill
rule: interior window sill must not impede the operation of the window (e.g., opening, closing, or locking mechanisms)

subject: Interior Window Sill
rule: interior window sill must have a finished top surface that is free of sharp edges or splinters where it contacts the window or is touched by occupants

subject: Interior Window Header/Transom
rule: interior window header/transom must be sized to structurally span the full rough opening width
conditions: when installed above a door or window opening

subject: Interior Window Header/Transom
rule: interior window header/transom must be laterally braced or connected to prevent rotation out of plane
conditions: when the header depth exceeds its thickness

subject: Interior Window Header/Transom
rule: interior window header/transom must not be notched or drilled in the middle third of its span in a manner that reduces its bending capacity below design requirements
conditions: when the header is load-bearing
exceptions: pre-engineered holes or notches permitted by manufacturer or engineering design

subject: Fixed Interior Window
rule: Fixed interior window must be installed in an interior wall or partition
conditions: when the window is part of a wall assembly

subject: Fixed Interior Window
rule: Fixed interior window must have a frame or surround that fully separates its glass from the adjacent wall finish

subject: Fixed Interior Window
rule: Fixed interior window must not be load-bearing

subject: Fixed Interior Window
rule: Fixed interior window glass must be safety-glazed (tempered or laminated) if installed in a door, within 60 inches of floor level, or in a hazardous location per code
exceptions: when the glass area is less than 9 sq ft and glazed with annealed glass that is not in a hazardous location

subject: Operable Interior Window (Casement/Sliding)
rule: operable interior window must have an opening mechanism (handle, crank, or sliding actuator) accessible from the interior side

subject: Operable Interior Window (Casement/Sliding)
rule: operable interior window must have a clear opening path that does not conflict with adjacent building elements (walls, columns, furniture, or other windows)

subject: Operable Interior Window (Casement/Sliding)
rule: operable interior window must not have a fixed or non-operable frame installed in lieu of the operable assembly

subject: Interior Window Hardware
rule: Interior window hardware must be mechanically fastened to the window frame or supporting structure
conditions: permanent installation
non-temporary application
exceptions: magnetic or adhesive-mounted hardware where the load rating and safety are certified

subject: Interior Window Hardware
rule: Interior window hardware must not obstruct the egress path or emergency escape opening of the window
conditions: window is designated as an egress or emergency escape opening
applicable building codes require clear opening dimensions
exceptions: hardware that is readily removable without tools or special knowledge and does not reduce the net clear opening below code minimum

subject: Interior Window Hardware
rule: Interior window hardware must be accessible and operable without requiring excessive force or specialized tools
conditions: hardware is used for manual operation of the window (e.g., sash locks, cranks, handles)
exceptions: hardware on windows intended only for maintenance access with restricted-use protocols

subject: Interior Window Trim/Casing
rule: Interior window trim/casing must be installed with expansion gaps at junctions with adjacent materials to accommodate thermal and moisture movement
conditions: trim spans across multiple stud bays or long continuous lengths
adjacent to materials with different thermal or moisture expansion rates
exceptions: trim pieces shorter than 600mm that are fully within a single conditioned space with stable humidity

subject: Interior Window Trim/Casing
rule: Interior window trim/casing must not block operable window sashes or hardware
conditions: window has operable sash
trim is applied on the interior side of the window frame

subject: Interior Window Trim/Casing
rule: Interior window trim/casing must be positively attached to the wall or window frame and not rely solely on adhesive
conditions: trim is larger than small decorative moulding (profile depth > 10mm)
exceptions: lightweight decorative quarter-round or cove moulding less than 10mm profile depth

subject: Borrowed Light Window
rule: A borrowed light window must be installed in an interior wall or partition, not an exterior wall
conditions: The borrowed light window is used to transmit light between interior spaces

subject: Borrowed Light Window
rule: A borrowed light window must be glazed with a transparent or translucent material

subject: Borrowed Light Window
rule: A borrowed light window must not compromise fire-rated assembly integrity
conditions: The wall or partition containing the borrowed light window is a fire-rated assembly
exceptions: Fire-rated glazing assemblies that meet the same fire-resistance rating as the surrounding wall may be used

subject: Interior Window with Integrated Blind (Between-Glass)
rule: The between-glass blind assembly must be hermetically sealed within the double or triple glazing unit
conditions: unit includes an integrated blind between glass panes

subject: Interior Window with Integrated Blind (Between-Glass)
rule: The blind control mechanism must not penetrate or compromise the edge seal of the insulated glass unit
conditions: window includes an integrated between-glass blind
exceptions: magnetic coupling systems that transmit torque through the glass without seal penetration

subject: Interior Window with Integrated Blind (Between-Glass)
rule: The blind slats or vanes must not interfere with the glass-to-glass or glass-to-spacer contact during assembly
conditions: window includes between-glass blind with movable slats

subject: Interior Window with Integrated Blind (Between-Glass)
rule: The magnetic or motorized blind actuation components must be operable without disassembling the sealed glazing unit
conditions: unit includes a between-glass blind with motorized or magnetic actuation

subject: Interior Window with Integrated Blind (Between-Glass)
rule: The blind material must withstand the temperature extremes within the sealed cavity without degradation
conditions: between-glass blind installed in a sealed IGU cavity

subject: Interior Pass-Through Window
rule: Interior pass-through window must have a fire-resistance rating consistent with the fire-rated assembly it penetrates (e.g., fire-rated wall, floor-ceiling assembly)
conditions: when the pass-through window penetrates a fire-resistance-rated wall or horizontal assembly
in buildings subject to building code fire-resistance requirements
exceptions: when the wall or assembly is not required to have a fire-resistance rating
when the opening is protected by an automatic fire-suppression system that the applicable code accepts as an alternative

subject: Interior Pass-Through Window
rule: Interior pass-through window must be glazed with safety glass (laminated, tempered, or equivalent) if located in a hazardous location as defined by building code
conditions: when the window is within 24 inches of a door swing
when the window extends to within 18 inches of the floor
when the window is in a wall adjacent to a walking surface where the glazing is subject to human impact
exceptions: when the glazing is fully protected by a permanent guard or barrier that prevents impact
when the opening is too small to allow passage of a 3-inch sphere (typically not applicable to pass-through windows)

subject: Interior Pass-Through Window
rule: Interior pass-through window must not compromise the smoke-tight or air-tight seal of a smoke barrier or smoke partition it penetrates
conditions: when the pass-through window is installed in a smoke barrier or smoke partition required by code
exceptions: when the opening is protected by a smoke damper or automatic-closing device that restores the barrier integrity upon smoke detection

subject: Interior Pass-Through Window
rule: Interior pass-through window that serves as an egress window must have a clear opening size meeting minimum egress requirements
conditions: when the pass-through window is also designated or intended as an emergency escape and rescue opening
exceptions: when the space served has another compliant means of egress
when the window is not in a sleeping room or habitable basement

subject: Interior Window Frame Anchors/Fasteners
rule: Interior window frame anchors/fasteners must be compatible with the window frame material to avoid galvanic corrosion or structural failure
conditions: When the window frame is made of metal (e.g., aluminum or steel)
exceptions: When a dielectric/insulating barrier is used between dissimilar metals

subject: Interior Window Frame Anchors/Fasteners
rule: Interior window frame anchors/fasteners must be rated for the full dead load of the window assembly

subject: Interior Window Frame Anchors/Fasteners
rule: Interior window frame anchors/fasteners must not penetrate the exterior weather barrier or vapor barrier without appropriate sealant and gasketing
conditions: When fasteners are installed through the window frame into exterior wall structure
exceptions: When the fastener is specifically designed with an integrated sealing system that maintains barrier continuity

subject: Interior Window Frame Anchors/Fasteners
rule: Interior window frame anchors/fasteners must be installed with torque within the manufacturer's specified range

subject: Intermediate Landing
rule: An intermediate landing that connects two flights of stairs must be at least as wide as the stair flights it serves
conditions: where stairs serve a habitable room or public means of egress

subject: Intermediate Landing
rule: Intermediate landing must have a minimum depth (run) in the direction of travel of at least 36 inches (914 mm) for residential or 44 inches (1118 mm) for commercial occupancies
conditions: where the landing serves as part of a means of egress
exceptions: winders or curved stair treads may reduce landing depth requirements under specific code sections

subject: Intermediate Landing
rule: Intermediate landing must have a non-slip surface or finish appropriate for pedestrian traffic
conditions: landing is exposed to weather, moisture, or exterior conditions
exceptions: interior landings with carpet or other slip-resistant finishes are acceptable

subject: Intermediate Landing
rule: Intermediate landing must not reduce the required headroom clearance (minimum 80 inches typically)
conditions: landing is part of a stairway serving as a means of egress

subject: Intermediate Landing
rule: Intermediate landing must be structurally capable of supporting the design live load for stairs (typically 100 psf for residential, up to 100 psf for commercial plus concentrated load)

subject: Half-Landing
rule: half-landing must have a horizontal landing surface with a depth equal to or greater than the width of the stair flight it serves
conditions: half-landing is part of a stair configuration with two straight flights meeting at a 180-degree turn

subject: Half-Landing
rule: half-landing must have a minimum clear width equal to the stair flight width

subject: Half-Landing
rule: half-landing must not have a step or ramp on its surface that breaks the level plane

subject: Half-Landing
rule: half-landing must have structural capacity to support the design live load plus the dead load of the stair flights it connects

subject: Stair Enclosure Wall
rule: Stair enclosure wall must have a fire-resistance rating consistent with local building code
conditions: building has more than one story
stair enclosure serves as required means of egress
exceptions: when building is of Type V construction and under a certain height threshold per code

subject: Stair Enclosure Wall
rule: Stair enclosure wall must be continuous from the lowest floor to the roof or to a fire-resistance-rated roof assembly
conditions: stair enclosure is part of a required means of egress serving more than one story

subject: Stair Enclosure Wall
rule: Stair enclosure wall must not be penetrated by openings other than required doors
conditions: wall is part of a required fire-resistance-rated enclosure
exceptions: penetrations protected by fire dampers and fire-resistive joint systems as permitted by code

subject: Stair Enclosure Wall
rule: Stair enclosure wall must not be used as a chase for plumbing or ductwork that would compromise its fire rating
conditions: wall is fire-resistance-rated
exceptions: where ducts are fire-rated to match the wall assembly and all penetrations are properly firestopped

subject: Stair Ventilation System
rule: Stair ventilation system must have a dedicated smoke exhaust outlet at the top of the stair shaft
conditions: stair serves a building with any floor more than 10 m above the fire service access level
exceptions: stair is a pressurised stairwell complying with AS 1668.1 alternative provisions for pressurisation

subject: Stair Ventilation System
rule: Stair ventilation system must maintain a minimum positive pressure differential of 50 Pa across the stair enclosure when the system is in pressurisation mode
conditions: stair pressurisation system is used as the smoke management strategy
exceptions: authority having jurisdiction has approved a site-specific performance-based alternative

subject: Stair Ventilation System
rule: Stair ventilation system must not recirculate exhaust air back into the building
conditions: system operates in smoke-exhaust mode during a fire event
exceptions: system is specifically designed and tested for energy recovery with fire-rated isolation dampers and smoke detectors that isolate recirculation on alarm

subject: Stair Ventilation System
rule: Stair ventilation system's smoke exhaust fan must be rated for continuous operation at the required temperature (typically 300 °C for 30 minutes or 400 °C for 15 minutes)
conditions: fan serves a smoke-exhaust function
exceptions: alternative fan rating is approved based on a fire-engineering analysis of expected temperatures and duration

subject: Stair Lighting
rule: Stair lighting luminaires must provide a minimum of 10 lux (1 footcandle) along the entire stair path, including treads and landings
conditions: Any enclosed stairway serving as a required means of egress
exceptions: Stairs in dwelling units where lower lighting levels are permitted by code

subject: Stair Lighting
rule: Stair lighting must not create glare that obscures the leading edge of stair treads (nosing)
conditions: All stairways

subject: Stair Lighting
rule: Stair lighting fixtures in enclosed stairwells must be protected against physical impact when mounted below 8 feet above the walking surface
conditions: Enclosed stairwells serving as required means of egress
Fixtures mounted less than 8 ft above the stair or landing

subject: Stair Lighting
rule: Stair lighting emergency egress illumination must remain operational for a minimum of 90 minutes upon loss of normal power
conditions: Stair lighting that serves as required egress illumination
exceptions: Stairs not part of the required means of egress

subject: Monumental Stair
rule: monumental stair tread depth must be at least 280 mm (11 inches) for the going
conditions: designed for public use
interior or exterior

subject: Monumental Stair
rule: monumental stair riser height must not exceed 180 mm (7 inches)
conditions: designed for public use
exceptions: private residential monumental stairs may have slightly relaxed limits per local code

subject: Monumental Stair
rule: monumental stair nosing projection must be between 16 mm and 19 mm
conditions: nosing is present
exceptions: flush riser designs where nosing projection is zero by design and handrail/lighting compensates

subject: Monumental Stair
rule: monumental stair handrails must be continuous on both sides of the stair flight
conditions: total stair width exceeds 1100 mm
more than 4 risers in a flight

subject: Monumental Stair
rule: monumental stair handrail height must be between 865 mm and 965 mm measured vertically from stair nosing

subject: Scissor Stair
rule: scissor stair runs must not intersect or share a common path
conditions: when configured as two interlocking stairs in the same enclosure

subject: Scissor Stair
rule: scissor stair must provide two separate means of egress from the same floor to different discharge points
conditions: when required by building code for the occupancy type

subject: Scissor Stair
rule: scissor stair runs must be separated by a fire-rated wall or partition along their full height
conditions: in buildings where scissor stairs are permitted as two separate exits
exceptions: where building code allows through-a-rating exceptions with specific fire-protection systems

subject: Scissor Stair
rule: scissor stair must not terminate at the same egress door or vestibule on the discharge level
conditions: when used as two required exits from a floor

subject: Corner Door Hardware
rule: Corner door hardware must provide a minimum of 3/4-inch (19 mm) latch bolt projection when in the locked/extended position
conditions: When used on egress doors
When used on fire-rated doors
exceptions: Latch bolts on locking devices that are solely for privacy (not life safety) may have shorter projection if permitted by local codes

subject: Corner Door Hardware
rule: Corner door hardware must not bind or interfere with the door edge, frame, or adjacent hardware during normal swing operation
conditions: For any swinging door installation

subject: Corner Door Hardware
rule: Corner door hardware fasteners must engage a minimum depth into the door or frame material sufficient to prevent pull-out under rated load
conditions: When installed on any door or frame

subject: Corner Door Weatherseal
rule: corner door weatherseal must maintain continuous line of contact with both door leaf and frame at the corner junction
conditions: when mounted at a door corner interface
when used in a weather-sealed assembly

subject: Corner Door Weatherseal
rule: corner door weatherseal must not have an exposed adhesive edge that can peel or degrade under cyclic door operation
conditions: when adhesive-backed attachment method is used
exceptions: when the adhesive is mechanically fastened or encapsulated as part of a rigid carrier system

subject: Corner Door Weatherseal
rule: corner door weatherseal material must be flexible enough to accommodate door-frame relative movement at the corner without permanent deformation or cracking
conditions: when installed in a door assembly subject to thermal expansion, building settlement, or operational vibration

subject: Folding Corner Door
rule: folding corner door must allow the door leaf to fold completely at the corner joint
conditions: when configured as a folding door system with a corner application

subject: Folding Corner Door
rule: folding corner door must not have stationary panels that block the folding path at the corner
conditions: when multiple panels are used in the corner configuration

subject: Revolving Corner Door
rule: revolving corner door must be fully enclosed and weatherstripped at all moving interfaces
conditions: when used as an exterior entrance

subject: Revolving Corner Door
rule: revolving corner door must not have a radius smaller than the minimum turning radius of the largest intended occupant or object
conditions: when the door is designed for public or goods access
exceptions: dedicated service doors with separately controlled access

subject: Revolving Corner Door
rule: revolving corner door must have a positive latching mechanism in at least one closed position per egress code
conditions: when the building is occupied and subject to egress codes

subject: Sliding Corner Door
rule: sliding corner door must have a clear operating path free of obstructions on both sides of the door leaf travel zone
conditions: when door is operable
when installed in a corner configuration

subject: Sliding Corner Door
rule: sliding corner door must not have a door leaf that exceeds the structural load capacity of its supporting track and corner mechanism
conditions: for any operable installation
exceptions: doors designed with independent floor-supported rollers that bypass the corner track load path

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Metal)
rule: Corner door leaf material (metal) must have sufficient thickness and strength to resist deformation under normal operation and wind loads
conditions: When used as a swing door leaf

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Metal)
rule: Corner door leaf material (metal) must be galvanically compatible with adjacent metal components (frame, hinges, hardware)
conditions: When installed in exterior or damp environments
exceptions: When all adjacent metal components are made of the same metal alloy

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Metal)
rule: Corner door leaf material (metal) must not have sharp edges or burrs at cut edges or corners

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Metal)
rule: Corner door leaf material (metal) must be non-combustible
conditions: When installed in fire-rated door assemblies or required by building code

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Glass)
rule: Corner door leaf material (glass) must be tempered or laminated safety glass
conditions: Door leaf is located in a commercial building
Door leaf is in a high-traffic area
Building code requires safety glazing
exceptions: If the glass is fully protected by a guardrail or barrier that prevents impact
Historically certified buildings with grandfathered non-safety glass

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Glass)
rule: Corner door leaf material (glass) must have a minimum thickness adequate for its size and wind load exposure
conditions: Door is exterior-facing
Door area exceeds local code minimum thresholds
Wind load rating is specified by local code
exceptions: Interior doors not exposed to wind loads

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Glass)
rule: Corner door leaf material (glass) must not have sharp exposed edges unless fully edge-finished or protected
conditions: Glass edges are exposed to human contact
Glass is not fully encased in a frame that covers all edges

subject: Corner Door Leaf Material (Glass)
rule: Corner door leaf material (glass) must comply with impact test requirements for hazardous locations
conditions: Door leaf is at grade level
Door is in a location classified as hazardous per IBC/CPSC

subject: Thick Wall Construction Types
rule: Thick wall construction must have a minimum thermal mass ratio to prevent overheating
conditions: wall is exposed to solar radiation
building is in a climate with significant diurnal temperature variation

subject: Thick Wall Construction Types
rule: Thick wall construction must not have continuous vapor-impermeable layers on both the interior and exterior without a drainage plane
conditions: wall assembly includes insulation
climate has freeze-thaw cycles or high humidity

subject: Thick Wall Construction Types
rule: Thick wall construction must have a foundation capable of supporting the increased dead load of the wall system
conditions: wall height exceeds one story
wall material density exceeds standard timber-frame density

subject: Non-Loadbearing Thick Wall
rule: Non-loadbearing thick wall must not support any vertical structural loads from roof, floors, or other building elements above it
conditions: Wall is classified as non-loadbearing
Wall is thick (greater than typical partition thickness)
exceptions: Wall may carry its own self-weight and lateral loads

subject: Non-Loadbearing Thick Wall
rule: Non-loadbearing thick wall must be capable of resisting self-weight and lateral loads (wind, seismic) without collapsing
conditions: Wall is thick and freestanding
Wall is subjected to lateral environmental loads

subject: Non-Loadbearing Thick Wall
rule: Non-loadbearing thick wall must be detailed with movement joints to accommodate thermal and moisture expansion without cracking
conditions: Wall is constructed of masonry, concrete, or other rigid materials prone to expansion/contraction
exceptions: Very short wall segments (length below material-specific threshold for crack-free performance)

subject: Non-Loadbearing Thick Wall
rule: Non-loadbearing thick wall must not obstruct required means of egress or fire exit pathways
conditions: Wall is located in a building with occupancy requiring means of egress compliance
exceptions: Wall is intentionally part of a fire-rated enclosure protecting an egress path (and does not block it)

subject: Thick Wall Insulation Layer
rule: thick wall insulation layer must maintain a continuous thermal barrier without gaps or compression
conditions: when installed in exterior wall assemblies
when serving as primary thermal control layer
exceptions: at structural penetrations that require fire-rated sealants

subject: Thick Wall Insulation Layer
rule: thick wall insulation layer must not be installed on the interior side of a vapor barrier in cold climates
conditions: in climate zones with predominant heating demand (ASHRAE climate zones 5 and colder)
exceptions: when a ventilated air gap separates the insulation from the vapor barrier

subject: Thick Wall Insulation Layer
rule: thick wall insulation layer must be rated for the fire-resistance requirements of the wall assembly in which it is installed
conditions: in buildings where the wall assembly requires a fire-resistance rating per building code
exceptions: when the insulation is protected by a code-compliant thermal barrier (e.g., gypsum board) on the occupied side

subject: Thick Wall Insulation Layer
rule: thick wall insulation layer must not exceed the cavity depth of the wall framing
conditions: when installed within framed wall cavities
exceptions: when a furring strip or rain-screen system provides additional depth

subject: Thick Wall Waterproofing Membrane
rule: thick wall waterproofing membrane must form a continuous barrier without gaps or perforations
conditions: when used as primary waterproofing layer
exceptions: intentional drainage openings designed into the system

subject: Thick Wall Waterproofing Membrane
rule: thick wall waterproofing membrane must be lapped at joints by a minimum distance specified by the manufacturer
conditions: when multiple membrane sheets are used

subject: Thick Wall Waterproofing Membrane
rule: thick wall waterproofing membrane must not be applied to a damp or frost-contaminated substrate
conditions: during installation

subject: Thick Wall Waterproofing Membrane
rule: thick wall waterproofing membrane must be protected from direct ultraviolet exposure
conditions: when not rated for UV exposure
exceptions: membranes specifically formulated with UV stabilizers per manufacturer specification

subject: Thick Wall Tie/Connector
rule: thick wall tie/connector must transfer lateral loads between wythes of a cavity wall
conditions: when used in cavity wall construction
when wythes are not structurally bonded by other means
exceptions: wall is a single wythe construction
wall uses alternative lateral load transfer system

subject: Thick Wall Tie/Connector
rule: thick wall tie/connector must not create a continuous thermal bridge across the cavity
conditions: when the cavity contains thermal insulation
exceptions: tie is made of non-thermally-conductive material (e.g., stainless steel with low thermal conductivity)
tie includes an integral thermal break component

subject: Thick Wall Tie/Connector
rule: thick wall tie/connector must be corrosion-resistant for its full service life
conditions: when exposed to exterior moisture or a coastal/marine environment
exceptions: tie is sacrificial and designed for replacement within building lifespan

subject: Thick Wall Opening Lintel
rule: lintel must extend sufficiently beyond the opening on both sides to transfer vertical loads to the adjacent wall masonry
conditions: lintel spans a wall opening
wall is load-bearing
exceptions: opening width is less than the masonry unit length
lintel is part of a continuous reinforced concrete bond beam

subject: Thick Wall Opening Lintel
rule: lintel depth must be sufficient to resist bending and shear stresses induced by the wall and floor/roof loads above
conditions: opening is in a load-bearing thick wall
exceptions: the opening is very narrow (e.g., less than 600 mm wide) and the wall above is lightly loaded

subject: Thick Wall Opening Lintel
rule: lintel must not be placed such that its top is below the underside of the wall's crown or roof plate without proper load redistribution detailing
conditions: lintel carries masonry above up to roof level
exceptions: a relieving arch or structural beam is provided directly above the lintel to redirect loads

subject: Thick Wall Foundation
rule: Thick wall foundation must have a continuous load path transferring building weight directly to the bearing soil
conditions: building has more than one story
building is constructed on compressible soil

subject: Thick Wall Foundation
rule: Thick wall foundation must not have drainage directed toward the base of the foundation wall
conditions: foundation is below grade

subject: Thick Wall Foundation
rule: Thick wall foundation frost depth must be below the local frost line
conditions: foundation is located in a climate with seasonal ground freezing
exceptions: foundation is on bedrock or non-frost-susceptible soil as confirmed by geotechnical report

subject: Thick Wall Coping/Parapet
rule: Thick wall coping/parapet must have a minimum height above the roof surface to prevent water ingress and wind-driven rain
conditions: when serving as a roof edge barrier
exceptions: when used solely as decorative non-water-shedding element with a separate waterproofing system

subject: Thick Wall Coping/Parapet
rule: Thick wall coping must not have open joints at the top surface
conditions: when installed as a weatherproof cap over parapet walls
exceptions: if joints are specifically designed with continuous metal flashing and sealed expansion joints

subject: Thick Wall Coping/Parapet
rule: Thick wall coping must overlap the parapet wall on both sides to shed water away from the wall face
conditions: when serving as a wall cap for weather protection

subject: Thick Wall Coping/Parapet
rule: Thick wall coping must be sloped to drain water off
conditions: when installed as a horizontal top surface exposed to rain
exceptions: if the coping is designed with an integrated gutter system or is sheltered by an overhang

subject: Closet Partition Walls
rule: Closet partition walls must extend from finished floor to finished structural ceiling or fire-rated assembly above
conditions: When closet is enclosed on all sides
When serving as part of a dwelling unit or occupancy separation
exceptions: When a bulkhead, soffit, or dropped ceiling is present and the partition is stopped at the bottom of that assembly with a fire-rated fill if required

subject: Closet Partition Walls
rule: Closet partition walls must not eliminate required clearances to electrical panels located within or adjacent to the closet
conditions: When an electrical panel is located within the closet or on the opposite side of the partition wall
exceptions: When the panel is relocated or the closet is designed to maintain the manufacturer's required working clearance (typically 30 in wide x 36 in deep x 6.5 ft tall)

subject: Closet Partition Walls
rule: Closet partition wall studs must be spaced at maximum 24 inches on center when supporting only closet shelving and lightweight finishes
conditions: When the partition is non-load-bearing
exceptions: When structural calculations or engineered design justify a different spacing
When the wall uses engineered studs or cold-formed steel with a manufacturer-listed alternative spacing

subject: Closet Partition Walls
rule: Closet partition walls must not block required egress path width when the closet door swings into a hallway or exit corridor
conditions: When the closet door opens into a corridor or exit access path
exceptions: When the door is designed to be sliding or pocket-type and does not encroach on the required egress width

subject: Closet Shelving
rule: shelving must be securely attached to wall studs to prevent tipping
conditions: closet shelving is wall-mounted
shelving is not freestanding/floor-supported
exceptions: freestanding closet systems with a floor-to-ceiling pole or sufficiently wide base that pass ANSI/BIFMA tip-over stability testing

subject: Closet Shelving
rule: shelving must not exceed the manufacturer's stated maximum uniform load per shelf
conditions: shelving is used for storage

subject: Closet Rod/Hanging Rail
rule: closet rod / hanging rail must be capable of supporting a distributed vertical load (e.g., clothes on hangers) without excessive deflection or failure
exceptions: decorative-only rods that explicitly state they are not load-bearing

subject: Closet Rod/Hanging Rail
rule: closet rod / hanging rail must be horizontal (within acceptable tolerance) when installed

subject: Closet Rod/Hanging Rail
rule: closet rod / hanging rail must not have sharp edges or burrs at garment contact surfaces

subject: Closet Rod/Hanging Rail
rule: closet rod / hanging rail must have a diameter (or equivalent cross-section) compatible with standard hanger hooks
exceptions: custom rods designed for non-standard hanger systems

subject: Closet Floor Finish
rule: Closet floor finish must be level and smooth to allow safe walking and placement of stored items
conditions: floor is intended for storage use or occupant access
exceptions: floor is intentionally sloped for drainage (e.g., in a closet containing mechanical equipment that may leak)

subject: Closet Floor Finish
rule: Closet floor finish must be compatible with the substrate and not cause moisture entrapment that leads to mold or rot
conditions: closet is enclosed and has limited ventilation
substrate is wood-based or moisture-sensitive
exceptions: a waterproofing membrane is installed between finish and substrate
closet is designed as a sealed mechanical space with drain

subject: Closet Ventilation Grille
rule: closet ventilation grille must have a net free ventilation area adequate for the closet volume
conditions: closet is enclosed
closet requires ventilation per building code
exceptions: closet is mechanically ventilated via ducted system

subject: Closet Ventilation Grille
rule: closet ventilation grille must not be fully obstructed by stored items, shelving, or adjacent construction
conditions: grille is installed in a closet used for storage
exceptions: grille is located at the top of the door and the door can still be opened/closed without obstruction

subject: Closet Ventilation Grille
rule: closet ventilation grille must be installed in a location that provides a continuous airflow path between the closet and a ventilated space (or directly to outdoors)
conditions: grille serves as the only ventilation opening for the closet

subject: Wall-to-Wall Closet
rule: wall-to-wall closet must have clear floor depth of at least 24 inches in front of the closet for door swing and access
conditions: closet has hinged doors
closet is located in an occupied space
exceptions: closet has sliding doors or accordion doors
closet is a reach-in closet with no door

subject: Wall-to-Wall Closet
rule: wall-to-wall closet must not have a door swing that conflicts with adjacent door swings or egress paths
conditions: closet door swings outward into a corridor or room used for egress
exceptions: closet door is a pocket door or sliding door

subject: Wall-to-Wall Closet
rule: wall-to-wall closet must not block or cover any HVAC supply or return register
conditions: closet is installed against a wall containing an HVAC register
exceptions: register has been relocated or a transfer grille is provided through the closet

subject: Wall-to-Wall Closet
rule: wall-to-wall closet must have structural support for any shelving or rod loads attached to walls or ceiling
conditions: closet contains built-in shelving or hanging rods that are attached to the building structure
exceptions: closet is a freestanding unit with no structural attachment

subject: Wall-to-Wall Closet
rule: wall-to-wall closet must not obstruct electrical panels, fire alarm devices, or sprinkler heads
conditions: closet is located in a utility room, corridor, or area with building service equipment
exceptions: panels or devices have been relocated per code

subject: Sunny Countertop Surface
rule: Sunny Countertop Surface must be made of a material that can withstand direct sunlight without warping, discoloring, or degrading
conditions: Countertop is installed outdoors or in a sun-exposed location

subject: Sunny Countertop Surface
rule: Sunny Countertop Surface must not have a dark-colored finish that absorbs excessive heat
conditions: Countertop is in direct sunlight for prolonged periods

subject: Sunny Counter Edge Profile
rule: 'Sunny Counter Edge Profile' must have a minimum 2-inch (50 mm) vertical rise at the counter edge to prevent water ingress and debris accumulation.
conditions: When used as a roof-to-wall or parapet transition flashing profile

subject: Sunny Counter Edge Profile
rule: 'Sunny Counter Edge Profile' must_not be installed without a continuous sealant bead at the top horizontal joint where the profile meets the vertical wall surface.
conditions: When terminating against a vertical masonry or concrete wall surface

subject: Sunny Counter Edge Profile
rule: 'Sunny Counter Edge Profile' must be positively fastened (mechanically or with adhesive rated for the substrate) at intervals not exceeding 12 inches on center.
conditions: When exposed to wind uplift forces in any climate zone

subject: Sunny Counter - L-Shaped Layout
rule: horizontal surfaces used for seating or food display must be stable and level to prevent tipping or spillage
conditions: when counter is used for seating or food display

subject: Sunny Counter - L-Shaped Layout
rule: the L-shaped counter must provide unobstructed access to at least one side for service staff
conditions: if the counter serves food or beverages

subject: Sunny Counter - L-Shaped Layout
rule: the counter surface must not have sharp exposed corners at 90-degree inside or outside turns that could cause injury
conditions: when the counter is at typical standing or seated height (30–42 inches) and accessible to users

subject: Wall Cleat
rule: wall cleat must be mechanically fastened to the wall structure
conditions: when used as a load-bearing anchor point
exceptions: temporary installations using friction-fit or adhesive-only methods that are explicitly designed for non-structural applications

subject: Wall Cleat
rule: wall cleat must not have sharp protruding edges or burrs in accessible locations
conditions: when installed within 2 m of occupied floor level or in pedestrian paths

subject: Shelf Pin/Clip
rule: Shelf pin/clip must be made of material with sufficient shear strength to support the applied shelf load without failure
conditions: shelf pin/clip is used to support a loaded shelf
exceptions: decorative/non-load-bearing installations explicitly labeled as such

subject: Shelf Pin/Clip
rule: Shelf pin/clip must have a diameter (or cross-section) that matches the receiving hole in the upright/standard within standard engineering tolerances
conditions: shelf pin/clip is inserted into pre-drilled holes in a shelf standard or upright

subject: Shelf Pin/Clip
rule: Shelf pin/clip must not extend beyond the shelf thickness or interfere with items placed on the shelf above
conditions: shelf is installed and loaded with items above the pin location

subject: Corbel
rule: a corbel must project horizontally from a wall or column to support a load above
conditions: when used as a structural support element

subject: Corbel
rule: a corbel must be constructed of a material with adequate compressive strength to resist crushing under the supported load
conditions: when corbel carries structural loads
exceptions: purely decorative corbels that carry no load

subject: Corbel
rule: corbel depth at support must be sufficient to prevent shear or flexural failure
conditions: when corbel is designed as a load-bearing structural element

subject: Open Shelf Panel/Board
rule: open shelf panel/board must be capable of supporting its intended load without excessive deflection
conditions: when used as a load-bearing storage surface

subject: Open Shelf Panel/Board
rule: open shelf panel/board must be made of a material that does not degrade under normal environmental exposure in its intended location
conditions: when the shelf is exposed to ambient indoor or outdoor conditions

subject: Open Shelf Panel/Board
rule: open shelf panel/board must not have sharp edges or protrusions that pose a laceration hazard in its installed configuration
conditions: when the shelf is accessible to users at typical reach heights

subject: Floating Shelf
rule: floating shelf must be anchored to a wall stud or equivalent solid backing
conditions: shelf is intended to bear load
shelf is attached to a vertical wall surface
exceptions: shelf is purely decorative and explicitly marked as zero-load

subject: Floating Shelf
rule: floating shelf must not exceed manufacturer's maximum static load rating
conditions: manufacturer provides a stated load capacity

subject: Floating Shelf
rule: floating shelf must not have a depth greater than its wall-bearing bracket embedment can cantilever without tipping
conditions: shelf projects more than 6 inches from the wall face

subject: Corner Shelf
rule: Corner shelf must have a solid back mounting surface to distribute load and prevent tipping
conditions: When mounted on a wall
When installed in a corner configuration
exceptions: Freestanding corner shelves that are floor-supported and do not rely on wall attachment

subject: Corner Shelf
rule: Corner shelf must not overhang beyond its mounting points by more than the shelf's own depth without additional support
conditions: When shelf is cantilevered or bracket-mounted
exceptions: Shelves that are fully supported from below (e.g., legs or a cabinet base)

subject: Corner Shelf
rule: Corner shelf must have a minimum depth of at least 100 mm at the outer edge to prevent items from sliding off
conditions: When designed to hold loose objects (not books or items with their own restraint)
exceptions: Decorative shelves that do not carry functional load

subject: Cantilevered Shelving System
rule: cantilevered shelving system must have its structural supports anchored to a load-bearing structure (wall, floor, or frame) capable of resisting the full overturning moment and shear forces

subject: Cantilevered Shelving System
rule: cantilevered shelving system must not exceed the rated load capacity per arm or per upright as specified by the manufacturer

subject: Cantilevered Shelving System
rule: cantilevered shelving system must have a minimum backspan-to-cantilever ratio that prevents forward tipping when uniformly loaded on the cantilevered portion
conditions: system is freestanding (not anchored to wall)
exceptions: system is rigidly anchored to a wall or floor with engineered brackets that resist tension uplift

subject: Cantilevered Shelving System
rule: cantilevered shelving system must be mounted plumb (vertical) within manufacturer's specified tolerance in both lateral and forward/backward directions

subject: Cantilevered Shelving System
rule: cantilevered shelving system's locking mechanism or anchor bolts must be fully engaged before placing any load on the arms

subject: Shelf Bracket
rule: Shelf bracket must support the design load (weight of shelf and its contents) without plastic deformation or failure
conditions: when installed as intended
under normal service loads

subject: Shelf Bracket
rule: Shelf bracket must be attached to a structural wall or framing member capable of supporting the bracket's rated load
exceptions: free-standing shelving systems where the bracket is part of a self-supporting frame

subject: Shelf Bracket
rule: Shelf bracket must not have sharp edges or protrusions that pose a laceration hazard during normal use or installation
conditions: when used in occupiable spaces
when accessible to occupants

subject: Shelf Bracket
rule: Shelf bracket must have a positive mechanical interlock or locking feature preventing unintentional dislodgement of the shelf from the bracket
conditions: when the shelf is not independently fastened to the bracket

subject: Free-standing Waist-high Shelf Unit
rule: shelf unit must have a flat and level base to prevent tipping
conditions: unit is free-standing
unit is waist-high
exceptions: unit is permanently anchored to floor or wall

subject: Free-standing Waist-high Shelf Unit
rule: shelf unit must not exceed its load capacity rating per shelf
conditions: shelves are used for storage

subject: Free-standing Waist-high Shelf Unit
rule: shelf unit must have a maximum height-to-depth ratio that prevents forward tipping when loaded
conditions: unit is not anchored to wall or floor

subject: Shelf to Backing Wall Interface
rule: shelf must transfer its full vertical load to the backing wall through direct bearing or properly rated shelf brackets anchored into the wall structure
conditions: shelf is supported by a backing wall
exceptions: freestanding shelving units that do not rely on a wall for support

subject: Shelf to Backing Wall Interface
rule: shelf must not rely solely on adhesive or surface friction at the backing wall interface to resist design-level vertical loads
conditions: shelf is expected to carry more than negligible decorative loads
exceptions: light decorative shelves with clearly posted weight limits not exceeding adhesive capacity

subject: Shelf to Backing Wall Interface
rule: shelf to backing wall interface must provide lateral restraint against forward pull-out at each bracket or attachment point
conditions: shelf is cantilevered from the wall
shelf carries live loads

subject: Shelf to Backing Wall Interface
rule: fasteners connecting shelf brackets to the backing wall must engage the wall's structural substrate (stud, masonry, or rated anchor substrate), not only the finish layer
conditions: wall finish layer (drywall, plaster, tile) alone cannot carry design loads

subject: Stadium Bleacher
rule: stadium bleacher must have a slip-resistant walking surface on all treads and aisles
conditions: bleacher is accessible to spectators

subject: Stadium Bleacher
rule: stadium bleacher must have guardrails or handrails where the drop height exceeds 30 inches
conditions: bleacher seating platform is elevated more than 30 inches above adjacent grade or floor
exceptions: the bleacher row is at ground level with no fall hazard

subject: Stadium Bleacher
rule: stadium bleacher must have aisle width meeting egress capacity requirements for occupant load
conditions: bleacher serves more than 49 spectators

subject: Stadium Bleacher
rule: stadium bleacher must not have openings between seat boards or between seat board and riser that exceed 4 inches in the smallest dimension
conditions: bleacher is accessible to children under 6 years old

subject: Stadium Bleacher
rule: stadium bleacher must have a structural load capacity that supports 100 psf live load on fixed seating areas
conditions: bleacher is designed for fixed spectator seating

subject: Seating Step/Terraced Step
rule: seating step/terraced step must have a horizontal surface (tread) width sufficient to safely support a seated or standing person
conditions: when intended for human occupancy
exceptions: decorative or non-accessible landscape features not designed for occupancy

subject: Seating Step/Terraced Step
rule: seating step/terraced step must have a riser height that does not exceed a safe stepping threshold
conditions: when used as stepped seating or accessible terrace
exceptions: when designed as accessible ramp with no discrete vertical risers

subject: Seating Step/Terraced Step
rule: seating step/terraced step must not have a tread surface with a slippery finish that causes loss of traction under expected conditions
conditions: when exposed to rain, moisture, or foot traffic
exceptions: temporary or ceremonial installations where slip risk is mitigated by supervision

subject: Seating Step/Terraced Step
rule: seating step/terraced step must have structural capacity to support anticipated live loads without collapse
conditions: when constructed as a load-bearing element
exceptions: purely decorative non-load-bearing landscape forms

subject: Fixed Waiting Area Seat
rule: Fixed waiting area seat must be securely anchored to the floor or structure
conditions: installed in a public transport waiting area
subject to public use
exceptions: temporary seating for events under 24 hours
seating designed to be moved for cleaning in low-traffic areas

subject: Fixed Waiting Area Seat
rule: Fixed waiting area seat must have a minimum seat width per person of at least 450 mm
conditions: serving general adult population
exceptions: seating designated exclusively for children under 12

subject: Fixed Waiting Area Seat
rule: Fixed waiting area seat must not have sharp edges or corners on occupant-contact surfaces

subject: Fixed Waiting Area Seat
rule: Fixed waiting area seat must have a slip-resistant seat surface
conditions: located outdoors or in areas exposed to moisture
exceptions: indoor seating in climate-controlled environments with documented low slip risk

subject: Courtroom Bench
rule: Courtroom bench must have a horizontal seat surface that is flat and level
conditions: when intended for seated occupancy

subject: Courtroom Bench
rule: Courtroom bench must have a minimum seat width per occupant that accommodates the hip breadth of the intended user population
conditions: when designed for simultaneous multiple occupants

subject: Courtroom Bench
rule: Courtroom bench must not have sharp edges or corners on surfaces contacted by seated occupants
conditions: in areas of occupant contact during normal use

subject: Cave Entrance Tunnel
rule: the cave entrance tunnel roof must provide adequate overhead rock cover or structural support to prevent collapse
conditions: tunnel is excavated through rock
tunnel serves as a primary means of access
exceptions: tunnel entrance is a natural existing cave requiring no excavation

subject: Cave Entrance Tunnel
rule: the cave entrance tunnel must have a continuous downward or outward drainage path from the entrance floor to prevent water pooling
conditions: tunnel is located in a region with precipitation or groundwater ingress
exceptions: tunnel is artificially sealed and actively pumped
tunnel is a seasonal archaeological site not requiring continuous occupancy

subject: Cave Entrance Tunnel
rule: the cave entrance tunnel must not have a floor slope that exceeds the safe walking gradient for its intended users
conditions: tunnel is designed for pedestrian access without handrails or mechanical assistance
exceptions: tunnel is exclusively for maintenance personnel using specialized equipment

subject: Cave Niche
rule: cave niche must have a continuous pathway for water drainage from the deepest interior point to the exterior
conditions: niche is formed in permeable or fractured rock
niche receives water ingress from seepage, condensation, or surface runoff
exceptions: niche is in extremely arid climate with no measurable precipitation or ground moisture
niche is artificially sealed with waterproof lining

subject: Cave Niche
rule: cave niche must not have a closed, unvented void that can trap radon gas or other heavier-than-air hazardous gases
conditions: niche is excavated or naturally formed below grade
niche is enclosed on more than 3 sides with limited top opening
exceptions: space is exclusively used for non-occupancy storage of inert materials and is permanently sealed and labelled as uninhabitable
forced mechanical ventilation is provided that maintains gas concentration below actionable thresholds at all times

subject: Cave Niche
rule: cave niche opening must have a clear egress dimension that allows a human body to pass in an emergency
conditions: niche is intended for human occupancy or periodic access
exceptions: niche is a purely decorative or display-only feature with no human entry permitted and is clearly marked as such

subject: Cave Structure Frame
rule: Cave structure frame must maintain a minimum rock/support thickness to prevent collapse under expected overburden and lateral loads
conditions: frame is load-bearing
frame supports overlying rock or soil mass
exceptions: frame is part of a reinforced or engineered support system with documented geotechnical analysis showing reduced thickness is acceptable

subject: Cave Structure Frame
rule: Cave structure frame must not have gaps or openings that permit uncontrolled rockfall or soil ingress into occupied or critical spaces
conditions: frame encloses an occupied or habitable space
frame is exposed to loose or fractured overburden
exceptions: planned ventilation or drainage openings are designed with rockfall prevention measures such as grilles or filters

subject: Cave Ventilation Grille
rule: cave ventilation grille must not be fully blocked or sealed
conditions: when the cave is occupied or used for any purpose requiring air exchange
exceptions: when the cave is permanently sealed for preservation or safety and no occupancy is allowed

subject: Cave Ventilation Grille
rule: cave ventilation grille must maintain a clear cross-sectional area adequate for the required ventilation rate
conditions: when the cave has any continuous occupancy or contains combustion sources
exceptions: when the cave is unoccupied and contains no combustion sources

subject: Cave Ventilation Grille
rule: cave ventilation grille must be positioned to avoid direct entry of surface water or debris into the cave
conditions: when the grille is at or below grade or in a location exposed to runoff or falling debris
exceptions: when the grille is equipped with a water/debris deflection hood or filter that prevents entry without blocking airflow

subject: Cave Window / Glazed Opening
rule: a glazed opening in a cave wall must be structurally supported to prevent collapse of the surrounding rock mass
conditions: the opening is cut into or penetrates the cave envelope
the surrounding rock is not self-supporting without intervention
exceptions: the opening is in a natural cave entrance that already has a stable arch or opening

subject: Cave Window / Glazed Opening
rule: a glazed opening in a cave must not create a path for uncontrolled water ingress into the habitable interior
conditions: the cave is located in a region with precipitation or groundwater flow
the opening penetrates the full thickness of the cave envelope
exceptions: the opening is expressly designed as a deliberate drainage or rainwater harvesting point with controlled routing

subject: Cave Window / Glazed Opening
rule: the glazing unit must be thermally isolated from the cave rock to prevent condensation-induced deterioration
conditions: the cave interior is conditioned (heated or cooled) to a temperature different from the rock mass temperature
the climate is humid enough for condensation to form on cold surfaces
exceptions: the cave environment is intentionally unconditioned and matches rock temperature

subject: Cave Access Hatch / Door
rule: Cave access hatch/door must be structurally capable of supporting the surrounding rock or earth loads without failure
conditions: When installed in a ceiling or overhead location
When earth or rock overburden is present above the hatch
exceptions: When the hatch is located in a wall or non-load-bearing partition
When a separate structural lintel or arch carries the overburden load independently of the hatch

subject: Cave Access Hatch / Door
rule: Cave access hatch/door must not open inward into a space where it would block egress or be blocked by debris
conditions: When the hatch is the primary emergency egress route from the cave space
exceptions: When the hatch is exclusively a utility/service access and not used for egress

subject: Cave Access Hatch / Door
rule: Cave access hatch/door must provide a weather-tight seal when closed
conditions: When the hatch is exposed to exterior weather conditions (rain, snow, groundwater) at grade or above grade
exceptions: When the hatch leads to a fully enclosed interior space that is itself weather-sealed and drained

subject: Cave Access Hatch / Door
rule: Cave access hatch/door must be openable from the inside without special tools or keys
conditions: When the space below or beyond the hatch is occupied by people
exceptions: When the hatch is a secured vault access with separate ventilation and emergency protocols
When the hatch is a maintenance-only access and the space is not intended for occupancy

subject: Panic Room / Safe Room
rule: panic room / safe room must have a dedicated, independent ventilation or air supply system that does not rely on the main building HVAC system
conditions: room is designed for extended occupancy (more than a few minutes)
room is sealed for security purposes
exceptions: room is only used for short-term concealment (minutes)

subject: Panic Room / Safe Room
rule: panic room / safe room must have a door that opens inward (or is designed to resist forced entry from the outside)
conditions: room is designed for occupancy during an intrusion

subject: Panic Room / Safe Room
rule: panic room / safe room must have a means of emergency egress or two-way communication to the outside
conditions: room is intended for occupancy by persons requiring rescue or evacuation

subject: Panic Room / Safe Room
rule: panic room / safe room must not rely on any single point of failure for locks, power, or ventilation that could be severed or disabled from outside
conditions: room is designed for security against an active threat

subject: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release
rule: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release must maintain magnetic engagement under specified load conditions
conditions: When used as a holding/latching mechanism
Under normal operating loads
exceptions: When intentionally released via control signal or manual override

subject: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release
rule: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release must not be exposed to direct weather ingress (rain or pressurised water) without appropriate weather sealing
conditions: When installed in outdoor or damp locations
exceptions: Latch is specifically rated for wet/outdoor use (IP65 or higher)

subject: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release
rule: Secret Latch / Magnetic Release must fail in a safe/default position (typically unlocked) upon power loss unless designed as a fail-secure system
