conditions: Used in egress paths or life-safety applications
exceptions: Installation complies with local fire/life safety codes allowing fail-secure configuration with manual release override

subject: One-Way Mirror / Observation Window
rule: One-way mirror / observation window must have the coated side facing the observed (dark) side and the observer side on the lit side for the mirroring effect to work
conditions: intended use as one-way observation

subject: One-Way Mirror / Observation Window
rule: observation window must be installed with sufficient lighting differential (bright on observer side, dim on observed side) to maintain the one-way effect
conditions: used as a one-way observation window for surveillance or research

subject: One-Way Mirror / Observation Window
rule: one-way mirror must not be subjected to temperatures exceeding the manufacturer's specified limit for the reflective coating material
conditions: any installation

subject: Hidden Surveillance System
rule: the system must be concealed such that its surveillance function is not visually detectable under normal operating conditions
conditions: when deployed in environments where covert operation is required
exceptions: in controlled/classified facilities where overt surveillance is legally permitted

subject: Hidden Surveillance System
rule: the system must not emit detectable signals (optical, acoustic, radio, or thermal) that would reveal its presence or function during covert operation
conditions: when operating in active surveillance mode within a sensitive environment
exceptions: during maintenance or testing in secured/isolated environments

subject: Hidden Surveillance System
rule: the system must have a self-contained or wire-tapped power source that does not require visible external cabling or frequent physical access for recharge
conditions: when deployed in locations where routine physical maintenance is not possible without exposing the system
exceptions: when power can be drawn from existing hidden infrastructure such as dedicated concealed conduit

subject: Acoustic Isolation Construction
rule: Acoustic isolation construction must have no rigid structural connections (acoustic bridges) between the isolated surface and the building structure
conditions: When providing acoustic isolation for walls, floors, or ceilings
exceptions: Decoupling via resilient mounts, spring hangers, or floating floor systems where the fastener itself includes an isolation element

subject: Acoustic Isolation Construction
rule: Acoustic isolation construction must have a sealed, airtight perimeter at all joints and penetrations
conditions: For any room or enclosure requiring acoustic isolation
exceptions: Intentional ventilation openings with properly designed acoustic labyrinth or silencer treatments

subject: Acoustic Isolation Construction
rule: Acoustic isolation construction must_not share a continuous structural substrate (e.g., common stud wall, continuous slab) with an adjacent space requiring different acoustic treatment
conditions: Where two adjacent spaces have different acoustic isolation requirements
exceptions: Where the substrate is decoupled with a resilient interlayer and verified by acoustic testing

subject: Acoustic Isolation Construction
rule: Acoustic isolation construction must have mass (surface density) sufficient for the target sound transmission class (STC) rating
conditions: Where a specific STC or Rw rating is required by design
exceptions: When using a tuned mass-spring-mass assembly (e.g., double-stud with insulation) that achieves the rating through resonance tuning rather than mass alone

subject: Concealed Wiring & Conduit System
rule: Concealed wiring and conduit system must be continuous and free from open joints or gaps that expose conductors
conditions: System is installed and active
exceptions: Junction boxes, pull boxes, or termination points that are properly enclosed and accessible

subject: Concealed Wiring & Conduit System
rule: Concealed wiring and conduit system must not be embedded in or directly contacting thermal insulation that prevents heat dissipation
conditions: System carries electrical current during normal operation
exceptions: Wiring specifically rated and listed for use in insulation (e.g., NM cable with 90°C rating installed per code ampacity tables)

subject: Bookshelf Door System
rule: The door must open fully without obstruction from bookshelf contents
conditions: when bookshelf is fully loaded
exceptions: if door is designed as a sliding/pocket door that clears the shelf depth

subject: Bookshelf Door System
rule: The hinge or pivot mechanism must support the combined weight of the door and attached bookshelf
conditions: when the door itself carries bookshelf structure
exceptions: if the bookshelf is floor-supported and the door is only a facade panel

subject: Bookshelf Door System
rule: The door must not swing into the pathway of users when opened on a pivot hinge
conditions: when installed in a corridor or passageway or near egress path

subject: Secret Floor Trapdoor
rule: trapdoor must be capable of supporting at least the design live load of the floor in which it is installed
conditions: installed in a load-bearing floor assembly
exceptions: when trapdoor is decorative only and clearly marked as non-load-bearing

subject: Secret Floor Trapdoor
rule: trapdoor must have a positive latching or locking mechanism that prevents unintended opening
conditions: trapdoor is located in a floor subject to pedestrian traffic
exceptions: trapdoor is secured with fasteners requiring tools for removal and area is not a means of egress

subject: Secret Floor Trapdoor
rule: trapdoor must not create a trip hazard when in the closed position
conditions: trapdoor surface is flush with surrounding finished floor
exceptions: trapdoor is in an area not intended for occupant traffic and is clearly marked

subject: Concealed Wall Safe
rule: Concealed wall safe must be installed within a wall cavity that has sufficient depth to accommodate the safe body without protruding beyond the finished wall surface
conditions: Safe is designed for flush-mount installation
exceptions: Safe is designed for surface-mount installation with intentional protrusion

subject: Concealed Wall Safe
rule: Concealed wall safe must have a door that opens fully without obstruction from adjacent wall studs, framing members, or interior wall finishes
conditions: Safe is installed within a stud-framed wall cavity
exceptions: Safe is specifically designed with a sliding or lift-off door mechanism that does not require swing clearance

subject: Concealed Wall Safe
rule: Concealed wall safe must not be installed in a wall that contains electrical wiring, plumbing pipes, or HVAC ducts within the intended installation cavity
conditions: Safe occupies the full depth of a standard stud bay (nominal 3.5" or 5.5" depth)

subject: Atrium / Internal Street
rule: atrium roof or glazing must be designed to prevent falling glass fragments in case of breakage
conditions: atrium has overhead glazing
atrium is located above occupied spaces or circulation paths
exceptions: atrium glazing is laminated safety glass with interlayer
atrium is not accessible to occupants below

subject: Atrium / Internal Street
rule: atrium floor area must be sprinkler-protected
conditions: atrium exceeds 55 ft (16.8 m) in height
atrium connects two or more floors
exceptions: atrium is separated from all adjacent spaces by fire-rated construction (not open to floors)

subject: Atrium / Internal Street
rule: atrium smoke control system must be provided
conditions: atrium connects more than two stories
atrium height exceeds limits in applicable building code
exceptions: building is fully sprinklered and atrium meets reduced-height exception per local code

subject: Atrium / Internal Street
rule: atrium must not be the sole means of egress for any occupied space
conditions: atrium is enclosed on fewer than three sides
atrium is open to multiple floors

subject: Community / Common Room
rule: Community / common room must have at least one means of egress (exit) door that leads directly to a exit discharge or public way
conditions: When the room is occupied
When designed for assembly use
exceptions: Rooms with occupant load below building code threshold for egress (typically <50 occupants) may have a single exit that leads through an adjacent space

subject: Community / Common Room
rule: Community / common room floor finish must have a slip-resistance rating appropriate for the expected use (wet or dry condition)
conditions: When the room includes food/drink service or is accessible to the general public
exceptions: Carpeted floors in dry-only lounge settings not used for food/drink

subject: Community / Common Room
rule: Community / common room must have a minimum ceiling height of 7 feet 6 inches (2.29 m) for the occupied area
conditions: When the room is intended for general assembly or gathering of people
exceptions: Existing buildings under renovation may comply with lesser heights if permitted by local code variance
Mechanical/structural soffits may project below the ceiling as long as the clear height over the occupied area meets code

subject: Community / Common Room
rule: Community / common room must not have a floor level change greater than 1/2 inch without a ramp or step treatment that complies with accessibility codes
conditions: When the room is accessible to the public or required to be accessible under ADA
exceptions: Single steps of 7 inches max rise may be used if not part of a required accessible route

subject: Integrated Bench / Window Seat
rule: Integrated bench / window seat must have structural attachment to the building frame or floor
conditions: When built as a fixed, non-freestanding element

subject: Integrated Bench / Window Seat
rule: Integrated bench / window seat must not block egress paths or required clearances
conditions: When located near doors, corridors, or means of egress

subject: Integrated Bench / Window Seat
rule: Integrated bench / window seat must have a seat height within ergonomic range for intended users
conditions: When intended for regular seating use by adults
exceptions: Custom designs for children or specific accessibility accommodations

subject: Integrated Bench / Window Seat
rule: Seat depth must not exceed a dimension that prevents comfortable upright sitting without back support
conditions: When designed without a backrest or as a simple bench
exceptions: When designed as a chaise lounge or daybed with reclined use

subject: Fitted Auditorium Seating / Tiered Benches
rule: Fitted auditorium seating / tiered benches must be securely fixed to the floor or structural substructure
conditions: Seating is installed in a fixed/permanent configuration
exceptions: Temporary or demountable seating systems designed for reconfiguration

subject: Fitted Auditorium Seating / Tiered Benches
rule: The riser height between successive rows of tiered benches must not exceed the maximum permitted by applicable building code for egress
conditions: Seating is arranged in tiered/stepped rows
exceptions: Where each row has its own independent guardrail and separate means of egress
Where local authority grants a performance-based equivalency

subject: Load-Bearing Frame
rule: A load-bearing frame must have a continuous load path from the point of load application down to the foundation
conditions: for any structural load-bearing configuration

subject: Load-Bearing Frame
rule: All members of a load-bearing frame must be capable of resisting the design loads (dead, live, wind, seismic) without exceeding material strength limits
conditions: under all expected design load combinations

subject: Load-Bearing Frame
rule: Connections in a load-bearing frame must transfer forces between connected members without premature failure
conditions: at all structural joints and connections

subject: Load-Bearing Frame
rule: A load-bearing frame must not have unstable buckling modes in compression members under design loads
conditions: for any compression member (column, strut, brace)

subject: Load-Bearing Frame
rule: The frame must have sufficient lateral stability (bracing, moment connections, or shear walls) to resist horizontal loads
conditions: when horizontal loads (wind, seismic, lateral earth pressure) can occur

subject: Lateral Force Resisting System
rule: lateral force resisting system must provide a continuous load path from the point of lateral force application to the foundation
conditions: building is subjected to lateral loads (wind, seismic, or other horizontal forces)

subject: Lateral Force Resisting System
rule: lateral force resisting system must not have stiffness discontinuities (soft/weak stories) that exceed code-allowed limits
conditions: building has multiple stories
seismic design category is D, E, or F
exceptions: buildings designed with energy-dissipating devices or special detailing specifically intended to accommodate the discontinuity

subject: Lateral Force Resisting System
rule: lateral force resisting system must be provided in each principal direction of the building
conditions: building is three or more stories in height
or building is in a high-seismic or high-wind region
exceptions: one-story buildings with symmetric, torsionally balanced layouts in low-seismic/low-wind regions

subject: Lateral Force Resisting System
rule: lateral force resisting system must resist torsion due to eccentricity between center of mass and center of rigidity
conditions: floor diaphragms are rigid or semi-rigid
and the building is not torsionally irregular per code definition

subject: Structural Connection
rule: a structural connection must transfer load between connected elements without relative movement exceeding serviceability limits
conditions: when the connection is designed as rigid or semi-rigid
exceptions: when the connection is intentionally designed as a slip-critical or movement joint

subject: Structural Connection
rule: a structural connection must not permit separation of connected members under factored design loads
conditions: under ultimate limit state loading conditions
exceptions: connections designed as intentional break-away or fuse elements in seismic or blast applications

subject: Structural Connection
rule: a structural connection must have a load path capable of transferring all applied forces (axial, shear, moment) to the supporting structure

subject: Structural Wall
rule: structural wall must be laterally braced or have adequate thickness to prevent buckling under design loads
conditions: wall is loadbearing
wall height exceeds allowable unbraced length
exceptions: walls designed as non-loadbearing partitions

subject: Structural Wall
rule: structural wall must transfer vertical loads continuously to the foundation without interruption
conditions: wall is loadbearing

subject: Structural Wall
rule: structural wall must not contain openings that reduce its effective structural capacity below required design loads
conditions: wall is loadbearing
exceptions: openings are structurally framed with lintels/headers and the remaining wall area is verified to carry all loads

subject: Structural Wall
rule: structural wall must be supported on a foundation or structural element capable of bearing its load
conditions: wall is loadbearing

subject: Structural Wall
rule: structural wall must have minimum reinforcement (or equivalent structural provision) to resist lateral wind or seismic forces
conditions: wall is designed as a shear wall
wall is in a seismically or wind-active zone
exceptions: walls in non-seismic and low-wind regions where code permits unreinforced masonry under strict height and thickness limits

subject: Structural Steelwork
rule: structural steelwork must be designed to support specified loads (dead, live, wind, seismic) without yielding, buckling, or excessive deflection
conditions: when structural steel is used as primary load-bearing frame
exceptions: temporary structures where controlled deformation is acceptable
non-structural steel elements such as cladding supports or handrails not required to carry primary loads

subject: Structural Steelwork
rule: structural steelwork welds and bolts must achieve specified minimum strength and ductility
conditions: when welded or bolted connections are used
for all load-bearing connections
exceptions: tack welds used only for temporary assembly
pins or specialty connections where code allows reduced ductility

subject: Structural Steelwork
rule: structural steelwork must not have material thickness below the minimum specified for corrosion allowance and buckling resistance
conditions: when exposed to outdoor environment or corrosive conditions
exceptions: steel protected by an approved corrosion protection system (e.g., galvanizing, paint system) that is maintained throughout design life

subject: Structural Steelwork
rule: structural steel members must be laterally braced to prevent lateral-torsional buckling at design loads
conditions: for beams and girders with unsupported compression flanges
exceptions: members where LTB is explicitly checked and the unbraced length is within code limits

subject: Structural Steelwork
rule: structural steelwork must have fire protection applied to achieve required fire resistance rating
conditions: when building code requires fire-rated structural framing
for steel members in enclosed occupied spaces
exceptions: exposed steel designed to maintain structural stability at elevated temperatures (e.g., fire-engineered design with verified performance)
steel in unoccupied or external areas where code exempts fire protection

subject: Structural Timber
rule: Structural timber must have a moisture content below 20% at time of enclosure to prevent fungal decay in service
conditions: timber is used in an enclosed building assembly
timber is not pressure-treated with preservatives
exceptions: timber in naturally well-ventilated open structures where drying can continue indefinitely

subject: Structural Timber
rule: Structural timber must not be in direct contact with ground or concrete without a capillary break (e.g., damp-proof membrane)
conditions: timber is used in foundation-level or ground-contact applications
exceptions: timber species with natural durability class 1 (e.g., greenheart) used in permanent ground-contact applications

subject: Structural Timber
rule: Structural timber must be protected from direct weather exposure when used in external applications unless the species has natural durability class 1 or 2
conditions: timber is exposed to exterior climatic conditions
timber is not preservative-treated to HAZ class 4 or higher
exceptions: durability class 1 heartwood (e.g., ipe, greenheart) used without additional cladding

subject: Structural Timber
rule: Structural timber connections must not rely solely on end-grain fasteners for load transfer in tension
conditions: connection is in tension or combined tension-shear
fasteners (screws, nails, dowels) are driven into end grain only
exceptions: screws specifically rated for end-grain withdrawal capacity with documented test data
epoxy-injected threaded rods in glulam

subject: Masonry Structure
rule: masonry structure must have a continuous load path from roof to foundation
conditions: applies to all load-bearing masonry structures
exceptions: non-load-bearing masonry veneer or cladding systems

subject: Masonry Structure
rule: masonry structure must not have unrestrained openings larger than the structural code allows without lintels or arches
conditions: applies to openings in load-bearing masonry walls
exceptions: openings fully within non-load-bearing infill panels
openings in reinforced masonry designed per engineered calculations

subject: Masonry Structure
rule: masonry structure must be designed to accommodate differential movement between masonry and other materials
conditions: applies where masonry interfaces with structural frames, foundations, or other dissimilar materials
exceptions: monolithic all-masonry construction with uniform materials throughout

subject: Masonry Structure
rule: masonry structure must have a moisture barrier or drainage plane between the masonry and interior spaces below grade
conditions: applies to below-grade masonry walls or retaining walls
exceptions: interior spaces not intended to be habitable or dry (e.g., ventilated crawlspaces with drainage)

subject: Precast Concrete Element
rule: Precast concrete element must have lifting inserts or anchor points for handling and erection
conditions: element is intended to be lifted or transported
element weight exceeds manual handling capacity
exceptions: element is cast-in-place without precasting (i.e., not actually precast)
element is designed with alternative integrated lifting system

subject: Precast Concrete Element
rule: Precast concrete element must have dimensionally consistent formwork to maintain specified tolerances
conditions: element is mass-produced in a precast plant
tolerances are specified in design documentation
exceptions: element is a one-off custom piece with post-cast adjustments

subject: Precast Concrete Element
rule: Precast concrete element must not have rebar less than the minimum cover specified for its exposure class
conditions: element is exposed to environmental conditions (e.g., moisture, chlorides, freeze-thaw)
exceptions: element is protected by a secondary cladding or coating system that provides equivalent durability

subject: Recycled Aggregate Concrete
rule: Recycled aggregate concrete must have a maximum replacement ratio of coarse natural aggregate with recycled aggregate
conditions: when used in structural applications
exceptions: non-structural applications like fill or sub-base

subject: Recycled Aggregate Concrete
rule: Recycled aggregate concrete must not contain recycled aggregate sourced from contaminated demolition waste (e.g., asbestos, chemicals, organic matter)
conditions: for any application where concrete is exposed to the environment or humans

subject: Recycled Aggregate Concrete
rule: Recycled aggregate must be pre-saturated or batched with additional water compensation
conditions: when used in structural concrete
exceptions: if a superplasticizer and low w/c ratio design is used with dry aggregate and verified workability

subject: Natural Stone
rule: Natural stone used as a cladding or veneer must be mechanically anchored to the structure
conditions: when used as exterior cladding
when used as wall veneer
thickness exceeds 2 inches
exceptions: cast stone or manufactured stone substitutes
thin stone veneer applied with adhesive only (typically under 2 inches thick and low height)

subject: Natural Stone
rule: Natural stone must not be used in direct contact with earth or buried without a capillary break or waterproofing barrier
conditions: when used at or below grade
in contact with soil
exceptions: stone foundations historically set in lime mortar may be acceptable in specific heritage contexts with appropriate drainage

subject: Natural Stone
rule: Natural stone lintels and sills must extend a minimum bearing length onto the supporting masonry on each side
conditions: when used as lintels over openings
when used as window sills

subject: Natural Stone
rule: Natural stone must not be used in horizontal or low-slope (less than 1:12 pitch) walking surfaces without proper slip resistance treatment
conditions: when used as paving
when used as stair treads
when used as flooring in wet areas
exceptions: surfaces finished with a textured or flamed finish that meets slip-resistance standards
surfaces not intended for pedestrian traffic

subject: Rapidly Renewable Flooring
rule: Rapidly renewable flooring must be installed over a structurally adequate, stable subfloor that meets minimum load-bearing requirements
conditions: Applies to all rapidly renewable flooring materials (e.g., bamboo, cork, linoleum, wheatboard)
exceptions: Temporary floating floor systems designed for event use may be exempt

subject: Rapidly Renewable Flooring
rule: Rapidly renewable flooring must not be installed in continuously wet or submerged conditions
conditions: Applies to most rapidly renewable materials such as bamboo, cork, and wheatboard which are not rated for continuous moisture exposure
exceptions: Some rapidly renewable materials (e.g., linoleum with proper backing and sealing) may tolerate occasional dampness but not standing water

subject: Rapidly Renewable Flooring
rule: Rapidly renewable flooring must be acclimated to the installation environment before installation
conditions: Applies to dimensionally responsive materials such as bamboo and cork

subject: Salvaged/Reclaimed Materials
rule: salvaged or reclaimed materials must be structurally sound and free of latent defects (e.g., rot, corrosion, fatigue cracks, chemical contamination) before incorporation into a load-bearing assembly
conditions: material is used in a structural or load-bearing capacity
exceptions: material is used solely for non-structural decorative or aesthetic purposes

subject: Salvaged/Reclaimed Materials
rule: salvaged or reclaimed wood must not contain active fungal decay, insect infestation, or embedded ferrous metal fragments that compromise fastener integrity
conditions: material is wood or timber
exceptions: contaminants can be fully removed by remediation or re-sawing without reducing member capacity below design requirements

subject: Salvaged/Reclaimed Materials
rule: salvaged steel members must be tested for brittle fracture susceptibility if they originate from pre-1970 construction or unknown source
conditions: material is structural steel
steel is used in a tension or moment-resisting connection
exceptions: certified mill test reports or equivalent material traceability confirms the steel is of known, weldable grade

subject: Recycled Metal Cladding
rule: Recycled metal cladding must be compatible with the substrate or framing system to which it is attached
conditions: When used as exterior wall cladding or rainscreen
exceptions: Self-supporting structural metal panel systems

subject: Recycled Metal Cladding
rule: Recycled metal cladding must not be used in direct contact with dissimilar metals without an isolation layer
conditions: When installed adjacent to galvanically incompatible metals (e.g., untreated steel, aluminum, copper) in the presence of moisture
exceptions: When a dielectric break or corrosion barrier is placed between the metals

subject: Recycled Metal Cladding
rule: Recycled metal cladding panels must be designed to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction
conditions: When installed in any exterior application with ambient temperature variation exceeding 20°C
exceptions: Very small panel sizes where expansion gaps are inherently provided by the joint detail

subject: Durable Composite Decking
rule: Durable composite decking must have a minimum slope of 1/4 inch per foot (2% grade) away from the building structure
conditions: when installed as a horizontal walking surface
when installed adjacent to a building
exceptions: when the decking is designed with a built-in drainage system that actively manages water

subject: Durable Composite Decking
rule: Durable composite decking must not be directly installed over solid substrate without ventilation gap
conditions: when installed over solid surfaces such as concrete slabs or roof membranes
exceptions: when manufacturer specifically certifies the product for direct-deck application over that substrate

subject: Durable Composite Decking
rule: Durable composite decking must be installed with expansion gaps at ends and between boards
conditions: in any installation
exceptions: when manufacturer's specifications explicitly state no-gap installation is acceptable for the specific product and climate

subject: Low-Embodied-Energy Masonry
rule: Low-embodied-energy masonry must not include Portland-cement-based mortars or binders that undergo high-temperature calcination
conditions: Material is classified as 'low-embodied-energy' masonry
Mortar or binder is part of the assembled masonry system
exceptions: Alternative low-carbon cements (e.g., geopolymer, alkali-activated) that have documented lower embodied energy may be acceptable

subject: Low-Embodied-Energy Masonry
rule: Low-embodied-energy masonry units must not be fired in kilns at conventional ceramic-firing temperatures (above 900°C)
conditions: Units are clay-based, terracotta, or ceramic masonry
exceptions: Units fired using entirely renewable energy with documented net-zero or net-negative embodied carbon

subject: Low-Embodied-Energy Masonry
rule: Low-embodied-energy masonry assembly must maintain structural stability under design loads without relying on high-embodied-energy reinforcement as the primary load-path
conditions: Masonry is used as a loadbearing element
Alternative low-embodied-energy reinforcement strategies (e.g., natural fiber, bamboo, unreinforced geometry) are feasible for the span and loading
exceptions: Localized steel reinforcement at connections or openings where no low-energy alternative can achieve code-required strength

subject: Recycled Plastic Construction Products
rule: Recycled plastic construction products must not be exposed to temperatures above their melting point or sustained softening temperature
conditions: When used in structural or load-bearing applications
When exposed to direct sunlight or high-heat environments
During processing, installation, or fire conditions
exceptions: Products specifically formulated with high-temperature stabilizers and fire retardants rated for the expected temperature range

subject: Recycled Plastic Construction Products
rule: Recycled plastic construction products must be protected from prolonged ultraviolet (UV) radiation unless specifically formulated for UV resistance
conditions: When used in exterior applications
When the product contains a significant fraction of recycled polymer that lacks UV stabilizers
exceptions: Products with verified UV stabilization (e.g., UV-absorbing additives, coextruded cap layers, opaque coatings) tested for the expected service life

subject: Recycled Plastic Construction Products
rule: Recycled plastic construction products used in load-bearing applications must have documented mechanical properties (strength, stiffness, creep resistance) from batch-specific testing
conditions: When the product is used as a structural element (e.g., beams, decking, piles, joists)
When design loads exceed 10% of the material's rated short-term capacity
exceptions: Non-structural uses only (e.g., trim, cladding, decorative elements)

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bale walls must be kept dry during construction and service life
conditions: All straw bale construction projects
exceptions: None

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bale walls must have a breathable (vapor-permeable) finish on both faces
conditions: All straw bale construction projects
exceptions: None

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bale walls must be raised off the ground on a plinth or foundation that prevents ground moisture wicking
conditions: All straw bale construction projects
exceptions: None

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bale walls must not be load-bearing for more than one story without engineered structural reinforcement
conditions: Straw bale load-bearing wall designs
exceptions: None

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bales must be densely packed and free of voids before plastering
conditions: All straw bale construction projects
exceptions: None

subject: Straw Bale Construction
rule: Straw bale walls must be protected from vermin and pest intrusion
conditions: All straw bale construction projects
exceptions: None

subject: Rammed Earth
rule: Rammed earth walls must have a continuous, impermeable capillary break (damp-proof course) between the wall and any foundation or ground-contact structure
conditions: wall is load-bearing
foundation is below grade or in contact with soil
exceptions: wall is built on a fully drained, raised plinth with no direct ground contact

subject: Rammed Earth
rule: Rammed earth must not be exposed to continuous lateral water pressure or standing water against the wall face
conditions: wall is exterior or retaining
exceptions: wall is designed specifically as a submerged rammed earth structure with full waterproofing and structural reinforcement

subject: Rammed Earth
rule: Rammed earth walls must be protected by an overhang, eaves, or gutter system that prevents rainwater from running directly down the wall face
conditions: wall is external and exposed to rainfall
exceptions: wall surface is treated with a tested, vapor-permeable water-repellent coating and has a sloped top cap

subject: Rammed Earth
rule: The formwork release agent used during compaction must not be a petroleum-based or non-biodegradable oil that contaminates the earth
conditions: formwork is used for rammed earth compaction

subject: Cob Construction
rule: cob walls must be protected from direct water erosion by a roof overhang, foundation plinth, or breathable render
conditions: wall is exposed to rainfall
exceptions: walls in arid climates with annual rainfall below 250mm

subject: Cob Construction
rule: cob walls must not be sealed with impermeable cement or acrylic renders
conditions: exterior finish is applied

subject: Cob Construction
rule: cob construction must not be used in seismic zones without reinforcement (vertical bamboo, timber, or steel rodding through the wall core)
conditions: building is located in seismic zone with expected peak ground acceleration > 0.1g
exceptions: single-storey buildings with height < 3 m and length < 8 m in very low seismicity areas

subject: Cob Construction
rule: cob walls must not exceed a height-to-thickness ratio of 8:1 for load-bearing walls
conditions: wall is load-bearing and unstabilised
exceptions: walls with mechanical stabilisation (cement or lime) or approved structural engineering

subject: Cob Construction
rule: cob foundation must extend at least 150 mm above finished grade

subject: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam
rule: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam must have a closed-cell structure or be protected by a vapor barrier when installed in high-humidity environments (e.g., below-grade, bathrooms, or continuous occupancy spaces with >60% RH)
conditions: installation in high-humidity environments
below-grade application
bathroom application
continuous occupancy spaces with >60% RH
exceptions: material is inherently hydrophobic and water-resistance testing confirms < 5% moisture absorption by volume

subject: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam
rule: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam must not be installed in direct contact with hot surfaces exceeding the material's maximum service temperature (typically 80°C / 176°F for polyurethane-based foams)
conditions: application near heat sources
adjacent to flues
adjacent to chimneys
adjacent to recessed lighting fixtures not rated for insulation contact (IC-rated)
exceptions: a thermal barrier or heat shield rated for that temperature is placed between the foam and the hot surface

subject: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam
rule: Low-Carbon Insulation Foam must achieve a minimum aged R-value per unit thickness as declared by the manufacturer under standardized test conditions (ASTM C518 or equivalent)
conditions: material is used as the primary thermal insulation layer in a building envelope assembly
exceptions: material is used only as an air-sealing gasket or filler rather than for thermal resistance
a secondary insulation layer compensates for the reduced thermal performance

subject: Green Roof Growing Medium
rule: Green roof growing medium must be stable enough to resist erosion from wind and water runoff without slumping or washing away
conditions: installed on a slope greater than 2:12
exceptions: when the growing medium is encapsulated within a rigid tray/module system that provides mechanical retention

subject: Green Roof Growing Medium
rule: Green roof growing medium must not contain components that will decompose and significantly shrink in volume over the design life of the roof

subject: Green Roof Growing Medium
rule: Green roof growing medium must be sufficiently permeable to allow water to drain through it to the roof drainage system

subject: Green Roof Growing Medium
rule: Green roof growing medium must have a particle size distribution that prevents migration of fines into the drainage layer
conditions: when a separate drainage layer is present below the growing medium
exceptions: when the growing medium and drainage layer are a single integrated manufactured system designed to accommodate fines migration

subject: Hempcrete
rule: Hempcrete must not be used in structural load-bearing applications such as primary beams, columns, or foundations
conditions: when used as the sole structural material
in load-bearing walls beyond low-rise single-story construction
exceptions: when used in timber-frame infill systems where the timber frame carries all structural loads
when combined with a separate structural frame (e.g., steel or timber post-and-beam)

subject: Hempcrete
rule: Hempcrete must be protected from continuous liquid water exposure and standing water
conditions: in foundation applications
in below-grade walls
in areas subject to ponding or hydrostatic pressure
exceptions: when fully encapsulated by a continuous waterproof barrier and drainage system designed by a licensed engineer

subject: Hempcrete
rule: Hempcrete must have a minimum density of 200 kg/m³ when used in wall applications
conditions: when used in exterior walls
when used in interior partition walls that require mechanical fixings
exceptions: when used as a loose-fill insulation in attic spaces where no mechanical loading or plaster attachment is required

subject: Hempcrete
rule: Hempcrete must not be exposed to sustained temperatures exceeding 200°C
conditions: in proximity to chimneys, flues, or heating appliances
in fire-rated assemblies without additional fire protection
exceptions: when separated by a minimum 200 mm air gap and a non-combustible barrier (e.g., mineral wool or fire-rated board)

subject: Mycelium Building Materials
rule: Mycelium building materials must remain dry during service life
conditions: When used as structural or insulating components in building envelopes
exceptions: Materials specifically engineered and tested for wet or submerged conditions

subject: Mycelium Building Materials
rule: Mycelium building materials must not be continuously submerged in water
conditions: When used as a permanent structural or insulating element
exceptions: Specially formulated or treated mycelium materials with proven waterproofing and submerged durability testing

subject: Recycled Bricks
rule: Recycled bricks must not be used in load-bearing structural applications without explicit engineering certification
conditions: Used in structural context
Load-bearing application
exceptions: Engineer has certified specific load capacity through testing

subject: Recycled Bricks
rule: Recycled bricks must be free of adhered mortar and debris before use in new masonry
conditions: Bricks are being laid with fresh mortar in new wall/assembly
exceptions: Bricks are used as crushed aggregate or fill material

subject: Recycled Bricks
rule: Recycled bricks must not be used in freeze-thaw exposed exterior applications unless proven frost-resistant
conditions: Exterior application
Climate with freeze-thaw cycles
Brick is exposed to moisture
exceptions: Each brick batch has been tested and shown to have freeze-thaw durability per ASTM C67 or equivalent

subject: Stiffness-Graded Frame
rule: a stiffness-graded frame must have a continuous load path from the topmost member to the foundation

subject: Stiffness-Graded Frame
rule: a stiffness-graded frame must not have abrupt or discontinuous changes in member stiffness between adjacent bays or storeys
exceptions: intentional weak-link fuse elements designed for ductile energy dissipation at predefined locations

subject: Stiffness-Graded Frame
rule: a stiffness-graded frame must have member-to-member connections capable of transferring the design forces at the stiffness transition interfaces

subject: Progressive Collapse Resistance
rule: Structural system must provide alternate load paths to redistribute gravity loads after a localized failure
conditions: Building is of normal occupancy Risk Category II or higher
Building height exceeds 4 stories or has critical public safety function
exceptions: Buildings designed for specific threats where alternative protective measures are used in lieu of redundancy
One-story buildings with low occupancy

subject: Progressive Collapse Resistance
rule: Tie forces must be continuous and capable of transferring tensile forces between vertical structural elements across all floor and roof levels
conditions: Building is of normal occupancy Risk Category II or higher
Structural system is of cast-in-place reinforced concrete, precast concrete, or structural steel
exceptions: Loadbearing masonry or timber structures where tie force provisions are replaced by alternative ductility measures

subject: Progressive Collapse Resistance
rule: Key structural elements (critical columns and transfer girders) must not be designed with a load-bearing capacity less than that required for the notional removal of an adjacent element
conditions: Building employs notional element removal as the verification method for collapse resistance
exceptions: Structures where alternate load path is verified through nonlinear dynamic analysis rather than reduced capacity of key elements

subject: Progressive Collapse Resistance
rule: Structural connection ductility must be sufficient to sustain rotations corresponding to the removal of a vertical support without brittle fracture
conditions: Steel or composite structural system
Connection involves welded or bolted moment-resisting joints
exceptions: Pinned connections not counted on for collapse resistance
Seismic-designed special moment frames with proven ductility exceeding collapse rotation demands

subject: Progressive Collapse Resistance
rule: Floor-to-floor vertical continuity of columns must be maintained without offset or transfer at intermediate floors that would eliminate the load path
conditions: Building is above 4 stories in height
Transfer girders or columns are present at intermediate levels
exceptions: Explicit structural analysis demonstrating that a transfer system redistributes loads under notional column removal

subject: Belt Truss / Outrigger System
rule: belt truss / outrigger system must connect the core to perimeter columns at one or more discrete heights along the building's vertical axis
conditions: building height exceeds approximately 30 stories
lateral loads (wind or seismic) govern structural design

subject: Belt Truss / Outrigger System
rule: belt truss / outrigger system must possess sufficient axial stiffness in the connecting elements (core-to-outrigger and outrigger-to-column) to develop the intended couple action
conditions: system is relied upon for lateral stability

subject: Belt Truss / Outrigger System
rule: outrigger system must not be interrupted at the level of a major vertical circulation or mechanical floor unless the truss is structurally continuous around the opening
conditions: a floor opening larger than one bay width exists at the outrigger level

subject: Tapered Building Form
rule: a tapered building form must have a roof drainage system that accommodates the non-horizontal roof slope(s)
conditions: the building has a roof
the roof is sloped due to the tapered form
exceptions: the tapered form does not include a roof (e.g., open-top structure)
the roof is intentionally designed as a water-collection surface with controlled drainage

subject: Tapered Building Form
rule: a tapered building form must not create a roof slope steeper than the maximum allowable for the roof membrane or cladding system specified
conditions: the tapered form results in a roof slope
a roof membrane or cladding is installed
exceptions: the roof membrane or cladding is specifically rated for the resulting slope
no membrane/cladding is used (e.g., green roof with engineered drainage layer)

subject: Tapered Building Form
rule: a tapered building form must provide lateral stability against the asymmetric loads induced by the taper
conditions: the taper introduces significant asymmetry in the building's lateral force-resisting system
the building is subject to wind or seismic loads
exceptions: the taper is slight and does not produce net eccentricity beyond code-allowed accidental eccentricity
the structure is designed with a lateral system that inherently resists asymmetric loads (e.g., central core)

subject: Stiffness-Tuned Floor Diaphragm
rule: stiffness-tuned floor diaphragm must maintain in-plane rigidity sufficient to distribute lateral loads to vertical lateral-force-resisting elements without excessive deformation
conditions: when functioning as a structural diaphragm in a seismic or wind load path

subject: Stiffness-Tuned Floor Diaphragm
rule: stiffness-tuned floor diaphragm must have continuous chord reinforcement or boundary elements at its perimeter to develop the required flexural and shear capacity
conditions: when constructed as a reinforced concrete or composite diaphragm

subject: Stiffness-Tuned Floor Diaphragm
rule: stiffness-tuned floor diaphragm must not have abrupt discontinuities or openings that exceed the proportion limits established by the structural design for stiffness tuning
conditions: where openings or discontinuities are present in the diaphragm
exceptions: openings that are specifically reinforced to maintain the intended stiffness distribution

subject: Transfer Plate / Podium Stiffening
rule: Transfer plate / podium stiffening must have sufficient reinforcement to resist punching shear at column-transfer plate junctions
conditions: where transfer plate supports columns from upper structure
where slab-column connections exist without drop panels
exceptions: when a validated structural analysis demonstrates that concrete alone provides adequate shear resistance without additional reinforcement

subject: Transfer Plate / Podium Stiffening
rule: Transfer plate / podium stiffening must not have abrupt changes in thickness exceeding the structural code limit for deep beam/slab transitions
conditions: where the transfer plate acts as a deep beam or thick slab
exceptions: when the transition zone is structurally reinforced and detailed according to a code-approved step detail

subject: Eaves / Soffit
rule: Eaves must provide a continuous drainage path from the roof surface to the gutter or ground
conditions: building has a pitched roof
building is located in a region with precipitation
exceptions: flat roof buildings where eaves are absent

subject: Eaves / Soffit
rule: Soffit must be ventilated when the roof assembly is designed as a cold roof with insulation at the ceiling plane
conditions: roof is a cold roof design with insulation at ceiling level
roof deck is not a warm roof/insulated roof deck assembly
exceptions: warm roof assemblies where insulation is above the roof deck
uninhabited buildings with no moisture-sensitive materials in the roof cavity

subject: Eaves / Soffit
rule: Eaves must not terminate within 900 mm of a flue or chimney outlet
conditions: building has a chimney or flue venting combustion products
exceptions: flue is tested and rated for closer proximity
flue extends at least 600 mm above the eave plane

subject: Roof Penetrations / Curbs
rule: roof curbs must be flashed and sealed watertight at the penetration-to-roof interface
conditions: roof penetration or curb is installed through the roof membrane

subject: Roof Penetrations / Curbs
rule: roof curbs must be structurally adequate to support the imposed load of the penetrating element (e.g., HVAC unit, pipe, vent)
conditions: curb supports equipment or a penetrating element that transfers load to the curb

subject: Roof Penetrations / Curbs
rule: roof penetrations must not compromise the fire rating of the roof assembly
conditions: the roof assembly has a required fire-resistance rating
exceptions: fire-rated penetration assemblies or firestop systems are used to maintain the rating

subject: Roof Penetrations / Curbs
rule: roof penetrations must not be located in a roof drainage valley or within the path of concentrated water flow

subject: Roof Truss
rule: roof truss must have a structural load path that transfers all design loads to supports
conditions: when used as a primary load-bearing element
exceptions: when truss is purely decorative and not part of the load-resisting system

subject: Roof Truss
rule: roof truss must have all members connected at nodes to form a triangulated framework
conditions: when designed as a triangulated truss system

subject: Roof Truss
rule: roof truss must not have connections that fail before the designed ultimate load is reached
exceptions: intentional fuse elements designed for controlled failure in specific scenarios such as seismic

subject: Roof Truss
rule: roof truss must have lateral bracing adequate to prevent buckling of compression members
conditions: when any truss member is in compression

subject: Roof Framing
rule: roof framing must have a minimum slope to ensure positive drainage
conditions: roof is flat or low-slope
roof is located in a region with precipitation
exceptions: roof is designed as a 'green roof' with engineered drainage layers
roof includes a tapered insulation system that creates slope

subject: Roof Framing
rule: roof framing must not allow ponding water under design live load conditions
conditions: roof is designed as a flat or low-slope roof
exceptions: roof is specifically designed for controlled water retention (e.g., vegetative roof with approved structural analysis)

subject: Roof Framing
rule: roof framing must resist uplift forces from wind
conditions: roof is located in a region subject to wind loads (all inhabited areas)

subject: Roof Framing
rule: roof framing must support the imposed dead load of roofing materials and live loads without exceeding allowable deflection

subject: Roof Framing
rule: roof framing must not have incompatible material interfaces that cause galvanic corrosion in structural connections
conditions: roof framing includes dissimilar metals in direct contact within an electrolyte-prone environment (e.g., coastal or industrial atmosphere)
exceptions: dissimilar metals are electrically isolated by non-conductive bushings, coatings, or flashing

subject: Gutter System
rule: gutter must have continuous slope toward downspout outlets
conditions: gravity drainage is used
exceptions: internal siphonic drainage systems that operate under negative pressure

subject: Gutter System
rule: gutter cross-sectional area must be sufficient for the design rainfall intensity and tributary roof area
conditions: system is designed for a known rainfall return period
exceptions: buildings in arid regions with no precipitation design requirement

subject: Gutter System
rule: gutter outlet must not be blocked by debris, bird mesh, or other obstruction at the point of discharge
conditions: outlet leads to a downspout

subject: Gutter System
rule: gutter material must be compatible with adjacent roof and flashing materials to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: adjacent metals are dissimilar and in direct contact
exceptions: insulating gaskets or separators are installed between dissimilar metals

subject: Flat Roof
rule: Flat roof must have a minimum slope (typically at least 1:80 or 1/8" per foot) for positive drainage
conditions: roof is designed as a low-slope flat roof
roof is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: roof is an interior/atrium roof with no weather exposure
roof is a green roof designed with engineered drainage layers that satisfy drainage via the substrate

subject: Flat Roof
rule: Flat roof must have a waterproof membrane or roofing system that is continuous and watertight
conditions: roof is exposed to weather
exceptions: roof is purely decorative with a conditioned space below that has its own independent waterproofing (extremely rare)

subject: Flat Roof
rule: Flat roof must not have standing water for more than 48 hours after rainfall
conditions: roof is classified as a low-slope or flat roof per building code
roof is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: roof is specifically designed as a ponding/water-retention roof for thermal or ecological purposes with structural capacity verified

subject: Flat Roof
rule: Flat roof must have overflow scuppers or secondary drainage when primary drains are blocked
conditions: roof has parapet walls
roof is located in a region with significant rainfall
exceptions: roof area is less than a threshold where code permits single drainage path
roof is designed with internal overflow standpipes meeting code

subject: Pitched Roof
rule: Pitched roof must have a drainage path that directs water away from the building
conditions: roof is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: roof is entirely enclosed by another structure and never exposed to rain/snow

subject: Pitched Roof
rule: Pitched roof must have a slope angle greater than 0 degrees relative to horizontal

subject: Pitched Roof
rule: Pitched roof must not have load-bearing elements that are incompatible with the rafter/truss span and pitch
conditions: roof supports additional live loads such as snow, maintenance personnel, or equipment
exceptions: roof is a purely decorative non-structural canopy with no load requirement

subject: Ceiling Membrane
rule: ceiling membrane must be installed with a vapour barrier on the warm side of the assembly
conditions: assembly is in a climate with significant heating or cooling season
membrane is part of a conditioned envelope
exceptions: membrane is part of a ventilated ceiling assembly specifically designed to manage moisture without a vapour barrier

subject: Ceiling Membrane
rule: ceiling membrane must not be installed in direct contact with recessed lighting fixtures not rated for insulation contact (IC-rated)
conditions: ceiling incorporates recessed lighting
exceptions: fixtures are IC-rated and listed for direct contact with the membrane material

subject: Ceiling Membrane
rule: ceiling membrane must be attached to a supporting structure capable of bearing its dead load plus any imposed live loads

subject: Suspended Ceiling Grid
rule: Suspended ceiling grid must be suspended from the structure above (slab or roof deck) by hangers/wires
conditions: Ceiling is present
Grid is load-bearing for ceiling tiles and light fixtures
exceptions: Non-suspended direct-fixed ceiling systems

subject: Suspended Ceiling Grid
rule: Suspended ceiling grid must have hangers spaced at maximum intervals specified by code/manufacturer
conditions: Ceiling weight and tile/ fixture loads are within standard ranges
exceptions: Engineered alternative systems with validated structural calculations

subject: Suspended Ceiling Grid
rule: Suspended ceiling grid must not be used as a structural support platform for heavy equipment not designed for ceiling integration
conditions: Equipment weight exceeds grid design load capacity
exceptions: Equipment specifically designed and rated for suspended ceiling attachment per manufacturer approval

subject: Suspended Ceiling Grid
rule: Suspended ceiling grid must maintain minimum clearance above ceiling tiles for fire sprinkler coverage and smoke control
conditions: Building is sprinklered
Ceiling is in a fire zone requiring sprinkler coverage
exceptions: Alternative engineered fire protection design approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Floor Finish Layer
rule: floor finish layer must be compatible with the substrate to which it is applied
conditions: when applied directly to a substrate
exceptions: when a proper bonding primer or underlayment is used as an intermediate layer

subject: Floor Finish Layer
rule: floor finish layer must not create a trip hazard at transitions
conditions: where the finish layer abuts another flooring material, a door threshold, or a change in elevation
exceptions: when a flush transition strip or tapered edge is installed per accessibility standards

subject: Floor Finish Layer
rule: floor finish layer must have adequate slip resistance for the intended occupancy
conditions: in wet areas such as showers, pool decks, commercial kitchens, or entryways
exceptions: in dry, low-traffic private residential areas where slip is not a primary risk

subject: Floor Finish Layer
rule: floor finish layer must not emit volatile organic compounds above regulated limits in enclosed occupied spaces
conditions: when installed in interior, conditioned, occupied spaces
exceptions: in exterior, unconditioned, or non-occupiable spaces such as mechanical rooms with dedicated ventilation

subject: Underlayment
rule: Underlayment must be installed directly over the roof deck and under the roof covering
conditions: roof assembly includes underlayment
exceptions: buildings with no roof covering (e.g., certain historic or decorative structures)

subject: Underlayment
rule: Underlayment must not have gaps, tears, or punctures that expose the roof deck
conditions: underlayment is installed

subject: Underlayment
rule: Underlayment must be fastened securely so it cannot be uplifted by wind before the roof covering is applied
conditions: underlayment is installed in a wind-prone region
roof covering is not yet installed
exceptions: fully adhered membrane systems that are self-adhering and do not require mechanical fasteners

subject: Radiant Floor Heating/Cooling
rule: Radiant floor heating/cooling water supply temperature must not exceed the maximum safe operating temperature of the flooring material directly above it
conditions: system is hydronic (water-based)
flooring material has a known maximum temperature rating
exceptions: a dedicated thermal break or decoupling layer rated for higher temperatures is installed between the tubing and the flooring

subject: Radiant Floor Heating/Cooling
rule: Radiant floor heating/cooling system must operate at fluid temperatures below the boiling point of the heat-transfer fluid at the system's operating pressure
conditions: system is hydronic
exceptions: the system is specifically designed as a steam-based or two-phase system with appropriate pressure-rated components

subject: Radiant Floor Heating/Cooling
rule: Radiant floor cooling system must maintain supply water temperature above the dew point of the conditioned space
conditions: system is used for cooling
exceptions: a dedicated condensation management system (drainage, waterproofing, and sloped substrate) is installed
the floor construction is fully sealed and condensation-tolerant

subject: Radiant Floor Heating/Cooling
rule: Radiant floor heating tubing or electric cables must be fully embedded in or thermally bonded to a thermally conductive screed, slab, or subfloor layer
conditions: system is installed in a new or replacement floor assembly
exceptions: systems designed as 'dry' or 'plate' systems where tubing clips into aluminum heat-diffusion plates under the subfloor

subject: Radiant Floor Heating/Cooling
rule: Radiant floor heating tubing must not be installed in or through expansion joints of the structural slab
conditions: system is embedded in a concrete slab
exceptions: a purpose-designed expansion loop or flexible coupling bridges the joint

subject: Structural Decking
rule: Structural decking must be designed to support its specified live load and dead load without exceeding allowable stress or deflection limits
exceptions: Temporary construction loads may be higher if explicitly accounted for in a separate engineered shoring/reshoring plan

subject: Structural Decking
rule: Structural decking must be securely attached to its supporting members (beams, joists, or framing) with connections capable of transferring all design forces

subject: Structural Decking
rule: Structural decking must not have unprotected penetrations or openings that compromise its required structural load path or fire-resistance rating
conditions: When the decking serves as a diaphragm or contributes to lateral load resistance
When the decking is required to provide a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: Penetrations that are properly framed, reinforced, and detailed by a structural engineer to maintain load transfer and fire rating

subject: Structural Decking
rule: Structural decking (metal or wood) must be protected from moisture exposure that would cause corrosion, rot, or decay during the service life
conditions: When the decking material is susceptible to moisture damage (e.g., untreated steel, untreated wood)
exceptions: Decking materials specifically rated for unprotected exterior exposure (e.g., galvanized steel, pressure-treated wood, or naturally durable species)

subject: Structural Decking
rule: Structural decking must be installed with proper bearing (minimum end bearing distance) on supports as specified by the manufacturer or governing design code

subject: Floor Drain & Trench
rule: Floor drain must be installed at the lowest point of the floor surface to ensure positive drainage by gravity
conditions: floor drain is intended to collect surface water or wash-down liquids
exceptions: floor is designed with a pumped drainage system

subject: Floor Drain & Trench
rule: Trench drain must have a continuous, uniform slope (minimum 0.5% unless superseded by code) along its entire length toward the outlet
conditions: trench drain is installed for gravity drainage
exceptions: trench drain is part of a fully pumped or vacuum drainage system

subject: Floor Drain & Trench
rule: Floor drain body must not be installed with its rim higher than the surrounding finished floor level at any point
conditions: drain is intended to receive floor-surface liquids

subject: Floor Drain & Trench
rule: Trench drain grate must be removable or openable for cleaning and maintenance access
conditions: trench drain is installed in a location where debris or sediment accumulation is possible
exceptions: trench drain is a sealed, single-use industrial system not intended for reuse

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger
rule: ceiling suspension hanger must be anchored to a structural element capable of supporting the intended load
conditions: when supporting a ceiling grid or suspended ceiling system
exceptions: when hanger is purely decorative and supports no load

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger
rule: ceiling suspension hanger must not be installed in a manner that creates a continuous conductive path between electrical components and building structure in the absence of proper grounding
conditions: when hanger is metallic and located near exposed electrical conductors or fixtures
exceptions: when bonding and grounding per applicable electrical code is provided

subject: Ceiling Suspension Hanger
rule: ceiling suspension hanger must have a minimum cross-sectional dimension and thickness as specified by applicable building code for its span and load
conditions: when hanger carries ceiling dead load
exceptions: when hanger assembly is certified by a licensed engineer for alternative dimensions

subject: Expansion Joint Cover
rule: Expansion joint cover must accommodate the full range of expected building movement (thermal, seismic, settlement) without binding or separation
conditions: Applied in any building expansion joint
exceptions: Joints designed for zero-movement applications (e.g., purely aesthetic trim on non-structural partitions)

subject: Expansion Joint Cover
rule: Expansion joint cover must maintain continuous fire-resistance rating equal to the adjacent floor or wall assembly where required by code
conditions: Installation in a fire-rated assembly (e.g., fire-rated floor, wall, or roof)
exceptions: Joints in non-rated assemblies where fire rating is not required by code

subject: Expansion Joint Cover
rule: Expansion joint cover must not create a tripping hazard or fall-through gap where installed in a walking surface
conditions: Installation in floors, decks, plazas, or other pedestrian-accessible horizontal surfaces
exceptions: Cover located in areas not accessible to pedestrians (e.g., on roofs with no public access, behind barriers)

subject: Expansion Joint Cover
rule: Expansion joint cover must provide a watertight seal at its junctions with adjacent building elements in weather-exposed locations
conditions: Installed in exterior walls, roofs, or other assemblies exposed to precipitation or drainage
exceptions: Interior-only applications with no exposure to moisture

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: Acoustic ceiling panel must be installed with a minimum 1-inch gap above the structural deck to accommodate MEP services and prevent direct contact with structure-borne vibration sources
conditions: Installed in suspended ceiling system
exceptions: Direct-application adhesive mount systems specifically rated for acoustic performance

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: Acoustic ceiling panel must not be installed in locations exposed to continuous direct water contact or saturated humidity conditions
conditions: Panel composition includes gypsum, mineral fiber, or cellulose-based materials
exceptions: Panels specifically manufactured with water-resistant core and hydrophobic face treatment rated for high-humidity environments

subject: Acoustic Ceiling Panel
rule: Acoustic ceiling panel must be supported by a grid system designed to carry the panel weight without deflection exceeding manufacturer specifications
conditions: Panel weight exceeds 1.5 psf (pounds per square foot)

subject: Floor Box / Floor Outlet
rule: floor box must be installed so its top edge is flush with or slightly below the finished floor surface
conditions: floor box is installed in a walking surface
exceptions: floor boxes in non-traffic areas where tripping hazard is not a concern

subject: Floor Box / Floor Outlet
rule: floor box must have a watertight cover or gasket when installed in locations subject to wet cleaning or moisture
conditions: floor box is installed in an area subject to wet cleaning, spill risk, or moisture (e.g., kitchens, bathrooms, outdoor covered areas)
exceptions: dry interior spaces with no wet cleaning or spill risk

subject: Floor Box / Floor Outlet
rule: floor box must not be installed in a location where it will be submerged or subject to standing water
exceptions: floor boxes specifically rated and listed for wet locations or submersion

subject: Floor Box / Floor Outlet
rule: floor box cover must be rated for the expected traffic load (pedestrian, light cart, or heavy vehicle)
conditions: floor box is located in a traffic area
exceptions: floor boxes in inaccessible or non-traffic areas

subject: Floor Box / Floor Outlet
rule: floor box wiring must comply with code-required bending radius and wire fill capacity

subject: Floor Framing (Joists & Beams)
rule: floor joists must have a minimum bearing length (typically 1.5 inches) on supports
conditions: wood or steel joists bearing on beams, walls, or girders
exceptions: joists supported by hangers or other mechanical connectors that transfer load without bearing

subject: Floor Framing (Joists & Beams)
rule: floor framing must not have notches or holes that reduce member depth beyond allowable limits
conditions: any solid-sawn lumber or engineered wood joist
exceptions: holes or notches within manufacturer-specified zones and size limits (e.g., within middle third of span, away from supports)

subject: Floor Framing (Joists & Beams)
rule: floor joists must be laterally restrained (bridging, blocking, or sheathing) at intervals to prevent rollover buckling
conditions: wood or cold-formed steel joists with depth-to-thickness ratio exceeding certain limits
exceptions: joists that are inherently laterally stable (e.g., deep composite steel beams with full composite slab connection)

subject: Floor Framing (Joists & Beams)
rule: floor beams must not be loaded beyond their bending or shear capacity under design loads
conditions: any beam in the floor framing system

subject: Floor Framing (Joists & Beams)
rule: floor framing must provide a continuous load path from the floor deck to the vertical supports
conditions: any floor framing system

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Track & Curtain
rule: ceiling-mounted track must be secured to structural ceiling framing capable of supporting the curtain load
conditions: track carries a curtain load
curtain weight exceeds track self-weight
exceptions: track is decorative only and supports no curtain load

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Track & Curtain
rule: ceiling-mounted track fasteners must not penetrate roofing membrane or waterproofing layer
conditions: ceiling above is directly below an occupied roof or terrace deck
track is installed through or near a waterproof membrane
exceptions: penetrations are properly sealed with a listed waterproofing boot and flashing detail

subject: Ceiling-Mounted Track & Curtain
rule: ceiling-mounted track must have a minimum clearance from sprinkler heads as required by fire code
conditions: space is sprinklered
track or curtain would encroach on sprinkler spray pattern
exceptions: track is installed according to an engineered alternative complying with NFPA 13 obstruction rules

subject: Sound Isolation Mat
rule: Sound isolation mat must be fully decoupled from the structural framing to prevent flanking noise transmission
conditions: when installed in floor/ceiling assemblies
when installed in wall assemblies
exceptions: when the mat is specifically designed as a bonded/constrained-layer damping treatment rather than a decoupling layer

subject: Sound Isolation Mat
rule: Sound isolation mat must not be compressed beyond its rated load capacity
conditions: when installed as part of a floating floor assembly

subject: Sound Isolation Mat
rule: Sound isolation mat must be continuous across the entire floor or wall area with no gaps or voids
conditions: when used as the primary sound isolation layer
exceptions: at expansion joints or control joints required by structural design

subject: Sound Isolation Mat
rule: Sound isolation mat must not be installed directly over an in-slab radiant heating system without manufacturer approval
conditions: when the mat is a closed-cell foam or rubber product with low thermal conductivity
exceptions: products specifically tested and rated for use over radiant heating by the manufacturer

subject: Fire-Rated Floor/Ceiling Assembly
rule: Fire-rated floor/ceiling assembly must have a fire-resistance rating (e.g., 1-hour, 2-hour) meeting the applicable building code requirements
conditions: The assembly separates occupancies, separates building areas of differing fire risk, or is required by local building code (e.g., IBC)
exceptions: When the entire building is sprinklered and code allows reduction or omission per specific trade-offs (e.g., IBC exception for NFPA 13 sprinkler coverage)

subject: Fire-Rated Floor/Ceiling Assembly
rule: Fire-rated floor/ceiling assembly must be continuous across the entire floor area it is required to protect
conditions: The assembly is designated as a fire barrier or fire partition in the code-required fire-resistance-rated construction
exceptions: Penetrations protected by approved firestop systems; joints protected by approved fire-rated joint systems

subject: Fire-Rated Floor/Ceiling Assembly
rule: Fire-rated floor/ceiling assembly must not have unprotected openings that exceed the maximum allowable size or aggregate area per code
conditions: The assembly includes any openings (doors, ducts, cable trays, piping, etc.)
exceptions: Openings protected with approved fire doors, fire dampers, or firestop systems that maintain the required fire-resistance rating

subject: Floor Leveling Compound
rule: floor leveling compound must have a minimum compressive strength sufficient to withstand the intended floor loading
conditions: when used as a load-bearing topping or screed
when installed over a structural substrate
exceptions: when used only as a decorative or thin finish layer not subject to point or dynamic loads

subject: Floor Leveling Compound
rule: floor leveling compound must be applied within its specified maximum layer thickness
conditions: when exceeding the manufacturer-recommended thickness per coat or total build
exceptions: when the product is specifically formulated and certified for deep-pour or thick-layer application

subject: Floor Leveling Compound
rule: floor leveling compound must not be applied over a substrate that is not clean, sound, and free of bond-breaking contaminants
conditions: when the substrate has laitance, oil, grease, dust, curing compounds, or existing loose coatings
exceptions: when a manufacturer-approved bonding primer or mechanical preparation specifically addresses the contaminant

subject: Floor Leveling Compound
rule: floor leveling compound must not be used to conceal or bridge active substrate cracks without appropriate crack-isolation treatment
conditions: when the substrate contains structural or moving cracks, expansion joints, or control joints
exceptions: when a specifically engineered crack-isolation membrane or flexible bridging system is included in the assembly

subject: Ceiling T-Bar Spline & Clip
rule: T-bar spline and clip must be mechanically engaged (fully seated and locked) with the T-bar grid main tee and cross tee slots
conditions: ceiling is of the suspended/dropped type using T-bar grid system

subject: Ceiling T-Bar Spline & Clip
rule: T-bar spline and clip material must be compatible with the T-bar grid material to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: dissimilar metals are used (e.g., steel grid with aluminum clip without isolation)
exceptions: if a dielectric barrier or approved corrosion-isolating coating is applied at the contact interface

subject: Ceiling T-Bar Spline & Clip
rule: T-bar spline and clip must not be installed in a manner that prevents thermal expansion movement of the grid
conditions: the ceiling spans more than 12 m (40 ft) in any direction
or the ceiling is exposed to temperature variation exceeding 30 °C

subject: Floor-to-Ceiling Height (Clearance)
rule: Floor-to-ceiling height (clearance) must be at least the minimum required for safe human passage and egress
conditions: Space is intended for human occupancy
exceptions: Unoccupied mechanical plenums
Crawl spaces not intended for occupancy

subject: Floor-to-Ceiling Height (Clearance)
rule: Floor-to-ceiling height must not be less than the minimum clearance required by applicable building code for the occupancy type
conditions: Space is classified as habitable or occupiable

subject: Floor-to-Ceiling Height (Clearance)
rule: Floor-to-ceiling height must accommodate the full vertical swing path of doors, operable windows, and overhead doors without obstruction
conditions: Space contains operable doors or windows that swing or slide into the volume
exceptions: Spaces with no openings

subject: Floor-to-Ceiling Height (Clearance)
rule: Floor-to-ceiling height must not be so low that it prevents the installation and safe operation of required mechanical, electrical, or fire-protection systems in the ceiling plane
conditions: Overhead systems (ductwork, sprinklers, lighting, conduit) are required in the space
exceptions: Spaces with no overhead systems required

subject: Stair Tread & Landing
rule: stair tread and landing must have a minimum depth sufficient for safe foot placement (typically ≥ 11" for treads, ≥ width of stair for landings) to prevent fall risk
conditions: applies to all stair treads and landings serving occupiable spaces
exceptions: industrial spiral stairs or ship ladders with alternate approval

subject: Stair Tread & Landing
rule: stair tread and landing must have a maximum riser height (typically ≤ 7.75" for risers between treads) to prevent unsafe stepping conditions
conditions: applies to stairs with treads and landings in a flight
exceptions: private residential stairs where local code allows up to 8.25" in some jurisdictions

subject: Stair Tread & Landing
rule: stair tread and landing surfaces must have slip resistance adequate for the expected use condition to prevent slipping
conditions: applies to all interior and exterior stair treads and landings
exceptions: temporary construction stairs or stairs not intended for occupancy use

subject: Stair Tread & Landing
rule: stair tread nosing must not project more than the code-allowable distance (typically ≤ 1.5") beyond the tread below
conditions: applies to treads with projecting nosing
exceptions: treads with beveled or rounded nosing that stays within the projection limit

subject: Stair Tread & Landing
rule: stair tread and landing must be slip-resistant when wet (exterior landings and treads)
conditions: applies to exterior stair treads and landings exposed to rain, snow, or ice
exceptions: fully covered/roofed exterior stairs where water does not reach tread surface

subject: Additional Insulation Layer
rule: additional insulation layer must be placed on the exterior side of the vapor barrier in cold climates
conditions: building is located in a cold climate zone (e.g., IECC climate zones 5 and above)
exceptions: buildings with a ventilated roof assembly designed to allow moisture to dry to the exterior

subject: Additional Insulation Layer
rule: additional insulation layer must be continuous with no thermal bridges through the assembly
conditions: insulation is part of a continuous exterior insulation system
exceptions: structural elements such as shelf angles or window frames that unavoidably penetrate the insulation

subject: Additional Insulation Layer
rule: additional insulation layer must not be compressed beyond its designed thickness
conditions: insulation material is compressible (e.g., mineral wool, fiberglass, foam board under load)

subject: Exterior Cladding Build-Out
rule: exterior cladding build-out must not exceed the structural depth limit of the supporting wall assembly
conditions: when cladding is applied over a framed wall
exceptions: when decorative or non-structural furring is specifically engineered and detailed for the added depth

subject: Exterior Cladding Build-Out
rule: exterior cladding build-out must maintain a minimum positive slope or drainage plane for moisture evacuation behind the cladding
conditions: when a drained cavity is required by the climate zone or cladding type
exceptions: when using a direct-applied or adhered cladding system with no cavity (e.g., thin brick veneer or direct stucco)

subject: Cavity Fill Insulation Upgrade
rule: Cavity fill insulation must be installed only if the cavity wall construction is sound and free from significant defects (e.g., cracked masonry, failed ties, missing damp-proof course) that would allow moisture penetration
conditions: When retrofitting existing buildings
exceptions: Temporary/protective installation where immediate remediation is planned

subject: Cavity Fill Insulation Upgrade
rule: Cavity fill insulation must not be installed if the cavity width is less than the minimum required for effective and safe installation (typically 50mm for blown mineral fibre or 40mm for EPS beads)
conditions: When cavity width is below manufacturer-specified minimum

subject: Cavity Fill Insulation Upgrade
