rule: Cavity fill insulation must not be installed where the building is located in a high exposure zone (exposure category very severe or extreme) unless specific design measures are taken
conditions: Where the site is classified as very severe or extreme exposure to wind-driven rain per BS 8104 or equivalent
exceptions: Where a full technical assessment demonstrates adequate weathertightness with additional measures such as improved cavity detailing or external cladding

subject: Cavity Fill Insulation Upgrade
rule: Cavity fill insulation must not bridge the cavity at the base of the wall or above openings (i.e., must not extend below the damp-proof course level or into the zone where cavity trays are installed)
conditions: At all locations where damp-proof course or cavity trays exist

subject: Cavity Fill Insulation Upgrade
rule: Cavity fill insulation must not be installed in walls where existing wall ties are corroded, loose, or spaced too far apart to maintain stability after filling
conditions: During retrofit assessment where wall tie condition is unknown or known to be poor
exceptions: Where wall ties are replaced or supplemented as part of the upgrade work

subject: Thickened Wall-to-Floor Connection
rule: The thickened wall-to-floor connection must have a load path that can transfer vertical and lateral forces from the wall to the floor diaphragm without rupture or excessive deformation
conditions: When the connection is part of a primary lateral force-resisting system
When the wall is load-bearing

subject: Thickened Wall-to-Floor Connection
rule: The connection must achieve a specified minimum embedment or bearing length for the wall reinforcement anchored into the thickened floor slab
conditions: When the connection uses cast-in-place or grouted reinforcement to achieve continuity

subject: Thickened Wall-to-Floor Connection
rule: The connection must not have a gap or unbonded interface that would allow the wall to lift off or slide relative to the floor under uplift or shear
conditions: When the connection is designed to resist overturning or sliding forces

subject: Expanded Window Reveal
rule: expanded window reveal must maintain minimum structural support for the wall above (lintel/header capacity)
conditions: when the reveal expands the original window opening width
exceptions: if a separate structural lintel or arch is independently provided above the reveal

subject: Expanded Window Reveal
rule: expanded window reveal must not reduce the lateral bracing contribution of the original wall to below code-minimum levels
conditions: when the reveal is created in a shear wall or braced wall line
exceptions: if alternative lateral load-resisting elements (e.g., moment frames, additional shear panels) are provided to compensate

subject: Expanded Window Reveal
rule: expanded window reveal must have a weather-tight seal between the new frame and the existing wall construction
conditions: when the reveal is installed in an exterior wall

subject: Thermal Break Insertion
rule: thermal break material must have thermal conductivity less than or equal to 0.5 W/(m·K)
conditions: thermal break is installed in a building envelope assembly

subject: Thermal Break Insertion
rule: thermal break must physically separate the interior-side conductive element from the exterior-side conductive element with no metal-to-metal continuity
conditions: thermal break is installed between interior and exterior metal components

subject: Thermal Break Insertion
rule: thermal break insertion must not introduce a plane of structural weakness that cannot resist the design loads
conditions: thermal break is located in a structural load path

subject: Thermal Break Insertion
rule: thermal break must be continuous along the entire thermal envelope separation path
conditions: thermal break is applied at a building enclosure interface
exceptions: deliberate design intent in a climate where intermittent thermal bridging has negligible impact, e.g., unheated buffer zones

subject: Reinforced Foundation Bearing
rule: reinforced foundation bearing must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement
conditions: when exposed to soil or weather
exceptions: when using corrosion-resistant reinforcement or protective coatings are applied

subject: Reinforced Foundation Bearing
rule: reinforced foundation bearing must not have tensile reinforcement ratio below code-specified minimum
conditions: for all reinforced concrete footings
exceptions: when foundation is designed as unreinforced (plain concrete) per code allowance

subject: Reinforced Foundation Bearing
rule: reinforced foundation bearing must have reinforcement properly anchored and developed beyond critical sections
conditions: at all tension lap splices, bends, or terminations

subject: Reinforced Foundation Bearing
rule: reinforced foundation bearing must not bear on uncompacted fill or organic soil without proper ground improvement
conditions: when bearing directly on soil subgrade
exceptions: when geotechnical analysis confirms adequate bearing capacity and settlement criteria are met

subject: Corner Column
rule: corner column must be continuous from its base to the structure it supports
conditions: column is load-bearing
exceptions: column is decorative only and not part of the structural frame

subject: Corner Column
rule: corner column must be laterally braced at each floor or roof diaphragm level
conditions: column is part of a multi-story frame
column is subject to lateral loads such as wind or seismic
exceptions: column is designed as a cantilever with an adequately stiff base connection verified by analysis

subject: Corner Column
rule: corner column must not have its structural capacity reduced by architectural notching, chases, or penetrations beyond what the design explicitly accounts for
conditions: column is load-bearing
exceptions: all reductions are verified by structural analysis and detailed reinforcement or strengthening is provided

subject: Corner Column Foundation
rule: corner column foundation must transfer vertical load from column to soil without exceeding bearing capacity of soil
conditions: when column is present
when foundation is in bearing soil
exceptions: foundation on competent bedrock where bearing capacity is not a concern

subject: Corner Column Foundation
rule: corner column foundation must resist overturning moment from lateral loads at building corner
conditions: when building is subject to lateral loads such as wind or seismic

subject: Corner Column Foundation
rule: corner column foundation must have minimum depth below frost line
conditions: when located in climate with seasonal frost
exceptions: foundations on non-frost-susceptible soils where frost heave does not occur
foundations designed with frost protection insulation per code

subject: Corner Column Foundation
rule: corner column foundation must not be placed on uncompacted fill without proper geotechnical evaluation
conditions: when fill is present at foundation location
exceptions: engineered fill placed under geotechnical supervision with compaction testing

subject: Corner Column Base Plate
rule: Corner column base plate must be anchored to the foundation
conditions: when used in a structural steel frame

subject: Corner Column Base Plate
rule: Corner column base plate must have bearing capacity equal to or greater than the applied column load divided by the plate area
conditions: under gravity loading

subject: Corner Column Base Plate
rule: Corner column base plate must be level within fabrication tolerances
conditions: at installation

subject: Corner Column Capital
rule: Corner column capital must transfer vertical load from beams or arches above to the column shaft below without structural failure
conditions: capital is load-bearing
capital is part of a structural column assembly
exceptions: purely decorative/non-structural capitals

subject: Corner Column Capital
rule: Corner column capital must not have a plan projection that exceeds the allowable building setback or encroachment limits
conditions: capital projects horizontally beyond column face
building is subject to zoning or public way clearance requirements
exceptions: historically protected structures with grandfathered projections

subject: Corner Column Capital
rule: Corner column capital must provide adequate bearing area for the supported element to prevent crushing or punching shear at the interface
conditions: capital supports a beam, arch, or lintel
material is masonry, stone, or unreinforced concrete
exceptions: steel-to-steel connections with stiffened bearing plates

subject: Corner Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: Corner column reinforcement cage must extend at least the full lap-splice length above and below the beam-column joint
conditions: Reinforced concrete moment-resisting frame

subject: Corner Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: Corner column reinforcement cage must have adequate concrete cover between the outermost bars and the exterior face
conditions: Exposure to weather or soil
exceptions: Interior columns not exposed to weather

subject: Corner Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: Corner column reinforcement cage must not have longitudinal bar splices located within the beam-column joint zone
conditions: Ductile or intermediate moment frame
exceptions: If the splice is fully confined by transverse reinforcement per special code provisions

subject: Corner Column Cladding
rule: Corner column cladding must be self-supporting or independently attached to the structure without relying on adjacent cladding panels for vertical load transfer
conditions: When used as a vertical element at building corners
exceptions: When specifically designed as a shared structural system with adjacent cladding

subject: Corner Column Cladding
rule: Corner column cladding must not create a thermal bridge that bypasses the building's primary thermal envelope
conditions: When the cladding system is part of or adjacent to the building envelope
exceptions: When the corner column is intentionally designed as an uninsulated structural element separated from the interior by a separate continuous insulation layer

subject: Corner Column Cladding
rule: Corner column cladding joints must accommodate differential movement between orthogonal facade planes
conditions: When spanning across the building corner where two facade planes meet

subject: Corner Column Connection Joint
rule: corner column connection joint must transfer vertical and lateral loads between connected members without failure

subject: Corner Column Connection Joint
rule: corner column connection joint must not have gaps or inadequate embedment that prevent full bearing of connected members

subject: Corner Column Connection Joint
rule: corner column connection joint must maintain structural integrity under design wind and seismic loads
conditions: when the building is located in a seismically active or high-wind region

subject: Corner Column Connection Joint
rule: corner column connection joint must be detailed to prevent brittle failure modes such as shear fracture or concrete crushing

subject: Corner Column Formwork
rule: corner column formwork must have sufficient structural rigidity to maintain its shape under concrete pouring pressure
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete columns

subject: Corner Column Formwork
rule: corner column formwork must be properly sealed at joints to prevent concrete leakage (grout loss)
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete columns

subject: Corner Column Formwork
rule: corner column formwork must be braced or tied to resist lateral displacement during concrete placement
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete columns

subject: Corner Column Formwork
rule: corner column formwork must not be stripped (removed) before the concrete has reached adequate strength to be self-supporting
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete columns

subject: Corner Column Waterproofing System
rule: Corner column waterproofing membrane must extend continuously from below grade to above finished grade without gaps or interruptions
conditions: system is applied to below-grade portions of corner columns
system terminates at or above finished grade level
exceptions: system designed as a fully integrated part of a waterproofed blind-side wall where continuity is achieved at the interface

subject: Corner Column Waterproofing System
rule: Corner column waterproofing must seal the transition between vertical and horizontal waterproofing planes at the column base
conditions: system interfaces with a horizontal waterproofing layer (e.g., basement slab membrane)

subject: Corner Column Waterproofing System
rule: Corner column waterproofing detail must not create a concealed cavity that traps water against the column surface
exceptions: cavity is positively drained to the exterior

subject: Corner Column Waterproofing System
rule: Corner column waterproofing termination at grade must be mechanically fastened or otherwise secured against vertical slip or peel-back
conditions: membrane terminates at or near grade without backfilling against it
exceptions: membrane is fully adhered with a bond strength exceeding expected peel forces and is protected by a rigid covering

subject: Seismic Corner Column Detailing
rule: corner column longitudinal reinforcement must be fully developed into the footing or foundation via standard hooks or mechanical anchorage
conditions: column is located at building corner
seismic design category D, E, or F
reinforced concrete moment frame
exceptions: light-frame construction
non-building structures

subject: Seismic Corner Column Detailing
rule: corner column transverse reinforcement must not have spacing exceeding the smallest of: 6 × longitudinal bar diameter, 1/4 of minimum column dimension, or 100 mm (4 in) within plastic hinge zones
conditions: moment-resisting frame
seismic design category D, E, or F
exceptions: columns designed with special detailing but located in SDC A, B, or C

subject: Seismic Corner Column Detailing
rule: corner column must have 135-degree seismic hooks on all transverse reinforcement in plastic hinge regions
conditions: seismic design category D, E, or F
cast-in-place reinforced concrete
exceptions: columns in SDC A or B where 90-degree hooks are permitted

subject: Seismic Corner Column Detailing
rule: corner column must have confinement reinforcement extending a minimum of 450 mm (18 in) into the supporting footing or mat foundation
conditions: embedded column-to-footing connection
seismic design category D, E, or F
exceptions: drilled pier or pile foundations with different detailing requirements
precast concrete with validated mechanical connections

subject: Column Size & Section
rule: column cross-section dimensions must be sufficient to prevent buckling under maximum expected axial load
conditions: column is in compression
slenderness ratio exceeds critical threshold
exceptions: tension-only elements such as hangers

subject: Column Size & Section
rule: column must have a minimum cross-sectional area to keep compressive stress below material yield strength
conditions: column is load-bearing

subject: Column Size & Section
rule: steel column section must not have a width-to-thickness ratio that exceeds the compactness limits of the applicable design code
conditions: column is steel
section is subject to compressive yielding before local buckling is reached

subject: Column Spacing
rule: column spacing must accommodate the structural bay widths required by the spanning system above
conditions: the column supports a beam, slab, or truss spanning between columns
exceptions: cantilevered or laterally-braced systems where columns do not define bay widths

subject: Column Spacing
rule: column spacing must not exceed the maximum span capacity of the structural framing system
conditions: the structure uses steel beams, precast planks, or reinforced concrete slabs spanning between columns
exceptions: long-span systems (trusses, space frames, arches) designed specifically for wide spacing

subject: Column Spacing
rule: column spacing must be uniform in a rectilinear grid to prevent accidental torsion or unbalanced lateral load paths
conditions: the building is in a seismic region or uses a rigid diaphragm lateral system
exceptions: irregular grids where explicit structural analysis justifies the layout

subject: Column Spacing
rule: column spacing must provide minimum clear distances required for fire-rated enclosure construction between columns
conditions: fire-resistance-rated walls or enclosures are required between columns
exceptions: columns are individually fire-protected and no enclosure wall is required between them

subject: Column Base Plate & Anchorage
rule: column base plate must be anchored to the foundation
conditions: column is present
foundation is present

subject: Column Base Plate & Anchorage
rule: anchor bolts must be fully embedded in grout or concrete to develop their design tensile capacity
conditions: anchor bolts are specified as load-bearing
exceptions: bolts used only for erection stability and later removed

subject: Column Base Plate & Anchorage
rule: base plate must bear evenly on the grout bed or foundation surface
exceptions: intentional gaps for levelling shims that are later grouted solid

subject: Column Base Plate & Anchorage
rule: anchor bolt holes in the base plate must not be smaller than the anchor bolt diameter

subject: Column Base Plate & Anchorage
rule: base plate thickness must be sufficient to resist bending under factored column loads without yielding

subject: Column Reinforcement
rule: column reinforcement must be placed within plastic hinge zones at column ends as required by seismic detailing
conditions: structure is in a seismic region
column is part of the lateral-force-resisting system

subject: Column Reinforcement
rule: column reinforcement must have adequate concrete cover to prevent corrosion and ensure fire resistance
conditions: column is exposed to environmental conditions
column requires fire rating
exceptions: precast/prestressed elements with factory-controlled cover

subject: Column Reinforcement
rule: column reinforcement must not have lap splices located in high-stress zones such as the mid-height of columns
conditions: column is subjected to significant bending moments at mid-height

subject: Column Reinforcement
rule: longitudinal column reinforcement ratio must not fall below the minimum specified by structural codes

subject: Column Reinforcement
rule: transverse reinforcement (ties/hoops) must be spaced closely enough to prevent buckling of longitudinal bars
conditions: column is in compression under design loads

subject: Column Splice Connection
rule: column splice connection must transfer full design axial force through the splice
conditions: column is designed as a continuous load-bearing element
splice is located in a gravity load path

subject: Column Splice Connection
rule: column splice connection must not have a net tensile capacity less than the required design tension for uplift or overturning
conditions: structure is subject to uplift loads
overturning moment induces tension at the splice location

subject: Column Splice Connection
rule: column splice connection must be proportioned to resist the design moment and shear at the splice location
conditions: splice is located at a point where moment or shear is present in the column
exceptions: moment-resisting splice not required if the splice is located at a point of zero moment and the connection is detailed as a pure compression splice

subject: Column Tie Beam Connection
rule: column tie beam connection must transfer lateral forces between columns and tie beams
conditions: in seismic or wind-resisting frames
exceptions: non-structural or decorative connections not carrying lateral loads

subject: Column Tie Beam Connection
rule: the connection between column and tie beam must maintain structural continuity without brittle failure modes
conditions: in reinforced concrete or steel moment-resisting frames
exceptions: connections designed as pinned (simple) connections where only gravity loads are transferred

subject: Column Tie Beam Connection
rule: column tie beam connection must not have inadequate reinforcement anchorage or embedment length
conditions: in reinforced concrete construction

subject: Column Tie Beam Connection
rule: the connection must provide sufficient shear capacity at the column-tie beam interface

subject: Pad Footing
rule: pad footing must have a minimum base area to limit soil bearing pressure to the safe bearing capacity of the soil
conditions: structure is founded on soil that can be classified for bearing capacity
exceptions: foundation is on solid rock with proven bearing capacity exceeding applied loads

subject: Pad Footing
rule: pad footing must be placed below the frost depth of the site location
conditions: site is in a climate zone where seasonal ground freezing occurs
exceptions: footing is designed with frost-protected shallow foundation methods (e.g., insulation per code)

subject: Pad Footing
rule: pad footing must not bear on fill, organic soil, or uncontrolled material unless that material has been properly treated and verified
conditions: subgrade material is classified as fill, organic soil, or uncontrolled material
exceptions: material has been engineered, compacted, and tested to meet bearing capacity and settlement criteria

subject: Pad Footing
rule: pad footing must have minimum reinforcement (or minimum thickness if unreinforced) to prevent structural failure under tensile and shear stresses
conditions: footing is reinforced concrete or plain concrete

subject: Raft Foundation
rule: raft foundation must be cast on a stable, load-bearing subgrade or compacted fill
conditions: all raft foundation applications
exceptions: when ground improvement techniques (e.g., soil stabilization, deep compaction) are employed to achieve required bearing capacity

subject: Raft Foundation
rule: raft foundation must have continuous steel reinforcement throughout the slab
conditions: reinforced concrete raft foundation
exceptions: unreinforced mass-concrete rafts for very light, low-rise structures where soil conditions are excellent and tensile stresses are negligible

subject: Raft Foundation
rule: raft foundation must not be placed directly on expansive clay soils without mitigation
conditions: site with expansive (shrink-swell) clay soils
exceptions: when a void former or compressible layer is provided beneath the raft to accommodate soil volume changes
when the soil has been chemically treated to reduce expansion potential

subject: Raft Foundation
rule: raft foundation concrete cover to reinforcement must meet minimum code requirements for ground-contact exposure
conditions: all reinforced concrete raft foundations
exceptions: when a waterproofing membrane and protective layer provide equivalent corrosion protection

subject: Raft Foundation
rule: raft foundation edge must be thickened or provided with a deepened beam at perimeter and under load-bearing walls
conditions: raft foundation supporting load-bearing walls or columns near the edge
exceptions: when structural analysis shows edge stresses remain within permissible limits with uniform thickness

subject: Mat Foundation
rule: mat foundation must be continuously reinforced to control temperature and shrinkage cracking
conditions: reinforced concrete mat foundation
exceptions: unreinforced mass concrete mats designed for crack control by other means
post-tensioned mats

subject: Mat Foundation
rule: mat foundation must have a minimum thickness to accommodate reinforcement cover, two-way shear, and punching shear requirements
conditions: reinforced concrete mat foundation

subject: Mat Foundation
rule: mat foundation bottom must bear on competent soil or engineered fill of adequate bearing capacity, or be supported by deep foundation elements

subject: Mat Foundation
rule: mat foundation must not be placed on frost-susceptible soil above frost depth without frost protection
conditions: cold climate regions where seasonal freezing occurs
exceptions: heated structures that prevent soil freezing beneath the mat
insulated mats designed to keep subgrade above freezing

subject: Mat Foundation
rule: mat foundation must have adequate drainage (e.g., perimeter drains or sub-slab drainage) to prevent hydrostatic uplift or water pressure buildup
conditions: mat below the water table or in poorly draining soils
exceptions: mats designed as waterproof basements with anchored resistance to hydrostatic uplift
mats on well-draining granular soils above the water table

subject: Caisson / Drilled Pier
rule: caisson or drilled pier must bear on competent load-bearing strata (bedrock or dense soil with adequate capacity)
conditions: when used as a deep foundation element
exceptions: when designed as a friction pier in materials that provide adequate skin friction resistance without end bearing

subject: Caisson / Drilled Pier
rule: caisson or drilled pier must have a minimum diameter sufficient to allow safe construction access and structural load transfer
conditions: when constructed with personnel entry required for inspection or cleaning of the shaft base
exceptions: small-diameter piers (micro-piles or auger-cast piles) that are constructed without personnel entry

subject: Caisson / Drilled Pier
rule: caisson or drilled pier must not be constructed in unstable ground conditions without temporary casing or slurry support
conditions: when soils are cohesionless, water-bearing, or prone to caving
exceptions: when the full shaft depth is in self-supporting rock or stiff clay that will not collapse before concrete placement

subject: Caisson / Drilled Pier
rule: concrete in a caisson or drilled pier must be placed by tremie or other method that prevents segregation and avoids free-fall through water or slurry
conditions: when concrete is placed under water, bentonite slurry, or polymer fluid
exceptions: when the shaft is completely dewatered and dry prior to concrete placement

subject: Caisson / Drilled Pier
rule: reinforcement cage in a caisson or drilled pier must have adequate concrete cover on all sides as required for fire resistance and corrosion protection
conditions: when reinforcement is used and the pier is exposed to environmental exposure or fire risk
exceptions: temporary or non-structural piers with no reinforcement

subject: Seismic Isolation Bearing
rule: Seismic isolation bearing must have a horizontal displacement capacity that accommodates the maximum considered earthquake (MCE) design displacement
conditions: Building is located in a seismically active region
Bearing is installed as part of the lateral-force-resisting system

subject: Seismic Isolation Bearing
rule: Seismic isolation bearing must not experience tensile stress that exceeds its tensile capacity
conditions: Bearing is an elastomeric type (e.g., natural rubber or lead-rubber bearing)
exceptions: Tension-capable isolation bearings specifically designed and tested for tensile loads

subject: Seismic Isolation Bearing
rule: Seismic isolation bearing must be designed to resist the full gravity load of the structure under service and seismic conditions

subject: Seismic Isolation Bearing
rule: Seismic isolation bearing must not experience roll-out (loss of contact between bearing surfaces) under design seismic displacement
conditions: Bearing is a flat sliding bearing or a bearing without mechanical restraint

subject: Seismic Isolation Bearing
rule: Seismic isolation bearing must maintain stability (no buckling) under maximum vertical load combined with maximum lateral displacement

subject: Anchor Bolt / Base Plate Assembly
rule: Anchor bolt must have a properly matched nut (or equivalent threaded engagement) to develop full tensile capacity
conditions: When used in tension-resisting connections
exceptions: When anchor bolt is designed as a permanently grouted or bonded dowel where nut is not the load-transfer mechanism

subject: Anchor Bolt / Base Plate Assembly
rule: Base plate must have a hole diameter no larger than the anchor bolt diameter plus the specified tolerance per applicable code (e.g., AISC/ACI)
conditions: For standard bearing-type connections with snug-tight or pretensioned bolts
exceptions: Oversized holes for anchor rods where shear is not resisted by bearing of the rod on the plate (e.g., shear is resisted by friction or separate shear lugs)

subject: Anchor Bolt / Base Plate Assembly
rule: Anchor bolt embedment depth must extend at least the minimum required development length into the concrete foundation
conditions: When designed to develop its full yield strength in tension
exceptions: When headed anchor bolts or other mechanical anchorage devices provide equivalent capacity at shorter embedment per code-recognized testing

subject: Anchor Bolt / Base Plate Assembly
rule: Base plate must not be so thin that it yields under the design bearing pressure from the concrete (must satisfy flexural limit state per code)
conditions: When subjected to compressive axial load and bending moment at the base

subject: Foundation Vapor Barrier
rule: Foundation vapor barrier must be installed on the warm side of the insulation (or in accordance with local climate region requirements)
conditions: Building is in a heating-dominated climate
Foundation has insulation
exceptions: Unconditioned spaces where moisture migration is not a concern
Certain vapor-open assembly designs where drying is intentional

subject: Foundation Vapor Barrier
rule: Foundation vapor barrier must be continuous and sealed at all seams and penetrations
conditions: Vapor barrier is required by design
exceptions: None for the sealed condition — any breach voids the barrier function

subject: Foundation Vapor Barrier
rule: Foundation vapor barrier must not be installed on both sides of a wall assembly where it can create a moisture trap
conditions: Foundation wall assembly has insulation within the cavity
exceptions: Specially engineered assemblies with vented drainage provisions that account for dual vapor retarders

subject: Slab structural layer
rule: slab structural layer must have a minimum thickness to span the clear distance between supports without excessive deflection or failure
conditions: slab is reinforced concrete
slab spans horizontally between supports
exceptions: pre-stressed or post-tensioned slabs may use reduced thickness due to pre-compression

subject: Slab structural layer
rule: slab structural layer must_not have tensile reinforcement placed below the cover requirement
conditions: slab is reinforced concrete
slab is exposed to exterior or aggressive environment

subject: Slab structural layer
rule: slab structural layer must have a continuous load path to its supporting beams or walls
conditions: slab is part of a gravity load-resisting system
exceptions: cantilevered or partially-supported slabs where the designed load path terminates at the free edge

subject: Reinforcement mesh
rule: Reinforcement mesh must be fully embedded in concrete for composite action
conditions: When used in reinforced concrete construction
exceptions: Pre-tensioned or post-tensioned systems where mesh serves only as temperature/shrinkage reinforcement and is not relied upon for structural composite action

subject: Reinforcement mesh
rule: Reinforcement mesh must not have a lap splice length less than the code-specified minimum
conditions: When multiple mesh sheets are lapped to achieve continuity
exceptions: When mechanical or welded splices are used and verified by testing per applicable building code

subject: Reinforcement mesh
rule: Reinforcement mesh must have minimum concrete cover as required by exposure class and fire rating
conditions: When mesh is used as primary reinforcement in concrete elements exposed to weather, soil, or fire
exceptions: When mesh is used only as crack control in non-structural slabs-on-grade with adequate alternative corrosion protection

subject: Reinforcement mesh
rule: Reinforcement mesh must not be placed such that its clear spacing prevents proper concrete placement and consolidation
conditions: In any cast-in-place concrete element
exceptions: Self-consolidating concrete with demonstrated flow through the mesh is used and verified

subject: Concrete cover / topping
rule: Concrete cover / topping must have a minimum thickness to protect reinforcement from corrosion and fire
conditions: when used as structural topping over precast or prestressed elements
when exposed to environmental conditions (moisture, chlorides, freeze-thaw)
exceptions: non-structural levelling screeds not intended for corrosion protection

subject: Concrete cover / topping
rule: Concrete cover / topping must not have a thickness that exceeds the structural design capacity
conditions: when acting as a structural topping bonded to a precast or existing slab
exceptions: purely non-structural levelling or slope-creating topping with no composite action assumed

subject: Concrete cover / topping
rule: Concrete cover / topping must have adequate bond with the substrate
conditions: when designed as composite topping over precast planks or existing slabs
exceptions: unbonded topping systems on a separation layer

subject: Vapor barrier
rule: vapor barrier must be installed on the warm side of the thermal insulation
conditions: assembly separates conditioned interior from unconditioned exterior or from a different thermal zone
assembly includes thermal insulation
exceptions: assemblies in hot-humid climates where the predominant moisture drive is inward
assemblies using materials that are vapor-permeable and the assembly is designed to dry to the interior

subject: Vapor barrier
rule: vapor barrier must not have two layers of impermeable materials on opposite sides of an assembly that trap moisture
conditions: assembly has a vapor barrier or Class I vapor retarder on one side
the opposite side of the same assembly also has a vapor barrier or Class I vapor retarder
the assembly has no intentional venting or drying provision between the two barriers
exceptions: assemblies specifically engineered as double-vapor-barrier systems with monitored drainage and drying (rare, specialized construction)

subject: Vapor barrier
rule: vapor barrier must be continuous and all seams must be sealed
conditions: vapor barrier is installed as a sheet membrane

subject: Vapor barrier
rule: vapor barrier must not be installed directly against a material that remains wet during service
exceptions: vapor barrier material itself is rated for direct contact with that wet material (e.g., below-grade damp-proofing membranes specifically designed for wet soil contact)

subject: Rigid insulation layer
rule: Rigid insulation layer must be continuous across the roof deck to prevent thermal bridging
conditions: when used as the primary thermal barrier in a roof assembly
when installed over structural deck
exceptions: at drainage pathways specifically designed to penetrate the insulation

subject: Rigid insulation layer
rule: Rigid insulation layer must be compatible with the roofing membrane's attachment method
conditions: when direct-adhered membrane system is specified
when mechanically fastened membrane system is specified
exceptions: fully ballasted systems that do not rely on adhesion or fastening through insulation

subject: Rigid insulation layer
rule: Rigid insulation layer must not be left exposed to UV radiation without a protective covering
conditions: when outside of temporary construction phasing
exceptions: insulation products specifically rated for UV exposure per manufacturer

subject: Blinding / lean concrete layer
rule: Blinding / lean concrete layer must have a minimum thickness to provide a stable working platform and prevent contamination of the foundation reinforcement
conditions: when used as a working platform for reinforced concrete foundations
exceptions: when blinding is not used and formwork is placed directly on compacted earth

subject: Blinding / lean concrete layer
rule: Blinding / lean concrete layer must be placed on adequately compacted and stable subgrade
conditions: always when blinding is specified

subject: Blinding / lean concrete layer
rule: Blinding / lean concrete must not be used as structural load-bearing element for permanent foundation loads
conditions: in all cases where blinding is specified as lean mix concrete
exceptions: when the blinding mix and thickness are specifically designed for structural load transfer per engineer's design

subject: Blinding / lean concrete layer
rule: Blinding layer must provide uniform support without voids or honeycombing beneath reinforcement
conditions: when placed directly under reinforced concrete foundation elements

subject: Expansion / contraction joints
rule: Expansion/contraction joints must be continuous through the building section (structure, cladding, finishes) to prevent differential movement damage
conditions: Building has multiple structural materials
Building length exceeds manufacturer/design-code spacing limits
Building has thermal or moisture movement potential
exceptions: Small buildings without significant thermal/moisture variation

subject: Expansion / contraction joints
rule: Expansion/contraction joints must not be located where they compromise structural stability or create a collapse hazard
conditions: Joint location is at a critical lateral-force-resisting element
Joint creates an unbraced segment exceeding code stability limits
exceptions: Joint detailed with shear-transfer or lateral-load devices to restore continuity of lateral system

subject: Expansion / contraction joints
rule: Expansion/contraction joint width must accommodate the calculated maximum movement range under worst-case temperature and moisture conditions
conditions: Joint is exposed to exterior temperature cycles
Joint separates materials with different thermal/moisture coefficients
exceptions: Interior conditioned space with negligible temperature variation

subject: Edge / perimeter insulation
rule: Edge / perimeter insulation must be continuous around the entire building perimeter at the foundation
conditions: When used as part of a continuous insulation (CI) system
When installed at the foundation-to-wall interface
exceptions: Buildings with deep pile foundations where perimeter insulation is not required
When thermal break is achieved through alternative approved assembly details

subject: Edge / perimeter insulation
rule: Edge / perimeter insulation must not be submerged in groundwater or wicking moisture from the ground
conditions: When the insulation material is not rated for below-grade or damp/wet service (e.g., standard EPS or fiberglass)
When installed below finished grade level
exceptions: Insulation materials specifically rated and tested for constant moisture exposure (e.g., Type IV/XPS, rigid foam with closed-cell structure and low water absorption)
When a fully sealed vapor barrier/drainage membrane protects the insulation from ground contact

subject: Ground bearing slab system
rule: ground bearing slab system must have a minimum thickness to resist ground-bearing pressures and prevent structural failure
conditions: slab is load-bearing
slab supports superstructure loads
exceptions: non-load-bearing ground slabs used only as a wearing surface (e.g., pathways) where thickness is governed by durability not structural capacity

subject: Ground bearing slab system
rule: ground bearing slab system must not be placed on uncompacted or non-engineered fill
conditions: slab is used in a permanent structure
exceptions: slab is temporary or placed on rock where compaction requirements differ

subject: Ground bearing slab system
rule: ground bearing slab system must have a moisture vapor barrier (or damp-proof membrane) below the slab when the interior environment is moisture-sensitive
conditions: interior space has finished flooring susceptible to moisture damage
building is enclosed and conditioned
exceptions: unconditioned exterior slabs with no moisture-sensitive finishes
slabs in arid climates where groundwater capillary rise is negligible and building code permits omission

subject: Ground bearing slab system
rule: ground bearing slab system must have a minimum depth of properly graded granular sub-base below the slab in non-rock conditions
conditions: subgrade soil has poor drainage or is frost-susceptible
slab is located in a climate with freezing temperatures
exceptions: slab is cast directly on sound rock or on a non-frost-susceptible granular subgrade with adequate drainage

subject: Suspended ground slab system
rule: Suspended ground slab system must have a minimum clear air gap or ventilated void beneath the slab to prevent moisture wicking and allow ground moisture dispersion
conditions: slab is in contact with or near natural ground
building is in a climate with any ground moisture
exceptions: slab is cast directly onto a properly designed capillary break and vapor barrier with sealed perimeter

subject: Suspended ground slab system
rule: Suspended ground slab system must not have continuous rigid thermal bridging through the slab to the exterior or unconditioned ground
conditions: slab is part of a conditioned space envelope
exceptions: the thermal bridge is intentionally part of a passive heating/cooling strategy and condensation risk is fully mitigated

subject: Suspended ground slab system
rule: Suspended ground slab system must be positively tied or anchored to supporting structure to resist lateral and uplift forces
conditions: slab is in a seismic zone
slab is in a wind zone with design wind speed over 160 km/h
exceptions: slab weight alone provides sufficient restoring force as verified by structural analysis

subject: Suspended ground slab system
rule: Suspended ground slab system must have reinforcement continuous through construction joints to transfer tensile forces
conditions: slab is designed as a structural diaphragm
slab is reinforced concrete
exceptions: joint is a designed movement joint with verified load path around it

subject: Radon extraction / vent mat
rule: radon extraction / vent mat must be installed with a continuous airtight seal to the building's substructure or slab
conditions: when installed as part of a soil depressurization radon mitigation system
when serving as a sub-slab or membrane vent path

subject: Radon extraction / vent mat
rule: radon extraction / vent mat must not be installed where it will be crushed, compressed, or flattened by overlying concrete or fill
conditions: when installed under a slab or floor assembly

subject: Radon extraction / vent mat
rule: radon extraction / vent mat must be connected to a powered vent fan or passive stack that terminates above the roof eave line
conditions: when used as the collection layer in an active or passive radon system

subject: Under-slab drainage layer
rule: Under-slab drainage layer must be installed at a continuous positive slope toward the drainage outlet
conditions: when gravity drainage is used
exceptions: when positive displacement pumping is used

subject: Under-slab drainage layer
rule: Under-slab drainage layer must not be omitted beneath a slab-on-grade in areas with high water table or poorly draining soils
conditions: when the building is slab-on-grade
when the site has a high water table or poorly draining soils
exceptions: when an engineered waterproofing and capillary break system is designed to manage groundwater without a dedicated drainage layer

subject: Under-slab drainage layer
rule: Under-slab drainage layer material must have a minimum compressive strength sufficient to resist the design load without crushing
conditions: when the drainage layer is load-bearing beneath the slab

subject: Under-slab drainage layer
rule: Under-slab drainage layer must not be connected directly to the building's interior storm drainage system without an air gap or trap
conditions: when connecting to the building's interior storm or sanitary drainage system

subject: Under-slab drainage layer
rule: Under-slab drainage layer must be separated from the foundation footing by a minimum distance or an impermeable barrier
conditions: when the drainage layer extends to the footing level
exceptions: when the footing is designed with a positive drainage system

subject: Slab waterproof coating
rule: Slab waterproof coating must form a continuous, uninterrupted membrane across the entire slab surface
conditions: when applied as a below-grade slab waterproofing system
when used as a liquid-applied or sheet membrane system
exceptions: where intentional drainage paths or control joints are designed with sealed termination details

subject: Slab waterproof coating
rule: Slab waterproof coating must not be applied over surfaces contaminated with oil, grease, dust, or laitance
conditions: prior to application of any bonded waterproofing membrane system

subject: Slab waterproof coating
rule: Slab waterproof coating must be protected from damage during backfilling and subsequent construction
conditions: when installed on exterior below-grade slabs that will be backfilled

subject: Slab void formers
rule: Slab void formers must be fully encapsulated by concrete to prevent collapse under load
conditions: Used in reinforced concrete slabs
Void formers are load-bearing during construction

subject: Slab void formers
rule: Slab void formers must be resistant to buoyancy forces during concrete placement
conditions: Void formers are hollow and enclosed
Concrete is placed in a single wet pour

subject: Slab void formers
rule: Slab void formers must not be used in locations where concentrated point loads are expected without additional local reinforcement
conditions: Slab is designed for heavy point loads such as columns or machinery
exceptions: Local reinforcement or thickened slab zones are provided around load points

subject: Underfloor heating pipes
rule: underfloor heating pipes must not be installed beneath fixed heavy fixtures (e.g., kitchen islands, bath tubs, structural walls)
conditions: permanent heavy fixtures are present above the floor slab
exceptions: if the pipe routing is fully contained within a dedicated thermal mass zone and the fixture does not impede heat dissipation or access

subject: Underfloor heating pipes
rule: underfloor heating pipes must be embedded at a depth that prevents damage from surface fasteners (e.g., nails, screws)
conditions: the floor finish will accept nailed or screwed fixings (e.g., timber flooring, carpet underlay)
exceptions: if a dedicated pipe-protection layer (e.g., steel mesh or screed cover) of documented puncture resistance is installed above the pipes

subject: Underfloor heating pipes
rule: underfloor heating pipes must not be laid directly against or in contact with thermal insulation that exceeds the pipe manufacturer's maximum rated surface temperature
conditions: insulation is placed in direct contact with the pipe outer wall
exceptions: if the insulation material is specifically rated for the maximum pipe operating temperature and the manufacturer certifies compatibility

subject: Structural screed
rule: Structural screed must have a minimum thickness to ensure structural integrity under design loads
conditions: when used as a load-bearing layer
exceptions: when screed is non-structural or purely a levelling layer

subject: Structural screed
rule: Structural screed must be placed on a adequately compacted or structurally sound substrate
exceptions: when screed is bonded directly to a concrete base slab that provides structural support

subject: Structural screed
rule: Structural screed must not be applied over a vapour barrier without appropriate reinforcement or design provisions
conditions: when a vapour barrier separates screed from the base
exceptions: when the screed is designed as an unbonded screed with reinforcement and movement joints per engineering specification

subject: Solid Box Column
rule: Solid Box Column must resist vertical compressive loads without buckling or crushing
conditions: When used as a load-bearing element
exceptions: When used purely as a non-structural decorative element

subject: Solid Box Column
rule: Solid Box Column must have its centroidal axis aligned with the resultant line of action of applied loads
conditions: When resisting primarily axial compression

subject: Solid Box Column
rule: Solid Box Column must not be constructed from materials that are incompatible in thermal expansion or electrochemically reactive when in contact
conditions: When fabricated as a composite assembly (e.g., steel tube filled with concrete)
exceptions: When a proven bond-breaker or isolation layer is used

subject: Hollow Box Column
rule: hollow box column must have a closed cross-section to resist torsion
conditions: when used as a structural element subject to torsional loading
exceptions: when open sections are specifically designed with supplementary torsional bracing

subject: Hollow Box Column
rule: hollow box column must have a minimum wall thickness sufficient to prevent local buckling
conditions: when subject to axial compressive loads
exceptions: when internal diaphragms or stiffeners are provided at close spacing

subject: Hollow Box Column
rule: hollow box column must not have voids or gaps in the steel plate welds at corner joints
conditions: when fabricated from welded steel plates

subject: Steel Box Column
rule: steel box column must be concentric with its applied axial load to within acceptable eccentricity limits
conditions: when column is subjected to axial compression
when column is part of a gravity load-resisting frame
exceptions: purposefully designed eccentrically loaded columns where eccentricity is explicitly accounted for in moment-axial interaction design

subject: Steel Box Column
rule: steel box column must not have a width-to-thickness ratio that exceeds the compactness limits for its intended plastic hinge rotation
conditions: when column is expected to sustain inelastic deformation (seismic or ductile design)
when column flanges and webs are slender elements
exceptions: columns designed elastically with no ductility demand where slenderness limits follow non-compact or slender-element rules per applicable design code

subject: Steel Box Column
rule: steel box column must have continuous load path from base to connection above
conditions: when column transfers gravity and lateral loads

subject: Steel Box Column
rule: steel box column must be braced against lateral-torsional buckling over its unbraced length
conditions: when column is subjected to flexure (combined axial and bending)
when unbraced length exceeds the limiting length for plastic or inelastic LTB per design code
exceptions: columns that are purely axially loaded with negligible bending moment

subject: Timber Box Column
rule: Timber box column must have vertical load-bearing capacity exceeding the sum of all design dead and live loads transmitted to it
conditions: column is a primary structural element
building is habitable or occupied
exceptions: temporary non-structural installations where column supports only its self-weight

subject: Timber Box Column
rule: Timber box column must maintain continuous load path from supported elements to foundation
conditions: column is part of the gravity load-resisting system

subject: Timber Box Column
rule: Timber box column must_not have unbraced length exceeding code-specified slenderness limits for its cross-section and material grade
conditions: column is subjected to compressive axial load
exceptions: column is temporarily braced during construction with approved shoring

subject: Timber Box Column
rule: Timber box column connections (base, cap, and any splices) must be designed to transfer all design forces (axial, shear, moment) acting at the connection
conditions: column is connected to other structural elements

subject: Timber Box Column
rule: Timber in box column must be protected from moisture content exceeding 19% for prolonged periods
conditions: column is in service (not during kiln-drying or controlled treatment process)
exceptions: column is of a species or treatment specifically rated for continuous wet service and designed accordingly

subject: Box Column Base Plate
rule: Box column base plate must have sufficient thickness to resist bearing and bending under applied compressive load
conditions: Column is in compression
Base plate supported on grout and concrete foundation

subject: Box Column Base Plate
rule: Box column base plate must have plan dimensions at least equal to the column outer dimensions plus allowance for welding or bolting
conditions: Column is welded or bolted to base plate
exceptions: Precision-machined bearing connection where column bears directly on support without plate overhang

subject: Box Column Base Plate
rule: Anchor rod holes in box column base plate must not be located inside the column profile without providing access for bolt tightening
conditions: Base plate uses anchor rods for connection to foundation
exceptions: Holes are oversized and used only for alignment with no tightening requirement

subject: Box Column Splice
rule: box column splice must develop the full strength of the connecting members in tension and compression
conditions: when column splice is located in a Seismic Demand Category (SDC) D, E, or F zone
when the column is part of the seismic load-resisting system
exceptions: if the splice is deliberately designed as a pinned connection and not part of the lateral system

subject: Box Column Splice
rule: box column splice must be proportioned such that the net section rupture strength at the splice equals or exceeds the required tensile strength
conditions: when the column is subjected to net tension

subject: Box Column Splice
rule: box column splice must not have less than 50% of the column shear strength when the splice is located within a moment frame beam-column joint region
conditions: when the splice occurs within the beam-column joint panel zone of a moment-resisting frame

subject: Box Column Fireproofing
rule: Box column fireproofing must fully encase the steel box column section
conditions: When fire resistance rating is required by building code
exceptions: When fire engineering analysis demonstrates equivalent performance through intumescent coating or other approved method

subject: Box Column Fireproofing
rule: Box column fireproofing must maintain minimum thickness as specified by fire rating design
conditions: When spray-applied fire-resistive material (SFRM) or board-type fireproofing is used
exceptions: When tested assembly certification demonstrates adequate performance at reduced thickness

subject: Box Column Fireproofing
rule: Box column fireproofing must not have gaps or unprotected penetrations through the fire-resistive envelope
conditions: Anywhere along the fire-rated column height
exceptions: Penetrations that are properly firestopped with listed through-penetration firestop system maintaining the required fire rating

subject: Box Column Fireproofing
rule: Box column fireproofing must remain securely attached to the steel column under thermal expansion and fire conditions
conditions: All fire-rated installations

subject: Engaged Box Column
rule: An engaged box column must transfer vertical load from the supported structure to the foundation without buckling or crushing
conditions: The column is load-bearing

subject: Engaged Box Column
rule: The engaged box column must be fabricated from materials with compressive strength sufficient for the design load
conditions: The column is load-bearing

subject: Engaged Box Column
rule: An engaged box column must not have a net cross-sectional area that decreases below the minimum required to resist the factored design loads
conditions: The column is load-bearing
exceptions: If deliberate weakening is part of a controlled fuse/energy dissipation mechanism certified by a structural engineer

subject: Box Column Cladding/Casing
rule: Box column cladding/casing must be securely fastened to the structural column
conditions: The cladding/casing is load-bearing or subject to wind loads
The cladding/casing is attached to a vertical structural column
exceptions: Temporary installation for inspection or maintenance with safety controls

subject: Box Column Cladding/Casing
rule: Box column cladding/casing must not obstruct required fire-resistance rating of the structural column
conditions: The column requires a fire-resistance rating per building code
exceptions: The cladding/casing itself provides an equivalent or better fire-resistance rating and is tested/listed as an assembly

subject: Box Column Cladding/Casing
rule: Box column cladding/casing must allow for differential thermal movement between cladding and structural column
conditions: The cladding material has a different coefficient of thermal expansion than the column material
The installation spans more than one story or exceeds 6 m in length

subject: Free-standing Box Column
rule: A free-standing box column must have a vertical load path that transfers its own weight and any superimposed loads continuously to the ground or foundation
conditions: The column supports any load beyond its self-weight
The column is installed on a load-bearing surface
exceptions: Temporary installations where the column is laterally braced by adjacent structures

subject: Free-standing Box Column
rule: A free-standing box column must not have a base connection that permits uplift under expected wind or lateral loads without adequate anchorage
conditions: The column is exposed to wind loads
The column is located outdoors
exceptions: Columns that are sufficiently heavy that their self-weight alone resists overturning moment without requiring base anchorage

subject: Box Column Formwork
rule: Box column formwork must fully contain wet concrete without leakage during pouring and curing
conditions: when used for cast-in-place concrete columns

subject: Box Column Formwork
rule: Box column formwork must withstand the full hydrostatic head pressure of wet concrete without bursting or excessive deflection
conditions: when subjected to concrete placement and vibration

subject: Box Column Formwork
rule: Box column formwork must not have gaps or openings larger than the maximum aggregate size of the concrete mix
conditions: when used with aggregate concrete

subject: Ring Beam
rule: ring beam must be a continuous closed loop (or effectively closed) to resist hoop tension
conditions: when acting as a tension ring for dome or shell structures
exceptions: when the ring beam is purely decorative and carries no structural load

subject: Ring Beam
rule: ring beam must not have unreinforced concrete sections when subjected to tensile hoop stresses
conditions: when the ring beam is constructed of reinforced concrete and resists tension from an overhead dome or shell
exceptions: when the ring beam is of steel or other ductile material
when the ring beam is compression-only (e.g., at the base of an inverted dome)

subject: Ring Beam
rule: ring beam must be adequately anchored or tied into the supporting structure to prevent overturning or sliding under lateral thrust
conditions: when the ring beam supports a dome or shell that generates significant horizontal thrust
exceptions: when the structure is designed to resolve all thrust into compression only (e.g., a properly designed masonry dome with sufficient buttressing)

subject: Box Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: longitudinal bars must be evenly distributed around the column perimeter
conditions: column has circular or polygonal cross-section
reinforcement cage is prefabricated

subject: Box Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: ties or hoops must fully enclose all longitudinal bars within the cage

subject: Box Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: clear spacing between longitudinal bars must not be less than 25 mm (or 1.5× maximum aggregate size, whichever is larger)
conditions: concrete will be cast around the cage

subject: Box Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: laps and splices must not be located in the same cross-sectional plane
conditions: cage includes spliced or lapped connections

subject: Box Column Reinforcement Cage
rule: welded wire fabric or ties must have bend diameters compliant with rebar diameter ratios per applicable code
conditions: cage uses bent ties or hoops

subject: Parapet Beam
rule: parapet beam must transfer lateral wind loads to the primary lateral force resisting system
conditions: parapet is present
building is in a wind zone requiring structural design
exceptions: parapet beam is purely decorative and not structurally connected

subject: Parapet Beam
rule: parapet beam must have a minimum top surface slope or be detailed to prevent water ponding
conditions: parapet beam has a horizontal top surface
exceptions: parapet is covered by a sloped metal coping that provides positive drainage

subject: Parapet Beam
rule: parapet beam must not be constructed of unreinforced masonry in seismically active regions
conditions: building is located in a high seismic zone (e.g., SDC D, E, F per ASCE 7)
exceptions: parapet beam is isolated from the structure and designed as a nonstructural element with adequate seismic ties

subject: Wall Starter Beam
rule: Wall starter beam must be anchored to the foundation or supporting wall
conditions: beam is at the base of a wall system
beam transfers vertical load from wall to foundation

subject: Wall Starter Beam
rule: Wall starter beam must have minimum bearing length on supporting structure
conditions: beam sits on masonry or concrete support
exceptions: beam is continuously supported along its full length by a steel or concrete element rated for its load

subject: Wall Starter Beam
rule: Wall starter beam must not have untreated end-grain in contact with concrete or masonry
conditions: beam is timber/wood
exceptions: beam is treated or preservative-impregnated per code
beam is separated by an approved moisture barrier

subject: Wall Starter Beam
rule: Wall starter beam must be located at or below finished floor level for the wall it supports
conditions: beam is used in a framed wall system with a defined finished floor elevation
exceptions: design explicitly allows a raised starter beam with alternative load path documented

subject: Perimeter Foundation Beam
rule: perimeter foundation beam must be continuous around the entire building perimeter
conditions: building has a closed perimeter foundation system
exceptions: building has discontinuous foundation system such as isolated piers

subject: Perimeter Foundation Beam
rule: perimeter foundation beam must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate bearing capacity
conditions: beam is load-bearing
exceptions: beam is supported on deep foundations (piles or caissons)

subject: Perimeter Foundation Beam
rule: perimeter foundation beam must not be placed below the frost line without frost protection
conditions: site is in a frost-prone climate
exceptions: frost-protected shallow foundation design is used per applicable code

subject: Perimeter Foundation Beam
rule: perimeter foundation beam must have reinforcement that extends into intersecting foundation walls or columns
conditions: beam is cast-in-place reinforced concrete

subject: Bond Beam
rule: A bond beam must be horizontally continuous around the entire perimeter of a masonry wall at its designated level
conditions: When used as a horizontal structural diaphragm chord
When used as a seismic or wind tie
exceptions: When wall terminates before completing a full perimeter

subject: Bond Beam
rule: A bond beam must contain continuous longitudinal reinforcement with proper lap splices at all locations
conditions: When bond beam is serving a structural role in lateral or vertical load resistance

subject: Bond Beam
rule: A bond beam must not have vertical reinforcement passing through it that is tied only to the bond beam without continuing into the wall below
conditions: When the bond beam is at a horizontal plane that is not the top of wall

subject: Bond Beam
rule: A bond beam must be grouted solid (fully filled with grout) when it is part of the primary lateral-force-resisting system
conditions: When bond beam is part of the seismic force-resisting system
When bond beam is part of the wind force-resisting system
exceptions: When bond beam is purely nominal (non-structural) — e.g., a control joint bond beam not part of the lateral system

subject: Perimeter Beam-to-Column Connection
rule: A perimeter beam-to-column connection must transfer gravity loads (vertical shear) from the beam to the column without failure
conditions: Connection is subject to gravity loading

subject: Perimeter Beam-to-Column Connection
rule: A perimeter beam-to-column connection must transfer lateral loads (moment and/or shear) from the beam to the column to maintain frame stability
conditions: Connection is part of a moment-resisting or braced frame system
Building is subject to wind or seismic lateral loads
exceptions: Pinned (simple shear) connections in braced frames where lateral loads are carried by separate bracing elements rather than through beam-to-column joints

subject: Perimeter Beam-to-Column Connection
rule: The connection must not exhibit brittle fracture at design load levels
conditions: Connection is welded or uses high-strength bolts in tension
Ambient temperature is within design range for the steel grade

subject: Perimeter Beam-to-Column Connection
rule: Bolts or welds in the connection must have adequate strength (tension, shear, and combined) to resist factored design loads

subject: Vapor Barrier / Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor barrier/retarder must be placed on the warm side of the insulation assembly
conditions: In building envelope assemblies in heating-dominated climates
When used to control moisture diffusion
exceptions: When a vented air space exists between insulation and vapor retarder
In some mixed or cooling-dominated climates where placement may differ based on hygrothermal analysis

subject: Vapor Barrier / Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor barrier/retarder must not be installed on both sides of the same wall assembly
conditions: In conventional wood-frame wall assemblies
exceptions: When explicitly designed as a 'drying chamber' or when one side is a smart vapor retarder with variable permeance

subject: Vapor Barrier / Vapor Retarder
rule: Vapor barrier/retarder must not be installed over wet or damp substrate material
conditions: During installation of vapor retarder in any building assembly

subject: Weather-Resistive Barrier (WRB)
rule: WRB must be installed in a continuous plane on the exterior side of the sheathing to prevent bulk water intrusion
conditions: Exterior wall assembly
Building envelope

subject: Weather-Resistive Barrier (WRB)
rule: WRB must be lapped shingle-fashion (top over bottom) to shed water downward
conditions: Horizontal seams in WRB installation

subject: Weather-Resistive Barrier (WRB)
rule: WRB must not be installed with penetrations that are left unsealed
conditions: Penetrations through the WRB layer (e.g., fasteners, pipes, vents, windows)

subject: Self-Adhered Membrane (Peel-and-Stick)
rule: Self-adhered membrane (peel-and-stick) must be installed on a clean, dry substrate free of moisture, ice, frost, and debris
conditions: during installation

subject: Self-Adhered Membrane (Peel-and-Stick)
rule: Self-adhered membrane must not be installed on a substrate that is too wet to absorb primer (if primer is required) or that has standing water
conditions: during installation
when primer is specified by manufacturer

subject: Self-Adhered Membrane (Peel-and-Stick)
rule: Self-adhered membrane must be installed at a substrate temperature above the minimum application temperature specified by the manufacturer (typically above 40°F/4°C)
conditions: during installation

subject: Fluid-Applied Membrane
rule: Fluid-applied membrane must be applied over a substrate that is clean, dry, and free of contaminants
conditions: when used as a primary waterproofing layer
when applied in liquid form
exceptions: substrates specially prepared with manufacturer-approved primers that can tolerate minor moisture

subject: Fluid-Applied Membrane
rule: Fluid-applied membrane must be applied within the temperature range specified by the manufacturer
conditions: during installation

subject: Fluid-Applied Membrane
rule: Fluid-applied membrane must not be applied over standing water or during active precipitation
conditions: during installation

subject: Fluid-Applied Membrane
rule: Fluid-applied membrane must be applied at the minimum dry-film thickness specified by the manufacturer
conditions: when serving as the primary waterproofing layer

subject: Drainage Membrane / Mat
rule: Drainage membrane/mat must be placed on the low side of the drainage plane to allow water to exit the assembly
conditions: When installed in a wall or roof assembly as part of a rainscreen or drained system
exceptions: When used solely as a capillary break rather than for gravity drainage

subject: Drainage Membrane / Mat
rule: Drainage membrane/mat must not be compressed to less than its nominal thickness under design loads
conditions: When installed behind cladding, siding, or veneer where it defines the drainage gap

subject: Drainage Membrane / Mat
rule: Drainage membrane/mat must be lapped or drained such that water cannot be trapped behind it at horizontal seams or terminations
conditions: When installed in shingle-lap orientation or with horizontal joints

subject: Drainage Membrane / Mat
rule: Drainage membrane/mat must not be installed in direct contact with materials that are chemically incompatible (e.g., uncoated copper or certain asphaltic compounds)
conditions: When the mat is a polyolefin, polyester, or other plastic-based product susceptible to chemical degradation or plasticizer migration
exceptions: When a manufacturer-approved separation layer is provided

subject: House Wrap
rule: House wrap must be installed with the correct siding-facing side outward
conditions: When used as a weather-resistant barrier behind exterior cladding
exceptions: House wrap products that are non-directional (same performance on both sides)

subject: House Wrap
rule: House wrap must be lapped shingle-fashion (top over bottom) at horizontal seams
conditions: Where horizontal seams exist between adjacent rolls or sheets of house wrap

subject: House Wrap
rule: House wrap must not be left exposed to direct sunlight for longer than the manufacturer's specified duration
conditions: During construction sequencing before cladding is installed
exceptions: House wrap products specifically rated for extended UV exposure per manufacturer

subject: House Wrap
rule: House wrap fasteners (caps, staples, or nails) must be spaced per manufacturer specification to prevent sagging or detachment
conditions: During installation of house wrap over sheathing
exceptions: Products with integrated adhesive backing that eliminate the need for mechanical fasteners

subject: House Wrap
rule: Penetrations through house wrap (windows, doors, vents, pipes) must be flashed and taped with compatible flashing tape or sealant
conditions: Where any penetration or opening cuts through the house wrap plane

subject: Building Paper (Asphalt-Impregnated Felt)
rule: Building paper (asphalt-impregnated felt) must be installed with overlaps in the direction of water flow (shingle fashion) to ensure water shedding
conditions: installed as underlayment on sloped roofs
exposed to weather prior to final roofing
exceptions: temporary weather protection where lapping is not required (e.g., vertical surfaces)

subject: Building Paper (Asphalt-Impregnated Felt)
rule: Building paper must not be left exposed to UV radiation for extended periods beyond manufacturer's specified exposure limit
conditions: used as roof underlayment
exceptions: products specifically UV-rated for extended exposure

subject: Building Paper (Asphalt-Impregnated Felt)
rule: Building paper must not be installed on roof slopes below the minimum manufacturer-specified slope (typically 1:4 or steeper)
conditions: used as roof underlayment for asphalt shingles
exceptions: low-slope systems designed with self-adhering membrane underlayment instead
when manufacturer explicitly lists product for lower slope

subject: Building Paper (Asphalt-Impregnated Felt)
rule: Building paper must be installed with each successive course overlapping the course below by at least the code-minimum lap (typically 2 inches horizontal, 6 inches vertical)
conditions: installed as roof underlayment
exceptions: product-specific manufacturer instructions may require greater laps

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing Membrane
rule: below-grade waterproofing membrane must form a continuous barrier without gaps or punctures
conditions: applied to below-grade surfaces
exceptions: intentional penetrations are sealed with相匹配 waterstops or sealants

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing Membrane
rule: below-grade waterproofing membrane must be applied to the positive side (exterior side) of the structure
conditions: new construction below-grade walls and slabs
exceptions: internal (negative-side) waterproofing may be used when exterior access is impossible

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing Membrane
rule: below-grade waterproofing membrane must not be exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods
conditions: membrane exposed before backfilling
exceptions: membrane products specifically UV-rated for extended exposure

subject: Below-Grade Waterproofing Membrane
rule: below-grade waterproofing membrane must be protected from damage during backfilling
conditions: after membrane application, before and during backfill operations
exceptions: self-adhered membranes with integral slip-sheet that also acts as a protection layer

subject: Spray-Applied Vapor Retarder
rule: Spray-applied vapor retarder must be applied to a clean, dry, frost-free surface
conditions: Any application
exceptions: Manufacturer explicitly approves application on damp substrate

subject: Spray-Applied Vapor Retarder
rule: Spray-applied vapor retarder must achieve the minimum dry film thickness specified by the manufacturer
conditions: Any application

subject: Spray-Applied Vapor Retarder
rule: Spray-applied vapor retarder must not be applied when ambient or substrate temperature is below the manufacturer's minimum application temperature
conditions: Any application

subject: Spray-Applied Vapor Retarder
rule: Spray-applied vapor retarder must not be installed on the cold side of an assembly where it would trap moisture within the wall or roof in a given climate zone when that is contrary to the vapor retarder class placement rules of the applicable building code
conditions: Assemblies in climate zones where the vapor retarder class dictates placement on the warm side
exceptions: Engineered design with verified hygrothermal analysis showing no moisture accumulation risk

subject: Membrane Flashing Components
rule: Membrane flashing must be mechanically fastened or fully adhered at all edges and seams
conditions: When used as termination for membrane roofing system
exceptions: Self-adhered flashing systems with factory-applied adhesive that meet peel strength requirements

subject: Membrane Flashing Components
rule: Membrane flashing must not have exposed fasteners in standing water zones
conditions: When installed on low-slope or flat roofs

subject: Membrane Flashing Components
rule: Membrane flashing base metal or substrate must be continuous and rigid at all attachment points
conditions: When flashing is terminating a single-ply membrane roof

subject: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
rule: polyethylene sheet vapor barrier must be installed on the warm side of the insulation
conditions: when used in wall, roof, or floor assemblies in conditioned buildings
when functioning as a vapor retarder
exceptions: when assembly is designed to dry to the interior (e.g., in hot-humid climates where vapor drive is inward)

subject: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
rule: polyethylene sheet vapor barrier must not have significant punctures, tears, or unsealed penetrations
conditions: when installed as a continuous air and vapor retarder layer
exceptions: small fasteners sealed with gaskets or tape are acceptable

subject: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
rule: polyethylene sheet vapor barrier must not be installed where operating temperatures exceed its melting point (typically ~110°C / 230°F)
conditions: when polyethylene is the selected material
exceptions: specially formulated high-temperature polyethylene variants exist but are not standard sheet vapor barriers

subject: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
rule: polyethylene sheet vapor barrier must be lapped and sealed at all joints to maintain continuity
conditions: when multiple sheets are used to cover an area

subject: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
rule: polyethylene sheet vapor barrier must not be used on both sides of an assembly in cold climates
conditions: in cold climates (heating-dominated)
when assembly contains insulation
exceptions: very specific engineered assemblies designed to dry in both directions

subject: Vault Structural Frame
rule: Vault structural frame must be designed as a compression-dominated system with continuous load paths to foundations
conditions: Entity is a vault structural frame
Vault type is masonry, stone, or unreinforced concrete
exceptions: Modern reinforced concrete or steel vaults designed as tension structures

subject: Vault Structural Frame
rule: Vault structural frame must not have lateral thrusts that are unbalanced or unrestrained
conditions: Entity is a vault structural frame
Vault is not a dome or other radially symmetric form
exceptions: Vaults with active tie-rods or buttressing systems designed to resist thrust

subject: Vault Structural Frame
rule: Vault structural frame must have all voussoir/block interfaces in compression under all credible load combinations
conditions: Entity is a masonry or stone vault structural frame
exceptions: Tension-resisting connections used in reinforced concrete or steel vaults

subject: Vault Structural Frame
rule: Vault structural frame must have a rise-to-span ratio that keeps the thrust line within the masonry depth
conditions: Entity is a masonry or stone vault structural frame
exceptions: Vaults with additional reinforcing, ties, or composite construction

subject: Vault Extrados / Backing
rule: Vault extrados/backing must provide continuous load distribution over the vault below to prevent point-load cracking
conditions: when acting as the structural backing for vault masonry or voussoirs
exceptions: when a separate load-distribution layer (e.g., concrete topping) is explicitly designed above the backing

subject: Vault Extrados / Backing
rule: Vault extrados/backing must not contain voids or uncompacted zones that could lead to differential settlement or thrust line deviation
conditions: when the backing is load-bearing and supports superimposed dead or live loads
exceptions: when the voids are intentional, controlled, and structurally analyzed (e.g., relieving arches or void formers designed by a structural engineer)

subject: Vault Extrados / Backing
rule: Vault extrados/backing must be fully bonded or keyed to the vault ring to prevent delamination under horizontal thrust
conditions: when the backing is cast or placed directly against the vault extrados without mechanical connectors
