exceptions: when a slip plane or separation layer is intentionally provided and accounted for in the structural design (e.g., for thermal movement or independent structural action)

subject: Vault Fill / Levelling Layer
rule: vault fill / levelling layer must be composed of material with adequate compressive strength to support overlying loads without excessive deformation
conditions: when used as a structural substrate beneath floor finishes or paving
exceptions: when the layer is purely decorative and experiences no load bearing function

subject: Vault Fill / Levelling Layer
rule: vault fill / levelling layer must not retain water that could cause freeze-thaw damage or moisture migration to adjacent materials
conditions: when installed in exterior or damp-exposure applications
exceptions: when the assembly includes a dedicated drainage system that renders water retention irrelevant

subject: Vault Reinforcing
rule: vault reinforcing must provide continuous load path from vault surface to foundation or supporting structure
conditions: when used in a structural vault system

subject: Vault Reinforcing
rule: vault reinforcing must have sufficient tensile capacity to resist hoop and diagonal tension stresses at vault springing points
conditions: when the vault spans more than a single small bay
when the vault is not completely buried/earth-supported

subject: Vault Reinforcing
rule: vault reinforcing must not be placed on the compression face of a thin-shell vault without adequate cover and bond
conditions: in thin-shell (membrane) vault construction

subject: Vault Reinforcing
rule: vault reinforcing must be anchored or tied into the vault's abutment or buttressing elements
conditions: for unreinforced masonry vaults being retrofit with reinforcing

subject: Vault Springing Point / Haunch
rule: a vault springing point/haunch must provide a continuous load path to transfer thrust forces from the vault web into the supporting structure (wall, column, or buttress)
conditions: the vault is masonry or unreinforced
the haunch carries net horizontal thrust
exceptions: vaults designed with a horizontal tie-rod or post-tensioned cable at the springing level that resolves thrust independently of the haunch

subject: Vault Springing Point / Haunch
rule: the haunch must not be detailed with a reduced cross-section or unreinforced notch at the springing line that creates a plane of weakness under asymmetric loading
conditions: the structure is subjected to uneven loading (e.g., snow drift, seismic, or one-sided live load)
exceptions: the notch is intentionally detailed as a controlled failure fuse in a seismic design with validated ductile behavior

subject: Vault Springing Point / Haunch
rule: the springing point must be restrained against horizontal displacement (i.e., cannot be a simple roller or free-sliding bearing at the springing line)
conditions: the vault is a non-prestressed masonry or concrete arch/vault
the supporting structure relies on the vault for lateral stability
exceptions: the vault forms part of a tied-arch or bowstring system where the tie resolves all horizontal reactions

subject: Vault Keystone / Crown
rule: vault keystone must be the last stone placed during arch construction
conditions: when constructing a true stone vault or arch
exceptions: modern reinforced concrete or monolithic construction where keystones are cast in place

subject: Vault Keystone / Crown
rule: vault keystone must transfer compressive load laterally to adjacent voussoirs
conditions: when the keystone is part of a load-bearing stone or masonry vault
exceptions: purely decorative keystones or crown elements with no structural function

subject: Vault Keystone / Crown
rule: vault keystone must not be removed while the vault is under load
conditions: when the vault supports any superimposed load beyond its self-weight
exceptions: during controlled demolition where temporary shoring is installed

subject: Vault Keystone / Crown
rule: vault keystone must have tapered sides narrower at the bottom than the top (wedge geometry)
conditions: when the keystone is a voussoir in a gravity-loaded arch or vault
exceptions: non-structural decorative keystones
keystones in tensile or cable-net structures

subject: Vault Tie Rod / Lateral Restraint
rule: tie rod must be in pure tension (no bending or compression)
conditions: when installed as a lateral restraint for a vault or arch

subject: Vault Tie Rod / Lateral Restraint
rule: tie rod end connections must be capable of developing the full tensile capacity of the rod
conditions: when used as a primary lateral restraint for a vault

subject: Vault Tie Rod / Lateral Restraint
rule: tie rod must not be post-installed in a way that damages the surrounding masonry or structure
conditions: when retrofitting into existing masonry vaults or walls

subject: Groin / Intersection Rib
rule: Groin/Intersection Rib must be aligned with the intersecting barrel vault geometries
conditions: When used at the intersection of two or more barrel vaults

subject: Groin / Intersection Rib
rule: Groin/Intersection Rib must transfer load from the vault web to the supporting columns or walls
conditions: When functioning as a load-bearing structural rib rather than purely decorative

subject: Groin / Intersection Rib
rule: Groin/Intersection Rib must not deviate from the true geometric intersection curve of the vault surfaces
conditions: In any load-bearing groin vault configuration

subject: Vault Formwork / Centering
rule: vault formwork/centering must maintain geometric continuity without abrupt changes in curvature or section
conditions: vault is constructed with continuous formwork panels
centering system supports the formwork during concrete placement
exceptions: vault has a deliberate segmented or faceted design intent

subject: Vault Formwork / Centering
rule: vault formwork/centering must not impose non-axial lateral thrusts on supporting falsework or shores
conditions: centering frame is of the 'arching' or 'ribbed' type
vault is under construction and uncured
exceptions: system is specifically designed with moment-resisting connections to absorb lateral forces

subject: Vault Formwork / Centering
rule: vault formwork/centering must be removable without damaging the hardened concrete or disturbing the vault's permanent structure
conditions: formwork is designed as 'striking' or 'de-centering' system
exceptions: vault formwork is designed as permanent (lost) formwork embedded in the final structure

subject: Vault Skylight / Oculus
rule: oculus opening must be weather-sealed against water ingress at all perimeter edges
conditions: oculus is exposed to exterior environment
exceptions: oculus is interior-only decorative element with no weather exposure

subject: Vault Skylight / Oculus
rule: vault skylight glazing must be impact-resistant or protected from overhead falling debris
conditions: skylight is located below roof elements or near structures that could shed ice, snow, or loose material
exceptions: skylight is in a location with no overhead hazard (e.g., below only open sky with no adjacent higher roof or facade)

subject: Vault Skylight / Oculus
rule: oculus must not create a condensation path that drips into occupied space
conditions: oculus is located in a climate where interior humidity can condense on cold surfaces
oculus has no active condensation management system
exceptions: oculus is in an unconditioned or arid space where dew point is never reached on the oculus surfaces

subject: Vault Skylight / Oculus
rule: vault skylight must be structurally capable of supporting its self-weight plus any imposed snow load
conditions: skylight is located in a climate with potential snow accumulation
exceptions: skylight is in a zero-snow climate or is steep enough that snow sloughs off before accumulating

subject: Barrel Vault
rule: a barrel vault must have its axis horizontal or nearly horizontal
exceptions: inclined barrel vaults used for stairs or ramps where the vault axis follows the slope

subject: Barrel Vault
rule: a barrel vault must have continuous support along its entire length (both edges or springing lines)
conditions: self-supporting masonry or unreinforced concrete barrel vault
exceptions: short vaults spanning between cross-walls or diaphragms that act as discrete supports; reinforced concrete or steel barrel shells that can cantilever

subject: Barrel Vault
rule: the horizontal thrust of a barrel vault must be resisted at both springing lines
conditions: masonry or unreinforced concrete barrel vault
exceptions: vault with tied rods across the span; vault abutted by opposing vault or buttress on both sides; reinforced concrete shell that can handle thrust through the shell membrane

subject: Barrel Vault
rule: the rise-to-span ratio of a barrel vault must not be excessively flat (below approximately 1:8)
conditions: masonry or unreinforced concrete barrel vault
exceptions: vault constructed with reinforcing steel or post-tensioning; vault with a stiffening edge beam

subject: Barrel Vault
rule: a barrel vault must not have large concentrated loads at mid-span unless the vault is appropriately reinforced
conditions: thin-shell or masonry barrel vault
exceptions: vault designed with ribs, stiffeners, or reinforced concrete capable of handling point loads

subject: Groin Vault / Cross Vault
rule: Groin vault / cross vault must have its diagonal ribs (groins) properly centered at the vault's apex to transfer thrust forces downward to the supporting piers or columns
conditions: The vault is constructed from masonry (stone or brick)
exceptions: Modern reinforced concrete groin vaults may not require centering of groins in the same way

subject: Groin Vault / Cross Vault
rule: Groin vault / cross vault must rest upon four supporting points (piers or columns) at the corners of the bay
conditions: The vault is a single square or rectangular bay
exceptions: Continuous series of groin vaults (e.g., in a basilica nave) may share supports between adjacent bays

subject: Groin Vault / Cross Vault
rule: Groin vault / cross vault must not have unsupported horizontal thrust at the springing points without lateral restraint (e.g., buttressing, tie rods, or abutment)
conditions: The vault is built from masonry materials
exceptions: Reinforced concrete or steel groin vaults can resist thrust through material tension capacity

subject: Rib Vault
rule: A rib vault must transfer its lateral thrust to a supporting buttress or adjacent vault
conditions: When constructed in stone or masonry
exceptions: When the rib vault is constructed from reinforced concrete or other materials with tensile capacity

subject: Rib Vault
rule: The diagonal ribs of a rib vault must intersect at the vault's apex and form a structurally continuous load path

subject: Rib Vault
rule: The web panels between ribs must be light enough that they do not cause the ribs to buckle or exceed their load capacity
conditions: When the webs are load-bearing masonry infill

subject: Fan Vault
rule: fan vault must have all ribs converging at a single central boss or ring
conditions: when constructed as a true fan vault (not a lierne or net vault)
exceptions: asymmetrical fan vaults where multiple centers exist due to irregular bay geometry

subject: Fan Vault
rule: fan vault must have vertical structural support at each springing point
conditions: for any fan vault spanning a bay
exceptions: when the fan vault is purely decorative (e.g., plaster replica attached to a separate structural ceiling)

subject: Fan Vault
rule: fan vault ribs must not be constructed from timber alone without embedding in a structural matrix
conditions: when the vault is a load-bearing stone fan vault (not a modern lightweight replica)
exceptions: timber fan vaults used as temporary formwork or ceiling linings where no structural load is carried

subject: Dome / Sail Vault
rule: dome or sail vault must have continuous compression ring at its base to resist lateral thrust
conditions: dome or sail vault is built in masonry or unreinforced concrete
dome or sail vault spans more than a minimal width
exceptions: dome or sail vault is a thin-shell reinforced concrete design with tension ring or post-tensioned edge beam

subject: Dome / Sail Vault
rule: dome or sail vault must not exceed the slenderness ratio where buckling is possible under its own weight
conditions: dome or sail vault is a thin-shell (thickness-to-span ratio less than about 1:100)
exceptions: vault is provided with stiffening ribs or a post-tensioned edge system that prevents bifurcation buckling

subject: Dome / Sail Vault
rule: dome or sail vault must have a waterproof outer layer or continuous drainage path to prevent water ponding
conditions: dome or sail vault is exposed to precipitation

subject: Dome / Sail Vault
rule: dome or sail vault must not have tension at the base if relying solely on unreinforced masonry
conditions: dome or sail vault is constructed from unreinforced masonry units without metal ties or reinforcement
exceptions: dome base is restrained by heavy buttresses, an external compression ring, or a surrounding structure that absorbs the tensile component

subject: Segment / Surbased Vault
rule: a surbased vault segment must have a continuous longitudinal thrust line contained entirely within the masonry section
conditions: the vault is constructed in unreinforced masonry

subject: Segment / Surbased Vault
rule: the rise-to-span ratio of a segmental surbased vault must be greater than zero

subject: Segment / Surbased Vault
rule: the horizontal thrust at the springings must be resisted by the supporting structure or tie-rods
conditions: the vault is a full-span segmental arch

subject: Segment / Surbased Vault
rule: voussoir bed joints must be normal to the intrados curve
conditions: the vault is constructed with cut stone voussoirs

subject: Guastavino / Tile Vault
rule: The tile vault must be constructed with interlocking masonry units arranged in a cohesive compression-only form, without tensile reinforcement
conditions: All tile vault designs
exceptions: Modern hybrid Guastavino systems that incorporate embedded steel or concrete reinforcement

subject: Guastavino / Tile Vault
rule: The tile vault must have a continuous compression thrust path to ground or to massive buttressing elements capable of resisting horizontal thrust
conditions: All tile vault designs where the vault is self-supporting without hidden steel tension ties
exceptions: Vaults where hidden steel tie rods are incorporated within the tile mass to absorb thrust

subject: Guastavino / Tile Vault
rule: The tile vault must not be subjected to significant point loads or asymmetric live loads that would generate tensile stresses in the masonry
conditions: Vaults without supplementary reinforcement or a suspended structural deck above the tiles
exceptions: Tile vaults designed as a permanent formwork (Guastavino 'suspended' system) where a concrete slab above carries loads independently

subject: Guastavino / Tile Vault
rule: The tile vault's construction sequence must proceed with each layer of tiles fully setting before the next layer is applied, and centering/formwork must remain in place until the mortar achieves sufficient strength
conditions: Vaults built in the traditional layered Guastavino method without modern fast-setting adhesives or permanent formwork
exceptions: Vaults using rapid-setting cements or permanent steel centering that remains in place

subject: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
rule: vault waterproofing membrane must be continuous across the entire vault surface without gaps or breaks
conditions: vault has below-grade or earth-covered portions
vault is exposed to water ingress risk
exceptions: intentionally designed penetration points with proper sealing details

subject: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
rule: vault waterproofing membrane must not be installed over unprepared or incompatible substrate that contains sharp protrusions, debris, or materials that can puncture the membrane
conditions: substrate is concrete, masonry, or other rigid backing
exceptions: a protective geotextile bedding layer is placed between substrate and membrane

subject: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
rule: vault waterproofing membrane must be protected from UV radiation if exposed above grade for more than the manufacturer's specified duration prior to backfill or covering
conditions: vault waterproofing membrane is exposed above grade for extended period before covering
exceptions: membrane material is specifically rated for prolonged UV exposure per manufacturer specification

subject: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
rule: vault waterproofing membrane must be lapped or joined at seams according to manufacturer-specified overlap dimension and bonding method
conditions: membrane is installed in multiple sheets or rolls requiring seams
exceptions: single-piece pre-fabricated membrane with no field seams

subject: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
rule: vault waterproofing membrane must not be installed when ambient or substrate temperature is outside the manufacturer's specified application temperature range
conditions: membrane is adhesive-applied, torch-applied, or self-adhering type with temperature-sensitive bonding

subject: Vault Acoustic Treatment
rule: Vault acoustic treatment must not obstruct required means of egress pathways
conditions: When installed in ceilings above occupied spaces
When located near exit routes or corridors
exceptions: When treatment is recessed above minimum height clearances required by code
When treatment is certified as non-combustible and rated for plenum use

subject: Vault Acoustic Treatment
rule: Vault acoustic treatment must have positive mechanical attachment to structure
conditions: When installed overhead in any occupiable space

subject: Vault Acoustic Treatment
rule: Vault acoustic treatment must not shed combustible debris into HVAC supply or return airstreams
conditions: When installed in ceiling plenums used for air handling
When material is fibrous or friable
exceptions: When material is fully encapsulated in non-combustible, non-shedding facing

subject: Cloister Vault / Domical Vault
rule: domical vault / cloister vault must have a continuous compression ring at its base to resist horizontal thrust
conditions: constructed in masonry
constructed in stone
constructed in brick
exceptions: when constructed in reinforced concrete with tension reinforcement
when constructed with buttressing or tie rods that counteract thrust

subject: Cloister Vault / Domical Vault
rule: cloister vault / domical vault must not have unsupported openings or penetrations that interrupt the structural continuity of the vault shell
conditions: load-bearing vault
exceptions: when edges of openings are reinforced with a structural ring or arch
when the vault is a non-structural ceiling finish only

subject: Cloister Vault / Domical Vault
rule: cloister vault / domical vault must have its springing points restrained against outward lateral movement
conditions: masonry or stone construction
exceptions: vault cast integrally with supporting walls in monolithic concrete that provides continuity

subject: Vault Drainage / Weep System
rule: vault drainage / weep system must have a continuous, unobstructed drainage path to the building exterior
conditions: when installed in a below-grade or earth-covered vault
when used to relieve hydrostatic pressure against the vault structure
exceptions: when drainage is directed to an active mechanical pumping system that removes water

subject: Vault Drainage / Weep System
rule: weep holes or drainage outlets must not be positioned below the exterior grade or finished floor level that would allow backflow of water into the vault
conditions: when weep holes are used as passive drainage outlets
exceptions: when a backflow prevention device or positive-pressure check valve is installed at each outlet

subject: Vault Drainage / Weep System
rule: the weep system drainage layer must have a filter fabric or aggregate gradation that prevents soil migration into the drainage system
conditions: when drainage system is in contact with native soil or backfill material

subject: Vault Ribbing
rule: vault ribbing must be continuous and unbroken across the span
conditions: when used in load-bearing vault construction
exceptions: ribs designed with intentional separation as part of a segmented or articulated structural system

subject: Vault Ribbing
rule: vault ribbing must not have abrupt changes in cross-section along its length
conditions: when the rib is structural (load-bearing)
exceptions: ribs where cross-section changes are deliberately engineered and reinforced at transition points

subject: Vault Geometry Types
rule: Vault must have a continuous thrust line contained entirely within the masonry section
conditions: When constructed in unreinforced masonry
When designed as a compression-only structure
exceptions: Reinforced or post-tensioned vaults

subject: Vault Geometry Types
rule: Vault geometry must be doubly curved (synclastic or anticlastic) to resist membrane forces without bending
conditions: When designed as a thin-shell concrete or masonry vault
When spanning more than 6 meters
exceptions: Barrel vaults with stiffening ribs
Vaults with active post-tensioning

subject: Vault Geometry Types
rule: Vault span-to-rise ratio must not exceed 4:1 for unreinforced masonry barrel vaults
conditions: When constructed in unreinforced masonry
When no buttressing or tie-rods are provided
exceptions: Vaults with external steel or concrete buttressing
Vaults with internal post-tensioning

subject: Vault Geometry Types
rule: Vault geometry must provide a continuous lateral thrust path to foundations or buttressing
conditions: When the vault is a barrel vault, groin vault, or cross vault
exceptions: Self-balanced forms such as domes on pendentives
Vaults with internal tie-rods

subject: Vault Haunch
rule: haunch must maintain a minimum depth to accommodate vault thrust and reinforcement cover
conditions: when used as a structural transition between column and vault

subject: Vault Haunch
rule: haunch reinforcement must be continuous with both column and vault reinforcement
conditions: when the vault haunch is monolithic reinforced concrete
exceptions: precast or post-tensioned connections where mechanical couplers provide equivalent continuity

subject: Vault Haunch
rule: vault haunch must not have abrupt changes in cross-section that cause stress concentration
conditions: in load-bearing vault structures
exceptions: if designed with verified finite element analysis showing acceptable stress distribution

subject: Vault Crown
rule: vault crown must be constructed of a material with sufficient compressive strength to resist the thrust forces generated by the arch geometry
conditions: the vault crown is part of a masonry or unreinforced stone arch
exceptions: vault crown is part of a reinforced concrete or steel arch where tensile forces are carried by reinforcement

subject: Vault Crown
rule: vault crown must not have a flat or horizontal extrados without proper drainage provision
conditions: the vault crown is exposed to weather
exceptions: the vault crown is covered by an impermeable membrane and positive roof drainage system

subject: Vault Crown
rule: vault crown must maintain a minimum thickness sufficient to prevent snap-through buckling under self-weight and imposed loads
conditions: the vault is a thin-shell or masonry construction
exceptions: the vault is a fully reinforced concrete shell designed with explicit buckling analysis

subject: Vault Voussoirs
rule: Voussoir wedge geometry must maintain radial compression (no tensile stress across joints)
conditions: When used in a vault or arch structure
exceptions: If voussoirs are bonded with high-tensile adhesive or reinforcement that resists tension

subject: Vault Voussoirs
rule: Voussoir bed faces must be cut to exact mating surfaces (no gaps that prevent full contact)
conditions: When voussoirs are dry-laid (without mortar)
exceptions: If mortar or grout is used to fill gaps and transfer load

subject: Vault Lateral Buttressing
rule: vault lateral buttressing must transfer horizontal thrust from the vault to the ground or a structurally equivalent rigid support
conditions: vault is masonry
vault is semicircular or pointed (Gothic)
exceptions: modern reinforced concrete vaults with tied rods acting as integrated buttressing

subject: Vault Lateral Buttressing
rule: vault lateral buttressing must be laterally continuous with no gaps in the thrust path at any horizontal section through the buttress
conditions: buttress is masonry

subject: Vault Lateral Buttressing
rule: vault lateral buttress must not be undermined by excavation below its foundation level
conditions: buttress is founded on soil
exceptions: excavation is compensated by deep foundation elements (piles or caissons) installed before excavation

subject: Vault Lateral Buttressing
rule: vault lateral buttress must have a width at its base sufficient to keep the resultant thrust within the middle third of the foundation
conditions: buttress is masonry
foundation is on compressible soil
exceptions: rock foundation where tensile capacity exists
buttress is reinforced concrete with continuous foundation tie

subject: Vault Infill / Backing
rule: vault infill or backing must not be used as the primary structural load-bearing element
conditions: when used in masonry vault construction
when the vault is expected to carry significant imposed loads beyond self-weight
exceptions: when the infill/backing material is specifically designed and engineered as a composite structural system (e.g., reinforced concrete fill in a ribbed vault)

subject: Vault Infill / Backing
rule: vault infill or backing must be adequately bonded to or interlocked with the primary vault structure
conditions: when the infill/backing is placed against structural ribs, voussoirs, or a masonry shell
exceptions: when a deliberate separation layer (e.g., slip plane or isolation membrane) is required for differential movement or waterproofing

subject: Vault Infill / Backing
rule: vault infill or backing material density must not exceed the bearing capacity of the supporting vault structure
conditions: when the infill or backing adds significant dead load to the vault
exceptions: when the vault and supports have been specifically designed and verified for the additional weight

subject: Vault Infill / Backing
rule: vault infill or backing must not act as a continuous water-saturated mass against the interior finish or structure
conditions: in exterior or semi-exposed vault applications
when the infill is hygroscopic or porous
exceptions: when a dedicated drainage plane, waterproofing membrane, and weep system are provided to keep the infill dry

subject: Vault Penetrations & Openings
rule: Penetrations through vault structures must maintain the structural integrity of the vault (no cutting or coring that reduces load-bearing capacity below design requirements)
conditions: Any penetration through a structural vault (concrete, masonry, or metal vault)
Penetrations for pipes, ducts, conduits, or cables
exceptions: Penetrations specifically designed into the vault structure by a structural engineer and reinforced per engineering specifications

subject: Vault Penetrations & Openings
rule: Vault penetrations must be fire-stopped and sealed to maintain the fire-resistance rating of the vault assembly
conditions: Vault forms part of a fire-rated assembly
Penetration passes through the vault boundary

subject: Vault Penetrations & Openings
rule: Vault penetrations must not create a water leakage path into the vault interior
conditions: Vault is located below grade, below a water table, or in a weather-exposed position

subject: Vault Penetrations & Openings
rule: Penetration sleeves or openings through vault walls must be provided with a watertight seal at both the interior and exterior faces of the vault
conditions: Vault is below grade or exposed to moisture

subject: Vault Edge / Wall Connections
rule: Vault edge/wall connection must transfer horizontal thrust from the vault to the wall
conditions: vault is non-counterforted
vault is not a tie-rod system
exceptions: vault is designed as a freestanding, self-balanced shell without thrust

subject: Vault Edge / Wall Connections
rule: Vault edge/wall connection must be capable of accommodating differential movement between the vault and the wall without loss of structural continuity
conditions: materials with differing coefficients of thermal expansion or creep are used
exceptions: vault and wall are monolithically cast from the same material

subject: Vault Edge / Wall Connections
rule: Vault edge must not be connected to a wall that lacks sufficient mass or stiffness to resist the vault's thrust
conditions: the wall is a lightweight partition
the wall is unreinforced and slender
exceptions: the vault is a simple barrel vault with buttresses or counterforts that independently resist thrust

subject: Vault Drainage Elements
rule: vault drainage elements must provide a continuous gravity-driven path for water to exit the building envelope
conditions: vault is exposed to precipitation
vault forms part of the building envelope
exceptions: vault is entirely interior and not exposed to water ingress

subject: Vault Drainage Elements
rule: vault drainage elements must not block or obstruct the designed drainage path
conditions: drainage path has been designed as part of the vault system

subject: Vault Drainage Elements
rule: vault drainage elements must have sufficient capacity to handle the design storm event flow rate
conditions: vault is subject to rainfall or snowmelt

subject: Vault Thermal Insulation Layer
rule: vault thermal insulation layer must maintain continuous thermal barrier without gaps or compression
conditions: vault is part of a conditioned building envelope
insulation is installed between structural and weathering layers
exceptions: intentional thermal breaks at structural connections

subject: Vault Thermal Insulation Layer
rule: vault thermal insulation layer must not be positioned where it would be compressed beyond its design thickness by vault curvature or structural loads
conditions: insulation material is fibrous or compressible (e.g., mineral wool, fiberglass)
vault curvature radius is smaller than manufacturer's minimum bend radius for the product

subject: Vault Thermal Insulation Layer
rule: vault thermal insulation layer must be protected from moisture ingress on the cold side
conditions: vault is exposed to exterior climate conditions
exceptions: insulation material is closed-cell and inherently moisture-impermeable

subject: Cross Vault Intersection
rule: Cross Vault Intersection must have a bearing capacity analysis
conditions: when used as a load-bearing structural element

subject: Cross Vault Intersection
rule: Cross Vault Intersection must maintain geometric continuity of the groin lines
exceptions: if the intersection is purely decorative and non-structural with separate independent support

subject: Cross Vault Intersection
rule: Cross Vault Intersection must_not have masonry voussoirs spanning across the intersection without proper centering during construction
conditions: when constructed in unreinforced masonry

subject: Operable Window
rule: operable window must have a functional opening mechanism (hinge, pivot, slider, or projection) that allows the sash to move between open and closed positions
conditions: window is designated as operable rather than fixed

subject: Operable Window
rule: operable window must have a weather seal or gasket system that prevents air and water infiltration when in the closed position
conditions: window is installed in an exterior wall exposed to weather

subject: Operable Window
rule: operable window must_not have its operating hardware (crank, handle, lock) obstructed by the window frame, surrounding structure, or adjacent window when moving through its full range of motion

subject: Operable Window
rule: operable sash must be retained within the frame by a physical restraint system (hinges, tracks, balances, or stays) that prevents unintended dislodgement under gravity or wind loads

subject: Operable Window
rule: operable window glass panel must be structurally capable of withstanding the design wind load without fracture when the window is in the closed and latched position
conditions: window is installed in a location subject to wind loading
exceptions: windows located in fully protected interior partitions not subject to wind

subject: Glass Curtain Wall
rule: glass curtain wall must have its weight transferred to the building structure at each floor level or at discrete anchorage points
conditions: multi-story building
curtain wall spans vertically beyond one story
exceptions: structural glass fins or mullions designed to cantilever from base without intermediate attachments

subject: Glass Curtain Wall
rule: glass curtain wall must accommodate differential movement between the curtain wall frame and the building structure
conditions: building experiences thermal expansion/contraction
building experiences structural settlement or drift

subject: Glass Curtain Wall
rule: glass curtain wall must not have water penetrate through the assembly into the building interior under wind-driven rain conditions
conditions: exterior exposure to rainfall
exceptions: intentionally designed rainwater harvesting systems where interior collection is planned and drained

subject: Glass Curtain Wall
rule: glass curtain wall must have thermally broken framing in conditioned building applications
conditions: building is heated or cooled
climate includes significant temperature differential between interior and exterior
exceptions: unconditioned buildings such as parking garages or unconditioned atriums

subject: Pivot Door
rule: pivot door must have a hinge axis that is plumb (vertical) relative to the finished floor
conditions: door is installed in a vertical wall opening
door is side-hung (standard pivot) rather than center-pivot

subject: Pivot Door
rule: pivot door must not have its pivot point located beyond the door leaf width from the door edge
conditions: door uses a floor-mounted or top-mounted pivot set

subject: Pivot Door
rule: pivot door must have a bottom clearance (gap) between door bottom and finished floor that accommodates the pivot arc
conditions: floor is level and rigid

subject: French Door
rule: french door must have tempered or laminated glass if located within 18 inches of a walking surface or within hazardous areas such as near bathtubs, showers, or pools
conditions: door is glazed
door is within 18 inches of floor or walking surface
door is adjacent to wet areas or hazardous locations
exceptions: fully tempered glass less than 6 inches above walking surface may still be required

subject: French Door
rule: french door must have a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches in emergency egress configuration when serving a sleeping room
conditions: door serves a sleeping room
door is part of the required egress path
exceptions: existing buildings under certain code cycles may have 28-inch minimum

subject: French Door
rule: french door must open outward when serving a space with limited interior floor area (e.g., closet under 10 sq ft) to avoid blocking interior space
conditions: door serves a very small interior space
exceptions: pocket or sliding french door types

subject: French Door
rule: french door frame must have a continuous load path and rough opening must be framed to transfer vertical and lateral loads to supporting structure
conditions: door is load-bearing or installed in a structural wall
exceptions: non-load-bearing interior french doors

subject: Folding Door (Bi-fold)
rule: a folding door (bi-fold) must have a hinge or pivot mechanism at each panel joint to enable folding motion
conditions: the door is operable
the door has more than one panel

subject: Folding Door (Bi-fold)
rule: a folding door (bi-fold) must have a top track or bottom guide (or both) to constrain panel travel
conditions: the door is top-hung or bottom-rolling
exceptions: a freestanding bi-fold screen with no floor or overhead track may use only hinges and a fixed pivot point

subject: Folding Door (Bi-fold)
rule: the total width of a folding door (bi-fold) must not exceed the opening width when fully unfolded
conditions: the door is installed in a framed opening

subject: Folding Door (Bi-fold)
rule: a bi-fold door must not have panels wider than the headroom available for stacking depth when fully folded
conditions: the door folds to one or both sides of the opening
stacking space is limited by adjacent walls or cabinetry

subject: Acoustic Door
rule: acoustic door must have an acoustic seal (gasket or drop seal) around its perimeter
conditions: used in noise-sensitive space (e.g., recording studio, theater, hospital room)

subject: Acoustic Door
rule: acoustic door must not have through-openings or gaps that bypass the acoustic barrier
conditions: door is in a rated sound-isolating assembly
exceptions: vision panels or louvers that are themselves acoustically rated and sealed

subject: Acoustic Door
rule: acoustic door must be installed in an acoustically rated frame with proper frame-to-wall sealant

subject: Door Frame & Lining
rule: door frame and lining must be plumb (vertically aligned) within structural tolerances
conditions: in all installations

subject: Door Frame & Lining
rule: door frame and lining must be rigidly fixed to the surrounding structural opening
conditions: in all installations

subject: Door Frame & Lining
rule: door frame and lining must not be installed where the structural opening is incomplete or unstable
conditions: during construction sequence

subject: Window Frame & Sash
rule: Window frame and sash assembly must be weather-sealed to prevent air and water infiltration at all interfaces between frame and wall opening
conditions: Window is installed in an exterior wall
Window is exposed to exterior environment

subject: Window Frame & Sash
rule: Sash must be capable of opening and closing freely within the frame without binding or jamming
conditions: Window is operable (not fixed/picture window)
exceptions: Fixed/picture windows with no operable sash

subject: Window Frame & Sash
rule: Window frame and sash assembly must accommodate differential thermal expansion between frame materials and glass without causing glass fracture or seal failure
conditions: Assembly contains dissimilar materials (e.g., aluminum frame with glass, or vinyl frame with glass)

subject: Window Frame & Sash
rule: Window frame must not transmit structural loads from the building structure through the glass panes
conditions: Window is non-structural (typical application)

subject: Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: Glass panel must have edge support (e.g., frame, structural sealant, or point-fixing) to prevent out-of-plane displacement under positive or negative wind load
conditions: installed vertically or inclined in a building envelope

subject: Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: Glass panel must not be subjected to hard-point contact (point load) on its face without load-spreading washer or bearing plate
conditions: used in point-fixed or bolted glazing system
exceptions: laminated glass with interlayer designed for local point loading per manufacturer specification

subject: Glazing / Glass Panel
rule: Glass panel must not be installed in a location where uniform temperature differential across the panel exceeds the glass type's rated thermal shock resistance
conditions: exposed to direct solar radiation with shaded or covered edge zones
exceptions: fully tempered glass rated for thermal shock per ASTM E2431

subject: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
rule: Door hinges must be made of a material with sufficient load-bearing capacity for the door weight
conditions: The door is in a permanent installation
The door is of standard construction (wood, metal, composite)
exceptions: Temporary or lightweight decorative doors that are non-load-bearing

subject: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
rule: Door lock/latch bolt must engage fully with the strike plate or frame receptor
conditions: The door is intended to be securable (latched or locked closed)

subject: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
rule: Handle or knob must be securely fastened to the spindle or mechanism such that it cannot detach under normal operating force

subject: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
rule: Door hardware must not have sharp edges or protrusions that pose laceration or snagging hazard at normal touch points

subject: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
rule: Lock cylinder must be compatible with the keyway (or credential type) it is intended to accept
conditions: The lock is a keyed or electronic-credential lock

subject: Window Hardware (Catch, Stay, Hinges)
rule: window hardware catch, stay, or hinges must be rated for the weight and size of the window sash they support
conditions: window assembly includes an operable sash

subject: Window Hardware (Catch, Stay, Hinges)
rule: window hinges must not be installed in a reverse orientation that prevents the sash from closing or locking
conditions: hinges are used on side-hung or top-hung casement windows

subject: Window Hardware (Catch, Stay, Hinges)
rule: window catch must engage positively with the striker plate when the sash is closed
conditions: window includes a locking catch mechanism

subject: Window Hardware (Catch, Stay, Hinges)
rule: window stay must have a friction or locking mechanism capable of holding the sash stationary against gravity at any intended opening angle
conditions: window is fitted with a friction stay or stay arm

subject: Lintel over Opening
rule: lintel over opening must have bearing length (end support) on each side of the opening
conditions: lintel is not continuous across multiple openings
lintel is simply supported
exceptions: lintel is cantilevered or fully continuous through the wall plane

subject: Lintel over Opening
rule: lintel over opening must support the self-weight of masonry or wall material above the opening plus any superimposed loads
conditions: lintel is loadbearing

subject: Lintel over Opening
rule: lintel must not be placed without proper lateral restraint at its ends
conditions: lintel spans an opening in a masonry wall
exceptions: lintel is cast monolithically with a concrete frame providing integral lateral stability

subject: Lintel over Opening
rule: lintel depth (height in the vertical plane) must be sufficient to resist the design bending moment and shear
conditions: lintel is a reinforced concrete or steel beam type

subject: Window Sill & Surround
rule: window sill must slope away from the window (minimum 5° downward pitch) to shed water
conditions: exterior wall
climatic region with precipitation
exceptions: window sill fully protected by an overhanging roof or canopy that prevents any rain from reaching the sill

subject: Window Sill & Surround
rule: window sill must project beyond the face of the wall below it (minimum 20 mm drip projection)
conditions: exterior wall
climatic region with precipitation
exceptions: sill integrated into a rainscreen system with separately detailed drainage behind cladding

subject: Window Sill & Surround
rule: window sill surface must be impervious or have a continuous waterproof layer across its top surface
conditions: exterior wall
climatic region with precipitation

subject: Window Sill & Surround
rule: window surround must not create a thermal bridge that bypasses the building's insulation layer at the window-to-wall junction
conditions: thermally insulated wall assembly

subject: Window Sill & Surround
rule: window sill must have a capillary break (a groove or drip notch) on the underside of the projecting edge
conditions: exterior wall
climatic region with precipitation
sill projects more than 20 mm beyond wall face

subject: Window Shading / Sunscreen
rule: Window shading / sunscreen must not block required emergency egress or rescue openings
conditions: When installed on windows that serve as emergency escape or rescue openings
Applicable to buildings with operable windows designated for egress per building code
exceptions: Window shading is designed to be readily removable from the inside without tools or special knowledge
Shading device automatically opens or retracts upon activation of fire alarm or smoke detection

subject: Window Shading / Sunscreen
rule: Window shading / sunscreen must not trap heat against the building envelope to the point of damaging glazing, sealants, or frame materials
conditions: When shading device is placed in close proximity (less than 6 inches) to the glazing surface
When device is dark-colored and directly sun-exposed on south or west orientations
exceptions: Shading device is specifically rated by the manufacturer for direct-contact or near-contact installation with the intended window system
Materials of both window and shading are verified to withstand the surface temperature reached in the specific climate zone

subject: Window Shading / Sunscreen
rule: Window shading / sunscreen must be structurally attached to withstand design wind loads and dead loads without failure
conditions: For all permanently installed exterior shading devices
Applicable in all wind zones
exceptions: Temporary or seasonal shading that is removed before any forecasted high-wind event
Interior shading that is not exposed to wind forces

subject: Low Sill Flashing
rule: Low sill flashing must be installed with a minimum 1:6 (approx. 10°) upward slope away from the wall
conditions: when installed as part of a window or door assembly
where the low sill flashing sits on a horizontal or near-horizontal substrate
exceptions: When manufacturer installation instructions explicitly specify a different slope angle

subject: Low Sill Flashing
rule: Low sill flashing must lap over the top of the drainage plane or weather-resistive barrier below it
conditions: when integrated into a wall assembly with a weather-resistive barrier

subject: Low Sill Flashing
rule: Low sill flashing must not be installed without end dams or turned-up ends
conditions: when the flashing is at the base of a rough opening for a window or door
exceptions: When the side jambs are designed with integral pan flashings that provide equivalent containment

subject: Low Sill Insulation
rule: Low sill insulation must maintain a minimum height above finished grade
conditions: Foundation wall with crawlspace or unconditioned basement
exceptions: When specified otherwise by engineered foundation design that accounts for termite protection and moisture management

subject: Low Sill Insulation
rule: Low sill insulation must not be used as a structural load-bearing element
conditions: Sill plate is supporting floor joists or roof loads
exceptions: Insulation product specifically engineered and rated for structural compressive loads per manufacturer specifications

subject: Low Sill Insulation
rule: Low sill insulation must be covered with a thermal barrier or ignition barrier when exposed to interior occupied spaces
conditions: Insulation is foam plastic
Interior side is accessible to occupied space
exceptions: When installed in an unoccupied crawlspace where a 15-minute thermal barrier is replaced by an approved ignition barrier per code

subject: Low Sill Insulation
rule: Low sill insulation must be installed in continuous contact with the sill plate and rim joist to prevent air leakage
conditions: Insulation is air-impermeable or an air barrier is required
exceptions: When a separate air barrier system is independently provided between the conditioned space and the sill area

subject: Low Sill Cill / Sill Board
rule: Low Sill Cill / Sill Board must be installed with a minimum 1:80 (or steeper) outward slope to shed water away from the building fabric
conditions: when installed as part of an external wall assembly
when exposed to rainwater

subject: Low Sill Cill / Sill Board
rule: Sill board must not be installed such that it bridges the cavity or creates a thermal bypass at the wall-floor junction
conditions: when used in cavity wall construction
when a thermal break or cavity closer is specified

subject: Low Sill Drip Edge / Groove
rule: drip edge groove must be lower than the roof membrane or waterproofing layer at the roof edge
conditions: where a low sill condition exists at roof edge

subject: Low Sill Drip Edge / Groove
rule: drip edge must project beyond the roof edge or wall face below
conditions: when used as a drip edge on a roof or parapet low sill

subject: Low Sill Drip Edge / Groove
rule: drip edge groove must not be filled or blocked by sealant, paint, or debris
conditions: where a continuous groove is formed into the metal or sill material

subject: Low Sill Weep Holes
rule: Low sill weep holes must be provided at the base of masonry cavity walls to allow moisture in the cavity to drain to the exterior
conditions: wall construction includes a cavity
exterior wall is masonry veneer or cavity wall
exceptions: wall systems that use interior drainage systems instead
walls with no moisture accumulation risk

subject: Low Sill Weep Holes
rule: Low sill weep holes must not be blocked or sealed by mortar droppings, insulation, or other debris during construction
conditions: during or after masonry wall construction
exceptions: none — blockages negate weep hole function

subject: Low Sill Weep Holes
rule: Low sill weep holes must be spaced at a maximum interval (typically 600–900 mm on center) along the base of the wall
conditions: continuous masonry cavity walls
exceptions: local building codes may specify different maximum spacing

subject: Low Sill – Window Interface
rule: low sill must have a continuous air barrier seal at the window-to-sill interface
conditions: when the low sill forms part of the exterior building envelope

subject: Low Sill – Window Interface
rule: low sill must be sloped or otherwise detailed to drain water away from the window assembly
conditions: when the low sill is exposed to rainwater or condensation runoff
exceptions: a low sill that is part of a fully interior, non-wet application where no moisture exposure occurs

subject: Low Sill – Window Interface
rule: low sill must not terminate below the finished floor drainage plane without a positive waterproofing transition
conditions: where the low sill is at or below grade and the window is in a below-grade or walkout condition

subject: Window Reveal Lining
rule: window reveal lining must maintain a minimum thickness of 10 mm to prevent buckling under thermal stress
conditions: when made of timber
when made of PVC
exceptions: when reinforced with metal substructure

subject: Window Reveal Lining
rule: window reveal lining must not obstruct the operation of the window sash

subject: Window Reveal Lining
rule: window reveal lining must be fixed to prevent movement that could cause glass breakage
conditions: when lining abuts fixed glazing directly
exceptions: when a flexible sealant gap is provided between lining and glass

subject: Low Sill – Wall Interface
rule: Low sill must be sealed against the wall to prevent water intrusion
conditions: Exterior application
Sill meets wall at horizontal joint
exceptions: Sill is part of a fully drained rainscreen assembly with an open joint detail

subject: Low Sill – Wall Interface
rule: Low sill must be sloped away from the wall (minimum 5 degrees) to shed water
conditions: Horizontal or near-horizontal sill surface
Exterior exposure
exceptions: Sill surface is protected by an overhang or drip edge that completely prevents water accumulation

subject: Low Sill – Wall Interface
rule: Low sill must not be in direct contact with moisture-sensitive wall cladding without a capillary break
conditions: Sill material is stone, concrete, or masonry
Wall cladding is wood, gypsum, or other moisture-absorptive material
exceptions: A continuous impermeable membrane or capillary break layer separates sill from cladding

subject: Door Reveal Lining
rule: Door reveal lining must be flush with the door frame to allow proper door operation
conditions: Door is hinged to the frame

subject: Door Reveal Lining
rule: Door reveal lining must not obstruct the door strike plate or latch pocket
conditions: Door has a locking or latching mechanism

subject: Door Reveal Lining
rule: Door reveal lining must be installed with adequate clearance for door swing
conditions: Door swings into or past the reveal opening

subject: Deep Reveal Sill
rule: Deep reveal sill must have a minimum depth of 4 inches (100 mm) from the glazing face to the exterior face of the wall below
conditions: Where the sill is installed in a wall assembly with exterior cladding
exceptions: When used with structural glazing systems where the sill is fully captured within the frame

subject: Deep Reveal Sill
rule: Deep reveal sill must have a continuous drip edge projecting at least 1/2 inch (12 mm) beyond the wall face below
conditions: When the sill is exposed to direct rainwater runoff
exceptions: Where a separate drip flashing is installed with an equivalent projection

subject: Deep Reveal Sill
rule: Deep reveal sill must not have horizontal joints or seams that are not sealed or lapped
conditions: Where the sill is composed of multiple sections joined together

subject: Reveal Soffit/Lintel Finish
rule: Reveal soffit/lintel finish must be located at the top of a wall opening (window or door) to create a shadow reveal
conditions: when designed as a shadow reveal detail
exceptions: when the reveal is purely decorative and not functioning as a water-shedding or visual termination element

subject: Reveal Soffit/Lintel Finish
rule: Reveal soffit/lintel finish must not bridge the drainage plane or block weeps if installed above a window/door head
conditions: when installed above an operable window or door with a head flashing and weep system
exceptions: when a separate continuous head flashing is provided outboard of the finish

subject: Low Door Leaf
rule: low door leaf must fit within the door opening frame with a clearance gap on all sides to allow free swing without binding
conditions: when installed in a framed doorway

subject: Low Door Leaf
rule: low door leaf must have hinges or pivot hardware capable of supporting its full weight without sagging or detachment
conditions: when side-hinged or pivoted
exceptions: sliding door leaves where weight is carried by overhead track or bottom rollers

subject: Low Door Leaf
rule: low door leaf must not warp or twist beyond the dimensional tolerance that prevents the latch or lock from engaging
conditions: when the leaf includes a latch or lock mechanism

subject: Low Door Leaf
rule: low door leaf must have a bottom edge clearance above the finished floor to avoid scraping or obstruction during swing
conditions: when the leaf swings over a floor surface
exceptions: doors designed with a sweep seal that contacts the floor intentionally

subject: Low Doorway Frame
rule: Low doorway frame must have a minimum clear opening height of at least 80 inches (2032 mm) to meet accessibility code for egress
conditions: Doorway serves as a primary means of egress
Building occupancy type requires accessible design
exceptions: Historical buildings with grandfathered status
Secondary non-egress doorways in single-family residential where local code permits lower height

subject: Low Doorway Frame
rule: Low doorway frame must_not have a clear opening width less than 32 inches (813 mm) when serving as an accessible entrance
conditions: Doorway is a required accessible entrance under ADA or equivalent accessibility standards
Building type is commercial, multi-family, or public assembly
exceptions: Residential bathrooms and other rooms where minimum clearance is reduced to 24 inches by code

subject: Low Doorway Frame
rule: Low doorway frame header must be structurally adequate to support the vertical load above the opening
conditions: Frame is located in a load-bearing wall
exceptions: Frame is in a non-load-bearing partition wall where the wall carries no structural load from floors or roof above

subject: Low Doorway Header/Lintel
rule: low doorway header/lintel must have sufficient load-bearing capacity to support the weight of the wall and structure above the opening
conditions: when acting as a structural beam over a doorway opening
exceptions: when the opening is purely decorative and does not support any wall above it

subject: Low Doorway Header/Lintel
rule: low doorway header/lintel must not create a head height below minimum building code clearance
conditions: when the doorway is intended for human passage
exceptions: non-egress openings such as crawlspace access hatches

subject: Low Doorway Header/Lintel
rule: low doorway header/lintel must be supported on each side by adequate bearing surfaces (jambs or wall sections)
conditions: when the lintel is load-bearing

subject: Clearance Height Marker
rule: Clearance Height Marker must display its minimum height value clearly and legibly
conditions: When installed as a physical sign or marker
exceptions: Digital/variable displays that show height dynamically

subject: Clearance Height Marker
rule: Clearance Height Marker must be positioned at or below the actual structural clearance height it marks
conditions: When mounted at the clearance point
exceptions: When used as an advance warning sign located before the actual clearance point

subject: Clearance Height Marker
rule: Clearance Height Marker must be visible from the approach direction of traffic
conditions: When installed at a vehicular clearance point

subject: Low Doorway Threshold
rule: low doorway threshold must not exceed 1/2 inch (13 mm) in vertical height
conditions: threshold is located at an accessible doorway (required by building codes for accessibility)

subject: Low Doorway Threshold
rule: low doorway threshold must be beveled with a slope no steeper than 1:2 if height exceeds 1/4 inch (6.4 mm)
conditions: threshold height is between 1/4 inch and 1/2 inch

subject: Low Doorway Threshold
rule: low doorway threshold must not create a gap exceeding 1/2 inch (13 mm) between the bottom of the door and the threshold surface
conditions: the door is an exterior door subject to weather exposure
exceptions: doors equipped with a separate integrated weatherseal sweep that bridges the gap

subject: Low Doorway Threshold
rule: low doorway threshold must provide a smooth transition surface free of sharp edges or abrupt changes exceeding 1/4 inch (6.4 mm)

subject: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad
rule: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad must be positioned at the leading edge of the low doorway opening
conditions: The doorway has a headroom height below a specified threshold (e.g., 6'8" or 2.03 m)

subject: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad
rule: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad must be made of energy-absorbing (compliant/compressible) material

subject: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad
rule: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad must be securely attached to the structure and remain in place under expected impact loads

subject: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad
rule: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad must not create a sharp or protruding edge that itself presents a laceration or puncture hazard

subject: Low Doorway in Partition Wall
rule: low doorway in partition wall must have a minimum clear height of at least 6 feet 8 inches (2030 mm) for typical occupancy
conditions: doorway serves habitable spaces
partition wall is in a means of egress path
exceptions: doorway serving only mechanical or utility spaces where crouching access is permitted
existing buildings where alteration work is limited and local building code allows reduced height

subject: Low Doorway in Partition Wall
rule: low doorway in partition wall must not reduce the required egress width of the path of travel
conditions: doorway is located on a means of egress route

subject: Low Doorway in Partition Wall
rule: low doorway in partition wall must have a minimum clear width of at least 32 inches (813 mm) between the door stop and the opposite jamb face
conditions: doorway serves as an accessible means of egress or is on an accessible route
exceptions: doorway serving only storage or utility rooms not required to be accessible

subject: Low Doorway in Loadbearing Wall
rule: low doorway in loadbearing wall must have a structural lintel or arch above the opening to transfer vertical loads around the opening
conditions: doorway is pierced through a loadbearing wall
doorway width creates a clear span requiring load redistribution
exceptions: wall is non-loadbearing
opening is small enough that the wall above acts as a deep beam without additional reinforcement (typically openings under ~600 mm width depending on masonry type and wall height)

subject: Low Doorway in Loadbearing Wall
rule: the lintel or arch must bear on adequate supporting masonry on each side of the opening (minimum bearing length typically 150 mm each side)
conditions: lintel or arch is used above the doorway
exceptions: engineered steel or reinforced concrete frame that cantilevers or is otherwise continuously supported

subject: Low Doorway in Loadbearing Wall
rule: doorway dimensions must not reduce the wall's lateral stability below code-required minimums in a seismic or high-wind zone
conditions: building is located in a seismic zone (SDC C, D, E, or F) or a high-wind region
wall is a shear wall or part of the lateral force-resisting system
exceptions: engineered analysis demonstrates adequate remaining wall capacity with the opening present

subject: Low Doorway in Historic Building
rule: low doorway must comply with applicable accessibility codes for minimum clear height (e.g., 80 inches for accessible routes in most building codes)
conditions: building is open to the public
doorway is on an accessible route
historic designation does not grant full exemption
exceptions: when the doorway leads to a non-occupiable space (e.g., crawlspace, mechanical attic)
when strict compliance is waived by the authority having jurisdiction under a historic waiver or variance

subject: Low Doorway in Historic Building
rule: low doorway must not obstruct emergency egress to a degree that violates minimum clear opening height requirements (typically not less than 80 inches in new construction, with lower allowances in existing/historic buildings granted by code)
conditions: doorway serves as an egress path
occupants are expected to pass through during evacuation
exceptions: when the doorway is to an unoccupied service space not part of the egress path
when a historic building code variance explicitly permits reduced egress height

subject: Low Access Hatch Doorway
rule: low access hatch doorway must have a clear opening area of at least 0.35 m²
conditions: when intended for emergency egress or rescue access
exceptions: when serving only non-egress maintenance access and local code allows smaller opening

subject: Low Access Hatch Doorway
rule: low access hatch doorway must have a maximum sill height of not more than 200 mm when serving as an egress opening for an occupied space
conditions: when the hatch serves as a required emergency escape opening
exceptions: when the hatch is not required as an egress opening (e.g., serving only crawl space or attic access)

subject: Low Access Hatch Doorway
rule: low access hatch doorway must be openable from the inside without tools, keys, or special knowledge
conditions: when the hatch provides access to or from a habitable space
exceptions: when the hatch serves only secure/utility areas (e.g., vaults, mechanical penthouses) where controlled access is intentional and alternative egress exists

subject: Low Access Hatch Doorway
rule: low access hatch doorway must not be located where its swing or opening trajectory would strike equipment, piping, or structural elements when fully opened
exceptions: when the hatch is designed as a removable panel rather than a hinged door

subject: Concrete Edge Formwork
rule: Concrete edge formwork must be designed to withstand the full hydrostatic pressure of wet concrete
conditions: When used in vertical or near-vertical applications
exceptions: When using self-compacting concrete with controlled low slump that does not generate full hydrostatic pressure

subject: Concrete Edge Formwork
rule: Concrete edge formwork must remain in place and rigid until the concrete achieves sufficient strength to be self-supporting
conditions: When supporting fresh concrete at an unsupported vertical edge

subject: Concrete Edge Formwork
rule: Concrete edge formwork must not have gaps larger than the maximum aggregate size of the concrete mix

subject: Edge Tapering Detail
rule: Edge tapering detail must maintain a minimum taper angle to prevent stress concentration and material failure
conditions: when used at corners or edges of structural panels
when joining dissimilar materials
exceptions: when a stress-relief fillet or transition piece is used

subject: Load-Bearing Edge Profile
rule: The load-bearing edge profile must be continuous along the entire supported span without abrupt gaps or breaks
conditions: When the edge profile is designed to transfer load from a structural element (e.g., beam, slab, or roof deck) to a support
exceptions: When the profile is intentionally segmented as part of a designed articulation or expansion joint that is independently structurally justified

subject: Load-Bearing Edge Profile
rule: The load-bearing edge profile must not have a cross-sectional dimension below the minimum required for the specified material strength and applied load
conditions: When the profile carries any portion of the design gravity or lateral load

subject: Load-Bearing Edge Profile
rule: The load-bearing edge profile must be positively attached to the supporting structure to prevent lateral displacement or rotation
conditions: When the edge profile is subject to out-of-plane or lateral loads (e.g., wind, seismic, eccentric gravity)

subject: Drip Edge / Drip Channel
rule: drip edge / drip channel must direct water away from the roof deck and underlying structure
conditions: roof has a sloped plane
water runoff is present at roof perimeter
exceptions: roof assembly is designed with an integrated gutter system that fully captures runoff before reaching the edge

subject: Drip Edge / Drip Channel
rule: drip edge must not be installed without an overlap transition at corners and splices that prevents water ingress under the material
conditions: multiple drip edge sections are joined
corner conditions exist at roof edges
exceptions: a single continuous drip edge piece spans the entire roof perimeter

subject: Drip Edge / Drip Channel
rule: drip edge must be installed such that the outer edge extends below the bottom edge of the roof sheathing and any exterior finish
conditions: roof has a fascia board
roof has vertical exterior cladding adjacent to the eaves

subject: Post-Tensioning Edge Anchor
rule: post-tensioning edge anchor must be cast into the concrete slab edge before the concrete reaches initial set
conditions: post-tensioning system uses bonded or unbonded tendons
edge anchor is installed at slab periphery
exceptions: precast concrete applications where anchors are installed after casting with epoxy

subject: Post-Tensioning Edge Anchor
rule: post-tensioning edge anchor must be aligned within the tendon profile tolerance (±5 mm typical)
conditions: anchor is installed at stressing end of tendon

subject: Post-Tensioning Edge Anchor
rule: post-tensioning edge anchor bearing plate must bear perpendicularly against the concrete edge face
conditions: anchor is at the live or dead end of the tendon
exceptions: anchors designed with articulated or spherical bearing surfaces

subject: Post-Tensioning Edge Anchor
rule: post-tensioning edge anchor must not be positioned closer to the slab edge than the minimum edge distance specified by the anchor manufacturer and applicable code
exceptions: edge distances may be reduced if specific local reinforcement (anti-burst steel) is detailed to handle the bursting forces

subject: Composite Deck Edge Closure
rule: Composite deck edge closure must maintain continuous fire-resistance rating equal to the deck assembly it terminates
conditions: when used in fire-resistance-rated floor/ceiling or roof/ceiling assemblies
exceptions: when the assembly is not required to have a fire-resistance rating per applicable building code

subject: Composite Deck Edge Closure
rule: Composite deck edge closure must not allow air or water infiltration between the deck edge and the exterior wall or parapet
conditions: when the deck is exposed to exterior conditions
when the deck forms an occupied interior space
exceptions: when the closure is specifically designed as a weeps-open vented system with documented drainage and insect screening

subject: Composite Deck Edge Closure
rule: Composite deck edge closure must be structurally secured to resist design wind uplift and lateral loads without detachment
conditions: when the deck is part of an enclosed or partially enclosed building
exceptions: when building is exempt from wind-load provisions per local code (e.g., temporary structures with engineering justification)

subject: Column Enclosure/Cladding
rule: Column enclosure/cladding must provide a complete separation between interior conditioned space and exterior environment
conditions: when used as exterior wall
exceptions: when column is located in unconditioned interior space
when column is purely decorative and not part of the building envelope

subject: Column Enclosure/Cladding
rule: Column enclosure/cladding must resist wind loads without detachment
conditions: when exposed to exterior wind pressures
exceptions: when column is entirely interior and not subject to wind loads

subject: Column Enclosure/Cladding
rule: Column enclosure/cladding must not create a continuous concealed combustible pathway across floors or fire compartments
conditions: when cladding material is combustible
exceptions: when firestops or cavity barriers are installed at every floor level and compartment boundary

subject: Column Enclosure/Cladding
rule: Column enclosure/cladding must accommodate differential thermal movement between the column structure and the cladding material
conditions: when column is exposed to outdoor temperature cycles and cladding has different coefficient of thermal expansion than structure
exceptions: when column and cladding are of the same material with equal thermal response

subject: Column-to-Beam Connection
rule: The column-to-beam connection must transfer vertical load from the beam to the column
conditions: gravity-loaded structure
exceptions: cantilevered beams where beam is supported from opposite side

subject: Column-to-Beam Connection
rule: The column-to-beam connection must not separate under design loads
conditions: any structural application

subject: Column-to-Beam Connection
rule: The column-to-beam connection must resist rotation (moment) according to its design assumption (rigid, pinned, or semi-rigid)
conditions: moment-resisting frame
exceptions: pinned connections in braced frames

subject: Column-to-Beam Connection
rule: The column-to-beam connection must have a failure capacity greater than or equal to the forces delivered by connected members
conditions: any structural system
exceptions: fuse/dissipative connections intentionally designed to yield first in seismic applications

subject: Column-to-Beam Connection
rule: The column-to-beam connection must not introduce significant eccentricity that causes unaccounted torsion in the column
conditions: axially loaded column
exceptions: connections designed with explicit eccentricity analysis

subject: Column-to-Slab Connection
rule: column-to-slab connection must transfer vertical load from column to slab without relative vertical displacement exceeding structural tolerance
conditions: connection is load-bearing
structure is in service

subject: Column-to-Slab Connection
rule: column-to-slab connection must not have a gap between column end and slab soffit that exceeds the specified bearing tolerance
conditions: connection is cast-in-place or dry-bearing
exceptions: connections designed as intentional separation with an independent load path (e.g., seismic isolation)

subject: Column-to-Slab Connection
rule: column-to-slab connection must be capable of transferring design lateral forces (shear) between column and slab
conditions: structure is not braced independently of slab-column joints
connection is part of lateral force-resisting system
exceptions: connections at expansion joints where lateral transfer is deliberately omitted and accommodated elsewhere

subject: Embedded Column Base Plate
rule: Embedded column base plate must have sufficient embedment depth to develop the full axial and moment capacity of the connected column
conditions: Column is subjected to moment or tension
Base plate is designed as fully restrained/rigid connection
exceptions: When the connection is designed as pinned with nominal axial load only

subject: Embedded Column Base Plate
rule: Embedded column base plate must not be placed on uncompacted or loose backfill
conditions: Base plate is embedded in soil rather than cast in concrete

subject: Embedded Column Base Plate
rule: Embedded column base plate must have a minimum concrete cover between the plate edge and the foundation reinforcement
conditions: Base plate is cast into a reinforced concrete foundation or pedestal
exceptions: When the foundation is unreinforced mass concrete and corrosion protection is not needed

subject: Embedded Column Base Plate
rule: Embedded column base plate must not be welded to column after concrete has fully cured unless post-installed anchorage is designed
conditions: Base plate is cast-in-place (embedded before concrete pour)
exceptions: When the weld is part of an intentional post-installed anchorage system designed for that condition

subject: Column Void/Shaft
rule: a column void/shaft must be continuous through all floors it serves without horizontal offset
conditions: when designed as a building service shaft (e.g., for HVAC, plumbing, electrical)
exceptions: when local codes allow limited horizontal offset with access panels at each change of direction

subject: Column Void/Shaft
rule: a column void/shaft must be enclosed with fire-resistance-rated construction matching the required fire rating of the floor or wall penetrations
conditions: when the shaft penetrates more than one floor
when required by building code (e.g., IBC for vertical shafts)
exceptions: when the void is a non-combustible open chase with no fire-separation requirement under local code

subject: Column Void/Shaft
rule: a column void/shaft must not be smaller than the minimum cross-section required for the intended service installation and access
conditions: when the shaft is intended to contain building services (e.g., ducts, pipes, cables)

subject: Pedestal Column
rule: Pedestal column must bear directly on a foundation or footing capable of supporting its full vertical load
conditions: column is load-bearing

subject: Pedestal Column
rule: Pedestal column must be centered or symmetrically aligned with its supporting foundation element
conditions: column supports a concentrated load
column is not part of an intentionally eccentric architectural design
exceptions: intentional eccentric design that accounts for overturning moment and eccentricity in reinforcement detailing

subject: Pedestal Column
rule: Pedestal column must have a minimum cross-sectional dimension not less than the unsupported height divided by an allowable slenderness ratio
conditions: column is unreinforced masonry or plain concrete
exceptions: reinforced concrete or steel-encased pedestal columns where slenderness effects are explicitly designed for

subject: Column Grid Line
rule: column grid lines must be orthogonally arranged to align with the principal structural axes of the building
conditions: building has a rectangular or orthogonal structural layout
exceptions: buildings with curvilinear or free-form structural geometry where radial or non-orthogonal grid lines are intentional

subject: Column Grid Line
rule: column grid lines must be continuous from foundation to roof without interruption
exceptions: transfer structures where a column terminates at a transfer girder and a new grid line begins at a different horizontal offset

subject: Column Grid Line
rule: column grid lines must not cross the building perimeter without tying to a structural element at the boundary
exceptions: architectural overhangs where a grid line extends beyond the last column to define a cantilever edge but still terminates at a structural beam

subject: Welded Column Connection
rule: welded column connection must have full joint penetration (FJP) groove welds at the column flange-to-beam flange interface in seismic force resisting systems
conditions: connection is part of a seismic force resisting system (SFRS)
beam-to-column moment connection
exceptions: connections in non-seismic zones or low-seismic regions where partial joint penetration (PJP) or fillet welds may be permitted per code

subject: Welded Column Connection
rule: welded column connection must not have weld access holes that reduce the column cross-section below the net section required for axial load capacity
conditions: column is subjected to axial compressive load
exceptions: when reinforcement is provided to compensate for reduced section

subject: Welded Column Connection
rule: welded column connection must have welds designed to transfer the full required strength of the connected member
conditions: connection is a fully restrained (FR) moment connection
exceptions: connections designed as partially restrained (PR) where intentional deformation is accounted for in the design

subject: Column Base Plate Connection
rule: base plate must transfer all column loads to the foundation without exceeding bearing capacity of the supporting material
conditions: column base plate is resting on concrete or masonry foundation
connection is designed for gravity load transfer

subject: Column Base Plate Connection
rule: base plate bolts must not fracture in tension under design uplift loads
conditions: connection is designed to resist overturning or uplift

subject: Column Base Plate Connection
rule: base plate must have sufficient thickness to prevent yielding under bending from bearing pressure and bolt tension

subject: Column Base Plate Connection
rule: weld between base plate and column must not have effective throat area less than required to transfer design forces
conditions: base plate is welded to column (not a pinned/bolted-only connection)

subject: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
rule: bolt group centroid must align with the centerline of the beam web to avoid eccentricity in the connection
conditions: connection is bolted
exceptions: connection is designed as an eccentric (extended) shear tab where eccentricity is explicitly accounted for in design

subject: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
rule: weld access holes must be provided at beam flanges when complete-joint-penetration (CJP) groove welds are used
conditions: welded moment connection
beam depth exceeds 12 inches
exceptions: proprietary connection details that have been tested and validated without access holes per AISC 358

subject: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
