rule: beam flange thickness must not exceed column flange thickness by more than 20% unless the column flange is reinforced with continuity plates or a stiffener
conditions: moment frame connection designed for seismic resistance per AISC 341
exceptions: engineered alternative verified by prequalified connection testing per AISC 358

subject: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
rule: continuity plates must be provided on the column when the beam flange force exceeds the column flange's local bending capacity
conditions: moment connection
column flange thickness is less than the beam flange thickness
column web slenderness ratio exceeds limit per AISC 360 Eq. J10-1
exceptions: deep column sections specifically tested without continuity plates per qualified testing program

subject: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
rule: bolts in beam-to-column shear connection must be designed for shear only, not for tension or moment
conditions: connection is designed as a simple shear connection (pinned, not moment-resisting)
exceptions: connection is explicitly designed as a partial-strength or full-strength moment connection

subject: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
rule: beam web must not be coped in a manner that reduces shear capacity below the required design shear force
conditions: beam web is coped (notched) to clear the column flange
exceptions: cope geometry is verified by calculation to retain sufficient net shear area and block shear strength for the design load

subject: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
rule: weld or bolt group must have adequate ductility to accommodate end rotation of the simply supported beam
conditions: connection relies on welds or bolts for shear transfer
exceptions: connection uses only bearing-type bolts in standard holes with sufficient slip capacity
connection is designed as a seated connection where rotation occurs at a distinct support line

subject: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
rule: supporting column web or stiffener must not yield under concentrated beam flange force at the shear connection elevation
conditions: connection is framed into the column web
beam depth is large relative to column section
exceptions: column web is stiffened with transverse stiffeners or doubler plates at the connection zone

subject: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
rule: eccentricity between the beam top flange and column centerline must not induce unacceptable torsion in the beam or column
conditions: connection is single-sided (beam on one side only)
load is not negligible
exceptions: direct calculation shows torsional stresses remain within allowable limits
a lateral brace or torsional restraint is provided at the connection

subject: Column Cap/Head Connection
rule: Column cap must be able to transfer compressive load from the column below to the column above or to the supported beam/slab without yielding or buckling
conditions: Column cap is present in a gravity-load-bearing column

subject: Column Cap/Head Connection
rule: Column cap must engage at least the full cross-section of the supported element (column above or beam)
conditions: Load is transferred through bearing

subject: Column Cap/Head Connection
rule: Column head connection must not introduce unintended moment restraint that conflicts with the assumed pinned condition of the joint
conditions: The connection is designed as a pinned (simple) connection

subject: Column Cap/Head Connection
rule: Bolt or dowel count in a column cap connection must meet or exceed the minimum required for the design shear and tension forces
conditions: Mechanical fasteners (bolts, dowels, or rebar) are used to connect the cap to the column

subject: Column Anchor Bolt Assembly
rule: Column anchor bolt assembly must use bolts that are long enough to engage at least one full nut thread beyond the nut when fully tightened
conditions: When used with a nut and washer
exceptions: When using fully threaded studs that extend completely through the nut

subject: Column Anchor Bolt Assembly
rule: Column anchor bolt assembly must not have a bolt diameter smaller than the minimum specified in the structural design drawings
conditions: For all structural column base plate connections

subject: Column Anchor Bolt Assembly
rule: Column anchor bolt assembly must not have bolts spaced closer than the minimum edge distance specified by the applicable steel design standard
conditions: For connections to concrete foundations

subject: Column Haunch Connection
rule: column haunch connection must transfer moment between column and beam
conditions: connection is in a moment-resisting frame
exceptions: connection is designed as a simple shear connection (pin)

subject: Column Haunch Connection
rule: haunch flange must not be coped or notched in a way that reduces its effective cross-section below the required strength
conditions: haunch is welded or bolted to transfer tensile forces
exceptions: notch is reinforced with a doubler plate restoring full strength

subject: Column Haunch Connection
rule: haunch web stiffeners must align with the column flange load path
conditions: stiffeners are provided at the haunch tip

subject: Column Connection Stiffener Plate
rule: A column connection stiffener plate must have thickness sufficient to prevent local buckling under the design axial load from the column and connection forces
conditions: When the stiffener plate is used to reinforce a column-to-beam or column-to-column moment connection
When the stiffener plate is subjected to compressive forces transferred from the column flange or web
exceptions: When the stiffener plate is designed as a non-structural, architectural feature only (e.g., cosmetic cover plate not intended to carry load)

subject: Column Connection Stiffener Plate
rule: A column connection stiffener plate must be welded or bolted with sufficient capacity to transfer the full design force across the joint without fracture or pull-out
conditions: When the stiffener plate is part of a load-resisting connection (moment frame, braced frame, or gravity connection)
exceptions: When the stiffener plate is only a handling/temporary erection aid and is not part of the final load path

subject: Column Connection Stiffener Plate
rule: A column connection stiffener plate must not reduce the clear spacing or access required for bolting or welding the primary connection elements
conditions: When the stiffener plate is installed in a location where primary connection hardware (bolts, welds, fittings) must be installed or inspected
exceptions: None — this is a basic constructability requirement; if clearance cannot be maintained the stiffener geometry must be revised

subject: Column Connection Stiffener Plate
rule: A column connection stiffener plate must be made of steel with yield strength and ductility compatible with the column and connection materials
conditions: When the stiffener plate is expected to yield or participate in ductile behavior (e.g., in seismic moment connections)
exceptions: None — material incompatibility leads to brittle failure or unreliable load transfer

subject: Column Connection Shear Tab
rule: shear tab must have bolt holes aligned with the supported beam web
conditions: when used with bolted shear connections

subject: Column Connection Shear Tab
rule: shear tab thickness must be sufficient to prevent bearing failure at bolt holes
conditions: under service loads

subject: Column Connection Shear Tab
rule: shear tab must not be welded to a column flange that is coped or notched beyond allowable limits
conditions: when welded directly to column

subject: Column Connection End Plate
rule: Column connection end plate must have bolt holes aligned with the column flange holes within specified tolerances
conditions: When end plate is bolted to column flange
exceptions: Welded-only connections without bolts

subject: Column Connection End Plate
rule: Column connection end plate thickness must be sufficient to resist design bearing and bending stresses without yielding
conditions: Subject to design loads (axial, moment, shear)

subject: Column Connection End Plate
rule: Column connection end plate material must have weldable ductility to avoid brittle fracture at welded joints
conditions: When end plate is welded to beam or column
exceptions: Cast-in-place or bolted-only connections

subject: Column Connection End Plate
rule: Column connection end plate must not have sharp re-entrant corners that create stress concentrations exceeding material capacity
conditions: Plate geometry includes cutouts or notches
exceptions: Stress analysis confirms all stress raisers are within acceptable limits

subject: Concrete Column Dowel Connection
rule: dowel bars must be embedded at least their full development length into both the column and the connecting element
conditions: connection is cast-in-place
dowels are the primary load path
exceptions: mechanical couplers or headed anchors are used as equivalent alternative

subject: Concrete Column Dowel Connection
rule: concrete cover around the dowel bars must not be less than the minimum specified by applicable building code for corrosion protection and fire resistance
conditions: connection is exposed to environment or weather
exceptions: stainless steel or epoxy-coated dowels with reduced cover allowances per code are used

subject: Concrete Column Dowel Connection
rule: dowels must be aligned within the column cross-section to avoid eccentricity that exceeds structural design assumptions
conditions: dowels carry moment or lateral load in addition to axial load

subject: Concrete Column Dowel Connection
rule: lap splice length between dowel bars and column longitudinal reinforcement must not be less than the code-required development length for the bar size and concrete strength used
conditions: dowels are lap-spliced with column reinforcement rather than continuous
exceptions: mechanical or welded splices are used per code

subject: Precast Concrete Column Socket Connection
rule: socket depth must be at least 1.5 times the column's minimum cross-section dimension
conditions: Connection is between a precast column and a foundation or footing

subject: Precast Concrete Column Socket Connection
rule: grout or dry-pack must completely fill the annular gap between column and socket wall
conditions: Connection uses grouted or dry-packed socket detail
exceptions: Dry connections designed with mechanical fasteners or shear keys that eliminate the need for gap filling

subject: Precast Concrete Column Socket Connection
rule: socket wall thickness must not be less than the column's minimum cross-section dimension
conditions: Socket is cast into a concrete footing or pile cap
exceptions: Thickness is verified by structural analysis to resist bursting and splitting forces with lower values

subject: Column Connection Fire Protection Wrap
rule: Column connection fire protection wrap must completely encircle the column-to-beam connection zone
conditions: When passive fire protection is required by building code
When column and beam are steel structural members
exceptions: When alternative fire protection system (e.g., active sprinklers + intumescent coating) provides equivalent fire resistance rating as accepted by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Column Connection Fire Protection Wrap
rule: Column connection fire protection wrap must not obstruct bolted or welded connections that are required for structural integrity
conditions: When the wrap is applied after connection installation

subject: Column Connection Fire Protection Wrap
rule: Column connection fire protection wrap must have a verified fire resistance rating equal to or greater than the required fire rating of the structural member it protects
conditions: When required by applicable building code (e.g., IBC, NFPA 5000)

subject: Column Connection Fire Protection Wrap
rule: Column connection fire protection wrap must not trap moisture against the steel column
conditions: When installed in interior conditioned spaces with potential for condensation
When installed in exterior or exposed environments
exceptions: When the wrap system is specifically tested and rated for wet service conditions with corrosion protection measures

subject: Stair Vault Enclosing Walls
rule: Stair vault enclosing walls must be rated for the required fire-resistance duration
conditions: building has more than one story
stair vault connects multiple floors
applicable building code requires fire-rated enclosure
exceptions: single-story building with no required fire separation

subject: Stair Vault Enclosing Walls
rule: Stair vault enclosing walls must be structurally self-supporting or adequately braced to resist lateral loads
conditions: stair vault extends more than one story in height

subject: Stair Vault Enclosing Walls
rule: Stair vault enclosing walls must not have openings that bypass the required fire-resistance rating
conditions: stair vault is required to be fire-rated
exceptions: openings protected with approved fire-rated doors or glazing assemblies matching the wall rating

subject: Stair Vault Fire Protection System
rule: Stair vault fire protection system must maintain a continuous water supply path from source to all sprinkler heads within the stair vault enclosure
conditions: system includes sprinkler-based fire suppression
exceptions: systems using gaseous clean agent instead of water-based suppression

subject: Stair Vault Fire Protection System
rule: Stair vault fire protection system must_not have any obstruction that blocks the discharge pattern of sprinkler heads within the stair vault volume
conditions: sprinkler heads are installed within the vault
exceptions: obstructions permanently integrated into listed sprinkler coverage plans approved by authority having jurisdiction

subject: Stair Vault Fire Protection System
rule: Stair vault fire protection system must maintain fire-resistance-rated enclosure integrity around all piping and components that pass through stair vault boundaries
conditions: stair vault is required to have a fire-resistance rating

subject: Stair Vault Ceiling/Soffit
rule: stair vault ceiling/soffit must have a minimum vertical clearance to the tread below (typically 6 ft 8 in / 2030 mm minimum)
conditions: applicable where stair vault ceiling/soffit projects over a stair run or landing
exceptions: existing structures under historic preservation requirements where full clearance is legally infeasible and alternative safety measures are provided

subject: Stair Vault Ceiling/Soffit
rule: stair vault ceiling/soffit must not be constructed with materials that have a Class III or lower flame-spread rating without an approved thermal barrier
conditions: when the stair is part of a required means of egress
exceptions: when the assembly is protected throughout by an automatic sprinkler system and local code allows reduced flame-spread ratings

subject: Stair Vault Ceiling/Soffit
rule: stair vault ceiling/soffit must not reduce the required width of the stairway
conditions: where the soffit projects laterally into the stairway clear width dimension

subject: Stair Vault Door
rule: Stair vault door must be rated for the same fire-resistance rating as the stair enclosure wall it is installed in
conditions: The stair enclosure is required to have a fire-resistance rating per building code
exceptions: When the stair is not required to be enclosed with a fire-resistance-rated assembly (e.g., certain small buildings or unrated egress paths)

subject: Stair Vault Door
rule: Stair vault door must swing in the direction of egress travel
conditions: The door serves an exit stair enclosure serving more than 50 occupants or as required by adopted building code
exceptions: When the door serves an occupant load of 50 or fewer and the code permits reverse swing

subject: Stair Vault Door
rule: Stair vault door must be self-closing and self-latching
conditions: The door is installed in a fire-rated stair enclosure

subject: Stair Vault Door
rule: Stair vault door must not be locked from the egress side during occupancy
conditions: The building is occupied
exceptions: When the door is equipped with approved panic hardware or a delayed-egress locking system complying with code

subject: Stair Vault Ventilation
rule: a stair vault ventilation opening must be connected to the exterior or to a naturally ventilated space
conditions: the stair vault is enclosed on all sides
mechanical ventilation is absent
exceptions: the stair vault serves a fully sprinklered building where pressurization is provided instead

subject: Stair Vault Ventilation
rule: the stair vault ventilation must not discharge directly into an interior corridor, habitable room, or unventilated enclosed space
conditions: the building is of combustible construction or contains occupancies that can generate smoke
exceptions: the receiving space is itself directly ventilated to the exterior at a rate meeting the same air-change standard as the stair vault

subject: Stair Vault Ventilation
rule: the ventilation opening to the exterior must be at least 0.33 m² (net free area) per 25 occupants served by the stair vault
conditions: natural ventilation is the only means of ventilation for the stair vault
exceptions: the building code specifies a different metric (e.g., percentage of stair area) that overrides this occupant-based rule

subject: Stair Vault Wall Finish
rule: Stair vault wall finish must be a non-combustible material
conditions: stair vault is enclosed
building requires fire-rated enclosure
exceptions: building is fully sprinklered and local code permits alternative finishes

subject: Stair Vault Wall Finish
rule: Stair vault wall finish must not produce toxic smoke when exposed to fire
conditions: stair vault is part of a means of egress

subject: Stair Vault Wall Finish
rule: Stair vault wall finish must have a Class A or Class B flame-spread rating
conditions: stair vault serves as a required means of egress
exceptions: fully sprinklered buildings where local code permits Class C in limited circumstances

subject: Duct
rule: duct must maintain adequate clearance from combustible materials
conditions: duct conveys heated air or combustion products
duct passes through or near combustible building elements
exceptions: duct is specifically listed for zero-clearance installation
duct is surrounded by approved fire-rated enclosure

subject: Duct
rule: duct must not have a cross-sectional area reduction that exceeds manufacturer specifications
conditions: duct is a rigid metal duct
duct serves an HVAC air distribution system

subject: Duct
rule: duct must be sealed to prevent uncontrolled air leakage
conditions: duct is part of a forced-air HVAC system
duct operates under positive or negative pressure relative to surrounding space
exceptions: duct is intentionally unsealed for ventilation or combustion air purposes as per design

subject: Duct
rule: duct must not be constructed from materials that degrade when exposed to intended operating temperatures and humidity
conditions: duct conveys air at temperatures or humidity levels outside standard human comfort range

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger/support must be attached to a structurally rated building element (e.g., structural slab, beam, joist, or rated deck)
conditions: When supporting HVAC ductwork
exceptions: If the supported element has its own independent structural support system that transfers load directly to the structure

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger/support must not be attached only to non-structural finishes, ceiling grid, or light-gauge furring
conditions: When supporting ductwork of any size

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger fasteners and anchors must be rated for the combined dead load of the hanger, insulation, and supported ductwork
conditions: In all installations

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger rod diameter must be sized to resist the imposed tensile load without yielding
conditions: For threaded rod hangers

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger/support must be spaced at intervals not exceeding the manufacturer's or governing code maximum spacing for the given duct size and gauge
conditions: Along the length of the duct run

subject: Duct Hanger/Support
rule: Duct hanger/support must not rely on adhesive-only attachment for load-bearing connection to the structure
conditions: When supporting any ductwork load

subject: Duct Sealant
rule: duct sealant must be compatible with the duct material it is applied to
conditions: when used to seal joints or seams in HVAC ductwork

subject: Duct Sealant
rule: duct sealant must not contain volatile organic compounds (VOCs) above the limit specified for the application environment
conditions: when used in occupied indoor spaces or spaces with occupied-zone air return

subject: Duct Sealant
rule: duct sealant must remain flexible and adhered across the full operating temperature range of the duct system
conditions: when applied to ducts that carry heated or cooled air

subject: Duct Damper
rule: duct damper must not obstruct airflow when in the open position
conditions: damper is installed in a ducted air system

subject: Duct Damper
rule: duct damper blade must be able to rotate or translate freely without binding against the duct wall or frame
conditions: damper is installed in an operating HVAC system

subject: Duct Damper
rule: duct damper must maintain structural integrity under maximum design pressure differential without permanent deformation or failure
conditions: damper is installed in a pressurized duct system with a specified pressure class

subject: Duct Damper
rule: duct damper gaskets or seals must not allow unacceptable leakage around the blade when the damper is in the closed position
conditions: damper is specified as a tight-sealing or low-leakage type

subject: Duct Turning Vane
rule: A duct turning vane must be installed with its curved surface facing the direction of airflow
conditions: When used in HVAC duct systems
At duct bends or turns

subject: Duct Turning Vane
rule: A duct turning vane must not obstruct the cross-sectional area of the duct beyond its intended aerodynamic profile
conditions: When installed in a duct fitting or elbow

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panels
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must be installed in direct contact with or within 1 inch of the structural ceiling deck to ensure proper heat transfer
conditions: When used for heating or cooling via hydronic or electric systems
exceptions: Suspended installations with reflective baffles specifically designed for radiant transfer

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panels
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must not be fully covered by thermal insulation on the room-side surface
conditions: When the panel is intended to provide heating or cooling to the occupied space
exceptions: Systems designed as radiant barriers where emission face is intentionally shielded

subject: Radiant Ceiling Panels
rule: Radiant ceiling panels must have continuous pipe or tube runs with no joints concealed above the ceiling
conditions: For hydronic radiant panels with embedded tubing
exceptions: Factory-tested brazed joints in prefabricated panels

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating must be embedded within or directly beneath the finished floor surface
conditions: For any building with radiant floor heating system installed

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating must not exceed maximum surface temperature limits for the floor finish material
conditions: For any radiant floor heating system
exceptions: Industrial or specialty applications where floor surface temperature limits are explicitly designed for higher tolerances

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating supply water temperature must not exceed the temperature rating of all piping and manifold components
conditions: For hydronic (water-based) radiant floor heating systems

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating must have a means to prevent air entrapment in hydronic loops
conditions: For hydronic radiant floor heating systems

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating tubing must maintain minimum bend radius as specified by the manufacturer
conditions: For any radiant floor heating system using continuous tubing

subject: Radiant Floor Heating
rule: Radiant floor heating must not have joints or connections embedded within the concrete or floor slab
conditions: For poured slab or embedded radiant floor heating installations

subject: Radiant Wall Panels
rule: Radiant wall panels must be installed with appropriate clearances from other building elements to allow for thermal expansion
conditions: when panels are subject to temperature fluctuations

subject: Radiant Wall Panels
rule: Radiant wall panels must not be blocked by furniture, equipment, or finishes that impede radiant heat transfer to the conditioned space
conditions: when panels are used for space heating or cooling
exceptions: decorative covers specifically designed and rated for radiant panel use

subject: Radiant Wall Panels
rule: Radiant wall panels must be connected to the correct hydronic or electric supply rated for their designed input
conditions: when panels are hydronic or electric type

subject: Hydronic Tubing (PEX/Copper)
rule: hydronic tubing (PEX/copper) must withstand the maximum operating temperature of the hydronic system without degradation
conditions: system is operational

subject: Hydronic Tubing (PEX/Copper)
rule: hydronic tubing (PEX/copper) must be rated for the maximum operating pressure of the hydronic system
conditions: system is pressurized

subject: Hydronic Tubing (PEX/Copper)
rule: hydronic tubing (PEX/copper) must not be exposed to freezing temperatures while containing water
conditions: tubing contains water
ambient temperature can drop below 0°C/32°F
exceptions: system is protected with antifreeze mixture
system is designed with self-draining/ dry-lay construction

subject: Hydronic Tubing (PEX/Copper)
rule: hydronic tubing (PEX/copper) must be installed with continuous support or anchoring to prevent excessive sagging or movement
conditions: tubing runs are longer than 6 feet horizontally
exceptions: tubing is embedded in a concrete slab or mortar bed

subject: Heat Source (Boiler/Heat Pump)
rule: Heat source (boiler/heat pump) must have an adequate combustion air supply or geothermal exchange medium
conditions: If boiler is combustion-based (gas, oil, biomass)
If heat pump is air-source, requires adequate outdoor air flow
If heat pump is ground-source, requires adequate ground loop volume/flow rate
exceptions: Electric resistance boilers (no combustion air needed)

subject: Heat Source (Boiler/Heat Pump)
rule: Heat source must not be operated without a minimum flow rate of water through the heat exchanger
conditions: Applies to all hydronic boilers and water-to-water/water-to-air heat pumps
exceptions: Non-hydronic systems (e.g., direct refrigerant, steam-only boilers with no water-side flow)

subject: Heat Source (Boiler/Heat Pump)
rule: Heat source flue gas vent (boiler) must be properly sized and routed to safely exhaust combustion products outdoors
conditions: Applies to all combustion-based boilers
exceptions: Condensing boilers with approved polypropylene venting (still must vent outdoors but materials differ)
Electric boilers (no flue)

subject: Heat Source (Boiler/Heat Pump)
rule: Heat source must have over-temperature and over-pressure safety relief protection
conditions: Applies to all pressurized hydronic boilers and heat pumps with closed loops
exceptions: Open-loop atmospheric systems not operating above atmospheric pressure

subject: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
rule: Embedded insulation (under-slab/perimeter) must be installed in full contact with the subgrade or continuous against the foundation wall without gaps
conditions: When placed under slab
When placed as perimeter insulation against foundation wall
exceptions: Void-form insulation systems designed to allow drainage

subject: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
rule: Under-slab embedded insulation must not be installed below the water table unless specifically designed for buoyancy resistance and hydrostatic pressure
conditions: When groundwater table is above the bottom of the insulation layer
exceptions: Insulation systems with engineered ballast or anchoring that resist uplift

subject: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
rule: Embedded perimeter insulation must extend to a depth of at least the frost line in cold climates
conditions: In climate zones where frost depth exceeds the foundation depth
When building has a heated interior space
exceptions: Unconditioned buildings or structures not subject to frost heave
Insulated foundations designed with frost-protected shallow foundation (FPSF) methods as per code

subject: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
rule: Embedded insulation (under-slab) must not be exposed to soil contaminants (e.g., petroleum hydrocarbons, solvents) that chemically degrade the insulation material
conditions: When site soil contains known chemical contaminants at concentrations that attack the specific insulation material type (e.g., EPS, XPS, polyiso)
exceptions: Insulation with a manufacturer-certified chemical-resistant barrier or coating

subject: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
rule: Embedded insulation (under-slab) must be covered with a protective concrete slab or topping of sufficient thickness before building loads are applied
conditions: When the insulation is load-bearing foam intended to support slab-on-grade
exceptions: Proprietary insulated panel systems specifically rated for direct exposure to construction loads

subject: Radiant Ceiling Hydronic Module
rule: hydronic radiant ceiling module must not be installed in ceilings that will later be penetrated by fire suppression sprinkler heads, light fixtures, or other devices that could puncture the hydronic tubing
conditions: when ceiling contains embedded hydronic tubing or panels
when ceiling is a finished surface with limited access for repairs
exceptions: when the module is a prefabricated cassette specifically designed to accommodate such penetrations with protective shielding

subject: Radiant Ceiling Hydronic Module
rule: radiant ceiling hydronic module must operate with a supply water temperature below the dew point of the conditioned space when cooling mode is active
conditions: when the system is used for sensible cooling
when the space has no dedicated dehumidification or vapor barrier
exceptions: when the space is actively dehumidified by a separate dedicated system that keeps dew point below panel surface temperature
when the ceiling surface is treated with a vapor-impermeable layer that prevents condensation

subject: Radiant Ceiling Hydronic Module
rule: hydronic radiant ceiling module must not be connected to a water distribution system containing dissolved oxygen above the corrosion threshold of the tubing material
conditions: when the tubing is ferrous metal or unlined copper
when the system is an open-loop or non-sealed configuration
exceptions: when all wetted components are corrosion-resistant (e.g., PEX, stainless steel, or aluminum with appropriate inhibitors)
when a closed-loop system uses properly maintained corrosion inhibitors

subject: Radiant Ceiling Hydronic Module
rule: hydronic radiant ceiling module must be installed with unobstructed air circulation across the exposed panel surface
conditions: when the module is an exposed-panel or unventilated ceiling type
exceptions: when the module is designed for conductive transfer through a finished ceiling surface (e.g., thermally conductive plaster or metal ceiling tiles)

subject: Floor Coverings for Radiant Systems
rule: Floor covering materials for radiant systems must have a thermal resistance (R-value) of 2.0 or less
conditions: System uses hydronic or electric radiant heating
exceptions: Systems designed as 'thermal mass' storage where higher R-value flooring is intentionally used with controlled cycling

subject: Floor Coverings for Radiant Systems
rule: Floor covering must not contain materials that degrade or outgas when subjected to sustained temperatures of 85°F (30°C)
conditions: System operates as a warming/heating system (not solely cooling)
exceptions: Manufacturer-certified products with documented testing at sustained elevated temperatures

subject: Floor Coverings for Radiant Systems
rule: Floor covering must be installed with gaps or expansion provisions at all perimeter walls and fixed penetrations
conditions: Floor covering is a solid surface material (tile, stone, engineered wood, luxury vinyl plank)
exceptions: Thin-set ceramic/porcelain tile over crack-isolation membrane with full coverage — though perimeter soft joints are still recommended per TCNA guidelines

subject: Floor Coverings for Radiant Systems
rule: Adhesive used for floor covering must be rated for radiant-heat applications
conditions: Floor covering requires adhesive for installation (e.g., engineered wood, LVT, carpet tile, sheet vinyl)
exceptions: Products using mechanical fastening or floating (click-lock) methods that do not rely on adhesive

subject: Radiant Zone Thermostat
rule: Radiant Zone Thermostat must be electrically powered within its rated voltage range

subject: Radiant Zone Thermostat
rule: Radiant Zone Thermostat must have a compatible temperature sensor (integrated or remote) capable of measuring the controlled zone's temperature

subject: Radiant Zone Thermostat
rule: Radiant Zone Thermostat must not be installed in a location exposed to temperatures exceeding its rated operating range

subject: Radiant Heating Control Valve
rule: A radiant heating control valve must be rated for the operating temperature range of the radiant heating system it serves

subject: Radiant Heating Control Valve
rule: A radiant heating control valve must be rated for the maximum operating pressure of the radiant heating system

subject: Radiant Heating Control Valve
rule: A radiant heating control valve must not be installed in a location where it will freeze unless it is freeze-protected
conditions: installed in a location subject to freezing temperatures
exceptions: the valve is specifically designed and rated for freezing conditions
freeze protection is provided (e.g., heat tracing, insulation, antifreeze in system fluid)

subject: Radiant Heating Control Valve
rule: A radiant heating control valve must be compatible with the heat transfer fluid used in the system (e.g., water, glycol mixture)

subject: Radiant Heating Control Valve
rule: A radiant heating control valve must be installed with the flow direction indicated by the arrow on the valve body oriented correctly relative to system flow
conditions: valve has a directional arrow marking
exceptions: valve is explicitly bidirectional and rated for bidirectional flow

subject: Dormer Frame
rule: dormer frame must be structurally connected to the primary roof structure
conditions: dormer frame is installed on a sloped roof

subject: Dormer Frame
rule: dormer frame must maintain minimum headroom clearance at the required egress or occupancy path
conditions: dormer frame encloses a habitable space
applicable building code requires minimum headroom

subject: Dormer Frame
rule: dormer frame must not interrupt the continuity of the primary roof's water-shedding layer

subject: Dormer Roof Deck
rule: Dormer roof deck must have a minimum slope for drainage
conditions: When the dormer roof deck is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: If the dormer roof deck is fully enclosed by a waterproof membrane and designed as a 'green roof' or ballasted with dedicated internal drainage

subject: Dormer Roof Deck
rule: Dormer roof deck must not have ponding water exceeding 48 hours after rainfall
conditions: When the deck is used as an occupiable surface or is not designed for standing water
exceptions: If the roof is explicitly designed as a plaza deck or fountain feature with controlled drainage and waterproofing

subject: Dormer Roof Deck
rule: Dormer roof deck must be capable of supporting design live load (typically 40-60 psf for residential occupiable roof decks)
conditions: When the deck is accessible and intended for occupancy or maintenance access
exceptions: Non-occupiable dormer roof decks with 'access only' designation may use lower loads per code

subject: Dormer Roof Covering
rule: Dormer roof covering must be waterproof to prevent water ingress into the structure below
conditions: when used as the outermost weather-exposed layer

subject: Dormer Roof Covering
rule: Dormer roof covering must be securely fastened to resist wind uplift forces

subject: Dormer Roof Covering
rule: Dormer roof covering must not create a fire hazard that would allow flame spread from an adjacent fire source into the building
conditions: when the building is in a jurisdiction with fire-rated roofing requirements
exceptions: non-combustible or Class A listed assemblies

subject: Dormer Flashing
rule: Dormer flashing must create a watertight seal at the intersection of the dormer and the main roof
conditions: dormer intersects main roof surface

subject: Dormer Flashing
rule: Dormer flashing must be sloped to shed water away from the dormer structure
conditions: flashing is installed on an exterior roof surface

subject: Dormer Flashing
rule: Dormer flashing must not create a dam or obstruction that prevents water drainage from the main roof above the dormer
conditions: flashing is installed at a location where roof runoff passes over or around it

subject: Dormer Window Trim
rule: Dormer window trim must be sealed against water infiltration at all joints with the roof surface and window assembly
conditions: where trim meets roof flashing
where trim meets window frame

subject: Dormer Window Trim
rule: Dormer window trim must not create a dam that prevents water runoff from the roof above
conditions: trim projects above the roof plane
trim is installed below an upper roof slope
exceptions: if trim is specifically designed as a diverter with sealed drainage behind it

subject: Dormer Window Trim
rule: Dormer window trim must be positively attached to the structure to resist wind uplift forces
conditions: in regions with design wind speed ≥ 100 mph

subject: Dormer Soffit & Fascia
rule: Dormer soffit & fascia must be weather-sealed at all joints and connections to prevent water infiltration
conditions: Applicable to all dormer soffit and fascia assemblies where exterior exposure exists

subject: Dormer Soffit & Fascia
rule: Dormer soffit must have adequate ventilation openings (or be designed as unvented per code) to prevent moisture accumulation in the attic/roof cavity
conditions: When the dormer encloses a conditioned or attic space that requires ventilation per building code
exceptions: When the assembly is designed as an unvented conditioned attic assembly with vapor control per IRC

subject: Dormer Soffit & Fascia
rule: Dormer fascia must not be installed with fasteners that penetrate the roof underlayment or waterproof membrane in a manner that creates leak paths
conditions: Where fascia is attached to the roof edge or rake

subject: Dormer Gutter & Downspout
rule: dormer gutter downspout must discharge water away from building foundation
conditions: gutter and downspout are installed on dormer
exceptions: downspout connects to a rainwater harvesting system that routes water to a storage tank located away from foundation

subject: Dormer Gutter & Downspout
rule: dormer gutter must have continuous slope toward downspout outlet
conditions: gutter is installed on dormer
exceptions: gutter is a built-in/internal gutter system that integrates with roof drainage membrane

subject: Dormer Gutter & Downspout
rule: dormer downspout cross-section must not be reduced below design minimum
conditions: downspout is installed
design rainfall intensity is known
exceptions: secondary overflow provisions are provided (e.g., additional scuppers or overflow downspout)

subject: Dormer Ice & Water Shield
rule: Dormer Ice & Water Shield must be installed directly over the roof deck and under the roofing material in a continuous layer covering the entire dormer roof area
conditions: When used on a dormer roof
exceptions: None — this is a physical requirement of the membrane to provide waterproofing

subject: Dormer Ice & Water Shield
rule: Dormer Ice & Water Shield must extend at least 6 inches (or per local code) up the vertical side walls of the dormer
conditions: When used on a dormer roof with side walls
exceptions: None — this is a standard waterproofing detail to prevent water intrusion at wall-to-roof intersections

subject: Dormer Ice & Water Shield
rule: Dormer Ice & Water Shield must not be installed over existing wet or frost-covered roof decking
conditions: During installation
exceptions: None — adhesion depends on clean, dry surface

subject: Dormer Ice & Water Shield
rule: Dormer Ice & Water Shield must lap correctly with the main roof ice and water shield (upper course over lower course)
conditions: When the dormer is installed on an existing roof with its own ice and water shield
exceptions: None — proper lapping is required to shed water

subject: Gable-Front Dormer
rule: gable-front dormer ridge must be aligned vertically with the main roof ridge or the dormer roof must have its own independent drainage path
conditions: when dormer is installed on a roof slope
when dormer ridge does not intersect the main ridge
exceptions: dormer with a valley gutter system that redirects water to the main roof drainage

subject: Gable-Front Dormer
rule: dormer sidewalls must be flashed against the main roof slope
conditions: when the dormer penetrates the roof plane

subject: Gable-Front Dormer
rule: the dormer roof-to-wall intersection must not be a concave inward corner without waterproof membrane

subject: Gable-Front Dormer
rule: dormer window sill must be at least 150 mm above the roof surface below
conditions: when the dormer is set back from the eave edge
when there is a roof surface directly below the window

subject: Shed Dormer
rule: shed dormer's roof must slope downward and away from the main roof ridge to allow water runoff
conditions: shed dormer is installed on a sloped main roof

subject: Shed Dormer
rule: shed dormer must not intersect the main roof's structural ridge beam

subject: Shed Dormer
rule: shed dormer sidewalls must be vertically plumb and bear on a continuous load path to foundation

subject: Hip Dormer
rule: hip dormer roof slope must match the main roof slope
conditions: when the dormer is set on a sloped main roof
exceptions: when designed as a 'shed dormer' variant (though technically not a hip dormer)

subject: Hip Dormer
rule: hip dormer must have a minimum roof pitch of 3:12
conditions: for weather-exposed residential construction with standard asphalt shingles
exceptions: when standing seam metal roofing or other high-performance waterproof membrane is used
when located in a very low snow-load climate region with engineered custom flashing

subject: Hip Dormer
rule: hip dormer must not have its ridge line lower than the attachment point to the main roof
conditions: when the dormer is installed on a sloped roof

subject: Flat-Roof Dormer
rule: the flat-roof dormer's roof must have a minimum slope of 1/8 inch per foot (approximately 1% or greater) to ensure positive drainage and prevent ponding water
conditions: the dormer has a flat roof configuration
exceptions: the dormer roof is designed as a 'green roof' with engineered drainage layers
the dormer roof is part of a building in a climate where snow/ice melt drainage is managed through other means such as internal drains, scuppers, or siphonic drainage systems

subject: Flat-Roof Dormer
rule: the flat-roof dormer must have waterproof membrane or roofing material covering the entire roof surface, with all seams and penetrations properly sealed
conditions: the dormer has a flat roof configuration

subject: Flat-Roof Dormer
rule: the flat-roof dormer must have a structural deck capable of supporting the design loads (dead load of roofing materials plus live loads including snow, maintenance, and water accumulation)
conditions: the dormer has a flat roof configuration

subject: Roof Cap Membrane
rule: roof cap membrane must form a continuous water barrier across the entire roof surface
conditions: when installed as the primary waterproofing layer
exceptions: at planned penetrations where proper flashings are installed

subject: Roof Cap Membrane
rule: roof cap membrane must be compatible with all adjacent materials and sealants to prevent chemical degradation
conditions: when in contact with other roofing materials, adhesives, or sealants

subject: Roof Cap Membrane
rule: roof cap membrane must not be installed on surfaces that are wet, frost-covered, or below the manufacturer's minimum application temperature
conditions: during installation

subject: Roof Cap Flashing
rule: roof cap flashing must be lapped in the direction of water flow (shingle fashion)
conditions: flashing is installed on a sloped roof

subject: Roof Cap Flashing
rule: roof cap flashing must not be installed without proper attachment (fasteners or mechanical anchorage)

subject: Roof Cap Flashing
rule: roof cap flashing material must be compatible with adjacent materials to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: dissimilar metals are in contact with the flashing
exceptions: materials are electrically isolated by a non-conductive barrier

subject: Roof Cap Flashing
rule: roof cap flashing must extend at least the minimum required distance up the vertical surface it covers
conditions: flashing terminates against a vertical wall or parapet

subject: Roof Cap Substrate/Deck
rule: roof cap substrate/deck must be sloped to provide positive drainage to roof drains or scuppers
conditions: roof is flat or low-slope (less than 1/4:12 pitch)
exceptions: roof is designed as a dead-level roof with active mechanical drainage system designed to handle standing water

subject: Roof Cap Substrate/Deck
rule: roof cap substrate/deck must have sufficient structural capacity to support dead load, live load, and any superimposed loads without excessive deflection

subject: Roof Cap Insulation
rule: Roof cap insulation must be continuous across the roof surface to prevent thermal bridging
conditions: where insulation is applied over structural deck
exceptions: intentional thermal breaks at structural penetrations

subject: Roof Cap Insulation
rule: Roof cap insulation must not be compressed beyond its rated thickness
conditions: when installed below roof membrane or cover board

subject: Roof Cap Insulation
rule: Roof cap insulation must remain dry (must not absorb or retain moisture)
exceptions: closed-cell foam products designed for wet service where manufacturer-certified

subject: Roof Cap Insulation
rule: Roof cap insulation must be protected from UV radiation when not covered by membrane
conditions: during construction staging periods exceeding manufacturer's exposure limit
exceptions: insulation types rated for UV exposure per manufacturer specification

subject: Roof Cap Coping
rule: roof cap coping must have a continuous seal at all joints to prevent water intrusion
conditions: coping is installed on a flat or low-slope roof
exceptions: coping is purely decorative and not exposed to weather

subject: Roof Cap Coping
rule: roof cap coping must overlap the underlying parapet or wall by a minimum of 1 inch (25 mm) on each side
conditions: coping is installed on a parapet wall
exceptions: coping is mechanically interlocked with the wall system via engineered anchors that provide equivalent positive attachment

subject: Roof Cap Coping
rule: roof cap coping must not have end joints aligned with building expansion joints below without an accommodating transition detail
conditions: coping spans a building expansion joint

subject: Roof Cap Gravel Stop
rule: gravel stop must be installed at roof perimeter edge with positive attachment to roof structure or deck
conditions: used as edge flashing termination
installed at roof perimeter
exceptions: roofs with integral parapet wall systems that serve as gravel stop

subject: Roof Cap Gravel Stop
rule: gravel stop must be installed with compatible flashing and counterflashing at adjacent wall intersections
conditions: roof abuts vertical wall or parapet
exceptions: monolithic roof systems with no wall penetrations or terminations

subject: Roof Cap Gravel Stop
rule: gravel stop must not be installed without a continuous roof membrane extending beneath or integrated with it
conditions: any installation

subject: Roof Cap Gravel Stop
rule: gravel stop must be installed at a height that is above the finished roof surface to retain gravel ballast
conditions: roof uses loose-laid gravel ballast
exceptions: systems where gravel stop serves only as fascia trim and ballast is restrained by other means

subject: Precast Concrete Roof Cap
rule: precast concrete roof cap must be bedded in mortar or a structural bearing pad on the supporting wall or beam
conditions: installed as a roof termination component
exceptions: mechanically anchored systems where manufacturer's approved hardware provides equivalent load transfer

subject: Precast Concrete Roof Cap
rule: precast concrete roof cap must have a minimum slope for positive drainage
conditions: used as a coping or roof-edge cap

subject: Precast Concrete Roof Cap
rule: precast concrete roof cap must not be installed without adequate overlap over the structure below
conditions: capping a parapet or wall
exceptions: systems with an engineered waterproof membrane that covers the full wall-to-cap junction

subject: Metal Roof Cap
rule: metal roof cap must have a minimum slope to drain water
conditions: installed as a standalone cap on a flat or low-slope surface
exceptions: when the cap is used solely as a decorative trim piece with no exposure to precipitation

subject: Metal Roof Cap
rule: metal roof cap must not have exposed fasteners that penetrate upward into the cap surface
conditions: when installed in a climate with rain or snow

subject: Metal Roof Cap
rule: metal roof cap must be made from a material with a melting point above 200°C if located near a chimney or flue
conditions: cap is installed within 600 mm horizontally or 1200 mm vertically of a chimney, flue, or other heat source
exceptions: when a thermal barrier rated for the expected temperature is placed between the cap and the heat source

subject: Stone Roof Cap
rule: stone roof cap must have a positive slope (pitch) to shed water
conditions: cap is exposed to precipitation

subject: Stone Roof Cap
rule: stone roof cap must have a continuous waterproof membrane or flashing beneath it at all joints and seams
conditions: cap is composed of multiple stone pieces
exceptions: cap is a single monolithic stone slab with no joints

subject: Stone Roof Cap
rule: stone roof cap must not be installed directly onto a combustible roof deck without a non-combustible separation layer
conditions: roof deck below is combustible (e.g., wood)

subject: Roof Cap Sealant Joints
rule: roof cap sealant joints must be fully sealed to prevent water intrusion
conditions: when roof assembly is exposed to precipitation
exceptions: temporary construction sequence where intentional drainage weeps are designed

subject: Roof Cap Sealant Joints
rule: roof cap sealant joints must accommodate thermal and structural movement without rupture or debonding
conditions: when the roof assembly is subject to temperature cycling or differential movement between substrates

subject: Roof Cap Sealant Joints
rule: roof cap sealant must not be applied over contaminated or wet surfaces
conditions: during installation of sealant joints

subject: Roof Cap Fasteners & Clips
rule: roof cap fasteners and clips must be compatible with the roofing material they fasten

subject: Roof Cap Fasteners & Clips
rule: roof cap fasteners and clips must be installed at the spacing specified by the roof panel manufacturer
conditions: when manufacturer specifications for fastener spacing are provided

subject: Roof Cap Fasteners & Clips
rule: roof cap fasteners and clips must not be over-driven or under-driven relative to the roofing profile

subject: Roof Cap Fasteners & Clips
rule: roof cap fasteners must not be installed through standing seam panel striations or swaged ribs
conditions: when the roof uses standing seam metal panels with factory-formed interlock striations

subject: Floor Base Layer / Screed
rule: floor base layer / screed must be placed on a structurally sound and stable substrate
conditions: applies to all floor screed installations

subject: Floor Base Layer / Screed
rule: floor base layer / screed must achieve a minimum compressive strength appropriate to its intended loading
conditions: where screed serves as a wearing surface or receives traffic loads
exceptions: bonded screeds that are purely levelling layers covered immediately by another finish may have lower strength requirements

subject: Floor Base Layer / Screed
rule: floor base layer / screed must not be applied over a damp-proof membrane without adequate curing or bonding preparation
conditions: when screed is placed directly on a DPM or vapour barrier
exceptions: unbonded screeds specifically designed and detailed for use over DPM with appropriate separation layer

subject: Floor Base Layer / Screed
rule: floor base layer / screed must be installed with adequate movement joints to control drying shrinkage and thermal movement
conditions: for large-area or long-span screed installations
exceptions: very small rooms or areas below the shrinkage crack risk threshold determined by design standards

subject: Vapor Barrier / Damp-proof Membrane
rule: vapor barrier must be installed on the warm side of the building assembly
conditions: In heated or conditioned spaces
In climates with significant heating degree days
exceptions: In hot-humid climates where the predominant moisture drive is from exterior to interior

subject: Vapor Barrier / Damp-proof Membrane
rule: vapor barrier must have a permeance rating appropriate to the climate zone and assembly type
conditions: When used in wall, roof, or floor assemblies in zones with defined moisture loading

subject: Vapor Barrier / Damp-proof Membrane
rule: vapor barrier must maintain continuity without gaps or tears at all joints and penetrations
conditions: When installed as a continuous plane in an assembly

subject: Vapor Barrier / Damp-proof Membrane
rule: vapor barrier must not be installed in assemblies designed to dry to the interior
conditions: In wall assemblies where the cladding is vapor-impermeable and the interior side is designed as the drying plane
In certain insulated masonry or concrete wall systems
exceptions: When a fully vapor-tight assembly is intentionally designed with interior mechanical dehumidification

subject: Floor Drain / Trench Drain
rule: floor drain or trench drain must be connected to a drainage piping system that leads to an approved discharge point
conditions: when installed as part of a building drainage system
exceptions: temporary installations where collected water is actively removed by pumping or manual means

subject: Floor Drain / Trench Drain
rule: floor drain or trench drain body must be watertight
conditions: when installed in a waterproofed area such as a shower, kitchen, or wet room
exceptions: drains installed in exterior or interstitial locations where minor leakage is acceptable

subject: Floor Drain / Trench Drain
rule: floor drain or trench drain must have a trap or other mechanism to prevent sewer gas entry into occupied spaces
conditions: when connected to a sanitary drainage system
exceptions: drains connected only to stormwater systems where no sewer gas is present
drains in unoccupied ventilated spaces

subject: Floor Drain / Trench Drain
rule: floor drain or trench drain must be installed with a slope in the surrounding floor surface directing flow toward the drain
conditions: when the drain is intended for surface water collection
exceptions: drains installed in a sump or pit where water enters by gravity pooling rather than surface sheet flow

subject: Expansion / Control Joint
rule: Expansion/control joints in building assemblies must be located where they allow free movement without transferring stress to adjacent materials or structural elements
conditions: when expansion/control joints are installed in walls
floors
roofs
or cladding systems

subject: Expansion / Control Joint
rule: Expansion/control joints must not be sealed with rigid materials that prevent joint movement
conditions: when a sealant or filler is applied at the joint location
exceptions: when the joint is intentionally designed as a 'fixed' connection and no longer functions as an expansion joint

subject: Expansion / Control Joint
rule: The joint width and spacing must be sized proportionally to the expected thermal/moisture movement of the materials being separated
conditions: when determining expansion joint layout in a continuous assembly

subject: Access Floor Panel
rule: access floor panel must be installed on a level and structurally adequate subfloor
conditions: when used as a raised floor system

subject: Access Floor Panel
rule: access floor panel must be able to support its design live load without excessive deflection or failure
conditions: when subject to expected occupancy or equipment loads

subject: Access Floor Panel
rule: access floor panel must not have exposed sharp edges or protrusions that could cause injury
conditions: in areas of pedestrian traffic

subject: Access Floor Panel
rule: access floor panel must be securely fastened or seated to prevent dislodgement under foot traffic or vibration

subject: Raised Access Floor System
rule: raised access floor system must be installed on a level and structurally sound subfloor capable of supporting the design load plus a minimum safety factor of 1.5
conditions: system is load-bearing and supports occupant or equipment loads

subject: Raised Access Floor System
rule: raised access floor system must have pedestal heights and lateral bracing designed to prevent buckling or overturning under the specified design live load
conditions: system height exceeds 300 mm (typical for most installations)

subject: Raised Access Floor System
rule: raised access floor panels must be positively interlocked or fastened to prevent vertical displacement under foot traffic or equipment vibration
exceptions: non-traffic zones where panels are only accessed by maintenance personnel and are designed to be loose-laid with perimeter restraints

subject: Raised Access Floor System
rule: raised access floor system must not be used in locations subject to flooding or standing water unless the system and all components are rated for wet conditions
conditions: system is installed in a below-grade or flood-prone area
exceptions: system is specifically designed and rated as flood-resistant with sealed pedestals, corrosion-proof materials, and drainage provisions

subject: Raised Access Floor System
rule: raised access floor system serving electrical or data cabling must have a fire-resistance-rated construction or be protected by an automatic fire suppression system in compliance with applicable building code
conditions: plenum space below the raised floor contains combustible cabling and is used as an air handling plenum
exceptions: local code explicitly exempts raised floor plenums with limited cable volume and fire-stop compartmentation

subject: Radiant Floor Heating / Cooling System
rule: hydronic radiant floor heating/cooling system must not have supply water temperature exceeding 140°F (60°C) for heating in embedded slab applications to avoid damaging the concrete or flooring materials
conditions: system is hydronic (water-based)
embedded in concrete slab or thin-pour gypcrete
heating mode
exceptions: systems using engineered slab materials rated for higher temperatures

subject: Radiant Floor Heating / Cooling System
rule: radiant floor cooling system must not supply water below the local dew-point temperature of the conditioned space to prevent condensation within the floor assembly
conditions: system is used for cooling (chilled water operation)
floor surface will be exposed to room air
exceptions: systems with dedicated dehumidification maintaining room dew point below floor surface temperature
systems with vapor barrier and drainage layer designed for condensation management

subject: Radiant Floor Heating / Cooling System
rule: radiant floor heating system must have automatic temperature-limiting controls to prevent floor surface temperature from exceeding 85°F (29°C) in occupied spaces with bare feet contact
conditions: system is in heating mode
occupiable space
flooring is tile, stone, concrete, or similar bare-foot-contact surface
exceptions: spaces not intended for bare-foot occupancy (e.g., warehouses, garages)

subject: Radiant Floor Heating / Cooling System
rule: radiant floor heating system must not be installed directly over expansion joints in the structural slab
conditions: tubing or cables embedded in, or attached directly to, the slab
exceptions: systems designed with expansion joint detailing that accommodates movement without damage to piping/cables

subject: Structural Floor Slab
rule: structural floor slab must be designed to support its specified live load and dead load without exceeding allowable stress or deflection limits

subject: Structural Floor Slab
rule: structural floor slab must have minimum concrete cover over reinforcement as specified by code for fire resistance and corrosion protection

subject: Structural Floor Slab
rule: structural floor slab must have adequate thickness to prevent punching shear failure at column connections

subject: Structural Floor Slab
rule: structural floor slab must not have reinforcement less than the minimum required ratio for temperature and shrinkage crack control

subject: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
rule: stair tread / landing surface must have a slip-resistant finish
conditions: surface is accessible to users
surface is indoor or outdoor
exceptions: emergency evacuation routes with specific temporary surface requirements

subject: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
rule: stair tread / landing surface must have a minimum coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.5 when wet
conditions: surface is exposed to precipitation or tracked water
building code jurisdiction adopts ASTM C1028 or equivalent standard

subject: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
rule: stair tread / landing surface must not deflect more than L/360 under design live load
conditions: surface spans between supports

subject: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
rule: stair tread / landing surface must have a minimum hardness/impact resistance to prevent spalling from heel impact and dropped objects
conditions: surface material is concrete, stone, or brittle tile
exceptions: surface protected by bonded resilient overlay

subject: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
rule: stair tread / landing surface must not have any protruding fasteners, sharp edges, or exposed reinforcement
exceptions: temporary construction-stage surfaces before handover

subject: Floor Socket / Floor Box
rule: Floor socket / floor box must be installed on a level, stable surface that supports its load
conditions: in use
installed in accessible pedestrian areas
subject to foot traffic or equipment loading

subject: Floor Socket / Floor Box
rule: Floor socket / floor box must not have its cover left open or unsecured when not in active use
conditions: installed in a trafficked floor area
exceptions: during active maintenance or cable-pulling operations with a temporary barrier or warning signage in place

subject: Floor Socket / Floor Box
rule: Floor socket / floor box cover must have a minimum load rating consistent with the expected traffic class of the installation area
conditions: installed in a floor subject to pedestrian or vehicular traffic

subject: Floor Socket / Floor Box
rule: Floor socket / floor box must not allow liquid ingress into electrical compartments when cover is closed and sealed
conditions: installed in wet-cleaned floors
installed in areas subject to liquid spill risk

subject: Floor Grating / Grate
rule: floor grating / grate must have adequate load-bearing capacity for its intended live load
conditions: when used in walkable areas or vehicle access zones
exceptions: non-traversable grates used only for light-duty ventilation covers

subject: Floor Grating / Grate
rule: floor grating / grate must have openings small enough to prevent foot or object penetration hazard
conditions: when installed in areas accessible to personnel or where small objects must be retained
exceptions: grates in secured non-accessible zones where fall-through risk is eliminated by other means

subject: Floor Grating / Grate
rule: floor grating / grate must be secured against lateral displacement or uplift
conditions: when subjected to foot traffic, wheel loads, or wind uplift conditions
exceptions: grates held in place solely by gravity in non-traffic areas where displacement poses no risk

subject: Floor Mat / Entrance Mat
rule: Floor mat / entrance mat must be slip-resistant on both top and bottom surfaces
conditions: when installed in a public or high-traffic entrance area
when installed on hard flooring surfaces such as tile, concrete, or hardwood
exceptions: mats designed exclusively for dry, low-traffic interior use where slip risk is negligible

subject: Floor Mat / Entrance Mat
rule: Floor mat must not create a trip hazard at edges taller than 1/4 inch (6 mm)
conditions: when installed at a doorway or transition between flooring surfaces
when the mat is not recessed or flush-mounted
exceptions: mats that are permanently recessed into the floor substrate

subject: Floor Mat / Entrance Mat
rule: Floor mat must be water- and dirt-absorbent when used as an entrance mat for moisture/debris control
conditions: when the mat is specified as an 'entrance mat' intended to capture moisture and dirt from foot traffic
exceptions: decorative or non-absorbent mats used strictly for branding or aesthetics in dry interior zones away from exterior doors

subject: Slip-resistant Floor Coating
rule: Slip-resistant floor coating must have a surface roughness (coefficient of friction) meeting or exceeding the applicable building code minimum for the occupancy type
conditions: applied to walking surfaces accessible to building occupants
exceptions: areas explicitly exempted by local building code (e.g., some mechanical rooms)

subject: Slip-resistant Floor Coating
rule: Slip-resistant floor coating must not be applied over substrates that are incompatible such that the coating delaminates or fails to cure properly
conditions: coating is applied over existing flooring, adhesives, sealers, or contaminated surfaces
exceptions: substrate prepared and primed per manufacturer specifications

subject: Slip-resistant Floor Coating
rule: Slip-resistant floor coating must not reduce the floor's fire-resistance rating below the code-required level for the occupancy
conditions: coating is applied to a floor assembly that requires a fire-resistance rating

subject: Lapped Wall Cladding
rule: Lapped wall cladding must maintain a minimum lap distance between adjacent boards to prevent water ingress
conditions: When installed on exterior walls
When boards are horizontally oriented
exceptions: When boards are designed with interlocking shiplap or tongue-and-groove profiles that provide the seal through joint geometry rather than overlap distance

subject: Lapped Wall Cladding
rule: Lapped wall cladding must be fixed to allow for thermal and moisture movement
conditions: When installed in climates with temperature variation exceeding 20°C annually
When substrate is moisture-sensitive

subject: Lapped Wall Cladding
rule: Lapped wall cladding must not be installed with gaps that allow direct water entry at end joints
conditions: At horizontal butt joints between boards

subject: Lapped Wall Underlay/Substrate
rule: lapped wall underlay/substrate must be installed with horizontal overlaps oriented to shed water downward and outward (top layer overlapping bottom layer)
conditions: wall underlay/substrate is installed on an exterior wall
wall is subject to moisture exposure
exceptions: temporary installation during dry conditions where no moisture exposure is expected before cladding installation

subject: Lapped Wall Underlay/Substrate
rule: lapped wall underlay/substrate must not be installed with reverse lap orientation (bottom layer overlapping top layer)
conditions: wall underlay/substrate is installed on an exterior wall
wall is subject to moisture exposure

subject: Lapped Wall Flashing
rule: Lapped wall flashing must have a minimum 2-inch overlap at all horizontal joints
conditions: When multiple pieces of flashing are joined along the horizontal direction
exceptions: Factory-fabricated continuous flashing sections without joints

subject: Lapped Wall Flashing
rule: Lapped wall flashing must slope downward toward the exterior (minimum slope of 1/2 inch per foot)
conditions: When installed above a building opening or as through-wall flashing

subject: Lapped Wall Flashing
rule: Lapped wall flashing must not terminate below the exterior cladding without a drip edge or kick-out
conditions: When the flashing projects beyond the wall plane

subject: Lapped Wall Ventilation Cavity
rule: Lapped wall ventilation cavity must maintain a minimum unobstructed cross-sectional area of at least 25 mm (or 1 inch) between the back of the cladding and the sheathing/insulation to allow continuous airflow.
conditions: Cavity is provided behind a drained and vented cladding system
exceptions: Cavity is part of a pressure-equalized rainscreen (PER) system where design verification demonstrates equivalent ventilation performance

subject: Lapped Wall Ventilation Cavity
rule: Lapped wall ventilation cavity must_not be blocked or filled at the top and bottom of the wall assembly; both vent openings (drainage/ventilation inlets and outlets) must be unobstructed.
conditions: Cavity is intended to be ventilated at both top and bottom
exceptions: A sealed cavity with mechanical ventilation designed per engineering analysis

subject: Lapped Wall Ventilation Cavity
rule: Lapped wall ventilation cavity must include a corrosion-resistant insect screen (mesh ≤ 6 mm openings) at all vent openings.
conditions: Building is located in a region with wood-destroying insects
Cavity is open to the exterior
exceptions: Entire building envelope is designed as a sealed system with no exterior vent openings to ambient air

subject: Lapped Wall Air Seal
rule: Lapped wall air seal must maintain continuous contact between lapped layers across the entire joint length

subject: Lapped Wall Air Seal
rule: Lapped wall air seal must not have gaps, tears, or punctures in any of the lapped membrane or tape layers

subject: Lapped Wall Air Seal
rule: Lapped wall air seal must be applied to substrates that are clean, dry, and free of frost, ice, or standing water
conditions: Adhesion-dependent lapped joint (e.g., tape or self-adhered membrane)

subject: Lapped Wall Air Seal
rule: Lapped wall air seal must have minimum overlap dimension as specified by manufacturer

subject: Interior Partition Wall
rule: must resist lateral loads and not collapse under its own weight
conditions: when the wall extends from floor to structural ceiling/deck
exceptions: non-structural partitions that are fully braced by adjacent structure at top and bottom
demountable partition systems designed to be non-load-bearing

subject: Interior Partition Wall
rule: must not be used as primary structural support for floors or roof above
conditions: unless specifically designed and detailed as a structural wall

subject: Interior Partition Wall
rule: must have a fire-resistance rating appropriate to its location and occupancy requirements
conditions: where required by building code for occupancy type, building height, or means of egress protection
exceptions: walls in fully sprinklered buildings where code permits reduced or no rating
walls that are not fire-separation rated (e.g., simple room dividers in single-family dwellings)

subject: Interior Partition Wall
rule: must not have openings that violate required fire-resistance continuity unless protected by rated assemblies
conditions: when the wall is required to have a fire-resistance rating
exceptions: doors, windows, or penetrations that are themselves fire-rated to match the wall rating
penetrations firestopped with approved systems

subject: Interior Partition Wall
rule: must be laterally braced at top and bottom or designed as a cantilever for its full height
conditions: for full-height partitions (extending to structural deck)
exceptions: partition systems specifically designed and tested as freestanding with engineered base anchorage

subject: Interior Wall Framing
rule: Interior wall framing must be designed to support lateral loads from wind or seismic forces
conditions: Building is located in a region with seismic activity or high wind loads
exceptions: Non-structural partitioning walls that are not part of the lateral force-resisting system

subject: Interior Wall Framing
rule: Interior wall framing must accommodate vertical gravity loads (self-weight and any imposed loads) without excessive deflection
conditions: Walls are load-bearing
exceptions: Non-load-bearing partition walls

subject: Interior Wall Framing
rule: Interior wall framing must not have stud spacing that exceeds the maximum allowed by code for the given wall height and loading
conditions: Wood or steel stud framing

subject: Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Wall insulation layer must maintain continuous thermal barrier without gaps
conditions: When used as primary thermal insulation

subject: Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Wall insulation layer must not be compressed beyond its designed thickness
conditions: When using compressible insulation materials such as fiberglass or mineral wool

subject: Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Wall insulation layer must be protected from liquid water ingress
conditions: When installed in exterior wall assemblies exposed to precipitation or ground moisture
exceptions: When insulation material is closed-cell foam rated for water exposure and the assembly is designed for drainage behind the insulation

subject: Wall Insulation Layer
rule: Wall insulation layer must not be installed in direct contact with a heat source exceeding its rated temperature
conditions: When used near flues, chimneys, recessed lighting, or other heat-producing elements

subject: Vapor Barrier / Air Barrier
rule: vapor barrier / air barrier must be located on the warm side of the insulation assembly
conditions: installed in a climate with significant heating or cooling demand
used in an opaque envelope assembly
exceptions: when the assembly is designed as a 'breathable' wall system that intentionally allows vapor diffusion in both directions
in hot-humid climates where the vapor barrier is placed on the exterior side

subject: Vapor Barrier / Air Barrier
rule: vapor barrier / air barrier must be continuous across the entire building envelope
conditions: used as the primary air barrier system
exceptions: at intentional openings such as windows, doors, and mechanical penetrations which must be sealed with compatible transition membranes

subject: Vapor Barrier / Air Barrier
rule: vapor barrier / air barrier must not be installed on both sides of a wall assembly
conditions: in a wall assembly in a cold or mixed climate
exceptions: when one of the barriers is specifically designed as a Class III vapor retarder (low permeability) and the assembly has a drying pathway to at least one side

subject: Vapor Barrier / Air Barrier
rule: vapor barrier / air barrier material must be compatible with adjacent building materials
conditions: in contact with solvent-based adhesives, sealants, or certain foam insulation products
exceptions: when a compatible separation layer (e.g., building paper, slip sheet) is installed between them

subject: Interior Wall Sheathing
rule: Interior wall sheathing must provide a continuous fire-resistance-rated barrier where required by building code
conditions: when serving as part of a fire-rated assembly
when required by local building code for occupancy type or building height
exceptions: where code allows non-rated sheathing in non-rated partitions

subject: Interior Wall Sheathing
rule: Interior wall sheathing must be attached to structural supports (studs or furring) with adequate fasteners to remain in place under service loads
conditions: in all occupied interior conditions

subject: Interior Wall Sheathing
rule: Interior wall sheathing must not be installed where it will be exposed to continuous liquid water or high moisture without appropriate moisture-resistant material
conditions: in wet areas such as showers, pool enclosures, or exterior-exposed interior walls
exceptions: when using moisture-resistant boards (e.g., MR gypsum, cement board)

subject: Wall Finish / Plaster
rule: plaster must be applied over a clean, sound, and properly prepared substrate
conditions: interior or exterior plaster application

subject: Wall Finish / Plaster
rule: plaster must not be applied in freezing temperatures or onto frozen surfaces
conditions: cementitious or gypsum plaster
exceptions: specialized cold-weather formulations explicitly rated for low-temperature application

subject: Wall Finish / Plaster
rule: plaster must be applied with maximum coat thickness not exceeding manufacturer specified limits per coat
conditions: any plaster type

subject: Wall Finish / Plaster
rule: plaster must have provisions to control cracking at building movement joints
conditions: plaster applied over substrates with structural or thermal movement joints
plaster spans dissimilar materials

subject: Interior Wall Paint / Coating
rule: Interior wall paint/coating must be applied only to surfaces that are clean, dry, and free of loose material
conditions: prior to paint application

subject: Interior Wall Paint / Coating
rule: Interior wall paint/coating must be compatible with the substrate material
conditions: when selecting paint system
exceptions: universal primer systems that bridge incompatible substrates

subject: Interior Wall Paint / Coating
rule: Interior wall paint/coating must not be applied when ambient or surface temperature is below the manufacturer's specified minimum
conditions: during application
exceptions: paints specifically formulated for low-temperature application

subject: Wall Corner Bead / Trim
rule: wall corner bead / trim must be installed at all external and internal wall corners where wall finish materials meet
conditions: where wall finish materials (such as drywall, plaster, or cement board) terminate or change direction at a corner
exceptions: where rounded corner profiles (bullnose) are used intentionally as the finish
where corner protection is provided by an alternative continuous structural element

subject: Wall Corner Bead / Trim
rule: wall corner bead / trim must be mechanically fastened or embedded in a setting compound
conditions: when installed on gypsum board or plaster wall surfaces
exceptions: when adhesive-backed trim is used on substrates specifically rated for adhesive-only application as per manufacturer specification

subject: Wall Corner Bead / Trim
