rule: wall corner bead / trim must not create a continuous moisture bridge from exposed exterior surfaces to interior framing
conditions: when used at exterior-facing wall corners in a building envelope assembly
exceptions: when the bead/trim is made of non-thermally-conductive material or is interrupted by a thermal break

subject: Wall Tile / Ceramic Wall Finish
rule: Ceramic wall tile must be installed over a waterproof or water-resistant substrate in wet areas (showers, tub surrounds, pool areas)
conditions: Tile installed in wet areas defined as locations subject to direct water spray or sustained high humidity
Tile installed over gypsum board without waterproofing
exceptions: Tile installed on non-absorbent backing like cement board or fiber-cement board that is itself water-resistant by manufacturer specification and code-compliant for the intended use

subject: Wall Tile / Ceramic Wall Finish
rule: Ceramic wall tile must not be installed on surfaces subject to continuous structural movement or deflection beyond the tile manufacturer's specified limits without a movement joint accommodation system
conditions: Substrate has calculated or known deflection exceeding L/360 for thin-set tile or L/480 for natural stone or large-format tile per ANSI standards
exceptions: Installation uses a crack isolation membrane or decoupling membrane rated for the expected movement and listed for ceramic tile installation

subject: Wall Tile / Ceramic Wall Finish
rule: Ceramic wall tile must be installed at a temperature above the tile setting material manufacturer's minimum application temperature (typically 50°F/10°C minimum)
conditions: Installation performed in unheated spaces or during cold weather conditions
Thin-set mortar, mastic, or grout is being used as the bonding/grouting medium
exceptions: Manufacturer specifically certifies the material for low-temperature installation with documented test data meeting bond strength requirements at the intended temperature

subject: Wall Tile / Ceramic Wall Finish
rule: Ceramic wall tile must have minimum 3mm (1/8 inch) movement joints at all changes of plane (corners, ceiling junctions, column wraps) and at maximum spacing intervals per TCNA/ANSI guidelines for the tile type
conditions: Tile is continuous across interior wall plane changes or exceeds maximum uninterrupted dimension (typically 12-16 feet for interior, 8 feet for exterior)
exceptions: Manufacturer-specified jointless installation system with tested expansion accommodation is used and complies with local building code

subject: Hidden Services Chase Wall
rule: hidden services chase wall must be large enough to accommodate all required mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems passing through it
conditions: chase walls enclose vertical or horizontal runs of building services

subject: Hidden Services Chase Wall
rule: hidden services chase wall must not obstruct required fire-rated separation between fire compartments
conditions: the chase wall penetrates a fire-rated assembly or connects multiple fire compartments

subject: Hidden Services Chase Wall
rule: hidden services chase wall must maintain structural integrity — it must not be removed or have its load-bearing capacity reduced without structural reinforcement
conditions: the chase wall is load-bearing or part of a shear-resisting system

subject: Interior Wall Expansion Joint
rule: Interior wall expansion joint must allow for differential movement between adjacent wall sections
conditions: where interior walls are constructed of materials with different thermal expansion coefficients
or where the wall span exceeds material-specific movement joint spacing requirements
exceptions: walls constructed as a single monolithic element with no anticipated differential movement

subject: Interior Wall Expansion Joint
rule: Interior wall expansion joint must be filled with a fire-rated sealant or material with an equal or greater fire-resistance rating than the wall assembly
conditions: when the wall is a fire-rated assembly
exceptions: non-rated interior partitions where fire separation is not required

subject: Interior Wall Expansion Joint
rule: Interior wall expansion joint must not create a continuous air or vapor barrier breach across the full height of the wall
conditions: when the wall separates conditioned and unconditioned spaces
or when the wall is part of a building's air barrier system
exceptions: where the joint is specifically designed as a controlled intentional opening with compensating HVAC design

subject: Sliding Window (Horizontal)
rule: A sliding window's horizontal sliding sash must be supported by a track or sill that prevents the sash from tilting or falling out of the frame
conditions: Window is operable (not fixed/louvered)
exceptions: Fixed non-operable horizontal window (no sliding sash)

subject: Sliding Window (Horizontal)
rule: A sliding window must not have a vertical sliding track mechanism

subject: Sliding Window (Horizontal)
rule: The horizontal sliding panel must have an overlap or interlock with the fixed panel or frame at the meeting stile to prevent direct air and water infiltration
conditions: Window is designed for weather-exposed exterior wall
exceptions: Interior-only non-weather-rated sliding window

subject: Pivot Window
rule: pivot window must have its pivot hinge axis positioned at the vertical centerline of the frame
conditions: window is a side-hung or top-hung pivot type

subject: Pivot Window
rule: pivot window must have a weatherstripping seal continuous around the entire perimeter of the opening frame
conditions: window is installed in an exterior wall and exposed to weather
exceptions: interior-only pivot window not exposed to exterior environment

subject: Pivot Window
rule: pivot window must have a locking mechanism that engages when the sash is closed

subject: Pivot Window
rule: pivot window must_not have its pivot mechanism installed without a counterbalance or friction stay if the sash weight exceeds 15 kg
conditions: sash weight exceeds 15 kg

subject: Jalousie / Louvre Window
rule: jalousie / louvre window must have operable glass or blade slats that can be adjusted to control airflow and light
exceptions: Fixed louvre windows (non-operable) used solely for architectural aesthetic

subject: Jalousie / Louvre Window
rule: jalousie / louvre window slats must be angled downward on the exterior side to shed rainwater away from the interior
conditions: When the window is installed in an exterior wall or opening exposed to weather
exceptions: Interior-use jalousie partitions not exposed to rain

subject: Jalousie / Louvre Window
rule: jalousie / louvre window must not have continuous sealed glazing across the full opening

subject: Jalousie / Louvre Window
rule: jalousie / louvre window must have slats that overlap or interlock when closed to provide a weather seal
conditions: When the window is required to be weather-tight or provide enclosure
exceptions: Interior decorative louvres, or jalousies in fully sheltered locations where weather sealing is not required

subject: Folding / Bi-Fold Window
rule: folding/bi-fold window when fully extended must not protrude beyond property boundary or into public right-of-way without permit
conditions: window is fully opened or extended outward
exceptions: local zoning variance or permit obtained

subject: Folding / Bi-Fold Window
rule: folding/bi-fold window must have a locking mechanism that prevents unintended folding or sliding when in closed or partially-open position
conditions: window is installed in any location accessible to occupants

subject: Folding / Bi-Fold Window
rule: folding/bi-fold window must not be installed in a location where the folded stack of panels blocks a required egress path when fully opened
conditions: the opening serves as or is adjacent to a required means of egress
exceptions: alternative egress path of equal or greater width is maintained

subject: Folding / Bi-Fold Window
rule: folding/bi-fold window must have a structural support system capable of carrying the full dead load of all panels plus specified live loads (wind, snow if sloped) without deflection exceeding manufacturer tolerance

subject: Tilt-and-Turn Window
rule: tilt-and-turn window must have a functional locking mechanism that secures both tilt and turn positions

subject: Tilt-and-Turn Window
rule: tilt-and-turn window must have hinges capable of supporting the sash weight in both tilt and turn orientations

subject: Tilt-and-Turn Window
rule: tilt-and-turn window must have a handle that transitions between operating modes without obstruction from the frame or surrounding structure

subject: Tilt-and-Turn Window
rule: tilt-and-turn window must not have the tilt axis positioned such that the sash strikes adjacent building elements when opening inward
conditions: when the window opens inward into an occupied space
exceptions: when sufficient clear zone is designed around the inward swing path

subject: Window Frame Assembly
rule: window frame assembly must be sealed between the frame and the rough opening to prevent air and water infiltration
conditions: window frame is installed in an exterior wall
window frame is exposed to exterior environment

subject: Window Frame Assembly
rule: window frame assembly must be anchored to the building structure with sufficient structural connections to resist wind loads
conditions: window frame is load-bearing or installed in an area subject to wind loading

subject: Window Frame Assembly
rule: window frame assembly must not create a thermal bridge that bypasses the insulation layer
conditions: window frame is installed in a thermally insulated wall assembly
exceptions: thermally broken frame designs that incorporate insulating material between interior and exterior metal components

subject: Window Frame Assembly
rule: window frame assembly must accommodate differential movement between the frame material and the surrounding wall structure
conditions: frame material has a coefficient of thermal expansion different from adjacent wall materials
frame spans multiple stories or long wall segments

subject: Window Frame Assembly
rule: window frame assembly must be installed with proper flashing at the head, sill, and jambs to direct water away from the interior
conditions: window frame is installed in an exterior wall above grade

subject: Operable Glazing Panel (Sash)
rule: an operable glazing panel (sash) must have at least one axis of rotation or translation to enable opening

subject: Operable Glazing Panel (Sash)
rule: an operable glazing panel (sash) must not have its entire perimeter fixed in place

subject: Operable Glazing Panel (Sash)
rule: an operable glazing panel (sash) must maintain a clearance gap around its moving edges to prevent binding

subject: Window Hinge and Hardware Set
rule: hinge pins and fasteners must be secured against loosening under cyclic operation
conditions: assembly includes removable pins or threaded fasteners

subject: Window Hinge and Hardware Set
rule: hinge material must not corrode when exposed to typical indoor humidity and occasional window condensation
conditions: window is installed in a habitable building interior
exceptions: windows in conditioned spaces with active dehumidification and no condensation history

subject: Window Hinge and Hardware Set
rule: screws or mounting hardware must engage the window frame material with sufficient pull-out resistance to support sash weight
conditions: hardware set includes screws for attachment to the window frame

subject: Window Operator / Crank Mechanism
rule: window operator/crank mechanism must have a mechanical connection (spindle or gear interface) that is compatible with the window sash it operates
conditions: when used as the actuation device for an operable window
exceptions: non-operable fixed windows

subject: Window Operator / Crank Mechanism
rule: window operator/crank mechanism must not have exposed sharp edges or pinch points in the normal operating zone of the handle
conditions: when the window is accessible to occupants

subject: Window Operator / Crank Mechanism
rule: window operator/crank mechanism must be rigidly attached to the window frame or sash such that it cannot detach under its own weight or normal operating force
exceptions: purposefully detachable mechanisms where the detachment is a designed feature (e.g., removable crank stored separately)

subject: Window Balance System
rule: window balance system must provide sufficient counterbalancing force to hold the sash stationary at any position within its travel range
conditions: window is a vertical or horizontal sliding sash window

subject: Window Balance System
rule: window balance system must not fail catastrophically (sudden loss of all tension)

subject: Window Balance System
rule: window balance system must fit within the available jamb channel depth and width without interfering with other components
conditions: window is of standard residential or commercial construction with defined jamb pocket dimensions

subject: Door Leaf (Solid Core with Glass Panel)
rule: door leaf must have a solid core that provides at least the minimum required fire rating for the assembly
conditions: when used in fire-rated assembly
when required by building code for occupancy
exceptions: when the glass panel exceeds the maximum allowable percentage for fire rating, in which case the entire assembly must be tested as a fire-rated glazing system

subject: Door Leaf (Solid Core with Glass Panel)
rule: glass panel must be safety-glazed (tempered or laminated) when located in a hazardous location
conditions: when the glass panel is within 60 inches of a floor
when the glass panel is within 24 inches of a door opening edge
when the door is in a commercial or public occupancy

subject: Door Leaf (Solid Core with Glass Panel)
rule: door leaf must not warp or sag under self-weight exceeding permissible deflection limits
conditions: when door leaf height exceeds 8 feet
when door leaf is heavier than standard due to glass panel size
exceptions: when door is reinforced with a steel stiffener channel or equivalent structural reinforcement

subject: Door Leaf (Solid Core with Glass Panel)
rule: glass panel must not create a thermal break that compromises the door's fire-resistance rating
conditions: when door leaf is rated for fire resistance
exceptions: when the glass panel is listed as part of a fire-rated door assembly tested per NFPA 252

subject: Window Opening Area
rule: window opening area must have a net clear opening area of at least 5.7 square feet (0.53 m²) for emergency egress and rescue
conditions: window serves a sleeping room
window serves a habitable room below the fourth story
building is subject to IBC or IRC egress requirements
exceptions: window opening area is at grade level and opens directly to the exterior
window serves a room protected by an automatic sprinkler system where code allows reduction
basement egress windows may use 5.0 sq ft minimum per some code versions

subject: Window Opening Area
rule: window opening area must have a minimum net clear opening height of 24 inches (610 mm)
conditions: window serves an egress-required room
building is subject to IBC or IRC egress requirements
exceptions: window at grade level where alternate means of egress exists

subject: Window Opening Area
rule: window opening area must have a minimum net clear opening width of 20 inches (508 mm)
conditions: window serves an egress-required room
building is subject to IBC or IRC egress requirements
exceptions: window at grade level where alternate means of egress exists

subject: Window Opening Area
rule: window opening area must not be obstructed by security bars, grilles, or screens that cannot be released from the inside without tools or special knowledge
conditions: window serves an egress-required room
security bars or grilles are present
exceptions: bars are equipped with approved quick-release mechanisms operable from inside

subject: Window Opening Area
rule: window opening area must have a sill height no greater than 44 inches (1118 mm) above the floor for emergency escape
conditions: window serves an egress-required room
building is subject to IBC or IRC egress requirements
exceptions: window opening area provides a step or other means to reach the sill
window is on the fourth story or above where egress windows are not required

subject: Door Frame (with Glazing Rebates)
rule: Door frame with glazing rebates must have a full perimeter seal between frame and wall opening to prevent air and water infiltration
conditions: frame installed in exterior wall
frame exposed to weather
exceptions: interior non-load-bearing partition applications where no weather barrier is required

subject: Door Frame (with Glazing Rebates)
rule: Glazing rebates must provide a minimum rebate depth sufficient to retain glazing unit under design wind load without mechanical fasteners pulling through
conditions: frame contains glass or infill panel
exceptions: frameless or structurally glazed systems where rebate is not the primary retention mechanism

subject: Door Frame (with Glazing Rebates)
rule: Door frame must not have sharp edges or burrs on glazing rebate surfaces that contact the glazing material
conditions: frame is fabricated from metal or rigid material
exceptions: surfaces that will be fully covered by a continuous protective gasket or tape before glazing installation

subject: Glass Panel/Glazing Insert
rule: glass panel/glazing insert must be structurally supported by a frame or substructure capable of bearing its weight and wind loads
conditions: when used as a vertical or overhead building enclosure element

subject: Glass Panel/Glazing Insert
rule: glass panel/glazing insert must not experience direct hard contact with dissimilar rigid materials without a resilient gasket, spacer, or setting block
conditions: when installed in a frame system

subject: Glass Panel/Glazing Insert
rule: glass panel/glazing insert must have a minimum edge clearance and bite dimension as specified by manufacturer or applicable standard
conditions: when installed in a glazing pocket or frame

subject: Glass Panel/Glazing Insert
rule: glass panel/glazing insert must not be installed in a location where predicted thermal stress exceeds the glass edge strength unless heat-treated glass is used
conditions: when exposed to direct solar radiation with shaded edges or contrasting conditions
exceptions: annealed glass is permitted if finite element analysis confirms thermal stress remains below allowable edge strength

subject: Transom Panel with Glass
rule: transom panel with glass must be structurally supported by a surrounding frame or rough opening
conditions: when installed as part of a door or window assembly

subject: Transom Panel with Glass
rule: glass in a transom panel must not directly contact dissimilar materials (e.g., untreated aluminum or steel) without an isolation layer
conditions: when the frame or adjacent construction is metal
exceptions: when the metal is stainless steel or has a compatible anodized/coated surface specifically rated for glass contact

subject: Transom Panel with Glass
rule: transom panel with glass must be sealed against water infiltration at all perimeter joints
conditions: when the transom is exposed to exterior weather or located above an occupied interior space
exceptions: when the transom is entirely interior and no moisture pathway exists

subject: Sidelight Glazing Panel
rule: sidelight glazing panel must be made of safety glazing material (tempered, laminated, or wired glass)
conditions: the panel is located adjacent to a door
the panel is within 24 inches of the door opening
the panel bottom is less than 60 inches above the floor or walking surface
exceptions: the panel is a decorative glass with a permanent intervening barrier that complies with safety glazing requirements

subject: Sidelight Glazing Panel
rule: sidelight glazing panel must not have a fully openable sash that reduces the clear opening width below the required egress minimum
conditions: the sidelight panel is operable (not fixed)
the sidelight is part of or immediately adjacent to a door assembly serving a dwelling unit or sleeping room
exceptions: the adjacent door itself provides the required egress opening without relying on the sidelight

subject: Sidelight Glazing Panel
rule: sidelight glazing panel must resist the design wind load for its location
conditions: the panel forms part of the building envelope
exceptions: the panel is entirely protected by a storm-rated exterior screen or shutter that independently meets wind load requirements

subject: Sidelight Glazing Panel
rule: sidelight glazing panel must not block the required area of vision from the door itself
conditions: the door requires a vision panel per building code (e.g., in certain egress corridors or hazardous locations)
exceptions: the door's required vision area is fully provided by a transom or separate vision panel not obstructed by the sidelight

subject: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
rule: door closer must be compatible with door weight and size as specified by manufacturer
conditions: door closer is surface-mounted
door closer is concealed

subject: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
rule: door closer must not be installed on fire-rated door assembly without UL/certified listing for that specific fire-rated assembly
conditions: door is fire-rated
exceptions: if the closer has been tested and listed as part of the fire door assembly per NFPA 80

subject: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
rule: door closer must be mounted in a position that allows full door swing without interference from adjacent walls, frames, or equipment

subject: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
rule: door closer must have the backcheck feature engaged to prevent door from slamming into adjacent walls or stops
conditions: door is in a high-traffic area
exceptions: if building code or occupancy type specifically exempts backcheck requirement

subject: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
rule: door closer sweep speed and latch speed must be adjustable and set to comply with ADA/proximity requirements for closing time
conditions: door serves an accessible route or is in a building subject to ADA or equivalent accessibility code

subject: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
rule: key must be insertable into and removable from the key cylinder
conditions: key-operated lock/latch set

subject: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
rule: latch bolt or deadbolt must retract when the key cylinder is turned (or knobs/levers are actuated) and extend when released

subject: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
rule: key cylinder must be securely fixed to the lock body such that it cannot detach under normal operating torque

subject: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
rule: moving components (latch bolt, deadbolt, cylinder plug, springs) must not bind or seize within the operating temperature and environment range

subject: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
rule: key cylinder must prevent operation of the locking mechanism when an incorrect key is inserted

subject: Door Handle/Pull (Back-to-Back)
rule: back-to-back door handles/pulls must be mechanically interlinked or synchronized so that operating one handle moves the other identically
conditions: door handle/pull is installed as a back-to-back pair on both sides of a door

subject: Door Handle/Pull (Back-to-Back)
rule: back-to-back door handles/pulls must not protrude beyond the door edge in a way that prevents the door from swinging freely
conditions: door is hinged and swings through a framed opening

subject: Door Handle/Pull (Back-to-Back)
rule: back-to-back door handles/pulls must have a common axis of rotation that is perpendicular to the door face
conditions: the pair uses a pivoting or lever action mechanism

subject: Door Handle/Pull (Back-to-Back)
rule: the mounting fastener through the door must not create a thermal bridge that causes condensation on interior surfaces under expected climate conditions
conditions: door separates conditioned interior space from exterior environment
door is in a climate where interior/exterior temperature differential exceeds 15°C

subject: Kick Plate (Metal or Plastic)
rule: kick plate must be installed at the bottom of a door to cover the gap between the door and the floor or threshold
conditions: when used as a door bottom component

subject: Kick Plate (Metal or Plastic)
rule: kick plate must be securely fastened to prevent detachment during normal door operation

subject: Kick Plate (Metal or Plastic)
rule: kick plate must not obstruct the operation of the door (swing, latch, or closer)

subject: Kick Plate (Metal or Plastic)
rule: kick plate must be made of a material (metal or plastic) that can withstand repeated impact from foot traffic without cracking or breaking

subject: Light Shelf
rule: light shelf must have a minimum width to provide meaningful shading
conditions: when used for shading

subject: Light Shelf
rule: light shelf must have a reflective top surface
conditions: when intended to redirect daylight into interior

subject: Light Shelf
rule: light shelf must be positioned above eye level of occupants
conditions: when installed in occupied spaces with windows

subject: Light Shelf
rule: light shelf must not obstruct required egress or fire safety sightlines
conditions: when mounted near exit paths or fire-rated glazing

subject: Light Tube / Solar Tube
rule: light tube / solar tube must have a continuous unobstructed path from roof aperture to ceiling aperture
conditions: when functioning as a daylighting device
exceptions: when tube is intentionally blocked for light control (e.g., with a dimming valve)

subject: Light Tube / Solar Tube
rule: light tube / solar tube must have a weather-tight seal at all roof penetrations
conditions: when penetrating a roof assembly

subject: Light Tube / Solar Tube
rule: light tube / solar tube must maintain a minimum clearance from combustible materials where required by fire code
conditions: when passing through fire-rated assemblies or through attic/plenum spaces
exceptions: when tube assembly is listed with a fire-resistance rating that matches the rating of the penetrated assembly

subject: Diffusing Glazing
rule: Diffusing glazing must be installed with the textured/diffusing side oriented toward the interior occupied space
conditions: When used in vision glazing applications
When the glazing has a single-sided texture or coating
exceptions: When the diffusing property is integral throughout the material thickness rather than surface-applied

subject: Diffusing Glazing
rule: Diffusing glazing must not be used in fire-rated assemblies unless specifically listed and tested as a fire-resistive glazing material
conditions: When the building code requires a fire-resistance rating for the opening
exceptions: When the diffusing glazing product carries a valid fire-rating listing per ASTM E119 or NFPA 252

subject: Diffusing Glazing
rule: Diffusing glazing exposed to direct solar radiation must be tempered or heat-strengthened to resist thermal stress fracture
conditions: When the glazing receives direct sunlight
When the glass area exceeds approximately 1 m²
exceptions: When the glazing is fully shaded or in a north-facing orientation in the northern hemisphere with no reflected solar gain

subject: Light-Directing Louvers
rule: Light-directing louvers must maintain a minimum angle relative to horizontal to prevent water pooling
conditions: Installed outdoors
exceptions: Installed under a weather-protected overhang or inside a sealed double-glazed unit

subject: Light-Directing Louvers
rule: Light-directing louvers must not block required egress or emergency ventilation openings
conditions: Installed in or adjacent to a window or façade opening that serves as an emergency egress or smoke vent
exceptions: Louvers are designed to automatically retract/fold away during egress or smoke events

subject: Light-Directing Louvers
rule: Light-directing louver pivot or adjustment mechanism must have a positive locking feature under wind load
conditions: Louvers are adjustable/movable
Installed in a location subject to wind loads
exceptions: Louvers are fixed/non-adjustable and designed as static elements

subject: Light-Directing Louvers
rule: Light-directing louvers must not shed concentrated glare or focused reflected light onto adjacent occupied buildings or pedestrian areas
conditions: Louvers have a reflective or specular surface finish
Adjacent properties or public rights-of-way exist within the potential reflection zone

subject: Prismatic Skylight
rule: skylight glazing must be constructed from laminated or tempered safety glass
conditions: when located in occupiable spaces
when located above walking surfaces
exceptions: when protected by a wire mesh or safety screen below the glazing

subject: Prismatic Skylight
rule: skylight must have a minimum slope for condensation runoff and drainage
conditions: when installed on a roof with a slope less than the manufacturer's minimum

subject: Prismatic Skylight
rule: prismatic skylight must not be installed in locations subject to wind-borne debris impact in hurricane-prone regions unless impact-rated
conditions: in hurricane-prone regions per building code definitions
exceptions: when the skylight has passed missile impact testing per applicable standards

subject: Prismatic Skylight
rule: skylight must have a thermal break between interior and exterior components
conditions: when installed in cold climates with average January temperature below 4Â°C

subject: Light Well / Atrium
rule: Light well / atrium must provide a means of natural ventilation or mechanical smoke extraction at the top
conditions: atrium serves as smoke reservoir
atrium connects more than two floors
exceptions: atrium is fully enclosed with fire-rated glazing and separate dedicated smoke control system is provided

subject: Light Well / Atrium
rule: Light well / atrium must have a minimum clear opening area at the top for natural ventilation
conditions: light well is enclosed on all sides
light well serves occupied spaces
exceptions: mechanical ventilation system is provided to all adjacent occupied spaces

subject: Light Well / Atrium
rule: Light well must not have a horizontal dimension smaller than its depth (aspect ratio constraint)
conditions: light well provides the sole source of daylight to occupied spaces
exceptions: artificial daylighting or light-redirecting systems are installed

subject: Light Well / Atrium
rule: Atrium floor must be accessible to fire brigade vehicles or have firefighting shafts within travel distance
conditions: atrium floor area exceeds 200 m²
building is sprinklered
exceptions: alternative firefighting access is provided per local code

subject: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly
rule: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly must be capable of supporting the full dead load of the lightshelf plus any anticipated live loads (e.g., snow accumulation if exterior, or maintenance loads)

subject: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly
rule: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly must be securely attached to the primary building structure (e.g., slab edge, spandrel beam, or curtain wall mullion) with fasteners rated for the applied loads

subject: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly
rule: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly must not have sharp edges or protrusions that could cause injury to occupants or maintenance personnel in accessible locations
conditions: when located within reachable zone of occupied spaces or maintenance catwalks

subject: Light-Redirecting Film
rule: Light-redirecting film must have a thickness sufficient to maintain structural integrity during handling and installation
exceptions: When the film is factory-bonded to a rigid substrate prior to transport

subject: Light-Redirecting Film
rule: Light-redirecting film must not contain materials that undergo irreversible photodegradation under expected solar exposure within the design life
conditions: When used in exterior applications or within 3 m of a glazed aperture
exceptions: When explicitly designed as a sacrificial layer with scheduled replacement

subject: Light-Redirecting Film
rule: Light-redirecting film must have an adhesion system (adhesive layer or mechanical attachment) capable of resisting gravity and thermal cycling without delamination
conditions: When applied to a vertical or overhead surface
exceptions: When the film is captured in a framed assembly that provides mechanical retention on all edges

subject: Light-Redirecting Film
rule: Light-redirecting film must not create a focused hot spot that exceeds the ignition temperature of adjacent combustible materials
conditions: When the film has lens-like prismatic or Fresnel microstructure and is used in direct sunlight

subject: Light-Redirecting Film
rule: Light-redirecting film must have a coefficient of thermal expansion compatible with the substrate to which it is bonded, within the expected temperature range
conditions: When permanently bonded to a substrate with a different CTE
exceptions: When the bond line is sufficiently elastic to accommodate differential strain without delamination or film buckling

subject: Window pane with small-divided lights
rule: Window pane with small-divided lights must have individual panes small enough that the total unsupported glass area per pane does not exceed the structural capacity of the glass thickness used
conditions: glass is annealed or standard float glass
pane is vertical or near-vertical
exceptions: laminated glass is used
tempered glass is used
glass thickness is increased to compensate

subject: Window pane with small-divided lights
rule: Window pane with small-divided lights must not have individual light dimensions so narrow that a standard glazing putty or seal cannot be properly applied between the pane and the frame
conditions: traditional wet-glazing (putty) method is used
exceptions: pre-sealed insulating glass units (IGUs) or structural glazing tape is used instead

subject: Window pane with small-divided lights
rule: Window pane with small-divided lights must have each individual pane thick enough to resist handling and cleaning forces without cracking
conditions: pane is accessible for manual cleaning from inside or outside
exceptions: pane is protected by an exterior grille or secondary glazing

subject: Muntin/grille bar
rule: Muntin/grille bar spacing must be compatible with the window's structural grid and mullion layout
conditions: when used in window or door assemblies with structural framing

subject: Muntin/grille bar
rule: Muntin/grille bar must not obstruct the intended operation (opening, tilting, sliding) of the window or door sash
conditions: when applied to operable windows or doors

subject: True divided light (TDL) sash
rule: True divided light (TDL) sash must have individual muntins that separate each lite of glass

subject: True divided light (TDL) sash
rule: TDL sash must accommodate thermal expansion and contraction of individual glass lites within each opening
conditions: when the sash is installed in a facade exposed to exterior temperature variation

subject: True divided light (TDL) sash
rule: TDL sash must not have muntin profiles that obstruct the operable function of the sash (e.g., swing, tilt, or slide)
conditions: when the sash is operable rather than fixed

subject: Small-pane interior transom window
rule: Small-pane interior transom window must have glass panes (or a transparent/translucent material) to function as a transom window
exceptions: Serving as a purely decorative/fixed panel where opacity is intentional

subject: Small-pane interior transom window
rule: Small-pane interior transom window must be installed above a door opening

subject: Small-pane interior transom window
rule: Small-pane interior transom window must not have individual pane dimensions that exceed the structural capacity of the muntin/mullion grid
conditions: When the window is part of an operable assembly (e.g., hinged or fixed frame)

subject: Simulated divided light (SDL) sash
rule: SDL sash must maintain thermal break continuity between interior and exterior metal components
conditions: when sash contains both interior and exterior metal elements
when used in thermally insulated glazing assemblies
exceptions: when sash is entirely non-metallic (e.g., all-fiberglass or all-vinyl construction)

subject: Simulated divided light (SDL) sash
rule: SDL sash must not have rigid grid bars that bridge the insulating glass cavity from the interior to the exterior glass surface
conditions: when SDL grids are applied as internal (between-pane) rather than external (surface-applied)
exceptions: when the grid bars incorporate a thermal break isolating interior and exterior glass temperatures

subject: Simulated divided light (SDL) sash
rule: SDL sash must accommodate differential thermal expansion between the simulated grid material and the glass or frame
conditions: when sash is exposed to exterior environmental temperature cycling
when grid material has a coefficient of thermal expansion differing from glass by more than 20%

subject: Simulated divided light (SDL) sash
rule: SDL sash must have weather seals that accommodate the additional thickness of the simulated grid applied to the glass surface
conditions: when SDL grids are surface-applied (externally bonded to glass)
exceptions: when grids are installed only on the interior face
when sash design accounts for the added thickness in the glazing channel and seal compression specifications

subject: Small-pane double-hung window assembly
rule: Small-pane double-hung window assembly must have at least one moveable sash that slides vertically within the frame

subject: Small-pane double-hung window assembly
rule: Small-pane double-hung window assembly must have individual panes (lights) separated by muntins that are structurally compatible with the sash frame
conditions: when described as 'small-pane'

subject: Small-pane double-hung window assembly
rule: Small-pane double-hung window assembly must_not have a single fixed pane of glass occupying the entire sash opening
conditions: when described as 'small-pane'

subject: Small-pane double-hung window assembly
rule: Small-pane double-hung window assembly must have a weatherseal between the meeting rails of upper and lower sashes when closed

subject: Small-pane casement window assembly
rule: Small-pane casement window assembly must have a weatherstripped or sealed perimeter between the frame and the wall opening
conditions: when installed in an exterior wall assembly

subject: Small-pane casement window assembly
rule: Small-pane casement window assembly must not have the hinge side positioned such that the opening sash swings inward when the window is fully opened in a location where the sash would block a required egress or passage
conditions: when the window is designated for emergency egress or located in a means of egress path
exceptions: provided that the sash can be fully released and removed, or the opening is not required for egress

subject: Small-pane casement window assembly
rule: Small-pane casement window assembly must have its operable sash secured with a locking mechanism that engages a keeper on the opposite jamb when closed
conditions: when installed in a location accessible from grade or from a balcony, porch, or fire escape
exceptions: when installed above 12 feet from the exterior grade or accessible surface

subject: Small-pane casement window assembly
rule: Small-pane casement window assembly must have glass panes (lights) sized and supported such that each individual pane does not exceed the manufacturer's rated wind-load capacity for the given exposure category
conditions: when installed in a building with a mean roof height over 30 feet or in a wind-exposure category B, C, or D
exceptions: when the assembly is located on a protected interior courtyard with negligible wind exposure

subject: Small-pane window sash
rule: small-pane window sash must be structurally attached to the window frame
conditions: when installed in a building opening

subject: Small-pane window sash
rule: small-pane window sash must not have glass panes that exceed the structural capacity of the muntins or sash frame
conditions: when glazed with glass

subject: Small-pane window sash
rule: small-pane window sash must have an operable or fixed configuration that maintains a weather seal when closed
conditions: when used in an exterior wall

subject: Small-pane fixed window assembly
rule: Small-pane fixed window assembly must be installed in an opening framed to match its exact dimensions
conditions: When installed in a wall or roof opening

subject: Small-pane fixed window assembly
rule: Small-pane fixed window assembly must have its panes rigidly supported within the frame to prevent glass breakage under wind load
conditions: When exposed to exterior wind loads

subject: Small-pane fixed window assembly
rule: Small-pane fixed window assembly must not have adjacent panes contacting each other without an intervening sealant or gasket
conditions: When mullions or muntins separate the panes

subject: Small-pane fixed window assembly
rule: Small-pane fixed window assembly must be weather-sealed at all perimeter joints between frame and surrounding wall/roof construction
conditions: When installed as an exterior building enclosure element

subject: Small-pane fixed window assembly
rule: Small-pane fixed window assembly must not have glass panes thinner than the minimum required for the given span and design wind pressure
conditions: Per applicable building code and structural design requirements

subject: Small-pane window frame
rule: window frame must accommodate the thickness of small-pane glass within its rebate
conditions: window frame is designed for small-pane glazing

subject: Small-pane window frame
rule: small-pane window frame must have sufficient muntin bars or glazing bars to separate individual panes
conditions: frame is divided into multiple lites
exceptions: single-pane configuration where a single sheet of glass fills the entire sash

subject: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead
rule: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead must remain flexible enough to accommodate differential thermal expansion between glass and frame without cracking
conditions: when used in exterior applications
when spanning multiple small panes in a single frame

subject: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead
rule: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead must not be applied over painted or oily surfaces without proper preparation
conditions: at time of initial installation
during reglazing
exceptions: when the paint is a specifically compatible primer designed for glazing compound adhesion

subject: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead
rule: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead must be back-bedded (bedded against a sealant or putty bed) on the interior side of the glass
conditions: in windows with traditional wood sash
when the putty serves as the primary weather seal
exceptions: when a separate interior glazing tape or gasket system is used as the primary seal

subject: Trim Fasteners
rule: Trim fasteners must have a head configuration compatible with the intended driving tool (e.g., Phillips, Torx, hex, or slotted)
conditions: when used with power tools or hand tools for installation

subject: Trim Fasteners
rule: Trim fasteners must not have a head diameter that exceeds the trim member's exposed face width or bearing surface
conditions: when the fastener head is intended to be visible or flush on the finished surface

subject: Mullion for small-pane window grouping
rule: Mullions must be load-bearing to support the combined weight of the small-pane window grouping and transfer it to the surrounding frame or structure
conditions: When mullions serve as structural vertical members within a window grouping
exceptions: When the window grouping is non-operable/decorative and fully supported by a separate structural frame (e.g., applied as a skin)

subject: Mullion for small-pane window grouping
rule: Mullion depth must accommodate the small-pane rebate or glazing stop depth to securely hold each pane
conditions: When mullions are designed with rebates or stops for individual small panes

subject: Mullion for small-pane window grouping
rule: Mullion must not thermally bridge between interior and exterior beyond acceptable limits for the given climate zone
conditions: In conditioned buildings where thermal performance is required
exceptions: In unconditioned buildings or purely decorative interior partitions

subject: Mullion for small-pane window grouping
rule: Mullion spacing must be less than the maximum unsupported span of the small panes under design wind load
conditions: When mullions are used to subdivide a larger opening into smaller panes

subject: Coped Joint
rule: coped joint must have a minimum contact area between the two coped members
conditions: the joint is load-bearing
the joint transfers shear or compression forces

subject: Coped Joint
rule: coped joint must not have abrupt re-entrant corners without a smooth transition radius
conditions: the cope is flame-cut or mechanically cut
exceptions: when the cope is punched or machined with an integrated radius per fabrication standard

subject: Coped Joint
rule: coped joint must have sufficient net section at the cope to resist the design shear force
conditions: the coped beam is subject to shear at the connection

subject: Mitered Corner
rule: When a mitered corner is used in an exterior application, the joint must be sealed against water intrusion
conditions: exterior application
exposed to weather
exceptions: interior-only applications with no moisture exposure

subject: Mitered Corner
rule: Mitered corner joint faces must have full, continuous contact along the entire miter cut surface
conditions: load-bearing application
structural joint
exceptions: purely decorative non-structural trim

subject: Mitered Corner
rule: Mitered corner must not have acute angles that leave insufficient material thickness at the tip for structural integrity
conditions: material is wood or other friable material
joint bears load
exceptions: material is metal with welded reinforcement at the tip

subject: Casing Trim (Half-inch)
rule: Casing Trim (Half-inch) must be installed with proper fasteners to remain mechanically attached under design loads
conditions: when used as part of the building enclosure

subject: Casing Trim (Half-inch)
rule: Casing Trim (Half-inch) must not obstruct the drainage plane behind the cladding
conditions: when installed around windows, doors, or other wall penetrations

subject: Shoe Molding (Half-inch)
rule: Shoe molding (half-inch) must be installed at the intersection of the wall and floor to cover the expansion gap left for flooring
conditions: when used in flooring/baseboard transition

subject: Shoe Molding (Half-inch)
rule: Shoe molding (half-inch) must not be installed in locations where the gap between baseboard and flooring is significantly larger than 1/2 inch
conditions: when gap exceeds the molding's coverage capacity

subject: Scarf Joint
rule: A scarf joint must be cut so that the mating surfaces overlap fully along the intended bond line

subject: Scarf Joint
rule: The inclined faces of a scarf joint must not exceed a slope ratio that would cause the joint to slip under design loads
conditions: When the joint is subjected to axial or bending loads
exceptions: When mechanical fasteners or supplementary shear keys are provided to resist slip

subject: Scarf Joint
rule: A scarf joint must have a length-to-thickness ratio (scarf ratio) appropriate for the materials being joined
conditions: For structural load-bearing applications

subject: Stadium Bench Seating
rule: bench seating must have a minimum tread depth (seat depth) of at least 300 mm (12 in) to provide adequate foot and leg support for spectators
conditions: fixed bench seating for spectator use

subject: Stadium Bench Seating
rule: bench seating riser height (vertical distance between rows) must not exceed 400 mm (16 in) to prevent fall hazards and ensure safe egress
conditions: multi-tiered bench seating rows

subject: Stadium Bench Seating
rule: bench seating must have a minimum clear aisle width of at least 300 mm (12 in) between seat rows for passage and emergency evacuation
conditions: fixed bench seating with multiple rows

subject: Stadium Bench Seating
rule: bench seating must be secured against overturning under a lateral live load of at least 730 N/m (50 lb/ft) applied to the seat
conditions: freestanding or non-structurally-integrated bench seating

subject: Stadium Bench Seating
rule: bench seating must not have sharp edges, corners, or protrusions on surfaces that contact spectators

subject: Bleacher System
rule: bleacher seating surface must have a lateral load path capable of transferring spectator-induced horizontal forces to the structure or ground
conditions: when bleachers are occupied by spectators
when bleachers are installed in seismic zones

subject: Bleacher System
rule: every seat or standing row in a bleacher system must provide a means of egress that meets minimum clear width and travel distance requirements
conditions: when bleacher seating capacity exceeds 50 persons

subject: Bleacher System
rule: bleacher components must not have openings or gaps that allow a 4-inch sphere to pass through between 0 and 15 inches above the seat surface
conditions: when bleachers serve children under 5 years old
when bleachers are in schools or daycare facilities

subject: Bleacher System
rule: bleacher system must have a positive locking mechanism that prevents unintended folding, collapsing, or telescoping
conditions: when bleacher system is a telescoping or folding type

subject: Bleacher System
rule: the vertical load on any bleacher foot or support point must not exceed the load-bearing capacity of the supporting soil or floor slab

subject: Seat Row Spacing Tread
rule: seat row spacing tread (riser) must have a minimum depth of 300 mm (12 inches) for occupiable seating rows to allow safe egress and passage
conditions: when used in occupiable seating areas such as theaters, stadiums, or lecture halls
exceptions: bleacher-style telescopic seating where treads fold or retract

subject: Seat Row Spacing Tread
rule: seat row spacing tread must not have a vertical riser height exceeding 430 mm (17 inches) between successive rows
conditions: where seating rows are stepped or tiered

subject: Seat Numbering & Wayfinding Plate
rule: seat numbering must be legible and readable from the intended viewing distance and angle
conditions: when installed in a venue
when used for occupant wayfinding

subject: Seat Numbering & Wayfinding Plate
rule: seat numbering must be durably marked so that it remains legible over the expected service life under cleaning, wear, and environmental exposure
conditions: when installed in a public or commercial venue

subject: Seat Numbering & Wayfinding Plate
rule: seat numbering plate dimensions must not obstruct emergency egress paths or create tripping/snagging hazards
conditions: when mounted on seating
when mounted adjacent to aisles or paths of travel

subject: Seat Numbering & Wayfinding Plate
rule: seat numbering must provide sufficient visual contrast (luminance contrast or color contrast) against its mounting surface
conditions: when required by accessibility codes (e.g., ADA, EN 17210)

subject: Fold-down Seat Mechanism
rule: fold-down seat mechanism must lock securely in both deployed and stowed positions
conditions: seat is designed for occupant use

subject: Fold-down Seat Mechanism
rule: fold-down seat mechanism must not pinch or shear body parts during folding operation

subject: Fold-down Seat Mechanism
rule: fold-down seat mechanism must withstand static and dynamic loads specified by applicable safety regulations without detachment
conditions: seat is intended for occupant seating during vehicle operation

subject: Fold-down Seat Mechanism
rule: fold-down seat mechanism must have a manual release that is accessible and operable without tools
conditions: mechanism includes a release to fold or stow the seat
exceptions: power-operated mechanisms that provide an emergency manual override

subject: Bench Backrest
rule: bench backrest must be rigidly attached to the bench seat or frame
conditions: backrest is present on a freestanding bench
exceptions: backrest is integrated as a single molded piece with the seat

subject: Bench Backrest
rule: bench backrest must not have sharp edges or protrusions in the occupant contact zone
conditions: bench is intended for public or commercial use
backrest has a defined occupant-facing surface
exceptions: sharp edges are intentionally designed as a theft-deterrent feature in a non-occupant-accessible context

subject: Bench Backrest
rule: bench backrest must have a minimum structural capacity to resist a backward horizontal load of at least 75 lb (334 N) without permanent deformation
conditions: backrest is designed for adult human use
exceptions: backrest is purely decorative and explicitly marked 'do not sit or lean'

subject: Bench Backrest
rule: bench backrest must not have gaps between 4 inches and 8 inches (100–200 mm) in the area behind the seated occupant's torso
conditions: bench is accessible to children
backrest has horizontal or vertical rails/balusters
exceptions: gap is at the very top of the backrest above 30 inches (760 mm) from the seat surface

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat must have a structural frame or base capable of supporting expected static and dynamic loads

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat must have a minimum seat height from ground that allows safe seated posture (typically 400-500 mm)

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat must not have sharp edges or corners on user-contact surfaces
exceptions: decorative/artistic bench seats explicitly designed with intentional sharp geometry where user contact is not intended or is at minimal/supervised use only

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat must not have a slatted or perforated top surface gap larger than limb-entrapment threshold (typically > 100 mm for body, or > 12 mm for fingers in child-accessible settings)
conditions: when bench seat is located in publicly accessible area or where children may use it unaccompanied

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat must be anchored or weighted sufficiently to resist overturning under lateral load (e.g., wind, leaning, climbing) in outdoor or public settings
conditions: when bench seat is intended for outdoor or public unsecured installation
exceptions: lightweight portable benches not intended to remain in place under lateral forces are exempt

subject: Bench Seat
rule: bench seat materials must be weather-resistant or treated when installed outdoors
conditions: when bench seat is installed outdoors or in exposed exterior conditions

subject: Bench Leg/Base Anchors
rule: Bench leg/base anchors must be secured to a stable, load-bearing surface capable of supporting the bench's design load
conditions: Anchor is installed as part of the bench assembly
Bench is intended for use/occupancy
exceptions: Freestanding bench designs that rely on gravity and surface friction without mechanical anchors

subject: Bench Leg/Base Anchors
rule: Anchor bolts or fasteners must have corrosion resistance appropriate for the intended environment
conditions: Anchor is exposed to outdoor weather or moisture
Anchor is metallic
exceptions: Indoor, climate-controlled settings with no moisture exposure
Non-metallic anchors (e.g., polymer) with adequate environmental durability

subject: Bench Leg/Base Anchors
rule: Anchor embedment depth must be sufficient to develop the full tensile capacity of the fastener without pullout failure
conditions: Anchors are embedded in concrete, masonry, or similar foundation material
exceptions: Through-bolt connections where a nut and washer provide clamping independent of embedment depth

subject: Freestanding Entry Bench
rule: bench must have a minimum width of at least 18 inches (457 mm) to provide stable seating
conditions: designed for seated use by adults

subject: Freestanding Entry Bench
rule: bench seat height must be between 16 and 19 inches (406–483 mm) from the ground
conditions: designed for seated use by adults

subject: Freestanding Entry Bench
rule: bench must not tip forward or backward when a person sits on the front edge

subject: Freestanding Entry Bench
rule: bench must support a minimum live load of 300 lbs (136 kg) concentrated in the center without collapse
conditions: designed for human occupation

subject: Bench-Floor Interface Trim
rule: Bench-floor interface trim must be compatible with the thermal expansion rates of both the bench material and the floor material to prevent buckling or gap formation
conditions: The bench and floor are made of different materials
The installation spans a temperature range of more than 20°C

subject: Bench-Floor Interface Trim
rule: The trim must not create a trip hazard exceeding the maximum allowable height differential specified in accessibility codes
conditions: The trim is installed in a pedestrian walkway or accessible route
The vertical step between bench and floor is less than the trim height
exceptions: Areas not accessible to the public or not subject to accessibility codes

subject: Bench-Floor Interface Trim
rule: Bench-floor interface trim must be securely fastened to prevent detachment or loosening under expected loads

subject: Bench Top Finish
rule: Bench Top Finish must be chemically resistant to acids, solvents, and reagents used in the laboratory or workspace environment
conditions: When the bench top is installed in a laboratory or workshop where chemicals are handled
exceptions: When the top is strictly used for non-chemical tasks such as computer workstations or dry assembly

subject: Bench Top Finish
rule: Bench Top Finish must be non-absorbent and impervious to liquids
conditions: When the bench top is in a wet lab, kitchen, or any area subject to liquid spills
exceptions: When the finish is explicitly a sacrificial or replaceable surface layer not relied upon as the primary liquid barrier

subject: Bench Top Finish
rule: Bench Top Finish must not produce ignitable dust or flammable vapors under normal use or abrasion
conditions: When the bench is used in an area with ignition sources such as bunsen burners, hot plates, or electrical equipment
exceptions: When the environment is rated and certified as a non-combustible/explosion-proof zone

subject: Bench Top Finish
rule: Bench Top Finish must be smooth and free of cracks, fissures, or surface defects that can trap biological or chemical contaminants
conditions: When the bench top is used in biosafety, pharmaceutical, or sterile processing environments
exceptions: None — this is a fundamental requirement for any cleanable surface in controlled environments

subject: Fire-Rated Bench Assembly
rule: Fire-rated bench assembly must maintain its fire-resistance rating (e.g., ASTM E119 / UL 263) for the rated duration
conditions: when the assembly is part of a fire-resistance-rated wall, floor, or other building element requiring fire separation

subject: Fire-Rated Bench Assembly
rule: Fire-rated bench assembly must not have unprotected penetrations or gaps that bypass the fire-resistive construction
conditions: when the assembly is installed in a fire-resistance-rated location
exceptions: penetrations that are properly firestopped with an approved system maintaining the same fire-resistance rating

subject: Fire-Rated Bench Assembly
rule: Fire-rated bench assembly must be structurally stable under its own weight and expected live loads during a fire exposure

subject: Sitting Wall Bench
rule: Sitting Wall Bench must have a minimum flat seat surface width of at least 300 mm to accommodate a seated person
conditions: bench is intended for sitting use
exceptions: decorative-only benches not intended for occupancy

subject: Sitting Wall Bench
rule: Sitting Wall Bench seat height above finished floor must be between 400 mm and 500 mm
conditions: bench is intended for sitting use by adults
exceptions: benches designed specifically for children or with accessible/universal design alternate heights

subject: Sitting Wall Bench
rule: Sitting Wall Bench must not have sharp corners or edges on the seat surface within the seated occupant zone
conditions: bench is in a location accessible to users

subject: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
rule: Accessible bench clearance zone must have a clear, level ground surface with a maximum slope of 1:50 (2%) in any direction
conditions: bench is intended for wheelchair users or persons with mobility impairments
zone is part of an accessible route
exceptions: site conditions where existing terrain makes achieving 2% slope physically impossible and alternative accessible seating is provided nearby

subject: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
rule: Accessible bench clearance zone must have a minimum clear width of 30 inches (760 mm)
conditions: bench is adjacent to an accessible route
clearance zone is parallel to bench

subject: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
rule: Accessible bench clearance zone must have a minimum clear depth of 48 inches (1220 mm) measured perpendicular from the bench seat
conditions: bench is intended for wheelchair users

subject: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
rule: Accessible bench clearance zone must not overlap with the swing radius of any door
conditions: bench is adjacent to a door
exceptions: doors that are automatic and open away from the bench clearance zone

subject: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
rule: Accessible bench clearance zone must be located such that the ground surface material is stable, firm, and slip-resistant

subject: Sitting Wall Foundation
rule: A sitting wall foundation must have its base at or below the frost line
conditions: In regions with seasonal freezing
exceptions: When foundation is placed on non-frost-susceptible bedrock

subject: Sitting Wall Foundation
rule: A sitting wall foundation must not bear directly on topsoil or organic material

subject: Sitting Wall Foundation
rule: A sitting wall foundation must have a continuous load path transferring vertical wall loads to the ground
conditions: When supporting a load-bearing wall above

subject: Sitting Wall Substructure
rule: Sitting wall substructure must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill with adequate capacity
conditions: When supporting a sitting wall above

subject: Sitting Wall Substructure
rule: Sitting wall substructure must not be placed on expansive clay without mitigation
conditions: When site soil contains expansive clay minerals
exceptions: If soil treatment or deep foundation bypasses the expansive zone

subject: Sitting Wall Substructure
rule: Sitting wall substructure must extend below frost depth
conditions: In regions where frost penetration occurs
exceptions: If the wall is designed as a frost-protected shallow foundation per code

subject: Sitting Wall Substructure
rule: Sitting wall substructure must have positive drainage away from the footing

subject: Sitting Wall Electrical Outlet
rule: sitting wall electrical outlet must be installed with a weather-resistant cover plate (e.g., bubble cover or in-use cover) when located outdoors or in a damp location
conditions: outdoor installation
damp location installation
exceptions: interior dry location only

subject: Sitting Wall Electrical Outlet
rule: sitting wall electrical outlet must have proper grounding (bonded to equipment grounding conductor)

subject: Sitting Wall Electrical Outlet
rule: sitting wall electrical outlet must not be positioned where it can be submerged in standing water (e.g., at grade level in a flood-prone area without elevation)
conditions: location subject to flooding or standing water
exceptions: outlet elevated per code-minimum height or protected by GFCI and listed for wet locations

subject: Sitting Wall Electrical Outlet
rule: sitting wall electrical outlet must be GFCI-protected when installed in bathrooms, kitchens, outdoors, garages, crawl spaces, unfinished basements, or within 6 feet of a sink
conditions: bathroom
kitchen
outdoor
garage
crawl space
unfinished basement
within 6 ft of sink

subject: Retaining Sitting Wall
rule: Retaining sitting wall must have adequate structural reinforcement (e.g., rebar) to resist lateral earth pressure
conditions: Wall retains soil higher than 0.5 m on the retained side
exceptions: Wall is purely decorative and does not retain any soil (i.e., free-standing)

subject: Retaining Sitting Wall
rule: Retaining sitting wall must have a drainage system (weep holes or gravel backfill) to prevent hydrostatic pressure buildup
conditions: Wall retains soil on one side
exceptions: Wall is in continuously dry climate with no water infiltration risk

subject: Retaining Sitting Wall
rule: Retaining sitting wall must not have a height exceeding its base width by more than the soil angle of repose without engineered design
conditions: Wall is retaining soil

subject: Retaining Sitting Wall
rule: Retaining sitting wall must have a minimum seating surface width of 300 mm to safely accommodate a seated person
conditions: Wall is intended for sitting use
exceptions: Wall is explicitly designated as non-sitting (e.g., purely decorative cap)

subject: Terraced Sitting Wall
rule: Terraced sitting wall must have a level top surface for safe sitting
conditions: when used as a seating element

subject: Terraced Sitting Wall
rule: Terraced sitting wall must have adequate structural stability to resist overturning under lateral load
conditions: when freestanding or retaining grade change

subject: Terraced Sitting Wall
rule: Terraced sitting wall must not have sharp edges or protrusions on seating surfaces
conditions: when used as a seating element

subject: Terraced Sitting Wall
rule: Terraced sitting wall step rise must not exceed 200 mm
conditions: when used as stepped seating or access

subject: Freestanding Sitting Wall
rule: Freestanding sitting wall must have a minimum top width sufficient to support the sitting function (typically at least 300 mm / 12 in)
conditions: Wall is intended for sitting use

subject: Freestanding Sitting Wall
rule: Freestanding sitting wall must have a maximum height appropriate for sitting (typically 400–600 mm / 16–24 in)
conditions: Wall is intended for sitting use

subject: Freestanding Sitting Wall
rule: Freestanding sitting wall must be structurally stable under lateral loads (wind, seismic, accidental leaning)

subject: Freestanding Sitting Wall
rule: Freestanding sitting wall must be founded on a base or footing adequate to prevent differential settlement or overturning

subject: Freestanding Sitting Wall
rule: Freestanding sitting wall surface must not have sharp edges or protrusions at sitting height that could cause injury

subject: Canvas Membrane
rule: canvas membrane must be tensioned to remain in place and avoid flutter
conditions: when used as a building envelope or roof

subject: Canvas Membrane
rule: canvas membrane must not be subjected to point loads exceeding its tear strength
conditions: when installed as a structural membrane
exceptions: if reinforced with local patches or secondary structure that distributes the load

subject: Canvas Membrane
rule: canvas membrane must be protected from prolonged direct flame or high heat
conditions: unless treated with fire retardant rated for the application

subject: Canvas Membrane
rule: canvas membrane must have a minimum slope or drainage path to shed water
conditions: when used as a roof or horizontal weather barrier
exceptions: if the membrane is not exposed to precipitation (e.g., fully enclosed interior application)

subject: Mast or Compression Strut
rule: mast or compression strut must be capable of resisting axial compressive loads without buckling
conditions: when used as a compression member
exceptions: members designed purely as tension-only ties

subject: Mast or Compression Strut
rule: mast or compression strut must have adequate end connections to transfer axial force into adjacent structural elements

subject: Mast or Compression Strut
rule: mast or compression strut must not have slenderness ratio exceeding the code-prescribed limit for its material and load case
conditions: when designed per structural building code

subject: Mast or Compression Strut
rule: mast or compression strut must be laterally restrained at intervals sufficient to prevent overall flexural-torsional buckling
conditions: when the strut is long and not continuously braced
exceptions: very short stocky struts where buckling length equals member length

subject: Mast or Compression Strut
rule: mast or compression strut must be fabricated from material with sufficient compressive yield or ultimate strength for the design load

subject: Foundation Anchors (for masts)
rule: foundation anchor embedment depth must reach below the frost line
conditions: mast is installed in a climate with seasonal freezing

subject: Foundation Anchors (for masts)
rule: foundation anchor must not bear directly on uncompacted, undocumented fill material
exceptions: engineered fill placed under controlled compaction and material specifications is acceptable

subject: Foundation Anchors (for masts)
rule: foundation anchor bolt circle must be concentric with the mast base plate within the specified tolerance
conditions: anchor is a bolt-type embedment for a steel mast base plate

subject: Foundation Anchors (for masts)
rule: foundation anchor grout or concrete must achieve minimum specified compressive strength before the mast is erected
conditions: anchor is cast-in-place concrete or grouted into bedrock

subject: Perimeter Ridge or Compression Ring
rule: A perimeter ridge or compression ring must be continuous and form a closed loop around the structure
conditions: Used as a structural perimeter element

subject: Perimeter Ridge or Compression Ring
rule: A compression ring must resist ring compression (hoop) forces without buckling
conditions: Ring is in compression under design loads

subject: Perimeter Ridge or Compression Ring
rule: A perimeter ridge must not have abrupt discontinuities or sharp re-entrant corners in plan
conditions: Element functions as a ridge transferring line loads

subject: Tensioning Turnbuckles and Plates
rule: tensioning turnbuckle and plate assembly must have matched thread engagement between turnbuckle barrel and threaded rods/ends
conditions: when used to connect two threaded rod ends or cables

subject: Tensioning Turnbuckles and Plates
rule: tensioning turnbuckle must not be loaded beyond its rated working load limit
conditions: when in service

subject: Tensioning Turnbuckles and Plates
rule: turnbuckle body and end fittings must be made of compatible materials to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: when installed in exterior or corrosive environment

subject: Tensioning Turnbuckles and Plates
rule: turnbuckle must be locked against unintended rotation after final adjustment
conditions: after final tension adjustment is complete

subject: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
rule: gutters and downpipes must have adequate capacity for the design rainfall intensity of the catchment area
conditions: rainwater collection system is installed
exceptions: building is in an arid region with no rainfall collection requirement
alternative drainage system (e.g., scupper drains, french drains) handles roof runoff without gutters

subject: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
rule: downpipes must discharge to an approved or lawful outlet and must not terminate within a building's foundation zone

subject: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
rule: gutters must slope continuously toward downpipe outlets (minimum fall of approximately 1:200)
conditions: gravity-fed gutter system is used
exceptions: siphonic/syphonic roof drainage system is employed where negative pressure moves water

subject: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
rule: gutter and downpipe materials must be compatible to prevent galvanic corrosion
conditions: dissimilar metals are used for gutter and downpipe components
exceptions: materials are isolated by dielectric connectors or coatings

subject: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
rule: gutters and downpipes must not obstruct or be blocked by building elements that prevent water flow

subject: Planter Box
rule: planter box must have a drainage path (drain holes or open bottom) to prevent waterlogging of soil and roots
conditions: when used as a container for live plants
when exposed to rainfall or irrigation
exceptions: when used strictly as a decorative shell with a sealed liner and no plants are grown directly inside

subject: Planter Box
rule: planter box must not retain water against adjacent building surfaces for extended periods
conditions: when installed directly against a building wall or facade
exceptions: when a waterproof membrane and drainage gap are provided between the planter and the building surface

subject: Planter Box
rule: planter box must have structural capacity to contain the full weight of saturated soil and plants without deformation or collapse
conditions: when elevated above grade (e.g., balcony, rooftop, or wall-mounted)

subject: Planter Box
rule: planter box material must be rot-resistant or treated/protected when in continuous contact with moist soil
conditions: when made of wood or other organic material
exceptions: if the planter has an internal impermeable liner fully separating soil from the structure

subject: Planter Wall
rule: planter wall must be watertight to retain soil moisture and prevent water leakage into building structure
conditions: when serving as a planter enclosure adjacent to interior spaces
when built into a building assembly
exceptions: when planter wall is designed as a fully drained system with a dedicated waterproof membrane and drainage layer

subject: Planter Wall
rule: planter wall must have adequate structural capacity to resist lateral soil pressure
conditions: when planter height exceeds 600 mm
exceptions: when soil is contained within a self-supporting liner that transfers all loads independently to the structure

subject: Planter Wall
rule: planter wall must not wick moisture from soil into adjacent building envelope components
conditions: when constructed of porous materials such as concrete block, brick, or untreated wood
exceptions: when a complete capillary break (such as a waterproof membrane or drainage cavity) is provided between the planter and adjacent building elements

subject: Drainage Layer
rule: A drainage layer must be permeable enough to allow water to pass through to the drainage outlet
conditions: The drainage layer is installed in a below-grade or roof assembly where water removal is required
exceptions: The drainage layer is used only as a capillary break in a non-draining assembly

subject: Drainage Layer
rule: A drainage layer must have a continuous path to an exit or weep system so that water is not trapped
conditions: The drainage layer is part of an exterior wall, roof, or below-grade system designed to evacuate water
exceptions: The drainage layer functions solely as a capillary break with no bulk water ingress expected

subject: Drainage Layer
rule: A drainage layer must not be compressed or crushed to the point where its drainage void space is eliminated
conditions: The drainage layer is subjected to backfill, structural loads, or overburden pressure
exceptions: The drainage layer is specifically designed as a compressible capillary break with negligible drainage function under load

subject: Geotextile Filter Fabric
rule: Geotextile filter fabric must be placed on the soil side (not the aggregate side) of a drainage system to prevent soil migration while allowing water passage
conditions: when used in subsurface drainage applications
when installed adjacent to granular drainage aggregate
exceptions: when the fabric is a specialized cuspated or geocomposite drain where both sides are designed for different functions

subject: Geotextile Filter Fabric
rule: Geotextile filter fabric must not be exposed to direct ultraviolet (UV) radiation for extended periods beyond its rated UV stability
conditions: when the fabric is not rated for UV exposure
when UV-stabilized additives are not specified
exceptions: when the fabric is specifically manufactured with UV stabilizers rated for the expected exposure duration

subject: Geotextile Filter Fabric
rule: Geotextile filter fabric must have an apparent opening size (AOS) smaller than the D85 particle size of the soil being retained
conditions: when used for soil filtration and retention
exceptions: when the application is separation only and not filtration

subject: Geotextile Filter Fabric
rule: Geotextile filter fabric must not be placed directly against a geomembrane liner without an adequate drainage layer between them
conditions: when used in composite lining systems for containment
exceptions: when specifically designed as a geotextile-protection layer bonded to the geomembrane and the system is designed for direct contact

subject: Irrigation System (Raised Planter)
rule: Irrigation water supply line must have a backflow prevention device (e.g., vacuum breaker or backflow preventer) at the connection point to the potable water supply
conditions: irrigation system is connected to a potable water supply
exceptions: system is exclusively fed by non-potable water source (e.g., rainwater harvesting, graywater)

subject: Irrigation System (Raised Planter)
rule: Irrigation system must be designed with an automatic shutoff or rain sensor that overrides scheduled watering during sufficient rainfall
conditions: system includes an automatic controller or timer
exceptions: system is entirely manual without any automatic controller

subject: Irrigation System (Raised Planter)
rule: Drip irrigation or soaker hose emitters must not be installed above-grade without being covered or shielded by mulch, soil, or other protective material
conditions: system uses drip tubing, drip tape, or soaker hoses exposed to sunlight
exceptions: emitters are UV-stabilized and rated for exposed above-ground use per manufacturer specifications

subject: Irrigation System (Raised Planter)
rule: Irrigation system emitter flow rates and spacing must be compatible with the planter's soil volume and drainage capacity to prevent surface runoff or ponding
conditions: planter has limited soil depth (< 12 inches) or subgrade drainage is restricted

subject: Green Facade Mounting System
rule: the mounting system must support the full dead load of the green facade (plants, growing medium, irrigation pipes, saturated weight) plus live loads (wind, snow, seismic) without exceeding allowable stress limits of any component
conditions: system is attached to a building wall or freestanding structure

subject: Green Facade Mounting System
rule: the mounting system must not transfer moisture or water intrusion to the building envelope behind it
conditions: system is attached to a building wall
exceptions: systems designed with a fully drained and ventilated cavity that separates the mounting system from the building envelope

subject: Green Facade Mounting System
rule: the mounting system must be anchored to structurally adequate building elements capable of supporting the imposed loads
conditions: system is attached to an existing building

subject: Green Facade Mounting System
